This protein belongs to the chymotrypsin subfamily A (which includes mostly eukaryotic proteases), having a structure and specificity profile resembling that of eukaryotic trypsin-like proteases. This domain is also found in some eukaryotic proteins, such as HYDIN and CFA65 from human (which contain repeated Ig-like domains). (from Pfam)

label: TY-Chap1
product_name: T3SS (YopN, CesT) and YbjN peptide-binding chaperone 1
name_orig: T3SS (YopN, CesT) and YbjN peptide-binding chaperone 1
hmm_name: T3SS (YopN, CesT) and YbjN peptide-binding chaperone 1
comment: This domain is observed in host systems predicted to counter viral ribosylating toxins. They are predicted to function as peptide-binding chaperone domains that target proteins modified by ADPr and potentially misfolded as a consequence [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: HAAS
comment: This entry represents the HAAS (HTH-associated alpha-helical signaling) domain, found N-terminal to DUF1700 (Pfam:PF08006) which represents the transmembrane segment (Preprint https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.09.24.301986). (from Pfam)

label: GGR_cat
comment: This entry represents the catalytic domain of archaeal geranylgeranyl reductases (GGR) [1-3]. This domain contains the PxxYxWxFP sequence motif, which defines a specificity pocket in the structure, providing a structural basis for the substrate specificity of GGRs (PMID: 20869368). (from Pfam)

label: ANCHR-like_BBOX
comment: This entry represents a B-box domain found in ANCHR, ZFYV1 and TRIM proteins, which is characterised by C6H2 zinc-binding consensus motif [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: SecDF_P1_head
comment: This entry represents the head subdomain from P1 domain from SecDF proteins, which constitutes a critical element for proton transport [1-3]. P1 domain P1 binds an unfolded protein, and undergoes functionally important conformational changes. SecDF functions as a membrane-integrated chaperone that mediates ATP-independent protein translocation. (from Pfam)

label: MTPAP-like_central
product_name: Poly(A) RNA polymerase, mitochondrial-like, central palm domain
name_orig: Poly(A) RNA polymerase, mitochondrial-like, central palm domain
hmm_name: Poly(A) RNA polymerase, mitochondrial-like, central palm domain
comment: This domain is found in human Poly(A) RNA polymerase, mitochondrial (MTPAP) and similar proteins from eukaryotes. MTPAP is a noncanonical polymerase that creates the 3' poly(A) tail of mitochondrial transcripts. It contains three domains: a N-terminal domain RL (Pfam:PF17797) and the canonical palm (this entry) and fingers domains. This domain shows a five -stranded beta-sheet with the three catalytic aspartic acid residues located on its surface (PMID: 21292163), together with several alpha- helices, forming an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: Cdc6-ORC-like_ATPase_lid
comment: This entry represents the AAA+ ATPase lid domain of eukaryotic Cdc6/ORC proteins and its homologues from archaea [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: HCS_D2
comment: This entry represents domain found in diverse homologues of Homocitrate synthase (HCS) (PMID: 19776021). This domain follows the catalytic domain and is required for the enzymatic activity. (from Pfam)

label: ACT_AHAS_ss
comment: This entry represents the ACT domain found at the N-terminal of acetolactate synthase small subunit from Escherichia coli and similar sequences. This domain is also found at the C-terminal of D-3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase, which are closely related [4-7]. Acetolactate synthase small subunit (ILVH) is the regulatory subunit of acetohydroxyacid synthase (AHAS), an enzyme hat catalyses the first step in the biosynthesis of the three branched-chain amino acids [4-7]. (from Pfam)

label: Cgl0159
comment: This domain is found in the homologues of uncharacterised protein Cgl0159. It adopts classical (beta/alpha)8 barrel. Members of this family share significant similarity with Deoxyribose-phosphate aldolase. (from Pfam)

label: RS_preATP-grasp-like
comment: This domain precedes the ATP-grasp domain in a number of ribonucleotide synthetases [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: Glyco_hydro_2_N2
comment: This domain is found in a number of proteins belonging to glycosyl hydrolase 2 family [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: T1R_D3-like
product_name: type I restriction enzyme subunit R domain-containing protein
name_orig: Type I restriction enzyme subunit R domain 3
hmm_name: Type I restriction enzyme subunit R domain 3
comment: This domain is found in a restriction (R) subunit of a number of type I restriction enzymes. Subunit R is required for both nuclease and ATPase activities, but not for modification (PMID: 12654995). This domain folds into an alpha/beta structure consisting of a central beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on both sides of it. (from Pfam)

label: Glyco_hydro_123_N_2
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of a group of glycoside hydrolases 123, from bacteria [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Gal80p_C-like
comment: This domain is found in the homologues of Gal80p, an yeast regulatory protein closely related to glucose-fructose oxidoreductase. In Gal80p, this domain is likely involved in the binding of Gal4p (PMID: 17121853). (from Pfam)

label: Semialdhyde_dhC_1
comment: This entry represents the dimerisation domain found in N-acetyl-glutamine semialdehyde dehydrogenase (AgrC) and related sequences not included in Pfam:PF02774 [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: Mala_s_1-like
comment: This protein family includes Mal s 1 allergenic protein from the yeast Malassezia sympodialis (Mala s 1), which forms a relatively compact cup-like beta-propeller consisting of six blades each with four antiparallel beta-strands (PMID: 17481656). (from Pfam)

label: NA-iREase1
comment: This entry represents a predicted sensor domain in bacterial NACHT conflict systems. It is likely to bind a ligand which could contribute to activation of enzymatic domains additionally fused to the N-terminus of the NACHT module (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: NNH3
comment: This is an helical domain found at the N-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems (PMID: 37160116). This position is frequently occupied by an effector domain. (from Pfam)

label: SHOCT-like_DUF2089-C
comment: This is a SHOCT-like domain that occurs as a fusion of ZnR+DUF2089-HTH+SHOCT-like. It is found at the C-terminal of DUF2089 (Pfam:PF09862). (from Pfam)

label: WsaF_C
comment: This entry represents a domain found C-terminal in WsaF from Geobacillus stearothermophilus and related bacterial proteins. WsaF catalyses the formation of beta-1-2-linkage of rhamnose sugars in the carbohydrate polymer. It consists of two domains, the N-terminal of which binds the acceptor (the growing rhamnan chain), and a C-terminal which binds the substrate (dTDP-beta-l-rhamnose) (PMID: 20097205). (from Pfam)

label: K_trans_C
comment: This is a family of K+ potassium transporters that are conserved across phyla, having both bacterial (KUP) (PMID: 8226635), yeast (HAK) (PMID: 7621817), and plant (AtKT) (PMID: 9350997) sequences as members. This entry represents the C-terminal non-membrane domain. (from Pfam)

label: HI0933_like_1st
product_name: HI0933-like protein barrel and H2TH domain
name_orig: HI0933-like protein barrel and H2TH domain
hmm_name: HI0933-like protein barrel and H2TH domain
comment: This entry represents two structural domains that are found inserted within a Rossmann domain. (from Pfam)

label: Tc-R-P
comment: This domain occupies the toxin tip position in a subset of polymorphic toxin domains [1,2]. This domain is found at the extreme C-terminal of certain polymorphic toxin-related Tc-like toxins deployed by bacteria against eukaryotic host cells. This position is where the toxin module delivered into the target cells host resides (PMID: 36968430). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7014
comment: This domain is found in a group of bacterial proteins. It is often found C-terminal to Pfam:PF18863. It is predicted to adopt an all-alpha helical fold. (from Pfam)

label: Pel9A-like_beta_helix
name_orig: Pel9A-like, right handed beta helix region
hmm_name: Pel9A-like, right handed beta helix region
comment: This region is found in Pectate lyase L from Erwinia chrysanthemi (Pel9A) and similar bacterial and fungal proteins. Pel9A shows endo-cleaving activity on polygalacturonate or partially methylated pectin and has an important role in soft -rot disease. This region forms a parallel beta helix domain (PMID: 14670977). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7019
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found mainly in actinomycetes. Their function is unknown. They are predicted to adopt OB fold with significant similarity to Rpa. (from Pfam)

label: zf-DPOE
product_name: Zinc finger domain of DNA polymerase-epsilon
name_orig: Zinc finger domain of DNA polymerase-epsilon
hmm_name: Zinc finger domain of DNA polymerase-epsilon
comment: This zinc finger domain is found in the epsilon subunit of DNA polymerase. (from Pfam)

label: ACOX_C_alpha1
comment: This entry represents the C-alpha1 domain from acyl-CoA oxidases which has an all-alpha helical structure that a forms a four-helix bundle [1-5]. This domain includes the FAD-binding and substrate-binding sites. (from Pfam)

label: Pol_BBD
comment: This domain is found in Retrovirus-related Pol polyproteins from transposon TNT 1-94. It is predicted to adopt a beta-barrel fold with significant similarity to retroviral acid proteases. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_69
comment: This entry represents a winged helix-turn-helix domain that may bind to DNA. (from Pfam)

label: HpiC1-like
comment: This entry represents the homologues of HpiC1, a Stig cyclase that catalyzes the formation of 12-epi-hapalindole U. This enzyme folds into a beta-sandwich with jelly-roll topology that is distantly related to galactose-binding domains. HpiC1 has two integral Ca2+ ions, each with octahedral coordination geometry. Ca2+ ions are required for catalytic activity. (from Pfam)

label: M_Eco57I_C
product_name: Type II methyltransferase M.Eco57I, C-terminal domain
name_orig: Type II methyltransferase M.Eco57I, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Type II methyltransferase M.Eco57I, C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal of the gamma subtype methylase Type II methyltransferase M.Eco57I from Escherichia coli. This domain is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta configuration and is often found associated with Pfam:PF07669. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7017
comment: This entry represents a domain consisting of TPR repeats found at the N-terminal of of group of uncharacterised sequences predominantly from bacteria, which seem to be related to TOTE conflict systems as they are associated with Pfam:PF22708. (from Pfam)

label: TPR_EMC2
comment: ER membrane protein complex subunit 2 (EMC2, also known as tetratricopeptide repeat protein 35) is a tetratricopeptide repeat-containing protein, and a component of the ER membrane protein complex (EMC), which is required for efficient folding of proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). EMC2 is a cytosolic component of the complex (PMID: 32459176). Purified recombinant EMC2 formed a stable complex with either EMC8 or EMC9 (PMID: 32459176). (from Pfam)

label: NOMO1-like_9th
product_name: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, beta sandwich domain
name_orig: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, beta sandwich domain
hmm_name: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, beta sandwich domain
comment: This domain is found in human BOS complex subunit NOMO1 and similar sequences mainly from animals and plants. NOMO1 is a component of the multi-pass translocon (MPT) complex that mediates insertion of multi-pass membrane proteins into the lipid bilayer of membranes (PMID: 36261522). This domain is predicted to adopt a seven stranded beta sandwich fold. (from Pfam)

label: GAF_NLP
comment: This entry represents a GAF-like domain found in plant NLP proteins. Several NLP proteins contain two copies of this domain family. Members of the NLP family all contain an amino-terminal GAF domain, an intermediate RWP-RK domain, and a carboxy-terminal Phox and Bem1 (PB1) domain. Additionally, a nuclear export signal domain is predicted in the N-terminus (PMID: 35871642). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7033
comment: This uncharacterised domain is found in a group of polysaccharide deacetylases and similar proteins from bacteria. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical configuration. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6907
comment: This entry represents a family of Actinobacterial proteins of unknown function. AlphaFold predicts a confident dimeric arrangement. This family appears to be distantly related to Pfam:PF19887. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6909
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of two domains. The predicted C-terminal domain share similarity with the catalytic domains of purine and uridine phosphorylases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6916
comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a RIFT-type beta(6)-barrel topology with a greater similarity to FAD-binding domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6920
comment: This entry represents a set of uncharacterised proteins found in prokaryotes. They share remote similarity to LolA and LolB outer-membrane lipoproteins. Similar to LolA and LolB these proteins are predicted to have a hydrophobic cavity consisting of an unclosed beta-barrel and an alpha-helical lid. (from Pfam)

label: LppM
comment: LppM is a putative lipoprotein of Mycobacterium tuberculosis that has been shown to affect both phagocytosis by macrophages and progression of the phagosome into a more acidified compartment. Homologs of LppM, most of them appearing to be lipoproteins, are found broadly in the Actinomycetes.

label: TetR_C_13_2
hmm_name: LmrA/YxaF family transcription factor ligand-binding domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in a group of TetR transcription regulators, including YxaF (also known as T1414) (PMID: 16475182) and LmrA from Bacillus subtilis, which are paralogous to each other (PMID: 17483215). LmrA and YxaF are repressors that bind specifically to almost the same cis sequences, LmrA/YxaF boxes, located in the promoter regions of the lmrAB operon, the yxaF gene, and the yxaGH operon (PMID: 17483215). (from Pfam)

label: Phage_int_M
comment: This is the central domain of phage integrases. This domain is known to mediate DNA binding and binds to the major groove adjacent to the site of DNA cleavage (PMID: 12887904). It consists of two pairs of antiparallel helices that pack together at nearly a right angle and form a four-helix bundle. (from Pfam)

label: B129_C2H2-zf
product_name: Uncharacterized protein B-129, C2H2 zinc finger
name_orig: Uncharacterized protein B-129, C2H2 zinc finger
hmm_name: Uncharacterized protein B-129, C2H2 zinc finger
comment: This entry represents a C2H2 zinc finger found at the C-terminal of of poorly characterised viral proteins, including the uncharacterised protein B-129 from Sulfolobus spindle-shape virus 1 (SSV1). (from Pfam)

label: HUTI_composite_bact
comment: This entry represents the composite domain usually found in metal-dependent hydrolases which is interrupted by the catalytic alpha/beta barrel domain (Pfam:PF01979). This domain has a pseudo-barrel fold. This model covers the N-terminal segment of the composite domain of bacterial proteins, such as imidazolonepropionases. (from Pfam)

label: Cep192_D4
comment: Cep192 is a centrosomal protein with key roles in centriole duplication and pericentriolar material recruitment, organisation and regulation. Most of the metazoan Cep192 homologs consist of eight ASH/PapD-like domains. These are located at the C-terminal part of the proteins and are likely arranged in a beads-on-string fashion. This entry represents the fourth domain of the metazoan Cep192 homologs. This domain along with domain 5 constitutes the so-called Spd2 domain that is ubiquitously present in all SPD2/CEP192 homologues beyond Metazoa and represents the most conserved region amongst them (PMID: 35383272). (from Pfam)

label: NorB_cytochrome_c-like
product_name: Nitric oxide reductase subunit B, cytochrome c-like domain
name_orig: Nitric oxide reductase subunit B, cytochrome c-like domain
hmm_name: Nitric oxide reductase subunit B, cytochrome c-like domain
comment: This domain is found in Nitric oxide reductase subunit B from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (NorB) and similar bacterial sequences. NorB is the large component of the anaerobic respiratory chain that transforms nitrate to dinitrogen (denitrification). This entry represents the cytochrome C-like domain of NorB, which has 12 alpha-helices in the transmembrane region with two heme irons and and one non-heme iron (PMID: 21109633). (from Pfam)

label: Fer4_Nqo3
comment: NADH-quinone oxidoreductase subunit 3 (Nqo3) is a component of respiratory complex I. This protein is located at the peripheral arm of the complex and consists of multiple domains. This entry represents the second ferredoxin-like domain which contains Fe4-S4 cluster, one of the redox centers of the complex [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: Fervidolysin_NPro-like
comment: The founding member of this family is the N-terminal prodomain of fervidolysin, an extracellular subtilisin-like serine protease. This domain folds into a globular alpha/beta structure consisting of four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and two alpha-helices packed on one side of it (PMID: 14687574). The prodomain is proteolytically cleaved and removed from the proenzyme. (from Pfam)

label: PSMA-like_N
comment: This domain is found in the maltose-forming alpha-amylase from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Pyrococcus sp. ST04 (PSMA). This enzyme is able to hydrolyse both alpha-1,4-glucosidic and alpha-1,6-glucosidic bonds. PSMA protein consists of two domains: an N-terminal domain with a typical glycoside hydrolase 57 family (beta]/alpha)7-barrel fold and a C-terminal domain composed of alpha-helical bundles. This entry represents the N-terminal domain [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: PH0730-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of PH0730 from Pyrococcus horikoshii and similar archaeal proteins that contain the domain Pfam:PF14544 at the C-terminal. This domain adopts a winged helix fold. (from Pfam)

label: FKBP26_IF
comment: This domain is centrally located in Long-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase from Methanocaldococcus jannaschii (FKBP26) and similar archaeal sequences. FKBP26 catalyses the cis-trans isomerisation of peptidyl prolyl bonds and exhibits chaperone -like activity. The latter activity requires a 50-residue insertion (IF domain, for 'Insert-in-Flap', this entry) in the catalytic FKBP domain (Pfam:PF00254). It resembles a fractured four-stranded beta-barrel with the first and second strands connected by a helix that partially covers the fracture. It shows a highly hydrophobic surface [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Csm6_6H
comment: This entry represents the six-helix domain (6H) of Csm6 from Thermus termophilus and relates sequences (PMID: 26763118). Csm6 is a ssRNA-specific endoribonuclease that provides an auxiliary RNA-targeting interference mechanism in type III-A CRISPR-Cas systems, working together with the RNA- and DNA-targeting endonuclease activities of the Csm effector complex. Csm6 consists of a CARF domain at the N-terminal, a 6H central domain and the HEPN domain (Pfam:PF09670) at the C-terminal [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: Cpf1_PI-like
comment: The CRISPR-Cpf1 system is a class 2 CRISPR-Cas system that mediates robust DNA interference. Cpf1 differ from Cas9 in many aspects including the guide RNAs and substrate specificity. The Cpf1-crRNA complex cleaves a target double-stranded DNA containing a short T-rich PAM motif on the 5' end of the non-target strand. This PAM motif is recognized by the Cpf1 PI (PAM-interacting) domain. This domain folds into array of four helices and along with the helix-loop-helix motif in the REC1 domain, channel the PAM strand into a cavity leading to the nuclease site [1-2]. (from Pfam)

label: ISP_coupler
product_name: Type ISP restriction-modification enzyme, coupler domain
name_orig: Type ISP restriction-modification enzyme, coupler domain
hmm_name: Type ISP restriction-modification enzyme, coupler domain
comment: Type ISP restriction-modification (RM) enzymes cleave random DNA between distant target sites when two enzymes collide following convergent ATP-driven translocation. This entry represents the all-helical coupler domain of type ISP RM enzymes, which links the ATPase to the MTase and the C-terminal TRD (target recognition domain) domains and seems to play a key role in transferring conformational strain during initiation [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DmmA-like_N
product_name: Dimethylamine monooxygenase subunit DmmA-like, N-terminal domain
name_orig: Dimethylamine monooxygenase subunit DmmA-like, N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Dimethylamine monooxygenase subunit DmmA-like, N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of the dimethylamine monooxygenase subunit DmmA from Methylocella silvestris (Msil_3607, Swiss:B8EJ00) and similar sequences, mainly found in proteobacteria and actinomycetes. Dimethylamine (DMA) monooxygenase is required for metabolism of trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) [1,2]. This domain may adopt a Rossmann-like fold similar to Ferredoxin/Ferric reductase-like NAD binding domain. (from Pfam)

label: ABhydrolase-like_N
comment: This is the N-terminal domain found in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins, which have a Phospholipase/carboxylesterase/thioesterase domain (Pfam:PF02230) at the C-terminal. This domain consists of ARM repeats. (from Pfam)

label: K319L-like_PKD
comment: This entry represents the PKD domain of Dyslexia-associated protein KIAA0319-like protein, in which it is found in four copies. This entry also includes Kunitz-type protease inhibitor 1 and LRP11 from human. (from Pfam)

label: Big-like
comment: This entry represents bacterial domains that are structurally similar to an immunoglobulin-like domain of intimins. Members of this family include Surface layer protein from Geobacillus stearothermophilus. (from Pfam)

label: Staph_reg_Sar_Rot
comment: This entry represents transcriptional regulatory proteins in Staphylococcal species including SarA and Rot [1-5]. Sar is a global regulator with both positive and negative effects that controls expression of several virulence factors and biofilm formation process in a cell density-dependent manner. Rot plays a key role in regulating S. aureus virulence through activation or repression of promoters that control expression of a large number of critical virulence factors (PMID: 25331435). (from Pfam)

label: MLPTv-like_HTH
comment: This entry represents a winged helix-turn-helix (wHTH) domain present in MLPTv (MarR-like protein from Thermoplasma volcanium) (PMID: 20162616). (from Pfam)

label: SYY_C-terminal
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of Tyrosine--tRNA ligases which contains the S4 motif that binds RNA [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: RepB_primase_C
comment: RepB_primase is a DNA-primase produced by P4-like phages. It is a zinc-independent primase unlike Pri-type primases. It takes up a dumbbell shaped consisting of an N-terminal catalytic domain separated by a long alpha-helix plus tether and a C-terminal helical-bundle domain. Primases are necessary for phage replication. RepBprime primases such as in this family recognise both ssiA and ssiB, ie only 1 single-stranded primase initiation site on each strand, independently of each other and then synthesise primers that are elongated by DNA polymerase III. The phage is thus replicated exclusively in leading strand mode (PMID: 19416864). (from Pfam)

label: choice_anch_I
comment: This entry represents the choice-of-anchor I domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6992
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are enriched with hydrophobic residues and are likely associated with the membrane. These proteins contain two conserved motifs GLDxxYxxxG and FLxxFD. (from Pfam)

label: PBP2
comment: This is a family of archaeal proteins, previously known as DUF6995, representing homologues of PolB1 Binding Protein 2 (PBP2). PBP2, is a subunit of PolB1 enzyme that is a member of the archaeal B-family of DNA polymerases. PBP2 along with PBP1, associate with distinct surfaces of the larger catalytic subunit and influence the enzymatic properties of the DNA polymerase (PMID: 28462924). Members of this family adopt a winged helix (HTH) fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6998
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share significant sequence similarity with PvuII endonucleases and are predicted to adopt similar structure. The predicted structures, however, do not suggest similarity in the active site architecture. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6999
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt alpha-helical structure. These proteins contain several invariant histidines and aspartates that may have a functional role. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7000
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure consisting of a cradle-like beta-sheet with alpha-helices pocked on the convex side of it. It contains a highly conserved GYMDFTYF sequence motif that may be of functional importance. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7004
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and archaea. Proteins in this family are approximately 160 amino acids in length. They are predicted to adopt globular alpha/beta structure. These proteins contain two highly conserved sequence motifs GxFDxWC and KRxKRLG that may be of functional importance. (from Pfam)

label: AEP-TOTE
product_name: TOTE conflict system archaeo-eukaryotic primase domain-containing protein
name_orig: TOTE conflict system, Archaeo-Eukaryotic Primase domain
hmm_name: TOTE conflict system, Archaeo-Eukaryotic Primase domain
comment: This entry represents the Archaeo-Eukaryotic Primase domain predicted to function as RNA polymerases in the TOTE (TPR, OB, TBP, Effector) conflict systems, potentially generating transcripts for hybrid duplex formation (PMID: 35609893). (from Pfam)

label: CesT_Tir_1
comment: This entry represents a novel member of the CesT/Tir superfamily of chaperones found linked to the yjfJ family of PspA genes (Preprint https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.09.24.301986). (from Pfam)

label: DuOB
comment: This entry contains two domain copies of the OB fold. There is nearly absolutely conserved cysteine, serine/threonine, arginine, and aspartate residues which are predicted to line a deep cleft formed at the interface of the two OB domains. The predicted spatial arrangement of the tandem OB domains closely parallels OB-dyads from single-stranded nucleic acid-end binding proteins, such as the telomere-binding domain alpha-subunit, with the nucleic acid being lodged in a cleft formed by the two OB domains. Drawing an analogy to the SRAP domain, it has been suggested that the DuOB domain could potentially form crosslinks to DNA at the abasic sites via its conserved cysteine. It is found on the genome adjacent to DUF488 and DUF4326 proteins, which could potentially also catalyse thiotransfer reactions required for forming or resolving the cysteine-DNA crosslinks, paralleling recent findings where HD phosphatases mediate the transfer of a phosphorylated substrate to a hydroxyl-group-containing residue (PMID: 36968430). (from Pfam)

label: GMT-wHTH
comment: This entry represents a rapidly-evolving wHTH domain C-terminally fused to Rossmann fold methylase specifically related to the guanine methylase. Often co-occurs on the genome across a broad range of bacterial phylogenies with a further gene encoding a RADICAL SAM enzyme (DUF5131 Pfam:PF07505). This two-gene island is predicted to catalyse a DNA/RNA guanine modification comparable to the precursors of Wybutosine. This wHTH domain could be a sensor that recognises a rapidly-evolving nucleic acid sequence, implicating the gene pair in a conflict response to an invasive genic element (PMID: 36968430). (from Pfam)

label: DCD_C
comment: This entry includes several bacterial 2'-deoxycytidine 5'-triphosphate deaminase proteins (EC:3.5.4.13) (DCD) which consist of two dUTPase-like domains (PDBe:2r9q). This entry represents the C-terminal domain. (from Pfam)

label: KYNU_C
comment: This domain is found only as a C-terminal region of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) dependent enzymes such as kynureninase and the pyoverdine biosynthesis enzyme PvdN.

label: DNAX_ATPase_lid
product_name: DNA polymerase III clamp loader subunit, ATPase lid domain
name_orig: DNA polymerase III clamp loader subunit, ATPase lid domain
hmm_name: DNA polymerase III clamp loader subunit, ATPase lid domain
comment: This entry represents the AAA+ ATPase lid domain of DNA polymerase III clamp loader subunit [1-4]. (from Pfam)

label: ECR1_N_2
product_name: Exosome RNA binding protein RRP4 N-terminal domain
name_orig: Exosome RNA binding protein RRP4 N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Exosome RNA binding protein RRP4 N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in exosome RNA binding protein RRP4 and related proteins [1-5]. RRP4 is a part of the exosome regulatory substrate recognition platform. This domain is structurally similar to ribosomal L27 protein. (from Pfam)

label: CBM_4_9_1
comment: This entry represents domain found in accessory protein BppA and related proteins. Given the structural similarity to carbohydrate binding domains, it is likely that this domain is a carbohydrate binding module. BppA is a virion's baseplate component. The precise role of this protein in absorption is elusive but the presence of a carbohydrate binding domain with an extended saccharidic binding site suggests that this protein probably participates in receptor binding together with the bona fide receptor binding proteins (PMID: 26814179). (from Pfam)

label: GKRP_SIS_N
product_name: Glucokinase regulatory protein N-terminal SIS domain
name_orig: Glucokinase regulatory protein N-terminal SIS domain
hmm_name: Glucokinase regulatory protein N-terminal SIS domain
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in glucokinase regulatory protein (GKRP) and related proteins. GKRP regulates glucokinase and it is activated by fructose 6-phosphate and inactivated by fructose 1-phosphate. It consists of two topologically identical SIS domains and and alpha-helical lid domain [1-4]. (from Pfam)

label: WHD_DUF6293
hmm_name: DUF6293 family protein C-terminal winged helix domain
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in functionally uncharacterised archaeal proteins. This domain is predicted to adopt winged helix domain structure. It is usually located upstream Pfam:PF19810 and this domain organisation as well as the predicted structure are reminiscent of CRISPR-associated protein, Csa3. (from Pfam)

label: Thiolase_C_1
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in a number of thiolases and their homologues. Thiolases are essential CoA-dependent enzymes in lipid metabolism. This domain folds into a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with helices packed on one side. (from Pfam)

label: Cas9_RuvC
comment: This entry represent a RuvC endonuclease domain (RNAseH-like) domain found in CRISPR-Cas9 from Streptococcus pyogenes and related sequences [1-5]. This domain, and the HNH (Pfam:PF13395) domain of Cas9, are used to cleave the DNA strands complementary (target) and non-complementary (non-target) to the crRNA, respectively (PMID: 26990991). This domain is related to Pfam:PF18541. (from Pfam)

label: PTP-NADK
name_orig: DSP-PTPase phosphatase fused to NAD+ Kinase
comment: While the land plant version of this DSP-PTPase domain is likely inactive as the catalytic cysteine is replaced by serine or threonine, the rest are predicted to be active. Keeping with the proposed sugar phosphatase activity in related members, these domains could potentially function as phosphatases converting NADP to NAD+. (from Pfam)

label: Nlig-Ia
comment: The alpha-helical Nlig-Ia domain is found at the N-terminal of DNA ligases and it has been proposed to either swivel the NAD+ close to the ligase active site lysine on the RAGNYA domain or function as an allosteric NAD+ binding site. The Nlig-Ia domain is also observed as a solo protein in phages that do not encode a separate NAD+-dependent ligase catalytic module, suggesting the domain can function independently of a DNA ligase. It has been proposed that these domains likely function as NAD+ sensors which might help indicate to the phage the development of NADase host effectors or shield NAD+ from the action of such effectors [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: VKGC_lumenal_dom
comment: Using reduced vitamin K, oxygen, and carbon dioxide, gamma-glutamyl carboxylase (VKGC) post-translationally modifies certain glutamates by adding carbon dioxide to the gamma position of those amino acids. In vertebrates, the modification of glutamate residues of target proteins is facilitated by an interaction between a propeptide present on target proteins and the gamma-glutamyl carboxylase (PMID: 10748045). This entry represents the lumenal domain found in animals and bacteria. This domain is associated with Pfam:PF05090 [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: PTP-SAK
name_orig: Swiss Army Knife protein, DSP-PTPase phosphatase domain
hmm_name: Swiss Army Knife protein, DSP-PTPase phosphatase domain
comment: The Swiss Army Knife class of proteins features a diverse domain repertoire acting to repair RNA damaged in the wake of RNase attacks. PTP-SAK is one such domain, a phosphatase of the rhodanese-phosphatase superfamily. It is predicted to 'clean' RNA ends by removing phosphate groups, preparing them for ligation by their associating RNA ligases [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: WelO5
comment: This entry represents the homologues of the carrier-protein-independent halogenase WelO5. This enzyme chlorinates C13 of 12-epi-fischerindole U to yield 12-epi-fischerindole G. This enzymatic transformation constitutes the first step in the oxidative maturation to welwitindolinones. WelO5 adopts a cupin-like fold that is also characteristic of Fe/2OG enzymes (PMID: 27348090). (from Pfam)

label: ApeI-like
comment: This entry represents the homologues of ApeI dehydratase. This enzyme forms a heterodimer with ApeP that carries out dehydratation in APE biosynthesis. Both subunits in this complex adopt a typical hotdog fold comprising six antiparallel beta-strands and a central alpha-helix (PMID: 30908039). (from Pfam)

label: GldL_N
comment: This entry represents a domain found N-terminal in homologues of Gliding motility protein GldL. GldL has two transmembrane helices (this entry) and a cytoplasmic domain. GldL is a component of the motor complex used by the T9SS and the gliding motility apparatus to transport proteins and gliding adhesin movement at the outer membrane. This motor complex consists of five copies of GldL surrounding two copies of GldM (PMID: 35446127). (from Pfam)

label: AIPR_N
product_name: Abortive infection phage resistance protein N-terminal domain
name_orig: Abortive infection phage resistance protein N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Abortive infection phage resistance protein N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents a N-terminal domain found in an abortive infection phage resistance protein often found in restriction modification system operons (PMID: 18346280). (from Pfam)

label: KH_PNO1_2nd
comment: This entry represents the second KH domain found in the PNO1 protein. PNO1 is part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit. (from Pfam)

label: NOMO1-like_1st
product_name: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, first beta sandwich domain
name_orig: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, first beta sandwich domain
hmm_name: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, first beta sandwich domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of human BOS complex subunit NOMO1 and similar sequences mainly from animals and plants. NOMO1 is a component of the multi-pass translocon (MPT) complex that mediates insertion of multi-pass membrane proteins into the lipid bilayer of membranes (PMID: 36261522). This domain is predicted to adopt a seven stranded beta sandwich fold. (from Pfam)

label: ATP-synt_VA_C
product_name: ATP synthase beta subunit C-terminal domain-containing protein
name_orig: C-terminal domain of V and A type ATP synthase
hmm_name: ATP synthase beta subunit-like C-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents a small alpha helical domain found at the C-terminus of a variety of ATP synthases. (from Pfam)

label: WHD
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with similarity to MarR family of transcription factors (Pfam:PF12802). This domain is found usually in combination with AAA ATPase domains (Pfam:PF00004). (from Pfam)

label: WHD_HRQ1
product_name: ATP-dependent helicase HRQ1, winged helix domain
name_orig: ATP-dependent helicase HRQ1, winged helix domain
hmm_name: ATP-dependent helicase HRQ1, winged helix domain
comment: This domain is found in the homologues of ATP-dependent helicase HRQ1. HRQ1 is a helicase with 3'-5' helicase activity involved in genome stability (PMID: 23456718). Hrq1 is able to unwind relatively long duplex DNA up to 120-bp and is significantly stimulated by a preexisting fork structure. This domain is predicted to form a globular structure with significant similarity to Winged helix HTH domains. (from Pfam)

label: P_loop_sacsin
comment: This roughly 80-amino acid domain belongs to the clan of ATP-binding domains with the Walker A motif (P-loop). It starts and ends with well-conserved alpha-helical regions, interrupted by a region of beta-strands that are prone to insertions of additional sequence. In a large fraction of members, the critical lysine (K) of the P-loop motif GxxGxGK[ST] is replaced by phenylalanine (F), making the function of the motif in those family members unclear. This domain tends to occur as a N-terminal domain of proteins that average over 1000 amino acids in length, such as the human protein sacsin.

hmm_name: phage tail tube protein, lmo2291 family

label: TenpIN
product_name: type III toxin-antitoxin system TenpIN family toxin
hmm_name: type III toxin-antitoxin system TenpIN family toxin
comment: A type III toxin-antitoxin system consists of a toxin protein and an antitoxin RNA. TenpIN family toxin is widely found in numerous bacteria and archaea.

label: CptIN
product_name: type III toxin-antitoxin system CptIN family toxin
hmm_name: type III toxin-antitoxin system CptIN family toxin
comment: A type III toxin-antitoxin system consists of a toxin protein and an antitoxin RNA. CptIN family toxin is widely found in numerous bacteria and archaea.

label: ATPase_Sll1717
comment: Members of this P-loop-containing ATPase (or possibly GTPase) protein family have been annotated as DNA repair protein, FunZ, but the function is unknown. Members often appear next to or fused to a second P-loop-containing ATPase domain more similar to that of ParA family proteins.

label: AAA_KGGVGR
comment: Members of this P-loop-containing domain, related to various AAA-type ATPases, have a well-conserved xKGGVGR[ST] that differs from the more typical GxxGxGK[ST] of P-loop motifs. This domain often is found in long, multidomain proteins that have an additional ATP-binding domain of a different type (see NF047389.1). Member protein Sll1563 was found to be downregulated during nitrogen starvation as part of the NtcA regulon, but its function was not determined.

label: barrel_OmpL47
comment: The Leptospira surface-exposed protein OmpL47 (see NF047441) contains three tandem copies of this predicted beta-barrel domain. The AlphaFold prediction for Q04PQ5 illustrates the fold prediction. Proteins may have as many as 12 copies of the domain. Members of this family are often annotated as Ig-like domain-containing proteins or as carbohydrate-active enzymes, largely based on other domains present. While repeats of the domain often have a periodicity of 80 amino acids or more, this HMM built with a length of 68, in part because the final repeat is often shorter.

label: LIC_12616_fam
hmm_name: phage neck terminator protein, myophage Pam3 family
comment: The founding member of this family, LIC_12616 from Leptospira interrogans, is known as an uncharacterized protein encoded at one end of a small, prophage-like genomic island. Members are found in Leptospira, Paenibacillus, Clostridium, etc. Protein Gp12 from myophage Pam3 was shown to be a phage neck terminator protein.

label: Rv3131_FMN_oxido
comment: Paralogs Rv2032, Rv3131, and Rv3127 in Mycobacterium tuberculosis are recognizably homologous to classical nitroreductases (see Pfam model PF00881). Rv2032 is known as Acg (Acr-coregulated gene) because Rv2032 and Acr (Rv2031c) are both highly upregulated by DosR (dormancy survival regulator), a response regulator transcription factor involved in the response to hypoxia and to the macrophage intracellular environment. Rv3131 and Rv3127 likewise belong to the DosR regulon. MSMEG_3955 from Mycobacterium smegmatis, most closely related to Rv3131, was reported to be a trimeric NADPH-dependent FMN oxidoreductase, and to lack detectable nitroreductase activity.

label: LIC_10190_fam
comment: Members of this broadly distributed proteins family average about 600 amino acids in length and are highly hydrophobic. Two of the very few invariant amino acids occur in a DxxxY motif. Some members of this family show sequence similarity to dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferases (see PF13231), suggesting they may be glycosyltranferases.

label: LA_3659_fam
comment: This family is named for founding protein LA_3659, even though that protein appears not to be complete at the N-terminus. For members in the genus Leptospira, a large number of fragmentary sequences occur in non-redundant protein sequence databases, suggesting negative selection in certain growth conditions. Members of this family are also found broadly outside of Leptospira. The function is unknown.

label: TPR_END_plus
comment: This HMM describes a 56 amino acid region found near or at the C-terminus of many bacterial tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) proteins, containing a variant form of the TPR repeat (about 34 amino acids) followed by a stretch of sequence unique to this sequence region.

label: IS66_ISAeme5_TnpA
product_name: IS66 family insertion sequence element accessory protein TnpA
hmm_name: IS66 family insertion sequence element accessory protein TnpA
comment: This family is based on IS66 family insertion sequence (IS element) accessory proteins for transposition, such as TnpA from ISAeme5.

label: NADase_discoid
comment: This family includes the glycan-binding N-terminal domain (called the translocation domain) of the nicotine adenine dinucleotide glycohydrolase toxin (NADase) of Steptococcus pyogenes. Related domains are often referred to as the discoidin domain.

label: seleno_TsoY
comment: Members of this rare protein family are selenoproteins. The name TsoY derives from its discovery next to TsoR, a transcription factor more commonly associated with a Three Selenoprotein Operon, TsoABC. That operon occasionally contains a fourth selenoprotein, TsoX.

label: TsoY_fam
comment: This family of proteins is named for its most distinctive branch, TsoY, in which all proteins are selenoproteins. Members known so far that fall outside the TsoY branch always have Cys at a position equivalent to the Sec (U) in TsoY selenoproteins. The function is unknown.

label: CopZ_Nterm_CC
comment: Members of this family are homologous to family NF045877 and to the N-terminal half of the copper chaperone CopZ from Archaeoglobus fulgidus. In contrast to NF045877, which contains a number selenoproteins with a CU motif near the N-terminus, it appears that all members of this family have cysteine only, usually including the motif CC.

hmm_name: type VII toxin-antitoxin system HepT family RNase toxin

hmm_name: type VII toxin-antitoxin system MntA family adenylyltransferase antitoxin

label: Clp_like_SDH
product_name: SDH family Clp fold serine proteinase
hmm_name: SDH family Clp fold serine proteinase
comment: Members of this family show a distant relation to Clp family serine proteinases, and are expected to have a related fold, but differ in the order of catalytic triad residues, SDH (Ser, Asp, His) instead of SHD. Members are found in both archaea and bacteria.

label: phas_rel_Lepto
comment: Members of this family are homologous to the phasin family proteins of Pfam model PF05597, but are found regularly in bacteria that lack the poly-hydroxyalkanoate inclusions where phasins are found. Three members of this family are found in the model strain Leptospira interrogans serovar Copenhageni str. Fiocruz L1-130, with locus tags LIC_10348, LIC_11972, and LIC_13183.

label: caspase_w_EACC1
comment: The caspase domain described in this model occurs in bacterial conflict systems, generally as the N-terminal region of longer effector proteins that are encoded next to EACC1 (effector-associated constant component 1) proteins.

label: CBU_0592_membra
comment: Most members of this family are about 90 amino acids in length and rich in hydrophobic residues, suggesting location largely in the membrane. A minority have an additional C-terminal domain related to cyclic nucleotide-binding domains. Some members of this family have two copies of the domain. The family is named for CBU_0592 from Coxiella burnetii RSA 493. The function is unknown.

label: CopZ_AFE_1862
comment: Members of this family, including AFE_1862 from Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans ATCC 23270 and TTHA1718 from Thermus thermophilus HB8, appear able to and be induced by copper, but also other metals such as cadmium.

label: TA_toxin_VapC
product_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system VapC family toxin
hmm_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system VapC family toxin

label: betaine_BCCT
comment: Members of this family are BCCT family transporters known or thought to be involved in the uptake of glycine betaine (known simply as betaine) for osmoprotection or metabolic utilization. Some members of the seed alignment were selected based on proximity to glycine betaine--corrinoid protein methyltransferase (EC 2.1.1.376) and are proposed to import betaine for utilization. The enzyme glycine betaine--corrinoid protein methyltransferase does not contain pyrrolysine, but is closely related to trimethylamine methyltransferase (EC 2.1.1.250), which does. Also included are OpuD from Bacillus subtilis, BetL from Listeria monocytogenes, and closely related proteins. Many members of the BCCT family transport multiple substrates, including also proline, choline, dimethylsulfoniopropionate, etc. This model was given fairly stringent cutoffs to enrich for family members whose primary role is betaine uptake.

label: spike_base
comment: Members of this family form the base of the spike on the capsids of phage and phage-related gene transfer agents.

label: YbjQ_2
comment: This domain is found in several copies in human C2 domain -containing protein 5 (C2CD5) and similar proteins predominantly found in animals. C2CD5 is required for insulin -stimulated glucose transport and glucose transporter SLC2A4 /GLUT4 translocation to the plasma membrane in adipocytes. This domain is predicted to show a beta-sheet and an alpha-helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7088
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal of a group of poorly characterised bacterial sequences. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7097
comment: This protein family includes a group of proteins from halobacteria. It shows several conserved motifs DCPH, RGCL and RPLL/VEEHHLSxY. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_EML_2
comment: This entry represents beta-propeller domains of echinoderm microtubule-associated protein (EMAP)-like (EML) proteins (PMID: 24706829), a family of proteins that contribute to formation of the mitotic spindle and interphase microtubule network (PMID: 24706829). In these proteins, the beta-propellers are intimately associated as a pair which was defined as tandem atypical propeller in EMLs (TAPE) domain. There is a hydrophobic core between the propellers which corresponds the HELP motif (Pfam:PF03451) that contributes blades 1 and 14 buried at the interface and joints them (PMID: 24706829). This model completes the second beta-propeller of the TAPE pair in EMLs. In some members, such as EML5 and EML6, there are three TAPE pairs. The first beta-propeller of the pair is represented in Pfam:PF23409. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7108_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of the uncharacterised protein HVO_0731 from Haloferax volcanii (Swiss:D4GTA0) and similar proteins from halobacteria. It is predicted to adopt an all-alpha structure. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7121
comment: This family represents a group of proteins mainly from halobacteria. Members are predicted to show an alpha-helical configuration forming an intramolecular coiled-coil structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7122
comment: This domain is found in a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7129
comment: This domain is found in a group of small proteins mainly from Halobacteria. It contains highly conserved cysteine residues arranged in two CxxC motifs that likely coordinate zinc. The first motif could be more broadly defined as YECxxCG. This domain is predicted to adopt zinc ribbon fold. (from Pfam)

label: LysM3_LYK4_5
comment: This entry represents the third LysM domain found in proteins from plants, including LYK4/5 from Arabidopsis thaliana. The LysM domain adopt a beta-alpha-alpha-beta fold, according to structure predictions. LYK4 is a chitin-binding protein and contributes to chitin-triggered immunity (PMID: 31969929). LYK5 has been identified as a receptor with a very high affinity to chitooligosaccharides (PMID: 31969929). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7133
comment: This domain is found in a number of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to form a a six-bladed beta-propeller with significant similarity to glucose/sorbosone dehydrogenases. (from Pfam)

label: AMP-binding_C_3
comment: This is a small domain that is found C terminal to Pfam:PF00501. It has a central beta sheet core that is flanked by alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: GH3_M
comment: The GH3 IAA-amido conjugating enzyme family consists of proteins that catalyze the synthesis of amino acid conjugates with indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) or jasmonate (JA), which are plant hormones. This entry represents the central domain of these enzymes. These enzymes play a crucial role in regulating plant hormone levels by conjugating excess IAA and JA to amino acids, thus providing a mechanism for plants to maintain hormonal homeostasis. The conjugation process is ATP-dependent and involves the adenylation of the hormone followed by the transfer to an amino acid. This family is involved in various plant physiological processes including disease resistance, stamen and carpel differentiation, floret fertility, and response to environmental stresses such as wounding and pathogen attack. Some members also exhibit activity towards synthetic auxins and may confer resistance to herbicides. The family's broad substrate specificity includes various amino acids and analogs of IAA, contributing to the complexity of hormone regulation in plants. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_NWD2_C
comment: This entry represents the beta-propeller found at the C-terminal of NACHT and WD repeat domain-containing protein 2 (NWD2) from human and similar eukaryotic proteins. The function of these proteins is not yet known. (from Pfam)

label: LRR_14
comment: This entry represents a region containing leucine-rich repeats found in a variety of plant resistance proteins. (from Pfam)

label: BP74_N
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in the Cyclic AMP-inducible protein BP74 from Dictyostelium discoideum and related proteins. The BP74 gene is a cyclic AMP-regulated and expressed during the Dictyostelium development (PMID: 2555685). This domain is predicted to fold into an open beta-barrel capped with two alpha-helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7151
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in bacterial proteins. Some of the members of this family might contain an EF-hand calcium binding site. The predicted structure of this domain consists of three beta sheets. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_BBS7
comment: BBS7 is one of seven proteins that form the BBSome complex, localised at ciliary bases in the cytoplasm (PMID: 23572516). The BBS7 beta-propeller interacts with the beta-propeller domain of another BBSome protein, BBS1, in order to control access of the membrane-recruiting protein ARL6 (PMID: 31303482). Mutations on or lack of BB7 (or any BBSome protein) causes Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS), characterized by cilium dysfunction (PMID: 16909204). (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_TiaS
comment: This entry represents the zinc ribbon domain (ZRD) found at the the C-terminal of tRNA(Ile2) 2-agmatinylcytidine synthetase TiaS. TiaS is an archaeal ATP-dependent agmatine transferase that catalyses the formation of 2-agmatinylcytidine (agm2C) at the wobble position (C34) of tRNA(Ile2) [1-3]. This modified base specifically recognises AUA codons. TiaS consists of four domains, the TCKD domain (Pfam:PF22641) at the N-terminal followed by the FLD domain (Pfam:PF08489), an OB fold domain and a C-terminal ZRD. The ZDR domain is responsible for the recognition of the acceptor arm of tRNA(Ile2) (PMID: 30121296). (from Pfam)

label: TIM-barrel_NCTSP
name_orig: Non-contractile tail sheath protein TIM barrel
hmm_name: non-contractile tail sheath protein TIM barrel domain
comment: This entry represents the TIM barrel domain found in the non-contractile tail sheath protein of Bacteriophage N4 (BPN4). This protein is essential for BPN4 infectivity and it is hypothesized that it mediates binding with target cell receptors (PMID: 18374942). The function of this domain is unknown. This entry also includes sequences from bacteria, predominantly from Sphingobium spp. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7211
comment: This entry represents a short highly motif that is found in some phage proteins, usually at the N-terminus. The function of this motif is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7226
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is usually found in combination with [Pfam:PF22515] and [Pfam:PF22518]. It is predicted to contain a winged helix (WH) domain that is flanked at the C terminus with a small helical subdomain. The latter packs on the WH domain to form a compact globular structure. (from Pfam)

label: LD_SV2
comment: This entry represents the luminal domain found in synaptic vesicle protein 2 A, B and C (SV2A, SV2B and SV2C) from animals. SV2s are specific to vesicles that undergo calcium-regulated secretion and are essential for normal nervous system function, particularly for neurotransmission (PMID: 30826548). SV2s have also been identified as targets for botulinum neurotoxins (BoNTs) serotypes A, D, E and F (PMID: 19476346). In the case of VS2C, this domain interacts directly and allows BoNT/A transport into host cells (PMID: 24240280). (from Pfam)

label: TPR_CcmH_CycH
name_orig: Cytochrome c-type biogenesis protein H TPR domain
comment: This entry represents the TPR domain found in cytochrome c-type biogenesis proteins CcmH and CycH from bacteria. These proteins are membrane-anchored thiol-oxidoreductases that are essential in the maturation of c-type cytochromes (PMID: 7635817). In the case of CycH, it has been hypothesised that this TPR domain interacts with other proteins in order to mediate the assembly of c-type cytochromes (PMID: 14758542). This entry also represents a TPR domain found in other proteins such as NRFG, NRFF and RNA polymerase-associated protein CDC27. (from Pfam)

label: SusG_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in the starch utilization system protein G (SusG) from bacteria. SusG forms part of the SusDEFG lipoprotein complex tethered to the outer surface of the cell and is involved in starch hydrolysis and subsequent utilization of the resulting sugars as an energy source (PMID: 10986238). SusG has been shown to have enzymatic starch-hydrolysing activity (PMID: 10572122). This entry also represents the C-terminal domain of other oligo-1,6-glucosidases, such as the trehalose-6-phosphate hydrolase TreA, glucan 1,6-alpha-glucosidase dexB and Oligo-1,6-glucosidase 1 malL from bacteria. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7281
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It shares some similarity to the C-terminal domain of JetD [Pfam:PF09983]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7287
comment: This entry includes uncharacterised archaeal proteins including Uncharacterized protein AF_0763 from Archaeoglobus fulgidus [Swiss:O29495]. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_tail_terminator_9
comment: This entry represents the neck terminator protein gp12 from cyanophage Pam3 (PMID: 36656854). Six gp12 subunits form a hexameric ring that terminates neck assembly and links to the tail tube/sheath. Each subunit has an N-terminal loop, a conserved globular domain, and a protruding beta-sheet domain. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_tail_tube_init
product_name: Putative phage tail tube initiator protein
name_orig: Putative phage tail tube initiator protein
hmm_name: Putative phage tail tube initiator protein
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Based on structure prediction these proteins show similarity to the Pam3 gp17 the tail tube initiator protein. Six gp17 subunits form a hexameric ring that initiates tail tube polymerization from the baseplate. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7310
comment: This entry represents a coiled-coil region found in uncharacterised archaeal proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7318
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised archaeal proteins. (from Pfam)

label: YQBQ
comment: This entry represents a domain found standalone in the Uncharacterized protein YqbQ, Phage-like element PBSX protein XkdQ and other related proteins. This domain is also found N-terminal in Clostridioides difficile endolysin (Ecd09610). It is predicted to adopt a globular structure comprised mainly of two beta-barrels arranged in a head-to-tail manner. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7342
comment: This family includes uncharacterised archaeal proteins that contain a HTH domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7343
comment: This entry represents the HTH domain found in group of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7350
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised archaeal proteins. It is predicted to adopt Ig-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_CAF1B_HIR1
comment: This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found in chromatin assembly factor 1 subunit CAF1B (also known as p60 subunit) from animals, and its homologues Cac2 from yeasts and FAS from plants. These proteins are involved in DNA synthesis-coupled chromatic assembly in S-phase and chromatin assembly following DNA repair alongside other CHAF proteins in what is known as CAF1 complex [1,2]. In plants, the loss of activity of the CAF1 pathway causes delay and arrest of the cell cycle during pollen development (PMID: 18045841). The CAF1 complex is also required for stable maintenance of telomeres and 45S rDNA in Arabidopsis (PMID: 20699390). This domain is involved in CAF1B interactions with other CAF1 complex subunits (PMID: 27221973). This entry also includes histone cell cycle regulator HIRA from animals and their yeast orthologues HIR1, which are required in replication-independent chromatic assembly (PMID: 15121850). The beta-propeller of HIRA proteins is involved in the protein interactions with Ubinuclein-1 (UBN1) to achieve chromatic-remodelling pathway in senescent cells (PMID: 19029251). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7384
comment: This is a group of uncharacterised sequences from archaea which are related to VapC (virulence-associated protein C) family of proteins. Members of this entry may adopt a PIN-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7390
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage protein. These proteins adopt a compact globular domain. The predicted structure of the domain shows a positively charged surface suggesting a possible nucleic acid binding function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7413
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests these proteins are composed of a three stranded beta sheet packed against a pair of alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7444
comment: This entry represents a conserved family found in various bacteriophages, particularly those infecting Escherichia, Klebsiella, and other Enterobacteriaceae. The function of this domain is currently unknown. This family is commonly found in phages belonging to the Drexlerviridae family, including genera such as Webervirus, Tempevirinae, and Tunavirinae. This entry shows some structurally similar features to Pfam:PF24227. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7502
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7507
comment: This domain of unknown function is found in multiple copies in a number of bacterial proteins. It is closely related to domains represented by DUF11 (Pfam:PF01345). Similarly to DUF11, this domain contains a conserved N-terminal lysine and a C-terminal asparagine with central aspartate/glutamate residues suggesting that it may contain an isopeptide bond. In addition, it contains a semi-conserved TNTGNV sequence motif in which a highly conserved asparagine probably plays a role in stabilising the rod structure formed by repetitive copies of this domain. (from Pfam)

label: nSTAND_NTPase4
hmm_name: STAND family AAA ATPase minor domain
comment: This entry represents a novel domain of the STAND-superfamily of AAA+ ATPases found in bacterial conflict systems (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7557
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in archaea. They may be part of toxin/antitoxin system. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7576
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. They contain two pairs of conserved cysteine residues and are predicted to adopt a fold typical for Treble-clef zinc fingers. (from Pfam)

label: CBM96
comment: This entry represents a CBM domain, a member of CBM96 family, found in functionally diverse multi-domain proteins including tRNA nuclease WapA, alginate lyase from Defluviitalea phaphyphila and chondroitinase from Dysgonomonas sp. The CBM96 domain from the latter proteins, has been structurally characterised. It fold into a beta-sandwich with significant structural similarity to nucleoplasmin (PDB:8WAB, PDB:7VBO) (PMID: 36592931). (from Pfam)

label: Phage_zn_bind_8
name_orig: Putative DNA-binding phage zinc finger domain
comment: This entry represents a large family of zinc binding domains that are found in both phage and bacterial proteins. The phage examples tend to be single domain proteins. The bacterial examples are often found in multidomain proteins. Structure predictions suggest this domain may bind to dsDNA. In about quarter of the proteins this domain is found associated with a resolvase domains Pfam:PF00239 found in site specific recombinases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7666
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein domain that is sometimes found associated with Pfam:PF01469. The family also includes an N-terminal domain found in the Pseudomonas syringae InaZ ice nucleation protein. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7670
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial membrane proteins that contain four transmembrane alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7689
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins. They are predicted to adopt a fold typical for cysteine proteinases and topology similar to that of NlpC/P60 family proteins. These proteins are likely enzymes as they have similar active site architecture. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7694
comment: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of an antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha helix packed on it. Most members contain a highly conserved HhW sequence motif where h is hydrophobic residue. (from Pfam)

label: Diguanyl_cycl_sensor
comment: This entry represents a sensor domain found at the N-terminal of the putative diguanylate cyclase from Shewanella oneidensis, whose structure was solved (PDBe:3mfx). (from Pfam)

label: AstE_AspA_cat
comment: This entry represents the catalytic domain found in Succinylglutamate desuccinylase (AstE), aspartoacylase (AspA) and related enzymes. AstE catalyses the fifth and last step in arginine catabolism by the arginine succinyltransferase pathway whereas AspA cleaves acylaspartate into a fatty acid and aspartate. Mutations in human AspA lead to Canavan disease disease (PMID: 8252036). The domain represented by this entry contains the residues which are essential for catalysis and has structural similarity to catalytic domains of enzymes that are members of the Zn-dependent exopeptidases clan (PMID: 20921362). (from Pfam)

label: PolC_DP2_central
product_name: DNA polymerase II large subunit DP2, central domain
name_orig: DNA polymerase II large subunit DP2, central domain
hmm_name: DNA polymerase II large subunit DP2, central domain
comment: This entry represents the central domain of DNA polymerase II large subunit from Pyrococcus abyssi (PolC) and similar sequences mainly found in archaea. This domain, which is found C-terminal to Pfam:PF03833, shows an alpha-beta configuration (PMID: 27548043). (from Pfam)

label: PolC_DP2_cat
product_name: DNA polymerase II large subunit DP2, catalytic domain
name_orig: DNA polymerase II large subunit DP2, catalytic domain
hmm_name: DNA polymerase II large subunit DP2, catalytic domain
comment: This entry represents the catalytic domain of DNA polymerase II large subunit from Pyrococcus abyssi (PolC) and similar sequences mainly found in archaea. This domain is found C-terminal to Pfam:PF24844 and shows a six-stranded double-psi beta-barrel (DPBB) (PMID: 27548043). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7035
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from Dictyostelia. It is predicted to adopt Ig-like fold with the fibronectin type III-like topology. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7065
comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in fungi and bacteria, which, according to structure predictions it adopts a lipocalin-like fold. This domain is found as a pair of two flattened, orthogonally packed, beta-barrels. This entry represents the N-terminal barrel of the pair. In some members, the lipocalin-like domains (also referred to as AttH-like) are associated with a protein kinase-like domain at the N-terminal (Pfam:PF01636). (from Pfam)

label: Exo_endo_phos_PGAP2IP
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in the human PGAP2-interacting protein (PGAP2IP) and its homologues in yeast CWH43. PGAP2IP is composed of three domains. Two of these domains are predicted to adopt very similar structure consisting of six transmembrane helices suggesting a possible duplication event in these proteins. Its yeast homologue CWH43 is involved in the remodeling of the lipid moiety of GPI anchors to ceramides (PMID: 17761529). The domain represented by this entry has a significant sequence similarity to DNase I-like domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. (from Pfam)

label: NFD4_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Protein NUCLEAR FUSION DEFECTIVE 4 from Arabidopsis thaliana (NFD4) and similar sequences predominantly found in plants. NFD4 is required for karyogamy during female gametophyte development, when the two polar nuclei fuse to form the diploid central cell nucleus. This protein is predicted to organise into two all -alpha domains, Pfam:PF06813 and this entry. (from Pfam)

label: CARF_Card1
comment: This is the CARF domain found at the N-terminal of a set of bacterial proteins, including Card1 (cyclic-oligoadenylate-activated single-stranded ribonuclease and single-stranded deoxyribonuclease 1) from Treponema succinifaciens (Swiss:F2NWD3), a protein that is part of type III CRISPR-Cas immune response system. This protein consists of a CARF (CRISPR-associated Rossmann fold) domain at the N-terminal, an helical hinge domain and a C-terminal endonuclease domain (Pfam:PF09002) (PMID: 33461211). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7111
comment: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs AxYxET, ERxL/VxF and GYAMLK/RVR. Members are predicted to show a beta-sheet and an alpha-helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7117
comment: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs WSYY, RxYxR and HxK/RR. Members are predicted to show a predominantly alpha configuration. (from Pfam)

label: SDR
comment: This entry represents a set of short-chain dehydrogenases/reductases (SDRs) proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7127
comment: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members adopt a beta configuration with high similarity to the CS domain (Pfam:PF04969). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7130
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from Halobacteria. It contains highly conserved cysteine residues arranged in two CxxC motifs that likely coordinate zinc. The first motif could be more broadly defined as a semi-conserved MWRCxxCGEM sequence motif. This domain is predicted to adopt a zinc ribbon fold with similarity to rubredoxin-like domains. (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_PF0610
comment: This rubredoxin-like zinc beta-ribbon domain is found in PF0610, a protein from the hyperthermophile Pyrococcus furiosus, and related homologous proteins. This domain is embedded in winged HTH fold (PMID: 17223696). (from Pfam)

label: Cap15_TM
comment: This entry includes CD-NTase-associated protein 15 (Cap15), an effector protein of a CBASS antivirus system (PMID: 34784509). These proteins occur in conserved genome contexts with the SMODS nucleotide synthetase (PMID: 34784509). Cap15 consists of two transmembrane segments (TM) at the N-terminal, represented in this entry, and a compact eight-stranded beta-barrel scaffold that forms a cyclic dinucleotide receptor domain (Pfam:PF18153) which oligomerises upon activation (PMID: 34784509). Activated Cap15 binds the cyclic nucleotide second messenger 3',3'-cGAMP, re localizes throughout the cell and specifically induces rupture of the inner membrane. (from Pfam)

label: DUF1512_C
comment: This family consists of several archaeal proteins of around 370 residues in length. This entry corresponds to the C-terminal domain. The function of this family is unknown. This domain shows structural similarity to peptidyl tRNA hydrolase enzymes. (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_HMPTM
comment: This domain is found in 7,8-dihydro-6-hydroxymethylpterin dimethyltransferase (HMPTM) and related proteins. HMPTM is involved in catalysing the methylation at C-7 and C-9 of 7,8-dihydro-6-hydroxymethylpterin, a common intermediate in both folate and MPT biosynthesis (PMID: 25002541). The domain represented by this entry is predicted to adopt a zinc beta-ribbon fold. It contains three invariant cysteines and one histidine arranged in two CxxC and CxxH sequence motifs. (from Pfam)

label: NBD_SMAX1
comment: This domain is found in a number of SMAX1-like proteins and in the chaperone protein ClpB. SMAX1-like proteins are thought to be components of a transcriptional corepressor complex whereas ClpB is a part of a stress-induced multi-chaperone system and it is involved in the recovery of the cell from heat-induced damage [1,2]. In ClpB from T. thermophilus, this domain is involved in ATP binding and contributes to the ATPase activity (PMID: 23341453). It has significant sequence and structural similarity to other known AAA+ nucleotide binding domains. (from Pfam)

label: GH3_C
comment: The GH3 IAA-amido conjugating enzyme family consists of proteins that catalyze the synthesis of amino acid conjugates with indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) or jasmonate (JA), which are plant hormones. This entry represents the C-terminal domain of these enzymes. These enzymes play a crucial role in regulating plant hormone levels by conjugating excess IAA and JA to amino acids, thus providing a mechanism for plants to maintain hormonal homeostasis. The conjugation process is ATP-dependent and involves the adenylation of the hormone followed by the transfer to an amino acid. This family is involved in various plant physiological processes including disease resistance, stamen and carpel differentiation, floret fertility, and response to environmental stresses such as wounding and pathogen attack. Some members also exhibit activity towards synthetic auxins and may confer resistance to herbicides. The family's broad substrate specificity includes various amino acids and analogs of IAA, contributing to the complexity of hormone regulation in plants. (from Pfam)

label: WHD_AprA
comment: This entry represents a domain found in the homologues of AprA Methyltransferase 1. AprA is an S-adenosylmethionine and Fe3+-dependent dimethyltransferase that acts in the initiation steps of apratoxin A biosynthesis [1,2]. This domain has similarity to winged helix domains. (from Pfam)

label: ELP3_N
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in the human Elongator complex protein 3 (ELP3) and related proteins. This protein is required for multiple modifications of tRNA. In the elongation complex, it acts as a tRNA uridine(34) acetyltransferase. It may also act as a lysine acetyltransferase by mediating acetylation of target proteins (PMID: 31309145). The domain represented by this entry is predicted to fold into a globular structure consisting of two nearly orthogonal alpha-helical hairpins. (from Pfam)

label: MftA
comment: This protein family includes Mycofactocin precursor peptide from Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MftA) and similar short sequences from actinobacteria (PMID: 36243697). MftA is a 29-residues long precursor peptide that leads to mycofactocin (MFT) after extensive post-translational modifications by enzymes encoded by adjacent genes. Mycofactocin acts as a redox cofactor of nicotinamide-dependent oxidoreductases encoded in the same locus. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7168
comment: This entry represents a protein domain found in phage proteins that usually contain an N-terminal Pfam:PF10979. The function of these protein is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7186
comment: This entry represents a small transmembrane protein found in Lactococcus 936-type phages. The function of this protein is unknown. It contains a single transmembrane helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7201
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins found to be associated with membranes, based on transmembrane region predictions. They are typically around 110 amino acids in length with a C-terminal membrane helix. Many also contain predicted coiled-coil region spanning the rest of the protein. The specific function is unknown. However, it could play a role in membrane fusion. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7220
comment: This short protein is found among some phage. It is possibly distantly related to the small terminase family Pfam:PF05119. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7253
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function, which is found in phage proteins, predominantly from Arthrobacter and Gordonia phages. The domain is approximately 110 amino acids in length. It shows similarity to the Phage_barrel superfamily. These proteins are often components of the phage neck complex. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7259
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from proteobacteria. It is usually found C-terminal to [Pfam:PF22288]. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with a beta-barrel shape. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7269
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Halobacteria. They are likely composed mainly of alpha-helices. These proteins contain a semi-conserved GxWTDDxxAA sequence motif toward their C terminus. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7288
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7305
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins most of which likely associated with proteins located in pilBC operon. It is frequently found inserted in [Pfam:PF23960]. This domain is predicted to adopt a single-stranded right-handed beta-helix with similarity to ice-binding proteins and other adhesive domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7309
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in uncharacterised proteins from bacteria, as well as in some plasmid pRiA4b ORF-3 family of proteins. (from Pfam)

label: PilB3_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal of PilB3 from Haloferax volcanii and similar archaeal proteins. PilB3 is associated with the assembly of genes. This domain, normally found C-terminal to Pfam:PF00437, is predicted to show an alpha-beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: Ig_DR_A0283-like
comment: This domain with an immunoglobulin (Ig)-like fold is found in the probable subtilase-type serine protease DR_A0283 from Deinococcus radiodurans. It shows high structural similarity with the first beta-sandwich domain (SD1) from Fervidolysin from Fervidobacterium pennivorans (PMID: 14687574). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7338
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins from phage. Structure prediction shows the proteins to be composed of an alpha helical N-terminal domain and a C-terminal domain composed of a 5 stranded beta meander. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7346
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised archaeal sequences containing a presumed HTH domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7351
comment: This is a presumed domain found at the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised archaeal sequences, which contain an HTH domain at the N-terminal. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7388
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised archaeal sequences. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_tail_C
hmm_name: phage upper tail fiber protein C-terminal domain
comment: This small region is found at the C-terminus of a variety of actinophage fiber proteins. According to structure predictions these proteins form homotrimers. Presumably this domain mediates interaction with either the host cell or with another phage tail fiber protein. The structure of this region forms three beta strands and up to two small alpha helices, with one of the beta strands in the trimeric structure strand swapping between the monomers. In some phage we find this domain in isolation in rather short 60 residue proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7450
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria that, according to structure predictions (SwissProt:A0A7C3HQW7 or SwissProt:A0A5C6D6K5), they may contain novel repeats that fold into twisted long beta-hairpins different from typical beta-barrel hairpins and they do not exhibit homology to any beta-barrel.
