(from Pfam)

label: HTH_HVO_0163_N
comment: This HTH domain is found at the N-terminal of the ArsR family transcription regulator HVO_0163 from Haloferax volcanii and similar archaeal sequences (from Pfam)

label: TRASH_HVO_1752_C
comment: This TRASH domain is found at the C-terminal end of the predicted Lrp/AsnC family transcription regulator from Haloferax volcanii and similar archaeal proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7473
comment: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7479
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains four invariant cysteines and it is predicted to adopt a Zn-ribbon fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7487
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised sequences from viruses. They may have a novel repeat fold consisting of two domains at the N- and C-terminal with beta-hairpin-beta-alpha configuration that are connected by nine alpha-helices linked by loops. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7490
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised archaeal proteins. Members of this family have a PGF-CTERM motif Pfam:PF18204 at the C-termini. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7513
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Halobacteria. It has a detectable sequence similarity to TRAM domains and it is predicted to adopt a similar structure. It is found as standalone domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7518
comment: This family includes a group of short proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure at the N terminus and show a disordered C-terminal region. In some lineages of archaea, the gene encoding these proteins is found upstream of SMC (chromosome segregation protein). (from Pfam)

label: ORC-CDC6-like
comment: This entry represents a group of sequences that belong to the ORC-CDC6-family of AAA+ ATPases associated with prokaryotic antiviral immunity and is commonly found with double CARF, methylase and protein containing variable effector domains (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7541
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Halobacteria. They are predicted to adopt a structure consisting of four alpha-helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7544
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. They are likely associated with the membrane and consists of several transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7546
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Halobacteria. These proteins are likely associated with the membrane. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7550
comment: This entry represents a group of small uncharacterised archaeal proteins. They are predicted to fold into a single alpha-helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7560
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in archaea. They contain two pairs of conserved cysteines that are likely involved in metal coordination. It is predicted they may structurally resemble Zinc-beta ribbon domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7561
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in archaea. They contain two pairs of conserved cysteines that are likely involved in metal coordination. These proteins are predicted to structurally resemble treble-clef zinc fingers. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7575
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised eu- and prokaryotic proteins. It contains four invariant cysteines and it is predicted to adopt a Zn-ribbon fold. (from Pfam)

label: PDDEXK_14
comment: This entry represents a small family of phage proteins that are structurally related to the PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily. The highest structural similarity is to Holliday junction resolvase Hjc proteins and tRNA-splicing endonucleases from archaebacteria. The exact function of this protein family is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: PDDEXK_15
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins that are structurally related to the PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily. The highest structural similarity is to Holliday junction resolvase Hjc proteins. The exact function of this protein family is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7657
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains a semi-conserved sequence motif TxYPGxR. It is likely that this domain is a transmembrane domain composed of alpha-helices. (from Pfam)

label: Kelch_KLHDC2_KLHL20_DRC7
comment: This entry represents a Kelch-repeats-like domain found in a diverse group of proteins, including KLHDC2, Kelch-like protein 20 and FBX42 from human, which are the substrate-recognition component of E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes. KLHDC2 is the substrate-recognition component of Cul2-RING (CRL2) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex of the DesCEND (destruction via C-end degrons) pathway, which recognises a C-degron located at the extreme C-terminus of target proteins, leading to their ubiquitination and degradation [1-3]. KLHL20 and its orthologue from Drosophila diablo, are the substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex, involved in interferon response and anterograde Golgi to endosome transport (PMID: 31279627). This domain can be found in DRC7 from C. reinhardtii and related sequences (PMID: 37258679). (from Pfam)

label: Vgb_lyase
comment: Virginiamycin B lyase enzymes inactivate type B streptogramin antibiotics by linearizing the lactone ring at the ester linkage. This reaction generates a free phenylglycine carboxylate and converts the threonyl moiety into 2-amino-butenoic acid. These enzymes play a crucial role in antibiotic resistance by neutralizing the antibacterial activity of streptogramins. (from Pfam)

label: LNS2_PITM1-3
comment: This entry represents the LNS2 domain found at the C-terminal of Membrane-associated phosphatidylinositol transfer protein 1-3 (PITM1-3, class II PITPs) and RDGB from Drosophila (PMID: 34098114). This domain, in contrast to lipins where it was first described, in class II PITPs can bind phosphatidic acid (PA) but not hydrolyse it (PMID: 34098114). RDGB is required to regulate phosphoinositide turnover during G-protein activated phospholipase C signalling (PMID: 34098114). PITM 1-3 catalyse the transfer of phosphatidylinositol (PI) between membranes [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: AtPDCT1_2
comment: This entry represents a domain found in the Phosphatidylcholine diacylglycerol cholinephosphotransferase 1 (PDCT1 or ROD1) and 2 (PDCT2) from Arabidopsis thaliana. PDCT1 catalyses the transfer of the phosphocholine headgroup from phosphatidylcholine (PC) to diacylglycerol, a major reaction for the transfer of 18:1 into phosphatidylcholine for desaturation and also for the reverse transfer of 18:2 and 18:3 into the triacylglycerols synthesis pathway [1,2,3]. This domain has a detectable similarity to domains members of the Acid phosphatase/Vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase superfamily and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. This domain is composed of five transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: GINT1_N
comment: This is the N-terminal domain of Glucosamine inositolphosphorylceramide transferase 1 from Arabidopsis thaliana (GINT1), a member of the Glycosyltransferase Family 64 that is involved in glycosylinositolphosphorylceramide and sphingolipid glycosylation. This domain is predicted to adopt a five-bladed beta-propeller fold. (from Pfam)

label: 8xMP
comment: This protein is an integral membrane protein composed of three integral membrane alpha helices. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins form an octameric complex (A0A0D0Q6W1 ipTM = 0.81 pTM = 0.82). This complex contains a central pore. The predicted complex has a flat face on the predicted extracellular face that suggests it may form a complex with another as yet unidentified partner. The alpha helices project into the cytoplasm. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7064
comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in fungi and bacteria, which, according to structure predictions it adopts a lipocalin-like fold. This domain is found as a pair of two flattened, orthogonally packed, beta-barrels. This entry represents the C-terminal barrel of the pair. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_TbsP_C
product_name: Transcriptional regulator TbsP-like, C-terminal HTH domain
name_orig: Transcriptional regulator TbsP-like, C-terminal HTH domain
hmm_name: Transcriptional regulator TbsP-like, C-terminal HTH domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal of the putative transcriptional regulator TbsP from Haloferax volcanii (Halobacterium volcanii) (Swiss:D4GXF9, also known as HVO_2861) and similar sequences predominantly found in Halobacteria. TbsP is required for adhesion to abiotic surfaces (i.e., biofilm formation) and maintains wild-type cell morphology and motility. This is predicted to MarR-type helix-turn-helix (HTH) structure (PMID: 38204420). (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_HVO_0234
comment: This family represents a group of proteins mainly from halobacteria, including HVO_0234 from Haloferax volcanii (Swiss:D4GZH9). Members are predicted to adopt a beta -propeller configuration. (from Pfam)

label: FAZ1_C
comment: The entry represents a repeats-containing region found at the C-terminal of FAZ1 from Trypanosoma brucei brucei and related proteins from typanosomatids. FAZ1 is a component of FAZ filament that is required for correct FAZ assembly and attachment (PMID: 17945531). These repeats consist of 36x14aa repeats in T.brucei and T.cruzi while in the Leishmania major LmjF34.0690 orthologue there are 70x14aa repeats (PMID: 17945531). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7108
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of the uncharacterised protein HVO_0731 from Haloferax volcanii (Swiss:D4GTA0) and similar proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs RLTR/KLxR and LVxHPxEW. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta structure. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7119
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from archaea. It is predicted to adopt an all-helical configuration. (from Pfam)

label: S1_RRP5
comment: This entry represents several divergent S1 domains found in RRP5 proteins. The RRP5 protein family is essential for ribosomal RNA (rRNA) biogenesis, playing a critical role in the formation of mature 18S and 5.8S rRNA components of the ribosome. Members of the RRP5 family are necessary for specific cleavage events at sites A0, 1, and 2 within the 47S precursor rRNA. They are also known to directly interact with U3 small nucleolar RNA (snoRNA), which is involved in the early steps of rRNA processing. The RRP5 family's function is conserved across eukaryotes, as evidenced by its involvement in rRNA processing in organisms ranging from yeast to humans. In plants, the RRP5 protein is additionally required for normal development of female gametophytes, indicating a broader role in cellular growth and development. (from Pfam)

label: zf-Tbcl_FmdE
comment: This treble clef zinc finger is found C-terminal in some members of FmdE family that are implicated in microbial methanogenesis (PMID: 20944230). This domain follows the alpha/beta core domain (Pfam:PF02663) and contains four invariant cysteine residues that coordinate the zinc atom. (from Pfam)

label: zf_Tbcl_2
comment: This presumed domain is found in a number of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria and archaea. This domain is predicted to adopt a treble clef fold. In some members this domain follows (Pfam:PF13451) which is also predicted to adopt treble clef fold. (from Pfam)

label: CysS_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal anticodon binding domain from Cysteinyl-tRNA ligase. The entry also includes the C-terminal domain of YqeB from B. subtilis. These proteins contain 2 transmembrane helices and a bacterial PH domain. (from Pfam)

label: CdpA_N
name_orig: Cell division protein A, N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Cell division protein A, N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of CdpA (Cell division protein A, HVO_0739) from Haloferax volcanii and similar archaeal proteins. CdpA is a ring assembly and anchor protein. It forms part of an anchor complex linked to FtsZ2 and other cell division proteins (PMID: 40450033). This domain, which is predicted to show four transmembrane helices, possibly together with the linker region of CdpA, are important for CdpA midcell localisation, FtsZ1 ring condensation, and FtsZ2 ring assembly and positioning (PMID: 40450033). In CdpA and other members of this group, this domain is found associated with Pfam:PF23601. In some other members these domains are associated with repeats of Pfam:PF07411. AlphaFold predicts a confident dimeric structure for this domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7144
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into a four-helical up-and-down bundle and it is likely transmembrane. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_IP5PC_F
comment: This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found mainly in plant inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatases (IP5P), such as Type I IP5P12/IP5PC and IP5P13/IP5PD and Type II IP5P14/IP5PE and IP5P15/IP5PF from Arabidopsis thaliana. IP5Ps have different functions, including the degradation of phosphoinositides in the signalling pathways of various cellular processes such as Ca2+ release, abscisic acid signalling and vesicle trafficking, among others (PMID: 31426386). In the case of IP5P13, the beta propeller domain interacts with the sucrose non-fermenting-1-related kinase (SnRK1.1) in order to achieve a regulatory role linking inositol, sugar and stress signalling (PMID: 18931139). (from Pfam)

label: S-AdoMet_lyase
comment: The S-Adenosylmethionine lyase family is involved in the regulation of viral genome methylation. It degrades the host cell's intracellular S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) pools and inhibits the host's S-adenosylmethionine synthase, leading to the prevention of viral genome methylation. This activity facilitates the transition of the virus from a lytic to a lysogenic infection under certain stress conditions, such as glucose starvation, by blocking viral expression. Additionally, the family induces the polymerization of the host's S-adenosylmethionine synthase into inactive filaments, which contributes to the unmethylated state of the viral genome, although it does not confer immunity against host restriction-modification systems. This family shows structural similarity to Pfam:PF12098. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7260
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Halobacteria. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed mainly of alpha-helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7261
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Halobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7283
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Halobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7307
comment: This entry represents a set of uncharacterised phage proteins that are related to the Pam3 phage gp33 protein. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7313
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised archaeal proteins. It is predicted to fold into a four-helical bundle and it is likely associated with the membrane. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7317
comment: This family includes a group of short archaeal proteins, that are distantly related to Pfam:PF03683. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7347
comment: This is a presumed HTH domain found at the N-terminal of a group of uncharacterised archaeal sequences. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7352
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage domains. These domains adopt a beta sandwich structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7379
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found towards the N-terminal of CHAT domain-containing protein, such as SwissProt:A0A100JVW6, from Streptomyces scabiei. This domain may adopt a A/B hydrolase fold and is often found in association with TCAD7 (Pfam:PF19973) and CHAT (Pfam:PF12770) domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7380
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed mainly of alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: FLAD1_M
comment: This domain is found in human FAD synthase (FLAD1) and similar sequences mainly found in eukaryotes. FLAD1 catalyses the adenylation of flavin mononucleotide (FMN) to form flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) coenzyme. This domain, which is predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration, is often found C-terminal to Pfam:PF00994 and N-terminal to Pfam:PF01507. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7383
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised archaeal sequences containing a galactose binding-like domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7387
product_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system HicB family antitoxin
hmm_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system HicB family antitoxin
comment: This entry includes uncharacterised archaeal sequences. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7405
comment: This entry represents a family or archaeal proteins whose function is unknown. They may adopt a dimeric alpha/beta barrel fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7407
comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from archaea. This domain may have a beta-sandwich fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7408
comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from archaea. It may adopt an amidotransferase-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7411
comment: This is a family of unknown function mainly found in archaea but also in some bacterial species. They may have a Rossmann-like alpha/beta/alpha fold. (from Pfam)

label: SU10_adaptor
comment: This entry represents adaptor proteins found in SU10-like bacteriophages and prophages. The dodecamer of SU10 adaptor proteins forms the interface between the dodecamer of portal proteins and hexamer of nozzle proteins (PMID: 36153309). The adaptor complex provides six attachment sites for long tail fibers, each of which is formed by a trimer of long tail fiber proximal proteins and a trimer of long tail fiber distal proteins. The adaptor protein of SU10 has the same domain organization as those of phages T7 and KP32. Its structure consists of an alpha-helical bundle domain composed of intertwined N- and C-terminal helices; and a beta-sandwich long tail fiber dock domain (PMID: 36153309). (from Pfam)

label: Beta-tre_PLH30
comment: This entry represents the beta-trefoil domain found in endo-acting ulvan lyase from bacteria. Ulvan lyases degrade the main polysaccharide component of green seaweed cell walls [1,2]. This domain binds to ulvan (PMID: 28327560). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7467
comment: This entry represents a beta sandwich domain found in a variety of bacterial cell surface proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7475
comment: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7482
comment: This entry includes a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria and archaea, which, according to structure predictions, they may have a novel repeat fold. They may consist of 5-6 antiparallel beta-strands decorated with short alpha-helices. (from Pfam)

label: FraC
comment: This entry represents the Filament integrity protein FraC and related proteins found in cyanobacteria. FraC, along with FraD and SepJ (FraG), is found at intercellular septa in heterocyst -forming filamentous cyanobacteria such as Nostoc punctiforme. This protein is involved in filament integrity and is required for the integrity of cell junctions in general (PMID: 38164507). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7504
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. They contain the typical P-loop motif and are probably structurally related to the P-loop NTPases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7523
comment: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to be organised into two domains, an N-terminal with an all-alpha configuration and a C-terminal with an alpha-beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7534
comment: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7536
comment: This family includes a group of short proteins from archaea. (from Pfam)

label: PRTase-CE
comment: PRTase-like domain predicted to act as an effector in multiple antiviral immunity systems by targeting nucleotides (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: HD-CE
comment: This entry represents an HD-like domain predicted to act as effector in multiples antiviral immunity system by targeting nucleotides (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: Pepco
comment: This entry represents a small domain co-occurring with peptidases like Trypsin, Caspase, and MPTase. The domain is homologous to Trypco1 and Trypco2 from MoxR-vWA-based ternary systems typically seen in multicellular bacteria. Peptidase cleavage of Pepco superfamily domains may trigger assembly into multimeric complexes, leading to cell suicide akin to processes seen in metazoan apoptosis [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: wHTH-PRTase_assc
comment: This entry represents a wHTH domain found at the C-terminal of proteins containing PRTase-CE (Pfam:PF24390) domain in the retron antiviral immunity system (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7549
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. They are predicted to adopt alpha/beta structure consisting of five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and five alpha-helices protruding from it. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7553
comment: This is a small family of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. They are predicted to fold into a helical hairpin. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7554
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in archaea. These proteins are likely associated with the membrane. They are predicted to fold into a single helix. (from Pfam)

label: RE_BanI
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain in P subtype restriction enzyme BanI that recognises the double-stranded sequence 5'-GGYRCC-3' and cleaves after G-1. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7573
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Halobacteria. They contain two pairs of conserved cysteines that are likely involved in metal coordination. (from Pfam)

label: SpaA_4
comment: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Some members are likely to contain an isopeptide bond. (from Pfam)

label: Rv0428c_C
comment: This GNAT domain-containing family includes the N-acetylglutamate synthase cg3035 (CAF20762.1) from Corynebacterium glutamicum, as well as Rv0428c, proposed to be a histone N-acetyltransferase.

label: YunG
comment: This entry represents the uncharacterised B. subtilis YunG protein and its homologues. These proteins contain a potential catalytic triad composed of Cys, His and Asp residues. (from Pfam)

label: FLQE3_permease
product_name: fluoroquinolone export ABC transporter permease subunit
hmm_name: fluoroquinolone export ABC transporter permease subunit
comment: The Fluoroquinolones export permease protein family is involved in the export of fluoroquinolones as part of an ABC transporter complex. This family is likely responsible for the translocation of substrates across the membrane and confers resistance to various fluoroquinolones, including ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin, moxifloxacin, and sparfloxacin. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7669
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins primarily found in Bacteria. It has a detectable similarity to winged helix HTH domain and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. This domain is frequently found in combination with Pfam:PF21818 and Pfam:PF20815. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7674
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 113 and 127 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7680
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. These proteins share a common semi-conserved EExxWY sequence motif which is predicted as a solvent-exposed in a alpha/beta structure consisting of a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. (from Pfam)

label: rva_4
comment: This domain is homologous to the integrase central catalytic domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7714
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. They are likely to contain two domains that create a compact elongated structure. Toward the C terminus, these proteins have two highly conserved pairs of cysteines which are likely to be involved in metal coordination. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7716
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either standalone or in combination with other domains. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of an antiparallel three-stranded beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. (from Pfam)

label: AraA_central
comment: This entry represents a domain found central in L-arabinose isomerases, AraA, EC:5.3.1.4. These enzymes catalyse the reaction: L-arabinose <=> L-ribulose. This reaction is the first step in the pathway of L-arabinose utilisation as a carbon source after entering the cell L-arabinose is converted into L-ribulose by the L-arabinose isomerases enzyme (PMID: 9084180). The domain represented by this entry is composed of a central parallel beta-sheet packed with alpha-helices on both sides and with topology similar to the topology of the N-terminal domain (PMID: 16756997). (from Pfam)

label: Anti-Pycsar_Apyc1
comment: This entry represents Anti-Pycsar protein Apyc1 and similar sequences which counteracts the endogenous Pycsar antiviral defense system (PMID: 35395152). These are phosphodiesterases that enables metal-dependent hydrolysis of host cyclic nucleotide Pycsar defense signals such as cCMP and cUMP (PMID: 35395152). These proteins have a metallo beta-lactamase (MBL)-like fold with homology to RNase and phosphodiesterase enzymes (PMID: 35395152). (from Pfam)

label: Gp80
name_orig: Podophage GP4 fiber I protein gp80
hmm_name: phage tail fiber protein, podophage GP4 gp80 family
comment: This entry represents the Podophage GP4 fiber I protein gp80 and related phage proteins. Bacteriophage tail fibers play a critical role in the early stage of infection by binding to the bacterial surface. In Podophage GP4, five fiber I, each composed of five dimers of gp80 and linked by rope protein, are attached to the five edges of the tail vertex of the icosahedral head of the phage (PMID: 37660940). The structure of gp80 has an unusual barrel-like topology with one strand contributed by the rope protein. The N terminus of gp80 folds into an alpha-helix which is involved in the dimerisation (PMID: 37660940). (from Pfam)

label: PDE8A_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal of human High affinity cAMP-specific and IBMX-insensitive 3',5'-cyclic phosphodiesterase 8A (PDE8A), which hydrolyses the the second messenger cAMP, a key regulator of many important physiological processes (PMID: 18983167). This domain is predicted to adopt a Rossmann fold similar to CheY-type chemotaxis response regulators. It is also known as REC domain [2, 3]. (from Pfam)

label: Ig-like_KY
comment: This domain is found twice in human Kyphoscoliosis peptidase (KY), a probable cytoskeleton-associated protease required for normal muscle growth. This domain, which is predicted to adopt an immunoglobulin-like structure. Members of this family are mainly found in animals. (from Pfam)

label: REP_ORF2-G2P
comment: This entry represents a domain find in a group of Replication-associated proteins including ORF2 from Spiroplasma virus 4 (SpV4) and G2P from phages, such as Xanthomonas phage phiLf and Bdellovibrio phage phiMH2K. These proteins play an essential role in viral DNA replication; they bind the origin of replication and cleaves the dsDNA replicative form I (RFI) and becomes covalently bound to it via phosphotyrosine bond, generating the dsDNA replicative form II (RFII). After one round of rolling circle synthesis, protein G2P is linked to the newly synthesized ssDNA and joins the ends of the displaced strand to generate a circular single-stranded molecule ready to be packed into a virion. (from Pfam)

label: IFT52_GIFT
comment: This domain is found in various eukaryotic and prokaryotic intra-flagellar transport proteins involved in gliding motility, as well as in several hypothetical proteins. Intraflagellar transport protein 52 homolog from human is included in this entry, which is essential for anterograde complex integrity and for the biosynthesis and maintenance of cilia (PMID: 27466190). This domain has been described as the GIFT domain in IFT52 whose function is not yet clear [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7096
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of proteins from eubacteria. It is predicted to show a mainly alpha-configuration. This entry is found associated with Pfam:PF23375 and Pfam:PF23374 (from Pfam)

label: DUF7124
comment: This domain is found in a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several W and R conserved residues. This domain is predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: WHD_SNRNP200
comment: This entry represents a winged Helix-Turn-Helix domain found in a variety of helicase enzymes. (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_PaaD
comment: This domain is found in a number of bacterial and archaeal proteins including PaaD from Escherichia coli that is thought to be a component of 1,2-phenylacetyl-CoA epoxidase multicomponent enzyme system which catalyzes the reduction of phenylacetyl-CoA to form 1,2-epoxyphenylacetyl-CoA (PMID: 16997993). This domain is predicted to adopt a zinc beta ribbon fold and contains two invariant CxxC sequence motifs. In addition, toward the C terminus it has a semi-conserved [EQ]PF[DEQ] sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7132
comment: This entry represents a small family from archaebacteria based on protein PF1546. AlphaFold models show that a dimer of this protein forms a flattened 10 stranded beta barrel structure. (from Pfam)

label: AtuA_ferredoxin
comment: This ferredoxin-like fold is often found at the C-terminus of AtuA proteins. Although it is sometimes found as a separate protein in the same operon as AtuA. The precise function of this domain is now known. (from Pfam)

label: Ig_VWA7
comment: This domain id found in the human von Willebrand factor A domain-containing protein 7 (VWA7) and related proteins. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich with an Ig-like topology. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_DCAF4
product_name: DDB1- and CUL4-associated factor 4 beta-propeller domain
name_orig: DDB1- and CUL4-associated factor 4 beta-propeller domain
hmm_name: DDB1- and CUL4-associated factor 4 beta-propeller domain
comment: This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found in DDB1- and CUL4-associated factor 4 (DCAF4) and DCAF4-like proteins 1 and 2 (DCAF4L1 and DCAF4L2) from mammals. These proteins are substrate receptors for the Cullin-DDB1 ubiquitin ligase complexes (PMID: 16964240). DCAF4 has been identified as a key protein in proper proteostasis of Cu, Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD1) (PMID: 32014991) and has been associated to Leukocyte telomere length (LTL) in humans, which in turn has been link to human diseases, including sporadic melanoma (PMID: 25624462). The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TAC_17
comment: This family represents a phage tail assembly chaperone protein based on structural similarities. This entry represents proteins found in bacteriophages from the Gordonvirus genus. (from Pfam)

label: NCTSP_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain found in the non-contractile tail sheath protein from Bacteriophage N4 (BPN4). This protein is essential for BPN4 infectivity and it is hypothesized that it mediates binding with target cell receptors (PMID: 18374942). The function of this domain is unknown. This entry also includes sequences from bacteria, predominantly from Sphingobium spp. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7217
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in phage and bacterial proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DpdA
product_name: deazapurine DNA modification protein DpdA family protein
comment: This entry represents the DpdA family of proteins, which are involved in the insertion of deazapurine modifications in bacterial and phage DNA. DpdA proteins are paralogues of tRNA-guanine transglycosylases (TGT), but have evolved to act on DNA rather than RNA. They catalyze the incorporation of 7-deazaguanine derivatives such as dADG (7-amido-7- deazaguanine) and dpreQ0 (7-cyano-7-deazaguanine) into DNA, which is thought to function as a protection mechanism against endonucleases. The dpdA gene is typically part of a genomic island, along with dpdB, dpdC and dpdD genes, and is proposed to be part of a restriction/ modification system that protects bacteria from foreign DNA. (from Pfam)

label: SU10_portal
comment: This entry represents the portal protein of Escherichia coli phage SU10. The portal protein, encoded by gp6, forms a dodecameric complex that replaces a pentamer of capsid proteins at one vertex of the prolate SU10 capsid. The portal complex enables packaging of the viral genome into the capsid as well as attachment of the phage tail. The portal protein contains wing, stem, clip, crown and barrel domains. The wing domain interacts with the viral DNA and the capsid proteins. The clip domain enables attachment of the adaptor protein complex. (from Pfam)

label: AAA_lid_PRS2_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal AAA+ lid domain of bacterial Putative 26S proteasome regulatory subunit homologues (PRS2). This alpha-helical bundle is found in association with a core AAA-ATPase domain (Pfam:PF00004). The 26S proteasome is a large multiprotein complex involved in the regulated degradation of ubiquitinated proteins. This complex can be divided in two sub-complexes, the core particle (CP, 20S) and the regulatory particle (RP, 19S). The RP consists of 19 subunits organised in two sub-structures, the base and lid complexes. The base consists of a ring of six AAA-ATPases. The C-termini of these ATPases dock into pockets present between the alpha-subunits of the CP, mediating the protein complex interactions (PMID: 20427185). (from Pfam)

label: TIM-barrel_EndoS
comment: This entry represents the TIM barrel domain found in Endo-beta-N-acetylglucosaminidase EndoS from Streptococcus spp. EndoS is a secreted protein that catalyses the hydrolysis of the N-linked oligosaccharides on opsonizing immunoglobulin G (PMID: 11406581), thus contributing to immune response evasion and increased survival of the bacteria in patients (PMID: 12438337). This domain binds to complex-type N-glycans and has enzymatic activity [3,4]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7263
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Halobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7282
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial and archaeal proteins. It is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich with an Ig-like topology, similar to domains members of clan CL0073. Some proteins contain multiple copies of this domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7311
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised archaeal proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7322
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised archaeal proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha-helical hairpin and it is likely associated with the membrane. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7336
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised domains found in a variety of phage and bacterial genomes. Structure prediction suggests the domain is composed of a small beta sheet of three strands and an alpha helix. There is some evidence from prediction that these domains might form a dimeric arrangement. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7348
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in a group of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. In some proteins, this domain precedes [Pfam:PF18069] and [Pfam:PF18009]. It is predicted to fold into a globular alpha/beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_ssDNA_bind
comment: This entry represents a small family of phage proteins that show structural similarity to other phage ssDNA-binding proteins. Structure prediction shows a plausible ssDNA binding pocket on the surface of the domain. This domain has an OB fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7382
comment: This is a Ig-like domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences, mainly from archaea. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7436
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of archaeal sequences that contain Pfam:PF01978 at the N-terminal. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: CrAss_Ring_1
comment: This entry represents the Ring 1 (R1) protein, also known as gp43, which is part of the tail assembly in crassviruses. The R1 protein forms one of five stacked dodecameric rings that make up the tail barrel. These proteins share a conserved fold consisting of two domains: an alpha-helical domain and a beta-sandwich domain. The extended tail barrel formed by these ring proteins is a distinctive feature of crassviruses and may assist the tail muzzle in reaching the outer cell membrane through the compact capsular polysaccharide layer of the host bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_Cmi2_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of the predicted ArsR family transcription regulator Cmi2. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7508
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. Is has significant sequence similarity to GIY-YIG endonuclease domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7520
comment: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7522
comment: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7531
comment: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7537
comment: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt a mainly beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: wHTH-HSP90_Na-assoc
comment: This is a wHTH domain commonly observed in tandem repeats with 5 or more modules and located at the C-terminal of HSP90 proteins engaged in antiviral immunity. These proteins often additionally feature an inactive HD-CE domain (Pfam:PF24401) at the N-terminal. Structural modelling suggests that the wHTH repeats form a ring-shaped module for recognising nucleic acids (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7547
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. These proteins probably do not adopt a globular structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7555
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in Halobacteria. These proteins are likely associated with the membrane. They are predicted to fold into a three helical bundle. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7567
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in Halobacteria. They contain two pairs of conserved cysteines that are likely involved in metal coordination. These proteins are predicted to structurally resemble Zinc beta-ribbon domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7577
comment: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins from prokaryotes. It contains two pairs of conserved cysteines that are likely involved in metal coordination. This domain is predicted to structurally resemble Zinc beta-ribbon domains. (from Pfam)

label: CT398_CC
product_name: CT398-like coiled coil hairpin domain-containing protein
comment: This entry, previously known as DUF7581, represents a coiled coil hairpin domain found N-terminal in CT398 from C. trachomatis, MSMEG_4306 M. smegmatis and related bacterial sequences predominantly from actinobacteria. Both CT398 and MSMEG_4306 proteins have been structurally characterised [1,2]. CT398 protein is involved in several aspects of chlamydial biology and pathogenesis, and is capable of interacting with multiple binding partners. The coiled coil hairpin domain of CT398 engages in interaction with RpoN as well as both T3SS ATPase-regulators FliH and CdsL (PMID: 26173998). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7619
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins frequently in multiple copies. Some proteins containing this domain contain LPXTG cell wall anchor motif Pfam:PF00746 at the C-terminus. It is likely that some members of this entry contain an intramolecular isopeptide bond. (from Pfam)

label: CEMIP_beta-hel
comment: This entry represents the beta-helix domain of CEMIP, CEMIP2 and related sequences (PMID: 37234743). Proteins in this entry proteins are involved in the metabolism of hyaluronic acid (HA) and mediate the depolymerization of high-molecular-weight HA into intermediate-sized fragments (PMID: 37527776), a process crucial for various physiological functions, including the regulation of angiogenesis, heart development, and cell migration [3,4]. This domain has the common structural motif of enzymes involved in polysaccharide degradation, encompassing both hydrolases and lyases, however, biochemical experiments failed to detect any hyaluronidase activity in CEMIP2 and the putative active site remains to be elucidated (PMID: 37234743). This entry also includes Fibrocystin (PKHD), a protein that promotes ciliogenesis within renal epithelial cells, contributing to the formation of kidney tubules and maintaining the lumen architecture [5,6]. It may participate in the regulation of the cholangiocytes proliferation and the CCN2 production in an CXCL8-dependent manner (PMID: 30898581). (from Pfam)

label: DHQS_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of 3-dehydroquinate synthase (DHQS) and related proteins. DHQS catalyses the formation of dehydroquinate (DHQ) and orthophosphate from 3-deoxy-D-arabino heptulosonic 7 phosphate. This reaction is part of the shikimate pathway which is involved in the biosynthesis of aromatic amino acids. DHQS consists of an N-terminal Rossmann fold domain and a C-terminal alpha-helical domain. The active site is located in a cleft between the two somains. This domain contains most of the residues involved in catalysis and in substrate and Zn2+ binding (PMID: 9685163). This domain is also found in AROM proteins which are pentafunctional enzymes that catalyse 5 consecutive enzymatic reactions in prechorismate polyaromatic amino acid biosynthesis. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7654
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: UGSC
comment: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins of unknown function. Some proteins in this family are selenoprotein which are characterised by a UGSC motif where U is a selenocysteine residue. However, this residue is recoded from a stop codon and most matches are split into two distinct gene predictions. The family also includes non-selenoproteins which have a CGSC motif and these appear as full length matches in the alignments. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7662
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is frequently found in combination with Pfam:PF21818 and Pfam:PF20815 which suggests that it may be involved in DNA binding and recognition. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7664
comment: This entry represents a small accessory domain found at the N-terminus of a small family of archaeal AGOG proteins. These proteins have 8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase activity. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7692
comment: This domain is found in a group of proteins from Halobacteria. It is predicted to adopt a structure that is reminiscent of ribbon-helix-helix fold. Members of this entry are likely to form dimers. They have a stretch of positively charged residues at the N terminus. (from Pfam)

label: SpoVR_C
comment: This entry represents a presumed domain found at the C-terminal of the stage V sporulation protein R, YcgB from E.coli and related sequences. Stage V sporulation protein R is involved in spore cortex formation (PMID: 8144469). Little is known about cortex biosynthesis, except that it depends on several sigma E controlled genes, including spoVR (PMID: 8982457). YcgB has been suggested to be part of a conserved signalling pathway with YeaH and YeaG. This pathway may be involved in nitrogen metabolism (see Supplementary note 5 in (PMID: 29769716)). This domain may adopt a fold consisting of four beta-strands and an alpha-helix. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_connect_2
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins that are structurally related to the HK97 gp6 protein that forms a head to tail connection. It is likely that these proteins form large homo-oligomeric rings. (from Pfam)

label: AMIN-like
comment: This entry represents a family of extracellular likely lipoproteins that adopt a structure similar to the AMIN domain. However, there are some topological differences between the two families. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7718
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. It is predicted to adopt alpha/beta structure consisting of a meander beta-sheet and a kinked alpha-helix. It contains several conserved aspartate and histidine residues that are predicted to come close in space and may constitute a metal binding site. (from Pfam)

label: DesA_ISL3_tail
product_name: DesA/ISL3 alpha bundle tail domain-containing protein
comment: This predicted helical bundle domain occurs in the C-terminal regions of ISL3 family transposases such as WP_076611107.1 and DesA-like fatty acid desaturases such as WP_017640882.1. See AlphaFold DB structures for A0A241PBY4 (an ISL3 family transposase) and A4BUZ4 (DesA-like fatty acid desaturase).

label: transpos_IS701_2
comment: Members of this family are transposases in the family of that of insertion element IS701, narrowly defined. Note that a molecular phylogenetic tree of the broader sets of transposases from IS elements classified as IS701 family or IS4 family by ISFINDER shows the two groups interleaved. Another, larger clade of IS701 family transposases is describe in model NF033540.

label: IS4_FS_Nterm
comment: Members of this family appear in protein sequence databases in two forms. Long proteins with this domain at the N-terminus are IS4 family transposases, whose proper translation by cellular machinery often requires a programmed frameshift to occur. Short forms, averaging about 60 amino acids in length, represent the DNA-binding protein that is produced when the termination occurs rather than continuation past the frameshift site is a different reading frame. In many transposase families, the short form made in this way acts as a repressor of transposase expression.

label: adjac_Cas3_IG
product_name: type I-G CRISPR-associated protein, Cas3-extension family
comment: This protein occurs in Cas (CRISPR-associated) protein regions of type I-G CRISPR/Cas systems, occasionally as an extra C-terminal domain of a long Cas3 protein.

label: cas4g_cas1g
comment: Members of this family are a fusion protein of Cas4 (N-terminal) and Cas1 (C-terminal) domains, and are found in type I-G CRISPR/Cas systems.

label: MandnitrLy
comment: hydroxynitrile lyase

label: DF_fam_seleno
comment: This novel domain has some sequence similarity with DUF2703 (PF10865), and some members have received that name. However, in the domain defined here, no CXXC motifs are found. Instead, there are there are just two columns in the alignment that are primarily Cys, and each of these is, in fact always either cysteine (C) or selenocysteine (U). This family was named DF by Xiao and Zhang (2025), where the more N-terminal selenocysteine was reported.

label: IS1_IS1595_Zn
product_name: IS1/IS1595 family N-terminal zinc-binding domain-containing protein

label: restrict_BbrUII
comment: Members of this family include the restriction enzyme BbrUII. Restriction enzyme HgiDII was inferred from the adjacent methyltransferase, but its sequence may be degraded, and HgiDII itself does not score above the cutoffs for this model.

label: Zn_HExGHH_YpfJ
comment: KPN_02809 from Klebsiella pneumoniae (given gene symbol ypfJ, the same as its ortholog in Escherichia coli) was characterized as a Zn-dependent metalloprotease with maximal protease activity at 30 C and pH 8.0. A single zinc ion is bound. The active site-containing motif is HXxGHH in most members of the family.

label: e_dPHAscl_type1
product_name: extracellular catalytic domain type 1 short-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoate depolymerase
hmm_name: extracellular catalytic domain type 1 short-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoate depolymerase

label: pip_6_carb_DH
comment: This HMM describes L-piperidine-6-carboxylate dehydrogenase, an enzyme involved in a pathway for the degradation of lysine to alpha-aminoadipate (or biosynthesis of lysine from that compound).

label: i_nPHAscl
comment: Intracellular poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) depolymerases can break down native PHB into smaller molecules in response to nutritional stress. Proteins of this family share the GXSXG lipase motif.

label: TA_anti_VapB_Sulfo
product_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system VapB family antitoxin
hmm_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system VapB family antitoxin
comment: The term VapB has been used for the antitoxin component of various type II toxin-antitoxin systems called VapBC but showing little or no sequence identity. The family described here includes member proteins from Sulfolobus solfataricus and closely related species.

label: ARM_TT21_2nd
product_name: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 second ARM domain
name_orig: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 second ARM domain
hmm_name: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 second ARM domain
comment: This entry represents the second ARM-repeats domain found towards the N-terminal of Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 (TT21) from human and its homologues. TT21 is an intraflagellar transport (IFT)-associated protein required for spermatogenesis. It is involved in sperm flagellar formation and intraflagellar transport (PMID: 30929735). (from Pfam)

label: ARM_TT21_N
product_name: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 N-terminal ARM repeat
name_orig: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 N-terminal ARM repeat

comment: This entry represents the N-terminal segment of ARM repeats of Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 (TT21) from human and its homologues. TT21 is an intraflagellar transport (IFT)-associated protein required for spermatogenesis. It is involved in sperm flagellar formation and intraflagellar transport (PMID: 30929735). (from Pfam)

label: Citrate_synth_N
comment: The ATP-citrate synthase family is responsible for the synthesis of cytosolic acetyl-CoA, a crucial substrate for de novo lipid synthesis, including cholesterol and fatty acids. In animals, these enzymes typically have a homomeric structure, whereas in plants, they are composed of distinct alpha and beta chains. The family plays a central role in lipid metabolism, contributing to the elongation of fatty acids and the biosynthesis of various compounds such as isoprenoids and flavonoids. This family is characterized by its membership in the succinate/malate CoA ligase subunit families, with distinct N-terminal and C-terminal sections. This entry represents the N-terminal ATP-grasp domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2110_N
comment: This domain, found in various hypothetical archaeal proteins, has no known function. It is found at the N-terminus of the DUF2110 family proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7779
comment: This is a presumed domain found in uncharacterised sequences from fungi. It may be a winged helix domain according to structure predictions. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7802
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial and eukaryotic proteins. It is predicted to contain nine transmembrane helices arranged in a bundle. This domain has similarity to domains members of the INSIG-like superfamily. (from Pfam)

label: HAD_PNKP
hmm_name: T4 polynucleotide kinase/phosphatase PNKP phosphatase domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the bifunctional enzyme T4 polynucleotide kinase/phosphatase, PNKP (also known as PseT). The PNKP phosphatase domain can catalyse the hydrolytic removal of the 3'-phosphoryl of DNA, RNA and deoxynucleoside 3'-monophosphates [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_TEP1_C
comment: This entry represents the beta-propeller found at the C-terminal of Telomerase protein component 1 (TEP1), a component of the telomerase ribonucleoprotein complex that is essential for the replication of chromosome termini (PMID: 19179534). It is also a component of the ribonucleoprotein vaults particle, a multi-subunit structure involved in nucleo-cytoplasmic transport (PMID: 11149928). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7743
comment: This is a presumed domain of unknown function found in uncharacterised proteins from Dictyosteliales. It may adopt a Ig-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7788
comment: This is a vWA-like domain found at the C-terminal of uncharacterised proteins containing the Pfam:PF11443 domain at the N-terminal (PMID: 36419248). (from Pfam)

label: THR4_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Threonine synthase from Saccharomyces cerevisiae (THR4), which catalyses the gamma-elimination of phosphate from L-phosphohomoserine and the beta-addition of water to produce L-threonine. This domain shows an alpha-beta configuration with a combined beta-sheet and an in-between helix (PMID: 23382856). (from Pfam)

label: VWA_4
comment: This domain is found in a number of proteins including VWA7, HMCN1, HMCN2, irg-7 and others. (from Pfam)

label: NfeD1b_N
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in the membrane protein NfeD1b from B. subtilis and related bacterial proteins. The NfeD1b is composed of an N-terminal cytoplasmic ClpP serine protease-like domain (this entry), transmembrane domain, and a C-terminal OB (oligosaccharide / oligonucleotide-binding) fold domain. NfaD1b is a member of the NfeD (nodulation formation efficiency D) family which was divided into two groups : long and short forms. Long-form NfeD homologs contain a putative ClpP serine protease-like domain while short-form homologs have in common the C-terminal OB fold domain (Pfam:PF01957). Despite global similarity to ClpP serine proteases, this domain lacks the typical for these enzymes Ser, His, Asp catalytic triad and of these, has only Ser residue conserved in equivalent position. (from Pfam)

label: Pyr4-TMTC
comment: This entry represents Pyr4 and related transmembrane terpene cyclases. These are noncanonical terpene cyclases that are involved in the biosynthesis of pyripyropene A, diterpenoid pyrones, novofumigatonin, austinol and dehydroaustinol and others (PMID: 38942513). Pyr4 was the first integral membrane terpene cyclase that was identified (PMID: 20861902). It is involved in the biosynthesis of pyripyropene A, a polyketide-sesquiterpenoid hybrid that is a potent inhibitor of acyl-coenzyme A:cholesterol acyl-transferase. These enzymes are presdicted to contain seven transmembrane helices. There is a highly conserved glutamate residue, part of [W/Y]ExxY motif, which is probably functionally important. (from Pfam)

label: TEN_NHL
comment: Teneurins are ancient cell-cell adhesion receptors that are vital for brain development and synapse organisation (PMID: 29540701). This entry represents the NHL six-bladed beta-propeller domain which packs against the TTR, FN and shell domains with the bottom face and it is held in place by the FN domain which acts as a wedge to position the NHL at an angle perpendicular to the YD-shell domain (PMID: 29540701). The top face of the NHL propeller contains extended loops, stabilised by five disulphide bonds, which are highly conserved among vertebrates members (PMID: 29540701). (from Pfam)

label: TEN_YD-shell
comment: Teneurins are ancient cell-cell adhesion receptors that are vital for brain development and synapse organisation (PMID: 29540701). This entry represents the YD-shell domain which forms a hollow tube, consisting of a single up-and-down spiralling beta-sheet with 78 strands (PMID: 29540701) and shows similarity to structures of bacterial toxin complexes TcB-TcC. This domain is the most most structurally conserved region of teneurins and the TcB-TcC toxin complexes (PMID: 29540701). This big domain comprises YD or rearrangement hotspot (Rhs) repeats. (from Pfam)

label: TTR_TEN1-4
comment: This entry represents the transthyretin-like (TTR-like) domain found in teneurins, ancient cell-cell adhesion receptors that are vital for brain development and synapse organisation (PMID: 29540701). (from Pfam)

label: ADH_Fe_C
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in the family of iron- containing alcohol dehydrogenases. It is usually found associated with Pfam:PF00171 and Pfam:PF00465. It folds into an array of alpha-helices [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_ATRN-LZTR1
comment: This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found in attracting (ATRN), LZTR1, among others. ATRN is involved in the initial immune cell clustering during inflammatory response and may regulate chemotactic activity of chemokines. It may play a role in melanocortin signaling pathways that regulate energy homeostasis and hair color (PMID: 9736737). It was thought to have dipeptidase activity but it was shown later to lack that activity (PMID: 17261078). LZTR1 is a substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex that mediates ubiquitination of Ras (K-Ras/KRAS, N-Ras/NRAS and H-Ras/HRAS). This domain can be found in a number of other proteins, such as KLHDC3, a substrate-recognition component of a Cul2-RING (CRL2) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex of the DesCEND (destruction via C-end degrons) pathway. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2110_C
comment: This domain, found in various hypothetical archaeal proteins, has no known function. It is found at the C-terminus of DUF2110 family proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7738
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial protein domains. The structure of these proteins shows some structural similarity to the PePSy domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7814
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into array of helices. It has similarity to helical domain found in MmeI restriction-modification enzymes. (from Pfam)

label: GMPPB_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of GMPPB (Mannose-1-phosphate guanylyltransferase catalytic subunit beta), which consists of a left-handed parallel beta-helix composed of tandem repeats of a [LIV]-G-X(4) hexapeptide (PMID: 33986552). This protein catalyses the formation of GDP-mannose, an essential precursor of glycan moieties of glycoproteins and glycolipids (PMID: 33986552). In S. pombe, it is required for proper septum structure and is involved cell cycle progression through cell-size checkpoint (PMID: 16049679). In budding yeasts Mgp1 (also known as Psa1) plays an important part in maintenance of cell-wall integrity (PMID: 11055399). (from Pfam)

label: LRR_R13L1-DRL21
comment: This entry represents Leucine-rich repeats (LRRs) found in R13L1, DRL21 from Arabidopsis thaliana and related plant proteins. R13L1 and DRL21 are likely disease resistance proteins. DRL21 has adenylate cyclase activity (PMID: 31850369). (from Pfam)

label: NPHP3_N
comment: This entry represents a P-loop like domain found at the N-terminal of nephrocystin-3, a protein required for normal ciliary development and function. It inhibits disheveled-1-induced canonical Wnt-signaling activity and may also play a role in the control of non-canonical Wnt signaling which regulates planar cell polarity (PMID: 18371931). This entry represents the N-terminal domain of nephrocystin-3 (NPHP3) which belongs to NACHT NTPases clade defined by a residue (glycine, alanine or serine) directly C-terminal of the Mg2+-coordinating aspartate, and two additional acidic residues one position downstream, with a consensus sequence hhhhD[GAS]hDE (PMID: 15381417). This domain is also found in Ankyrin repeat domain-containing protein 50 from human. (from Pfam)

label: PRC_RimM
comment: This entry represents a PRC-barrel domain found in the RimM protein family. The RimM family comprises ribosome maturation factors essential for the final assembly of the 30S ribosomal subunit, particularly the head region. These proteins facilitate the efficient processing of 16S rRNA and may function both before and after RbfA during 16S rRNA maturation. RimM proteins have a specific affinity for free 30S ribosomal subunits but not for 70S ribosomes. The PRC barrel domain within these proteins binds to ribosomal protein uS19, playing a crucial role in the assembly process. In some organisms, RimM is one of several proteins, including Era, RbfA, and RsgA/YjeQ, that assist in the late stages of 30S subunit assembly, ensuring the correct assembly of head-associated ribosomal proteins and preventing the accumulation of precursor rRNA forms. (from Pfam)

label: TYW2_N_2
comment: This is the N-terminal domain of the tRNA-wybutosine synthesizing enzyme TYW2 from Pyrococcus horikoshii and related sequences (PMID: 19717466). This domain consists of six beta-strands and three alpha-helices. (from Pfam)

label: YkcB_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of the putative mannosyltransferase YkcB from Bacillus subtilis and similar sequences. This domain is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta configuration. It is usually found associated with Pfam:PF13231. (from Pfam)

label: ARM_TT21
comment: This entry represents an ARM-repeats domain found in the middle region of Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 (TT21) from human and its homologues. TT21 is an intraflagellar transport (IFT)-associated protein required for spermatogenesis. It is involved in sperm flagellar formation and intraflagellar transport (PMID: 30929735). (from Pfam)

label: ARM_TT21_5th
comment: This is the fifth ARM-repeats domain found towards the C-terminal of Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 (TT21) from human and its homologues. TT21 is an intraflagellar transport (IFT)-associated protein required for spermatogenesis. It is involved in sperm flagellar formation and intraflagellar transport (PMID: 30929735). (from Pfam)

label: ARM_TT21_C
product_name: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 C-terminal ARM domain
name_orig: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 C-terminal ARM domain
hmm_name: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 C-terminal ARM domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal ARM-repeats domain of Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 (TT21) from human and its homologues. TT21 is an intraflagellar transport (IFT)-associated protein required for spermatogenesis. It is involved in sperm flagellar formation and intraflagellar transport (PMID: 30929735). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7737
comment: This domain is found in proteins that contain Pfam:PF13569. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DrmE_C
product_name: DISARM anti-phage system protein DrmE domain-containing protein
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of DISARM protein DrmE from Bacillus paralicheniformis and similar uncharacterised bacterial proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7768
comment: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It has a detectable similarity to domains members of N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like superfamily and is predicted to adopt similar structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7800
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins that also contain Pfam:PF09423. This domain is predicted to show an immunoglobulin-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: Hexapep_GlmU
hmm_name: GlgC family sugar phosphate nucleotidyltransferase C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Bifunctional protein GlmU from Streptococcus pneumoniae and similar sequences. This domain is responsible for the transfer of acetyl group from acetyl coenzyme A to glucosamine-1-phosphate (GlcN-1-P) to produce N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate (GlcNAc-1-P). This domain consists of hexapeptide repeats that form a left-handed beta-helix (PMID: 11118459). (from Pfam)

label: ILV_EDD_C
comment: This is the C-terminal domain of Ilv/ED dehydratase protein family which includes dihydroxy-acid/6-phosphogluconate dehydratases, and pentonate dehydratases (PMID: 1624451). Members of this entry are involved in various biosynthetic and carbohydrate metabolic pathways (PMID: 28574691). Dihydroxy-acid dehydratase catalyses the fourth step in the biosynthesis of isoleucine and valine, the dehydration of 2,3-dihydroxy-isovaleic acid into alpha-ketoisovaleric acid. 6-Phosphogluconate dehydratase catalyses the first step in the Entner-Doudoroff pathway, the dehydration of 6-phospho-D-gluconate into 6-phospho-2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-gluconate. They consist of two domains, N- and C-terminal, the latter contains residues (Ser490 and Thr492) that participate in the formation of the substrate binding site. This domain is composed of a beta-sheet consisting of six parallel and two anti-parallel beta-strands that are arranged like a beta-barrel [2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: LbH_EIF2B
comment: This entry represents the central Left-handed parallel beta-Helix (LbH) domain of Translation initiation factor eIF-2B subunit epsilon (EIF2B), a guanine nucleotide-exchange factor that mediates the exchange of GDP (bound to initiation factor eIF2) for GTP, generating active eIF2-GTP complex. EIF2B is a complex multimeric protein consisting of five subunits, alpha, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: NET2A
comment: This domain is found in Protein NETWORKED 2A from Arabidopsis thaliana (NET2A) and similar plant proteins. NET2A associates with F-actin at the plasma membrane in growing pollen tubes. This domain is predicted to adopt an all-alpha configuration. (from Pfam)

label: NET2A_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Protein NETWORKED 2A from Arabidopsis thaliana (NET2A) and similar plant proteins. NET2A is an actin binding protein that associates with F-actin at the plasma membrane in growing pollen tubes. This domain is predicted to have an all-alpha helical configuration. (from Pfam)

label: NfeD_membrane
comment: This entry represents the central integral membrane domain found in the NfeD protein. (from Pfam)

label: vWA_Ro60
comment: This entry represents the vWA domain of RNA-binding protein RO60 which is found after the TROVE domain at the N-terminal [1-3]. This domain closes the ring from by the TROVE domain. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_CGLA
comment: This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found at the N-terminal of Lambda-carrageenases (CGLA), a protein that hydrolyses lambda-carrageenan with inversion of anomeric configuration (PMID: 16926183). (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_WDR3_1st
comment: This is the first beta-propeller domain of WDR3 from animals and its homologues. It is part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, the first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit (PMID: 34516797). (from Pfam)

label: COR-B
comment: The C-terminal of Roc domain, COR, along with Roc functions as the putative regulator of kinase activity. It functions as a proper GTP-binding protein with a low GTPase activity somehow stimulating the kinase activity (PMID: 18650931). COR is divided in two subdomains: COR-A and COR-B. This entry corresponds to COR-B, located at the C-terminal of COR. COR-B serves as the main dimerisation interface in the full-length LRRK2 structure (PMID: 37189360). It interacts with the kinase domain, which is essential for LRRK2 kinase activity (PMID: 32814344). COR-B consists of four flanked helices, a central seven-stranded antiparallel sheet, and a hairpin motif (PMID: 37189360). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7832
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised bacterial protein domain. This domain is found in single domain proteins as well as in large multidomain proteins that contain immunity related domains. This suggests that this family may play a role in a toxin/antitoxin system. The domain contains two structural sites that contain two conserved histidines and an aspartate that may be functionally important. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7846
comment: This is a domain of unknown function, mainly found in a group of archaeal sequences such as HVO_1708 (Swiss:D4H053). This domain may have a fold related to glycosyltransferases. (from Pfam)

label: Golvesin_C
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in Golvesin and in related proteins. Golvesin is a protein associated with membranes of the Golgi apparatus and post-Golgi vesicles in Dictyostelium cells (PMID: 11229601). This domain is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich with topology similar to Galactose-binding domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7836
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in Halobacteria. They contain two pairs of conserved cysteines that are likely involved in metal coordination. These proteins are predicted to structurally resemble Zinc beta-ribbon domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7863
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed of array of helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7910
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to adopt beta-Trefoil fold. It is closely related to members of Fascin Pfam:PF06268. (from Pfam)

label: WHD_NWD1
comment: This domain is found in human NACHT domain- and WD repeat -containing protein 1 (NWD1) and similar animal proteins. NWD1 may play a role in the control of androgen receptor protein steady-state levels. This domain is predicted to adopt a winged helix-turn-helix fold. (from Pfam)

label: HVO_A0261_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal HTH domain of a group of sequences mostly from archaea, such as HVO_A0261 (swiss:D4GQU0) from H. volcanii. This entry also includes bacterial sequences. (from Pfam)

label: ANG-1
comment: This presumed domain is found in human Angiopoietin-1 (ANG-1) and similar animal sequences. ANG-1 plays an important role in the regulation of angiogenesis, endothelial cell survival, proliferation, migration, adhesion and cell spreading, reorganisation of the actin cytoskeleton and maintenance of vascular quiescence. It is required for normal angiogenesis and heart development during embryogenesis. This domain, which is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical configuration, is often found associated with Pfam:PF00147. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7847
comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in a group of archaeal and bacterial sequences, including HVO_0229 (Swiss:D4GZH4). This domain may consist of several transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7862
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich with Ig-like topology. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7898
comment: This entry describes the N-terminal domain of unknown function of DNA polymerase theta subunit (PolQ) majoritarily from fungal and and yeast proteins. Structural predictions suggest that this family adopts Helix-Helix-Helix (HHH) motifs. Proteins containing HHH motifs are typically associated with DNA-binding functions. These structural elements are often found in enzymes involved in DNA metabolism, such as DNA polymerases and helicases [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: HVO_A0114
comment: This entry includes archaeal and bacterial sequences, which are mostly uncharacterised, such as HVO_A0114 (swiss:D44GQE6) from Haloferax volcanii. This is a HTH domain, also found in CRISPR locus-related putative DNA-binding protein Csa3 from Saccharolobus solfataricus. (from Pfam)

label: AAA_lid_RFC1
comment: This domain is found in human Replication factor C subunit 1 (RFC1) and similar sequences with an AAA domain (Pfam:PF00004). RFC1 could play a role in DNA transcription regulation, DNA replication and/or repair. This domain adopts an alpha configuration [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_WDR41
comment: This entry includes WDR41, the non-catalytic component of the C9orf72-SMCR8 complex which has guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) activity and regulates autophagy [1,2]. This complex also acts as a negative regulator of autophagy initiation by interacting with the ULK1/ATG1 kinase complex and inhibiting its protein kinase activity [3,4]. WDR41 plays an essential role in C9orf72 lysosome recruitment, which is important for lysosomal responses to changes in amino acid availability (PMID: 29995611). WDR41 also interacts with PQLC2, a lysosomal cationic amino acid transporter that serves as a sensor that responds to scarcity of its substrates by recruiting C9orf72-SMCR8-WDR41 complex to the surface of lysosomes (PMID: 33597295). (from Pfam)

label: CoiA_N
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in the Competence protein CoiA and related proteins. It contains three highly conserved cysteine and histidine residues that are probably involved in metal coordination. This domain is frequently preceding Pfam:PF06054. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7830
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It has three highly conserved cysteine residues and a histidine that may be involved in zinc coordination. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7839
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised archaeal proteins. This domain is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure. Members of this family have an HTH domain at the N terminus. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7845
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function. In some proteins the is a C-terminal HTH domain that presumably binds to DNA. This domain may bind to an as unyet identified ligand to enable regulation of bacterial genes. This domain contains a large beta sheet composed of 11 beta strands with helices packed on the convex face. There is some evidence from structure prediction that this domain may dimerise and form a large structure that has a large hole through it that might accommodate DNA. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7864
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure with similarity to AAA proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7916
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a TIM-barrel structure. It shares detectable similarity with Mycobacterium tuberculosis Indole-3-glycerol phosphate synthase (TrpC). (from Pfam)

label: DeaD_dimer
comment: This entry represents the dimerisation domain found in the ATP-dependent RNA helicase DeaD (also known as CsdA) and related proteins. DeaD is involved in various cellular processes after cold shock, including ribosome biogenesis, mRNA degradation and translation initiation. It was found to unwind double-stranded RNA in the absence of ATP. In E.coli DeaD is associated with the pre50S particles and is involved in the biogenesis of the 50S subunit, and plays an essential role in the survival at low temperature. DeaD is a multidomain protein, composed of a conserved helicase core and a C-terminal domain that is probably involved in RNA recognition. The domain represented by this entry is indispensable for stabilizing the DeaD dimeric structure (PMID: 29107486). This domain consists of three alpha-helices, two of which entangle with the helices of another monomer and tightly pack to form the dimeric core (PMID: 29107486). (from Pfam)

label: Tad3
comment: This entry represents the Tad3 family of phage proteins that inhibit the bacterial Type I Thoeris defense system. Tad3 forms a homodimer that binds two ThsB proteins, blocking their active sites by inserting a conserved serine residue (S48) that forms a hydrogen bond with the ThsB catalytic residue E85. This prevents the production of the immune signaling molecule gcADPR. The structure has been solved in complex with ThsB at 1.8A resolution. The protein contains N-terminal helices that mediate homodimer formation and C-terminal regions that make extensive contacts with ThsB. (from Pfam)

label: Volactin
comment: Volactin (Haloferax volcanii actin) is an actin-like protein that contributes to disk-shape morphogenesis in Haloferax and related bacteria.

label: Khk
comment: This family includes Ketohexokinase from Haloferax volcanii, which catalyses the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of the ketose sugar fructose to fructose-1-phosphate (PMID: 38587824). (from Pfam)

label: LMF1_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of a family transmembrane proteins that includes the lipase maturation factor, LMF1. Lipoprotein lipase and hepatic lipase require LMF1 to fold into their active states (PMID: 17994020). It acts as a chaperone required for maturation and transport of active lipoprotein lipase (LPL), through the secretory pathway [2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: LdpA_Fe-S-bd
comment: This entry represents the Fe-S cluster-binding domain of LpdA from Synechococcus elongatus, which is inserted in the TIM barrel domain (Pfam:PF12617). LpdA plays a role in controlling the redox state in cyanobacteria to modulate its circadian clock [1,2]. This entry also includes uncharacterised sequences from plants and archaea. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_capsid_4
comment: This entry represents a family of phage capsid proteins including Swiss:A9CRA7 from Staphylococcus phage phiMR11 and Swiss:Q859Q5 from Enterobacteria phage N4. (from Pfam)

label: Ribosomal_L19e_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of the large ribosomal subunit protein eL19 found in eukaryotes and archaea. This is an helical domain that assumes an orthogonal bundle topology. (from Pfam)

label: TAF2_3rd
comment: This entry represents the immunoglobulin-like domain found in transcription factor TFIID subunit 2 (TAF2). This domain is inserted between subdomains 2 and 4 of the aminopeptidase-like region of TAF2. The aminopeptidase-like region of TAF2 is involved in downstream promoter recognition and plays an important role in transcription initiation. The specific function of this Ig-like domain within the context of TAF2's role is not yet fully characterized. (from Pfam)

label: WDGH
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from phages and bacteriophages. It is predicted to adopt an unique alpha/beta structure composed of a central mixed four-stranded beta-sheet and alpha helices packed on one side of it. Members of this entry contain a highly conserved WDGH sequence motif after which it was named. (from Pfam)

label: nSTAND6
comment: This entry represents a novel domain of the STAND-superfamily of AAA+ ATPases, found in bacterial conflict systems (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: LbH_GLGC
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal left-handed parallel beta helix (LbH) domain of glucose-1-phosphate adenylyltransferases (GLGC).
