comment: Galvan, et al. (PMID:34378964) identified a 3-gene cluster for biosynthesis and export of arsinothricin, an arsenic-containing antibiotic., with key enzyme ArsL, a radical SAM enzyme, catalyzing the first step. The cassette contains a methyltransferase, designated ArsM, capable both of completing arsinothricin biosynthesis and of methylating inorganic arsenite (see NF040538). Examination of additional genomic neighborhoods of ArsL showed that in species such as Paenibacillus sambharensis and Vogesella fluminis, this arsenite methyltransferase appears to replace NF040538.

label: trim_DfrE
comment: DfrE was discovered as a plasmid-borne dihydrofolate reductase from Staphylococcus (Mammaliicoccus) sciuri conferring trimethoprim resistance. Note that the name DfrE previously was assigned to an intrinsic, trimethoprim-sensitive dihydrofolate reductase of Enterococcus faecalis.

label: rSAM_RCCLKC
product_name: arsinothricin biosynthesis radical SAM protein ArsL
hmm_name: arsinothricin biosynthesis radical SAM protein ArsL
comment: ArsL performs the first step in biosynthesis of arsinothricin and other, yet-uncharacterized arsenicals. This atypical radical SAM enzyme cleaves S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) in an unusual way, generating a 3-amino-3-carboxypropyl (ACP) group that it transfers to arsenite, forming a C–As bond. Members of this family terminate with an intriguing, nearly invariant RCCLKC motif that is critical to its interaction with arsenic.

label: rSAM_CUAEP
comment: Members of this family are radical SAM enzymes with an N-terminal apparent B12-binding domain. Some members of the family have Cys-Cys motif about 10 amino acids before the C-terminus, but the majority of the family are selenoproteins with the second Cys replaced by selenocysteine, in a strongly conserved motif W[YF]C[CU]AEP. The proximity of the selenocysteine-encoding TGA codon to the C-terminus may have impeded recognition of this novel family of selenoproteins.

label: DUF2007_rel
comment: This family of small proteins, 74 amino acids in length on average, includes some proteins included in the seed alignment for Pfam model PF09413 (DUF2007), but most members of this HMM, apparently a distinctive branch within the family of DUF2007-related proteins, fall below the detection limits of PF09413.

label: peroxidase_FMP
comment: This novel form of the heme-binding enzyme peroxidase was originally described as occurring in Flavobacterium meningosepticum (now called Elizabethkingia meningoseptica), hence FMP (F. meningosepticum peroxidase), although the species attribution may have been incorrect.

label: T2SS_GspM_XpsM
product_name: type II secretion system protein GspM
hmm_name: type II secretion system protein GspM, XpsM type
comment: This form of the type II secretion system (T2SS) protein GspM (general secretion pathway M - the old name for T2SS) is more closely related to the type IV pilus protein PilO than to other GspM. Note that PF04612 refers to this type of GspM as type b.

label: cas_Cas7fv
comment: Cas7fv is one of the CRISPR associated (Cas) proteins of type I-F variant (I-Fv) CRISPR-Cas system. CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats)-Cas modules are adaptive immune systems found in archaea and bacteria against foreign nucleic acids such as phages and plasmids via RNA-guided endonucleases. CRISPR-Cas systems are classified based on Cas protein content and arrangement in CRISPR-Cas loci into two main classes (1 and 2) and at least six types (I, II, III, IV, V, VI). Class 1 systems utilize multiple Cas proteins and CRISPR RNA (crRNA) to form an effector complex while class 2 systems employ a large, single effector with crRNA to mediate interference. Type I CRISPR-Cas systems are most widespread in nature and the Cas protein composition of the employed Cascade interference complexes differ between seven subtypes (A-F, U). Type I-F variant (I-Fv) is a subtype that rely on a minimal set of five Cas proteins and has structural differences with I-F and I-E Cascades. Double strand DNA recruitment and recognition in the type I-Fv Cascade is facilitated from the major groove side by Cas5fv instead of the large subunit Cas8 and the finger domain of Cas7fv.

label: FxsC_Nterm
comment: Members of this protein family, FxsC, occur in the context of FxSxx-COOH class RiPP precursors (FxsA) and their radical SAM/SPASM domain maturases (FxsB). Most but not all members have an additional C-termimal domain (see TIGR04276).

label: choice_anch_O
comment: Members of this rare protein family have been observed with the JDVT-CTERM sorting signal at the C-terminus, or with a low-scoring variant of the GlyGly-CTERM domain (see WP_188923155.1), or with alternative sequence regions not currently recognizable as sorting signals or homology domains. The function is unknown.

label: MXAN_2562_fam
product_name: MXAN_2562 family outer membrane beta-barrel protein
hmm_name: MXAN_2562 family outer membrane beta-barrel protein
comment: This homology domain, found in Deltaproteobacteria such as Myxococcus xanthus, comprises the near full-length of proteins about 240 amino acids in size, or the C-terminal domain of longer proteins. A distant relationship to PF13505 suggests these proteins may form outer membrane beta-barrels.

label: TerS_not_xtmA
comment: Members of this family are phage terminase small subunit proteins, based on adjacency to terminase large subunit proteins, and on a small N-terminal homology domain, described by PF10668, about 67 amino acids in length, shared with TerS from PBSX (XtmA) and from phage related to PBSX. Terminase small subunits related to XtmA of defective prophage PBSX have a C-terminal PF03592 domain, accounting for most of the length of those proteins. Members of this family differ from XtmA-like TerS over most of the their lengths, C-terminal to the PF10668 domain, and show no trace of homology to PF03592.

label: division_SteA
comment: Members of this family on membrane proteins from Actinobacteria were reported (in 2019) to be SteA (Sensitive To Ethambutol A), a cytokinetic ring protein that partners with SteB and contributes to proper cell division. A short region of sequence similarity to some proteins characterized as thiamine pyrophosphokinases may cause confusion in functional annotation.

label: PPA1309_fam
comment: This family of uncharacterized proteins, restricted to the Actinobacteria but absent from the genus Mycobacterium, is named for founding member PPA1309 from Cutibacterium (Propionibacterium) acnes.

label: CatA_like_2
comment: Members of this family are homologs to members of the CatA family of chloramphenicol acetyltransferases, although less than 30% identical. There is no evidence that members of this family act on or confer resistance to chloramphenicol.

label: CatA_like_3
comment: Members of this family are homologs to members of the CatA family of chloramphenicol acetyltransferases, although less than 35% identical. There is no evidence that members of this family act on or confer resistance to chloramphenicol.

label: YcgZ_fam
comment: YcgZ, as found in Escherichia coli, is a small protein of unknown function that appears to participate in regulatory cascades involved in processes such as biofilm formation and response to blue light. YcgZ is homologous to YmgB/AriR, a paralog also found in E. coli and described as having a role in regulatory cascades.

label: immun_SitI3
comment: The founding member of this protein family, SitI3 from Myxococcus xanthus (WP_020478554.1), is an immunity protein encoded immediately downstream of a lipoprotein toxin, SitA3, that can move between cells by means of a transfer system for exchange of outer membrane lipoproteins involved in kin recognition. It is not yet clear what fraction of the members of this family are immunity proteins from other toxin/immunity-type conflict systems.

label: attach_TipJ_rel
product_name: host specificity factor TipJ family phage tail protein
hmm_name: host specificity factor TipJ family phage tail protein
comment: Members of this family form a family related to that of host specificity protein J of phage lambda, a tail tip protein that mediates attachment to LamB on the surface of E. coli. Binding of the phage tail to the LamB receptor triggers the injection of phage DNA into host cells. Proteins with this domain are likely also to be phage tail proteins.

label: GPS-CTERM
comment: The GPS-CTERM domain, defined by this HMM, is found in Actinobacteria such as Nocardia and Streptomyces, at the C-terminus of at least two otherwise unrelated protein families. It is an apparent novel protein-sorting domain.

label: recomb_assoc
comment: Members of this family are found regularly in the context of a XerC/XerD-related recombinase and with a member of family PF13009, called a putative integrase by Pfam. The family is named GmtX, for Gammaproteobacterial Mobile Trio system protein of unknown (X) function. Members of this family include VPA1268 found in a pathogenicity island of Vibrio parahaemolyticus.

label: recomb_GmtY
comment: GmtY (gamma-mobile-trio system tyrosine recombinase) is a putative integrase regularly found associated with two other proteins of unknown function, in a cassette found sporadically in various Gamma-proteobacteria. Members of this family include VPA1270, found in pathogenicity island 6 of Vibrio parahaemolyticus RIMD2210633.

label: VPA1262_fam
comment: Members of this family occur in mobile elements, as for example VPA1262 found in pathogenicity island 6 of Vibrio parahaemolyticus RIMD2210633.

label: SepH
comment: Septation protein H (SepH) was firstly characterized in Streptomyces venezuelae, and homologs were identified in Mycobacterium smegmatis. SepH contains a N-terminal DUF3071 domain and a conserved C-terminal region. It binds directly to cell division protein FtsZ to stimulate the assembly of FtsZ protofilaments.

label: ZapE
comment: The ATPase ZapE directly interacts with cell division protein FtsZ. It has been reported that ZapE destabilized FtsZ polymers in an ATP-dependent manner. In addition, ZapE is required for E. coli to grow under conditions of low oxygen, suggesting ZapE is a stress-regulated cell division protein.

label: BcsP_of_Ic
hmm_name: cellulose biosynthesis protein BcsP N-terminal domain
comment: BcsP is a protein of bacterial cellulose biosynthesis, encode in the beta-proteobacteria in type Ic cellulose biosynthesis operons. Only the N-terminal region, homologous to the much smaller protein BcsR, is well-conserved. Pfam model PF10945 describes the region shared by BcsP, BcsR, and some other cellulose biosynthesis proteins.

label: SBP_SaoB_CU
comment: Members of this family are apparent substrate-binding proteins of an ABC transporter, found in Clostridium difficile and a number of other anaerobic heterotrophs, as part of the SAO (selenocysteine organometallic-assisted) locus. Six of the nine core proteins of the SAO locus can be selenoproteins, including this protein and the permease subunit, SaoP, encoded next to it.

label: MerB_rel_SaoL
comment: Nearly all members of this family, SaoL, are selenoproteins with a CU motif that suggests interaction with a heavy metal such as mercury. While SaoL is homologous to the organomercurial lyase MerB, its context is different. SaoL occurs as part of the SAO (selenocysteine-assisted organomercurial) locus, with nine conserved proteins. Six SAO proteins can be selenoproteins, including multiple subunits of an unusual ABC transporter with one permease subunit but two associated substrate-binding proteins.

label: ABC_ATP_SaoA
comment: SaoA is the ATP-binding subunit of an ABC transporter in which both the permease subunit SaoP, and the substrate-binding protein SaoB, are nearly always selenoproteins that were unrecognized as such until recently (2022). The SAO system is found in Clostridium difficile and various other anaerobic heterotrophs.

label: CxCC_doxin
comment: SaoT is a predicted cytosolic protein, usually a selenoprotein, from the SAO (selenocysteine-assisted organometallic) locus. Other proteins in the system include a putative metal efflux protein, a surface protein, an ABC transporter with multiple selenoprotein subunits, and the selenoprotein SaoL, a homolog of the organomercurial lyase MerB of some mercury resistance systems. The SAO system may use mercury or another heavy metal atom as a cofactor, incorporating it into an organometallic intermediate, associated with import of that metabolite, and then exporting the metal after its release for use in a subsequent cycle.

label: flavo_sub_EftB
comment: Members of this family electron transfer flavoprotein subunit beta (EftB) as found in pathways for leucine reduction to isocaproate as seen in the strict anaerobe Clostridium difficile.

label: ABC_perm_U
comment: SaoP, one of the nine proteins of the SAO (selenocysteine-associated organometallic) locus, is nearly always a selenoprotein, and is one of six novel selenoprotein families from that locus. The Sec (U) residue occurs at a position described in other ABC transporter permease homodimers as the channel-gating position. A role in importing (and perhaps even forming) organometallic compounds, in a cycle in which the metal atom is reexported and reused, as a cofactor that aids in utilization of some otherwise refractory substrate, has been suggested. The SAO system occurs in Clostridium difficile (a human gut pathogen), Brachyspira pilosicoli (an intestinal spirochete in chicken), Desulfopila aestuarii (a deltaproteobacterial sulfate reducer from estuary sediment), etc. Most members of this family are selenoproteins with the selenocysteine residue at the channel-gating position.

label: CC-COOH_SaoC
comment: Members of this family, now called SaoC, include CD2366 from Clostridium difficile. The most striking conserved motif in this family is a pair of cysteine residues at the C-terminus, which takes the form Cys-Sec (CU) in the occasional members of this family that are selenoproteins. Selenoprotein examples include WP_252346676.1 (Finegoldia magna), WP_252346670.1 (Merdimonas faecis), and WP_252346671.1 (Lachnospiraceae bacterium). The SAO (selenocysteine-assisted organometallic) system contains six selenoproteins overall, including three ABC transporter subunits and a homolog (SaoL) of organomercurial lyases. SaoC is proposed to play a role in chaperoning heavy metal atoms effluxed by SaoE to an ABC transporter with selenoprotein permease and substrate-binding proteins, for reuptake after covalent incorporation into an organometallic intermediate of some unknown class of fermentable nutrient.

label: SBP_SaoX
comment: Members of this family include CD2365 from Clostridium difficile, and are identified as SaoX of the selenocysteine-assisted organometallic (SAO) system. SaoX, an ABC transporter substrate-binding subunit, is an occasional selenoprotein. Partner proteins SaoB (another substrate-binding protein) and SaoP (an ABC transporter permease subunit) are selenoproteins most of the time. The transporter complex likely imports some (currently unknown) organometallic compound, and might actually couple its formation to its transport, employing a heavy metal atom as an inorganic cofactor that lowers activation energies for anaerobic fermentation of refractory substrates.

label: efflux_SaoE
comment: Members of this family, including CD2367 from Clostridium difficile, are related to efflux proteins associated with resistance to arsenic or organoarsenicals, copper, and zinc.

label: peroxi_PrxU
comment: Most members of this family contain a selenocysteine.

label: ornith_Ord
comment: This model does not distinguish between 1.4.1.26 (NAD-only) and 1.4.1.12 (NAD or NADP).

label: racem_Orr
comment: This type of ornithine racemase occurs in an operon for anaerobic oxidative degradation of L-ornithine as occurs in strict anaerobes such as Clostridium sticklandii. The enzyme from C. sticklandii was shown to act on the basic amino acids ornithine, lysine, and arginine. Additional close homologs, outside the family defined by this HMM, likely have similar activity profiles, but occur in different genomic contexts and would not receive the gene symbol orr.

label: ornith_Or-4
comment: Members of this uncharacterized protein family, given the temporary name Or-4, occur as a part of a conserved gene cluster for anaerobic oxidative degradation of L-ornithine. That cluster includes a B-12-dependent enzyme, D-ornithine 4,5-aminomutase. Or-4 is related to but distinct from GlmL, a protein of unknown function encoded next to subunits of a coenzyme B12-dependent glutamate mutase.

label: accessory_GlmL
comment: GlmL (glutamate mutase operon protein L), a protein with unknown activity, occurs invariably as part of a locus that also includes the E (epsilon) and S (sigma) subunits of methylaspartate mutase (also called glutamate mutase. A related protein occurs exclusively in a locus the anaerobic degradation of ornithine, where a different cobalamin-dependent enzyme occurs. It seems likely that GlmL is an accessory protein for the methylaspartate mutase.

comment: Protein C is the shared acetyl-phosphate-forming component of three types of selenoprotein-containing complexes, acting on glycine, sarcosine, or betaine. Protein C itself has a large subunit and a small subunit (sometimes fused), and does not contain selenocysteine. This HMM describes the large subunit, called beta.

comment: Protein C is the shared acetyl-phosphate-forming component of three types of selenoprotein-containing complexes, acting on glycine, sarcosine, or betaine. A different subunit, B, determines the substrate. Protein C itself has a large subunit and a small subunit (sometimes fused), and does not contain selenocysteine. This HMM describes the small subunit, called alpha.

label: reduct_selen_A
comment: Selenoprotein A (GrdA) is the A subunit of a complex whose specificity is determined by a different subunit, B, in a glycine or sarcosine or betaine reductase complex. In some species, only one type of B subunit (also a selenoprotein) occurs. Protein C is usually a heterodimer of two subunits called beta (GrdC) and alpha (GrdD), and is not a selenoprotein.

label: SelL_rel_redox
comment: Members of this family are related to the C-terminal region of selenoprotein L (SelL), found in many non-mammalian animals. But while SelL itself has a pair of selenocysteine (U) residues (e.g. XP_029705782.1), typically in the motif ULPU, this family is defined more broadly. Most members of the seed alignment for this HMM are bacterial proteins that have one or zero selenocysteine residues, and are shorter than SelU, although SelU members are also included.

label: AAH_UGLYAH2
comment: The UGLYAH2 family acts primarily as allantoicase (allantoate amidinohydrolase, EC 3.5.3.4), while unrelated to the AllC family of allantoicase enzymes. It belongs to a broader family of enzymes with (S)-ureidoglycine aminohydrolase activity (EC 3.5.3.26) carried out at the same active site. However, Puggioni, et al. consider that activity secondary, as (S)-ureidoglycine is an unstable compound expected only as a product of allantoate amidohydrolase (AAH) activity, and AAH is nearly always absent when UGLYAH2 is present. UGLYAH2 is an acronym for (S)-ureidoglycine aminohydrolase type 2.

label: CD3324_fam
comment: Members of this family include CD3324 and CD1583A from Clostridium difficile and YraL from Bacillus subtilis. Members show stretches of sequence homology to Mor, which is a transcriptional activator from phage Mu, and to other members of Pfam model PF08765.

label: spore_GerD
comment: This HMM describes the spore germination GerD, as found in Bacillus subtilis and other endospore-forming bacteria. It appears that every member of this family has a lipoprotein-type signal sequence.

label: lxa_BCAM0308
comment: Members of this family average about 170 amino acids in length, and have a conserved pair of CxxC motifs, suggesting metal-binding. Many of this proteins register as part-length, borderline-scoring hits to Pfam model PF04981, which hits the N-terminal domain of Nmd3 (nonsense-mediated decay 3) in yeast, involving in export of the 60S ribosomal subunit from the nucleus, as well as archaeal homologs of Nmd3. This HMM was built to provide a clear separation of member proteins from that family. The family is named for BCAM0308 from Burkholderia cenocepacia, one of many proteins in the lxa (low oxygen-activated) locus, whose proteins are induced when oxygen concentrations are low.

comment: This small and previously undescribed domain, just over 30 amino acids in length, occurs primarily in small proteins of unknown function. It is identified as a probable heavy metal-binding domain by its CysCys pair (seen often in mercury resistance proteins), by the presence of metal-binding or transport domains such PF00403, N-terminal or C-terminal to this domain, in longer members of the family, in some cases by local genomic context.

label: NuoF_pre_CCxxC
product_name: CCxxC motif-containing NuoF prefix domain-containing protein
comment: This domain of about 50 residues, containing seven invariant Cys residues, is a rare N-terminal extension to the NADH-quinone oxidoreductase subunit NuoF.

label: OadG_rel_small
comment: Members of this family are transporter subunits of small size, related to the N-terminal region of OadG the oxaloacetate decarboxylase gamma subunit. OadG itself is described the longer model PF04277.

label: CD1871A_fam
comment: Members of this family typically are small proteins (often less than 50 amino acids in length) with a highly conserved C-terminal motif CLECxGIG that features an apparent redox-active disulfide bond. The N-terminal portion is hydrophobic and resembles a transmembrane alpha-helix.

label: hypo_ExtJ
comment: ExtJ, encoded within a selenite/tellurite reduction operon, has an N-termainl signal peptide, and an unusual Gly-Cys dipeptide at the C-terminus. The length is variable, with the longer form averaging about 105 amino acids, and the shorter form averaging about 75.

label: CCC_membrane
comment: Members of this family average about 150 amino acids in length and are hydrophobic, with several probable transmembrane alpha helices. A notable feature is a Cys-rich cluster, often CCC, starting at about position 22. Members of both this family and NF040944 previously were both included in Pfam model PF07666. But while both families are hydrophobic, they appear not to be truly homologous. NF040944 identifies members of a paralogous family in Mycoplasma penetrans that includes protein MYPE2350, and consequently some members of this family have carried names suggesting (improperly, we think) a relationship to that family.

label: MamK
comment: Magnetosomes are special lipid-bound organelles that comprise magnetic mineral crystals in magnetotactic bacteria (MTB). Magnetosomes are important for MTB to search for preferred microaerophilic environment. Proteins of this family include the magnetosome protein MamK, which is encoded by the mamK gene on the magnetosome island (MAI), and MamK paralogs/homologs. It has been reported that MamK and MamK paralogs are important for magnetosome chain formation in MTB. MamK family proteins can also be found in bacteria without magnetosomes.

label: cytb_ExtP
product_name: selenite/tellurite reduction operon b-type cytochrome ExtP
hmm_name: selenite/tellurite reduction operon b-type cytochrome ExtP

label: PP0621_fam
comment: Members of this family of small proteins have an N-terminal signal peptide and three invariant Cys resisdues, two in a CXXC motif.

label: acVLRF1_NCBI
comment: Members of this family, found in many Actinobacteria, share a consistent architecture and belong to the larger set of Vms1/Ankzf1 family peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase, which release nascent polypeptide chains from stalled ribosomes. The broader family is quite variable in domain architecture.

label: antiphage_dGTPase
comment: Proteins of this family are distant homologues of human antiviral protein SAMHD1. It has been shown that proteins of this family protected bacteria from phage infection by degrading dGTP into phosphate-free deoxyguanosine. The anti-phage dGTPase may also be involved in other biological processes.

label: GSU2204_Se_pt_1
comment: Most members of this family, including founding member GSU2204, are selenoproteins that average about 730 amino acids in length, with a cytochrome c-like CxxCH motif and also a selenocysteine site, typically GUA, about 145 amino acids from the proper C-terminus. This family was listed in Zhang, et al., in Biomolecules (2022). This HMM describes the family up to the residue immediately N-terminal to what is normally a selenocysteine residue. Cutoffs are set so as to exclude most homologs from related clades in which both the CXXCH and the U/C sites are missing, suggesting a similar architecture but different function.

label: decahem_GSU2203
comment: Members of this family are DmsE family decaheme c-type cytochromes (see TIGR03508), but belong to a narrow clade that includes GSU2203, and that co-occurs with a GSU2204 family protein, most of which are selenoproteins (see NF041027).

label: GIVxVP
comment: GIVxVP is a rare, small, uncharacterized protein found in Cyanobacteria such as Synechococcus lacustris, Cyanobium gracile, and Microcystis elabens, in a conserved gene neighborhood of unknown function. Member sequences are about 70 amino acids in length with two apparent transmembrane segments.

label: WAxxUGC_long
hmm_name: ResA-like WAxxUGC motif-containing protein, long form
comment: Members of this family average about 350 amino acids in length. Many are selenoproteins, with a motif WAxxUGC, located in region homologous to smaller proteins such as the thiol-disulfide oxidoreductase ResA of Bacillus.

label: RQC_minor_1
comment: The DNA-binding RQC domain (PF09382) appears primarily in RecQ, a DNA helicase involved in recombination, replication, and repair. However, it appears also in this uncharacterized protein family, to which we give the name "RQC-minor-1 family DNA-binding protein." A majority of members contain an additional C-terminal predicted zinc-ribbon domain. Members appear not to show any conserved gene neighborhood.

label: HPE1_fam_CxxC
product_name: plant virulence effector HPE1-like domain-containing protein
comment: This HMM describes the N-terminal 90 to 100 amino acids of a family bacterial proteins from plant-associated species. Most members of this family have some form of additional C-terminal domain of similar length. However, the best-studied members of this family are shorter proteins, virulence effectors from two plant pathogens, HPE1 ("hypothetical protein effector 1") from Candidatus Liberibacter solanacearum, and CLIBASIA_00460 from Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus. Members of this family begin with an N-terminal signal peptide, for apparent Sec-mediated secretion, and nearly all share a CxxC motif.

label: chap_CsgH_alph
product_name: curli-like amyloid fiber formation chaperone CsgH
hmm_name: curli-like amyloid fiber formation chaperone CsgH
comment: The designation CsgH was given to the broad set of homologs, found outside the Enterobacteriales, of the curli amyloid fiber formation periplasmic chaperone CsgC from species such as Escherichia coli and Salmonella. Members of the seed alignment belong to the Alphaproteobacteria. Because CsgC and CsgH proteins are related, and CsgH is defined broadly, this model does not exclude CsgC proteins, although they are covered also by a more specific HMM NF007507 (PRK10102.1).

label: SAV_2336_NTERM
comment: This HMM describes an N-terminal domain shared by SAV_2336 (BAC70047.1) whose C-terminal region suggests restriction enzyme activity (PMID: 18456708), and with other proteins with unrelated C-terminal regions. A member protein was also identified in a kanamycin biosynthetic gene cluster (PMID:16766657), while N-terminal regions of two other member proteins were named Trypco1 in a bioinformatic study (PMID:32101166) of predicted bacterial conflict systems.

label: RicT_YaaT_fam
comment: RicT in Bacillus subtilis (originally YaaT) was described as stage 0 sporulation protein affecting phosphorelay signals. However, RicT belongs to a iron-sulfur containing regulatory complex that is conserved also in many non-sporulating species, together with homologs of YmcA (RicA) and YlbF (RicF).

label: expansin_EXLX1
comment: This HMM represents nearly the full length of EXLX1 (YoaJ) of Bacillus subtilis, a cellulose-binding bacterial expansin, and similar domains in related bacteirial proteins. Expansins, which are small and non-catalytic, have the ability to loosen plant cell wall material and improve enzyme access, but an expansin domain can occur as an auxiliary domain in cellulases such as CelA of Clavibacter michiganensis, a bacterial pathogen of tomato plants. Pfam model PF01357 (expansin C-terminal domain), somewhat less than half the size, is related but is oriented toward plant expansin and hits relatively few members of this family above cutoffs (as of version PF01357.23).

label: encap_f2a
comment: Capsid-like encapsulin nanocompartments are commonly found in bacteria and archaea. Encapsulin nanocompartments, which are assembled from shell proteins, encapsulate various cargo proteins, typically peroxidases or ferritin-like proteins, to protect cells from oxidative stress caused by peroxide.

label: SenA
comment: Selenoneine is the selenium analog of ergothioneine, a sulfur-containing derivative of a hercynine, which derives from histidine by trimethylation of its amino group. SenA, a homolog of ergothioneine biosynthesis protein EgtB, completes selenoneine biosynthesis in a pathway that also requires a SelD protein to prepare selenophosphate, EgtD to prepare hercynine, and the selenosugar-producing glycosyltransferase SenB (TIGR04348). SenA catalyzes selenium-carbon bond formation between hercynine and selenosugar to produce selenoneine. Other enzymes that create carbon-selenium bonds include SelA, involved in selenocysteine biosynthesis, SelU, involved in selenouridine biosynthesis, and SbtM, a radical SAM enzyme involved in post-translational modification of the RiPP precursor SbtA (see PMID:34730336).

label: encap_f3
comment: Capsid-like encapsulin nanocompartments are commonly found in bacteria and archaea. Encapsulin nanocompartments, which are assembled from shell proteins, encapsulate various cargo proteins, typically peroxidases or ferritin-like proteins, to protect cells from oxidative stress caused by peroxide.

label: ScbA_BarX_GamBu
comment: Members of this family initiate the biosynthesis of gamma-butyrolactone autoregulators, a class of compound that include A-factor in (2-isocapryloyl-3R-hydroxymethyl-y-butyrolactone) in Streptomyces griseus. Through its receptor, a member of the TetR/AcrR family of transcriptional regulators, gamma-butyrolactones can control various processes such as antibiotic biosynthesis.

label: trx7_PDZ_seleno
comment: Members of this family, most of which are selenoproteins, have an average length of about 420 amino acids, with an N-terminal signal peptide and then a PF13899-type thioredoxin-like domain (Trx7), followed by a more C-terminal PDZ domain. The selenocysteine residue occurs in a CxxU or UxxU motif.

label: mob_BfmA_Nterm
comment: BfmA was identified as a mobilization protein for a pathogenicity island that includes fragilysin (Bacteroides fragilis toxin, or BFT) and the fragilysin family metalloproteinase MP-II. BfmA has partner proteins BfmB (a member of the PF18976) and BfmC. The distantly related protein BtgA, also found in Bacteroides fragilis, is a mobilization factor for antibiotic resistance factors.

label: rhodanese_LYCAU
comment: Most members of this family of rhodanese-related putative sulfurtransferases are selenoproteins with one or two selenocysteines in a CxU or UxU motif.

comment: Members of this family are almost entirely selenoproteins, with an average length of 370 amino acids and typically with the motif CFYUT. Cutoffs are set so that most incomplete proteins that run from the N-terminus to the selenocysteine-encoding TGA codon, ending CFY, still score above cutoffs. So far, the vast majority of family members are reported from uncultured organisms assembled out of metagenomic sequence.

label: Moor_selen_rel
comment: Many members of this family have a double-Cys motif. Others, including several from the genus Moorella such as WP_263870381.1 and WP_263870380.1, have a selenocysteine at a similar location once structural annotation is corrected.

label: YhfZ_full
comment: Full-length homologs of the transcriptional regulator YhfZ from Escherichia coli, with an N-terminal GntR-like domain, are quite divergent. See PF14503 (YhfZ_C) for the broader family. This HMM identifies a subset in which the motif MPLPYxxxYEGLA and the C-terminal PxY motifs are both well conserved, suggesting orthology with conserved function.

label: motor_HelR
product_name: RNA polymerase recycling motor ATPase HelR
hmm_name: RNA polymerase recycling motor ATPase HelR group 1
comment: This HMM describes one of two "HelR" subclasses of the RNA polymerase recycling motor protein HelD for which at least a few members have genes preceded by a Rifamycin Associated Element (RAE) and are known or predicted to be induced by rifampicin, a rifamycin-type antibiotic. HelD proteins, including HelR, are helicase-like motor proteins that play a role in transcription, removing and recycling stalled transcription complexes that could interfere with normal transcription or with DNA replication.

label: mono_DmmA_fam

label: actino_IHF
comment: Members of this family are nucleoid-associated dsDNA-binding proteins called integration host factor (mIHF in mycobacteria and sIHF in streptomycetes) because of similarities in cellular role, not in sequence, to the integration host factor proteins of Escherichia coli. Actinobacterial-type IHF actually shows more sequence similarity to 30S ribosomal subunit protein S13. Some members are fused to an additional guanylate kinase domain. This HMM assigns the gene symbol mihF broadly across the actinobacteria.

label: relax_RlxS
comment: I built this because a sul1 chimera in AMR looks like the C-terminus.

label: coba_remo_CbiR
comment: Rare cobamides, analogs of B12 with critical differences in the lower ligand, can become available for a salvage-like pathway to B12 biosynthesis through the action of enzymes that cleave the lower ligand. Members of this family are CbiR, a phosphodiesterase, which joins CbiZ, a previously discovered amidohydrolase, in the guild of cobamide remodeling enzymes.

label: CmcJ_NvfI_EfuI
comment: Members of this family are typically biosynthetic cluster enzymes, including the Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase NvfI, the hydroxylase/desaturase EfuI, and the hydroxylase-like subunit CmcJ of the CmcI/CmcJ methoxylation complex involved in cephamycin biosynthesis.

comment: Most members of this family, called OS_HP4 in a review by Zhang, et al., are selenoproteins.

label: Trx_VPGUxxT_two
comment: Type 2 members of the VPGUxxT family thioredoxin-like (seleno)protein have two sites where selenocysteine residues appear, with motifs EVPGUxxC and UFWxGE.

comment: This HMM somewhat overlaps with Pfam model PF07811 but extends coverage to include Rv3655c from Mycobacterium tuberculosis and related species. Rv3655c belongs to a cassette that produces an Flp-like type IV pilus structure, and has been ascribed an ability to suppress macrophage apoptosis.

label: ArsI_CadI_VOC
product_name: ArsI/CadI family heavy metal resistance metalloenzyme
hmm_name: ArsI/CadI family heavy metal resistance metalloenzyme
comment: This family belong to the broader VOC (Vicinal Oxygen Chelate) domain family (see PF00903), which includes glyoxalase I, fosfomycin resistance proteins FosA and FosB, and dioxygenases such as 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase. Members of this specific family include none of those, but instead include CadI from Mycobacterium tuberculosis and ArsI from Bacillus sp. MD1. They have an invariant CC motif at about position 95, and have poorly conserved C-terminal extension regions that nearly always contain at least one addition CC motif, often several. ArsI has been characterized as an organoarsenical lyase.

label: CC_star_Cory
comment: Members of this family have the CC-star motif (Cys-Cys-COOH), that is, a pair of Cys residues as the final two residues. A founding member is WP_085549354.1 from Corynebacterium pollutisoli. Members of this family typical are encoded next to an ArsA family ATPase (e.g. WP_085549353.1), suggesting a role in heavy metal metabolism, and predicted carbon starvation protein A (e.g. WP_085549355.1).

label: TfpZ
product_name: TfpX/TfpZ family type IV pilin accessory protein
hmm_name: TfpX/TfpZ family type IV pilin accessory protein

label: C_hydro_YcaC
comment: YcaC is a well-conserved cysteine hydrolase of unknown function, found in both Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli K-12, with an isochorismate family crystal structure.

label: phage_reg_YmfL
hmm_name: YmfL family putative phage regulatory protein
comment: Members of this family are homologs of the e14 prophage region protein YmfL from Escherichia coli K-12. Distant homology to phage regulatory protein CII, as described by Pfam model PF06892, suggests a similar function.

label: formate_DH_Act
comment: Members of this family are the enzyme formate dehydrogenase, of a type found in the Actinomycetota, as in the genera Streptomyces, Nocardiopsis, Gordonia, and Saccharomonospora. Many are selenoproteins.

label: GspC_delta
product_name: type II secretion system protein GspC
hmm_name: type II secretion system protein GspC, deltaproteobacterial-type
comment: Members of this family are GspC (general secretion protein C), a component of type II secretion systems (T2SS), of a form found prmarily in deltaproteobacteria. This HMM is designed to be complementary to other HMMs that identify GspC rather that to separate a distinct subtype.

label: PA2928_fam
comment: This family is named for the locus PA2928 of Pseudomonas aeroginosa PAO1, as the family member most frequently cited in the literature, although PA2928 itself is significantly shorter at the N-terminus than most other members of this family, and is probably non-functional. WP_017001489.1 represents an intact equivalent to the PA2928 pseudogene.

label: bluetail
comment: Bluetail is a short protein domain, about 55 amino acids long, found primarily in Cyanobacteria (blue), at the extreme C-terminus of proteins (tail), that otherwise may differ in length and domain content. This pattern of occurrence suggests a role in anchoring proteins on the cell surface, although bluetail does not have the tripartide structure of signature motif, then transmembrane alpha helix, then cluster of Arg residues like the sorting domains PEP-CTERM, Gly-Gly-CTERM, MYXO-CTERM, etc.

label: ArsM_DUF2284_UU
comment: Members of the seed alignment for this protein are selenoproteins with two selenocysteine-containing motifs. The first is in the N-terminal arsenite methyltransferase region, typically QUEGG, and the second is in a C-terminal DUF2284 domain, typically TUPSG.

label: fosX-Cc
comment: FosXCC (FosX from Campylobacter coli) is rare, mobile antimicrobial resistance protein. Most members of the family are seen not only outside of the genus Campylobacter, but in Gram-positive species such as C. difficile.

label: YlcI_YnfO_N
comment: The seed alignment of this HMM (86 proteins after non-redundification to a maximum 80 percent amino acid identity) represents are a large expansion relative to PF13132.9 (3 proteins), named DUF3950. Members are small bacterial proteins, often from prophage regions. This model is short (42 amino acids), which high sequence diversity among seed members, and has relatively high cutoffs for its length. Some family members and additional apparent homologs scoring below the current cutoffs of the model include putative DNA-binding proteins such as HicB family antitoxin components of type II toxin-antitoxin systems.

label: CBO2463_dom
comment: This domain occurs in proteins encoded typically between known subunits of the selenocysteine-containing D-proline reductase complex, a key contributor to Stickland metabolism. In Stickland metabolism, amino acids proline or glycine, or certain other compounds such as betaine or sarcosine, can be reduced, enabling energy-generating oxidation of various substrates such as other amino acids. Some members of this protein family have two copies of this domain.

label: T6SS_Burk_ExIF
product_name: putative type VI secretion system effector
hmm_name: putative type VI secretion system effector, ExIF family
comment: Members of this family are found typically in type VI secretion system (T6SS) regions of Burkholderia, Paraburkholderia, Acinetobacter, and related lineages, and may be effector proteins. The family is provisionally named ExIF after a motif well conserved across most family members.

label: Jag_EloR
comment: Members of this family are nucleic acid-binding proteins (RNA or single-stranded DNA) with a KH domain at the N-terminus, an R3H domain at the C-terminus, and additional regions of homology. The founding member of this family was JAG (spoIIIJ Associated Gene) from Bacillus subtilis, but later work in other lineages, such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, as established a role in controlling cell elongation and the operation of the elongasome. The S. pneumoniae protein, a protein that undergoes regulatory phosphorylation and dephosphorylation, is also called RNA-binding cell elongation regulator EloR, and also KhpB.

label: malolactic
comment: Malolactic enzyme converts L-malate anaerobically to L-lactate and carbon dioxide.

label: CxxC_VVA0879
comment: Members of this rare but broadly distributed family average about 120 amino acids in length, including an apparent redox-active disulfide motif CxxC and two other invariant Cys residues. The family is named for VVA0879 from Vibrio vulnificus but occurs also in Gram-positive species such as Clostridium botulinum.

label: MXAN_5187_C_dom
comment: This domain occurs at the C-terminus of MXAN_5187 from Myxococcus xanthus. Member proteins, most of which belong to Myxococcales branch of the Deltaproteobacteria, can have very different architectures outside of this domain.

label: trifunc_aldol
comment: The N-terminal region of this protein resembles the bifunctional KHG/KDPG aldolase (4.1.2.14 and 4.1.3.16), while the C-terminal region resembles 2-dehydro-3-deoxygluconokinase and 2-dehydro-3-deoxygalactonokinase.

label: RAxF_45
comment: Members of this family of small proteins are found broadly within the order Bacillales. The family is named for its best conserved motif, a nearly invariant RAxF motif, and its small size, about 45 amino acids in length.

label: prot_kin_PA4780
comment: Members of this family are putative serine/threonine-protein kinases, closely related to founding member PA4780 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1, which was shown to be upregulated by and important for the biodegradation of phenanthrene and naphthalene. Members belong more generally to the RIO1 atypical kinase family (see PF01163).

label: ABC_perm_CPBP
product_name: ABC transporter permease subunit/CPBP intramembrane protease
hmm_name: ABC transporter permease subunit/CPBP intramembrane protease
comment: The C-terminal region of this ABC transporter permease contains a CPBP family glutamic-type intramembrane protease domain, related to the eukaryotic type 2 CAAX prenyl protease Rce1.

label: peri_hyde_PaoC
comment: PaoC is the molybdopterin-cytosine-dinucleotide cofactor-binding subunit of the periplasmic aldehyde oxidoreductase PaoABC. The enzyme is known formally as carboxylate reductase (EC 1.2.99.6).

label: transp_NF041680
comment: Members of this family are uncharacterized mobilome proteins homologous to IS4-like and IS701-like element transposases, and likely to be transposases themselves. Many members of this family are recognized by Pfam model PF13546 (DDE superfamily endonuclease).

label: HGxxPAAW
comment: Members of this uncharacterized protein family occur in the taxonomic class Actinomycetes, are hydrophobic over most of their lengths, which averages about 94 amino acids, and are named for the best conserved motif, HGxxPAAW, located near the N-terminus.

label: RIPP_cyclo_YhhA
comment: Members of this family are triceptide-type riibosomally translated, post-translationally modified peptide natural products (RiPPs). Maturation begins with a cyclophane-forming cyclization in the YxRxHxRHxR motif of the core region by a radical SAM/SPASM enzyme, called YhhB, followed by hydroxylation by a 2OG-Fe(II) oxygenase called YhhC. triceptide-type peptide natural product; maturases include a radical SAM/SPASM enzyme and a 2OG-Fe(II) oxygenase

label: 2OG_matur_YhhC

The enzyme introduces cyclophane formation. The peptide modifications also include hydroxylation by a 2OG-Fe(II) oxygenase called YhhC. Many YhhB proteins contain an additional metallopeptidase-like C-terminal extension.

label: rSAM_phane_AMC

hmm_name: cyclophane-forming radical SAM peptide maturase AmcB
comment: AmcB (Actinobacterial multiple cyclophane B) is a cyclophane-forming radical SAM peptide maturase. Peptides modified by this enzyme contain multiple three-residue motifs in which the first amino acid is Trp or Phe, an aromatic residue. Crosslinking of the side chain to the third residue in the motif creates a strained cyclophane moiety. Peptides with this type of three residue cyclophane are called triceptides

EstT belongs to the larger family of alpha/beta-fold hydrolases. Members of this family are regularly found in the context of other antimicrobial resistance proteins, such as in the tet(X4)-bearing plasmid p47EC of E. coli 47EC (see PMID: 31133751). Some members of this family may have two alternative start sites, the shorter form likely cytosolic, the N-terminally extended form about 24 amino acids longer and containing an apparent lipoprotein signal peptide.

Some members of family NF041762 have an extension with this motif while others do not. Twelve otherwise unrelated proteins in Desulfatibacillum aliphaticivorans strain AK-01 (CP001322.1) share the motif at or close to the C-terminal. The Cys-aliphatic-aliphatic CFI motif suggests processing by a CPBP-family glutamic intramembrane endopeptidase, as is the case with Rce1 cleavage of the CAAX box in eukaryotes, but this has not yet been established.

Sequential motifications to create the Dmp are catalyzed by a an oxidative decarboxylase, an aminotransferase, and a methyltransferase. The founding member of this family, from Microbacterium paraoxydans DSM 15019 (mpa), is designated MpaA1.
