label: HetE-N
comment: This entry corresponds to a domain found at the N-terminus of fungal Heteroincompatibility HetE proteins and in biological conflict systems of bacteria (PMID: 34061031). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6825
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in plants and cyanobacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 108 and 202 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6829
comment: This family is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is around 420 amino acids in length. Structurally, this family is made of alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: Caudo_bapla_N
product_name: Lactophage receptor-binding protein N-terminal shoulder domain
name_orig: Lactophage receptor-binding protein N-terminal shoulder domain
hmm_name: Lactophage receptor-binding protein N-terminal shoulder domain
comment: Caudo_bapla_RBP is a family of proteins expressed from ORF18 of the Lactococcus P2-like phage. This is one of three protein domain, shoulder, neck, and head, that form the phage tail base-plate. This entry represents the shoulder domain. This domain contains a beta sandwich fold (PMID: 20351260). (from Pfam)

label: RecJ_C_Deinoc
comment: This domain is found at the C terminus of Single-stranded-DNA- specific exonuclease RecJ from Deinococci. This protein has four domains that form a molecule with an O-like structure (PMID: 20129927). The fourth domain (this entry) binds the C-terminal region of Single-stranded DNA-binding protein (Pfam:PF00436) to efficiently process broken DNA ends for homologous recombination (PMID: 27058167). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6558_C
comment: This family includes uncharacterised proteins from Firmicutes and phages, some members are phage tail-related proteins. Included in this entry is the prophage-derived protein YomH from Bacillus subtilis (swiss:O31977). (from Pfam)

label: MACPF_D2
comment: This domain is found in proteins of the membrane-attack complex/ perforin (MACPF) family from Bacteroidetes. These transmembrane pore- forming proteins are organized into three structured domains: an MACPF domain (Pfam:PF01823) and two C-terminal domains, D2 and D3. This entry represents the D2 domain, which adopts an alpha/beta fold (PMID: 20944225). (from Pfam)

label: RNase_E_G_Thio
comment: Both RNase E and its homologue RNase G are endoribonucleases that play central roles in RNA processing. RNase E shows two globular domains. This entry represents the smaller domain, which shows a thioredoxin-like fold [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6843
comment: This protein family includes Putative lipoprotein BA_2398 from Bacillus anthracis and similar proteins from bacteria, predominantly Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes. (from Pfam)

label: GP7
comment: This family represents Major capsid protein GP7 from Salmonella phage epsilon15 and similar proteins found in tailed bacteriophages and bacterial prophages. GP7 adopts a canonical phage structure, showing different structural features (an N-arm, an F-loop, an E-loop, a P-domain, a long alpha-helix, an A-domain and the C-terminal end) (PMID: 23840063). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6847
comment: This family represents bacterial uncharacterised proteins such as Uncharacterized conserved protein Dip1984 from Corynebacterium diphtheriae, which shows an all-alpha structure. Some members of this family are annotated as septicolysin, such as Swiss:H6NMB2, a cholesterol-dependent pore-forming cytolysin that acts to facilitate the infection of certain pathogenic gram-positive bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: Caud_bapl16_2nd
product_name: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein N0 domain
name_orig: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein N0 domain
hmm_name: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein N0 domain
comment: Caudo_bapla16 is a family of ORF16 tail-phage P2-like proteins that forms part of the base-plate at the tip of the phage tail. The whole base-plate complex is involved in host recognition and attachment, and consists of several proteins derived from consecutive open-reading-frames. This entry represents the N0 domain (PMID: 20351260). (from Pfam)

label: DUF4931_C
name_orig: Domain of unknown function (DUF4931) C-terminal domain
comment: This family consists of uncharacterized proteins around 270 residues in length and is mainly found in various Bacillus cereus species. Some members of this family are annotated as Galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferases, but the specific function of this family is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_p2_ORF12
comment: ORF12 from Lactococcus lactis phage p2 is thought to be a chaperone for the tape measure protein that might help to maintain the tape measure protein in solution during tail assembly. This late- expressed protein shows an all-alpha structure with five alpha- helices oriented to form a hydrophobic cleft on the inner surface of the protein. It adopts a trimeric assembly, forming long spirals (PMID: 19047351). (from Pfam)

label: MASE11
comment: This entry represents the membrane-associated sensor domain 11 (MASE11), a predicted transmembrane domain that has been found in association with HD-GYP (Pfam:PF01966), PAS (Pfam:PF13426), GAF (Pfam:PF01590) and GGDEF (Pfam:PF00990)-EAL (Pfam:PF00563) domains. It is also present in sensor histidine kinases with various domain architectures (PMID: 34928179). (from Pfam)

label: I-TevI_DNA-bd
comment: This domain is found in Intron-encoded endonuclease 1 (I-TevI) from Bacteriophage T4. I-TevI is a site-specific endonuclease that belongs to the GIY-YIG family that shows a catalytic domain (Pfam:PF01541) and a DNA-binding domain (this entry), which is organised into three DNA recognition subdomains: a Zn finger, an elongated subdomain that includes a minor groove-binding alpha- helix and a helix-turn-helix subdomain (PMID: 11447104). (from Pfam)

label: YqiJ_N
comment: This entry represents a presumed helical domain found at the N-terminal of several bacterial proteins, including the inner membrane protein YqiJ from E. coli, whose function is not clear. (from Pfam)

label: HA2_C
comment: The helicase associated domain (HA2) has an all alpha-helical fold and consists of a N-terminal winged-helix (WH) domain (Pfam:PF04408) and a C-terminal degenerate helical-bundle domain, referred to as the ratchet-like domain [1,2,3]. These domains collaborate with the RecA domains at the N-terminal in completing an RNA binding channel to allow the helicases to keep a stable grip on the RNA (PMID: 32179686). This entry represents the ratchet-like domain, which may be important for RNA translocation [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: BipA_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the TypA/BipA protein. The C-terminal domain of BipA, consisting of residues, forms a unique motif with two crossed beta sheets (comprising of two and four beta-strands, respectively) wrapped by three short alpha helices forming a nearly equilateral triangle (PMID: 26163516). (from Pfam)

label: EryCIII-like_N
product_name: Erythromycin biosynthesis protein CIII-like, N-terminal domain
name_orig: Erythromycin biosynthesis protein CIII-like, N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Erythromycin biosynthesis protein CIII-like, N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal of Erythromycin biosynthesis protein CIII (EryCIII) from Saccharopolyspora erythraea and similar proteins predominantly found in Actinobacteria and Enterobacterales. This protein is organised into two domains, both of them with a Rossmann-like alpha/beta fold. The N-terminal domain contains acceptor binding site (PMID: 22056329). (from Pfam)

label: GDH_ACT3
comment: Glutamate dehydrogenases (GDHs) are a broadly distributed group of enzymes that catalyse the reversible oxidative deamination of glutamate to ketoglutarate and ammonia (PMID: 10924516). The structure of GDH from Mycobacterium smegmatis revealed that it has a long N- and C-terminal segments flanking the catalytic core, comprising several domains. The flexible N-terminal domain comprises three ACT-like (ACT1-3) and PAS-type domains which could act as metabolic sensors for allosteric regulation (PMID: 34083757). This entry represents ACT3 domain. (from Pfam)

label: P-loop_SecA
hmm_name: preprotein translocase subunit SecA P-loop domain
comment: SecA is the preprotein translocase ATPase subunit and a superfamily 2 (SF2) RNA helicase (PMID: 17229438). This entry corresponds to the second P-loop domain. (from Pfam)

label: CDI_toxin_EC869_like
comment: Contact-dependent growth inhibition (CDI) systems encode polymorphic toxin/immunity proteins that mediate competition between neighbouring bacterial cells (PMID: 23236156). Despite sharing little sequence identity, the toxin domains are structurally similar and have homology to endonucleases. The EC869 toxin is a Zn(2+)-dependent DNase capable of completely degrading the genomes of target cells (PMID: 23236156). (from Pfam)

label: CsgH
comment: CsgH is a Curli-like protein found in proteobacteria and Bacteroidetes (PMID: 27098162). These proteins adopt a seven stranded beta sandwich fold (PMID: 27098162). CsgH is a functional homologue of CsgC and is a potent inhibitor of CsgA amyloid formation (PMID: 27098162). (from Pfam)

label: DDR1-2_DS-like
comment: Discoidin domain-containing receptor 1/2 (DDR1/2) are receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) whose activating ligands are various collagens [1,2] and consist of extracellular domains comprising the N-terminal discoidin domain (DS, Pfam:PF00754) followed by a DS-like domain and the cytoplasmic kinase domain (Pfam:PF07714) [1,2]. Impairment in signaling by DDR1 and DDR2 is associated with the progression of various human diseases, including fibrosis, atherosclerosis and cancer, therefore, inhibition of signaling using monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) may be an useful therapy. This entry represents the DS-like domain, which mediates binding to triple-helical collagen together with the DS domain and contains the epitopes of all mAbs (PMID: 30612951). (from Pfam)

label: TibC_1st
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Glycosyltransferase TibC from Escherichia coli and similar bacterial. TibC is an autotransporter adhesin heptosyltransferase (AAH) homologue that catalyses the heptosylation of the autotransporters AIDA-I/TibA and confers AIDA-I-mediated bacterial adhesion to host cells. This domain adopts a beta-barrel fold with two four-stranded sheets that pack against each other [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: MFD_D3
comment: The transcription-repair coupling factor (TRCF, also known as MFD) couples transcription and DNA repair in bacteria. MFD removes transcription elongation complexes stalled at DNA lesions and recruits the nucleotide excision repair (NER) machinery to the site (PMID: 33480355). This protein consists of eight domains [3,4], of which D3 is represented in this entry and its function is unknown. This domain plays a critical role in unmasking of the UvrA binding site (PMID: 33480355). (from Pfam)

label: FkbO_Hyg5-like_N
comment: This domain is found in the N-terminal region of Chorismatase from (FkbO) and 3-hydroxybenzoate synthase (Hyg5) from Streptomyces hygroscopicus and in similar bacterial proteins. These enzymes catalyse the hydrolysis of chorismate into pyruvate and (dihydro)benzoic acid derivatives and are involved in the biosynthetic pathways forming polyketidic immunosuppressants such as ascomycin (FK520) and tacrolimus (FK506), which prevent T-cell proliferation through initial binding to the immunophilin FKBP12. FkbO is organised into three domains: N-terminal, central and C-terminal. This entry represents the N-terminal and central domains of FkbO, which show two beta-sheets and three alpha-helices. This fold is also found in Hyg5, which employ a fundamentally different reaction mechanism than the typical hydrolysis seen in FkbO [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: RecR_C
comment: The bacterial protein RecR is an important regulator in the RecFOR homologous recombination pathway during DNA repair. It acts with RecF and RecO forming a complex that facilitates the loading of RecA onto ssDNA. RecR is a zinc metalloprotein consisting of a N-terminal helix-hairpin-helix (HhH) motif, a middle region containing a zinc finger motif (Pfam:PF02132) and a Toprim domain (Pfam:PF13662), and a C-terminal domain comprising a Walker B motif and a C-terminal helix [1,2]. This is the C-terminal domain of RecR, which has a divergent Walker B motif, suggesting a nucleotide binding site [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: TadZ-like_ARD
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal of TadZ from Eubacterium rectale and similar bacterial proteins. TadZ is is an essential component of the Tad secretion system that probably functions as a localization factor. This protein is composed of two domains, both of which have lost its active sites. This entry represents the N-terminal atypical receiver domain (ARD), which is structurally similar to the RD of response regulators such as the chemotaxis protein CheY (PMID: 22211578). (from Pfam)

label: PcrA_UvrD_tudor
comment: The PcrA/UvrD helicase binds directly to RNA polymerase (RNAP). This entry represents the C-terminal tudor domain that mediates interaction with RNA polymerase [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: TetR_C_5-like
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Transcriptional regulator, TetR family from Thermotoga maritima (TM_1030) and similar sequences from bacteria. TM_1030 shows high similarity to members of the TetR family at the N-terminal DNA-binding domain (Pfam:PF00440). However, differences are much greater in the C-terminal regulatory domain, which shows an all-helical structure [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Helic-prim_T7_N
product_name: Bacteriophage T7 DNA helicase/primase, N-terminal a+b fold
name_orig: Bacteriophage T7 DNA helicase/primase, N-terminal a+b fold
hmm_name: Bacteriophage T7 DNA helicase/primase, N-terminal a+b fold
comment: Bacteriophage T7 DNA helicase/primase (also known as Gp4) is an ATP-dependent DNA helicase and primase that is essential for viral DNA replication and recombination [1-4]. Primase activity synthesises short RNA primers at the sequence 5'-GTC-3' on the lagging strand that the polymerase elongates using dNTPs and providing the primase is still present. It consists of an N-terminal zinc ribbon (Pfam:PF08273) followed by a RNA Polymerase Domain that can be subdivided in an N-terminal alpha+beta structure, represented in this entry and a C-terminal TOPRIM fold (Pfam:PF13155) (PMID: 12769857). At the C-terminal end of the protein there is a DNA helicase domain (Pfam:PF03796). (from Pfam)

label: Bact_transglu_N_2
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of transglutaminases and similar sequences from bacteria. This domain is often found associated to Pfam:PF01841. Its structure resembles that of Pfam:PF08379. (from Pfam)

label: EthR_C
comment: HTH-type transcriptional regulator EthR is involved in the repression of the monooxygenase EthA which is responsible of the formation of the active metabolite of ethionamide (ETH). It is responsible for the low sensitivity of the human pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis to ethionamide. It consists of a DNA-binding HTH domain at the N-terminal and a C-terminal helical domain that binds its ligand [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: TetR_C_41
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of transcriptional regulators of the TetR family, including Swiss:O53623 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Swiss:Q1D4I5 from Myxococcus xanthus. This is the all-helical ligand-binding domain, which interacts with the respective effector molecule and transmits the signal to the DNA binding domain (Pfam:PF00440). (from Pfam)

label: Gp6-like_1st
product_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp6-like, helical domain
name_orig: Baseplate wedge protein gp6-like, helical domain
hmm_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp6-like, helical domain
comment: This domain is found in Baseplate wedge protein gp6 from Enterobacteria phage T4 and similar sequences predominantly from tailed bacteriophages. Gp6 is a protein involved in tail assembly. This entry represents its N-terminal helical domain (PMID: 26929357). (from Pfam)

label: Gp6_C-I
product_name: Baseplate structural protein gp6, C-terminal domain I
name_orig: Baseplate structural protein gp6, C-terminal domain I
hmm_name: Baseplate structural protein gp6, C-terminal domain I
comment: Baseplate structural protein gp6 is located next to the tail tube and is an intermediate (or inner) baseplate protein involved in tail assembly. Two molecules of gp6 form a complex with gp25 and gp7 which is involved sheath contraction [1-3]. This domain has been described as C-terminal domain I, and adopts a 2-layer beta-sandwich fold. (from Pfam)

label: tyr_de_CO2_C
comment: This is the C-terminal (or small) domain of tyrosine decarboxylase from Enterococcus faecalis and related species [1,2]. These are PLP-dependent decarboxylases that catalyse tyrosine decarboxylation to produce tyramine. This domain may play a regulatory role. (from Pfam)

label: LinB-like_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Lincosamide nucleotidyltransferase from Enterococcus faecium (LinB) and similar proteins from bacteria. LinB catalyses adenylylation of the lincosamide class of antibiotics. This domain folds into an alpha-helical bundle, which consists of five alpha-helices (PMID: 20004168). (from Pfam)

label: Tautomerase-like
comment: This protein family includes Swiss:A9W9V0 from Chloroflexus aurantiacus (Caur_1358), a 4-Oxalocrotonate tautomerase (4-OT). This protein adopts a beta-alpha-beta scaffold and forms part of a functional heterohexamer 4-OT (hh4-OT) that contains three heterodimer units, each composed of one alpha-subunit (Pfam:PF01361) and one beta-subunit (this entry) (PMID: 20465238). (from Pfam)

label: Col-Pyo_DNase
comment: This entry represents the DNAse domain from colicin/pyocin bacteriocins, such as pyocin-S2 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and colicin E7/E9 from E. coli. This domain has an alpha/beta fold containing a Zn2+ ion binding site [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: G3P_pilus-bind
comment: Attachment protein G3P from filamentous phages plays essential roles both in the penetration of the viral genome into the bacterial host via pilus retraction and in the extrusion process. In the initial stages of infection, G3P mediates adsorption of the phage to its primary receptor, the tip of host F-pilus. Subsequent interaction with the host entry receptor tolA induces penetration of the viral DNA into the host cytoplasm (PMID: 22591114). This entry represents the N-terminal (N1) pilus-binding domain from Salmonella phage IKe and Enterobacteria phage I2-2 GP3. It clamps together with the adjacent N2 domain (referred to as TolA binding domain in (PMID: 22591114)) by the hinge region to form a bilobal, horseshoe-like structure. (from Pfam)

label: PaaA-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of PaaA from Enterobacter agglomerans, an enzyme involved in post-translational modification and host immunity. PaaA is composed of two domains: Pfam:PF00899 and the domains represented by this entry, which folds into a globular domain and has similarity to RiPP precursor peptide recognition elements or RREs (PMID: 27088303). (from Pfam)

label: YqeH-like_C
comment: This entry is found at the C-terminal of Nitric oxide-associated protein 1 (NOA1) from animals and rice, BPG2 from Arabidopsis and YqeH from B. subtilis. YqeH is an orthologue of NOA1. This domain has a beta-sandwich structure with homology to the RNA-binding regulator TRAP, and the hypoxia factor pVHL. The residues for RNA recognition in TRAP are conserved in members of this entry, suggesting that these are G-proteins that may regulate nucleic acid recognition (PMID: 18801747). (from Pfam)

label: Tailspike_C
comment: Tailspike protein from Shigella phage Sf6 specifically mediates the attachment to their hosts. Its structure revealed a conserved architecture with a central, right-handed beta-helix. The C-terminal domain adopts a beta-sandwich fold, is represented in this entry, and is reminiscent of viral capsid proteins [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Pept_S41_N_bact
product_name: Bacteroidetes, Peptidase, S41 family, N-terminal domain
name_orig: Bacteroidetes, Peptidase, S41 family, N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Bacteroidetes, Peptidase, S41 family, N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Peptidase, S41 family Bacteroides uniformis and similar proteins from bacteroidetes. It is found associated with Pfam:PF03572 and shows an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: TetR_C_43
hmm_name: SbtR family transcriptional regulator C-terminal domain
comment: Members of this family are TetR family transcriptional regulators, based on the N-terminal DNA-binding domain, but share this additional C-terminal domain with SbtR from Thermus thermophilus, OxiR (Rv0067c) from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and SCO0520 from Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2).

label: CRLF2-like_D2
comment: CRLF2 is a receptor for thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP). It forms a functional complex with TSLP and IL7R which is capable of stimulating cell proliferation through activation of STAT3 and STAT5. CRFL2 is implicated in the development of the hematopoietic system (PMID: 28368013). It consists of two FnIII-like domains, D1 and D2. This entry represents the membrane-proximal D2 domain, which displays a an ABE/C'CFG topology with two disulfide bridges (PMID: 28368013). This domain interacts with IL7R D2 domain and forms a compact network of interactions (PMID: 28368013). This domain is also found in the cytokine receptor common subunit gamma (IL2RG), a common subunit for the receptors for a variety of interleukins [2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: vRNAP_plug
product_name: Virion DNA-directed RNA polymerase, plug insertion
name_orig: Virion DNA-directed RNA polymerase, plug insertion
hmm_name: Virion DNA-directed RNA polymerase, plug insertion
comment: This domain is found in Virion DNA-directed RNA polymerase from Bacteriophage N4 (vRNAP), responsible for the transcription of the early region of the double-stranded linear DNA genome of the lytic coliphage. This entry represents a short insertion that forms a globular module named plug, which blocks the activity of the protein [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6856
comment: This entry includes a set of mycoplasma lipoproteins related to uncharacterized Mycoplasma genitalium lipoprotein MG348. (from Pfam)

label: DNA_pol3_delta_C
product_name: DNA polymerase III delta subunit, C-terminal domain
name_orig: DNA polymerase III delta subunit, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: DNA polymerase III delta subunit, C-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the delta subunit from the clamp-loader complex of Bacillus subtilis and other Gram-positive bacteria, which is structurally similar to that of the DNApol3 delta subunit from E.coli [1-3]. This domain interacts with other subunits in the complex (tau and delta') and the nature of these interactions appear to be hydrophilic in contrast with the one observed in Gram-negative bacteria (PMID: 23525462). (from Pfam)

label: Ppx_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Exopolyphosphatase from Agrobacterium fabrum (Ppx) and similar proteins mainly found in alphaproteobacteria. This domain is usually found associated with Pfam:PF02541. (from Pfam)

label: dnstrm_HI1420
comment: This entry represents a helix-turn-helix domain that is found in the HI1420 protein. Members of this strictly bacterial protein family are small, at roughly 100 amino acids. The gene is almost invariably the downstream member of a gene pair. It is a predicted helix-turn-helix DNA-binding protein. These gene pairs, when found on the bacterial chromosome, are located often with prophage regions, but also both in integrated plasmid regions and in housekeeping gene regions. Analysis suggests that the gene pair may serve as an addiction module. (from Pfam)

label: T7SS_signal
comment: This alpha helical domain is likely to mediate secretion via a type VII secretion system due to similarity to Pfam:PF06013. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6869
comment: This short family of bacterial proteins contains a potential alpha helical solenoid structure. The function of these proteins is unknown. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Proteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: YpoC
comment: This family of proteins contains the B. subtilis YpoC protein Swiss:P39789. It is largely confined to bacilli bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6870
comment: This entry represents a small bacterial protein o unknown function. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Firmicutes. (from Pfam)

label: DEDDh_C
product_name: DNA polymerase III subunit epsilon-like, C-terminal domain
name_orig: DNA polymerase III subunit epsilon-like, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: DNA polymerase III subunit epsilon-like, C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of QDE-2-interacting protein from Neurospora crassa, DNA polymerase III subunit epsilon from Treponema pallidum (DnaQ) and similar fungal proteins that belong to the DnaQ-like (or DEDDh) exonuclease superfamily. These proteins catalyze the excision of nucleoside monophosphates at the DNA or RNA termini in the 3'-5' direction. Most DEDDh exonucleases are the proofreading subunits (epsilon) or domains of bacterial DNA polymerase III, the main replicating enzyme in bacteria, which functions as the chromosomal replicase. This domain shows an alpha -beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: MgtC_SapB_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminus of proteins that are members of MGTC/SAPB family. It adopts a ferredoxin-like fold and has a significant structural similarity to ACT-like domains. In contrast to the canonical ACT-like domains, this domain doesn't dimerize or bind to small molecules. It is probably involved in protein-protein interactions (PMID: 22984256). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6875
comment: This entry represents family of uncharacterised proteins. They share an N-terminal CPF/Y motif that is characteristic of the NCPF superfamily of proteins. (from Pfam)

label: Bflower_2
comment: This family of proteins have a repetitive structure composed of pairs of beta strands. In this family the proteins usually have five copies of the beta hairpin repeat. (from Pfam)

label: Cas3-like_C
product_name: CRISPR-associated Cas3 subtype I-F/YPEST-like, C-terminal domain
name_orig: CRISPR-associated Cas3 subtype I-F/YPEST-like, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: CRISPR-associated Cas3 subtype I-F/YPEST-like, C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of CRISPR-associated nuclease/helicase Cas3 subtype I-F/YPEST from Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Cas3 contains an HD nuclease domain (Pfam:PF18019), RecA1, RecA2, a long linker region, and this C-terminal domain. This domain shows two alpha-helices and two six-stranded beta-blades [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Glyco_hydro_84_hel
comment: This is a helical domain found after the catalytic domain of enzymes from the Glycoside hydrolase family 84 from Bacteroides spp. and certain pathogenic Clostridia spp [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6809
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. Proteins in this family are found in bacteria, are typically around 85 amino acids in length and have a conserved motif FxxGF. (from Pfam)

label: MSG_insertion
product_name: Malate synthase G, alpha-beta insertion domain
name_orig: Malate synthase G, alpha-beta insertion domain
hmm_name: Malate synthase G, alpha-beta insertion domain
comment: Malate synthase (MS) catalyses the aldol condensation of glyoxylate with acetyl-CoA to form malate as part of the second step of the glyoxylate bypass and an alternative to the tricarboxylic acid cycle in bacteria, fungi and plants. There have been identified two isoforms, A and G (MSA and MSG, respectively) that differ in size and is attributed to an inserted alpha/beta domain in MSG that may have regulatory function [1,2,3,4]. Members of the isoform G family are only found in bacteria. This entry represents the alpha/beta insertion domain from MSG, which buttressed one side of the TIM-barrel domain (PMID: 18714089). (from Pfam)

label: MS_C
comment: Malate synthase (MS) catalyses the aldol condensation of glyoxylate with acetyl-CoA to form malate as part of the second step of the glyoxylate bypass and an alternative to the tricarboxylic acid cycle in bacteria, fungi and plants. There have been identified two isoforms, A and G (MSA and MSG, respectively) that differ in size and is attributed to an inserted alpha/beta domain in MSG that may have regulatory function [1,2]. In malate synthases, the TIM beta/alpha-barrel fold and the C-terminal helical domain are well conserved and the cleft between them forms the active site [1,2,3,4]. This entry represents the C-terminal domain which consists of a five-helix 'plug' connected to the barrel by an extended loop and caps the active site. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6812
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. Proteins in this family are found in bacteria. There is a conserved RxxD sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: Sec10_N
comment: This entry contains the Sec10 component (approximately 650 residues long) of the eukaryotic exocyst complex, which mediates the tethering of post-Golgi secretory vesicles to the plasma membrane and promotes the assembly of the SNARE complex for membrane fusion. It is also involved in cell polarisation, primary ciliogenesis, cytokinesis, pathogen invasion, tumourigenesis and metastasis [1,2]. The exocyst is a member of the Complex Associated with Tethering Containing Helical Rods (CATCHRs) which also includes DSL1, COG and GARP complexes, evolutionary related. They share structural features comprising alpha-helical bundles towards the C-terminal and coiled-coil regions at the N-terminal. This entry represents the N-terminal coiled-coil region (also referred to as CorEx motif) of Sec10 and its homologues from animals ECOC5 (Exocyst complex component 5), which participates in the central pair-wise interactions by forming an intact antiparallel 'zipper' which Sec15 subunit. Sec10-Sec15 CorEx motifs interact with Exo70-Exo84 dimers and form a four-helical bundle (PMID: 29335562). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6815
comment: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised and is found in bacteria and eukaryotes. It may contain an ATP-grasp-like fold which suggest an ATP-binding function. There are several conserved motifs: EGxxR, PxxWxxDF and ExNCSCV. (from Pfam)

label: CsoSCA_cat
product_name: Carboxysome Shell Carbonic Anhydrase, catalytic domain
name_orig: Carboxysome Shell Carbonic Anhydrase, catalytic domain
hmm_name: Carboxysome Shell Carbonic Anhydrase, catalytic domain
comment: Carboxysome Shell Carbonic Anhydrase is a bacterial carbonic anhydrase localised in the carboxysome, where it converts bicarbonate ions to carbon dioxide for use in carbon fixation. It contains three domains, these being: (1) an N-terminal domain composed primarily of four alpha-helices; (2) a catalytic domain containing a tightly bound zinc ion and (3) a C-terminal domain with weak structural similarity to the catalytic domain (PMID: 16407248). This entry represents the catalytic domain, consisting of a central five-stranded mixed beta-sheet with two helices flanking one side of the sheet and one helix flanking the other side (PMID: 16407248). (from Pfam)

label: TAGT
comment: This entry represents a Family 2/fringe-like glycosyltransferase domain that is found in DNA-modifying proteins of phages and eukaryotes (PMID: 23814188). The name TAGT is derived from phage versions that are operonic with TET/JBP-dioxygenases (PMID: 23814188). In kinetoplastids, the TAGT enzyme catalyses the second step in forming the hypermodified base J [1,2]. The vertebrate GREB1 protein appears to catalyse the O-GlcNAcylation of ERalpha, protecting it from ubiquitination-based degradation (PMID: 33731348). (from Pfam)

label: HTH_64
comment: This entry represents a DNA-binding helix-turn-helix domain found at the C-terminus of the DpiA transcriptional regulator protein. (from Pfam)

label: GKRP-like_C
product_name: C-terminal lid domain of glucokinase regulatory protein
name_orig: C-terminal lid domain of glucokinase regulatory protein
hmm_name: C-terminal lid domain of glucokinase regulatory protein
comment: This domain is found at the C terminus of Glucokinase regulatory protein (GKRP) from animals and N-acetylmuramic acid 6-phosphate etherase (MurQ) from bacteria. GKRP binds Glucokinase (GK) mainly through hydrophobic interactions, functioning as an allosteric switch in blood glucose control by the liver (PMID: 23733961). GKRP is trilobal in shape, consisting of two topologically identical sugar isomerase (SIS) domains (Pfam:PF01380 and Pfam:PF13580) capped by an alpha helical C-terminal domain (this entry). The Lid domain consists of a bundle of seven alpha helices with a core that shows a UBA-like fold (PMID: 23621087). MurQ, which also shows a SIS domain, plays a key role in the peptidoglycane recycling pathway. Its crystal structure shows each monomer have an alpha-beta-alpha sandwich fold commonly found in regulatory proteins controlling the expression of genes involved in the synthesis of phosphosugars. The C-terminal domain of this protein (this entry) is comprised of five alpha helices (PMID: 24226772). (from Pfam)

label: PAP_NTPase
comment: In eukaryotes, polyadenylation of pre-mRNA plays an essential role in the initiation step of protein synthesis, as well as in the export and stability of mRNAs. Poly(A) polymerase, the enzyme at the heart of the polyadenylation machinery, is a template-independent RNA polymerase which specifically incorporates ATP at the 3' end of mRNA (PMID: 10944102). The N-terminal catalytic domain of Poly(A) polymerase is a member of the nucleotidyltransferase superfamily (PMID: 10944102). (from Pfam)

label: Phage_tail_terminator_8
comment: This entry represents a family of likely phage tail terminator proteins which form a hexameric complex that joins the phage neck to the tail. (from Pfam)

label: YuA_Gp49
comment: This domain family includes proteins from tailed bacteriophages such as Pseudomonas phage YuA. Gp49 shows an alpha-beta fold. Its function is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: bPH_7
comment: This entry represents a group of bacterial PH domains that contain two transmembrane helices. The function of this family is uncertain, but they may act as antitoxins or as chaperones for membrane bound complexes. (from Pfam)

label: PDDEXK_13
comment: This entry contains a family of uncharacterised proteins. Structure prediction suggests it is likely to be an endonuclease enzyme related to the PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily. (from Pfam)

label: HepT-like_2
comment: This family of proteins are related to the HepT toxin-antitoxin system proteins Pfam:PF01934. This suggests that these proteins are ribonuclease toxins. (from Pfam)

label: DNA_pol_IIIA_C
product_name: DNA polymerase III subunit alpha, C-terminal domain
name_orig: DNA polymerase III subunit alpha, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: DNA polymerase III subunit alpha, C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of DNA polymerase III subunit alpha and similar proteins from Proteobacteria and Actinobacteria. This protein, which is the replicative DNA polymerase, consists of six domains that form an irregular pyramid around a central cavity. The C-terminal domain lies on top of this structure (PMID: 16959569). (from Pfam)

label: BscB_a-b
product_name: Cellulose Synthase Subunit B, alpha-beta domain
name_orig: Cellulose Synthase Subunit B, alpha-beta domain
hmm_name: Cellulose Synthase Subunit B, alpha-beta domain
comment: This domain is found in Cellulose Synthase Subunit B (BscB) from Cereibacter sphaeroides and similar sequences predominantly found in bacteria. BscB, involved in bacterial cellulose biosynthesis, is organized into two periplasmic carbohydrate binding domains (CBD-1/2, Pfam:PF03170) and two alpha/beta-domains with similarity with a flavodoxin-fold (FD1 and FD2) (PMID: 23222542). This entry represents FD2. (from Pfam)

label: SPOCS_spoVID-N
comment: This is the SPOCS (SpoVID-CotE-SipL) domain consisting of a beta-strand-rich sandwich fold with long twisted strands (PMID: 35065768) found at the N-terminal of Stage VI sporulation protein D (SpoVID) from Bacillus subtilis. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4785_3rd
name_orig: Domain of unknown function (DUF4785) C-terminal domain
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 392 and 442 amino acids in length. This entry represents the C-terminal immunoglobulin-like domain. (from Pfam)

label: Flu_PB2_1st
product_name: Influenza RNA polymerase PB2 N-terminal region
name_orig: Influenza RNA polymerase PB2 N-terminal region
hmm_name: Influenza RNA polymerase PB2 N-terminal region
comment: Influenza virus encodes a large, multidomain RNA-dependent RNA polymerase that can both transcribe and replicate the viral RNA genome. In influenza virus, the polymerase is composed of three polypeptides: PB1, PB2 and PA/P3. PB1 houses the polymerase active site, whereas PB2 and PA/P3 contain, respectively, cap-binding (PMID: 8806170) and endonuclease domains required for transcription initiation by cap-snatching (PMID: 26503046). This entry represents the N-terminal extended region of Flu PB2 protein, which is the N-terminal PB1 interaction domain. (from Pfam)

label: Flu_PB2_7th
product_name: Influenza RNA polymerase PB2 C-terminal domain
name_orig: Influenza RNA polymerase PB2 C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Influenza RNA polymerase PB2 C-terminal domain
comment: Influenza virus encodes a large, multidomain RNA-dependent RNA polymerase that can both transcribe and replicate the viral RNA genome. In influenza virus, the polymerase is composed of three polypeptides: PB1, PB2 and PA/P3. PB1 houses the polymerase active site, whereas PB2 and PA/P3 contain, respectively, cap-binding (PMID: 8806170) and endonuclease domains required for transcription initiation by cap-snatching (PMID: 26503046). This entry represents the C-terminal domain of Flu PB2 protein. (from Pfam)

label: Caud_bapl16_3rd
product_name: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein C-terminal insertion domain
name_orig: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein C-terminal insertion domain
hmm_name: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein C-terminal insertion domain
comment: Caudo_bapla16 is a family of ORF16 tail-phage P2-like proteins that forms part of the base-plate at the tip of the phage tail. The whole base-plate complex is involved in host recognition and attachment, and consists of several proteins derived from consecutive open-reading-frames. This entry represents the insertion domain found within the C-terminal RIFT barrel domain (PMID: 20351260). (from Pfam)

label: Caud_bapl16_4th
product_name: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein C-terminal barrel domain
name_orig: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein C-terminal barrel domain
hmm_name: Phage tail base-plate attachment protein C-terminal barrel domain
comment: Caudo_bapla16 is a family of ORF16 tail-phage P2-like proteins that forms part of the base-plate at the tip of the phage tail. The whole base-plate complex is involved in host recognition and attachment, and consists of several proteins derived from consecutive open-reading-frames. This entry represents the C-terminal RIFT barrel domain (PMID: 20351260). (from Pfam)

label: DnaX_C
product_name: DNA polymerase III subunit tau, C-terminal domain
name_orig: DNA polymerase III subunit tau, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: DNA polymerase III subunit tau, C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of the subunit tau of bacterial DNA polymerase III (DnaX). It binds to the C terminus of the alpha subunit of the same complex through its C-terminal helix and the adjacent loop (PMID: 23478062). (from Pfam)

label: MASE7
comment: This entry represents a predicted integral membrane sensor domain (MASE7) (PMID: 35311563), which is found in association with GGDEF domain (Pfam:PF00990), histidine sensor kinases and adenylate cyclase output domain (Pfam:PF00211). (from Pfam)

label: WDR54
comment: WDR54 has a regulatory effect on ERK signaling pathway activity in response to EGF stimulation, when is cross-linked to form dimers and trimers. It colocalizes with the EGF receptor in a WDR54-specific vesicle where it sustains the internalisation and controls the degradation of the EGF receptor after EGF stimulation (PMID: 30458214). (from Pfam)

label: ZSWIM1-3_RNaseH-like
product_name: Zinc finger SWIM domain-containing protein 1/3, RNaseH-like domain
name_orig: Zinc finger SWIM domain-containing protein 1/3, RNaseH-like domain
hmm_name: Zinc finger SWIM domain-containing protein 1/3, RNaseH-like domain
comment: This is a domain found at the N-terminal of Zinc finger SWIM domain-containing protein 1 and in the central region of ZSWIM3, whose function is not yet clear. ZSWIM1 may play a role in the development or function of T helper cells (PMID: 24508175). This domain may adopt an alpha-beta conformation according to AlphaFold structure predictions, closely related to RNaseH-like domains. (from Pfam)

label: GDH_HM1
comment: Glutamate dehydrogenases (GDHs) are a broadly distributed group of enzymes that catalyse the reversible oxidative deamination of glutamate to ketoglutarate and ammonia (PMID: 10924516). The structure of GDH from Mycobacterium smegmatis revealed that it has a long N- and C-terminal segments flanking the catalytic core, comprising several domains. The flexible N-terminal domain comprises ACT-like and PAS-type domains which could act as metabolic sensors for allosteric regulation (PMID: 34083757). It also has three helical motifs (HM1-3), this entry represents the first one (HM1). (from Pfam)

label: GDH_ACT2
comment: Glutamate dehydrogenases (GDHs) are a broadly distributed group of enzymes that catalyse the reversible oxidative deamination of glutamate to ketoglutarate and ammonia (PMID: 10924516). The structure of GDH from Mycobacterium smegmatis revealed that it has a long N- and C-terminal segments flanking the catalytic core, comprising several domains. The flexible N-terminal domain comprises thre ACT-like (ACT1-3) and PAS-type domains which could act as metabolic sensors for allosteric regulation (PMID: 34083757). This entry represents the ACT2 domain. (from Pfam)

label: PKS_DH_N
comment: This domain is part of a dehydratase domain found in diverse PKS enzymes. This domain adopts a HotDog fold. (from Pfam)

label: CarD_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal helical domain of CarD from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a RNAP-binding protein that regulates transcription and essential processes [1-3]. This domain binds DNA in a non-specific manner (PMID: 29973616). (from Pfam)

label: DyP_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal dimeric alpha beta barrel domain from the dye-decolorizing peroxidase (DyP)-type peroxidase family. This is one of the six families of peroxidases (PMID: 21569205). (from Pfam)

label: T4_UVSX_C
product_name: Bacteriophage T4, Recombination and repair protein, C-terminal domain
name_orig: Bacteriophage T4, Recombination and repair protein, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Bacteriophage T4, Recombination and repair protein, C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is mainly found in proteins from tailed bacteriophages, including Recombination and repair protein from Bacteriophage T4 (UVSX). This protein is organised into a larger N-terminal 'core' domain and a smaller C-terminal domain (this entry) with mainly alpha-helical structure (PMID: 21035462). (from Pfam)

label: T6PP_C
comment: This is the catalytic C-terminal domain of trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase from parasitic nematodes such as Brugia malayi. This domain adopts a C2B-type HAD phosphatase fold (PMID: 24992307). In C. elegans, T6PP is essential for survival due to the toxic effect(s) of the accumulation of trehalose 6-phosphate. (from Pfam)

label: A2M_bMG2
comment: Bacterial alpha-2 macroglobulin (A2M) are located in the periplasm and may protect the cell by trapping external proteases through a covalent interaction with an activated thioester [1,2]. Macroglobulin (MG) beta sandwich domains appear to play a structural role. This entry represents bacterial MG2 (bMG2) domain which, with MG1, plays the role of a linker associating the main body of A2M to the bilayer [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6852
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of BVU_3817 from Phocaeicola vulgatus (Swiss:A6L6W4) and similar proteins mostly found in Bacteroidetes. This domain shows an alpha/beta structure and is normally found associated with Pfam:PF18347. Its function is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Rep3_C
comment: This protein is an initiator of plasmid replication. RepB possesses nicking-closing (topoisomerase I) like activity. It is also able to perform a strand transfer reaction on ssDNA that contains its target. This family also includes RepA which is an E.coli protein involved in plasmid replication. The RepA protein binds to DNA repeats that flank the repA gene [1-3]. These proteins consist of two domains containing a winged helix-turn-helix motif: the N-terminal one, WH1, is involved in the dimerization of RepE and an auxiliary binding to DNA; the C-terminal one, WH2, represented in this entry, is related to a sequence-specific binding to the common 8 bp of the iteron [4,5]. (from Pfam)

label: Bac_rhamnosid-like_N
comment: This domain is found in a group of alpha-rhamnosidases predominantly from Bacteroidetes, including the putative alpha-rhamnosidase from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, whose structure shows similarity with a galactose-binding domain. (from Pfam)

label: RecQ-1-like_HTH
comment: This domain is found in a group of bacterial DNA helicases, including RecQ-1 from Porphyromonas gingivalis, which shows an all-helical structure (PMID: 26675735). This entry represents the helix-turn-helix (HTH) domain. (from Pfam)

label: Phosphatase-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal of a group of bacterial phosphatases and arsenate reductases, including Protein-tyrosine- phosphatase from Corynebacterium glutamicum. This domain, often found associated to Pfam:PF01451, forms a three-helical bundle that interacts with the active site of the other chain in the dimeric interface (PMID: 22032722). (from Pfam)

label: UvsW_N
comment: This is the small N-terminal alpha+beta domain of the DNA helicase UvsW from bacteriophage T4 [1,2], which consists of five beta-strands and two alpha-helices. This domain is structurally homologous to the DNA-binding domain of the T4 transcription factor MotA, thus, it likely binds the nucleic acid substrate [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Glyco_hydro_120_ins
comment: This insertion domain is found in a group of bacterial glycoside hydrolases from the CAZy family 120, including Parallel beta-helix repeat protein from Thermoanaerobacterium saccharolyticum (also known as xylosidase). It is often found associated to Pfam:PF13229. (from Pfam)

label: SOGP_4th
comment: Glycoside phosphorylases catalyze the phosphorolysis of oligosaccharides into sugar phosphates (PMID: 28198470). This domain is the C-terminal domain found in the L. phytofermentans SOGP (sophoro-oligosaccharide beta-1,2-gluco-phosphorylase) (PMID: 28198470). (from Pfam)

label: TetR_C_40
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of bacterial transcriptional regulators, including RolR from Corynebacterium glutamicum (Swiss:Q8NR95), which is involved in aromatic catabolism. This signal-receiving domain shows an all-alpha-helical fold. It is found associated with Pfam:PF00440, responsible for DNA-binding (PMID: 21559286). (from Pfam)

label: FAN1_HTH
comment: FAN1 is a DNA structure-specific nuclease involved in the processing of DNA interstrand crosslinks (ICLs). It maintains genomic stability and prevents tissue decline in several organs. This protein possesses preferential endonuclease activity toward 5' flap structures [1-5]. FAN1 is present in most eukaryotes and some bacterial sequences. It consists of four characterised domains: UBZ, SAP, TPR and VRR nuclease (Pfam:PF08774). However, monocellular eukaryote and bacterial homologues lack the UBZ domain (PMID: 25319828). The N-terminal helical domain of FAN1 can be subdivided in a winged-helix (WH) DNA-binding domain, represented in this entry, and a SAP domain (bacterial Pfam:PF18081 and eukaryotic Pfam:PF21169) [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: TRAF-mep_MATH
comment: Intracellular TRAFs and extracellular meprins share a conserved region of about 180 residues, the the meprin and TRAF homology (MATH) domain which adopts a beta-sandwich structure. This is the MATH domain of TNF receptor-associated factors (TRAFs) and meprins. In TRAFS, it is essential for self-association and receptor interaction [1-3]. Meprins are mammalian tissue-specific metalloendopeptidases involved developmental, normal and pathological processes. (from Pfam)

label: YceM-like_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Putative oxidoreductase YceM from Escherichia coli and similar bacterial sequences. It adopts an alpha-beta configuration. It is often associated with Pfam:PF01408. (from Pfam)

label: Cas3_I-F_Cas2
product_name: CRISPR-associated nuclease/helicase Cas3, I-F/YPEST, Cas2 domain
name_orig: CRISPR-associated nuclease/helicase Cas3, I-F/YPEST, Cas2 domain
hmm_name: CRISPR-associated nuclease/helicase Cas3, I-F/YPEST, Cas2 domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of CRISPR-associated nuclease/helicase Cas3 subtype I-F/YPEST from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and similar sequences predominantly found in proteobacteria. In the type I-F CRISPR-Cas system, Cas3 is fused with Cas2 at the N terminus. This entry represents the Cas2 domain of Cas3, which shows a four-stranded beta-sheet and two alpha-helices, in a structure that resembles that of Cas2 from the Escherichia coli. It appears N- terminal to the histidine-aspartate (HD)-type nuclease domain (Pfam:PF18019) [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DTP-pb9_A-dom_C

Domain A adopts a split barrel fold and includes residues 1 to 82-172 to 205. This entry covers the C-terminal region of the A domain (PMID: 24155371). (from Pfam)

Domain A adopts a split barrel fold and includes residues 1 to 82-172 to 205. This entry covers the N-terminal region of the A domain (PMID: 24155371). The C-terminal segment of the A domain is represented in Pfam:PF21424. (from Pfam)

label: Gp7_5th
product_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp7, domain V
name_orig: Baseplate wedge protein gp7, domain V

comment: This domain is found in Baseplate wedge protein gp7 from Bacteriophage T4 and similar proteins predominantly found in tailed bacteriophages. Gp7 provides the primary control of the conformational changes of the viral baseplate during assembly and infection. This protein is organised into six domains connected by flexible linkers. This entry represents Domain V, which is an insertion into domain IV and consists of an eight-stranded beta- barrel followed by two short alpha-helices (PMID: 26929357). (from Pfam)

label: Gp44_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Sliding-clamp-loader large subunit from Bacteriophage T4 (Gp44) and similar proteins predominantly found in tailed bacteriophages. Gp44 functions as an ATPase enzyme. It also contains an AAA module (Pfam:PF00004) [1,2]. (from Pfam)

name_orig: Distal tail protein pb9, B domain
hmm_name: Distal tail protein pb9, B domain
comment: This entry includes phage distal tail proteins which form a hexameric ring located at the tail tube end, such as pb9 from bacteriophage T5 (PMID: 24155371). pb9 consists of two domains, A and B. This entry represents domain B which adopts an OB fold and is inserted in domain A (PMID: 24155371). (from Pfam)

label: MenC_N
comment: MenC (o-succinylbenzoate synthase OSBS converts 2-succinyl-6-hydroxy-2,4-cyclohexadiene-1-carboxylate (SHCHC) to 2-succinylbenzoate (OSB). It belongs to the enolase superfamily [1-4]. This entry represents the N-terminal domain of MenC. (from Pfam)

label: DUF1980_C
comment: Members of this family are found in a set of prokaryotic hypothetical proteins. Their exact function, has not, as yet, been defined. This entry represents the C-terminal domain. (from Pfam)

label: PorZ_N_b_propeller
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of PorZ (also known as Immunoreactive 84kD antigen PG93) from Porphyromonas gingivalis and in similar proteins predominantly found in Bacteroidetes. PorZ is an essential component of the type-IX secretion system (T9SS) machinery. It consists of three domains. This entry represents the first domain, which folds into a seven-stranded beta-propeller (PMID: 27883039). (from Pfam)

label: FGGY_C_2
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Carbohydrate kinase, FGGY from Novosphingobium aromaticivorans and similar bacterial proteins. This protein may catalyse the transfer of a phosphate group from ATP to their carbohydrate substrates. It contain two large domains, which are separated by a deep cleft. This domain, thought to be responsible for ATP binding, shows an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: SlpA_C
comment: This entry represents the beta-barrel found at the C-terminal of S-layer protein SlpA and similar S-layer proteins. SlpA plays an important role in the structural organisation and integrity of the S-layer [1,2]. In Deinococcus radiodurans, SlpA binds the carotenoid deinoxanthin, a strong protective antioxidant specific of this bacterium suggested to be part of the first lane of defense against UV radiation, especially under desiccation (PMID: 26909071). (from Pfam)

label: MPI_cupin_dom
comment: This domain is found in Mannose-6-phosphate isomerase from Archaeoglobus fulgidus (MPI) and similar bacterial sequences. This enzyme catalyses the interconversion of mannose 6-phosphate and fructose 6-phosphate [1,2]. This entry represents the C-terminal domain, which is found associated with PFam:PF20511. This domain shows an all-beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: ACTMAP-like_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of proteins that includes the human protein ACTMAP (actin maturation protease, also known as C19orf54) and similar sequences from animals. ACTMAP is responsible for the noncanonical excision of the acetylated methionine of actin molecules after translation. It seems to have a crucial effect in all cell types (PMID: 36173861). (from Pfam)

label: RPOC_hybrid
product_name: DNA-directed RNA polymerase subunit beta', hybrid domain
name_orig: DNA-directed RNA polymerase subunit beta', hybrid domain
hmm_name: DNA-directed RNA polymerase subunit beta', hybrid domain
comment: This is a hybrid domain found in DNA-directed RNA polymerase subunit beta' (RPOC) found in Deinococcus [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: GpP-like_1st
name_orig: Mu phage baseplate assembly protein GpP-like, N-terminal
hmm_name: Mu phage baseplate assembly protein N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Mu phage baseplate assembly protein GpP from Shewanella oneidensis and similar proteins predominantly found in tailed bacteriophages and bacterial prophages. (from Pfam)

label: GlnR_1st
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Transcription regulator GlnR from Amycolatopsis mediterranei and similar sequences predominantly found in actinobacteria. GlnR plays a key role in the global regulation of nitrogen metabolism. It belongs to the OmpR/PhoB subfamily. This domain shows five alternating beta-strands and alpha- helices that form a five-stranded parallel beta-sheet in the middle surrounded by two alpha-helices on one side and three on the other, showing great structure similarity with most of the known structures of the typical RR receiver domains (PMID: 24733389). This domain is usually found associated with Pfam:PF00486. (from Pfam)

label: Spt6_S1
comment: This entry represents the S1/OB-fold domain of Spt6. This domain has structural similarity to S1 domain but lacks the typical S1 binding cleft residues involved in nucleic acid binding (PMID: 21419780), therefore, this domain in Spt6 may be involved in interactions with other partners. (from Pfam)

label: DncV_C
comment: This domain is found Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase from Vibrio cholerae (DncV), a prokaryotic cGAS-like enzyme that synthesises cyclic GMP- AMP (c-GAMP) and stimulates intestinal colonization. DncV adopts a structure and topology that are typical of the nucleotidyltransferase superfamily. It is organised into two domains: an N-terminal domain that contains the catalytic loop (Pfam:PF21654) and a C- terminal helix bundle that consists of eight helices and one pair of anti-parallel beta-sheets (this entry) [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: IRX15_IRX15L_GXM
comment: This entry represents a group of sugar methyltransferases found in plants and bacteria, including protein IRREGULAR XYLEM IRX15/IRX15L, glucuronoxylan 4-O-methyltransferases 1-3 (GXM1-3) and AMG1/2 (probable methyltransferase At1g27930 and At1g67330, respectively) from Arabidopsis (PMID: 31245760). GXMs and IRX15/15L are all expressed in secondary wall-forming cells and they are all involved in xylan biosynthesis. However, they have different functions [1,2,6]. IRX15/IRX15L are required for xylan biosynthesis and/or xylan deposition, although their enzymatic activity is unknown [3,4,6]. GXMs catalyse the 4-O-methylation of the glucuronic acid substituent on xylan [1,2,5,6]. This entry also includes AGM1 (also known as probable methyltransferase At1g27930) and AGM2 (At1g67330) which are required for 4-O-methylation of glucuronic acid of arabinogalactan proteins, a different plant cell wall component (PMID: 31245760). (from Pfam)

label: DACNV
comment: This entry represents a potential sensor domain found at the N-terminal of bacterial diadenylate cyclases, which is typically followed by the DAC (Pfam:PF02457) domain. DACND consists of a compact core formed by seven beta-strands and two or three alpha-helices, according to structure predictions. It is found in various phyla, including acidobacteria, actinobacteria, bacteroidetes, cyanobacteria and planctomycetes. (from Pfam)

label: NagJ_C
comment: This domain is located at the C-terminus of proteins that are members of family 84 glycoside hydrolases.These enzymes directly hydrolyse O-GlcNAcylated peptides/proteins. This domain folds into a five helical bundle with up-and-down topology. It may function in substrate binding or recognition [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6874
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins that contain a small alpha helical bundle domain. (from Pfam)

label: Bflower_3
comment: This family of proteins have a repetitive structure composed of pairs of beta strands. In this family the proteins usually have six copies of the beta hairpin repeat with a central alpha helix in the barrel. (from Pfam)

label: Transposase_29
comment: This family was identified by Pfam as a probable transposase family by the similarity of predicted structures to those of known transposases.

label: Dit_like
comment: Members of this family are found as a component of phage baseplate structures. Many members of this family have a peptidoglycan-binding LysM domain.

label: DUF6814
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. Proteins in this family are predominantly found in Bacteroidetes and are approximately 80 amino acids in length. There are several conserved motifs: IxxGL, FGxY and GEY. (from Pfam)

label: TRADD-like_N
comment: This is the RRM fold domain prototyped by the version at the N-terminus of the TRADD protein. The TRADD-N domain is widely present in bacterial conflict systems and in a spectacular diversity of counter-invader systems in metazoa, especially in aggregating marine invertebrates. The domain is predicted to function as a signalling bridge linking invader sensing and effector deployment in multidomain proteins. Metazoans have two broad families of TRADD-N domains, the NCOA6 and the TRADD/DEDD-2 families respectively that are named after the prototypic vertebrate proteins in which they are found (PMID: 34061031). (from Pfam)

label: YPEB_N
comment: This is the N-terminal region of YpeB, a protein restricted to endospore-forming species in the Firmicutes lineage of bacteria, that have been found in all such species to date except Clostridium perfringens. YpeB and the spore-cortex-lytic enzyme SleB are required for normal germination (PMID: 26219275). This protein is essential in stabilising SleB enzyme in Bacillus spores, and may regulate its activity during germination (PMID: 26219275). (from Pfam)

label: TssR_M
comment: This entry represents the second domain of TssR which adopts small beta barrel structure. T6SSs are toxin delivery systems. It is a multiprotein complex requiring numerous core proteins (Tss proteins) including cytoplasmic, transmembrane, and outer membrane components. The needle or tube apparatus is comprised of a phage-like complex, similar to the T4 contractile bacteriophage tail, which is thought to be anchored to the membrane by a trans-envelope complex (PMID: 26768901). (from Pfam)

label: Cmr2_hel_dom2
product_name: CRISPR RNA silencing complex Cmr2 subunit, second helical domain
name_orig: CRISPR RNA silencing complex Cmr2 subunit, second helical domain
hmm_name: CRISPR RNA silencing complex Cmr2 subunit, second helical domain
comment: The prokaryotic CRISPR RNA-Cas protein (Cmr) complex provides protection against mobile genetic elements by cleaving foreign RNA. Its largest subunit is Cmr2. This protein shows a N-terminal HD (histidine-aspartate) domain, two RRM domains resembling adenylate cyclase and two alpha-helical domains. This entry represents the second alpha-helical domain. It is similar to the small subunit Cmr5, which contains six alpha-helices and two helical insertions that fold into a single globular structure [1-5]. This domain is also found in Cas10 proteins from bacteria (PMID: 33352158). (from Pfam)

label: Relaxase_M
comment: This domain is found in some relaxase proteins. (from Pfam)

label: SVN
comment: Scytovirin is a protein from the cyanobacteria Scytonema varium with anticytopathic activity against some strains of HIV. The protein, which adopts a monomeric assembly, has two repeats that form similarly structured domains. Remarkably, it has a high percentage of cysteine residues, all participating in disulfide bonds [1-3]. This family also includes proteins from Proteobacteria and plants. (from Pfam)

label: phiKZ_gp29PR
comment: This domain is found in the Tail sheath protein gp29 from the giant Bacteriophage phiKZ. This entry represents a protease resistant fragment of this protein, gp29PR, which consists of a single domain showing a seven-stranded beta-sandwich with long insertions connecting adjacent beta-strands, including a long alpha-helix (PMID: 22153511). (from Pfam)

label: MASE9
comment: This entry represents the membrane-associated sensor domain 9 (MASE9), which has been found in combination with HD-GYP and GGDEF-EAL domains , or in MASE9-HD-GYP-GAF-GGDEF domain architecture (PMID: 34928179). It has 8 predicted transmembrane (TM) segments of which two are likely to form an intramembrane hairpin. It has several charged residues in the hydrophobic core of the membrane, that, in addition to the poor conservation of the short periplasmic segments, suggests that ligand binding and/or protein-protein interactions by MASE9 may occur within the membrane (PMID: 34928179). (from Pfam)

label: DGCcoil
comment: This entry represents the DGC-associated coil (DGCcoil) domain found widespread in gammaproteobacteria (PMID: 35311563). This is an alpha-helical cytoplasmic domain found N-terminal of the GGDEF domain (PMID: 35311563). (from Pfam)

label: DUF1285_C
name_orig: Protein of unknown function (DUF1285), C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of several hypothetical bacterial proteins. The structure revealed a superficial similarity of this domain to pleckstrin homology-like folds (PMID: 20944214). (from Pfam)

label: Glyco_hydro_78_N
product_name: Glycosyl hydrolase family 78 alpha-rhamnosidase N-terminal domain
name_orig: Glycosyl hydrolase family 78 alpha-rhamnosidase N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Glycosyl hydrolase family 78 alpha-rhamnosidase N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of glycosyl hydrolase family 78 alpha-rhamnosidase proteins (PMID: 25846411). This domain is involved in dimerisation of the enzyme (PMID: 25846411). (from Pfam)

label: STPRs
product_name: STPRs (score and three amino acid peptide repeats)
name_orig: STPRs (score and three amino acid peptide repeats)
hmm_name: STPRs (score and three amino acid peptide repeats)
comment: The silkgland-specific transcription factor FMBP-1 from the silkworm Bombyx mori contains a unique DNA-binding domain of four tandem STPRs, namely the score and three amino acid peptide repeats (PMID: 26939889). In the presence of target DNA, STPRs adopts a zig-zag structure of three or four tandem alpha-helices that run along the major groove of DNA (PMID: 26939889). (from Pfam)

label: BT_MCC_alpha
comment: This domain is found in the biotin-containing alpha subunit of the Methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase complex (MCC) from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Swiss:Q9I299) and similar proteins. MCC is essential for the metabolism of leucine. The alpha subunit is organised into the N-terminal biotin carboxylase (BC), the C-terminal biotin carboxyl carrier protein (BCCP) domains, and a domain that mediates BC-CT interactions (BT domain, this entry). This domain shows a central alpha-helix surrounded by a seven-stranded, highly-twisted anti-parallel beta-sheet, with an overall structure that has great similarity with the beta-barrel of the BT domain of the human MCC (PMID: 22158123). (from Pfam)

label: YgjK_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Glucosidase YgjK from Escherichia coli and similar bacterial enzymes from the glycoside hydrolase family 63 (GH63) from bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes. YgjK is organised into N- and A- domains and a linker between them. This entry includes the N-domain and the linker. The N-domain is composed of 18 antiparallel beta-strands divided into two beta- sheets and is classified as a super-beta-sandwich. The linker is composed of two helices and produces a significant curvature between the two domains [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DksA_N
product_name: DnaK suppressor protein DksA, N-terminal domain
name_orig: DnaK suppressor protein DksA, N-terminal domain
hmm_name: DnaK suppressor protein DksA, N-terminal domain
comment: DksA is a transcription factor that directly binds RNA polymerase and controls the bacteria response to stress and starvation. DksA is all helical and comprises a coiled-coil (CC) and globular domains [1-4]. This is the N-terminal domain which extends through the secondary channel toward the RNAP active site and serves as a conduit for the substrate NTPs. This domain consists of two helices arranged in an antiparallel alpha-hairpin with left-handed twist. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6851
comment: This domain of unknown function is found in the N-terminal region of a group of bacterial proteins, including Haloperoxidase from Muricauda lutaonensis. In this protein, this domain is found associated to Pfam:PF01569. Its specific function is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: SsfX3_N
comment: This domain is found in the protein SsfX3 from Streptomyces sp. and in similar bacterial proteins. SsfX3 is an acyltransferase involved in the biosynthesis of the anticancer natural product SF2575. This protein is organised into two distinct domains: an N-terminal beta-sandwich (this entry) and a C-terminal catalytic domain (GDSL-like Lipase/Acylhydrolase domain, Pfam:PF13472). This domain resembles a carbohydrate-binding module (CBM) domain and is critical for substrate binding (PMID: 21965680). (from Pfam)

label: RecD_N
product_name: RecBCD enzyme subunit RecD, N-terminal domain
name_orig: RecBCD enzyme subunit RecD, N-terminal domain
hmm_name: RecBCD enzyme subunit RecD, N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found in RecBCD enzyme subunit RecD from Escherichia coli and in similar proteins mostly found in Gammaproteobacteria. RecD is a 5'-3' helicase that comprises three domains. This entry represents the N-terminal domain of RecD, which forms the principal interface between RecD and domain 2B of RecC and leads to the conformational change in RecD that has significant effects on the conformation of the RecC subunit [1-4]. (from Pfam)

label: MalQ_N
comment: Amylomaltase MalQ is essential for the metabolism of maltose and maltodextrins in Escherichia coli. It catalyzes transglycosylation/disproportionation reactions in which glycosyl or dextrinyl units are transferred among linear maltodextrins of various lengths (PMID: 26139606). This domain called N2 resembles a beta-sandwich consisting of a five-stranded mixed beta-sheet and a short two-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet. The N2 structure is reminiscent of carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) (PMID: 26139606). However, a comparison with structurally known CBMs did not reveal significant similarities. (from Pfam)

label: Mann_GBD_bact
comment: This is a galactose-binding domain-like found at the C-terminal of alkaline mannanases, such as Swiss:Q4W8M3 from Bacillus sp. JAMB-602 (PMID: 15272186) and related bacterial sequences which belong to the Glycoside Hydrolase Family 5 (Pfam:PF00150). (from Pfam)

label: Rgg_C
name_orig: HTH-type transcriptional regulator Rgg, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Rgg family transcriptional regulator, C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of HTH-type transcriptional regulator Rgg from Streptococcus gordonii, and similar proteins predominantly found in Firmicutes. Rgg is a peptide pheromone receptor that directly binds pheromones transported to the cytosol. The large C-terminal repeat domain contains five HTH folds and a capping helix that form a right-handed superhelical structure, resembling a TPR domain superhelix [1-5]. This domain is found associated with the N-terminal Pfam:PF01381. (from Pfam)

label: BetaGal_ABD_1
comment: Beta-galactosidases belong to glycosyl hydrolase 35 family (GH35) which catalyse the cleaveage of beta-linked terminal galactosyl residues from gangliosides, glycoproteins, and glycosaminoglycans. These proteins consist of a catalytic TIM-barrel and two all-beta domains (ABD1 and ABD2) [1-5]. This entry represents the first all-beta domain ABD1. ABD2 is represented in Pfam:PF13364. (from Pfam)

label: Polysacc_lyase-like
comment: This domain is found in Cip1 from Hypocrea jecorina and similar sequences predominantly found in fungi. Cip1 is a cellulose induced protein with a carbohydrate binding module (Pfam:PF00734) connected via a linker region to a domain with yet unknown function (this entry). This domain shows a beta- sandwich jelly-roll fold with two anti-parallel beta-sheets that consist on eight and seven strands and pack on top of one another. Structural analysis suggest it may function as a lyase (PMID: 24039705). (from Pfam)

label: ACAD9-ACADV_C
comment: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases catalyse the alpha,beta-dehydrogenation of acyl-CoA thioesters to the corresponding trans 2,3-enoyl CoA-products with reduction of enzyme-bound FAD. They consist of an N-terminal all-alpha domain, a middle open (5,8) barrel domain and a four-helical bundle C-terminal domain. Members of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase family differ in the number of C-terminal domains. This entry represents the second C-terminal domain, from ACAD9 and Very long-chain specific acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (ACADV) (PMID: 18227065). (from Pfam)

label: Irp3-like_C
comment: Thiazolinyl imine reductases catalyse the NADPH-dependent reduction of a thiazoline to a thiazolidine, a step involved in formation of the siderophores yersiniabactin (Yersinia spp.) and pyochelin (Pseudomonas aeruginosa) [1,2]. These proteins consist of two domains, an N-terminal dinucleotide-binding domain (Pfam:PF01408) and a C-terminal alpha/beta domain, involved in substrate binding and oligomerisation. This entry represents the C-terminal domain of Thiazolinyl imine reductase Irp3 from Yersinia enterocolitica and PchG from Pseudomonas aeruginosa [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-ketacyl_N
comment: This is the N-terminal adenylation (A) domain of bacterial beta-ketoacyl synthases (PMID: 32066969). This domain selects the alpha-keto acid that then adenylates and transfer to the PCP domain. (from Pfam)

label: MTR4-like_stalk
comment: Exosome RNA helicase MTR4 is a conserved RNA helicase that functions together with the nuclear exosome and it is involved in processing of structured RNAs, including snRNAs and snoRNAs. It also plays a role in nuclear RNA surveillance pathways involving the so-called TRAMP complex [1,2]. It contains an arch domain, required for proper 5.8S rRNA processing, and appears to function independently of canonical helicase activity (PMID: 22114319). The arch domain comprises an helical stalk/elbow that flanks a KOW module which adopts a beta-barrel fold. This entry represents the helical stalk found at the N-terminal of KOW beta-barrel from MTR4 [1-3]. This entry also includes Ski2-like helicases which have an overall similar structure to MTR4 proteins. However, Ski2 from yeast does not have the KOW motif and the beta-barrel is tightly packed against the helical stalk (PMID: 22114319). (from Pfam)

label: RoxA-like_Cyt-c
comment: This entry represents a cytochrome c-like domain described in RoxA from Xanthomonas sp (PMID: 23922395), one of only two known enzymes able to catalyse the oxidative cleavage of latex for biodegradation. This domain contains the second heme-binding motif. This domain is found in the uncharacterised proteins y4iM and Y4IJ from Sinorhizobium fredii. (from Pfam)

label: Gp7_helical
product_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp7, helical domain
name_orig: Baseplate wedge protein gp7, helical domain
hmm_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp7, helical domain
comment: This domain is found in Baseplate wedge protein gp7 from Bacteriophage T4 and similar proteins predominantly found in tailed bacteriophages. Gp7 provides the primary control of the conformational changes of the viral baseplate during assembly and infection. This protein is organised into six domains connected by flexible linkers. This entry represents helix-turn-helix motif that is part of the long linker connecting the second and fourth domains (PMID: 26929357). (from Pfam)

label: Gp7_6th
product_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp7, domain VI
name_orig: Baseplate wedge protein gp7, domain VI
hmm_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp7, domain VI
comment: This domain is found in Baseplate wedge protein gp7 from Bacteriophage T4 and similar proteins predominantly found in tailed bacteriophages. Gp7 provides the primary control of the conformational changes of the viral baseplate during assembly and infection. This protein is organised into six domains connected by flexible linkers. This entry represents Domain VI, which forms a ribbon-like structure that interacts with N-terminal region of the protein Gp10 (PMID: 26929357). (from Pfam)

label: HL_N-beta
comment: Hyaluronate lyase degrades hyaluronan and certain chondroitin sulfates at beta-1,4 glycosidic linkages and constitutes a virulence factor of Streptococcus agalactiae (PMID: 11527972). It consists of three structural domains, an N-terminal beta-sheet domain (also referred as to beta1), a middle catalytic alpha-helical domain (Pfam:PF08124) and a C-terminal beta-sheet domain (beta2, Pfam:PF02278) (PMID: 11527972). This entry represents the N-terminal beta-sheet domain which adopts a Ig-like fold and may serve as a connection of the alpha-domain with another structural domain (PMID: 11527972). (from Pfam)

label: Gp6_2nd
product_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp6, domain II
name_orig: Baseplate wedge protein gp6, domain II
hmm_name: Baseplate wedge protein gp6, domain II
comment: This domain is found in Baseplate wedge protein gp6 from Enterobacteria phage T4 and similar sequences predominantly from tailed bacteriophages. Gp6 is a protein involved in tail assembly. This entry represents the first part of Domain II (PMID: 26929357). (from Pfam)

label: Pif1_2B_dom
comment: Pif1 is a DNA helicase conserved from bacteria to humans. It suppresses both G-quadruplex-associated DNA damage and telomere lengthening. In budding yeast, it exists in two forms, nuclear and mitochondrial forms. Its nuclear form inhibits telomerase, while its mitochondrial is involved in repair and recombination of mitochondrial DNA. These proteins belong to the helicase superfamily 1 (SF1) and contain RecA-like domains (1A and 2A) which, together with two additional domains, 1B and 2B, form the helicase core [1,2]. This entry represents domain 2B, which adopts a SH3-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: CvfB_2nd
product_name: Virulence regulatory factor CvfB, second domain
name_orig: Virulence regulatory factor CvfB, second domain
hmm_name: Virulence regulatory factor CvfB, second domain
comment: This domain is found in the virulence regulatory factor CvfB from Streptococcus pneumoniae and in similar proteins predominantly found in Firmicutes. CvfB is composed of three consecutive S1 RNA-binding domains and a winged-helix (WH) domain (Pfam:PF17783). This entry represents the second S! domain, an RNA-binding module that adopts the typical S1 fold that consists of a five-stranded, antiparallel beta-sheet forming a beta-barrel (PMID: 20399190). (from Pfam)

label: RhaB_D2
comment: This domain is found in Alpha-L-rhamnosidase from Bacillus sp. (RhaB), a member of glycoside hydrolase (GH) family 78 that catalyses the hydrolytic release of rhamnose from polysaccharides and glycosides, degrading the bacterial biofilm gellan. RhaB is organised into five domains: Pfam:PF08531, this entry, Pfam:PF05592, Pfam:PF17389 and Pfam:PF17390. This domain shows a beta-sandwich structure with 13 beta-strands and two short helices (PMID: 17936784). (from Pfam)

label: Caudo_bapla_RBP_neck
product_name: Lactococcus phage p2, Receptor binding protein, neck domain
name_orig: Lactococcus phage p2, Receptor binding protein, neck domain
hmm_name: Lactococcus phage p2, Receptor binding protein, neck domain
comment: This domain is found centrally located in Receptor binding protein from Lactococcus phage p2 (RBP, also known as Gp18) and similar proteins from closely related lactococcal phages. RBP shows three domains: the N-terminal shoulder domain (Pfam:PF20747), which is attached to the phage, the neck domain (this entry) and the C -terminal receptor-recognition head domain (Pfam:PF08931). The central domain folds into four beta-strands, which interlace with the beta-strands of two other subunits to form an equilateral triangular prism around the three-fold axis of a triple-stranded beta-helix [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: NagA_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Beta-N- acetylglucosaminidase from Thermotoga maritima (NagA), which hydrolyses chitooligomers into monomer beta-N-acetylglucosamine. NagA forms a dimer structure in which the monomer structure is organised into an N- and a C-terminal domain (Pfam:PF00933 and this entry, respectively).
