This domain shows an alpha-beta- alpha-sandwich fold, which comprises six beta-strands with two alpha-helices on either side of the sheet [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: AIMA-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal 1,3-alpha-isomaltosidase from Kribbella flavida (AIMA, also known as Kfla1895) and sequences from actinomycetes. AIMA is involved in the intracellular degradation of the cyclic tetrasaccharide cyclobis-1-6-alpha-nigerosyl formed extracellularly from starch. It catalyses the hydrolysis of the alpha-1,3-glucosidic linkage of cyclobis-1-6-alpha-nigerosyl to yield isomaltose via a possible linear tetrasaccharide (PMID: 27819654). This domain folds into an Ig-like beta-sandwich. (from Pfam)

label: DraIII
comment: This protein family includes DraIII from Deinococcus radiophilus, a type IIP restriction endonuclease that recognises a gapped double-stranded DNA sequence and nicks creating a double strand break with a three base 3' overhang. DraIII adopts a homodimeric configuration. Each monomer shows a beta-beta-alpha-metal fold in the C terminus, where the HNH active site is located. It also has two zinc- and one magnesium-binding sites (PMID: 24733184). (from Pfam)

label: Bc2l-C_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Lectin from Burkholderia cenocepacia (Bc2l-C) and similar bacterial sequences. Bc2l-C is a soluble lectin involved in bacterial adhesion and subsequent deadly infection to the host. It has two domains: a C-terminal domain Pfam:PF07472 and this domain, which adopts a compact jellyroll architecture composed of 11 beta-strands and a short helix. It shows specificity for fucosylated human histo-blood group epitopes H-type 1, Lewis b, and Lewis Y [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: GldM_3rd
comment: This immunoglobulin-like domain is found in bacteria in the GldM protein. GldM, is named for the member from Cytophaga johnsonae (Flavobacterium johnsoniae), which is required for a type of rapid gliding motility found in certain members of the Bacteriodetes (PMID: 16199564). (from Pfam)

label: FabD_helical_ins
comment: This domain is found in the C-terminal region of [Acyl-carrier-protein] S-malonyltransferase from Bacillus velezensis (FabD) and similar bacterial proteins. FabD, a marine polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) synthase involved in difficidin A biosynthesis, is is organised into two domains: anacetyl-transferase (AT) domain (Pfam:PF00698) and an enoyl reductase (ER) domain that consists of a TIM-barrel domain (Pfam:PF03060) and an inserted alpha-helical substrate-binding domain (this entry). (from Pfam)

label: CBM-like_2
comment: This domain is found in a a group of bacterial proteins, including the uncharacterised Fibronectin type-III domain-containing protein from Agathobacter rectalis (Swiss:C4ZEB7). It adopts a jelly roll structure. (from Pfam)

label: NarE
comment: This is a group of short bacterial sequences that includes NarE from Neisseria meningitidis. NarE is a protein with predicted ADP-ribosyltransferase activity. It shows an alpha-beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6858
comment: This family of proteins are distantly related to Pfam:PF03625. Their function is as yet unknown. (from Pfam)

label: GIDA_C_1st
product_name: tRNA modifying enzyme MnmG/GidA C-terminal helical domain
name_orig: tRNA modifying enzyme MnmG/GidA C-terminal helical domain
hmm_name: tRNA modifying enzyme MnmG/GidA C-terminal helical domain
comment: The GidA associated domain is a domain that has been identified at the C-terminus of protein GidA. It consists of several helices, the last three being rather short and forming small bundle. GidA is an tRNA modification enzyme found in bacteria and mitochondrial. Based on mutational analysis this domain has been suggested to be implicated in binding of the D-stem of tRNA (PMID: 19446527) and, in particular the small bundle, to be responsible for the interaction with protein MnmE (PMID: 18565343). Structures of GidA in complex with either tRNA or MnmE are missing. Reported to bind to Pfam family MnmE, Pfam:PF12631. This entry represents the first helices of the GidA associated domain. The last three helices are covered in Pfam:PF13932. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6861
comment: This domain is a likely integral membrane domain that contains a glycine-zipper motif. This domain is found associated with toxin domains. (from Pfam)

label: 10_blade
comment: This entry represents a family of beta propeller repeats identified in metagenomics data. They have 10 blades in an arrangement similar to the sortilin protein. (from Pfam)

label: DJR-like_dom
comment: This entry represents a domain found in a group of proteins mainly from arthropods containing a jelly-roll domain, which has similarity to domains otherwise found in a variety of large dsDNA virus capsid proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6867
comment: This entry represents a likely integral membrane protein. These proteins are composed of three alpha helices followed by a short beta hairpin. This family is called DUF6867. Proteins in this family are found in Proteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: Dit_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Distal tail protein from Lactococcus phage p2 (Dit or Gp15) and similar proteins predominantly found in virus. Dit self-associates as two rings organised back to back, with a central channel allowing DNA ejection through the viral tail. This domain is located at the ring periphery and display a galectin fold [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: SDR-like
comment: This family of uncharacterised proteins appear to be related to known short-chain dehydrogenase enzymes. They are rather short having a Rossmann fold domain which consists of only four beta-strands. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Proteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: WHD_PKMT
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal winged helix domain of PKMTs. PKMTs are protein-lysine methyltransferases that catalyze the methylation of lysine residues on many different proteins. They consist of N-terminal S-adenosylmethionine binding domain, a middle domain and a C-terminal domain. The middle and the C-terminal domain share significant structural similarity and are both distantly related to HTH winged helix DNA-binding domains (PMID: 27474738). (from Pfam)

label: Dynamin-like_hel_bact
comment: This is the helical region from bacterial dynamin-like proteins which covers the middle and GED domains which mediate extensive protein-protein contacts [1,2]. These proteins are large GTPases with the same multidomain architecture that is found in dynamin-like proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6880
comment: This entry represents a family of proteins that form an alpha-helical solenoid structure of HEAT-like repeats. Proteins in this family are found in various bacterial species, but most commonly in proteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: CapR
comment: This entry represents a domain that is found in in the CapR proteins of PLE phage satellites (PMID: 33823541). Proteins in this family are DNA-binding proteins. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TAC_15
name_orig: Phage tail assembly chaperone protein, TAC
comment: This is a family of phage tail assembly chaperone proteins. (from Pfam)

label: MS_N
comment: Malate synthase (MS) catalyses the aldol condensation of glyoxylate with acetyl-CoA to form malate as part of the second step of the glyoxylate bypass and an alternative to the tricarboxylic acid cycle in bacteria, fungi and plants. There have been identified two isoforms, A and G (MSA and MSG, respectively) that differ in size and is attributed to an inserted alpha/beta domain in MSG that may have regulatory function [1,2]. They consist of an N-terminal alpha-helical claps, a central TIM barrel and a C-terminal alpha-helical plug. This entry represents the N-terminal clasp that wraps around one side of the TIM barrel and buttressed it [1,2,3,4]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6811
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. Proteins in this family are approximately 90 amino acids in length and are predominantly found in Deltaproteobacteria. There are several conserved motifs: ExCxGCxR, PxxKW, GxCNFATH and KxNPLKASK. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6817
comment: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised, found in bacteria and plants. It is approximately 160 amino acids in length and it has two conserved sequence motifs, HL and GLxHxxY. Several members of this entry also has TPR regions. (from Pfam)

label: bDLD3
comment: This bacterial adaptor domain of the Death-domain fold is involved in protein-protein interactions in biological conflict systems. bDLDs show a characteristic architectural pattern. One copy is always fused, typically to the N- or C-terminus, of a core component of a biological conflict system; examples include VMAP and iSTAND. Further copies of the same bDLD are fused to either effector or signal-transducing domains, or additional Effector-associated domains (EADs). bDLD pairs are frequently observed together on the genome in conserved gene neighborhoods, but can also be severed from such neighborhoods and located in distant regions, indicating the bDLD-bDLD coupling approximates the advantages of collinear transcription. bDLD3 is closest in sequence and likely progenitor of the metazoan Death-superfamily. bDLD3 shows a greater diversity of contextual associations in conflict systems in comparison to bDLD1 and bDLD2 (PMID: 34061031). (from Pfam)

label: KH_NucS_shadow
comment: This entry represents a shadow ORF found on the opposite strand to Endonuclease NucS. Unlike most shadow ORFs this appears to be a genuine protein coding gene. A structural model suggests the protein has some similarity to the KH domain suggesting it may be an RNA-binding protein of unknown function. This family was formerly in the AntiFam database with accession ANF00096. (from Pfam)

label: PE-PGRS_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminus of some PE-PGRS proteins from Mycobacteria. The domain is related to aspartyl peptidases. (from Pfam)

label: Lambda_ea8_5
comment: This domain is found in Protein ea8.5 from Bacteriophage lambda and similar protein sequences mostly from tailed bacteriophages and bacterial prophages. It ranges from around 45 to 90 residues in length and is associated with nucleic acid binding function, playing an essential role in the inhibition of the initiation of DNA synthesis in the phage host. NMR analysis shows it adopts an homeodomain/zinc-finger fold, which suggests a regulatory role [1, 2, 3]. (from Pfam)

label: TACO1_YebC_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal helical bundle domain from proteins in the TACO1/YebC family which are thought to act as transcriptional regulators. In mammals, The TACO1 protein activates the translation of mitochondrially-encoded COX1 [2,4]. In bacteria, it negatively regulates the quorum-sensing response regulator by binding to its promoter region (PMID: 18641136). (from Pfam)

label: TssR_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain from the TssR protein. T6SSs are toxin delivery systems. It is a multiprotein complex requiring numerous core proteins (Tss proteins) including cytoplasmic, transmembrane, and outer membrane components. The needle or tube apparatus is comprised of a phage-like complex, similar to the T4 contractile bacteriophage tail, which is thought to be anchored to the membrane by a trans-envelope complex (PMID: 26768901). (from Pfam)

label: MACPF_D3
comment: This domain is found in proteins of the membrane-attack complex/ perforin (MACPF) family from Bacteroidetes. These transmembrane pore- forming proteins are organized into three structured domains: an MACPF domain (Pfam:PF01823) and two C-terminal domains, D2 and D3. This entry represents the D3 domain, which adopts an alpha/beta fold and functions as a wedge between D2 and MACPF (PMID: 20944225). (from Pfam)

label: MdcG_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal SH3-like domain from MdcG which is a phosphoribosyl-dephospho-CoA transferase that is involved in the biosynthesis of the prosthetic group of malonate decarboxylase (PMID: 11052675). Malonate decarboxylase from Klebsiella pneumoniae contains an acyl carrier protein (MdcC) to which a 2'-(5' '-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA prosthetic group is attached via phosphodiester linkage. MdcG catalyses the following reaction: 2'-(5''-triphosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA + apo-[acyl-carrier-protein] = holo-[acyl-carrier-protein] + diphosphate. (from Pfam)

label: G1_gp67_C
comment: gp67 from Staphylococcus virus G1 binds to the sigma(A)-subunit of the RNA polymerase (RNAP) of its host to block cell growth by inhibiting transcription. This protein is organized in two domains, an N-terminal beta-sheet-rich domain and a C-terminal alpha-helical domain, which are connected by a linker-alpha-helix on the surface of gp67 opposite the interaction surface. This entry includes the C- terminal domain and the helical linker (PMID: 23178120). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6848
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised protein rbstp2171 from Bacillus stearothermophilus and similar proteins found in bacteria and tailed bacteriophages. (from Pfam)

label: MASE8
comment: This entry represents the membrane-associated sensor domain MASE8 (PMID: 35311563), which is found in association with GGDEF domain (Pfam:PF00990), histidine sensor kinases and adenylate cyclase output domain (Pfam:PF00211). This domain is widespread among various classes of proteobacteria and is also found in other phyla. (from Pfam)

label: MASE10
comment: This is the membrane-associated sensor domain 10 (MASE10) which has conserved Cys, Ser and Trp residues in the periplasmic loop, conserved aromatic residues and four charged (Arg, Asp, Lys, and another Asp) residues in the predicted transmembrane segments, suggesting specific interaction with its small molecule or protein ligands (PMID: 34928179). It has been found in c-di-GMP phosphodiesterases, adenylate/guanylate cyclases and Ser/Thr protein phosphatases of the PP2C family, in which MASE10 is followed by the signal-transducing HAMP domain (PMID: 34928179). (from Pfam)

label: PROPPIN
comment: This entry includes PROPPIN family members, which are beta-propellers that bind polyphosphoinositides, conserved from yeast to human. These are PI(3)P sensors that share a beta-propeller fold and the presence of an FRRG motif required for phosphoinositide binding and autophagy, playing a key role in autophagosome biogenesis. Four PROPPINs are known in human (WIPI1-4) and three in yeast (Atg18, Atg21 and Hvs2) [1-5]. EPG6 from C. elegans is an homologue of human WIPI4 (PMID: 30102152). (from Pfam)

label: Csx12
comment: This entry represents the alpha-helical lobe of the Francisella novicida Cas9 protein. (from Pfam)

label: GDH_ACT1
comment: Glutamate dehydrogenases (GDHs) are a broadly distributed group of enzymes that catalyse the reversible oxidative deamination of glutamate to ketoglutarate and ammonia (PMID: 10924516). The structure of GDH from Mycobacterium smegmatis revealed that it has a long N- and C-terminal segments flanking the catalytic core, comprising several domains. The flexible N-terminal domain comprises ACT-like and PAS-type domains which could act as metabolic sensors for allosteric regulation (PMID: 34083757). This is the first ACT-like domain (ACT1) found at the N-terminal of GDH. The ACT domains of these proteins differ from the archetypal ACT fold in that strand strand beta1 is located in the position usually occupied by strand beta4 creating an ACT-like topology with a beta1-4 antiparallel sheet (PMID: 34083757). (from Pfam)

label: WHD_DUF4423_like
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminus of the TruD protein (PMID: 24214017) a protein involved in cyanobactin heterocyclisation. It adopts a winged helix-turn-helix structure. It is also found in the related LynD protein (PMID: 26098679). (from Pfam)

label: Glyco_hydro_134
comment: This entry represents glycoside hydrolase family 134 which contains beta-1,4-mannanase enzymes. This enzyme has a lysozyme like fold. (from Pfam)

label: RecA_C
comment: This entry represents a small domain found at the C-terminus of RecA. The recA gene product is a multifunctional enzyme that plays a role in homologous recombination, DNA repair and induction of the SOS response This domain adopts a structure composed of a beta hairpin and three alpha helices. It has been shown to bind to dsDNA (PMID: 9398528). (from Pfam)

label: DprA_N
comment: This Helix-hairpin-helix domain is found at the N-terminus of predicted Rossmann fold nucleotide-binding protein DprA/Smf involved in DNA uptake. (from Pfam)

label: DksA-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of DnaK suppressor protein from Agrobacterium fabrum (DksA) and similar proteins predominantly found in Alphaproteobacteria. This domain shows an all-alpha structure and is often found N-terminal to Pfam:PF01258. (from Pfam)

label: RecR_HhH
comment: The bacterial protein RecR is an important regulator oin the RecFOR homologous recombination pathway during DNA repair. It acts with RecF and RecO forming a complex that facilitates the loading of RecA onto ssDNA. RecR is a zinc metalloprotein consisting of a N-terminal helix-hairpin-helix (HhH) motif, a middle region containing a zinc finger motif (Pfam:PF02132) and a Toprim domain (Pfam:PF13662) and a C-terminal domain comprising a Walker B motif and a C-terminal helix (Pfam:PF21175) [1,2]. This is the HhH motif found at the N-temrinal of RecR which is essential for DNA binding and association with RecO [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: BldD-like_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of DNA-binding protein BldD from Streptomyces venezuelae (Swiss:F2RCL8) and similar proteins found in Actinobacteria. This domain shows two beta-alpha- alpha repeats and a short C-terminal helix. It is responsible for the binding of the protein to the second messenger 3',5'-cyclic diguanylic acid (c-di-GMP) [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: Bbp16
comment: This protein family includes Bbp16 from Bordetella phage BPP-1 and similar proteins from tailed bacteriophages and prophages mainly found in Proteobacteria. Bbp16, which adopts a dimeric configuration, is essential for forming infectious phage particles. This cement protein has a jellyroll fold with two beta-sheets, each consisting of four anti-parallel strands (PMID: 24347545). (from Pfam)

label: PaaA2
comment: This protein family includes Stability determinant from Escherichia coli (PaaA2) and similar proteins predominantly found in bacteria. PaaA2 is an antitoxin from prokaryotic type II toxin-antitoxin three- component module paaR2-paaA2-parE2 that belongs to the RelB- antitoxin family but lacks a DNA-binding domain. This protein shows two alpha-helices and adopts defined loop conformations when it wraps itself around the toxin ParE2 [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: RuBisCO_activase_AAA_helical
product_name: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase activase, AAA, helical
name_orig: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase activase, AAA, helical
hmm_name: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase activase, AAA, helical
comment: This domain is found in Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase activase from Nicotiana tabacum (RuBisCO activase) and similar proteins from plants and cyanobacteria. This enzyme facilitates the removal of the sugar phosphate inhibitors of RuBisCO, the enzyme that catalyses the fixation of atmospheric CO2 in photosynthesis. This protein is organised into an N-terminal, followed by a AAA module and a 23-residue C-terminal extension. The AAA module has an alpha-beta and an alpha-helical subdomains. This entry covers part of the alpha-helical subdomain and the C-terminal extension [1-4]. (from Pfam)

label: Nakanori
comment: This entry include the Nakanori protein a nontoxic mushroom protein that specifically binds to a complex of sphingomyelin, a major sphingolipid in mammalian cells, and cholesterol (PMID: 27492925). (from Pfam)

label: SOGP_2nd
comment: Glycoside phosphorylases catalyze the phosphorolysis of oligosaccharides into sugar phosphates (PMID: 28198470). This domain is the second of four domains (nDom2) found in the L. phytofermentans SOGP (sophoro-oligosaccharide beta-1,2-gluco-phosphorylase) (PMID: 28198470). This domain shows structural similarity to nDom1 (PMID: 28198470). The third domain is the catalytic GH94 domain (PMID: 28198470). (from Pfam)

label: Acyl-CoA-dh_C
comment: This is an all-alpha up-and-down bundle found in acyl-CoA dehydrogenases, such as Swiss:O32176 from Bacillus subtilis. (from Pfam)

label: SBB_T7
comment: Single-stranded DNA-binding proteins (SSB, also known as helix-destabilising proteins and gp2.5) from Bacteriophage T7 is expressed in the late stage of lytic development, binding binding preferentially to single-stranded DNA and is implicated in DNA replication, formation of concatemers, recombination and repair of double-stranded breaks (PMID: 11481454). It physically interacts with T7 DNA polymerase and T7 primase-helicase during replication to coordinate events at the replication fork (PMID: 11481454). (from Pfam)

label: YlmH_1st
comment: This is a domain found at the N-terminal of the Putative RNA-binding protein YlmH. (from Pfam)

label: YhfX-like_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of bacterial proteins, including Uncharacterized protein YhfX from Escherichia coli, which may be related to DNA recombination. The function of this domain is still unknown. It is often found associated to Pfam:PF01168. (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_RlmA
comment: This is the N-terminal zinc-binding domain of 23S rRNA (guanine(745)-N(1))-methyltransferase RlmA from E. coli and similar proteins, which is responsible for specific recognition and binding of its rRNA substrate (PMID: 14999102). (from Pfam)

label: type_II_gspD_N0
comment: GspD is a type II general secretion pathway protein involved in protein export. This is the N0 domain found at the N-terminal of GspD type II secretins and its close homologues [1-5]. These proteins form a dodecameric ring, in which the N0 domain mediate extensive contacts suggesting that dodecameric N0 ring is an important feature of T2SS secretins (PMID: 23820381). This domain is also found in virion export proteins, proteins thought to form a channel across the host outer membrane for the purposes of extruding the bacteriophage. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_RBD_prop
name_orig: Phage 5-bladed beta propeller receptor binding platform domain
comment: This entry represents the receptor binding domain of a variety of bacteriophage. The cell wall of S. aureus typically contains poly-ribitol phosphate type wall teichoic acid (WTA), which is modified with D-alanine and N-acetyl-glucosamine (GlcNAc). It has been shown that phage psi11 requires GlcNAc residues on WTA for adsorption8. Gp45 of phage psi11 was identified and characterized as the receptor-binding protein (RBP) (PMID: 27212064). This entry represents the 5 bladed beta propeller platform domain that has been suggested to bind to the GlcNac substrate (PMID: 27282779). (from Pfam)

label: HTH_66
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminus of the VapB45 protein that is thought to be part the antitoxin component of a Toxin-Antitoxin system. This domain adopts a helix-turn-helix structure that is likely to be a DNA-binding domain. (from Pfam)

label: Peptidase_M17_N_1
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of bacterial M17 aminopeptidases that contain Pfam:PF00883 at its C-terminal end. This domain has several highly conserved W and Y residues. (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_Thio2
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of thioredoxin 2, which is a zinc finger domain, unusual in thioredoxin proteins [1,2]. Thio2 reduces disulfide bonds and is an efficient electron donor for the essential enzyme ribonucleotide reductase. This domain may mediate protein-protein interactions (PMID: 17913712). (from Pfam)

label: MurD_N
comment: This is the N-terminal catalytic domain of MurD ligases (PMID: 23826965). (from Pfam)

label: Phage_pb10_N
comment: Bacteriophage capsids constitute icosahedral shells of exceptional stability that protect the viral genome. Many capsids display on their surface decoration proteins whose structure and function remain largely unknown. The decoration protein pb10 of phage T5 binds at the centre of the 120 hexamers formed by the major capsid protein (PMID: 28165000). Pb10 consists of an N-terminal alpha-helical capsid-binding domain (this entry) and an Ig-like domain (PMID: 28165000). (from Pfam)

label: Reelin_subrepeat-B
comment: Reelin is an extracellular matrix serine protease that plays a role in layering of neurons in the cerebral cortex and cerebellum. It regulates microtubule function in neurons and neuronal migration. It binds to the extracellular domains of lipoprotein receptors VLDLR and LRP8/APOER2 which induces tyrosine phosphorylation of DAB1 and modulation of TAU phosphorylation. Reelin consists of a signal sequence, an F-spondin-like region and nine sequentially concatenated repeat units. Each complete reelin repeat contains a central epidermal growth factor (EGF) module flanked by two subrepeats of 150-190 amino acids (subrepeats A and B) [1-3]. This entry represents subrepeat B (also referred to R3B) which adopts a beta jelly-roll fold similar to bacterial xylanase. They contain the signature Asp-box motif [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: gp6_C-domII
product_name: Baseplate structural protein gp6, C-terminal domain II
name_orig: Baseplate structural protein gp6, C-terminal domain II
hmm_name: Baseplate structural protein gp6, C-terminal domain II
comment: This entry represents domain II found in the C-terminal of gp6 from bacteriophage T4, which adopts a beta-barrel fold. This protein is involved in tail assembly. It forms the gp25-(gp6)2-gp7 module, involved in sheath contraction [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: YqbF_HeH
comment: This entry represents the HeH domain of the uncharacterised protein YqbF from Bacillus subtilis. (from Pfam)

label: ParM_N
comment: This entry consists of several bacterial ParM/StbA plasmid stability proteins [1-3]. ParM is involved in the control of plasmid partition and required for the accurate segregation of the plasmid, which forms filaments to drive partition. This protein is an actin homologue and consists of two domains (I and II) with the same conformation [1-3]. This entry represents the C-terminal domain. (from Pfam)

label: Stv
comment: This entry represents a putative adhesin domain found in gram negative bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: Gp34_2nd
product_name: Long-tail fiber proximal subunit, C-terminal, second
name_orig: Long-tail fiber proximal subunit, C-terminal, second
hmm_name: Long-tail fiber proximal subunit, C-terminal, second
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Long-tail fiber proximal subunit from Bacteriophage T4 (Gp34), an structural component of the proximal-half of the long-tail fiber. This protein adopts a trimeric configuration. This domain shows a core antiparallel beta-sheet (PMID: 28665339). (from Pfam)

label: CBM30
comment: This carbohydrate binding domain is found at the N-terminal end of Glycoside hydrolase family 9 (GH9) from Acetivibrio thermocellus (Swiss:A3DD30). This protein contains GH9 and GH44 as catalytic modules (Pfam:PF00759 and Pfam:PF12891). It also presents a family 30 carbohydrate binding domain (CBM30), which displays affinity for beta-1,4-glucopolymers and plays a pivotal role in the function of of GH9, a typical processive endoglucanase. This domain adopts a beta-sandwich fold with two five-stranded beta-sheets (PMID: 16314409). (from Pfam)

label: PvuRts1I-like_N
hmm_name: AbaSI family 5-hydroxymethylcytosine-specific restriction endonuclease, N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Restriction endonuclease PvuRts1 I from Proteus vulgaris and similar bacterial sequences. PvuRts1I a modification-dependent endonuclease with high selectivity for 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, an epigenetic marker that is crucial for multiple biological processes, over 5-methylcytosine and cytosine. This protein is organised into a nuclease domain (this entry) and a C-terminal SRA domain (Pfam:PF18491). This domain adopts a typical three- layered alpha-beta-alpha sandwich configuration, with a central five-stranded beta-sheet surrounded by three alpha-helices on one side and one alpha-helix on the other side [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6855
comment: This single domain protein is found a range of bacteria such as actinobacteria, bacteroidetes and firmicutes. It is functionally uncharacterised. The proteins are about 130 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: TetR-C_39
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Transcriptional regulator from Lactococcus lactis (YgfC, also known as heme- regulated transporter regulator, HrtR) and similar proteins predominantly from firmicutes. YgfC senses and binds a heme molecule to regulate the expression of the heme-efflux system responsible for heme homeostasis in this bacteria. This member of the TetR family of transcriptional regulators shows two helical domains and adopts a dimeric configuration (PMID: 22798069). This entry represents the heme-sensing (heme-binding) domain, which contains the alpha-helices that form the four-helix bundle that constitutes a dimer interface. (from Pfam)

label: pulA_all-beta
comment: This entry represents the all-beta domain found at the C-terminal of pullulanase A proteins, members of the glycosyl hydrolase family 13 (PMID: 19382205). (from Pfam)

label: WipA_Phos
comment: This entry represents the phosphatase domain of WipA protein from Legionella pneumophila. WipA is one of the effector proteins involved in pathogenesis and targets tyrosine-phosphorylated peptides (PMID: 28389563). (from Pfam)

label: T2SSK_1st
product_name: Type II secretion system (T2SS), protein K
name_orig: Type II secretion system (T2SS), protein K
hmm_name: Type II secretion system (T2SS), protein K
comment: Members of this family are involved in the Type II protein secretion system. The T2SK family includes proteins such as ExeK, PulK, OutX and XcpX. They consist of two tandem SAM-like domains, this entry represents the first one. (from Pfam)

label: TM1266-like
comment: This protein family includes Iron-only hydrogenase system regulator, putative from Thermotoga maritima (TM1266) and similar bacterial proteins. Members of this family are thought to play a role as a transcription factor. (from Pfam)

label: KaiA_N
product_name: Circadian clock protein KaiA, N-terminal domain
name_orig: Circadian clock protein KaiA, N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Circadian clock protein KaiA, N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Circadian clock protein KaiA from Synechococcus elongatus and similar bacterial proteins. KaiA is essential for circadian timekeeping. This protein organised into two domains. This entry represents the a pseudo-receiver domain, which has a similar fold with that of bacterial response regulators, with an alpha-beta structure [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6868
comment: This entry represents a small bacterial integral membrane protein of unknown function that is composed of two transmembrane helices. The function of this protein is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DACNK
comment: This entry represents a potential sensor domain found at the N-terminal of bacterial diadenylate cyclases, which is typically followed by the DAC (Pfam:PF02457) domain. This domain is mainly found in actinobacteria and cyanobacteria; structure predictions suggest that this domain may consist of five alpha-helices and five beta-strands. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6873
comment: This family is uncharacterized but is described as having a five fold symmetric alpha/beta propeller fold belonging to the GME (guanidino-group modifying enzymes) superfamily.

label: DUF6877
comment: This entry represents a small family of short uncharacterised proteins. They are predicted to adopt a three helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6881
comment: This entry represents a small bacterial protein of unknown function. Its predicted structure shows a 6 stranded beta sheet with a C-terminal helix packed on one side. In a few proteins this domain is associated with Pfam:PF15595 a presumed immunity protein, which could suggest this domain may have a toxin function or be involved in a toxin/antitoxin system or in phage defence. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6883
comment: This entry represents a protein domain that is often found in single domain proteins. It is also sometimes found in larger multi-domain proteins. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6886
comment: This is a family of proteins whose function is unknown. They may be distantly related to ADP-ribosylating toxins. (from Pfam)

label: Xrt_dep_XDD4
comment: XDD4 (exosortase-dependent surface domain 4) is the fourth in a series of domains or full-length proteins that appear always, or nearly always, to have a C-terminal sorting signal such as PEP-CTERM that is recognized and processed by XrtA or another exosortase.

label: HepA_fam_ABC
product_name: heterocyst formation ABC transporter subunit HepA
hmm_name: heterocyst formation ABC transporter subunit HepA
comment: HepA is an apparent ABC transporter subunit, with an N-terminal permease domain and a C-terminal ATP-binding cassette domain. HepA is required for assembly of an envelope polysaccharide layer that is required for heterocyst formation.

label: Glp_gephyrin
comment: Glp (gephyrin-like protein), a molybdotransferase-like protein involved in cell division in Actinobacteria, is related to the eukaryotic protein gephyrin, which has a scaffolding role in post-synaptic membranes in neuronal cells and an unrelated role in molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis in non-neuronal cells. In Corynebacterium, Glp and its membrane receptor SepX/GlpR bind to FtsZ and Wag31 to form a tight protein complex, which plays an important role in divisome-elongasome transition. A molybdotransferase role for Glp should not be assumed, as genomes with Glp are paralogous to authentic MoeA proteins, described by model NF050098.

label: MXAN_6640_HExxH
comment: Members of this domain family are probably metalloproteases with an invariant HExxH motif. The domain may be found as a surface-anchored protein, as various members have the MYXO_CTERM sorting domain, the CFI-box-CTERM domain (NF041770), or the T9SS type A sorting domain. Pfam model PF19527 (DUF6055) overlaps somewhat with this family.

label: LegP
product_name: Dot/Icm T4SS effector Zinc-dependent metalloprotease LegP
hmm_name: Dot/Icm T4SS effector Zinc-dependent metalloprotease LegP

label: small_EYxxD
comment: This small protein has an EYxxD-like motif (for which it is named) near its N-terminus, a 20-residue highly hydrophobic stretch, and a short, positively charged region rich in Lys and Arg residues, for an average length in one clade of 36 residues. Strong upstream RBS motifs, ATG start codons, appropriate amino acid substitution patterns, and broad conservation in the Bacillales lineage all provide evidence for interpreting members as real proteins, despite the small size. Most or all members are encoded adjacent to a DUF2892 domain-containing protein (PF11127). A founding member of this family is BH0635 from Bacillus halodurans C-125. In one clade within this family, members typically are encoded with the tail (3-prime) end of the coding region overlapping with the tail end of the purD gene.

label: scaf_prot_MCP2
product_name: prohead protease/major capsid protein fusion protein
hmm_name: prohead protease/major capsid protein fusion protein

label: Clp_rel_HeadMat
comment: Members of this family may be found as free-standing proteins that are phage head maturation proteases, or as the N-terminal domain of phage fusion proteins that include a longer major capsid protein region.

label: aroma_sacti_dom
comment: The aroma-sacti cluster domain appears to be found exclusively in biosynthetic gene clusters (BGC) that include both a radical SAM/SPASM domain peptide maturase and RiPP precursor peptide. In some cases, the domain ocurrs in the N-terminal region of RiPP precursors with known sulfur-to-alpha-carbon (sacti) bonds formed between a Cys and a Gly residue (see model NF045559 for examples). Other members of the family (e.g. WP_083192440.1) lack the critical Cys residues, but instead have an aromatic C-terminal residue, either Phe or Trp. Strangely, however, some members of the family have long N-terminal extensions with domain content suggesting MFS transporter activity.

label: HepHepsulflyase
comment: heparinase II

label: sacti_mat_StsB
product_name: StsB family radical SAM/SPASM domain sactipeptide maturase
hmm_name: StsB family radical SAM/SPASM domain sactipeptide maturase
comment: Members of this family are radical SAM/SPASM enzymes that modify RiPP precursor peptides to introduce sulfur-to-alpha-carbon amino acid side chain crosslinks. Peptides modified in this way are often called sactipeptides. The enzyme crosslinks Cys residues to Gly residues in antiparallel peptide chain motifs of CxCxC to GxGxG in StsA, and CxC to GxG in related peptides.

label: export_MbnM
comment: Members of this family of MATE type efflux transporter occur in methanobactin biosynthesis loci and are presumed to function in the export of methanobactin, a siderophore analog that is synthesized, exported so that it can bind copper ion with high affinity, and then reimported.

label: PG0541_fam
comment: The founding member of this family, PG0541 (AAQ65733) from Porphyromonas gingivalis, is found as the fourth gene in the operon that encodes the RND efflux pump XepCAB. The average member is about 100 amino acids in length. Similar contexts are seen for the majority of family members, in lineages as diverse as Treponema, Borrelia, Thermotomaculum, Pelotomaculum, Lujinxingia, and Fusobacterium. Members of this family have at least superficial similarity to the nitrogen regulatory protein P-II (see PF00543), the significance of which is unclear.

label: Npun_R2479_HDIG
comment: This family, found primarily in the subset of Cyanobacteria that contain cyanoexosortase B (CrtB), contains the signature HDIG motif of HD domain proteins.

label: bili_reduct_N
comment: Members of this family are the enzyme bilirubin reductase, as found in the gut microbiome (e.g. WP_021359617.1 from Clostridioides difficile), or longer proteins that functionality in the N-terminal domain (e.g. WP_009244284.1 from Mediterraneibacter gnavus). Bilirubin, a heme breakdown product excreted in bile into the human gut, is converted to urobilinogen by gut bacteria, in a process protective against jaundice from bilirubin reabsorption. Urobilinogen oxidizes to urobilin, which gives urine its yellow color.

label: flavodox_BilS
comment: BilS is a flavodoxin-like protein, regularly found in operons with the bilirubin reductase BilR and the MarR family transcriptional regular BilQ, primarily in Gram-positive bacteria of the gut microbiome.

label: bili_reduct_long
comment: Bilirubin is a haem by-product excreted into the human gut through bile, and an excess of bilirubin in the blood can lead to neurological damage. Proteins belonging to this family are bilirubin reductases (BilR) of the long form, which convert bilirubin into urobilinogen. BilR is present in various bacteria, including Clostridium symbiosum, Clostridioides difficile, and Mediterraneibacter gnavus, within the gastrointestinal tract and related species.

label: xseB_Acin_var
hmm_name: exodeoxyribonuclease VII small subunit, variant type
comment: This HMM represents variant forms of the exodeoxyribonuclease VII small subunit (XseB), as found in Acinetobacter rather than in Escherichia coli. Members mostly fall outside the reach of TIGRFAMs model TIGR01280. Members score typically near and sometimes below the cutoffs of Pfam HMM version PF02609.19.

label: exo_Victor_syst
comment: Members of this hydrophobic protein family are found associated with the protein-sorting cysteine endopeptidase XrtV (exosortase V as in Victor), and likely participate in the proper targeting and localization of client PEP-CTERM proteins. The system is seen the most often in the genus Sphingomonas.

label: EpsI_type_V
comment: This variant form of EpsI occurs with the type V (as in Victor) exosortase, XrtV, involved in sorting a subclass of PEP-CTERM proteins to the cell surface.

label: small_CydP
product_name: cytochrome oxidase putative small subunit CydP
hmm_name: cytochrome oxidase putative small subunit CydP
comment: Members of this family are small proteins with a highly hydrophobic core region. Because they are invariably found in the context of larger subunits of cytochrome bd oxidases, they are presumed to be small subunit or assembly factor.

label: GCX_COOH
comment: This homology domain is most often seen as the C-terminal domain of a larger protein, typically with Gly-Cys-Xaa(-Xaa) as the last three (or four) amino acids, or just upstream from type IX secretion system (T9SS) C-terminal sorting signal domain. The fold prediction for AlphaFoldDB entry A0A6M5Y4F8 shows a mostly beta structure for this domain with the backbone resembling a stack of three wire coathangers, the first of which is the most poorly conserved and mostly trimmed from the seed alignment.

label: DVU_1557_fam
comment: This family of putative redox proteins includes DVU_1557 from Desulfovibrio vulgaris, as well as the related paralogs CLJU_RS11820 and CLJU_RS11860 from Clostridium ljungdahlii. Members are found in an extended conserved gene neighborhood that also includes a molybdopterin-dependent aldehyde oxidoreductase (see NF045668) and the radical SAM (seleno)protein TrsS (NF045646). The presence in Clostridium ljungdahlii, a species apparently without heme biosynthesis, has implications for the electron transfer pathways to which the proteins of the conserved gene neighborhood contribute.

label: CD1247_Nterm
comment: This HMM describes the N-terminal domain of a family of proteins names after CD1247 from Clostridioides difficile and found primarily in Gram-positive anaerobes. Most members share a C-terminal region with two CxxC motifs likely to have zinc-binding activity.

label: diclust_near_Sec
comment: Founding members of this family include the short protein CLJU_RS11820 (WP_013239051.1) from Clostridium ljungdahlii and the C-terminal domain of the fusion protein DVU_1557 from FAD-binding pyridine nucleotide-disulfide oxidoreductase and CCG domain pair iron-sulfur cluster-binding oxidoreductase. Member proteins appear in a large conserved gene neighborhood with a molybdenum-dependent aldehyde dehydrogenase, and with the radical SAM enzyme TrsS, a few of whose members are encoded as selenoproteins.

label: XdhC_rel_AOR
product_name: XdhC family aldehyde oxidoreductase maturation factor
hmm_name: XdhC family aldehyde oxidoreductase maturation factor
comment: This XdhC-like protein is a proposed maturation factor for molybdopterin-dependent aldehyde oxidoreductase. It is regularly found encoded near the aldehyde oxidoreductase (NF045668) and of the radical SAM (seleno)protein TrsS (NF045646).

label: NTPtran_DVU1551
comment: Members of this family occur regularly in the context of a molybdopterin-dependent aldehyde oxidoreductase (see NF045668) and of the radical SAM (seleno)protein TrsS. The N-terminal 200 amino acids are homologous to the molybdenum cofactor cytidylyltransferase MocA of Escherichia coli. The C-terminal 170 amino acid region contains an HDIG (or HD superfamily) phosphohydrolase-like domain. This family is likely to be involved biosynthesis of the molybdopterin cofactor used by the aldehyde oxidoreductase.

label: DVU1553_fam_AMP
comment: Members of this family are AMP-dependent CoA ligases, fairly closely related to the phenylacetate--CoA ligase PaaK, and found regularly in the conserved gene neighborhood of the molybdopterin-dependent aldehyde oxidoreductase described by model NF045668. Part of that conserved gene neighborhood is the radical SAM (seleno)protein TrsS (NF045646).

label: MTase_DVU1556
comment: This family of methyltransferases occurs exclusively in the context of a molybdopterin-dependent aldehyde oxidoreductase (see NF045668) and surrounding proteins, including the unusual radical SAM enzyme TrsS, some of whose members are selenoproteins.

label: pterin_aldehy
comment: Members of this family are molybdopterin-dependent enzyme that perform oxidative hydroxylation of aldehydes. Members are encoded in an eight-gene context that includes a radical SAM enzyme we designate TrsS, as it is the Third Radical SAM (Seleno)protein family discovered to have at least some members encoded with a selenocysteine (Sec, U) replacing an otherwise conserved Cys residue.

label: DVU1555_fam_CGA
comment: Members of this family are found regularly near a molybdopterin-dependent aldehyde oxidoreductase (NF045668) and the radical SAM (seleno)protein TrsS (NF045646).

label: quin_L_LdhH
comment: Members of this family, such as founding protein DVU3033 from Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, contain an N-terminal lactate utilization (LUD) domain (see PF02589) as found in lactate utilization proteins LutB and LutC in Bacillus subtilis, but also a C-terminal GlpC-like domain. This enzyme differs from both NAD-dependent and cytochrome-dependent L-lactate dehydrogenases.

label: MCP_gp7_epsi_15
hmm_name: phage major capsid protein, epsilon15 Gp7 family
comment: This is a family of phage major capsid proteins. Gp7 from phage epsilon15 has a solved crystal structure. This family is similar to Pfam family PF05065 and to encapsulins.

label: rubredox_RCKP
comment: This domain HMM describes an uncharacterized variant form of rubredoxin-like full-length protein, about 35 amino acids long, or domain in a larger protein. Of the five invariant Cys residues in the seed alignment, the first two and last two are shared with typical rubredoxin-like domains, but the central Cys, in a well-conserved Arg-Cys-Lys-Pro, is distinctive.

label: XXplasma_LP
product_name: Vmc-like lipoprotein signal peptide domain-containing protein
comment: Lipoprotein signal peptides in the Mollicutes genera Mycoplasma, Ureaplasma, Mesoplasma, Spiroplasma, Williamsoniiplasma, etc. are distinctive enough to behave as a homology domain. Lipoproteins from a number of different paralogous families, including the Vnc family from Mycoplasma capricolum, are detected by this HMM. This model has extensive overlap with NF038029, which likewise was built to detect lipoprotein sequence peptide-containing proteins in the Mollicutes.

label: StyMonoxStyB
product_name: styrene monooxygenase NADH-dependent flavin reductase subunit StyB
hmm_name: styrene monooxygenase NADH-dependent flavin reductase subunit StyB

label: cytochro_C551
comment: CccB (c-type cytochrome c551) differs from its close homolog CccA by having a lipoprotein signal peptide.

label: PT-DNA_restrict
comment: Members of this family are somewhat distantly related to the C-terminal half of the type IV restriction endonuclease McrA from Streptomyces coelicolor (WP_011029780.1). That enzyme can act on phosphorothioated DNA (PT-DNA), as do members of this family.

label: seleno_TsoX
comment: This rare selenoprotein family, with about 100 known members, has a UxxC selenocysteine-containing motif immediately preceded by a signature motif HSGNPX. More than 95 percent of family members contain selenocysteine. At least five members are fusion proteins with a C-terminal thioredoxin-disulfide reductase (EC 1.8.1.9) region (see TIGR01292). Members of this family are given the gene symbol TsoX (Three Selenoprotein Operon protein X), as it occasionally occurs in the same operon as selenoproteins TsoA, TsoB, and TsoC.

label: restrict_HinfI
product_name: HinfI family type II restriction enzyme
hmm_name: HinfI family type II restriction enzyme
comment: Members of this family are type II restriction enzymes. The founding member, HinfI from Haemophilus influenzae, has the recognition sequence GANTC.

label: restrict_HpyAIV
product_name: HpyAIV family type II restriction enzyme
hmm_name: HpyAIV family type II restriction enzyme
comment: The founding member of this family, HP1351 from Helicobacter pylori 26695, designated HpyAIV by the restriction enzyme database REBASE, is a type II restriction enzyme that recognizes GANTC.

label: ICE_MMCAP2_0565
product_name: Mbov_0395 family pilin-like conjugal transfer protein
hmm_name: Mbov_0395 family pilin-like conjugal transfer protein
comment: Members of this family, such as Mbov_0395 and MMCAP2_0565, occur in Integrative Conjugal Element (ICE) regions, as in Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri str. GM12. The family overlaps with family of putative type IV secretion system pilin proteins described in Pfam model PF18895.

label: conj_pls20_p028
product_name: pLS20_p028 family conjugation system transmembrane protein
hmm_name: pLS20_p028 family conjugation system transmembrane protein
comment: Members of this family are large, membrane-embedded proteins of mobile elements such as the Bacillus subtilis natto plasmid pLS20, and show distant relationships to better characterized VirB-like conjugal transfer proteins. This family also shows homology to the family of Mbov_0396-like transmembrane proteins found in ICE elements of Mycoplasmopsis bovis and related species. The Transporter Classification Database (TCDB) assigns 3.A.7.13.2 to the plasmid pLS20-like conjugation system, whose member proteins include VirB1, VirB4, VirB11, VirD2, and VirD4 homologs.

label: PKS_plus_SDR
hmm_name: type I polyketide synthase with SDR domain
comment: This HMM describes a recurring sub-architecture, about 1500 amino acids long, with an SDR (short-chain alcohol reductase) at its C-terminus, in addition to a trio of domains shared by all type I polyketide synthases. While the actual function of member proteins is specific to the natural product made, this model is assigned family type equivalog_domain to elevate its precedence in automated annotation software and prevent the misapplication of even more generic annotation.

label: tail_region
comment: Members of this family of small proteins, about 60 amino acids long, regularly are found encoded in the tail regions of apparent prophage regions of bacterial genomes.

label: SCO3242_trans
comment: Members of this family, found in Streptomyces and related lineages, resemble prenyltransferases such as geranylgeranylglycerol-phosphate geranylgeranyltransferase (EC 2.5.1.42) and 4-hydroxybenzoate polyprenyltransferase (EC 2.5.1.39), but are uncharacterized.

label: MAG4270_fam
comment: Members of this family are largely restricted to the Mycoplasmatota, including members of the genera Mycoplasma, Mycoplasmopsis, and Spiroplasma. The C-terminal region is distantly related to the type II restriction enzyme HphI and to HNH family endonucleases (see PF13391). Members regularly are found encoded next to a MAG4250 family DNA (cytosine-5-)-methyltransferase (EC 2.1.1.37), supporting the notion that this endonuclease activity acts in restriction.

label: restrict_UpaP162
product_name: UpaP162 family type II restriction enzyme
hmm_name: UpaP162 family type II restriction enzyme

label: conju_CD1110
product_name: VirB4-like conjugal transfer ATPase, CD1110 family
hmm_name: VirB4-like conjugal transfer ATPase, CD1110 family
comment: Members of this family average 800 amino acids in length, resemble VirB4 of type IV secretory systems, and appear to be involved in DNA transfer as by conjugative transposons or plasmids. Member proteins include CD630_11100 (CD1110), CD630_18560 (CD1856), and CD630_04180 (CD0418) from the model strain Clostridium difficile 630, and gbs1135 from the Enterococcus faecalis conjugative plasmid pCF10.

label: conju_CD1115
product_name: VirD4-like conjugal transfer protein, CD1115 family
hmm_name: VirD4-like conjugal transfer protein, CD1115 family

label: conju_CD1108
hmm_name: CD1108 family mobile element protein, central domain

label: MAG1210_fam
comment: Members of this family are found mostly within Mycoplasma-like bacteria, but occasionally in other lineages.

label: RespRegCpdRBruc
product_name: cell cycle two-component system response regulator CpdR
hmm_name: cell cycle two-component system response regulator CpdR

label: carphisopro
comment: The carph-isopro domain is about 60 amino acids long, is composed mostly of alpha-helical structure, and contains a near-invariant Trp residue. It name derives from its frequent appearance as a prefix domain to the carbamoyl-phosphate synthase small subunit and to 2-isopropylmalate synthase.

label: rep_init_NGO0469
product_name: phage replication initiation protein, NGO0469 family
hmm_name: phage replication initiation protein, NGO0469 family

label: citrull_CtlX
comment: This enzyme, designated CtlX, is known from mutational studies to be important for the utilization of both citrulline and orrnithine. It is often encoded next to ornithine cyclodeaminase. While it is presumed to be a hydrolase that acts on citrulline, the exact enzymatic function is unknown.

label: oxepin_alt
comment: This protein was identified as a probable oxepin-CoA hydrolase, an enzyme of a phenylacetate degradation pathway, based on a computational analysis of loss of fitness mutants in high throughput-generated TnSeq mutation data.

label: monocarbox_MctP
comment: Members of this family, while related to the sodium:solute symporter family, seem to be symporters of H+ with panels of monocarboxylate solutes. The first characterized member, the MctP of Rhizobium leguminosarum, was found to transport alanine, pyruvate, and lactate, among other monocarboxylates, and to prefer three-carbon compounds as substrates.

label: LPS_M949_RS01915
product_name: M949_RS01915 family surface polysaccharide biosynthesis protein
hmm_name: M949_RS01915 family surface polysaccharide biosynthesis protein
comment: Disruption of the founding member of the family, M949_RS01915 from the Gram-negative duck pathogen Riemerella anatipestifer, causes a defect in lipopolysaccharide (LPS) structure with altered serology and apparent changes in O-antigen structure. Homologs are found in about three percent of bacteria. Homologs are likely to be involved in some way in surface polysaccharide biosynthesis, but it has not been shown that the affected pathway product will always be LPS.

label: STM4504_CBY0614
comment: Members of this family share an N-terminal AbiJ-NTD4 domain (see PF18863), but are full-length homologs. STM4504 from Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium was predicted as a possible secreted virulence effector.

label: BFO_1060_trans
comment: BFO_1060 from Tannerella forsythia, a founding member of this family, is proposed to be a glycosyltransferase for a pseudaminic or legionaminic acid derivative.

label: CD3337_EF1877
comment: Members of this family regularly are found in mobile elements. Only the N-terminal 450 amino acids or so are well-conserved. That portion is strongly hydrophobic the protein is predicted to embed in the membrane. Members of this family appear to have at least local sequence similarity with TrbL/VirB6 family conjugal transfer proteins (see PF04610).

label: AZOBR_p60025_fam
product_name: AZOBR_p60025 family cell surface glycopolymer formation protein
hmm_name: AZOBR_p60025 family cell surface glycopolymer formation protein
comment: Members of this family, including AZOBR_p60025 from a plasmid of Azospirillum brasilense, are apparent membrane proteins of surface polysaccharide biosynthesis. A region within the seed alignment shows distant sequence similarity to the dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase family described by PF13231, suggesting glycosyltransferase activity.

label: RSP_7527_fam
comment: The hypothetical protein RSP_7527 from the facultative phototrophic alphaproteobacterium Rhodobacter sphaeroides is notable because a 67 nucleotide small structural RNA, UdsC (UTR-derived sRNA C), derives from the 3'-untranslated region of its mRNA. Homologs of RSP_7527 are found in about two percent of bacterial proteomes.

label: MSMEG_6209_Nter
comment: This uncharacterized domain, about 56 amino acids long, occurs most often at the N-terminus of proteins from the Actinomycetes. In Cg_ArsC1', the region is a three-helix bundle responsible for dimerization (see PDB:3t38), in an N-terminal extension region that most other arsenate reductases lack.

label: SCO4848_fam
comment: SCO4848 from Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2) is a 79 amino acid putative membrane protein. It is best known for having the integration site for Streptomyces phage phiBT1 lie within its gene. Homologs of SCO4848 are found broadly within Streptomyces, Saccharomonospora, Arthrobacter, and Nocardioides, and related genera.

label: memb_SCO4225
comment: This founding member of this protein, SCO4225, is regulated by MacR, a response regulator transcription factor that also controls expression of morphogenic membrane protein A (MmpA; SCO6728), MmpB (SCO4924), and MmpC (SCO4011), all of them physical interaction partners with SCO4225. Some homologs of SCO4225, such as WP_019072487.1 and WP_062708824.1, are nearly twice as long because of a duplication.

label: DUF6899
comment: This entry represents a bacterial protein of unknown function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6900
comment: This entry represents a small domain found in a range of bacterial and phage proteins. In a few proteins it is associated with Pfam:PF11994. This region is composed of two alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6904
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of bacterial proteins. Members of the family are about 250 residues in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6906
comment: This entry represents a small domain found in a range of phage and bacterial proteins. Structurally it is composed of a three stranded beta meander packed against an alpha helix. The function of these proteins is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6910
comment: The function of this family of proteins is unknown. They are predicted to adopt a five-bladed beta-propeller and are probably distantly related to apyrase. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6912
comment: This is a family of uncharacterized proteins.Their predicted structure shows some similarity to ADP-rybosylating toxins. (from Pfam)

label: Glyco_transf_99
product_name: GT99 family glycosyltransferase N-terminal domain-containing protein
comment: This entry represents the Glycosyltransferase 99 family N-terminal domain, which is found in a new family of glycosyltransferases (GTs) assigned as family GT99 in the CAZy database. The GT99 family includes a prototype beta-Kdo GT from WbbB, a modular protein participating in lipopolysaccharide (LPS) O-antigen synthesis in Raoultella terrigena. Kdo (3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid) is an eight-carbon sugar mostly found in Gram-negative bacteria, where it is involved in attaching surface polysaccharides to their lipid anchors. Alpha-Kdo provides a bridge between lipid A and the core oligosaccharide in all bacterial LPSs, while an oligosaccharide of beta-Kdo residues links group 2 capsular polysaccharides to (lyso)phosphatidylglycerol. beta-Kdo is also found in a small number of other bacterial polysaccharides. The structure and function of the prototypical cytidine monophosphate-Kdo-dependent alpha-Kdo glycosyltransferase from LPS assembly is well characterized. The WbbB2-401 protein structure is built around two alpha/beta domains with recognizable Rossmann-fold topology, broadly meeting the criteria of conforming to a GT-B fold. (from Pfam)

label: SOGP_N
comment: This is the N-terminal domain of 1,2-beta oligoglucan phosphorylase (SOGP). This enzyme phosphorolyzes beta-1,2-glucooligosaccharides (sophorooligosaccharides, Sops) with degrees of polymerization (DP) of 3 or more. It consists of four domains: two beta-sandwich domains, (alpha/alpha)6 catalytic domain and a beta-sheet domain. The N-terminal domain adopts a supersandwich fold in which 18 beta-strands define two beta-sheets (PMID: 28198470). (from Pfam)

label: MGS_C
comment: Mannosylglycerate synthase catalyses the formation of the stress protectant 2-O-alpha-D-mannosyl glycerate (PMID: 15951819). It consists of a GT-like domain at the N-terminal and a C-terminal helical domain, represented in this entry, that is apparently involved in protein oligomerization (PMID: 15951819). (from Pfam)

label: HisZ-like
comment: HisZ is composed of two domains for the catalytic reaction and for anticodon binding. In contrast to other class-II aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases it lacks the essential editing domain. The C-terminal anicodon binding domain consists of three-stranded parallel beta-sheet flanked on each side with helices. (from Pfam)

label: OrtA
comment: This entry represents 2-amino-4-ketopentanoate thiolase (also known as AKP thiolase) subunit OrtA. OrtA is a subunit of a PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyses the thiolytic cleavage with coenzyme A (CoA) to form acetyl-CoA and alanine. OrtA is predicted to adopt a beta-barrel structurally similar to the beta-barrel of Tudor/PWWP/MBT superfamily. (from Pfam)

label: FabMG
product_name: enoyl ACP reductase FabMG family protein
comment: FabMG is a triclosan-insensitive from of enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase, found in bacteria of triclosan-contaminated soils.

label: DUF6939
comment: This is a family of bacterial proteins with unknown function. They share sequence similarity with the N-terminal part of NADAR domain and are predicted to adopt structure that is globally similar to the structure of E.coli protein YbiA, a member of the NADAR domain family. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6940
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria and eukaryotes. These proteins are probably distantly related to HIT-containing uridylyltransferases and are likely to adopt the same structure. (from Pfam)

label: Mtrc-MtrF_II-IV_dom
name_orig: Outer membrane cytochrome MtrC/MtrF-like, domains II/IV
comment: This entry includes decaheme cytochrome c component MtrC from the MtrCAB complex and its homologues MtrF (which is part of the MtrFDE complex) and OmcA. In Shewanella oneidensis, these proteins are located at the bacterial cell surface at the termini of trans-outer-membrane electron transfer conduits and allow the utilization of extracellular mineral forms of iron and manganese as respiratory electron acceptors [5,6]. MtrC/MtrF/OmcA consist of four domains: domain I and III containing seven antiparallel beta-strands in an extended Greek key topology; domains II and IV each bind five tightly packed hemes covalently attached to the Cys residues of the five CXXCH motifs in each domain and form the central core, flanked by domains I (Pfam:PF22111) and III [5,6]. This entry represents domains II and IV. (from Pfam)

label: DM_Arn
comment: This entry represents Arn (Anti-restriction nuclease) proteins found in Caudoviricetes phages. The structure of Arn consists of a three- stranded, anti-parallel beta-sheet on one side, while on the otherside, four alpha-helices are bundled together. Arn was identified as an inhibitor of the restriction enzyme McrBC. A structural analysis of Arn revealed that its shape and negative charge distribution are similar to dsDNA, suggesting that this protein could act as a DNA mimic (PMID: 25118281). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6946
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either standalone or in combination with other domains. It is distantly related to the type II restriction endonucleases with predicted similar active site architecture. These proteins are most likely endonucleases based on the strict conservation of the putative active site residues. (from Pfam)

label: Cas_Csm6_6H
comment: This entry includes Csm6 from bacteria (i.e Enterococcus italicus), a Cas (CRISPR-associated) protein from type III-A CRISPR-Cas system. It consists of a CARF domain at the N-terminal, a six-helix (6H) domain and a C-terminal HEPN domain at the C-terminal, which has RNase activity (PMID: 32221291). This is the 6H domain (PMID: 32221291). (from Pfam)

label: TraI_hel_assoc_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal fragment of the helicase-associated ssDNA binding domain of the conjugative transfer relaxase/helicase TraI [1,2]. This domain adopts a globular structure that closely resembles that of the RecD N-terminal despite little sequence similarity [1,2]. It is part of a larger domain, referred to as vestigial helicase domain, that functions as a ssDNA binding domain [1,2]. This region doesn't have helicase activity or measurable DNA binding affinity itself but it may play a role in either DNA unwinding or regulation of ssDNA transfer from host to recipient cell. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6947
comment: This is a domain found in a group of uncharacterised bacterial sequences whose function is unknown. This domain adopts a galactose-binding-like structure (PDBe:4lr4). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6948
comment: This domain is found either as standalone or in combination with other domains in a group of uncharacterised proteins. It is distantly related to EDC3 mRNA-decapping protein 3 and it could be involved in RNA-binding. It is predicted to adopt a barrel-like structure with a typical Sm-like fold. The pair of glycines responsible for maintaining the Sm-barrel curvature are also conserved in the members of this family. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6959
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They contain conserved Pro-Gly-rich motif with a semi- conserved pattern PGRxFPGx3QGD. (from Pfam)

label: CydS
product_name: cytochrome bd oxidase small subunit CydS
hmm_name: cytochrome bd oxidase small subunit CydS
comment: This entry represents the CydS subunit of the cytochrome bd oxidase (PMID: 27126043). This protein is very short and forms a single alpha helix that is part of the complex (PMID: 27126043). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6960
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are composed of two tandem domains with similarity to SH3 domains, in particular to YorP. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6961
comment: This is a family of small, about 60 residues in length, bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of three helices. The N- and C-terminal helices contain highly conserved aromatic residues in addition to the nearly invariant glycines located at the interhelical connecting loops. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6972
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either standalone or in combination with other domains. It is probably distantly related to the C-terminal domain of CdiA toxin (CdiA-CT), known member of RNase A superfamily. (from Pfam)

label: Pyruv_OxRed_insertion
comment: This entry represents the insertion domain of Pyruvate-flavodoxin oxidoreductases [1,2], which adopts a four helical bundle fold. (from Pfam)

label: YgxA-like_sub_bind
comment: This entry represents the substrate binding domain of YgxA from Bacillus subtilis and similar sequences. (from Pfam)

label: GSPE_N1E
comment: GSPE is an ATPase component of the type II secretion system required for the energy-dependent secretion of extracellular factors such as proteases and toxins from the periplasm. This entry represents the N1E domain at its N-terminal end which associates with the cytoplasmic domain of the inner membrane protein GspL [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Fervidolysin_SD2
comment: This entry represents the second beta-sandwich domain (SD2) present in fervidolysin (keratinolytic enzyme) (PMID: 14687574). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6975
comment: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found in Proteobacteria. It shares significant sequence similarity with enzymes members of Heme oxygenase-like superfamily and are predicted to adopt similar structure consisting of a bundle of six alpha-helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6981
comment: This entry represents an alpha-lytic protease prodomain-like domain present in a protein of unknown function from Desulfovibrio piger. It structure has been characterized (PDB:4HLB). (from Pfam)

label: Hia_Tpr_ring_dom
product_name: Trimeric autotransporter adhesin, Trp ring domain
name_orig: Trimeric autotransporter adhesin, Trp ring domain
hmm_name: Trimeric autotransporter adhesin, Trp ring domain
comment: This domain is found in Adhesin from Haemophilus influenzae (Hia) and similar proteins predominantly from proteobacteria. Hia is a trimeric autotransporter that mediates bacterial adherence to the respiratory epithelium. This protein shows a modular architecture with repeats of structurally distinct domains. This entry represents one of the Trp-ring domains (PMID: 18948113). (from Pfam)

label: HutF_N
comment: This small domain is found at the N-terminal end of Formimidoylglutamate deiminase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (also known as N-formimino-L-Glutamate Iminohydrolase, HutF) and similar proteins predominantly found in proteobacteria. HutF catalyzes he deamination of N-formimino-l-glutamate to N-formyl-l-glutamate and ammonia in the histidine degradation pathway (PMID: 25559274). The domain represented by this entry folds into an open beta-barrel which is completed by two strands located at the C terminus of the protein. (from Pfam)

label: CLIC-like_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of chloride ion channels CLIC and related sequences. (from Pfam)

label: Gp49_Pectate_lyase_like
product_name: phage tailspike polysaccharide lyase family protein
hmm_name: phage tailspike polysaccharide lyase family protein
comment: This entry represents the beta-helix repeats from the catalytic domain of tailspike Gp49 from phage LKA1 (PMID: 29176754). Gp49 binds and cleaves B-band LPS of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, reducing its virulence (PMID: 29176754). (from Pfam)

label: YhfS-like_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the uncharacterised protein YhfS from E.coli and similar sequences. This is an alpha/beta domain commonly found in PLP-dependent enzymes. (from Pfam)

label: RepD-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Replication initiation protein from Staphylococcus aureus (RepD) and similar bacterial sequences. RepD shows similarity with the extended beta-sheet in TATA binding protein (TBP) (PMID: 26792891). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6988
comment: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found mainly in Proteobacteria. These proteins are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure. They contain a highly conserved RXXXE-motif and an invariant histidine that may have a functional role. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_92
comment: This is a helix-turn-helix (HTH) domain found in quorum-sensing regulator RsaL and related proteins. (from Pfam)

label: H2TH_5
comment: This entry represents helix-two turn-helix (H2TH) domains that is found in ribosomal S13 proteins and related proteins. (from Pfam)

label: TY-Chap2
name_orig: T3SS (YopN, CesT) and YbjN peptide-binding chaperone 2
comment: This domain is observed in host systems predicted to counter viral ribosylating toxins. They are predicted to function as peptide-binding chaperone domains that target proteins modified by ADPr and potentially misfolded as a consequence. (from Pfam)

label: iREC
comment: iREC is predicted to dimerize with active counterparts as part of signal transduction relays in a subset of TOTE (TPR, OB, TBP, Effector) biological conflict systems (PMID: 35609893). (from Pfam)

label: CFAP143
comment: This family represents the homologues of Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 143 (CFAP143, also known as SPAG8). CFAP143 is one of the core microtubule inner proteins (MIPs) of the doublet microtubules (DMTs) in cilia and sperm axoneme [1,2]. It binds to protofilaments A09-A13 in the sperm DMTs. CFAP143 was found to play a role in regulation of the cell cycle by controlling progression through the G2/M phase (PMID: 19548270). (from Pfam)

label: Sialidase-like_CBM
comment: This entry represents a carbohydrate binding module (CBM) found in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DNA_polI_exo1
product_name: DNA polymerase I, ribonuclease H-like domain
name_orig: DNA polymerase I, ribonuclease H-like domain
hmm_name: DNA polymerase I, ribonuclease H-like domain
comment: This domain is responsible for the 3'-5' exonuclease proofreading activity of E. coli DNA polymerase I (polI) and other related enzymes. It is one of the constituent domains of Klenow fragment. (from Pfam)

label: OYE-like_second_a-b
comment: This domain is found in a group of diverse dehydrogenases from the old yellow enzyme (OYE)-like family, such as histamine dehydrogenase from Nocardioides simplex, trimethylamine dehydrogenase from Methylophilus methylotrophus (sp. W(3)A(1)) and 2-naphthoyl-CoA reductase (NCR) [1-4], which has been described as a small, second alpha/beta domain [3,4]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7008
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains a number of highly conserved positively charged residues that may have functional role. (from Pfam)

label: Exo_endo_phos2
comment: This large family of proteins includes a number of nucleases and phosphatases such as DNAase I, Exonuclease III and Phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate 5-phosphatase [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: GalA_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Alpha-galactosidase from Thermotoga maritima (GalA), which hydrolyses the short-chain alpha-galactosaccharides raffinose, melibiose and stachyose. This GH36 enzyme is organised into three domains: an N-terminal beta -sandwich fold domain (this entry), a canonical (beta/alpha)8-fold domain housing the active site (Pfam:PF02065), and a C-terminal beta-sandwich domain with a Greek-key motif (PMID: 30104598). (from Pfam)

label: Lmo2446-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of bacterial proteins, including Lmo2446 protein from Listeria monocytogenes, a functionally uncharacterised extracellular lipidated protein. Lmo2446 contains a glycoside hydrolase 31 family (GH31) catalytic domain (Pfam:PF01055) flanked by three structural beta-domains. This domain folds into a carbohydrate binding module (CBM)-like beta-sandwich (PMID: 27819654). (from Pfam)

label: FAS_AT_central
product_name: Fatty acid synthase central AT domain
name_orig: Fatty acid synthase central AT domain
hmm_name: Fatty acid synthase central AT domain
comment: This entry includes a domain found in the central region of the acyltransferase domain (AT) from fungal type I fatty acid synthase (FAS, such as FAS1 from yeast) and mycobacteria, which have secondary-structure elements and sequence homology [1-5]. Mycobacterial fatty acid synthase (FAS) complex is an homohexameric multifunctional enzyme that catalyses the synthesis of fatty acid precursors of mycolic acids, the major components of the cell wall in Mycobacteria and play an important role in pathogenicity (PMID: 23291528). (from Pfam)

label: MACPF_1
comment: This entry represents a MACPF-like domain in uncharacterised proteins primarily found in Fungi. (from Pfam)

label: Mu_Gam-Sipho_Gp157-TOTE
product_name: Mu Gam/Sipho_Gp157-like domain of the TOTE conflict systems
name_orig: Mu Gam/Sipho_Gp157-like domain of the TOTE conflict systems
hmm_name: Mu Gam/Sipho_Gp157-like domain of the TOTE conflict systems
comment: This entry represents a DNA/RNA hybrid duplex binding domain found in the TOTE (TPR, OB, TBP, Effector) conflict systems (PMID: 35609893). This domain occasionally displaces the more widely observed TOTE-TPR domain (PMID: 35609893). (from Pfam)

label: NCH4
comment: This is a helical domain found at the C-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: E217_gp28
comment: E217 is a Pseudomonas phage used in an experimental cocktail to eradicate cystic fibrosis-associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The collar protein gp28 is located at the neck of the E217 virion. Gp28 consists of a small beta-barrel decorated by an alpha-helix and two wing-like lateral extensions. Six collar proteins pack under the head-to-tail dodecamer with gp28 N-helix positioned orthogonal to two gp27 subunits. On the opposite side of the gp28 barrel, the wing-like extensions contact two gateway subunits (PMID: 37422479). (from Pfam)

label: DUF4026_C
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is usually associated with Pfam:PF13218 and Pfam:PF10077 that flank this domain from N- and C-terminal ends, respectively. This domain is distantly related to SUFU-like domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7012
comment: This domain of unknown function is found in a group of proteins mainly from alphaproteobacteria. It is normally found N-terminal to Pfam:PF10074. It is predicted to adopt a configuration formed mainly by beta-strands. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7013
comment: This is a presumed domain found at the N-terminal of phage sequences, which also have a FN3-like domain (Pfam:PF21470) at the C-terminal. (from Pfam)

label: Ams1-like_1st
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Alpha-mannosidase 2C1 from Schizosaccharomyces pombe (Ams1) and similar sequences mainly from eukaryota and some species from actinomycetes. Ams1 hydrolyse terminal alpha-linked mannoses in free oligosaccharides released from misfolded glycoproteins or lipid-linked oligosaccharide donors. This entry represents the jelly-roll domain (PMID: 32981237). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6890
comment: This entry represents a family of small proteins composed largely of a single alpha helix. Some proteins in this family are annotated as from phage. The function of these proteins is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6896
comment: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins of unknown function. The domain structure includes a four stranded beta sheet which has two conserved aspartates in a DXDXG motif close to a highly conserved histidine. These three residues may for the potential active site. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6902
comment: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins that have an alpha/alpha(6) toroid structure. This suggests that these proteins are likely to be an as yet uncharacterised family of glycosyl hydrolases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6903
comment: This entry represents a family of small putative integral membrane proteins with two transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6913
comment: This is a family of uncharacterized proteins. They share remote similarity to both domains of proteins members of UDP-glycosyltransferase superfamily. In contrast to them, these proteins are predicted to consist of a single standalone domain. (from Pfam)

label: N4_RNAP_helical
product_name: Bacteriophage N4 RNA polymerase, helical domain
name_orig: Bacteriophage N4 RNA polymerase, helical domain
hmm_name: Bacteriophage N4 RNA polymerase, helical domain
comment: This is a helical domain, also known as 'Fingers subdomain', found in the bacteriophage N4 virion RNA polymerase (PMID: 18362338). This domain possesses two essential functions of the RNAP: the N-terminal part plays a role in the nucleotide addition cycle, whereas the C-terminal part is involved in promoter recognition (PMID: 19061645). A swing motion of the N-terminal part of the Fingers is coupled with nucleotide addition, translocation of the DNA-RNA hybrid, and downstream double-strand DNA opening. (from Pfam)

label: BDI_0842
comment: This entry contains the BDI_0842 protein from Parabacteroides distasonis, for which there is a known structure.
