The structure entry states that the protein has an alpha-lytic protease prodomain-like fold. Proteins in this family have an N-terminal lipoprotein attachment motif. The function of these proteins is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: BON_like
comment: This entry represents BON-like domain that appears to lack the first alpha helix of the classical BON domain structure. (from Pfam)

label: TetR_C_45
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of CprB from Streptomyces coelicolor (Swiss:O66122) and similar bacterial transcriptional regulators. This region is the ligand-binding domain (LBD) [1,2]. It is often found associated with Pfam:PF00440. (from Pfam)

label: RecX_HTH3
comment: This entry represents the third three-helix domain (HTH-like) found in RecX family of proteins. RecX functions as a regulator of DNA recombination and repair pathways in bacterial cells (PMID: 23284295). RecX protein is known to inhibit the activity of RecA protein in DNA recombination [2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: PhyR_sigma2
comment: This is the N-terminal domain of response regulator PhyR and related proteins. It consists of three alpha-helices and together with sigma4 constitutes the PhyR sigma-like (SL) domain. This domain was shown to bind to anti-sigma factor NepR (PMID: 22550171). (from Pfam)

label: CmlS_C
comment: Chloramphenicol halogenase CmlS belongs to the large and diverse superfamily of flavin-dependent halogenases. CmlS is one of the few enzymes known to halogenate an alkyl group. This entry represents the C-terminal domain of CmlS that resembles an arch-like structure above a central alpha-helix. This domain creates a T-shaped tunnel leading to the halogenation active site and thus likely directs substrates into the active site to achieve the desired specificity (PMID: 20080101). (from Pfam)

label: X25_BaPul_like
comment: X25 is a domain inserted in X45 domain of Bacillus acidopullulyticus pullulanase. This type of insertion is common in proteins containing X45-X25 pair. X25 domain itself is also found in tandem copies, such as in the highly modular amylopullulanase from Geobacillus stearothermophilus. It is likely that this domain is a carbohydrate-binding domain which targets mixed alpha-1,6/alpha-1,4 linked D-glucan polysaccharides such as pullulan. (from Pfam)

label: C2c1_Nuc-II
comment: C2c1 is a class 2 type V-B effector protein that was shown to be active for target DNA cleavage in vivo and in vitro. In contrast to Cpf1, this enzyme cleavage activity requires both crRNA and tracrRNA. The structure of C2c1 consists of an alpha-helical recognition (REC) lobe, including Helical-I and Helical-II, and a NUC lobe, including OBD, RuvC, and two Nuc domains [1-2]. This entry represents the C-terminal second Nuc (Nuc-II) domain. This domain folds into an open five-stranded beta-barrel and an alpha-helix. Nuc-II is essential for cleavage activity. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6941
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share sequence similarity to Ig-like domains found in a number of proteins such as xylosyltransferase, alkylpurine DNA glycosylase, cycloisomaltooligosaccharide glucanotransferase and are predicted to adopt the same structure. (from Pfam)

label: NGO1945_C
comment: HvfC, as described in Haemophilus influenzae, is a partner protein to the multinuclear nonheme iron-dependent oxidase (MNIO) enzyme HvfB, and participates in post-translational modification that converts the precursor protein HvfA (Haemophilus virulence factor A) into a copper-binding metallophore and a contributor to the cell's ability to contribute to invade host cells and survive as an intracellular pathogen. The related protein NGO_1945 occurs in a similar genomic context, and was previously suggested to be a DNA-binding protein. This HMM describes the C-terminal region of HvfC, NGO_1945, and various other proteins partnered with MNIO family peptide modification enzymes.

label: Phage_gp38
comment: The gene product 38 (gp38) from Lactococcus phage P008 is a short protein consisting of 71 amino acids. It is also known as the AbiQ resistance protein due to its involvement in escaping bacterial killing mediated by the AbiQ protein. Gp38 is expressed early in the viral replication cycle and is essential for virus function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6898
comment: This entry represents a small protein that has a domain with a structure resembling a double stranded RNA-binding domain such as Pfam:PF00035. Thus suggesting this protein may also have a dsRNA binding function. This is supported by the presence of several conserved positively charged residues. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6905
product_name: Lin0368 family putative glycerol transporter subunit
hmm_name: Lin0368 family putative glycerol transporter subunit
comment: Members of this family are annotated in SwissProt as Putative glycerol transporters SwissProt:Q92EU1. Members of the family contain four potential transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: RepB_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal oligomerisation domain (OD) of plasmid replication proteins, such as RepB. These proteins are essential for replication of plasmids, the Rep proteins are topoisomerases that nick the positive stand at the plus origin of replication and also at the single-strand conversion sequence (PMID: 26875695). They consist of a N-terminal origin binding domain (OBD, Pfam:PF01719) which is the DNA-binding/catalytic domain that belongs to the HUH endonuclease superfamily and this C-terminal helical domain, which is responsible for the hexameric state of the protein (PMID: 36688326). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6915
comment: This family of proteins is primarily found in proteobacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 124 and 153 amino acids in length. Proteins in this family has several conserved histidine residues that may form zinc binding sites. (from Pfam)

label: vRNAP_dom_2
comment: This domain is found in Virion DNA-directed RNA polymerase from Bacteriophage N4 (vRNAP), which is injected into the host upon infection and transcribes the phage early genes from promoters that have a 5-bp stem-3 nt loop hairpin structure. This entry represents a region located C-terminal to the mini-vRNAP, which possesses all RNAP functions [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6918
comment: This is a family of uncharacterized bacterial proteins with a length of ~140-150 residues. They are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure consisting of two structural repeats. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6919
comment: This domain is found standalone in bacteria. Its function is unknown but it has a significant sequence similarity to the C-terminal SAM-binding regulatory domain of 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR). (from Pfam)

label: Cel124_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal catalytic domain of endo-acting cellulase Cel124 and related proteins. The active site architecture of this cellulase shares significant structural similarity to GH23 enzymes, a family that contains inverting lysozymes and lytic transglycosylases (PMID: 21393568). These proteins adopt typical lysozyme (muramidase)-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: GH85_C
product_name: GH85 family endohexosaminidase C-terminal domain-containing protein
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of GH85 endohexosaminidases.These enzymes cleave the glycosidic linkage between the two N-acetylglucosamine units that make up the chitobiose core of N-glycans. The C-terminal domain adopts a typical fibronectin Ig-like fold (PMID: 19181667). (from Pfam)

label: NMB0537_N
comment: This entry represents a pair of helices found at the N-terminus of some CBS domain proteins. A pair of these regions dimerise to form a four helical bundle. Proteins in this family have this region followed by two CBS domains and Pfam:PF03471. (from Pfam)

label: ABM-like
comment: This domain is found in Swiss:Q8KDY2 from Chlorobaculum tepidum and similar bacterial proteins. It adopts an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6924
comment: This domain of unknown function is found mainly in bacterial proteins, either standalone or in combination with other domains. It is probably remotely related to the anticodon binding domain observed in histidyl, glycyl, threonyl and prolyl tRNA synthetases. (from Pfam)

label: Arc1p_N_like
comment: This is the N-terminal domain of nuclear-export cofactor Arc1p (Arc1p-N). Arc1p-N and GluRS-N are known to be necessary and sufficient for formation of the yeast aaRS complex in vivo and in vitro. They are likely to form a stable complex with each other. Arc1p-N adopts a fold similar to the C-terminal domain of glutathione S-transferase (GST-C). (from Pfam)

label: MksE
comment: This entry represents a small family of MksE proteins. These proteins are part of MksBEF complex, which primarily function in structural chromosome maintenance (PMID: 35072315). The N-terminal part of MksE is remotely related to the chromosome partition protein MukE and most likely adopts the same structure that consists of two winged helix domains (WHD) (PMID: 19135891). (from Pfam)

label: Hen1_N
comment: This is the N-terminal domain of Hen1. The bacterial RNA repair complex composed of three proteins: Pnkp1, Rnl and Hen1, neutralises the damage inflicted by ribotoxins which is essential for cell survival. The Pnkp-Hen1 RNA repair complex carries out methylation of the 2'-OH group that is responsible for the RNA cleavage and thus the repaired RNA resists future RNA damage by the same ribotoxin. The N-terminal domain of Hen1 activates the ligase activity of Pnkp by locking the insertion domain of Pnkp into a conformation that allows access to the ligase pocket (PMID: 25882814). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6935
comment: This is a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either as standalone or in combination with other domains. It is remotely related to soluble lipid-binding protein MlaC and it is predicted to adopt a similar structure with a typical NTF2-like topology. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6937
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain has a significant sequence similarity to the N-terminal domains of a number of proteins members of UDP-Glycosyltransferase/glycogen phosphorylase superfamily. It is predicted to adopt the same alpha/beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: Cep192_D3
comment: Cep192 is a centrosomal protein with key roles in centriole duplication and pericentriolar material recruitment, organisation and regulation. Most of the metazoan Cep192 homologs consist of eight ASH/PapD-like domains. These are located at the C-terminal part of the proteins and are likely arranged in a beads-on-string fashion. This entry represents the third domain found in the metazoan Cep192 homologs. (from Pfam)

label: Cep192_D6
comment: Cep192 is a centrosomal protein with key roles in centriole duplication and pericentriolar material recruitment, organisation and regulation. Most of the metazoan Cep192 homologs consist of eight ASH/PapD-like domains. These are located at the C-terminal part of the proteins and are likely arranged in a beads-on-string fashion. This entry represents the sixth domain of the metazoan Cep192 homologs. (from Pfam)

label: SwaI-like
comment: SwaI is a Type IIP restriction endonuclease that recognizes a palindromic eight base pair symmetric sequence, 5'-ATTTAAAT-3', and cleaves this target sequence at its center to generate blunt-ended DNA fragments. SwaI forms a dimeric alpha/beta structure with each subunit having a central credle-like mixed beta-sheet with two helices packed on its concave side and a C-terminal helix contributing to the dimer interface (PMID: 28180307). SwaI has a significant similarity to other restriction endonucleases such as HincII, NlaIV, HindIII, EcoRV and others. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6944
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Gram-positive bacteria. They are predicted to be associated with the membrane and to adopt structure that has topological similarity to the common structural core of Succinate-acetate permease (SatP) superfamily proteins. (from Pfam)

label: C2c1_RuvC-like
comment: This entry represents the RuvC-like domain of C2c1 CRISPR-Cas endonuclease (also known as Cas12b) [1-3]. C2c1 is a class 2 type V-B effector protein that site-specifically targets and cleaves both strands of target DNA. (from Pfam)

label: AcrIC5
comment: AcrIC5 is one of the earliest discovered AcrIC families that inhibit type I-C CRISPR-Cas systems. AcrIC5 adopts an alpha/beta structure consisting of a beta-hairpin and three alpha-helices (PMID: 35952606). The presence of a highly acidic surface patch suggests that AcrIC5 might inhibit the type I-C CRISPR-Cas system by directly binding to the DNA target binding site in the system by mimicking DNA. (from Pfam)

label: Tt1218-like
comment: The founding member of this family is Tt1218 that is a type IV pilin. This protein is likely involved in the formation of polymers that extend from the surface of the bacterial cell and could mediate a wide variety of functions such as adhesion, motility and natural competence. This domain is closely related to type II secretion pseudopilin EpsI. It consists of the canonical type IV pilin structural core comprising an alpha-helix packed against a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet (PMID: 27612581). (from Pfam)

label: C2c1_helical
product_name: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1 second helical domain
name_orig: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1 second helical domain
hmm_name: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1 second helical domain
comment: This entry represents the second helical domain (REC2) from CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1, also known as Cas12b. C2c1 is a guide RNA-mediated type V-B CRISPR-Cas endonuclease that site-specifically targets and cleaves dsDNA. This domain, together with the first helical domain (helical-I or REC1) forms the alpha-recognition (REC) lobe, which recognises a 20bp guide:target heteroduplex in RNAs [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: Gp5_trimer_C
product_name: bacteriophage T4 gp5 trimerisation domain-containing protein
name_orig: Bacteriophage T4 gp5 C-terminal trimerisation domain
hmm_name: Bacteriophage T4 gp5 C-terminal trimerisation domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal trimerisation domain of bacteriophage T4 gp5. This domain associates to form a triple-stranded beta-helix that forms an equilateral triangular prism, which acts as a membrane-puncturing needle [1,2]. The interior of the beta-helix has an increased hydrophobicity toward the C terminus. The middle part of the helix has a pore, enriched with polar and charged side chains. (from Pfam)

label: PNGase_F-II_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of N-glycanase peptide from Elizabethkingia meningoseptica (PNGase F-II) and other bacterial sequences mainly found in flavobacteriales. This is often found associated with Pfam:PF09112 and Pfam:PF09113. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6954
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are enriched in hydrophobic residues and are likely associated with the membrane. (from Pfam)

label: DmmA-like_C
product_name: Dimethylamine monooxygenase subunit DmmA-like, C-terminal domain
name_orig: Dimethylamine monooxygenase subunit DmmA-like, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Dimethylamine monooxygenase subunit DmmA-like, C-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the dimethylamine monooxygenase subunit DmmA from Methylocella silvestris (Msil_3607, Swiss:B8EJ00) and similar sequences, mainly found in proteobacteria and actinomycetes. Dimethylamine (DMA) monooxygenase is required for metabolism of trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6968
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either standalone or C-terminal to HTH winged helix domains. It has a partial sequence similarity to ribosome associated factors that are members of Pfam:PF02482. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6969
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Proteobacteria. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta globular structure. It has three highly conserved histidines that are predicted to cluster together in space and are likely involved in metal coordination. (from Pfam)

label: RhiE-like_linker
comment: This entry represents a linker domain found in polyketide synthases, which connects the N-terminal domains with the B-domain as described in RhiE [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6976
comment: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found mainly in Proteobacteria. It is likely to consists of two domains that engage in extensive contacts mainly via hydrophobic residues. The predicted structure of the N-terminal domain has similarity to chorismatases. (from Pfam)

label: EEP_ig-like
comment: This entry corresponds to the C-terminal immunoglobulin-like domain of a putative endonuclease/exonuclease/phosphatase from Beutenbergia cavernae (PDB:4ruw). (from Pfam)

label: TubZ-like_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of TubZ from Bacillus thuringiensis and related bacteria. TubZ structure consists of an N-terminal GTPase domain and a C-terminal domain. TubZ is part of the polymerizing cytomotive filament, a complex that drives newly replicated plasmids to opposite ends of the dividing cell [1,2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: Thiaminase-1_dom
comment: This domain is found in Thiaminase-1 from Paenibacillus thiaminolyticus and similar bacterial sequences. This enzyme degrades thiamine by replacing its thiazole moiety with a wide range of nucleophiles. This entry represents one if its two alpha/beta-type domains (PMID: 9843405). (from Pfam)

label: Fer4_NDSU1
comment: This entry represents the 4Fe-4S domain of NADH-ubiquinone oxidoreductase NDUFS1 from mammals and NuoG from bacteria, which are part of respiratory chain complex I [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: ExsA_N
comment: ExsA is an AraC-type transcriptional activator protein that is regulated through protein-protein interactions rather than small molecule ligands. Prior to infection, ExsA is inhibited through a direct interaction with the anti-activator ExsD. Upon host cell contact this interaction is disrupted by the anti-antiactivator protein ExsC. The regulatory domain of ExsA mediate ExsD binding and is represented by this entry. The structure of this domain closely resembles those of the regulatory domains of AraC and ToxT, having typical cupin-like fold (PMID: 26317977). (from Pfam)

label: C2c1_helical_1st
product_name: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1 first helical domain
name_orig: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1 first helical domain
hmm_name: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1 first helical domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of CRISPR-associated endonuclease Cas12b from Alicyclobacillus acidoterrestris and similar sequences from firmicutes. Cas12b, also known as C2c1, is a type V-B CRISPR-Cas system dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease that site-specifically targets and cleaves dsDNA. This domain, together with the second helical domain (Pfam:PF22172) forms the alpha-recognition (REC) lobe, which recognises a 20bp guide:target heteroduplex in RNAs [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: C2c1_WED-II
product_name: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1, wedge domain, second region
name_orig: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1, wedge domain, second region
hmm_name: CRISPR-associated endonuclease C2c1, wedge domain, second region
comment: This domain is found in CRISPR-associated endonuclease Cas12b from Alicyclobacillus acidoterrestris and similar sequences from firmicutes. Cas12b, also known as C2c1, is a type V-B CRISPR-Cas system dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease that site-specifically targets and cleaves dsDNA. This entry represents the second region of the wedge domain (WED-II). It adopts an oligonucleotide-binding (OB) fold with eight beta-stranded distorted beta-sheets flanked by two alpha-helices and one beta-hairpin [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Cas_Csm6_CARF
comment: This entry includes Csm6 from bacteria (i.e Enterococcus italicus), a Cas (CRISPR-associated) protein from type III-A CRISPR-Cas system. It consists of a CARF domain at the N-terminal, represented in this entry a six-helix domain (Pfam:PF22206) and a C-terminal HEPN domain (Pfam:PF09659), which has RNase activity (PMID: 32221291). This domain is a ring nuclease (PMID: 32221291). (from Pfam)

label: Sas-6_C_CC
product_name: Spindle assembly abnormal protein 6 homolog, C-terminal coiled coil
name_orig: Spindle assembly abnormal protein 6 homolog, C-terminal coiled coil
hmm_name: Spindle assembly abnormal protein 6 homolog, C-terminal coiled coil
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal coiled-coil (CC) domain found in Spindle assembly abnormal protein 6 homolog from Drosophila melanogaster (Sas-6) and similar sequences found predominantly in arthropods. Sas-6 is a central scaffolding component of the centrioles ensuring their nine-fold symmetry. Sas-6 forms a dimer through this domain to then further homo-oligomerise to form a ring structure from which the CC domains emanate as spokes (PMID: 26002084). (from Pfam)

label: PhyR_sigma-like
comment: PhyR is a signal transduction response regulator found in Alphaproteobacteria with a C-terminal receiver domain (Pfam:PF00072) and extracytoplasmic function (ECF) sigma factor-like domain at the N-terminal which is represented in this entry [1-3]. PhyR is the regulator of the two-component signal transduction system which controls transcription in response to general stress. (from Pfam)

label: 6PGD_like
comment: This alpha helical domain is found at the C-terminus of proteins that contain an N-terminal Rossmann domain. This domain belongs to the 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase C-terminal domain-like superfamily. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5018-rel
comment: This domain is found in the putative secreted protein BF4250 from Bacteroides fragilis (Swiss:Q5L7M9) and similar bacterial functionally uncharacterised proteins. This domain seems to be related to Pfam:PF16410. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6950
comment: This domain if found in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is related to NlpC/P60 domains and it is likely to adopt similar structure as well as to possess an endopeptidase activity. All members of this family contain a conserved cysteine residue that is predicted to occupy equivalent spatial position as in the NlpC/P60 domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6957
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into a beta-barrel that has some similarity to the replication focus targeting sequence (RFTS) domain of Dnmt1 methyltransferase 1. (from Pfam)

label: PccH
comment: This entry represents the PccH protein, a unique cytochrome c (GSU3274) found in Geobacter sulfurreducens. PccH is a small (15 kDa) cytochrome that contains a single c-type heme and plays an essential role in electron transfer from graphite electrodes to fumarate, the terminal electron acceptor, in G. sulfurreducens. The crystal structure of PccH, reveals a distinct fold characterized by two lobes with the heme located in a cleft between them. Notably, PccH exhibits a low reduction potential of -24 mV at pH 7, which is unusual for monoheme cytochromes. Based on structural and phylogenetic analyses, PccH represents a novel subclass of class I monoheme cytochromes. The unique structural features and low reduction potential of PccH likely enable its redox activity within the typically negative potential range encountered by G. sulfurreducens. Although located in the periplasm, PccH is not involved in the initial electron transfer from the electrode but is believed to participate in downstream electron transport events in the periplasm (PMID: 25786707). (from Pfam)

label: AUDH_beta_propeller
comment: This domain is found in Aldos-2-ulose dehydratase from Phanerodontia chrysosporium (AUDH) and similar sequences from invertebrates and fungi. AUDH is a bifunctional enzyme which catalyses the dehydration of anhydrofructose into ascopyrone M, and the isomerisation of ascopyrone M into microthecin. It is organised into three domains: an N-terminal domain with a beta-propeller fold (this entry), a middle domain containing two cupin folds (Pfam:PF18637) and a C-terminal lectin domain. This domain folds into a seven-bladed beta-propeller, where each blade is made up of a four-stranded, antiparallel beta-sheet (PMID: 22330145). (from Pfam)

label: TubZ_C_2
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Phage tubulin-like protein from the Pseudomonas phage phiKZ (TubZ) and similar viral sequences. TubZ is a tubulin-like GTPase that forms filaments, which are required for positioning viral DNA and capsids in the middle of the host cell for optimal replication. This protein adopts a tubulin/FtsZ protein family fold organised into two domains, a canonical N-terminal GTP-binding domain, and a C-terminal GTPase activation domain (this entry). This domain shows an alpha-beta structure [3,4]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6980
comment: This is a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain occurs either standalone or in combination with other domains. It contains conserved cysteines and histidine that may be involved in Zn2+ coordination. (from Pfam)

label: GMC_oxred_C_1st
comment: This domain is found in a group of GMC oxidoreductases mainly from actinomycetes, including Cholesterol oxidase from Streptomyces sp. (ChoA). ChoA is organised into two domains, an FAD-binding domain (Pfam:PF00732) and a substrate binding domain (formed by this entry and Pfam:PF05199) [1-5]. This domain consists of six beta -sheets and one alpha-helix. (from Pfam)

label: FitA-like_RHH
comment: This domain is found in Antitoxin FitA from Neisseria gonorrhoeae and similar bacterial sequences. FitA is the antitoxin component of a type II toxin-antitoxin (TA) system. It binds DNA through its ribbon-helix-helix motif (this entry) (PMID: 16982615). (from Pfam)

label: PreP_C
comment: PreP is a protease that degrades targeting peptides as well as other unstructured peptides in both mitochondria and chloroplasts. This entry represents the C-terminal domain of PreP and related proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7003
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure with a central antiparallel beta-sheet and helices packed on it. (from Pfam)

label: 2CompART
comment: This entry represents the 2CompART domain, which coupled with its partner 2CompARG, forms a two-domain T-A-like association in the duplex-forming systems likely functioning as the principal effector of these systems. One is likely to function as the antitoxin, regulating the toxin activity of the other (PMID: 35609893). (from Pfam)

label: Fe_hydrogense_Fe-S_bd
comment: This entry represents a Fe-S centre binding domain found in iron hydrogenases [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: IPMS_D2
comment: This entry represents domain found in homologues of alpha-isopropylmalate synthase (IPMS). This domain follows the catalytic domain and is required for the enzymatic activity (PMID: 25128527). (from Pfam)

label: I-TevI_ZnF
comment: This entry represent the unusual zinc finger domain present in the -ntron-associated endonuclease 1 (I-TevI) [1,2], which comprises the unusual sequence CXCX10CXXC. The Zn finger interacts with the DNA through two hydrogen bonds, between the main chain nitrogen atoms of residues Tyr162 and Ser165 (PMID: 11447104). (from Pfam)

label: MinC_N_1
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of MinC and related proteins. MinC is a cell division inhibitor that blocks the formation of polar Z ring septums. It consists of two domains. The N-terminal domain interacts with FtsZ and inhibits FtsZ polymerization while the C-terminal interacts with MinD and inhibits the bundling of FtsZ filaments. (from Pfam)

label: SET7_N
product_name: Histone H3 K4-specific methyltransferase SET7 N-terminal
name_orig: Histone H3 K4-specific methyltransferase SET7 N-terminal
hmm_name: Histone H3 K4-specific methyltransferase SET7 N-terminal
comment: This entry includes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD7 (also known as SET7/9) which specifically monomethylate Lys-4 of histone H3, creating a specific tag for epigenetic transcriptional activation [1-5]. This entry represents the N-terminal region, which consists of MORN repeats. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7007
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of segregated alpha-helices and a five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet. This domain contains two highly conserved sequence motifs TxxHGG and YEED that may be of a functional importance. (from Pfam)

label: YycE-like_C
comment: This entry represents a VOC-like domain found at the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised bacterial sequences, such YycE from Bacillus subtilis. (from Pfam)

label: Gp10_D3
comment: This domain is found in Baseplate wedge protein gp10 and related proteins. This domain folds into a beta-sandwich. (from Pfam)

label: Gp18_domIII_N
product_name: Tail sheath protein Gp18 domain III N-terminal region
name_orig: Tail sheath protein Gp18 domain III N-terminal region
hmm_name: Tail sheath protein Gp18 domain III N-terminal region
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal segment of domain III from the phage tail sheath protein Gp18 y similar sequences [1-5]. Domain III is completed by Pfam:PF04984 with an overall structure consisting of a beta-sheet with five parallel and one anti-parallel beta-strands plus six alpha-helices, which surround the beta-sheet. (from Pfam)

label: C2185-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised proteins from Clostridia, including C2185 from Clostridium acetobutylicum (Swiss:Q97H28). This domain is found associated with Pfam:PF08942 and shows a NAD(P) binding Rossmann fold. (from Pfam)

label: FGAR-AT_PurM_N-like
comment: This entry represents the PurM_N-like domain of formylglycinamide ribonucleotide amidotransferase (FGAR-AT) and related proteins. FGAR-AT catalyzes the ATP-dependent conversion of formylglycinamide ribonucleotide (FGAR) to formylglycinamidine ribonucleotide (FGAM) in the fourth step of the purine biosynthetic pathway. This domain consists of an antiparallel beta-sheet with two helices packed on one side [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: CtpB_N-like
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in Carboxy-terminal processing protease CtpB and related proteins. This enzyme is involved in signal transduction pathway leading to the proteolytic activation of the mother cell transcription factor pro-sigma-K during sporulation. This domain contains auto-cleavage site at which it is proteolytically cleaved. The remaining part in the mature enzyme is involved in dimerisation (PMID: 24243021). (from Pfam)

label: CBM13-like
comment: This is a carbohydrate-binding module family 13 domain that is found in homologues of Alpha-galactosidase. (from Pfam)

label: S1CSD-TOTE-2
product_name: S1/CSD-like domain 2 of the TOTE conflict systems
name_orig: S1/CSD-like domain 2 of the TOTE conflict systems
hmm_name: S1/CSD-like domain 2 of the TOTE conflict systems
comment: This entry represents a presumed ribonucleoprotein complex-forming domain of the TOTE ((TPR, OB, TBP, Effector) conflict systems, potentially binding ssRNAs derived from hybrid duplexes bound by the systems. It is typically found in a two-domain tandem repeat arrangement, this is the second domain of the two (PMID: 35609893). (from Pfam)

label: SNaCT8
comment: The SNaCT domains are a rapidly evolving, monophyletic assemblage of domains found C-terminal to the NACHT module in several bacterial NACHT conflict systems. They contain a well-conserved aspartate near the N-terminus of the domain. SNaCT domains are thought to occlude the NTP-binding region, potentially until they interact with phage-encoded bNACHT inhibitors (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: TBP-TOTE
product_name: TATA-binding-like protein domain of the TOTE conflict systems
name_orig: TATA-binding-like protein domain of the TOTE conflict systems
hmm_name: TATA-binding-like protein domain of the TOTE conflict systems
comment: This entry represents the principal predicted hybrid duplex-binding domain of the TOTE (TPR, OB, TBP, Effector) conflict systems described as TATA-binding-like protein (TBP) domain of the TOTE (TBP-TOTE) in (PMID: 35609893). (from Pfam)

label: NCH2
comment: This is an helical domain found at the C-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: NCH3
comment: Helical domain found at the C-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems. (from Pfam)

label: NNH1
comment: This entry represents an helical domain found at the N-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems (PMID: 37160116). This position is frequently occupied by an effector domain. (from Pfam)

label: NNH6
comment: This is the helical domain found at the N-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems. This position is frequently occupied by an effector domain (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: PapZ_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of RapZ which belongs to the Rhodanese-Phosphatase superfamily. It has been shown to bind multiple ligands as part of the regulation of glucosamine-6-phosphate (GlcN6P) levels, which is a precursor to the bacterial cell wall polymer peptidoglycan. Assignment to the greater Rhodanese-Phosphatase superfamily has led to the prediction that, as part of this regulation, it functions as a sugar phosphorylation-dephosphorylation switch (PMID: 36968430). (from Pfam)

label: ThcOx
comment: Thus entry represents the second peptide-clamp domain described in cianobactin oxidase ThcOx from Cyanothece sp. (PMID: 27841750). The first one is represented in Pfam:PF18679 and at the C-terminal it contains a nitroreductase domain (Pfam:PF00881) (PMID: 27841750). In this domain, the binding site is buried by an interaction with the other clamp domain and thus it is unlikely to be active (PMID: 27841750). (from Pfam)

label: MRM3-like_sub_bind
comment: MRM3 catalyses the formation of 2'-O-methylguanosine at position 1370 Gm1370) in the 16S mitochondrial large subunit ribosomal RNA (mtLSU rRNA), a conserved modification in the peptidyl transferase domain of the mtLSU rRNA [1-3]. This entry represents the substrate binding domain of MRM3 from animals and related sequences from bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: Neopullulanase-like_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal all-beta domain found in (Neo)pullulanase (Swiss:Q5SI17) from Thermus thermophilus (PDBe:2Z1K) and similar sequences. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6982
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 135 and 1024 amino acids in length. This family of proteins are structurally related to Pfam:PF03614 a family of transcriptional repressors of phase-1 flagellin genes. The family appears to contain two related subdomains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6984
comment: This entry represents a bacterial family of unknown function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6993
comment: This entry represents a bacterial domain of unknown function. (from Pfam)

label: 2H-SAK
comment: The Swiss Army Knife class of proteins features a diverse domain repertoire acting to repair RNA damaged in the wake of RNase attacks. 2H-SAK is one such domain, a phosphatase of the rhodanese-phosphatase superfamily. It is predicted to 'clean' RNA ends by removing phosphate groups, preparing them for ligation by their associating RNA ligases (PMID: 22731697). (from Pfam)

label: TY-Chap3
name_orig: T3SS (YopN, CesT) and YbjN peptide-binding chaperone 3
hmm_name: T3SS (YopN, CesT) and YbjN peptide-binding chaperone 3
comment: This circularly-permuted TY-Chap domain is observed in host systems predicted to counter viral ribosylating toxins. They are predicted to function as peptide-binding chaperone domains that target proteins modified by ADPr and potentially misfolded as a consequence [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DAM-like-phage1
comment: This domain has been characterised as part of a nucleic acid modifying system in certain phages. This system may modify tRNAs that are encoded adjacent to the system on the genome. These tRNAs are then possibly packaged into the viral head, to render them resistant to host restriction (PMID: 36968430). (from Pfam)

label: GNAT-phage-like
comment: This domain has been characterised as part of a nucleic acid modifying system in certain phages. This system may modify tRNAs that are encoded adjacent to the system on the genome. These tRNAs are then possibly packaged into the viral head, to render them resistant to host restriction (PMID: 36968430). (from Pfam)

label: Amylosucrase_C-like
comment: This entry represents a domain found C-terminal in amylosucrase and related proteins. This domain follows the catalytic beta/alpha barrel domain. It folds into a beta-sandwich with a greek-key topology. (from Pfam)

label: dCache_1_like
comment: This entry represents a sensor domain found in histidine kinase receptors members of subfamily C. It folds into an alpha/beta structure consisting of a curved beta-sheet and an alpha-helix packed on the concave side of it. (from Pfam)

label: CurL-like_PKS_C
comment: This entry represents the polyketide synthase C-terminal extension from cyanobacterial CurL polyketide synthase and similar proteins from other bacteria and fungi [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: FlgK_D1
name_orig: Flagellar hook-associated protein FlgK helical domain
hmm_name: Flagellar hook-associated protein FlgK helical domain
comment: This entry represents a mainly helical domain found in flagellar hook-associated protein FlgK and related proteins. FlgK is one of three hook associated proteins that form the hook-filament junction. This domain adopts a broken antiparallel helical bundle comprising six helical segments [1-2]. (from Pfam)

label: At5g48480-like_C
comment: This entry includes plant sequences that belong to the Lactoylglutathione lyase/glyoxalase I family. They are poorly characterised and contain two characteristic VOC domains. Members of this entry contain conserved metal binding amino acids with the type I extradiol dioxygenases, which shows no domain swapping. This entry represents the C-terminal domain. (from Pfam)

label: SpoU_sub_bind_like
comment: This domain is found in a number of rRNA methyltransferases that belong to SpoU family. They are composed of two domains: N-terminal, represented by this entry, RNA-binding domain and C-terminal domain responsible for AdoMet-binding, catalysis and dimerization (PMID: 15581897). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7009
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of two nearly orthogonal beta-sheets and two helices that connect them. Toward the C terminus these proteins contain a highly conserved enriched with negatively charged residues region having nearly invariant EKDFxC sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: LlgE_F_G_D1
product_name: Flagellar hook protein FlgE/F/G D1 domain
name_orig: Flagellar hook protein FlgE/F/G D1 domain
hmm_name: Flagellar hook protein FlgE/F/G D1 domain
comment: This entry represents the D1 domain found in three closely related flagellar proteins usually denoted FlgE, FlgF and FlgG. In FlgE there is an additional domain (D2, Pfam:PF07559) outside D1 [1-5]. The flagellar hook is a short, highly curved tubular structure that connects the flagellar motor to the long filament acting as a helical propeller. (from Pfam)

label: S1CSD-TOTE-1
product_name: S1/CSD-like domain 1 of the TOTE conflict systems
name_orig: S1/CSD-like domain 1 of the TOTE conflict systems
hmm_name: S1/CSD-like domain 1 of the TOTE conflict systems
comment: This entry represents a presumed ribonucleoprotein complex-forming domain of the TOTE systems, potentially binding ssRNAs derived from hybrid duplexes bound by the systems. It is typically found in a two-domain tandem repeat arrangement, this is the first domain of the two. (from Pfam)

label: SNaCT14
comment: The SNaCT domains are a rapidly evolving, monophyletic assemblage of domains found C-terminal to the NACHT module in several bacterial NACHT conflict systems. They contain a well-conserved aspartate near the N-terminus of the domain. SNaCT domains are thought to occlude the NTP-binding region, potentially until they interact with phage-encoded bNACHT inhibitors (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: NCAB2
comment: This is a domain containing alpha-helices and beta-strands, found at the C-terminus of certain bacterial NACHT conflict systems (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: NNH2
comment: This is an helical domain found at the N-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems (PMID: 37160116). This position is frequently occupied by an effector domain. (from Pfam)

label: NNH5
comment: This entry represents the helical domain found at the N-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems (PMID: 37160116). This position is frequently occupied by an effector domain. (from Pfam)

label: NA-iREase3
comment: This entry represents a predicted sensor domain in bacterial NACHT conflict systems. It is likely to bind a ligand which could contribute to activation of enzymatic domains additionally fused to the N-terminus of the NACHT module (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: Phage_cement
hmm_name: phage minor capsid protein, E217-Gp24 family
comment: E217 is a Pseudomonas phage used in an experimental cocktail to eradicate cystic fibrosis-associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Gp24 is a trimeric structural protein and component of the E217 icosahedral head.Gp24 adopts a beta-tulip fold similar to the gp87 protein found in the thermophilic phage P74-26. Each gp24 subunit consists of two anti-parallel beta-sheets, that form a tulip-like structure. Gp24 structural protein probably stabilises the E217 capsid. This entry includes the cement protein gp6 of cyanophage Pam3. It consists of an N-terminal beta-tulip domain followed by a C-terminal domain of seven antiparallel beta-strands. Gp6 trimers sit at the icosahedral threefold and quasi-threefold axes, stabilizing the capsid shell. (from Pfam)

label: E217_GP41
comment: E217 is a Pseudomonas phage used in an experimental cocktail to eradicate cystic fibrosis-associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Gp41 ia a baseplate cap protein that forms a complex with gp36, gp37 and gp38 proteins. These four proteins are evolutionarily related to the tail tube and adopt a similar fold, consisting of two orthogonally packed beta-sheets that form the inner lumen of the tail (PMID: 37422479). (from Pfam)

label: YkoP
comment: This entry represents proteins that are related to the YkoP protein from B. subtilis Swiss:O34495. This protein is as yet uncharacterised. AlphaFold prediction shows that is is composed of a single domain. The structure shows similarity to GNAT family acetyltransferases. This domain is sometimes associated with Pfam:PF01522, which is a polysaccharide deacetylase enzyme. (from Pfam)

label: RsiG
comment: This entry represents a domain found in homologues of RsiG protein from Streptomyces. This domain adopts an alpha-helix and in Streptomyces self associates to form a dimer. This dimer binds c-di-GMP via two E(X)3-S(X)2-R(X)3-Q(X)-D repeat motifs, one on each helix. The complex RsiG-(c-di-GMP) binds to the sporulation-specific sigma factor, WhiG. Some homologues of RsiG contain a second helix and hence two c-di-GMP binding motifs. (from Pfam)

label: CatAgl_D2
comment: This entry represents a domain found in the homologues of Alpha-1,3-glucanase. This domain is found C-terminal in the catalytic domain (CatAgl-FH1). It folds into a right-handed beta-helix fold (PMID: 31788942). (from Pfam)

label: ApeP-like
comment: This entry represents the homologues of ApeP dehydratase. This enzyme forms a heterodimer with ApeI that carries out dehydratation in APE biosynthesis. Both subunits in this complex adopt a typical hotdog fold comprising six antiparallel beta-strands and a central alpha-helix (PMID: 30908039). (from Pfam)

label: DUF3097_N
comment: This entry represents an N-terminal Tudor-like domain found in DUF3097 proteins. This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Actinobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: BT_3657-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal of BT_3657 from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and similar bacterial sequences. BT_3657 has been reported to be an arabinosidase (PMID: 34420703). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7021
comment: This entry represents a beta barrel domain which is found associated with Pfam:PF10020. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7022
comment: This uncharacterised protein is found in the T5 bacteriophage. The function of this protein is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DA_C
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in a number of fungal Diels-Alderases, including mycB, mpsD, cghA and others. Diels-Alderases catalyse different pericyclic [4+2] cycloaddition reactions that synthesise potential pharmaceuticals and mycotoxins [1,3,4,5]. These enzymes consist of two similar beta-barrel domains with arrangement similar to AttH. Both domains share some similarity to lipocalins. (from Pfam)

label: Caulimovir_coat_dom
comment: This is a conserved domain found in Cauliflower mosaic virus coat protein. Caulimoviruses are encapsidated plant viruses that contain circular double-stranded DNA. The viral coat proteins contain a fairly hydrophilic N-terminal region and a highly-basic C-terminal domain, which may be involved in DNA-binding. This domain may adopt an all-helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: Integrase_p58_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Integrase p58, the last chain cleaved from the Transposon Ty3-G Gag-Pol polyprotein from Saccharomyces cerevisiae. This domain, found C-terminal to Pfam:PF17919, is also called SH3 domain (PMID: 34848735). Proteins in this group are found in eukaryota. (from Pfam)

label: SpnB_Rossmann
name_orig: Polyketide synthase extender module SpnB, Rossmann fold domain
comment: This entry represents a domain found in a group of proteins mainly found in actinomycetes, including the polyketide synthase extender module SpnB from Saccharopolyspora spinosa. This domain shows a classical Rossmann fold (PMID: 22634636). (from Pfam)

label: Myb_DNA-bind_8
comment: This entry represents a Myb-like domain. These domains are short DNA-binding domains. (from Pfam)

label: MrpR_N_CB
product_name: phage lytic cycle repressor MrpR family protein
comment: This family includes the MrpR protein from Bacillus subtilis (also known as YopR), the master repressor of the lytic cycle of the temperate phage SPbeta. MrpR, a DNA-binding protein that has lost its recombinase function, shows a tyrosine recombinase fold with an N-terminal core-binding (CB) domain with four alpha -helices (this entry) and a C-terminal catalytic domain (PMID: 37602373). (from Pfam)

label: AimR
comment: This entry includes AimR transcriptional regulator from Bacillus phage and related sequences found in tailed bacteriophages and prophages. AimR (arbitrium receptor), which is a part of the so-called phage arbitrium system, is a DNA-binding phage regulatory protein that acts as a receptor for a 6-amino acid signaling peptide cleaved rom the C terminus of AimP. AimR controls expression of AimX, the third member of the quorum sensing-like arbitrium system and an inhibitor of phage lysogeny (PMID: 28099413). AimR assembles in an alpha-alpha superhelix fold and accommodates the signaling peptide encircled by its tetratricopeptide repeats, which is reminiscent of RRNPP family members from the quorum-sensing system [2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: OB_RNR_1st
product_name: Ribonuclease R, OB first domain, N-terminal
name_orig: Ribonuclease R, OB first domain, N-terminal
hmm_name: Ribonuclease R, OB first domain, N-terminal
comment: This entry represents a N-terminal OB (oligonucleotide/ oligosaccharide binding) domain found in a set of bacterial Ribonuclease R proteins. Ribonuclease R proteins are 3'-5' exoribonuclease that releases 5'-nucleoside monophosphates and is involved in maturation of structured RNAs (PMID: 21135037). (from Pfam)

label: crAss001_48
comment: This entry represents a family of proteins that are present in crAss phage. AlphaFold predicts these short proteins to adopt an alpha helical hairpin structure. The function of these proteins is unknown. Members of this family form a confident homodimer according to structure prediction. The highly conserved residues are found in this interaction interface. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6889
comment: This entry represents a family of small proteins that are largely composed of a single alpha helix. Some members of the family are found on phage. The function of these proteins is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6893
comment: This entry represents a small protein that has a likely signal peptide that takes up most of the sequence. Thus a small peptide might be released from these proteins. (from Pfam)

label: Gp53-like_C
name_orig: Putative tail fiber protein gp53-like, C-terminal
hmm_name: Putative tail fiber protein gp53-like, C-terminal
comment: This entry represents a domain found at the C-terminal of putative tail fiber protein from Acinetobacter phage AP22 (Swiss:I2GUG0, gp53) and similar uncharacterised sequences from tailed bacteriophages and prophages mainly found in proteobacteria. It shows structural similarities to other phage/virus host cell-binding fibres. These domains form a trimeric arrangement. (from Pfam)

label: MTHFR_C
comment: This is the C-terminal SAM-binding regulatory domain of 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) that follows the catalytic domain and is unique to eukaryotes. This domain provides the required interface for MTHFR homo-dimerization, thus positioning the N-terminal serine-rich phosphorylation region near the SAM-binding site. The core of this domain comprises two mixed beta-sheets, one of which flanked with helices. This regulatory domain represents distinct architecture from the classical SAM-dependent methyltransferases and non-methyltransferases (PMID: 29891918). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6921
comment: This family of proteins is based on the known structure of a protein from Ruminococcus gnavus PDB:3noh. The structure shows similarity to solute binding proteins. The exact function of these proteins is not yet known. (from Pfam)

label: GpP_4th
name_orig: Mu phage baseplate assembly protein GpP, fourth domain
hmm_name: Mu phage baseplate assembly protein GpP, fourth domain
comment: This domain is found in Mu phage baseplate assembly protein GpP from Shewanella oneidensis (Swiss:Q8EDP4) and similar sequences found in tailed bacteriophages and prophages from proteobacteria. It is normally found associated with Pfam:PF21683. (from Pfam)

label: TetR_C_46
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of DesT from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and similar bacterial transcriptional regulators. DesT is involved in the control of the unsaturated:saturated fatty acid ratio available for membrane lipid synthesis. This region folds into six helices that create the ligand-binding domain (PMID: 20639888). It is normally found associated with Pfam:PF00440. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6922
comment: This family is found in bacterial proteins either as a standalone domain or in combination with an HTH domain that resembles lambda C1 repressor DNA-binding domain. This family has a partial sequence similarity to the RAP1 C-terminal (RCT) domain. (from Pfam)

label: RecX_HTH1
comment: This entry represents the first three-helix domain (HTH-like) found in RecX family of proteins. RecX functions as a regulator of DNA recombination and repair pathways in bacterial cells (PMID: 23284295). RecX protein is known to inhibit the activity of RecA protein in DNA recombination [2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: TR61B_FKBP-like
comment: This is the FKBP-like domain found towards the N-terminal of TR61B (tRNA (adenine(58)-N(1))-methyltransferase from human and similar proteins. This mitochondrion-specific protein catalyses the formation of N1-methyladenine at position 58 (m1A58) in various tRNAs (PMID: 23097428) and the formation of 1-methyladenosine at position 947 of mitochondrial 16S ribosomal RNA which is most likely important for mitoribosomal structure and function (PMID: 27631568). TR61B is most similar to bacterial TrmI than to eukaryotic Trmt61A, according to phylogenetic tree analysis (PMID: 23097428). The function of this domain is not clear but it may be necessary for overall folding and full enzymatic activity. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6928
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt alpha/beta structure with a central nine-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with helices packed on both sides. The predicted structure has some partial structural similarity to bacterial S-adenosylmethionine decarboxylases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6929
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to fold into five-bladed beta-propeller that has similarity to apyrase but it is circularly permuted. The C-terminal two beta-strands of this domain occupy the position of the two N-terminal beta-strands in apyrase. (from Pfam)

label: PG_1098_Fer
comment: This entry represents a ferredoxin-like domain found in a group of poorly characterised sequences, including the putative methyltransferase PG_1098 from Porphyromonas gingivalis (Swiss:Q7MVG6, PDB:3ll7). Members of this entry contain a THUMP-like domain at the C-terminal (Pfam:PF18096), following this domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6933
comment: This domain is found in bacterial and archaeal uncharacterised proteins. It is typically between 150 and 160 amino acids in length. It is remotely related to ribonuclease H-like nucleases but it is unlikely to possess any enzymatic activity. (from Pfam)

label: GST_C_7
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Glutathione transferase (GST) Swiss:I6ZUH3 from Phanerodontia chrysosporium and similar sequences mainly found in fungi and also in some plant and proteobacterial species. This protein belongs to the "etherase-like" class of fungal cytosolic GSTs. This protein is capable of binding nonsubstrate ligands derived from lignin degradation [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: Cep192_D8
comment: Cep192 is a centrosomal protein with key roles in centriole duplication and pericentriolar material recruitment, organisation and regulation. Most of the metazoan Cep192 homologs consist of eight ASH/PapD-like domains. These are located at the C-terminal part of the proteins and are likely arranged in a beads-on-string fashion. This entry represents the eighth domain found in the metazoan Cep192 homologs. (from Pfam)

label: CT0912-like_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Swiss:Q8KDY2 from Chlorobaculum tepidum (CT0912), a functionally uncharacterised protein with a ferredoxin-like domain repeat. This domain shows an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6943
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share significant sequence similarity with each of the specificity subunit target recognition domains of type I restriction-modification enzymes and are predicted to adopt the same structure. (from Pfam)

label: GST_C_8
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Glutathione S-transferase from Agrobacterium fabrum (Atu5508, Swiss:Q7D2W7) and similar sequences mainly found in proteobacteria. This domain adopts an alpha-helical configuration (PMID: 16988933). (from Pfam)

label: TilS-like
comment: This entry represents a C-terminal domain (CTD) present in TilS ligases proteins, probably implicated in the recognition of the tRNA accetor stem (PMID: 15894617). TilS ligates lysine onto the cytidine present at position 34 of the AUA codon-specific tRNA(Ile) that contains the anticodon CAU, in an ATP-dependent manner (PMID: 15894617). (from Pfam)

label: PFIN
product_name: plasmid fertility inhibition factor family protein
hmm_name: plasmid fertility inhibition factor family protein
comment: FiwA-like proteins are fertility inhibition factors (FIN), which are employed by plasmids to block import of rival plasmids [1,2]. FiwA is encoded by plasmid RP1 and blocks the transfer of plasmid R388 (PMID: 2559940). A FiwA-like protein called Osa (oncogenic suppressive activity) inhibits the oncogenic properties of Agrobacterium tumefaciens (PMID: 9864329). Osa is structurally similar to the ParB/Sulfiredoxin fold (PMID: 25358815). Osa has been shown to have ATPase and DNAse activities, and can block T-DNA transfer into plants [5,6]. (from Pfam)

label: IBR_1
comment: This entry represents an IBR domain, related to Pfam:PF01485. (from Pfam)

label: GKRP_SIS_2
product_name: Glucokinase regulatory protein, second SIS domain
name_orig: Glucokinase regulatory protein, second SIS domain
hmm_name: Glucokinase regulatory protein, second SIS domain
comment: Glucokinase regulatory protein (GKRP) binds glucokinase (GK) mainly through hydrophobic interactions, functioning as an allosteric switch in blood glucose control by the liver (PMID: 23733961). GKRP is trilobal in shape, consisting of two topologically identical sugar isomerase (SIS) domains capped by an alpha-helical lid domain (Pfam:PF20741). This entry represents the second SIS domain from GKRP (PMID: 23733961). (from Pfam)

label: Rv2466c-like
comment: Mycothiol-dependent nitroreductase Rv2466c is a key oxidoreductase that mediates the reductive activation of TP053, a thienopyrimidine derivative that kills replicating and non-replicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This enzyme transforms nitro-containing compounds to their corresponding amine and uses as a cofactor, a low molecular weight sugar thiol, mycothiol. The Rv2466c structure adopts a thioredoxin-like fold but it forms an unique homodimer in which the C-terminal beta-strand is swapped between the thioredoxin domains of each subunit [1-3]. Rv2466c undergoes significant conformational changes upon formation of its oxidized state (PMID: 26546681). (from Pfam)

label: PFF1_TM
comment: This entry includes fungal vacuolar membrane proteases, such as PFF1 from yeast, which may be involved in vacuolar sorting and osmoregulation (PMID: 23679341). It is the homologue of human ERMP1 (PMID: 35175277). According to AlphaFold structure prediction, these proteins consist of a M28 peptidase domain (Pfam:PF04389) at the N-terminal, a central transmembrane domain (TM) and a C-terminal domain with an elongated beta-sandwich-like fold (Pfam:PF22250), similar to the Mu homology domain (MHD) (Pfam:PF00928). This entry represents the TM domain of PFF1 and fungal its homologues. (from Pfam)

label: Gp44-like_2nd
product_name: Baseplate hub protein gp44-like, second domain
name_orig: Baseplate hub protein gp44-like, second domain
hmm_name: Baseplate hub protein gp44-like, second domain
comment: This domain is found in Baseplate hub protein gp44 from Escherichia phage Mu and similar proteins found in tailed bacteriophages and proteobacterial prophages. This domain is located C-terminal to Pfam:PF21683 and N-terminal to Pfam:PF21929. (from Pfam)

label: BDI_1685-like_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of BDI_1685 from Parabacteroides distasonis (Swiss:A6LCM3) and similar bacterial sequences. This domain is usually found associated with Pfam:PF17128. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6953
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share significant sequence similarity to HTH winged helix domains, in particular to the N-terminal domain of transcriptional regulator BrxR and RNA polymerase III subunit RPC82. (from Pfam)

label: TraI-like_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of TraI proteins, which adopts an OB fold-like structure. TraI is a plasmid-specific component required for the initiation process of transfer DNA synthesis, as part of a specialised nucleoprotein complex - the relaxosome, together with TraH, I, and J. Site- and strand-specific cleavage at the transfer origin is dependent of TraI and TraJ. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6970
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from bacteria and protostome animals. It is predicted to fold into a curved meander beta-sheet. It contains four highly conserved cysteine residues, two of which are predicted to cluster together in space and are likely involved in disulfide bond formation. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_91
comment: This winged helix-turn-helix domain is often found in proteobacteria and is likely to be involved in DNA-binding. (from Pfam)

label: PBP2_Ca3427_like
comment: This entry represents domain II of CA3427 from Candida albicans which consists of a 5 stranded beta-sheet (PMID: 21494601). (from Pfam)

label: PaaX-like_Fer-like
comment: This entry represents a ferredoxin-like domain in PaaX-like protein from Jannaschia sp. (PDB:3l09). PaaX-like is a putative transcriptional regulator. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6985
comment: This entry represents a family of bacterial domains of unknown function. (from Pfam)

label: MATH_2
comment: This motif has been called the Meprin And TRAF-Homology (MATH) domain.ED A0A835B747.1/23-123; A0A835B747.1/23-76; (from Pfam)

label: DUF7002
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share sequence similarity with DarT toxin and are likely to adopt the same structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7005
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. These proteins share partial sequence similarity to the collagenase catalytic core with invariant HExxH motif. (from Pfam)

label: ARPP-2
comment: ARPP-2 (ARG and Rhodanese-Phosphatase-superfamily-associated Protein domain 2) shows a distinguishing group of absolutely conserved residues distinct from ARPP-1 (Pfam:PF20208). ARPP-2 is typically found fused to a C-terminal HTH domain and adjacent to a Rot/TROVE domain fused to a vWA domain [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DAM-like-phage2
comment: This domain has been characterised as part of a nucleic acid modifying system in certain phages. This system may modify tRNAs that are encoded adjacent to the system on the genome. These tRNAs are then possibly packaged into the viral head, to render them resistant to host restriction (PMID: 36968430). (from Pfam)

label: HisKin-conflict
product_name: Histidine Kinase domain observed in conflict contexts
name_orig: Histidine Kinase domain observed in conflict contexts
hmm_name: Histidine Kinase domain observed in conflict contexts
comment: This Histidine Kinase domain is predicted to function in signal transduction during effector activation in at least a subset of (TOTE TPR, OB, TBP, Effector) biological conflict systems (PMID: 35609893). (from Pfam)

label: LiaI-LiaF-TM_PspC
comment: This entry represents the transmembrane region found in LiaI-LiaF, found fused to some PspC, an integral membrane protein first identified in the proteobacterial PSP system. PspC is critical in sensing the membrane stress response and restoring envelope integrity (Preprint https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.09.24.301986). (from Pfam)

label: Scabin-like
comment: This entry represents a group of mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase toxins, including scabin (Swiss:C9Z6T8), a novel DNA-targeting enzyme from the plant pathogen Streptomyces scabiei [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: RskA_N
hmm_name: RskA family anti-sigma factor N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of the anti-sigma-K factor from Mycobacterium tuberculosis (RskA), which positively regulates expression of the antigenic proteins MPB70 and MPB83 [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: BphC_D1
comment: This domain is found in dihydroxybiphenyl dioxygenase BphC and related proteins. This enzyme contains a non-heme iron atom and plays an important role in degrading biphenyl/polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs). (from Pfam)

label: Gp18_dom_I
product_name: Tail sheath protein Gp18-like domain I
name_orig: Tail sheath protein Gp18-like domain I
hmm_name: Tail sheath protein Gp18-like domain I
comment: This entry represents domain I from bacteriophage tail sheath proteins such as Gp18, a protein that surrounds the central non-contractile tail tube of the tail sheath from bacteriophages, which contracts during infection [1,2]. These proteins consist of three domains, domains I, II (Pfam:PF17481) and III (Pfam:PF17482). Domains I and II form the protease-resistant fragment (PMID: 19229296). (from Pfam)

label: NagA_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal region of the composite domain from NagA (N-acetylglucosamine-6-phosphate deacetylase), a protein that catalyses the hydrolysis of the N-acetyl group of N-acetyl-glucosamine-6-phosphate (GlcNAc-6-P) to glucosamine 6-phosphate and acetate, the first committed step in the biosynthetic pathway to amino-sugar-nucleotides [1-3]. This domain has a pseudo-barrel fold that is interrupted by the catalytic beta/alpha barrel domain. (from Pfam)

label: EF_0837-like_N
comment: This entry includes proteins that can catalyse the deacetylation of acetyl-(R)-mandelate in vitro, but with very low efficiency, such as deacetylase Oant_2987, Atu3266 and EF_0837 (PMID: 23214420). This entry represents the composite domain. (from Pfam)

label: SSB_1
comment: This family includes single stranded binding proteins. They play an important role in DNA replication, recombination and repair. (from Pfam)

label: Ribosomal_uL24m-like
comment: This entry represents a domain found in the homologues of large ribosomal subunit protein uL24m. This protein is a component of the mitochondrial ribosome (mitoribosome) (PMID: 24675956). (from Pfam)

label: Hda_lid
comment: This model was built to identify the lid domain of HdaA, a DnaA homolog that acts in the regulatory inactivation of DnaA. However, in a number of species, this HMM has two qualifying his, a strong one to HdaA, and a much weaker hit to DnaA that just manages to exceed the gathering thresholds.

label: SNaCT5
comment: The SNaCT domains are a rapidly evolving, monophyletic assemblage of domains found C-terminal to the NACHT module in several bacterial NACHT conflict systems. They contain a well-conserved aspartate near the N-terminus of the domain. SNaCT domains are thought to occlude the NTP-binding region, potentially until they interact with phage-encoded bNACHT inhibitors (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: NA-iREase2
comment: This entry represents a predicted sensor domain in bacterial NACHT conflict systems. It is likely to bind a ligand which could contribute to activation of enzymatic domains additionally fused to the N-terminus of the NACHT module (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: NCH1
comment: This is a helical domain found at the C-terminus of bacterial NACHT conflict systems (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: Toast-rack_PspC-Cterm
comment: This entry represents the ToastRack domain found fused to some PspC (PMID: 38809013). (from Pfam)

label: Gp38_E217
comment: E217 is a Pseudomonas phage used in an experimental cocktail to eradicate cystic fibrosis-associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This entry represents the homologs of E217 baseplate cap component gp38. Gp38 forms a heterodimeric complex with gp37. These proteins adopt a similar fold, consisting of two orthogonally packed beta-sheets that coil into a barrel shape. (from Pfam)

label: E217_Gp32
comment: E217 is a Pseudomonas phage used in an experimental cocktail to eradicate cystic fibrosis-associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Stacked hexamers of the tail tube protein gp32 form the central tube of the E217 tail. The tail tube protein is structurally conserved and homologous to the tail tube protein found in non-contractile tails, bacterial pyocins, and type VI secretion systems. Gp32 consists of a classical beta-sandwich that contains two four-stranded sheets facing each other and surrounded by a long alpha-helix and an extended beta-turn (PMID: 37422479). (from Pfam)

label: GA_3
comment: This entry represents a small domain found in bacterial cell surface proteins. It adopts a three helical bundle structure and is often found in several tandem copies. This domain was identified in potential periscope proteins. Most member proteins occur in the Bacillota, and nearly half of members have LPXTG-like sortase recognition and processing site.

label: CatAgl_D1
comment: This entry represents a domain found in the homologues of Alpha-1,3-glucanase. This domain is found N-terminal in the catalytic domain (CatAgl-FH1). It folds into a beta-sandwich that bears similarity to CBM35 domains and is thought to possess carbohydrate-binding function (PMID: 31788942). (from Pfam)

label: PsaO_TMD
comment: PsaO is one of the nine membrane-embedded subunits of photosystem I. This entry represents the transmembrane domain that was shown to consists of three transmembrane helices arranged in an L-shape (PMID: 36951548). (from Pfam)

label: TraI_middle
comment: This entry represents a domain found in the middle region of TraI-like proteins (such as Swiss:I1YLR9), following the N-terminal relaxase domain. (from Pfam)

label: GT-D-like
comment: This domain is related to the GT-D fold glycosyltransferase domain (Pfam:PF08759). These protein domains share a common sequence motif R[VIL]GDGE, significant structural similarity based on the predicted AF2 model, but low sequence similarity. This domain is found standalone and in combination with other domains in a number of proteins mainly from Firmicutes. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7020
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins of unknown function. AlphaFold shows confident dimer interaction. (from Pfam)

label: NOMO1-like_2nd
product_name: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, second beta sandwich domain
name_orig: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, second beta sandwich domain
hmm_name: BOS complex subunit NOMO1-like, second beta sandwich domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of human BOS complex subunit NOMO1 and similar sequences mainly from animals and plants. NOMO1 is a component of the multi-pass translocon (MPT) complex that mediates insertion of multi-pass membrane proteins into the lipid bilayer of membranes (PMID: 36261522). This domain is predicted to adopt a seven stranded beta sandwich fold. (from Pfam)

label: PRISE
comment: This NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold-like domain is found in a number of enzymes with oxidoreductase activity. Amongst them are the PRISEs (Progesterone 5beta-reductase and/or iridoid synthase-like 1,4-enone reductases) that are involved in cardenolide and iridoid biosynthesis. This domain is also found in the short chain dehydrogenase ausT, involved in the terpenoid biosynthesis pathway. (from Pfam)

label: RM44_endonuclase
product_name: Large ribosomal subunit protein mL44, endonuclease domain
name_orig: Large ribosomal subunit protein mL44, endonuclease domain
hmm_name: Large ribosomal subunit protein mL44, endonuclease domain
comment: Large ribosomal subunit protein mL44 (RM44) is a component of the 39S subunit of mitochondrial ribosome. It may play a role in the assembly/stability of nascent mitochondrial polypeptides exiting the ribosome. This entry represents the endonuclease (RNase III-like) domain [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_68
comment: This entry represents a putative helix-turn-helix domain that may be involved in DNA binding. (from Pfam)

label: LEM-3_GIY-YIG
comment: This domain is found in the metazoan homologues of LEM-3 DNA nuclease. LEM-3 processes chromatin bridges that arise from incomplete DNA replication, unresolved recombination intermediates, or the perturbance of chromosome structure (PMID: 29463814). It localizes to the midbody and this localization depends on factors needed for midbody assembly. LEM-3 is composed of two domains: a LEM domain and a GIY-YIG nuclease domain represented by this entry. (from Pfam)

label: RsmI_C
comment: This entry represents a small helical domain at the C-terminus of RsmI that folds into a typical three helical DNA/RNA binding bundle containing HTH motif. This domain is found in Ribosomal RNA small subunit methyltransferase I (RsmI) and related proteins. RsmI is an S-adenosyl-L-methionine-dependent methyltransferase that catalyses the 2-O-methylation of the ribose of cytidine 1402 (C1402) in 16S rRNA. It may play a role in fine-tuning the shape and functions of the P-site to increase the translation fidelity. In vitro, active on the assembled 30S subunit, but not naked 16S rRNA or 70S ribosomes. (from Pfam)

label: SCO7613_CTERM
comment: This HMM describes a conserved region found at the C-terminus of large but variable length hydrophobic proteins found mostly in members of the Actinomycetes such as Streptomyces, Micromonospora, Actinoplanes, and Nocardioides. The founding protein, SCO7613 from Streptomyces coelicolor, is among a limited set of proteins directly regulated by the response regulator transcription factor MacR (Morphogenesis and ACtinorhodin Regulator, SCO2120).

label: phage_HTJ
hmm_name: phage head-tail joining protein, gpW family
comment: Pfam model PF02831.19 describes protein W, a head-tail joining protein of phage lambda that is just 68 amino acids long, but that model is rather narrowly defined. This model represents a large expansion of the family, and makes the presumption that additional proteins found similarly serve as phage head-tail joining proteins.

label: hydrolase_RcgR
product_name: RcgR family putative quorum lactone hydrolase
hmm_name: RcgR family putative quorum lactone hydrolase
comment: RcgA (Rhizobial Conjugative Gene A), from a Rhizobium favelukesii plasmid, plays an essential role in a quorum sensing-dependent conjugative transfer system. It is thought to be a transporter that allows uptake of a quorum-signaling lactone. Its partner protein, RgcR, with an alpha/beta hydrolase domain, inhibits the transfer, probably by inactivating the signaling molecule.

label: RNA_bind_RnpM
comment: Pfam model PF04296 identifies the DUF448 or YlxR family of RNA-binding proteins, a broad family with considerable variety in length. This model describes for now a limited set of the proteins from that family, similar to NP_389543.1 from Bacillus subtilis, with similar lengths and conservation of several motifs, pending confirmation that more distant homologs act in a similar manner.

label: tail_chap_PVL
hmm_name: phage tail assembly chaperone G, phiN315 family
comment: Analogous to gpG from phage lambda, but not obviously homologous, members of this family are tail assembly chaperone proteins, required for a scaffold function during tail assembly but not a part of mature phage. It appears that this protein behaves the same as lambda gpG, with a -1 frameshift site near its C-terminus that enables about 1 in 20 translations be synthesized in a longer form. The region downstream of the frameshift is represented by NF047426.

label: collar_FlbB
comment: Members of this family, found only spirochetes, are the collar protein FlbB of periplasmic-type (i.e. spirochete-type) flagella. Note that the term FlbB is used in other lineages to describe a flagellar transcriptional activator unrelated to this protein.

label: HeatShock_HspR
product_name: heat shock protein transcriptional repressor HspR
hmm_name: heat shock protein transcriptional repressor HspR
comment: HspR (heat shock protein repressor) binds a widely conserved DNA element known as HAIR (HspR-associated inverted repeat). All members of the seed alignment were found encoded in the vicinity of DnaJ. This HMM represents a strongly conserved central region of about 92 amino acids. Member proteins occur in lineages as distant as Campylobacter, Helicobacter, Mycobacterium, Streptomyces, Bifidobacterium, and Deinococcus. HspR forms a homodimer, although in some species, double-length proteins with a tandem duplication are found (see NF047377). In Mycobacterium tuberculosis, DnaK was shown to bind directly to the HspR-HAIR complex.

label: TAA_AbiEi
product_name: type IV toxin-antitoxin system AbiEi family antitoxin
hmm_name: type IV toxin-antitoxin system AbiEi family antitoxin

label: T4SS_SepA_fam
comment: A member of this family, BAB1_1492 from Brucella abortus (CAJ11448.1), was described as a novel secreted effector protein and named SepA (secreted effector protein A). Oddly, it is reported to aggregate in the periplasm rather than engaging immediately with the type IV secretion system (T4SS). Full length homologs are found in a wide range of species, complicating the picture of how its secretion occurs.

label: BrnA_antitoxin_add
product_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system BrnA family antitoxin
hmm_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system BrnA family antitoxin

label: MazE_PemI_antitoxin
product_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system PemI/MazE family antitoxin
hmm_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system PemI/MazE family antitoxin

label: TA_anti_VapB15
product_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system VapB15 family antitoxin
hmm_name: type II toxin-antitoxin system VapB15 family antitoxin

label: Cys_reg_CymR
comment: CymR, the master regulator of cysteine metabolism in Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus, belongs to the Rrf2 family of transcriptional regulators. Most members of the family have no Cys residue, but the member from Staphylococcus aureus, with a lone Cys residue at position 25, is reported to use that residue to sense oxidative stress.

label: sig_GCG_CRPN_rpt
comment: Members of this family have an architecture consisting of a signal peptide, then this conserved domain with a core region featuring two invariant Cys residues in the consensus sequence GCGPGFHRGPWGGCRPN, and then usually repetitive, low-complexity (reduced alphabet) sequence to the C-terminus.

label: EF_P_mod_YmfI
comment: Members of this family, named YmfI after the founding member from Bacillus subtilis, are restricted to bacterial species in which the post-translational modification of elongation factor P (EF-P) is 5-aminopentanol at Lys-32. This protein, a homolog of the 3-keto-acyl ACP reductase FabG, reduces EF-P 5-aminopentanone to EF-P 5-aminopentanol. All 427 members of the seed alignment are from species in which YmfF and YmfH homologs are encoded by an adjacent gene pair.

label: BOW99_gp33_fam
comment: Members of this family of small proteins occur in phage genomes and prophage regions of bacterial genomes. The family is named for an arbitrarily selected member protein, BOW99_gp33 from Streptococcus phage phiARI0462. This family includes clusters 9965, 10400, 12290, 57631, 82802, and 119767 from the work of Sberro, et al. The function is unknown.

label: tail_chap_PVL_C
hmm_name: phage tail assembly chaperone GT carboxyl-terminal domain
comment: A common motif in phage that rely on a tape measure protein to control the length of the tail tube is to have two tandem ORFs, with protein biosynthesis that makes the upstream protein, but a small percentage of the time undergoes a -1 frameshift at a slippery site near the C-terminus and then continues through the downstream ORF to make a long version of the protein. The short form is referred to as gpG, and the long form as gpGT. This HMM represents the coding region C-terminal to that frameshift, present in gpGT but not in gpG. However, a number of member proteins, such as WP_311056037.1, represent the long form, gpGT, encoded with no frameshift. The region upstream of the frameshift is represented by NF047360.

label: ribo_bS22
