comment: 30S ribosomal protein bS22 is a bacterial ribosomal protein of very small size, with a limited species distribution that includes Mycobacterium tuberculosis and related species. It has also been called uL41, but the designation now apparently agreed by the crysallographic community is bS22.

label: LA_2272_repeat
hmm_name: LA_2272 family surface protein repeat (two copies)
comment: This HMM, with a length of 30, describes two tandem 15-amino acid repeats. Numbers of repeats in proteins vary. Notable surface-exposed proteins with this repeat domain include lipoproteins LA_2272 and LA_2273 from Leptospira interrogans and VC2662 from Vibrio cholerae.

label: LA3751_2_3_fam
comment: Members of this family of uncharacterized membrane proteins, averaging over 500 amino acids in length, occur primarily in the genus Leptospira. Four paralogs are encoded in Leptospira interrogans serovar Lai str. 56601, including tandem proteins LA_3751, LA_3752, and LA_3753. Weak hits by a minority of the members of this family to Pfam model PF13231, named after dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferase, suggests that members of this family on the whole may be glycosyltransferases.

label: WxxxWxxW_dom
comment: This extremely hydrophobic domain is found in Clostridia and related Gram-positive species, either as the C-terminal portion of a protein with an N-terminal helix-turn-helix predicted DNA-binding domain, or as nearly the full length of a protein. This domain includes a highly unusual motif within a strongly hydrophobic stretch, WxxxWxxWxxY, in which all four aromatic residues are invariant.

label: LA_3696_Nterm
comment: Members of this family, found primarily but not exclusively in the genus Leptospira, share this homology domain at the N-terminus, typically share a shorter C-terminal domain as well, and are variable in length and sequence between the two well-conserved regions. The function is unknown.

label: YonT_type_I_tox
product_name: type I TA system toxin YonT
hmm_name: type I TA system toxin YonT
comment: YonT, encoded in a prophage region in Bacillus subtilis, is type I toxin-antitoxin (TA) system about 59 amino acids in length.

label: XAC2610_fam
comment: The founding member of this family, XAC2610, whose structure has been solved, is an apparent type IV secretion system effector protein. This HMM describes a central region of that protein.

label: telomere_Tpg
comment: Tpg (terminal protein gene) and Tap (telomere-associated protein) together act to maintain the linear topology and telomere regions of the linear chromosome, and some linear plasmids, in Streptomyces and a few related bacteria. Thr-114, in a motif TD[DQ] is the site of DNA attachment to protein.

label: orf58_phage_fam
comment: Proteins of this family are homologs of the phage protein (orf58) annotated from the genome of Actinobacillus actinomycetemcomitans bacteriophage (PMID: 15292156). Their function is not clear yet.

label: BPSS1187_fam
comment: BPSS1187 from Burkholderia pseudomallei was identified as a type III secretion system (T3SS) protein, and a useful marker for detecting Burkholderia pseudomallei and discriminating it from multiple other Burkholderia species. Members of the broader family represented by this HMM occur in genera widely separated taxonomically, including Leptospira (Spirochaetia), Rhodopirellula ( Flavobacteriales), Gloeobacter (Cyanobacteriota), Mesorhizobium (Alphaproteobacteria), and Polyangium (Myxococcota).

label: IS66_ISRel24_TnpA
hmm_name: IS66-like element accessory protein TnpA, ISRel24 branch
comment: Members of this family include the transposase accessory protein TnpA of IS66-like insertion sequences. It shows N-terminal domain of IS3 family transposases.

label: antiviral_Brig1
comment: Brig1 is a DNA glycosylase that targets a-glucosylated hmC nucleobases in the viral DNA to provide defense against viral infections. It excises a-glucosyl-hmC nucleobases from ssDNA to generate abasic sites.

label: throspo3_MtsC
comment: MtsC (Myxococcus thrombospondin repeat protein C) is part of an operon of at least four tandem thrombospondin type 3 (TSP3) repeat, and is the only one with a MYXO-CTERM sorting signal domain at the C-terminus. It functions in cell-cell cohesion that contributes to social motility and fruiting-body development, among other processes.

label: FFLEE_fam
comment: This uncharacterized family is named for its most strongly conserved motif, FF[LVF][ED][ED]LY. Members of this family are found in mostly in gamma-proteobacterial genera such as Acinetobacter, Aeromonas, Alteromonas, and Psychrobacter, but also in beta-proteobacteria and in the Leptospira genus of spirochetes.

label: lipo_NMCC_0638
comment: Members of this protein, including NMCC_0638 from Neisseria meningitidis, have two mostly invariant Cys residues. In about a quarter of family members, an additional Cys residue is present in what appears to be a lipoprotein signal peptide.

label: HYC_CC_PP
comment: This uncharacterized protein family, widespread in the widespread, is named for three well-separated strong motifs, HYC, CC (which may appear twice), and PP.

label: PP_RS20740_fam
comment: A missense mutation (V338F) in the uncharacterized protein PP_RS20740 of Pseudomonas putida improved tolerance to furfural, a metabolite of pentose degradation. The function is unknown.

label: slr1658_superfam
comment: It has been reported that Slr1658 had extensive effects on the expression of genes encoding regulatory proteins, proteins involved in the remodeling and degradation of the photosynthetic apparatus and proteins modulating electron transport in Cyanobacteria. Slr1658 homologs have been identified in many species.

label: SCO6745_fam_HTH
comment: This family is related to Pfam model PF21863, but is more selective, and identifies only full length homologs of SCO6745 from Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2) and MSMEG_6750 from Mycobacterium smegmatis str. MC2 155. PF21863 suggests a relationship to helix-turn-helix transcriptional regulators such as MarR.

While PF18085 describes an N-terminal cap domain found in maltokinase, models NF047743 and NF047744 describe much shorter proteins, typically in contexts that do not include maltokinase-like proteins.

comment: This family is named for LIC_13387 from Leptospira interrogans, but members are found in wide variety of bacterial species. In Leptospira, LIMLP_17285 was observed to have lower expression in response to hydrogen peroxide stress. The family is otherwise uncharacterized.

label: Omp85_fam
comment: Omp85 family outer membrane proteins play essential roles in outer membrane biogenesis in diderm bacteria. The majority of Omp85 orthologs are bipartite and consist of a conserved OM-embedded 16-stranded beta-barrel and variable periplasmic functional domains.

label: leader_Chryseo
comment: The sequence region that defines this family, is found primarily in the genus Chryseobacterium, always at the N-terminus. It ends with a Gly-Gly (or Gly-Ala) motif, following which members of this family, while usually Cys-rich, become highly diverse. This behavior is highly typical of bacteriocin leader peptides. Some members of this family (e.g. WP_266173784.1) are found near C39 family GlyGly peptidase domain-containing transporter proteins, lantibiotic dehydratases, etc.

label: MST_Rv0443
comment: Members of this protein, found in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and related actinobacterial species, attach mycothiol to the Cys-derived sulfur of mycothiol, an analog of glutathione.

label: SS_mature_LptM
comment: The small outer membrane lipoprotein LptM (previously called YifL) binds LptD and assists it in properly forming its disulfide bonds.

label: relax_MbeA_E1

comment: MbeA, as described in the mobilization region of the ColE1 plasmid, fully overlaps two tandem mobilization proteins on the same strand, MbeB and MbeD.

comment: Members of this family of uncharacterized proteins have two CxxC motifs, suggesting metal (probably zinc)-binding activity. The family is named for member protein ECs_2282 from Escherichia coli O157:H7 str. Sakai.

label: pyridox_DH_SDR
comment: The pyridoxal 4-dehydrogenase of Mesorhizobium loti is homotetrameric, and belongs to the SDR family of oxidoreductases. All members of the seed alignment are encoded near a gene for 4-pyridoxolactonase.

label: pyridox_lacton
comment: 4-pyridoxolactonase, while related to quorum-quenching N-acyl-homoserine lactonases, is instead an enzyme of pyridoxine degradation via 4-pyridoxolactone. All members of the seed alignment are encoded near a gene for pyridoxal 4-dehydrogenase.

label: ABC_BMP_B6

hmm_name: putative B6 ABC transporter substrate-binding protein
comment: Members of this family are found regularly in the vicinity of a trio of proteins responsible for the degradation of pyridoxine (a form of vitamin B6), and are proposed here to be the substrate-binding protein of B6 uptake ABC transporter complex.

label: lamb_exclu_cor
comment: The lipoprotein Cor, as found in temperate lambdoid phage that depend on FhuA as a phage receptor, functions in phage exclusion through its interaction with FhuA.

label: lactonase_AidB

comment: AidB (AutoInducer-Degrading gene from Bosea sp.), a quorum-quenching N-acyl homoserine lactonase (QEM23349.1), gives its name to a distinctive subfamily of N-acyl homoserine lactonases, one that appears more closely related to subclass B3 metallo-beta-lactamases than most other family subfamilies.

label: RDAC_fam
comment: Members of this uncharacterized protein family average about 80 amino acids in length, and do not seem to belong to any well-conserved gene neighborhoods. The family is named for a motif rather well conserved in one branch of the family.

label: GTA_spike_fiber
product_name: phage head spike fiber domain-containing protein
comment: This domain is found in the fiber proteins of spikes that decorate the heads of phage and of phage-like particles such as the gene transfer agent of Rhodobacter capsulatus. In many proteins, the domain is repeated two or more times, and other domains may be present.

label: IS256_N_4Cys
comment: This domain, with two CxxC motifs, occurs as the N-terminal region of subsets of transposases from insertion sequence (IS) mobile elements of at least the IS256, IS1595, IS6, and IS1 families.

label: IS256_Zn_var
product_name: IS256 family transposase, variant Zn-binding type
hmm_name: IS256 family transposase, variant Zn-binding type
comment: Members of this family are transposases related to ISKpn71, which ISFinder groups with the IS256 family, but which differs considerably and has an apparent Zn-binding 34-amino acid N-terminal domain with (usually) two CxxC motifs (model NF048018). See BlastRule NBR016911 for more information about ISKpn71.

label: DUF7034
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from Dictyostelia. It is predicted to adopt Ig-like fold with the fibronectin type III-like topology. (from Pfam)

label: KH_NusA_C
product_name: Transcription termination/antitermination protein NusA, KH domain
name_orig: Transcription termination/antitermination protein NusA, KH domain
hmm_name: Transcription termination/antitermination protein NusA, KH domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Transcription termination/antitermination protein NusA from a group of bacterial proteins. NusA contains two KH domains that associate with each other to produce a single continuous binding surface, which interacts with a short ribonucleotide recognition sequence (PMID: 16193062). This entry represents the second KH domain. (from Pfam)

label: HalD
comment: This domain is found in ornithine halogenase HalD and related proteins including L-lysine 4-chlorinase BesD and L-lysine 5-chlorinase HalB. In addition to ornithine, HalD chlorinates lysine but with slower rate. This preference of HalD for ornithine is due to a narrower active site pocket (PMID: 36913566). These enzymes are structurally very similar and adopt a typical cupin-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: IG_AIR9
comment: This entry represents an Ig-like domain known as the A9 domain that is repeated in the members included here, such as AIR9 from A. thaliana and related proteins from plants, in which it appears 10/11 times, which in other sequences, it appears 5/6 times such as AMP-ACTIVATED PROTEIN KINASE from Trypanosoma cruzi (PMID: 17027491). AIR9 and TAN1 function redundantly to maintain POK1 at the division site to ensure correct cell wall placement and interactions between POK1 and AIR9 are important for division plane orientation and plant growth (PMID: 36005863). (from Pfam)

label: KOW2_Spt5
product_name: Transcription elongation factor SPT5, second KOW domain
name_orig: Transcription elongation factor SPT5, second KOW domain
hmm_name: Transcription elongation factor SPT5, second KOW domain
comment: This entry includes Transcription elongation factor SPT5, a component of the elongation factor DRB-sensitivity inducing factor (DSIF) that plays multiple roles during transcription [1-4]. SPT5 is a multidomain protein consisting of an N-terminal NusG domain (Pfam:PF03439), tandem of KOW domains and and a mobile C-terminal-repeat region. This entry represents the second KOW domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7079
comment: This is a presumed domain found in a set of bacterial sequences, whose function is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7107
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised domains that show similarities to members of the colipase superfamily/ (from Pfam)

label: AprA_N
comment: This entry represents a domain found N-terminal in the homologues of AprA Methyltransferase 1. AprA is an S-adenosylmethionine and Fe3+-dependent dimethyltransferase that acts in the initiation steps of apratoxin A biosynthesis [1,2]. This domain has similarity to winged helix domains. (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_FGT1_2
comment: This domain is found in the Arabidopsis FORGETTER1 and related proteins (FGT1). FGT1 mediates stress-induced chromatin memory by modulating nucleosome occupancy (PMID: 27680998). This protein interacts with chromatin remodelers of the SWI/SNF and ISWI families, which also display reduced heat stress memory. The domain represented by this entry is predicted to adopt a zinc ribbon fold and it is the second of the predicted pair of two. (from Pfam)

label: CILP
comment: This domain is found in human Cartilage intermediate layer protein 1 (CILP) and similar animal proteins. CILP is thought to play a role in cartilage scaffolding. This domain is predicted to show a 7 stranded beta sandwich fold. It is often found C-terminal to Pfam:PF13927. (from Pfam)

label: WZC_N
comment: This domain is found in the homologues of Tyrosine-protein kinases Wzc and Etk [1,2]. The later are expressed only in enteropathogenic strains. Wzc is required for the extracellular polysaccharide colanic acid synthesis. The autophosphorylated form of this enzyme is inactive. This domain folds into a beta-sandwich. (from Pfam)

label: Ig_ILCR1
comment: This domain is found in Interleukin cytokine receptor-related protein 1 (ILCR1) from C.elegans and related proteins. This protein forms a receptor complex together with receptor ILCR2, which upon activation acts as a modulator of neuronal activity. When IL-17 binds to the ILCR-1/2 receptor complex, a signaling cascade is triggered that activates the downstream signaling components and results in increased neuronal activity in response to input from oxygen-sensing neurons (PMID: 28099418). The domain represented by this entry is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich with Ig-like topology. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7149
comment: This domain is found in related bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta globular structure and shares significant sequence and structural similarity to members of PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily, in particular, BpuSI N-terminal nuclease domain (Pfam:PF15516). (from Pfam)

label: YnaL
comment: This protein family includes Protein YnaL from Escherichia coli (PMID: 29645342), a 57-residues long protein encoded by a small open reading frame (smORF). (from Pfam)

label: ORF29
comment: This protein family includes ORF29 from Fowl aviadenovirus 4, a 63-residues long protein sequence (PMID: 36851744). (from Pfam)

label: YsdD
comment: This protein family includes Protein YsdD from Escherichia coli (PMID: 29645342), a 26-residues long sequence. (from Pfam)

label: Tubby_C_like
comment: This entry represents a bacterial protein domain that is structurally similar to the C-terminal domain of the tubby protein. It consists of 12 beta strands organised into a barrel with a central C-terminal Alpha helix. This family shows distant sequence similarity to both the Tubby C-terminal domain and the LURP 1 family. (from Pfam)

label: LysC
comment: This entry represents a group of proteins from tailed bacteriophages and bacterial prophages mainly found in proteobacteria, including LysC from Burkholderia phage ST79 (Bacteriophage ST79) (Swiss:R4JDL9). LysC is an Rz1-like component of a phage lytic system, substantially overlapping although not fully embedded in the gene for the Rz-like LysB component. The phage lysis defect in the absence of a functional LysB/LysC system appears in the presence of high concentrations of divalent cations (PMID: 27038077). (from Pfam)

label: Phage_Gp84
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins. One example is the Gp84 protein from Mycobacteriophage L5 Swiss:Q05301. An AlphaFold model of a family member:K5BEF7 has a compact fold of one alpha helix followed by a three stranded beta sheet. The function of these proteins is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7180
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein that is found in a variety of phage, predominantly infecting bacteria from the Enterobacteriaceae family such as Escherichia and Salmonella. The protein is typically between 75-120 amino acids in length. These proteins have a highly conserved N-terminus. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TTP_14
comment: This entry represents a family of bacteriophage tail tube proteins. The tail tube forms the inner channel of the contractile tail which is used for DNA transfer from the capsid to the host during infection. The family is found in a wide variety of phages that infect bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: RHH_10
comment: This entry represents a family of phage Ribbon-helix-helix proteins. Members of the RHH superfamily are often parts of toxin/antitoxin systems, suggesting these proteins may form part of a phage immunity response. (from Pfam)

label: AdfA
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins including Anti-DarT factor A from Enterobacteria phage RB69 (AdfA), which plays a role in counteracting the host DarT defense system (PMID: 35725776). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7188
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein of around 185-188 amino acids found in phages that infect Cutibacterium and Propionibacterium species. The function of this protein is currently unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7198
comment: This entry represents a family of putative phage membrane proteins. It is characterized by a single transmembrane helix at the N-terminus that likely serves to anchor these proteins to the membrane. The exact functions of the proteins containing this domain remain unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7205
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins that adopt a small beta barrel-like domain. The family is found in phages infecting members of the Enterobacteriaceae, such as Escherichia, Salmonella, Klebsiella, Cronobacter, Citrobacter, Erwinia, and Pectobacterium. The exact function of this protein within the phage tail is unknown. The family shows a highly conserved length of around 60-75 amino acids, with a few members having N- or C-terminal extensions. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_tail_terminator
comment: This entry represents a family of phage tail terminator proteins. These proteins form a hexameric ring at the top of the phage tail tube in the neck of the phage. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_tail_terminator_3
comment: This entry represents the phage tail termination protein found in a variety of tailed phages that infect Enterobacter. These proteins form a hexameric ring that caps the tail tube at the neck of these bacteriophage. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7218
comment: This entry represents a small conserved sequence region found in a variety of largely mycobacterial phage proteins as well as bacterial proteins. It is often found N-terminal to Pfam:PF07498. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7225
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised protein YnaC and related bacterial proteins. It is usually associated with (Pfam:PF22522). This domain is a winged helix (WH) domain decorated at the C terminus with a small three stranded beta-sheet that packs on the WH domain to form a single globular structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7230
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterized proteins found in phage and bacterial species, particularly in the Gammaproteobacteria class. Members of this family are typically short proteins, ranging from 32 to 85 amino acids in length. Many members are predicted to contain disordered regions and AlphaFold predictions show a non-globular structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7234
comment: This family represents a domain of unknown function, which is found in phage proteins ranging in length from 75 to 88 amino acids. The domain is found in phage that infect Salmonella, Shigella, Serratia, and Enterobacter species. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7240
comment: This protein is found in uncharacterized proteins from various mycobacteriophages and bacterial species including Nocardia and Mycobacterium. The protein is typically around 100 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7257
comment: This entry represents a phage protein which contains a C1q and TNF superfamily domain. Structure prediction suggests that this domain forms a confident homotrimeric interaction. (from Pfam)

label: LtfC
comment: This entry, previously known as DUF7264, represents a domain found in the Minor tail protein Gp6, Collar protein p132, Lateral tail fiber protein C (LtfC) and related phage proteins. This domain folds into a beta-sandwich fold with and extended beta-hairpin that projects away from it. The minor tail proteins Gp6 are likely involved in the assembly or function of the tail structure in bacteriophages. The collar protein p132 forms the T5 phage collar structure, which serves as an anchoring point for the side tail fiber protein pb1, suggesting a role in stabilising the tail fibers and ensuring proper attachment to the host cell (PMID: 36961893). The lateral tail fiber protein C (LtfC) is a component of the DT57C bacteriophage tail tip complex where it forms a dodecameric ring (PMID: 38081816). LtfC adopts a compact, single-domain structure. The LtfC ring is complemented by another lateral tail fiber protein, LtfA. Each of the LtfA monomers is connected to the LtfC assembly in a unique way by augmenting the edges of LtfC beta-sheets with two short beta-strands and thus completing the LtfC beta-sandwich structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7267
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests this protein adopts a rather open conformation of three alpha helices and a possible beta strand suggesting it must interact with other proteins to function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7275
comment: This entry represents the central alpha helical domain from a large family of uncharacterised phage proteins that typically contain three domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7279
comment: This family represents a family of uncharacterised proteins from T even phage. (from Pfam)

label: LRR_EndoS
comment: This entry represents the leucine-rich repeat domain found in Endo-beta-N-acetylglucosaminidase EndoS from Streptococcus spp. EndoS is a secreted protein that catalyzes the hydrolysis of the N-linked oligosaccharides on opsonizing immunoglobulin G (PMID: 11406581), thus contributing to immune response evasion and increased survival of the bacteria in patients (PMID: 12438337). The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Pam3_gp32
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins from phage that includes the Pam3 phage gp32 protein. Structure prediction shows that the protein is composed of a small globular domain. This protein forms a confident dimer according to structure prediction. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7337
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7355
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. The family includes the y13F protein from bacteriophage T4 Swiss:P39499. Structure prediction shows this protein has a compact globular fold composed of three beta strands and two alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7391
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Many of them are annotated as phage tail assembly chaperones, but there does not appear to be any evidence to support this annotation. (from Pfam)

label: SsdA_C
product_name: Single-strand DNA deaminase toxin A, C-terminal
name_orig: Single-strand DNA deaminase toxin A, C-terminal
hmm_name: Single-strand DNA deaminase toxin A, C-terminal
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Single-strand DNA deaminase toxin A from Pseudomonas syringae (SsdA) and similar bacterial and fungal sequences. SsdA shows a typical alpha-beta deaminase configuration (PMID: 33448264). (from Pfam)

label: Cas8b_C
product_name: Type I-B CRISPR Cas8b C-terminal domain
name_orig: Type I-B CRISPR Cas8b C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Type I-B CRISPR Cas8b C-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of Type I-B CRISPR Synechocystis Cas8b and related proteins. Type I CRISPR-Cas systems employ multi-subunit effector Cascade and helicase-nuclease Cas3 to target and degrade foreign nucleic acids, representing the most abundant RNA-guided adaptive immune systems in prokaryotes. Cas8b subunit displays very low sequence similarity with the large subunits of any other known type I CRISPR systems. Cas8b N-terminal domain is involved in PAM recognition (PMID: 38750051). The C-terminal domain of Cas8b and three Cas11b small subunits together form the inner 'belly' of the cascade integral complex. They provide support for the non-target strand within the full R-loop state structure (PMID: 38750051). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7399
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins. The proteins appear to contain two domains. The N-terminal domain contains a small beta sheet wrapped around an alpha helix. The second domain is composed of a pair of alpha helices. The proteins are found in several viruses within the proposed new Crassvirales order of bacteriophages. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7402
comment: This entry represents the domain of unknown function found in bacterial and fungal sequences, including some F5/8 type C domain-containing proteins such as Swissprot:A0A4V0YDU8. This domain may adopt a galactose-binding domain-like fold. This domain is found in several copies, predominantly between two and six times, and it is found in association with PIG-L (Pfam:PF02585) domain. (from Pfam)

label: K1-lyase_C
product_name: K1 capsule-specific polysaccharide lyase, C-terminal domain
name_orig: K1 capsule-specific polysaccharide lyase, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: K1 capsule-specific polysaccharide lyase, C-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of K1 capsule-specific polysaccharide lyase and related proteins. K1-lyase functions as a receptor binding protein (RBP) and mediates the attachment to the host capsular exopolysaccharides (PMID: 35130876). This enzyme possesses a lyase activity that specifically degrades the K1-type polysaccharides of Klebsiella pneumoniae capsule (PMID: 35130876). This domain adopts a beta-sandwich fold (PMID: 35130876). (from Pfam)

label: HCP
comment: This entry represents the Head completion protein (HCP) found in T5-like bacteriophages. HCP forms dodecameric ring assembly and is a component of the bacteriophage neck. It holds the portal protein PrtP dodecameric ring and connects with the trimeric layer of the tail tube via contacts with the tail completion (TCP) hexameric ring (PMID: 38081816). HCP makes contacts with DNA. HCP consists of two domains. The first domain folds into an alpha helical bundle composed of N- and C-terminal helices whereas the second domain adopts a beta-sandwich (PMID: 38081816). (from Pfam)

label: TMP_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal conserved region of the Tape measure protein PB2 and related proteins found mainly in T5-like phages. PB2 functions as a tape measure protein that serves as a base for tail tube protein polymerization and acts as a template for tail length determination [1,2]. This protein fills the tail tube with its long coiled-coil domain and is expelled during the conformation changes that follow T5 binding to host FhuA receptor (PMID: 36961893). The tape measure protein N-terminal region is organized within the tail tube in a three-stranded parallel alpha-helical coiled coil which makes direct contact with the genomic DNA (PMID: 38081816). (from Pfam)

label: PB4_spike
product_name: Straight fiber protein PB4 spike domain
name_orig: Straight fiber protein PB4 spike domain
hmm_name: Straight fiber protein PB4 spike domain
comment: This entry represents the Straight fiber protein PB4 spike found in T5-like bacteriophages. PB4 along with PB3, forms the central straight fiber, bearing the receptor binding protein PB5 at its C terminus (PMID: 36961893). Upon PB5 binding to the host receptor FhuA, the central fiber reorganises and undergoes structural rearrangements that lead to its bending, bringing PB3 close to the host membrane for anchoring (PMID: 36961893). In this process the PB4 spike undergoes structural rearrangement as well. The PB4 spike forms a hetero trimer containing several small distinct subdomains some of which defining a beta-helix, others beta-prism (PMID: 36961893). (from Pfam)

label: Fn3-I_PB4
product_name: Straight fiber protein PB4 first Fn3-like domain
name_orig: Straight fiber protein PB4 first Fn3-like domain
hmm_name: Straight fiber protein PB4 first Fn3-like domain
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal Fn3-like domain of the Straight fiber protein PB4 found in T5-like phages. PB4 along with PB3, forms the central straight fiber, bearing the receptor binding protein PB5 at its C terminus (PMID: 36961893). Upon PB5 binding to the host receptor FhuA, the central fiber reorganises and undergoes structural rearrangements that lead to its bending, bringing PB3 close to the host membrane for anchoring (PMID: 36961893). The PB4-PB3 interactions are ensured by the proximal loops of the first of the three Fn3-like domains of PB4. These interactions are disrupted upon binding to the host receptor and the string of PB4 Fn3-like domains undergoes drastic conformational changes. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7416
comment: This entry represents a small uncharacterised enterobacterial phage protein family. Structure prediction suggests these proteins might adopt a pair of alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7427
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Family members are largely found in mycobacterial phage. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7430
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: T4_RIIA1
comment: This entry represents a family of small uncharacterised proteins found in phage, including T4 RIIA.1 protein (PMID: 2379817). Structure prediction suggests the small proteins adopt a three helical bundle structure. (from Pfam)

label: H_T_assoc
product_name: Phage head to tail associated domain
name_orig: Phage head to tail associated domain
hmm_name: Phage head to tail associated domain
comment: This entry represents a protein domain that is found associated with phage head to tail connector domains Pfam:PF24214, which suggests this domain is part of the phage structure. This region forms a large mainly alpha helical domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7441
comment: This entry represents a conserved domain found predominantly in bacteriophage proteins. The domain is characterized by a highly conserved YDRH motif, which likely plays an important role in the domain's function or structure. This family includes proteins from various phages that infect cyanobacteria, particularly Synechococcus and Prochlorococcus species. The proteins contain a central small domain composed of a three stranded beta sheet with an alpha helix inserted between the second and third strands. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7442
name_orig: Phage membrane protein Family of unknown function (DUF7442)
comment: This entry represents a family of putative membrane proteins found in various bacteriophages. The proteins in this family typically contain two transmembrane helices. The function of these proteins is currently unknown. They are predominantly found in phages infecting Salmonella, Escherichia, and other enterobacteria. The proteins in this family are generally short, with most members being around 80-81 amino acids in length (from Pfam)

label: DUF7486
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised sequences that, according to structure predictions. they may consist on a novel repeat fold which comprise beta-hairpin-beta units organised in four and five units, forming two domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7489
comment: This entry represents a domain from uncharacterised proteins mainly found in Actinomycetes. They are predicted to adopt an OB fold-like beta-barrel. (from Pfam)

label: AEP-like
comment: This entry represents a nucleotidyltransferase of the archaeo-eukaryotic primase superfamily predicted to produce an oligo/cyclic nucleotide signal that activates the associated effectors in the associated prokaryotic antiviral immunity system. These feature a single aspartate in the DXD active site (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: T4_y05I_C
product_name: y05I-like putative transcription factor C-terminal domain
name_orig: y05I-like putative transcription factor C-terminal domain
hmm_name: y05I-like putative transcription factor C-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of family of uncharacterised phage protein that includes T4 y05I protein Swiss:P39240. The family also includes homologues from T2 and T6 phage among others. These proteins contain two domains. These domains appear to be related to those found in the eukaryotic PurA transcription factor. This N-terminal presumably single stranded DNA binding domain contains two copies of a PurA-like repeat. The C-terminal domain contains a single copy that may mediate dimerisation in an analogous fashion to PurA. (from Pfam)

label: T4_y05I_N
product_name: y05I-like putative transcription factor N-terminal domain
name_orig: y05I-like putative transcription factor N-terminal domain
hmm_name: y05I-like putative transcription factor N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of family of uncharacterised phage protein that includes T4 y05I protein Swiss:P39240. The family also includes homologues from T2 and T6 phage among others. These proteins contain two domains. These domains appear to be related to those found in the eukaryotic PurA transcription factor. This N-terminal presumably single stranded DNA binding domain contains two copies of a PurA-like repeat. The C-terminal domain contains a single copy that may mediate dimerisation in an analogous fashion to PurA. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7566
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins from phage. Structure predictions suggest the protein is composed of a larger N-terminal domain with an 8 stranded beta sheet. Followed by a C-terminal helical domain. (from Pfam)

label: CON_HrpB
product_name: ATP-dependent RNA helicase HrpB, connector region
name_orig: ATP-dependent RNA helicase HrpB, connector region
hmm_name: ATP-dependent RNA helicase HrpB, connector region
comment: This domain is found in ATP-dependent RNA helicase HrpB from Escherichia coli and similar proteins mainly found in proteobacteria. It is a connector element (CON) found immediately C-terminal to Pfam:PF08482 (PMID: 30174149). (from Pfam)

label: CC_PcsB
comment: This coiled-coil (CC) domain is found at the N-terminal of Peptidoglycan hydrolase PcsB from Streptococcus pneumoniae (Swiss:Q8DMY4) and similar bacterial proteins. PcsB forms a dimer, and the CC domain as a pair of molecular tweezers locking the catalytic domain of each dimeric partner in an inactive configuration (PMID: 24804636). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7616
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins from enterobacterial phage. The proteins are around 56 residues in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7638
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure consisting of curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on the concave side of it. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7665
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial protein. Proteins in this family are about 150 residues in length. (from Pfam)

label: YxiG_2
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in actinobacteria. Although this family does not contain the YxiG protein from B. subtilis Pfam:PF24711 it is clearly highly related from a structural point of view. These proteins like YxiG are also strongly predicted to form homodimers. (from Pfam)

label: YxiF
comment: This entry represents the uncharacterised YxiF protein from B. subtilis Swiss:P42298. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7677
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria. These proteins are predicted to adopt globular structure that folds into a three helical bundle. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7682
hmm_name: DUF7682 family zinc-binding protein N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents a small zinc-binding domain found to the N-terminus of proteins that belong to the ParE toxin superfamily. The exact function of this domain is unknown. The zinc ligands are composed of the cys and his in the N-terminal CGH motif and the cys residues in the C-terminal CHXC motif. (from Pfam)

label: ParE_like
comment: This entry represents a ParE-like domain found in bacteria, bacteriophages and bacterial prophages. It is predominantly present in RelE/HigB/ParE toxins and some DNA-binding proteins such as transposases and endonucleases. The ParE-like domain is located at the C-terminal in proteins with an N-terminal zinc-binding domain IPR056099. Members of the family that lack the zinc finger appear to form confident homodimers based on structure prediction and are often associated with likely antitoxin proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7685
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains two pairs of conserved cysteine residues and it is predicted to adopt a fold typical for treble clef zinc fingers. It has a detectable similarity to the N-terminal zinc finger domain of the bacterial AAA+ disaggregase ClpG, which confers extreme heat resistance to bacteria. The latter is is crucial for structural integrity and disaggregase functionality of ClpG. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7687
comment: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It shares detectable similarity to a number of type II restriction endonucleases such as DpnII and Ecl18kI and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. It is likely to possess endonuclease activity given the conservation of putative functional site residues. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7693
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and helices packed on one side of it. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7697
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins. Although apparently having a bacterial origin these proteins appear in genomic contexts suggesting they are part of an integrated phage genome. Structurally these proteins are composed of a beta hairpin followed by a pair of alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7700
comment: This domain is usually found in tandem in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a curved anti-parallel beta-sheet and alpha helices packed on one side of it. It contains highly conserved aspartate and histidine residues that may constitute a metal binding site. (from Pfam)

label: Duc1_FFAT_like
comment: This entry represents the FFAT-like motif found in proteins such as Duc1 that interact with VAP (VAMP-associated protein) family members like Scs2 and Scs22. The motif is characterized by two adjacent aromatic residues (typically FF, but YF in Duc1) downstream of an acidic tract. It also contains conserved alanine and glutamate residues at the second and fourth positions after the aromatic pair, respectively. This motif mediates interactions with the Major Sperm Protein (MSP) domains of VAP proteins, playing a crucial role in tethering proteins to ER-PM contact sites. In Duc1, the core of this motif is Y374 and F375, which are essential for the protein's interaction with Scs2 and Scs22, and consequently for its proper localization and function in maintaining plasma membrane lipid composition and cytokinetic ring anchoring. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7713
comment: This entry represents a protein domain that forms an intimate self-self dimer. The domain is found at the C-terminus of proteins that often have a Pfam:PF24735 domain. (from Pfam)

label: NQRA_2nd
comment: This domain is found in several bacterial Na(+)-translocating NADH-quinone reductase subunit A (NqrA) proteins. The Na(+)-translocating NADH: ubiquinone oxidoreductase (Na(+)-NQR) generates an electrochemical Na(+) potential driven by aerobic respiration (PMID: 10587447). This domain has an alpha/beta structure and binds an FMN cofactor (PMID: 25471880). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7723
comment: This small family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins are often found adjacent to proteins from Pfam:PF13711. Structure prediction shows that these proteins are very likely to form a complex. (from Pfam)

label: Gp77
name_orig: Podophage GP4 fiber-tail adaptor protein gp77
comment: This entry represents the Podophage GP4 fiber-tail adaptor protein gp77 and related phage proteins. Bacteriophage tail fibers play a critical role in the early stage of infection by binding to the bacterial surface. In Podophage GP4, five fiber I, each composed of five dimers of gp80 and linked by rope protein, are attached to the five edges of the tail vertex of the icosahedral head of the phage (PMID: 37660940). The fiber-tail adaptor acts as a fulcrum, encircling the dodecameric adaptor I and providing the anchoring sites for the 5-fold symmetric fibers I and II. This circular fiber-tail adaptor consists of 15 copies of protein gp77. Gp77 folds into a beta-sandwich with an Ig-like topology (PMID: 37660940). (from Pfam)

label: AEP_C962R
comment: This AEP domain is found N-terminal in the C962R protein from African swine fever virus and related proteins. C962R protein possesses both DNA polymerization and DNA unwinding activities. This protein adopts a ring-shaped conformation and the N-terminal AEP domain is responsible for the DNA polymerization activity (PMID: 37587714). The C962R AEP domain utilises similar two-cation-assisted mechanism in catalysis as observed in distantly related bacterial and archaeal AEP domains. (from Pfam)

label: WHD_4th_Lhr
comment: This is a winged-helix (WH) domain found in Large helicase -related protein from Escherichia coli (Lhr), DEAD/DEAH box helicase from Mycolicibacterium smegmatis (Swiss:A0QT91) and similar bacterial sequences. These proteins have a C-terminal domain composed of a series of five WH modules (named WH2 to WH6) and a beta-barrel module. This entry represents WH4. It shows three alpha-helices followed by two loops or 'wings' and two beta-strands forming an antiparallel beta-sheet (PMID: 33744958). (from Pfam)

label: HYR_4C
comment: This domain is found in tandem arrays in bacterial cell surface proteins. It contains four cysteines that appear to be likely to form two disulphide bridges between adjacent pairs of domains. It seems likely that these domains form rigid stalks. These domains show sequence similarity to HYR domains. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_WDR19_1st
comment: This entry represents the first beta-propeller of WRD19 (also known as IFT144) from animals and the orthologue from C.elegans DYF2. WDR19 is a core component of the IFT complex A (IFT-A, together with IFT140 and IFT122), a complex required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [1,2]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of beta-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins (PMID: 36462505). (from Pfam)

label: Acb1
comment: This family represents Anti-CBASS protein Acb1 and related homologs. These proteins are components of the cyclic oligonucleotide-based antiphage signalling system (CBASS) which is one of the antiphage defence systems in diverse bacteria that use cyclic nucleotide signals to induce cell death and prevent viral propagation. Acb1 are phosphodiesterases that enable metal-independent hydrolysis of the cyclic di- and trinucleotide CBASS signals (PMID: 35395152). Acb1 enzymes adopt a fold typical for phosphodiesterases consisting of a duplicated beta-alpha-beta-alpha-beta structural motif that coils into a beta-barrel (PMID: 35395152). (from Pfam)

label: bPH_10
comment: This family represents a bacterial PH domain from a set of proteins related to YqeB from B. subtilis. These proteins contain 2 transmembrane helices and bacterial PH domain that includes an unusual alpha/beta/beta/alpha subdomain. The function of these protein is unknown. They contain a C-terminal domain related to an anticodon binding domain found in cysteinyl tRNA ligases. This suggests these proteins may have a role in translation. (from Pfam)

label: TraK_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain from TraK proteins. The TraK C-terminal domain is a structural motif identified within bacterial type IV secretion systems (T4SSs), which are key players in the dissemination of multi-drug resistance. This domain contributes to the formation of the outer-membrane core complex (OMCCF) of T4SS encoded by conjugative F plasmids. The structure of the TraK C-terminal domain shows a compact fold consisting of 4 beta-strands and one alpha helix. This domain interacts with other components of the OMCCF, including TraV and other TraK C-terminal domains. Within the structural unit of the OMCCF, TraK C-terminal domains assemble as dimers, with each domain flipped 180 degrees relative to the other. The TraK C-terminal dimer sits laterally on top of the TraK N-terminal dimer, contributing to the overall stability of the complex. An electrostatic interaction between specific residues within TraK subunits likely participates in the stabilization of the TraK C-terminal dimer (PMID: 34824240). (from Pfam)

label: DesK_N
comment: The protein family includes sensor histidine kinases that function as part of two-component regulatory systems. These kinases are involved in sensing environmental stimuli and initiating appropriate cellular responses. Specifically, one member of the family, DesK, is responsible for detecting changes in membrane fluidity during cold stress and activating the response regulator DesR by phosphorylation, which leads to the induction of the des gene for Delta5 acyl-lipid desaturase [1, 2, 3]. Another member, YvfT, is part of the YvfT/YvfU regulatory system and likely activates the response regulator YvfU by phosphorylation. These kinases play a critical role in adapting to environmental changes by modulating the activity of their respective response regulators. This domain is composed of 5 transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: T4_gp9_10_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of Baseplate protein gp9 from Bacteriophage T4, a component of the viral baseplate (PMID: 12626685). Gp9 connects the long tail fibres of the virus to the baseplate and triggers tail contraction after viral attachment to a host cell. The protein is active as a trimer, with each monomer being composed of three domains. The C-terminal domain is thought to be essential for trimerisation and is organised into an eight- stranded antiparallel beta-barrel, which was found to resemble the 'jelly roll' fold found in many viral capsid proteins (PMID: 10545330). Together with gp11, gp10 initiates the assembly of wedges that then go on to associate with a hub to form the viral baseplate (PMID: 12626685). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7146
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It has significant sequence similarity to the alpha+beta domain found in DNA primases and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. (from Pfam)

label: VapB
comment: This protein family includes a group of uncharacterised short sequences from actinobacteria, including the predicted Antitoxin VapB from Streptomyces cyaneogriseus. Members of this family are predicted to adopt an alpha-beta structure. (from Pfam)

label: RsgI_M
comment: The heat shock genes in B. subtilis can be classified into several groups according to their regulation (PMID: 11157964), and the sigma gene, sigI, of Bacillus subtilis belongs to the group IV heat-shock response genes and has many orthologues in the bacterial phylum Firmicutes (PMID: 11157964). Regulation of sigma factor I is carried out by RsgI from the same operon, and this entry represents the central cytoplasmic portion of RsgI C-terminal to the single transmembrane helix. (from Pfam)

label: Pre_tape_measure
comment: This entry represents a conserved region found in bacteriophage pre-tape measure proteins, located just upstream of the tape measure protein. The region is typically around 140-160 amino acids in length. In some phages the pre-tape measure protein is produced by a programmed translational frameshift. (from Pfam)

label: Kyano_Gp96
comment: This family represents the Gp96 protein from Synechococcus phages. Sequences in the family are typically around 110 residues in length. Gp96 homologues are found in a variety of different Synechococcus phages belonging to the Kyanoviridae family of viruses. The function of Gp96 is currently unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7173
comment: This family contains a set of uncharacterized proteins found predominantly in viruses, particularly bacteriophages. The proteins are typically 130-150 amino acids in length. AlphaFold models of this family show some weak partial structural similarity to the Recombination-associated protein RdgC. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7174
comment: This protein is found in caudoviruses, which are tailed bacteriophages. The protein is typically around 150-180 amino acids in length. Its function is currently unknown. It is found in viruses from the Drexlerviridae family, including Rogunavirinae, Braunvirinae, Tempevirinae, and Kyungwonvirus genera. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_tail_terminator_7
comment: The Tail Tube Terminator Protein family is involved in the assembly of bacteriophage tail structures. Members of this family, such as the Tail Tube Terminator Protein p142, are responsible for capping the tail tube during its polymerization, ensuring that it reaches the correct length. This capping function is crucial for the proper formation of the phage tail, which is essential for the phage's ability to infect host bacteria by facilitating the injection of genetic material. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7203
comment: These proteins are found in various phages infecting bacteria from the Enterobacteriaceae family, such as Escherichia, Salmonella, Shigella, Klebsiella, and Yersinia. They are typically around 100 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7206
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins including from bacteriophage T6. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7207
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various bacteriophages that infect cyanobacteria and other bacterial hosts. The protein ranges in length from approximately 75 to 136 amino acids. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7208
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in large phage virion structural proteins. The domain is approximately 290 to 330 amino acids in length. It is found in a variety of phage proteins infecting bacterial hosts such as Pseudomonas, Vibrio, Ralstonia, and Erwinia, among others. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7210
comment: This entry represents a small domain found in a variety of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7227
comment: This domain of unknown function is found in various phage and bacterial proteins. The domain length ranges from approximately 200 to 260 amino acids. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7228
comment: This family of uncharacterized proteins is found in several Lactococcus phages. All members are short proteins, between 33-59 amino acids in length. The family shows some conserved polar residues at the N-terminus. These proteins appear to be disordered. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7235
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various phages that infect bacteria. The function of this protein is currently unknown. It is typically around 300-340 amino acids in length. This protein contains a predicted coiled-coil region near its C-terminus. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7237
comment: This entry represents a protein of unknown function found in phage proteins. The domain contains approximately 77 residues and may contain a single transmembrane helix near the N-terminus. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_Gene47
comment: This entry represents the gene 47 protein found in Mycobacterium phage L5. This protein forms a small globular beta domain that is related to LSM superfamily proteins such as Hfq. AlphaFold modelling suggests this protein forms an unusual octameric arrangement. Based on similarity to LSM proteins these proteins may bind to RNA. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7243
comment: This family of phage proteins adopt a structure composed of a pair of jelly roll fold domains with one nested within the other. This fold is suggestive of a phage head structural protein. Structure predictions suggest that these proteins can form pentameric or hexameric arrangements mediated by the outer of the two domains. (from Pfam)

label: Ig_CycH
name_orig: Cytochrome c-type biogenesis protein H Ig-like domain
hmm_name: c-type cytochrome biogenesis protein CcmI/CycH Ig-like domain
comment: This entry represents the immunoglobulin-like domain found in cytochrome c-type biogenesis protein CycH from bacteria. CycH is involved in the attachment of heme to cytochrome c apoproteins (PMID: 7665469). This entry also represents the Ig-like domain of the uncharacterised protein AQ_1241 from Aquifex aeolicus. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_zn_bind
comment: This small domain is found in a variety of uncharacterised enterobacterial phage proteins. Structure prediction shows that it is likely zinc binding, with an N-terminal conserved CXXC motif and more central CXXXXC motif providing the zing binding residues. The domain adopts a four stranded beta meander fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7248
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins that have a single transmembrane helix followed by a conserved C-terminal sequence. The family includes proteins from phage T4 and T6. (from Pfam)

label: Terminase_6
comment: The small subunit of terminase, a DNA packaging enzyme of bacteriophages, plays a role in binding and cutting the phage DNA during packaging into the capsid. This entry represents diverse small subunits from a wide range of actinobacteriophages and some Bacillota phages. The domain is often found at the N-terminus of proteins, followed by a disordered or low complexity region at the C-terminus. In some larger proteins, additional C-terminal domains may also be present. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7293
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein of approximately 54 amino acids found in T5-like bacteriophages that infect Escherichia coli and Salmonella. Homologs have been identified in several T5-like phages including bacteriophage T5, Salmonella phage vB_SenS_SB13, and Escherichia phage vB_EcoS-26175V. Structure prediction suggests that this protein forms a strand swapped homodimeric arrangement. The dimeric structure forms two four stranded sheets that are connected by two alpha helices. The C-terminal of each protein is donated to the sheet made by the other monomer. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7299
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7302
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins that have a small N-terminal domain composed of three beta strands and an alpha helix. (from Pfam)

label: XM1_gp53_minor_capsid
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins related to Myoviridae Phage XM1 gp53 minor capsid protein. These proteins form a trimeric arrangement which stabilises the phage capsid (PMID: 37632015). They adopt a structure which is known as a beta-tulip fold. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_holin_10
comment: This family includes Pam3 gp28 which is annotated as a phage holin. These proteins contain two predicted transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7320
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in T4-like bacteriophages. It is found between the cd and pseT genes in the T4 phage genome. The function of this protein is unknown. Structure prediction suggests these proteins have a compact fold composed of five beta strands and an alpha helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7326
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7335
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7341
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of an uncharacterised family of phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: T4_Cef
comment: This entry represents proteins that are related to the phage T4 cef protein. This protein adopts a compact globular domain composed of 5 beta strands and one alpha helix. The beta strands adopt the order 1-5-4-3-2 with the alpha helix found between strands 1 and 2. This family shows structural similarity to Pfam:PF24005. (from Pfam)

label: T4_MRH
comment: This family includes the mrh gene Swiss:P16007 and the uncharacterised gene y01F from bacteriophage T4. Mrh plays a role in transcriptional regulation of late T4 genes. It modulates the phosphorylation status of host heat shock sigma factor rpoH which is an initiation factor that promotes the attachment of host RNA polymerase to specific initiation sites. Structure prediction suggests that this protein may oligomerise with the C-terminus contacting the next subunit in a cyclic homo-oligomer. Structure prediction weakly suggests Mrh forms a hexamer. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_zn_bind_3
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. According to structure predictions this domain contains two zinc binding clusters. This domain contains a highly conserved sequence motif FDXHR where X can be any amino acid. (from Pfam)

label: T7_gp14
product_name: virion core protein, T7 gp14 family
name_orig: T7 virus internal virion protein gp14 family
hmm_name: virion core protein, T7 gp14 family
comment: The T7 phage internal virion protein gp14 family is involved in the assembly of the cylindrical core on the inner surface of the viral capsid. This core, composed of stacked rings of gp14, gp15, and gp16 proteins, plays a crucial role in the ejection of viral DNA into the host cell. Upon binding to the host cell surface, the internal core disassembles, and gp14, along with gp15 and gp16, is ejected into the infected cell. The family may also form a simple channel spanning the outer membrane. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-sol_PIC_HAP1_IgA0_2nd
comment: This entry represents the second solenoid-repeat region found in some serine peptidase autotransporters from bacteria, including IgA0, HAP1, Pic, SepA and EspC. These proteins have been associated to virulent strains [1,2]. Pic and other bacterial autotransporters confer serum resistance but do not degrade immunoglobulin [1,3], as in the case of IgA0 (PMID: 4199558). This region counts with insertions between beta-solenoid repeats which have been suggested to be involved in forming a unique structure for recognition and binding of protein substrate (PMID: 19393662). (from Pfam)

label: Cds6_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of Cds6 from H. pylori, a cell shape-determining protein that plays key roles in alteration of cross-linking or by trimming of peptidoglycan muropeptides. It is also involved in deglycosylation of the flagellar protein FlaA. This domain adopts NTF2-like topology (PMID: 26306031). This domain contains a putative binding pocket for pseudaminic acid suggesting this domain may function as pseudaminase (PMID: 26306031). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7396
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in several bacteriophages that infect bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Enterobacter, Klebsiella and Shigella. The protein is short, around 44-51 amino acids in length. It is predicted to contain a single transmembrane helix. The function of this protein is currently unknown. One representative of this family is the Swiss:P18922 protein from bacteriophage T4. (from Pfam)

label: K1-lyase_Rider
product_name: K1 capsule-specific polysaccharide lyase, Rider domain
name_orig: K1 capsule-specific polysaccharide lyase, Rider domain
hmm_name: K1 capsule-specific polysaccharide lyase, Rider domain
comment: This entry represents the so-called Rider domain of K1 capsule-specific polysaccharide lyase and related proteins. K1-lyase functions as a receptor binding protein (RBP) and mediates the attachment to the host capsular exopolysaccharides (PMID: 35130876). This enzyme possesses a lyase activity that specifically degrades the K1-type polysaccharides of Klebsiella pneumoniae capsule (PMID: 35130876). The Rider domain folds into a beta-barrel, participates in polysaccharide binding to both carbohydrate-binding sites of the enzyme and makes an important contribution to the structural stability of the trimeric K1-lyase (PMID: 35130876). (from Pfam)

label: NTE_Ploop
product_name: Neuropathy Target Esterase family P-loop like domain
name_orig: Neuropathy Target Esterase family P-loop like domain
hmm_name: Neuropathy Target Esterase family P-loop like domain
comment: This domain is fond in a variety of Neuropathy Target Esterase family proteins. This domain appears to be structurally realted to P-loop ATPases, but it appears to not contain the typical APT-binding motifs. The NTE family comprises intracellular phospholipases B that catalyze the double deacylation of phosphatidylcholine (PC) to glycerophosphocholine (GroPCho). These enzymes play a crucial role in membrane lipid homeostasis and are responsible for the rapid turnover of PC in response to various stimuli such as inositol, elevated temperatures, or choline presence. Additionally, some members of the family, like the neuropathy target esterase (NTE), are involved in the signaling mechanisms between neurons and glia, regulating glia wrapping during brain development and ensuring cell survival. The family also includes lysophospholipases that preferentially deacylate unsaturated lysophosphatidylcholine, generating glycerophosphocholine and other lysophospholipids. (from Pfam)

label: Mycobacteriophage_TM
comment: This entry represents a family of proteins of unknown function found in mycobacteriophage genomes. The family includes short proteins between 44-60 amino acids in length that contain a single predicted transmembrane helix. The presence of these proteins in numerous mycobacteriophage genomes suggests they may play a role in phage biology, but their specific function has yet to be determined experimentally. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7438
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterized proteins found in bacteriophages. The function of this protein family is currently unknown. The family appears to be conserved across various phage species that infect Escherichia coli and related bacteria. The family includes members from Phage T2, T4 and T6. Members of this family are typically short proteins of around 60-67 amino acids in length. Bacteriophage T4 contains four proteins that belong to this family. The structure of these proteins is predicted to be composed of two alpha helices that pack together. Structure prediction suggests these proteins may homodimerise (iPTM=0.83). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7449
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in pseudomonas phage. The protein contains a compact domain composed of two alpha helices followed by four beta strands that form a beta sheet. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7455
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised actinobacterial zinc binding domains. The proteins contain a characteristic CXHH motif. Only the second of those two histidines acts as the zinc ligand according to structure prediction (ipTM = 0.94). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7459
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein domain found in a mycobacterial phage proteins. These domains form a zinc binding cluster where 8 cysteine and histidine residues bind two zinc ions according to structure prediction (iPTM=0.87). (from Pfam)

label: OLD-like_TOPRIM_1
comment: This entry represents a Toprim domain predicted to act as a nuclease like those seen in the OLD systems (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: HTH_upst_double_PIN
comment: This is an HTH domain found upstream to the double PIN in the permuted GreA/B-C conflict system (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: wHTH-Calcineurin_assc
comment: This entry represents a wHTH domain found at the C-terminal of proteins containing Calcineurin-CE (covered by Pfam:PF00149), in antiviral immunity systems containing an ORC/CDC6 like AAA+ ATPase (Pfam:PF24389) (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: Ig_J_second
product_name: phage tail tip protein J-related protein
name_orig: Tip attachment protein J second Ig-like domain
hmm_name: Tip attachment protein J second Ig-like domain
comment: This is the second Ig-like domain found in Tip attachment protein J from Escherichia phage lambda. J is a tail fibre protein that attaches the virion to the host receptor LamB, inducing viral DNA ejection [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7587
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins predominantly from fungi. It has a detectable similarity to ADP ribosyltransferase domains and it is predicted to adopt a similar structure. (from Pfam)

label: SH3_Rv0428c
name_orig: Probable histone acetyltransferase Rv0428c SH3 domain
hmm_name: Probable histone acetyltransferase Rv0428c SH3 domain
comment: This entry represents the SH3 domain found at the N-terminal of Rv0428c, a probable histone acetyltransferase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It may be involved in survival under stress conditions (PMID: 35175508). (from Pfam)

label: Int_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of phage integrases, including the member from Escherichia phage P2. This protein is necessary for integration of the phage into the host genome by site-specific recombination (PMID: 26453836). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7639
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed of a three helical bundle. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_OMP
product_name: Cyanophage outer membrane protein like beta barrel domain
name_orig: Cyanophage outer membrane protein like beta barrel domain
hmm_name: Cyanophage outer membrane protein like beta barrel domain
comment: This entry represents a family of small uncharacterised membrane bound beta barrel-like proteins found in cyanophage. The putative membrane beta barrel is incomplete composed of only 6 beta strands. However, the proteins form a confident homodimer (ipTM=0.78) composed of a flattened 12 stranded beta barrel. The proteins likely contain an N-terminal signal peptide that is cleaved during membrane insertion. (from Pfam)

label: NpmA
comment: This entry represents the 16S rRNA (adenine(1408)-N(1))-methyltransferase [1-4]. (from Pfam)

label: TreTu_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of TreTu from Salmonella enterica and related proteins. TreTu is a part of the TreTu/TriTu toxin/antitoxin system and is involved in the ADP-ribosylation of the EF-Tu GTP-bound form. The C-terminal domain of TreTu adopts a typical ADP-ribosyltransferase fold. The TreTu activity is neutralised by TriTu immunity protein which acts like a lid that closes the TreTu catalytic site and traps the NAD+ (PMID: 36484105). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7660
comment: This family represents a set of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Structure prediction shows them to be composed of three alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: PITM1-3
comment: This is a presumed beta-sandwich domain found towards the C-terminal of Membrane-associated phosphatidylinositol transfer proteins 1-3 (PITM1-3) and RDGB from Drosophila. These are class II phosphatidylinositol transfer proteins (PITPs) which can transfer phosphatidylinositol (PI) between membranes (PMID: 34098114). RDGB can also transfer phosphatidic acid (PA) between membranes (PMID: 22822086). PTIM1/2 bind PI, phosphatidylcholine (PC) and (PA) with the binding affinity order of PI > PA > PC (PMID: 22822086). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7663
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is frequently found in combination with Pfam:PF21818. It is predicted to adopt a complex alpha/beta structure composed of a curved beta-sheet that encloses an alpha-helix and a number of helices packed on its exterior. (from Pfam)

label: WapI
comment: The WapI family comprises immunity proteins that are part of a toxin-immunity protein module functioning as a cellular contact-dependent growth inhibition (CDI) system. These proteins neutralize the tRNase activity of their cognate toxin WapA upon expression in E.coli. Notably, they do not inhibit WapA from other strains of Bacillus subtilis. The WapA C-terminus cannot be expressed independently in E.coli but can be cloned when its cognate immunity protein gene is present. The structure of these proteins resembles the fold of the Whirly ssDNA binding proteins. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_73
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. These proteins structurally resemble a HTH domain. They are often found genomically associated with likely restriction modification systems. Structure prediction suggests that these domains homodimerise and bind to the major groove of double-stranded DNA. (from Pfam)

label: Imm33-like
comment: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins that are structurally related to the Imm33 family of putative immunity proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7676
comment: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins that based on structural similarities are likely to bind to heme or a related derivative molecule. Structural modelling suggests these proteins are likely to form homodimers and that this complex can bind to two heme-like molecules. Each heme binding site is composed of parts of both subunits. (from Pfam)

label: Acb2_Tad1_hairpin
comment: This domain, previously known as DUF7681, is found in phage proteins including Anti-CBASS protein 2 (Acb2) and Thoeris anti-defense 1 (Tad1). It folds into an alpha-helical hairpin that is found either standalone (in Acb2) or in combination with a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet domain (in Tad1) [1,2,3]. Prokaryotic anti-phage immune systems use TIR and cGAS-like enzymes to produce 1-3-glycocyclic ADP-ribose; and cyclic dinucleotide and trinucleotide signalling molecules, respectively, which limit phage replication. The Thoeris anti-defence proteins Tad1 and Tad2 are both pronged inhibitors and antagonise immunity alongside Anti-CBASS protein 2. These proteins achieve anti-cyclic-oligonucleotide-based anti-phage signalling system (anti-CBASS) activity by sequestering a considerable amount of cyclic nucleotides. Each of these proteins is using distinct binding pockets. The residues conserved in Tad1 and Acb2 are located near these binding sites [3,4]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7683
comment: This family represents uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria. These proteins are related to members of Pfam:PF03513 which are described as immunity proteins. They are predicted to adopt similar structure composed of a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with alpha-helices packed on one side of it. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7684
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins found in bacteria. They are predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure that has some similarity to MurD C-terminal domain. (from Pfam)

label: AlkZ-rel
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised bacterial proteins that have a detectable similarity to AlkZ-like proteins Pfam:PF06224. AlkZ adopts a unique fold in which three tandem winged helix-turn-helix (HTH) motifs scaffold a positively charged concave surface shaped for binding to duplex DNA (PMID: 28396405). In contrast, the members of this family contain two instead of three tandem HTH motifs. They still probably retain the basic interface to bind DNA however it is unclear whether these proteins possess enzymatic activity. (from Pfam)

label: MavL
comment: This entry represents the Legionella macrodomain effector MavL, an ADP-ribosyl hydrolase that reverses the arginine ADP-ribosylation, to minimize potential detrimental effects caused by the modified ubiquitin. Legionella pneumophila mediates atypical ubiquitination of host targets using the SidE effector family (PMID: 38503748). (from Pfam)

label: FNIII-A_GpJ
product_name: TipJ family phage tail tip protein
comment: This domain is found towards the N-terminal end of Tip attachment protein J from the bacteriophage lambda (GpJ) and similar sequences from tailed bacteriophages and bacterial prophages (PMID: 38096144). GpJ is involved in the induction of viral DNA ejection. It attaches the virion to the host receptor. This domain shows an Ig-like structure [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: CC_BshC
product_name: Bacillithiol biosynthesis BshC, C-terminal coiled-coil domain
name_orig: Bacillithiol biosynthesis BshC, C-terminal coiled-coil domain
hmm_name: Bacillithiol biosynthesis BshC, C-terminal coiled-coil domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal coiled-coil domain of the bacillithiol biosynthesis protein BshC from Bacillus subtilis, which has been described as a cysteine-adding enzyme. This domain, found associated with Pfam:PF10079, shows a four-helix bundle and is responsible for the dimerisation of the protein [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: AMP-dom_DIP2-like
comment: This domain is found in Disco-interacting protein 2 from Drosophila melanogaster (DIP2) and similar sequences from eukaryotes and bacteria. DIP2 is required for precise axonal bifurcation in mushroom body neurons and may play a role in fatty acid metabolism. This protein harbours one DNA methyltransferase 1-associated protein 1-binding (DMAP1- binding) domain (Pfam:PF06464) and two AMP-dependent synthase (AMP) domains (this entry) (PMID: 27908785). This domain is often found associated to Pfam:PF00501 and shows an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: MG280
comment: This entry includes uncharacterised proteins from Mycoplasma, such as MG280 from Mycoplasma vaginalis. These proteins are typically 260 aa long, with a hydrophobic predicted transmembrane alpha-helix toward each end. (from Pfam)

label: Xre-MbcA-ParS_M
comment: This entry represents a small domain found in the middle region of a group of bacterial sequences related to the antitoxin components of a type II toxin-antitoxin (TA) system Xre/MbcA/ParS. This domain may consist of four beta-sheets and two short alpha-helices, which is followed by a toxin-binding domain (Pfam:PF09722). (from Pfam)

label: OB_YrrC
name_orig: ATP-dependent DNA helicase YrrC, OB-fold domain
hmm_name: YrrC family ATP-dependent DNA helicase, N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents a domain which is found N-terminal in ATP-dependent DNA helicase YrrC and related proteins. This domain is predicted to adopt a beta-barrel with an OB-fold topology. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_RNase_II
comment: This entry represents a double HTH domain found in a set of largely bacterial ribonuclease II domain proteins (PMID: 22133431). (from Pfam)

label: WHD_3rd_Lhr
hmm_name: Lhr family ATP-dependent helicase winged helix 3 domain
comment: This is a winged-helix (WH) domain found in Large helicase -related protein from Escherichia coli (Lhr), DEAD/DEAH box helicase from Mycolicibacterium smegmatis (Swiss:A0QT91) and similar bacterial sequences. These proteins have a C-terminal domain composed of a series of five WH modules (named WH2 to WH6) and a beta-barrel module. This entry represents WH3. It shows three alpha-helices followed by two loops or 'wings' and two beta-strands forming an antiparallel beta-sheet (PMID: 33744958). (from Pfam)

label: WHD_2nd_Lhr
comment: This is a winged-helix (WH) domain found in Large helicase -related protein from Escherichia coli (Lhr), DEAD/DEAH box helicase from Mycolicibacterium smegmatis (Swiss:A0QT91) and similar bacterial sequences. These proteins have a C-terminal domain composed of a series of five WH modules (named WH2 to WH6) and a beta-barrel module. This entry represents WH2. It shows three alpha-helices followed by two loops or 'wings' and two beta-strands forming an antiparallel beta-sheet (PMID: 33744958). (from Pfam)

label: WDR90_beta-prop_4th
comment: This entry represents the fourth beta-propeller found in WD repeat-containing protein 90 from mouse and human, and the orthologue POC16 from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. WDR90 proteins constitute an evolutionary conserved central core microtubule triplet component that is essential for maintaining the inner centriolar scaffold components in centrioles (PMID: 32946374). POC16 is important for flagellum assembly as two poc16 mutants display shorter flagella and cannot swim (PMID: 28781053). (from Pfam)

label: Lsr2_DNA-bd
comment: Lsr2 is a small, basic DNA-bridging protein present in Mycobacterium and related actinomycetes. It is a functional homologue of the H-NS-like proteins (PMID: 20133735). H-NS proteins play a role in nucleoid organisation and also function as a pleiotropic regulator of gene expression [1,2]. This entry represents the DNA-binding domain found at the C-terminal, which binds AT-rich regions of chromosomal DNA and physically protects DNA from damage by reactive oxygen intermediates [1,2]. This domain is also found in protein Ku from Mycobacterium phage Omega. (from Pfam)
