label: Beta-prop_WDR90_POC16_2nd
comment: This entry represents the second WD40 beta-propeller found in WD repeat-containing protein 90, identified in animals, and the homologue protein POC16 found in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. WDR90 is proposed to be localised in the centriole and required for ciliogenesis (PMID: 28781053). The similarities between WDR90 and the flagellar inner B-microtubule protein FAP52/WDR16 lead to the proposal that the WD40 domains of WDR90 might be located within the B-microtubule of the centriole triplet (PMID: 32946374). (from Pfam)

label: MSMEG_3727_PQQ-assoc
comment: Members of this entry are restricted to members of the Actinobacteria that synthesise PQQ. These are small proteins 155 amino acids long on average, found regularly next to a much larger protein, a PQQ-dependent oxidoreductase, and might be a companion subunit or an accessory protein such as chaperone involved in cofactor insertion. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6688_C
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 360 and 412 amino acids in length. This entry corresponds to the alpha-helical C-terminal domain. (from Pfam)

label: ParB_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal dimerisation domain found in ParB proteins. The ParB family proteins are key players in bacterial chromosome partitioning, a critical process for cell division and genetic material distribution. Members of the ParB family are involved in recognizing and binding to specific DNA sequences at the origin of replication. They localise to the cell poles after DNA replication is complete, ensuring proper segregation of chromosomes into daughter cells during cell division. These proteins may interact with other partitioning proteins and DNA sites to facilitate the orderly distribution of chromosomes. (from Pfam)

label: YqhI
comment: This protein family includes Protein YqhI from Escherichia coli (PMID: 29645342) and similar bacterial short sequences. YqhI is a 47-residues long protein encoded by a small open reading frame (smORF). (from Pfam)

label: GBD_T9SS_assoc
comment: This entry represents a Galactose binding domain-like domain that is found in a variety of bacterial cell surface proteins that usually have a C-terminal type 9 secretion signal domain. The domain contains four conserved cysteines. AlphaFold models suggest that the first and third form one disulphide bond and the second and fourth form a second disulphide bond. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-barrel_GLAA-B_I
comment: This entry represents the first beta-barrel domain found towards the N-terminal in Alpha-1,3-galactosidase A-B (GLAA-B)from bacteria. This proteins share a domain architecture consisting of a core beta-helix surrounded by two small beta-barrel domains (domains I and II), which are involved in protein dimerization (PMID: 18227066). GLAA-B are alpha-galactosidases grouped in the GH110 subfamily by its narrow subtract specificity. This proteins remove branched alpha-1,3-linked galactose residues present in blood group B antigens (PMID: 33127644). (from Pfam)

label: Beta-barrel_GLAA-B_II
comment: This entry represents the second beta-barrel domain found in Alpha-1,3-galactosidase A-B (GLAA-B)from bacteria. This proteins share a domain architecture consisting of a core beta-helix surrounded by two small beta-barrel domains (domains I and II), which are involved in protein dimerization. The alpha-helix of domain II folds over and along the wall of the active site of the adjacent monomer, with several residues protruding into the cleft that contains the active site pocket (PMID: 18227066). Proteins GLAA-B are alpha-galactosidases grouped in the GH110 subfamily by its narrow subtract specificity. This remove branched alpha-1,3-linked galactose residues present in blood group B antigens (PMID: 33127644). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7167
comment: Members of this family in bacteria are found in prophage regions.

label: Phage_g100
comment: This entry includes Yersinia phage phiR1-RT g100 protein Swiss:I7LH63 which shows a partial beta barrel topology according to AlphaFold prediction. The function of members of this family is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_holin_2
comment: This entry represents a family of putative holin proteins found in various phages infecting actinobacterial hosts, particularly Gordonia, Mycobacterium, Arthrobacter, and Microbacterium. Holins are small membrane proteins involved in the timing of host cell lysis during bacteriophage infection. Members of this family typically range from 94 to 151 amino acids in length and contain 3 to 4 predicted transmembrane helices. While some members have an N-terminal signal peptide or lipoprotein signal, most do not. It is unclear where the annotation for these proteins as holins arose. However it appears plausible based on their sequence features. This entry shows similarity to Pfam:PF19447 a bacterial family of unknown function. (from Pfam)

label: CD1375-like
comment: This entry represents a short uncharacterized domain of about 50 residues. It is found in phage proteins from a variety of phages infecting Bacilli or Clostridia bacteria. Structural predictions suggest it adopts an alpha helical fold. Its function is currently unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7177
comment: The domain is around 80 amino acids in length. It occurs in phage that infect a variety of bacteria including Escherichia, Salmonella, Shigella, Klebsiella, Vibrio, Pantoea, Pectobacterium, Yersinia and Serratia. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_holin_9
comment: This entry represents a family of bacteriophage holin proteins. Holins are small membrane proteins that control the timing of host cell lysis during the phage lytic cycle. Holins typically have 2-4 transmembrane helices. The exact mechanism of how holins trigger cell lysis is not fully understood. The holin family is found in phages that infect Actinobacteria, primarily Mycobacteria and Gordonia species. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7192
comment: This entry represents a bacterial domain of unknown function. The domain is around 270 to 300 amino acids in length. It is found in a variety of bacterial phyla including Actinobacteria, Bacteroidota, Pseudomonadota and Verrucomicrobiota. The domain is also found in some bacterial phages. The function of this domain is unknown. The structure of this domain shows similarity to VWFA domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7193
comment: This entry represents a family of viral proteins that are found in various bacteriophages infecting Gram-negative bacteria, such as Pseudomonas, Vibrio, Erwinia, Ralstonia, and Klebsiella. The family members are typically 800-1200 residues in length. Many are annotated as putative virion structural proteins, suggesting they may play a role in phage particle structure or assembly. However, the precise function of this family remains unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7194
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein family found in viruses from the order Caudoviricetes. The family contains proteins between 199 and 219 amino acids in length. The function of this family is currently unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7195
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterized bacteriophage proteins, typically around 70-80 amino acids in length. They are found in phages infecting Escherichia, Pseudomonas, Salmonella, Vibrio, and other bacterial hosts. (from Pfam)

label: Cache_WalK
product_name: WalK sensor protein kinase Chache domain
name_orig: WalK sensor protein kinase Chache domain
hmm_name: WalK sensor protein kinase Chache domain
comment: This entry represents the Cache domain found in the sensor protein kinase WalK (or YycG) from bacteria. The WalK protein, alongside its response regulator WalR, is part of a two-component signal transduction system involved in diverse cellular processes, including cell wall metabolism, virulence regulation, biofilm production, among many other cellular processes [1, 2]. This domain is extracellular and is involved in WalK dimerization necessary for protein function (PMID: 27389096). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7222
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in various cyanophages, bacteriophages and bacteria species. The domain is approximately 100-160 amino acids in length. Structure prediction shows this domain is alpha helical. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7239
comment: This entry reprepsents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in mycobacterial phage. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7241
comment: This entry represents a family of small phage proteins found in a variety of mycobacteriophage genomes. The family members are typically around 70-75 amino acids in length. The function of these proteins is currently unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7244
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various bacteriophages that infect bacteria in the family Enterobacteriaceae, including phages of Escherichia, Shigella and Citrobacter. The protein is approximately 55-60 amino acids in length. An AlphaFold model shows this domain adopts a small beta barrel structure. This domain is possibly related to the KOW motif. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_zn_bind_2
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins that likely binds to zinc. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7246
comment: This entry describes a domain of unknown function found in phage proteins. The proteins containing this domain average 90 to 100 amino acids in length and is found in a variety of phage proteins, particularly those from Streptomyces and Mycobacterium phages. The domain usually occurs near the middle or C-terminus of proteins. The domain forms a small beta barrel. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7295
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various bacteriophages that infect Salmonella, Escherichia, Shigella, Pantoea and Serratia species. This family includes a member in bacteriophage T5. The function of this protein is currently unknown. Structure prediction does not predict a globular compact fold for this protein. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TTP_15
comment: This entry shows structural similarity to the Afp1 tail tube protein from the AFP antifeeding prophage of Serratia. This suggests that this family is also likely to form the inner tail tube. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7324
comment: This entry represents a small putative zinc binding motif found in a small number of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7339
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in bacteriophage proteins, particularly those infecting Lactococcus species. The domain is approximately 115 amino acids in length. It is found in a small number of bacterial proteins as well. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7349
comment: This family of uncharacterized proteins is found in various phages that infect bacterial hosts such as Bacillus, Staphylococcus, Enterococcus, Listeria, Lactobacillus, and Brochothrix species. The proteins in the family are typically 75 to 100 amino acids in length. The protein contains a small N-terminal domain represented by this entry followed by a C-terminal disordered region. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7365
hmm_name: DUF7365 family protein putative coiled-coil domain
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins that have a predicted N-terminal transmembrane helix and a coiled-coil region. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins may adopt a trimeric coiled-coil structure. Many of these proteins are annotated as holins, however the origin of that annotation is unclear. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7367
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. These proteins range in length from 94 to 110 amino acids and adopt a small domain composed of four alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7368
comment: ThiS entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7369
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests that this protein forms a small domain that likely forms a stable dimeric complex. In this predicted complex there is a C-terminal alpha helix that binds to the opposite oligomer in a helix swapped arrangement. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7376
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests these protein may form a homodimer. The dimer contains a large circular channel that is positively charged suggesting a possible DNA-binding function. (from Pfam)

label: Cas8b_N
product_name: Type I-B CRISPR Cas8b N-terminal domain
name_orig: Type I-B CRISPR Cas8b N-terminal domain
hmm_name: Type I-B CRISPR Cas8b N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of Type I-B CRISPR Synechocystis Cas8b and related proteins. Type I CRISPR-Cas systems employ multi-subunit effector Cascade and helicase-nuclease Cas3 to target and degrade foreign nucleic acids, representing the most abundant RNA-guided adaptive immune systems in prokaryotes. Cas8b subunit displays very low sequence similarity with the large subunits of any other known type I CRISPR systems. Cas8b N-terminal domain is involved in PAM recognition (PMID: 38750051). (from Pfam)

label: YphA
comment: This entry represents a family of proteins related to B. subtilis YphA protein. These proteins are predicted as integral membrane proteins and are structurally related to Pfam:PF07758. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7395
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins, that includes the L1 protein from Lactococcus phage c2 Swiss:Q38296. Structure prediction indicates this small protein adopts a compact domain composed of a three stranded sheet with a single alpha helix. (from Pfam)

label: TMP_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal conserved region of the Tape measure protein PB2 and related proteins found mainly in T5-like phages. PB2 functions as a tape measure protein that serves as a base for tail tube protein polymerization and acts as a template for tail length determination [1,2]. This protein fills the tail tube with its long coiled-coil domain and is expelled during the conformation changes that follow T5 binding to host FhuA receptor (PMID: 36961893). The tape measure protein C-terminal region is composed of two alpha-helices that are organized in an extended L-shape. The C-terminal region of the TMP was found within the tail tip suggesting that the tail tip complex returns to its original state after DNA ejection (PMID: 38081816). (from Pfam)

label: Fn3-II_PB4
product_name: Straight fiber protein PB4 second Fn3-like domain
name_orig: Straight fiber protein PB4 second Fn3-like domain
hmm_name: Straight fiber protein PB4 second Fn3-like domain
comment: This entry represents the second Fn3-like domain of the Straight fiber protein PB4 found in T5-like phages. PB4 along with PB3, forms the central straight fiber, bearing the receptor binding protein PB5 at its C terminus (PMID: 36961893). Upon PB5 binding to the host receptor FhuA, the central fiber reorganises and undergoes structural rearrangements that lead to its bending, bringing PB3 close to the host membrane for anchoring (PMID: 36961893). The PB4-PB3 interactions are ensured by the distal loops of the second of the three Fn3-like domains of PB4. These interactions are disrupted upon binding to the host receptor and the string of the three PB4 Fn3-like domains undergoes drastic conformational changes. (from Pfam)

label: Fn3-III_PB4
product_name: Straight fiber protein PB4 third Fn3-like domain
name_orig: Straight fiber protein PB4 third Fn3-like domain
hmm_name: Straight fiber protein PB4 third Fn3-like domain
comment: This entry represents the third Fn3-like domain of the Straight fiber protein PB4 found in T5-like phages. PB4 along with PB3, forms the central straight fiber, bearing the receptor binding protein PB5 at its C terminus (PMID: 36961893). Upon PB5 binding to the host receptor FhuA, the central fiber reorganises and undergoes structural rearrangements that lead to its bending, bringing PB3 close to the host membrane for anchoring (PMID: 36961893). The PB4-PB3 interactions are ensured by the proximal loops of the first and the distal loops of the second of the three PB4 Fn3-like domains. These interactions are disrupted upon binding to the host receptor and the string of the three PB4 Fn3-like domains undergoes drastic conformational changes. (from Pfam)

label: MsddA-like
comment: This domain is found in bacterial deaminases. Some members of this family also contain RHS repeats. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7415
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage domains. This domain is found in one to two copies per proteins. It seems likely that the proteins with a single copy of the domain form homodimers. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7421
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised enterobacterial phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7424
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised lipoproteins. The family includes a range of both bacteria and phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7426
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised domain found in phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_ProQ_C_like
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage and bacterial proteins. Structurally the proteins include an N-terminal beta barrel domain that shows some structural similarity to the C-terminal domain of the ProQ RNA-binding domain. That domain has been described as being similar to the Tudor domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7440
comment: This entry represents a protein family of unknown function found in various bacterial phage proteins. The family typically consists of proteins around 140-160 amino acids in length. It is found in phages that infect bacteria such as Salmonella, Escherichia, Shigella, and Dickeya. The function of this family remains unclear. Some members of this family are annotated as uncharacterized or hypothetical proteins. AlphaFold predictions suggest the proteins in this family contain two distinct domains, with a central domain composed of a three stranded beta sheet and a C-terminal small 3-helix bundle domain. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TreK
product_name: Staphylococcus phage terminal repeat-encoded protein TreK
name_orig: Staphylococcus phage terminal repeat-encoded protein TreK
hmm_name: Staphylococcus phage terminal repeat-encoded protein TreK
comment: This entry represents a terminal repeat-encoded protein (TreK) found in Twort-like Staphylococcus phages. Twort-like viruses are members of the Myoviridae family and are characterized by large genomes (>125 kb) with a low G+C content (30-31%) and terminally redundant ends. These terminal repeats are several thousand base pairs long and may influence the host range. The TreK protein is encoded within these terminal repeat regions. Twort-like phages are known for their broad host range and strictly lytic life cycle, making them suitable candidates for phage therapy against Staphylococcus aureus infections. This domain is often found in various Staphylococcus phages, particularly those belonging to the Herelleviridae family. The protein is typically around 90-95 amino acids in length. While its exact function remains unknown, its conservation among Twort-like phages suggests it plays an important role in phage biology, possibly related to host range determination or genome packaging. Structure prediction shows these proteins form a globular domain that includes a 5 stranded highly curved beta sheet with a C-terminal helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7448
comment: This entry represents a conserved viral protein domain of unknown function (DUF4241). The domain is approximately 130-160 amino acids in length and is found in various bacteriophages and large DNA viruses. The alignment shows several conserved residues, including a highly conserved DCC motif. The protein contains a beta sandwich domain structural. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7452
comment: This entry represents a presumed domain found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria. This domain may adopt an all-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7453
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. According to structure predictions, these proteins may comprise novel repeats consisting of an arrangement of four beta-strands in which the second one is longer and curved. This arrangement is repeated eight times in SwissProt:A0A5B9QB27, which form a closed repeat. (from Pfam)

label: Ig_CFAP65
product_name: Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 65-like, Ig-like domain
name_orig: Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 65-like, Ig-like domain
hmm_name: Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 65-like, Ig-like domain
comment: This domain is found in human Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 65 (CFAP65) and similar animal sequences. CFAP65 plays a role in flagellar formation and sperm motility. This protein is predicted to have several Ig-like domains, one of which is represented by Pfam:PF22544. This entry represents an Ig-like domain located towards the C-terminal part of the sequence. (from Pfam)

label: Permuted_GreAB-C
comment: This is a circular permuted GreAB-C-domain in antiviral immunity systems featuring TPR-repeats, a GreA/B-C-terminal domain and a PIN domain, with a variable N-terminal domain often harbouring effector domains [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Parb-CE
comment: This entry represents a ParB-like domain predicted to act as a catalytic effector (CE) in multiple antiviral immunity systems and predicted to target nucleotides along Calcineurin-CE, HD-CE and PRTase-CE (PMID: 37889040). This domain shares structural similarity to the N-terminal of ParB which has NTP hydrolase catalytic activity. ParB plays a vital role in chromosome partitioning and nucleoid occlusion. These proteins are essential for ensuring proper chromosome segregation during cell division by binding to the DNA origin of replication and localising to both poles of the predivisional cell following DNA replication. (from Pfam)

label: nSTAND_NTPase7
comment: This entry represents a novel domain of the STAND-superfamily of AAA+ ATPases found in bacterial conflict systems (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7570
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. The proteins are composed of an N-terminal three helical bundle followed by an alpha helical region at the C-terminus. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7574
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: Nm-ACP
comment: This domain, previously known as DUF7606, is found in Neisseria Adhesin Complex Protein (ACP) and in a group of uncharacterised sequences from proteobacteria. It folds into an eight-stranded beta-barrel, stabilised by a disulphide bond between the first and last beta-strands (PMID: 28662181). Nm-ACP is structurally similar to members of the MliC/PliC protein family of lysozyme inhibitors. Despite it does not share any conserved MliC/PliC sequence motifs associated with lysozyme recognition, ACP is capable of inhibiting lysozyme. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_YunG-like
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. These proteins show structural similarity to the B. subtilis YunG protein and appear to conserve a putative catalytic triad of cys, his and asp. Structure predictions suggest that these proteins may form homodimers. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7673
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of proteins, which are typically between 100 and 122 amino acids in length. This protein is often found to be plasmid borne and in a few cases is associated with ParBc domains that are critical for plasmid segregation. This suggests that this domain may play a role in chromosome segregation or plasmid partitioning. Structural modelling suggests this domain will form a homodimeric complex. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7678
comment: This entry represents a conserved domain of unknown function (DUF7678) found in various bacterial species. The domain is approximately 75-100 amino acids in length and contains several highly conserved residues. The function of this domain remains to be determined. Structure prediction suggests this domain is composed of a 6 stranded beta sheet with an Alpha helix packed on one side. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7686
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is usually found next to Pfam:PF24734. It is predicted to adopt alpha/beta structure consisting of a four-stranded beta-sheet curved around an alpha-helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7691
comment: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share detectable similarity to proteins members of Pfam:PF08974 whose function is unknown. Their predicted structures resemble the structure of DNA mimic protein DMP12 but elaborated with additional alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7695
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains a pair of conserved cysteines and it is predicted to adopt a fold which is typical for zinc-ribbon domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7698
comment: This entry represents a domain from uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Firmicutes. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. It contains a number of conserved aromatic hydrophobic residues, some of which are predicted to be solvent-exposed. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7715
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised actinobacterial proteins that are related to Pfam:PF20115. (from Pfam)

label: CSD_RNase_II
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminus of a family of largely bacterial ribonuclease II proteins. It may have an RNA-binding activity. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7059
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. These proteins are probably distantly related to Aeronamide N-methyltransferases AerE. They share two similar domains that are predicted in the same arrangement. This domain is found N-terminal to the methyltransferase domain and has a weak sequence similarity to various HTH domains. (from Pfam)

label: LRR_LRWD1
product_name: Leucine-rich repeat and WD repeat-containing protein 1, LRR
name_orig: Leucine-rich repeat and WD repeat-containing protein 1, LRR
hmm_name: Leucine-rich repeat and WD repeat-containing protein 1, LRR
comment: This entry represents the Leucine-rich repeat domain found at the N-terminal of Leucine-rich repeat and WD repeat-containing protein 1 (LRWD1) from animals and related sequences. LRWD1 (also known as CENP-33 and ORCA) is required for for G1/S transition. It recruits and stabilizes the origin recognition complex (ORC) onto chromatin during G1 to establish pre-replication complex (preRC) and to heterochromatic sites in pre-replicated cells [1-3]. This proteins consist of a LRR domain at the N-terminal and a WD (beta-propeller) domain at the C-terminal. (from Pfam)

label: KOW7_SPT5
product_name: Transcription elongation factor SPT5, seventh KOW domain
name_orig: Transcription elongation factor SPT5, seventh KOW domain
hmm_name: Transcription elongation factor SPT5, seventh KOW domain
comment: This entry includes Transcription elongation factor SPT5, a component of the elongation factor DRB-sensitivity inducing factor (DSIF) that plays multiple roles during transcription [1-4]. SPT5 is a multidomain protein consisting of an N-terminal NusG domain (Pfam:PF03439), tandem of KOW domains and and a mobile C-terminal-repeat region. The KOW domains differ in number between yeast, which has five, and animals, which have seven. This entry represents the seventh KOW domain of Spt5 from animals, which is located at the very C-terminal of the sequences (PMID: 28892040). The KOW domains of these proteins play critical roles in recruitment of multiple other eukaryotic transcription elongation and RNA biogenesis factors and they are also involved in the binding of the eukaryotic Spt5 proteins to RNA polymerases. (from Pfam)

label: ACP_SdgA_C
name_orig: Highly reducing polyketide synthase sdgA, C-terminal ACP domain
hmm_name: Highly reducing polyketide synthase sdgA, C-terminal ACP domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal of Highly reducing polyketide synthase sdgA from Emericella nidulans and related proteins. SdgA is part of the gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of the polyenes aspernidgulenes (PMID: 30302871). This domain is predicted to adopt an all alpha-helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: RDM3_C
comment: This entry represents a beta-solenoid domain found at C-terminal region of Protein RNA-directed DNA methylation 3 (RDM3) from Arabidopsis thaliana and similar proteins from plants. RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) initiates and re-establishes silencing of transposable elements through de novo methylation of cytosines (PMID: 31274236). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7092
comment: This domain represents a small beta barrel domain that is found at the N-terminus of some bacterial peptidase M48 proteins. It has a PH-domain like structure. It likely acts as a chaperone for membrane protein complexes. May interact with Pfam:PF05987 members based on AlphaFold predictions. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_IFT140_1st
comment: IFT140 is one of the core components (together with WDR19/IFT144 and IFT122) of the IFT-A complex which is required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [1,2]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of beta-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins (PMID: 20889716). The beta-propeller domains of IFT140 contact the beta-propeller domains of IFT121 from the adjacent complex (PMID: 36462505). This entry represents the first beta-propeller of IFT140. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7103
comment: This is a family of unknown function. It is structurally similar to Frag1-like domain, composed of a six-alpha-helix bundle transmembrane region (PMID: 37704730). (from Pfam)

label: Methyltransf_36
comment: This entry represents a methyltransferase domain found in the homologues of AprA Methyltransferase 1. AprA is an S-adenosylmethionine and Fe3+-dependent dimethyltransferase that acts in the initiation steps of apratoxin A biosynthesis [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7134
comment: This domain is composed of 6 transmembrane alpha helices and is found at the N-terminus of a large family of bacterial signalling proteins. It is structurally related to the N-terminus of the DesK protein. That region is believed to be involved in sensing membrane fluidity.ED A0A1A9IX15.1/7-166; A0A1A9IX15.1/7-50; (from Pfam)

label: GBD_Hemicentin
comment: This entry represents a galactose-binding domain-like found in hemicentin and Willebrand factor A domain-containing proteins. The Hemicentin and von Willebrand factor A domain-containing protein family is involved in various cellular and developmental processes. Members of this family play a crucial role in the rearrangement of the podocyte cytoskeleton, influenced by transforming growth factor beta, which includes the modulation of F-actin fibers and changes in podocyte morphology. They are also implicated in the organisation of the basement membrane and may contribute to cleavage furrow maturation during cytokinesis in embryos. Additionally, they are involved in the structural integrity of adhesive and flexible epithelial cell junctions and may influence cardiac fibroblast migration during myocardial remodeling. (from Pfam)

label: YnhH-like
comment: This protein family includes Protein YnhH from Escherichia coli, a 64-residues long microprotein encoded by a small open reading frame (smORF)(PMID: 34662240). (from Pfam)

label: Rcc01698_C
comment: This small domain appears in baseplate proteins with a variety of large, multidomain architectures. The baseplate is located at the distal end (far from the phage head) of the phage tail. It is responsible for phage attachment and host specificity.

label: DUF7164
comment: This domain is found either standalone or in tandem in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It has a weak sequence similarity to Nucleotide-diphospho-sugar transferases, in particular to Glycolipid 2-alpha-mannosyltransferases (Pfam:PF01793) and is predicted to adopt similar structure. (from Pfam)

label: Gp41_Mu
comment: This entry includes the probable tail assembly protein gp41 from Bacteriophage Mu (Mup41 and FS-gp41) and Mu-like prophage FluMu protein gp41 from H. influenzae. Mup41 and FS-gp41 may act as a chaperone mediating the interaction between the tape measure protein (TMP) and the tail tube protein (TTP) thereby directing the polymerization of TTP to form a tail of the correct length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7169
comment: This domain family consists of a group of uncharacterized proteins, typically between 99 to 116 amino acids in length, found in bacteriophages that infect Microbacterium and Arthrobacter bacterial hosts. These proteins are encoded in the genomes of phages belonging to the Caudoviricetes class, primarily within the families Azeevirinae, Dismasvirus, Yangvirus, Manhattanvirus, Liebevirus, Zetavirus, and Armstrongvirus. An AlphaFold prediction shows these proteins are composed of two alpha helices. AlphaFold also predicts that these proteins likely form homodimers. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7170
comment: The DUF7170 domain family consists of several uncharacterized phage proteins of around 50 amino acids in length. The family is found in a variety of phages that infect bacterial hosts such as Escherichia, Salmonella, Klebsiella, Vibrio, Citrobacter, Shigella, Pseudomonas and Aeromonas. A few longer proteins of around 60-90 amino acids are also included. (from Pfam)

label: Baseplate_Tube_p140
comment: The Baseplate tube protein family is involved in the assembly of the simplified baseplate structure of bacteriophages. Members of this family, such as Baseplate tube protein p140, interact with other proteins including the p132 collar protein ring and components of the cone, namely DTP-pb9 and BHP-pb3, to form a crucial part of the phage's baseplate. This structure is essential for the phage to attach to and penetrate the host bacterial cell wall during infection. (from Pfam)

label: SH3_YKFC_2nd
comment: This entry represents the second of two N-terminal bacterial SH3 (SH3b2) domains found in bacterial dipeptidyl-peptidases VI such as Gamma-D-glutamyl-L-lysine dipeptidyl-peptidase (YKFC). YKFC consist of three domains, the N-terminal SH3b1 (Pfam: PF18348), SH3b2 and a C-terminal NlpC/P60 (Pfam: PF00877). The active site is located at the SH3b1-NlpC/P60 interface, whereas the SH3b2 domain is distal to this [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7176
comment: This family consists of short bacterial phage proteins, typically around 90 amino acids in length, that contain two transmembrane helices. The family is found in phages that infect Enterobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7178
comment: This entry describes a family of identified in phage metagenomic datasets. The family contains proteins from a variety of phages that infect actinobacteria, particularly Mycobacterium, Gordonia, and Streptomyces. The exact specificity and function of this metagenomic family is currently unknown. Some members are described as N-glycosylases but the source of that information is uncertain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7179
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in phage, predominantly those infecting bacteria in the Enterobacteriaceae family such as Escherichia, Salmonella, Klebsiella and Vibrio. The protein is typically around 80 to 100 amino acids in length. In some phage the protein contains a predicted central coiled-coil region. The function of this protein family is currently unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TAC_18
comment: This entry represents a putative phage tail assembly chaperone protein domain found primarily in viruses that infect bacteria. The domain is typically around 100 amino acids in length. Tail assembly chaperones are known to assist in forming and attaching phage tails. This entry is found in caudoviruses of several families including Myoviridae, Podoviridae and Siphoviridae, but is not universal in phages. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7202
comment: This entry describes a domain of unknown function (DUF). It is found in phage proteins, generally around 70 amino acids in length. The domain is found in a variety of phages infecting hosts such as Escherichia, Shigella, Yersinia, Erwinia, Providencia, and Pectobacterium. No functional information is known. An AlphaFold model shows this protein adopts a three stranded beta sheet structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7219
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function. The domain is found in bacteria, primarily in cyanobacteria and their phage. It is typically around 80-90 amino acids in length. AlphaFold prediction suggests this protein is composed of two longer paired alpha helices followed by a shorter third helix. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TAC_19
comment: This entry represents a family of phage tail chaperone proteins found in viruses and cyanobacteria. Based on a structure prediction of family members, they are similar to other phage tail chaperone proteins. The family contains proteins between 50-164 amino acids in length. Phage tail chaperone proteins play a role in the assembly of the phage tail apparatus. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7224
comment: This entry represents a metalloprotease-like domain found in ABC transporter permease from bacteria, predominantly Streptomyces spp. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Crass_capsid
comment: This entry represents the major capsid protein found in viruses from the Crassvirales order. The major capsid protein self-assembles to form an icosahedral capsid. In the bacteriophage crAss001, the capsid has a T=9 symmetry and is about 77 nm in diameter. The major capsid protein displays an HK97-like fold with an insertion domain that protrudes at the capsid surface. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7249
comment: This family represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in phage proteins, mostly from Caudovirales. The domain is around 70-120 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7255
comment: This entry represents uncharacterised bacterial proteins that were predicted to possess defence functions (PMID: 32855333). They contain highly conserved aspartate and histidine residues that may have functional role. (from Pfam)

label: SP10_terminator
comment: This entry represents a likely phage terminator protein which terminates the elongation of the phage tail tube. This protein shows structural similarity to the PAM3 terminator protein (PMID: 36656854) which forms a hexameric ring. This protein has a beta sandwich domain nested within the terminator like domain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7277
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain from a large family of uncharacterised phage proteins that typically contain three domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7296
comment: This entry represents a family of domains found in phages that infect a variety of bacterial hosts including Streptococcus, Streptomyces, Pseudomonas and Paenibacillus species. The Domain is typically around 110-130 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7300
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. These proteins contain a small compact globular domain composed of a four stranded meander followed by a C-terminal alpha helix. (from Pfam)

label: Pam3_Gp34
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of phage proteins related to Pam3 phage gp34 protein. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7340
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal zinc binding domain of an uncharacterised family of phage proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7354
comment: This domain of unknown function, which is found in a small group of bacterial proteins, shows a high structural similarity with the N-terminal domain of Magnetotaxis protein MtxA from Magnetospirillum gryphiswaldense (Swiss:A4TUL6). (from Pfam)

label: YOMG_N
comment: This entry represents the N-teminal domain of SPbeta prophage-derived uncharacterized protein YomG from Bacillus subtilis (strain 168). This domain adopts a beta-barrel fold and is usually found in association with a neighbour prophage endopeptidase tail domain (Pfam:PF06605). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7359
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in SPbeta prophage-derived uncharacterized protein (YomG) from Bacillus subtilis (strain 168). This domain may adopt a FN3-like fold and can be found in association with a prophage endopeptidase tail domain (Pfam:PF06605). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7362
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found at the N-terminal of CHAT domain-containing, such as SwissProt:A0A100JVW6, protein from Streptomyces scabiei. This domain may be found in association with TCAD7 (Pfam:PF19973) and CHAT (Pfam:PF12770) domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7363
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in CHAT domain-containing protein, such as SwissProt:A0A100JVW6, from Streptomyces scabiei. This domain may be found in association with TCAD7 (Pfam:PF19973) and CHAT (Pfam:PF12770) domains. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_BT_1020
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal region of BT_1020 from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, which covers part of its 5-bladed beta propeller domain. It is usually found associated with Pfam:PF22585. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7370
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Many of these proteins are annotated as gp11, but the origin of this annotation is unclear. Structure prediction shows this protein adopts an alpha helical fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7372
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction shows the proteins form a compact globular domain composed of a four stranded beta sheet, with a strand order of 4-1-2-3 with an alpha helix between strands 3 and 4. (from Pfam)

label: CdiI_ImmP
comment: CDI toxins are expressed by Gram-negative bacteria as part of a mechanism to inhibit the growth of neighbouring cells. This entry represents the inhibitor (CdiI, also called CdiI immunity protein) of the CdiA effector protein from Escherichia coli A0 34/86, and similar proteins. E.coli A0 CdiI adopts an alpha/beta structure consisting of a central antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on it PDB:5T86. (from Pfam)

label: Subterisin
comment: This entry represents the lasso peptide subterisin and related peptides from proteobacteria. Lasso peptides are a class of ribosomally biosynthesised and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) with common motif of a knot structure in the molecule. The amino group of N-terminal amino acid forms an isopeptide bond with beta- or gamma- carboxyl group of Asp or Glu located near the N-terminus, resulting in formation of a macrolactam ring. The macrolactam ring looks like a loop of a "lasso" with a tail of the C-terminal linear peptide that normally locates through the ring PDB:5XM4. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7417
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in various phage and bacterial proteins. The domain is approximately 60-80 amino acids in length. The domain is composed of four alpha helices that form a small bundle. The surface of the domain is negatively charged. (from Pfam)

label: Antiholin
comment: Antiholins (also known as RI) are bacteriophage proteins that inhibit lysis of host cells by interacting and inhibiting holin, the protein that forms micropores in the host bacterial cell membrane. Antiholin prevents holin forming homo-oligomers. Antiholin has an N-terminal signal anchor release (SAR) domain which not only directs itself to the periplasm, but also targets itself for degradation by the host serine peptidase DegP. These proteins share a C-terminal three helical bundle domain. This may form a homodimer according to structure predictions. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_H_T_join_2
comment: This entry represents a putative phage head to tail joining protein. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7446
comment: This entry represents a highly conserved domain found in various bacteriophages, particularly those infecting Salmonella and related bacteria. The domain is also present in some bacterial species, suggesting possible horizontal gene transfer. The function is unknown, but the high degree of conservation implies an important role in phage biology. A conserved motif DVT is present centrally in many family members. The aspartate and threonine form side chain hydrogen bonds that help stabilise the dimeric interaction. Structure prediction suggests these proteins form a confident homodimer (iPTM=0.83). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7447
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized family found in various bacteriophage proteins. It is predominantly found in phages infecting diverse bacterial species including Burkholderia, Bacillus, Streptomyces, Listeria, and Caulobacter. The proteins are typically around 100-150 amino acids in length. Many of the proteins containing this domain are annotated as uncharacterized or hypothetical proteins. The proteins form a compact domain composed of a four stranded antiparallel beta sheet. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7477
comment: This entry represents a domain consisting of a novel repeat fold which containing five repeats, each of them comprising three antiparallel beta-strands and a short alpha-helix, according to structure predictions (e.g SwissProt:S8CFV9). This domain is found in Casein kinase 1-like protein HD16 from rice, a protein involved in the regulation of flowering time through gibberellin (GA) signaling and independently of photoperiod (PMID: 20400938). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7478
comment: This entry represents a domain containing a novel repeat fold, according to structure predictions. It may comprise six repeats, each of them consisting of two antiparallel beta-strands and a short alpha-helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7483
comment: This entry includes uncharacterised bacterial sequences that may adopt a novel fold consisting on three repeat units, each of them are type of beta-sandwich with three beta-strands on one side and four or five on the other. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7484
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of phage proteins. These proteins consist of two domains. The first is composed of four alpha helices that are contributed by both the N and C-terminus of the protein. The second domain is a central beta domain. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins might form a large homo-oligomeric ring of 8-10 subunits, but the iPTM scores are marginal. (from Pfam)

label: Tle3
product_name: T6SS effector phospholipase Tle3 domain-containing protein
comment: This entry represents an alpha/beta domain found in the type VI secretion system (T6SS) Tle3 phospholipase effector from adherent-invasive Escherichia coli and related proteins. Tle3 has a phospholipase A1 activity and its toxicity is neutralised by the cognate immunity protein Tli3. Tli3 and Tle3 form a stable complex in which a loop of Tli3 inserts deeply in the Tle3 substrate-binding pocket and thus inhibiting its function (PMID: 36675258). This Tle3 domain folds into a globular alpha/beta structure consisting of a central beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on both sides. It contains the typical nucleophile-elbow motif and structurally resembles classical alpha/beta hydrolase fold but elaborated with a number of large loops. (from Pfam)

label: iHD-CE
comment: This entry represents an inactive HD-CE domain (iHD-CE) which acts as a sensor in the antiviral immunity systems and it is predominantly located within HSP90 systems. Specifically, it is associated with wHTH repeats located at the C-terminal (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: iHKD
comment: This entry represents an inactive HKD-REase domain typically fused to the ParB-CE domain and predicted to be involved in conflict (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: Pua-like
comment: Members of the PUA family play a crucial role in binding and recognising RNA and DNA with modified bases. They are often linked with Calcineurin-CE domains, indicating their function as sensors in prokaryotic antiviral immunity by recognising modified DNA in invasive DNA elements (PMID: 37889040). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7617
comment: This domain is found in multiple copies in a number of bacterial proteins mainly from Actinomycetales. It is closely related to domains represented by Pfam:PF01345 and Pfam:PF24346. Similarly to them, this domain contains a conserved N-terminal lysine and a C-terminal asparagine with central aspartate/glutamate residues suggesting that some members may contain an isopeptide bond. This domain is sometimes found in combination with Pfam:PF01345 or Pfam:PF24346. (from Pfam)

label: B-barrel_PelB_C
comment: This transmembrane beta-barrel domain is found at the C-terminal end of PelB from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and similar proteins from proteobacteria. PelB plays a key role in biofilm formation in this organism (PMID: 28972168). (from Pfam)

label: CBM_AftD

comment: This is the third carbohydrate binding module (CBM) found in Arabinofuranosyltransferase D from Mycolicibacterium smegmatis (AftD) and similar proteins from actinomycetes. AftD is made up of five distinct domains: a domain of mixed alpha/beta folds (Pfam:PF11847) three CBMs and one structural beta-sandwich domain [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Ig_SibA
comment: This immunoglobulin-like domain (Ig-like) is found in Integrin beta-like protein A from Dictyostelium discoideum (SibA) and similar sequences mainly found in lower eukaryotes. SibA is involved in cellular adhesion to substrate or phagocytic particles (PMID: 16699495) (from Pfam)

label: Phage_blade
comment: This entry represents a small family of short uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction of A0A1J0MI44 suggests the protein adopts a four stranded sheet that can form homo-oligomers, with a homohexamer forming a beta propeller structure (iPTM=0.93). The function of these protein is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: TriTu
comment: This entry represents the Immunity protein TriTu from Salmonella enterica and related proteins. TriTu is a part of the TreTu/TriTu toxin/antitoxin system. TriTu immunity protein neutralises TreTu activity by acting like a lid that closes the TreTu catalytic site and traps the NAD+ (PMID: 36484105). TriTu is composed of a flat five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet flanked on one side by two alpha-helices (PMID: 36484105). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7659
comment: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found in bacteria and phage. Proteins in this family are typically between 128 and 147 amino acids in length. The proteins contain two subdomains separated by an alpha-helical linker. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7661
comment: This entry represents a family of small uncharacterised bacterial proteins that adopts a compact domain composed of 5 beta strands and a single alpha helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7667
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Structure prediction shows these proteins are alpha helical with a long central alpha helix packed against two shorter N and C-terminal helices. Structure prediction suggests these proteins may form homodimers. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7668
comment: This entry represents a bacterial protein domain of unknown function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7672
comment: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found in bacteria (Bacteroidota and Chloroflexi). Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. The proteins are likely to be integral membrane proteins with two transmembrane alpha helices. Structural modelling suggests that these proteins form a dimeric arrangement with the pairs of alpha helices tilted at close to 45 degrees angle compared to the lipid membrane. Based on the positive inside rule it is likely that the N and C-terminii of the proteins have a cytoplasmic location. Given the geometry of the protein complex it may not span the entire membrane. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7675
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of proteins is found in bacteria and viruses. Proteins in this family are typically between 69 and 93 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7690
comment: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is found N-terminal to Pfam:PF24736. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed of four alpha- helices. (from Pfam)

label: RXYLT1_C
comment: This domain is found in human Ribitol-5-phosphate xylosyltransferase 1 (RXYLT1) and related proteins. RXYLT1 acts as an UDP-d-xylose,ribitol-5-phosphate beta1,4-xylosyltransferase in the biosynthetic pathway of O-mannosyl glycan (PMID: 27733679). This domain has a detectable similarity to domains members of Glycosyl transferase clan GT-B and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7701
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from bacteria. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure with a highly conserved DVHDxWxxW sequence motif which may constitute a ligand binding site. This domain is likely to form a homodimer. Investigation of STRING networks suggests this protein may functionally interact with Pfam:PF24838 a likely octameric membrane complex. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7706
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of bacterial proteins. Structure prediction (Swiss:B2VAQ8 AF3 iPTM=0.93) suggests that these proteins form dimers. The monomer is composed of three alpha helices. STRING provides some weak evidence that these proteins may be immunity proteins or perhaps part of a plasmid addiction system. (from Pfam)

label: differ_SCO3897
comment: This domain, with four near-invariant Cys residues, occurs in a single copy at the C-terminal region of SCO3897 from Streptomyces coelicolor, a protein reported to be involved in differentiation in that species. The N-terminal region of that protein is rich in Gly, Pro, and Gln. This domain occurs also in the putative lipoprotein LppU (Rv2784c) of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Proteins in the more narrowly defined LppU family (see NF049864) contain eight invariant Cys residues, and approximate having two copies of this domain, although the second copy in Rv2784c scores below cutoffs. Most members of the LppU famiily are apparent lipoproteins, with a ninth conserved Cys residue, but a few instead have an extended N-terminal region compositionally similar to that of SCO3897.

label: FhaB_Rv0019c
comment: Proteins in this family, including founding member Rv0019c from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, contain a unique small hydrophobic N-terminal domain, a spacer region of hydrophilic low-complexity sequence, and C-terminal FHA (forkhead-associated) domain. Rv0019c, reported to be phosphorylated serine/threonine protein kinase PknB, has been called both FhaB (FHA domain-containing protein B) and FipA (FtsZ-interacting protein A), but the original paper providing the name FipA has been retracted.

label: resolv_YneB
comment: The family resembles the N-terminal half of IS607-like element transposases. The founding member of the family, YneB (NP_389670.1) from Bacillus subtilis, belongs to the three-gene operon yneA, yneB and ynzC, which is transcribed divergently from the SOS regulon repressor DinR, and is described as resembling transposon resolvases.

comment: Members of this family include FomA itself, from the genus Fusobacterium (see NF049909), and additional homologs from other lineages. FomA, although porin-like in structure, is best known for adhesive-like functions such as binding to surfaces and bridging other bacteria in mixed species biofilms.

label: SF0329_fam
comment: This family is named for SF0329 (NP_706281.1) from Shigella flexneri. Full length homologs of SF0329 are found in hundreds of bacterial species. Note that the first 10 and last 17 amino acids of its 151 amino acid length perfectly match a 27 amino acid translation from Escherichia coli K-12 (YP_009518750.1) that was mistaken for a small functional protein and named YkiD. We suggest that YkiD is nonfunctional remnant, and that the name YkiD should not be used.

label: ISAon1_upstream
product_name: ISAon1 family transposase N-terminal region protein
comment: ISAon1 is a variant from of ISL3 family transposase that lacks the two CXXC motifs in the N-terminal region found in typical ISL3 family transposases. ISAon1 family transposases are proposed to require a +1 frameshift to produce the functional form of the transposase, about 440 amino acids in length. This HMM describes the N-terminal region of about 120 amino acids, which likely would be made as transposase-related short protein when the frameshift does not occur. Based on the behavior of other transposases with programmed frameshifts, the short protein, once made, is likely to bind DNA and act as a suppressor of its own transcription.

label: ISAon1_downstr
comment: ISAon1 is a variant from of ISL3 family transposase that lacks the two CXXC motifs in the N-terminal region found in typical ISL3 family transposases. ISAon1 family transposases are proposed to require a +1 frameshift to produce the functional form of the transposase, about 445 amino acids in length. This HMM describes the C-terminal region of about 325 amino acids likely to be expressed only when translation of the N-terminal region (see NF049916) continues through the programmed frameshift.

comment: Flavin-dependent monooxygenase QhpG is a key component in the maturation of quinohemoprotein amine dehydrogenase (QHNDH) through dihydroxylating a tryptophan residue.

comment: QhpR is an AraC-like transcriptional regulator that controls the expression of the qhp operon in response to primary amines.

comment: Members of this family include lariocidin, the first lasso peptide demonstrated to act as broad spectrum antibiotic by binding to the bacterial ribosome and inhibiting protein translation. Note that triculamin is a related RiPP (ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide) with a very similar core, but a different architecture for the precursor peptide.

label: lario_core
product_name: lariocidin/triculamin family lasso peptide core domain
hmm_name: lariocidin/triculamin family lasso peptide core domain
comment: This HMM describes the conserved core domain of two types of lasso peptide-forming ribosomally synthesized, post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) precursor. One form (see NF050021) has a leader peptide region N-terminal to the core domain. Another form has the core domain as the amino-terminal portion of a peptide with additional C-terminal region. Member of this family include lariocidin, the first lasso peptide demonstrated to act as broad spectrum antibiotic by binding to the bacterial ribosome and inhibiting protein translation. Triculamin (also called alboverticillin), a related antibiotic RiPP peptide, also functions as an antibiotic, and likely also targets the ribosome.

label: SMU1112c_YaeR
comment: Members of this family are VOC domain-containing metalloproteins related to lactoylglutathione lyase (GloA, glyoxalase I, EC 4.4.1.5) but distinct from it. The family includes SMU1112c from Streptococcus mutans, EF2214 from Enterococcus faecalis, and YaeR from Escherichia coli K-12. The first two have solved crystal structures. SMU1112c is called a paralog of GloA and referred to as GloA2. Its mutation did not adversely affect tolerance to methylglyoxal, but instead caused increased sensitivity to fructose. A suggestion was made that fructose catabolism, following the conversion to fructose-1-phosphate during import by a PTS system, could result in the production of toxic Reactive Electrophile Species (RES) analogous to but distinct from methylglyoxal.

label: sort_motif_YLP
comment: The very short C-terminal protein sequence region described here is a putative protein-sorting signal, the YLP-box, whose hypothesized cognate sorting/anchoring partner remains unknown. Proteins ending with this sequence region average over 700 amino acids in length, the HMM models just eleven residues, and the well-conserved portion of the seed alignment is just eight residues. Because the HMMER package assigns a lower score to the same sequence region when it appears in a longer protein protein, it is impossible to set cutoffs such that the motif is found in long proteins without large number of false-positives being encountered in much shorter proteins or in spurious translations. However, the 135 sequences in the seed alignment, all derived from Chloroflexota lineage bacteria with at least two member proteins per genome, provide a recording of NCBI curator finding of validated examples of the new YLP-box putative sorting/anchoring signal. For another example of a very short putative novel sorting/anchoring signal, see model NF041763.

label: Myco_VOC_HglS
comment: Members of this family, well-conserved in Actinobacteria such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis, appear to be the actinobacterial counterpart to the lysine degradation enzyme 2-oxoadipate dioxygenase/decarboxylase (EC 1.13.11.93) of Pseudomonas putida, given the gene symbol hglS becayse the enzyme is known also as 2-hydroxyglutarate synthase. Supporting this hypothesis is frequent proximity of family members to other homologs of other lysine degradation enzyme. Neighboring proteins include L-lysine 6-transaminases such as WP_038579006.1, and dehydrogenases such as WP_020732096.1, in the family of L-piperidine-6-carboxylate dehydrogenases.

It was later shown to be a ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) with copper-binding oxazolone/thioamide sites formed by a multinuclear nonheme iron-dependent oxidase (MNIO). HvlX is encoded in a four-gene operon that also includes HvlA, a ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) that, after post-translational modification, carried out by a MNIO family peptide maturase, becomes a copper ion-binding protein.

label: RiPP_RRE_HvfC
comment: HvfC, as described in Haemophilus influenzae, is a partner protein to the multinuclear nonheme iron-dependent oxidase (MNIO) enzyme HvfB, and participates in post-translational modification that converts the precursor protein HvfA (Haemophilus virulence factor A) into a copper-binding metallophore and a contributor to the cell's ability to contribute to invade host cells and survive as an intracellular pathogen.

label: MNIO_BufB
comment: This HMM identifies multinuclear nonheme iron-dependent oxidative (MNIO) enzymes encoded in clusters with either (or both) type of bufferin precursor, BufA1 or BufA2, and designated BufB. Bufferins are unusual ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) precursors in that they have conventional signal peptide that direct Sec system-dependent translocation of the plasma membrane. Post-translational modification of BufA1 and BufA2 results in mature forms that are able to bind to copper and that may alleviate stress from excess concentrations of copper or other transition metals.

Mutation of the sorting enzyme, cyanoexosortase B, blocks hormogonium motifility. Homologs of Npun_F0296, identified by this HMM, are found widely in bacteria, linked to widely varying forms of C-terminal sorting domain, recognized and processed by various lineage-specific subtypes of exosortase, such as exosortase Z (NF050190), which recognizes the PGAP-CTERM sorting signal (NF050189).

label: DUF7744

label: Receiver_CRE1
comment: This entry represents the first receiver domain found in AHK4/CRE1/WOL from Arabidopsis thaliana, CRE1 from Medicago truncatula and homologues sequences from plants (PMID: 34630499). Alternative splicing of AHK4/CRE1 results in fine-tuning the cytokinin signalling pathway (PMID: 39501563). This domain mediates dimerisation through 3D domain swapping, which suggests that a considerable change of conformation must occur upon the phosphorylation reaction to allow HPt binding (PMID: 34630499). (from Pfam)

Sucrose synthases are sucrose-cleaving enzymes that provides UDP-glucose and fructose for various metabolic pathways. (from Pfam)

name_orig: Integrin beta-like protein A-E, second Ig-like domain
hmm_name: Integrin beta-like protein A-E, second Ig-like domain
comment: This entry represents the second Ig-like domain (according to structure predictions) of Integrin beta-like proteins A-E (SIBA-E) from Dictyostelium discoideum and similar sequences. These proteins may be implicated in cellular adhesion to substrate or phagocytic particles (PMID: 16699495). (from Pfam)

label: VWA7_N
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in the human von Willebrand factor A domain-containing protein 7 and related proteins. VWA7 is found in the major histocompatibility complex class III region and may be implicated in susceptibility to lung tumors (PMID: 10803853). This domain is usually followed by Pfam:PF25106. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_TEP1_2nd
comment: This entry represents the second of three presumed beta-propeller domains found at the C-terminal of Telomerase protein component 1 (TEP1), a component of the telomerase ribonucleoprotein complex that is essential for the replication of chromosome termini (PMID: 19179534). It is also a component of the ribonucleoprotein vaults particle, a multi-subunit structure involved in nucleo-cytoplasmic transport (PMID: 11149928). (from Pfam)

label: CBM87_Agd3
comment: This entry represents the carbohydrate binding module (CBM) domain found at the N-terminal of the exopolysaccharide deacetylase Agd3 from Aspergillus fumigatus, a protein required for biofilm formation (PMID: 32415073). This is the founding member of CBM family 87 (PMID: 32415073). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7734
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is predicted to adopt globular structure consisting of a curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. It contains a semi-conserved FKGFSS sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7782
comment: This is a presumed domain found at the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised sequences from Nocardia sp. According to structure predictions, this domain may adopt a winged helix fold with an insertion consisting of a long beta-hairpin and a short beta-strand. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7790
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised protein from Leptospira interrogans serogroup Icterohaemorrhagiae serovar Copenhageni and related bacterial proteins. Its structure was determined (PDB:6ULO) and shares a significant similarity to various methyltransferases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7793
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It shares detectable similarity to SpoIIAA-like domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7821
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in uncharacterised protein PM0657 and its paralogue PM1082 from Pasteurella multocida and related bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a alpha/beta globular structure consisting of a central antiparallel beta- sheet and helices packed on both sides. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7825
comment: This is a presumed domain found at the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. It may adopt a TPR-like fold. It is found associated with Pfam:PF20103 at the N-terminal and Pfam:PF25148 in the middle. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_H_T_join_3
comment: This entry is related to Pfam:PF05521 which is a phage protein that acts as a stopper to retain phage DNA in the capsid as well performing a head tail connector function. (from Pfam)

label: TPR_NPHP3
comment: This entry represents the TPR domain found at the C-terminal of nephrocystin-3 (NPHP3), a protein required for normal ciliary development and function. It inhibits disheveled-1-induced canonical Wnt-signaling activity and may also play a role in the control of non-canonical Wnt signaling which regulates planar cell polarity (PMID: 18371931). (from Pfam)

label: vWA_SIBA-E
comment: This entry represents a presumed vWA-like domain (according to structure predictions) of Integrin beta-like proteins A-E (SIBA-E) from Dictyostelium discoideum and similar sequences. These proteins may be implicated in cellular adhesion to substrate or phagocytic particles (PMID: 16699495). (from Pfam)

label: ACT_ACR9_3rd
comment: This is the third ACT domain of ACT domain-containing protein ACR9 from Arabidopsis thaliana and similar sequences mainly from plants and proteobacteria. ACR9 may bind amino acids (PMID: 21861936). (from Pfam)

label: ALN_composite
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal region of the composite domain of Allantoinase (ALN), a protein that catalyses the conversion of allantoin (5-ureidohydantoin) to allantoate by hydrolytic cleavage of the five-member hydantoin ring (PMID: 23940254). The composite domain of metal-dependent hydrolases has a pseudo-barrel fold that is interrupted by the catalytic beta/alpha domain. (from Pfam)

label: ARM_TT21_4th
product_name: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 forth ARM domain
name_orig: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 forth ARM domain
hmm_name: Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 forth ARM domain
comment: This entry represents the forth ARM-repeats domain found around the middle of Tetratricopeptide repeat protein 21 (TT21) from human and its homologues. TT21 is an intraflagellar transport (IFT)-associated protein required for spermatogenesis. It is involved in sperm flagellar formation and intraflagellar transport (PMID: 30929735). (from Pfam)

label: Agd3_CE
comment: This entry represents the carbohydrate esterase (CE) domain of the exopolysaccharide deacetylase Agd3 from Aspergillus fumigatus, a protein required for biofilm formation (PMID: 32415073). This domain has structural similarity to members of the carbohydrate esterase family (CE4) but the amino acid sequences is too divergent and constitutes a founding member of a CE family (PMID: 32415073). (from Pfam)

label: DSRM_2
comment: This entry represents a a set of divergent dsRNA binding domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7739
comment: This entry includes the Shigella phage Sf6 gene 22 protein Swiss:Q716F3. (from Pfam)

label: HEAT_EF3_N
comment: This entry represents the first five HEAT repeats found at the N-terminal of elongation factor 3 (EF3) from yeast, which is followed by a block of three HEAT repeats (Pfam:PF24984) (PMID: 16929303). EF3 is a ribosome-dependent ATPase that functions in cytoplasmic translation elongation. It is required for the ATP-dependent release of deacylated tRNA from the ribosomal E-site during protein biosynthesis [1,2]. This block is also found twice in the central region of the stalled ribosome sensor GCN1, a ribosome collision sensor that plays a key role in the RNF14-RNF25 translation quality control pathway, a pathway that takes place when a ribosome has stalled during translation, and which promotes ubiquitination and degradation of translation factors on stalled ribosomes. This entry also includes NEW1 from S. cerevisiae, a translation termination and ribosome biogenesis factor. It is an ATP-binding cassette protein that cosediments with polysomes and is required for biogenesis of the small ribosomal subunit (PMID: 31299085). (from Pfam)

label: LRR_Zer-1
comment: This region of leucine-rich repeats (LRR) is found in Zyg eleven-related protein 1 from Caenorhabditis elegans (Zer-1) and similar eukaryotic proteins. Zer-1 functions as a target recruitment subunit in the E3 ubiquitin ligase complex zer-1-cul-2-elc-1. (from Pfam)

label: NANM
comment: This entry includes N-acetylneuraminate epimerase (NANM) from Haemophilus influenzae, E. coli and its homologues. It converts alpha-N-acetylneuranimic acid (Neu5Ac) to the beta-anomer, accelerating the equilibrium between the alpha- and beta-anomers [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: NTF2_YvbJ
comment: This domain is found in Uncharacterized membrane protein YvbJ and related proteins. YvbJ contain a pair of NTF2-like domains toward the C terminus. This domain is the first in the pair. (from Pfam)

label: PGM1_C_vert_fung
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of phosphoglucomutase-1 (PGM1) from human, and its homologues from vertebrates and fungi, which catalyses the bi-directional interconversion between alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate (G1P) and alpha-D-glucose 6-phosphate (G6P), a reaction that is essential for normal carbohydrate metabolism and is also important in the cytoplasmic biosynthesis of nucleotide sugars needed for glycan biosynthesis [2-5]. This domain contains a six-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with two alpha-helices lying on the face of the sheet opposite the active site which is located centrally, in a deep cleft between the four domains of these proteins [1-5]. This domain contains the phosphate-binding loop which interacts with the substrate phosphate moiety (PMID: 32221390). (from Pfam)

label: SIBA-E_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal Ig-like domain (according to structure predictions) of Integrin beta-like proteins A-E (SIBA-E) from Dictyostelium discoideum and similar sequences. These proteins may be implicated in cellular adhesion to substrate or phagocytic particles (PMID: 16699495). (from Pfam)

label: SUS_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of sucrose synthases, which corresponds to the cellular targeting domain (CTD, also referred to as SSN1) and together with the EPBD domain (SSN2), they have regulatory functions in plant species, however, the function of these domains in bacteria is not yet clear [1,2]. Sucrose synthases are sucrose-cleaving enzymes that provide UDP-glucose and fructose for various metabolic pathways. (from Pfam)

label: Rv0361_Cterm
comment: Rv0361 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis was shown to undergo secretion, and to end up either on the cell surface or in the extracellular environment. This HMM describes the conserved C-terminal region shared by a large number of homologs of Rv0361 in the Actinobacteria, starting with a long hydrophobic segment likely to span the membrane. Members of the family differ greatly in the lengths of protein regions predicted N-terminal to this hydrophobic stretch.

label: PepSY_MTB
comment: This HMM was built to find PepSY domain-containing proteins that are missed by Pfam model PF03413, such as Rv0603 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

label: sunset
comment: This domain, about 42 amino acids long, is named sunset because it nearly always occurs at the end of a longer protein. Many examples of ribosomal proteins L4, L17, L20, S2, and S16 have this domain at the C-terminus, as do many endonucleases, membrane proteins, and proteins of unknown function.

label: 50S_L17_sunset
product_name: 50S ribosomal protein L17, sunset domain variant
hmm_name: 50S ribosomal protein L17, sunset domain variant
comment: Members of this family are a variant form of the 50S ribosomal protein L17 with an additional C-terminal region containing first a Glu/Asp/Ala-rich spacer region and then a 42-amino acid sunset domain (NF051437), so named (by us) because it is found at the very end (C-terminus) of a variety of proteins, some of which are ribosomal proteins (ribosomal proteins L4, L17, L20, S2, and S16).

label: acrylyl_AcuI
comment: AcuI (acrylate utilization I), as described in Rhodobacter sphaeroides, is an acrylyl-CoA reductase encoded in an operon involved in the catabolism of dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP), which is biosynthesized by marine phytoplankton as a compatible solute and is abundant in marine environments. YhdH from Escherichia coli K-12 also functions as an acrylyl-CoA reductase

label: acryl_TF_AcuR
comment: AcuR (acrylate utilization transcriptional regulator) from Rhodobacter sphaeroides is TetR/AcrR family transcription factor regularly found encoded just upstream of the dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) utilization enzyme AcuI, which acts on acrylate produced by cleavage of DMSP.

label: bifunc_PcaDC
comment: In this type of protocatechuate degradation bifunctional protein, the N-terminal region has 3-oxoadipate enol-lactonase activity, EC 3.1.1.24 (see TIGR02427, PcaD), while the C-terminal region has 4-carboxymuconolactone decarboxylase activity, EC 4.1.1.44 (see TIGR02425, PcaC).

label: Beta-prop_WDR36-Utp21_2nd
comment: This entry includes WDR36 from human and its orthologue from yeasts, Utp21, which are part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, the first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit. They are involved in the nucleolar processing of SSU 18S rRNA [1,2]. This entry represents the second beta-propeller domain, found in the middle region of these proteins. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_WDR3_2nd
comment: This is the second beta-propeller domain of WDR3 from animals and its homologues. It is part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, the first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit (PMID: 34516797). (from Pfam)

label: CGLA_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of Lambda-carrageenase (CGLA), a protein that hydrolyses lambda-carrageenan with inversion of anomeric configuration (PMID: 16926183). This domain may adopt a beta-sandwich fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7826
comment: This entry represents a family of small uncharacterised bacterial alpha solenoid proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7840
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold onto a meander beta-barrel and it is likely associated with the membrane. It is frequently found in combination with Pfam:PF13387. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7867
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from alphaproteobacteria. This domain is usually found associated with Pfam:PF13400 and is predicted to form a three -sided beta-helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7869
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed of a curved beta-sheet and helices packed on it. It contains conserved histidine and aspartate residues some of which cluster in space. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7901
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich structure with significant topological similarity to known galactose-binding domains, in particular to lectin-like domain of the Cwp84, a surface layer associated protein of Clostridium difficile. It is likely that this domain is involved carbohydrate binding. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7902
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a three-helical bundle with some topological similarity to spectrin. (from Pfam)

label: Decapeptide
comment: This entry corresponds to a region composed of a 10 residue repeat that forms an alpha helical solenoid structure. (from Pfam)

label: Gp54
comment: This entry represents a small phage protein of approximately 66 amino acids that acts as a trigger for bacterial antiviral defence systems (PMID: 39415022). The protein adopts a rare six-stranded beta-barrel fold in its unbound state.
