Upon binding to the bacterial CapRel defence protein, Gp54 undergoes a dramatic conformational change where the beta-barrel unfolds and forms a hybrid eight-stranded beta-sheet with CapRel. The interaction is entropically driven and activates CapRel's antiviral response. The beta-barrel structure is unique, with the closest structural homologues being five-stranded SH3 domains. Gp54 represents one of two known protein triggers for the CapRel defence system, the other being phage major capsid proteins. (from Pfam)

label: 5TMH_Lnb
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in Lipoprotein N-acyltransferase Lnb from Bacteroides and related uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Lnb functions as a lipoprotein N-acyltransferase in its native cell environment (PMID: 39495918). It is composed of two domains, N-terminal periplasmic domain and C-terminal alpha-helical transmembrane domain (this entry) which is predicted to contain five transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: 6TM_PilS
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in Sensor protein kinases PilS and RegB, and related bacterial proteins. PilS is a member of the two-component regulatory system PilS/PilR that regulates the expression of multiple genes including the type IV pilus major subunit PilA (PMID: 7911557). It is a membrane-associated protein kinase that phosphorylates PilR in response to environmental signals. RegB is a member of the two-component regulatory system RegB/RegA, which is involved in the positive regulation of photosynthesis gene expression in response to anaerobiosis. This domain is predicted to contain six transmembrane helices. (from Pfam)

label: AAA_lid_BCS1
product_name: Mitochondrial chaperone BCS1-like, ATPase lid domain
name_orig: Mitochondrial chaperone BCS1-like, ATPase lid domain
hmm_name: Mitochondrial chaperone BCS1-like, ATPase lid domain
comment: This ATPase lid domain is found at the C-terminal end of human Mitochondrial chaperone BCS1 and similar eukaryotic proteins. BCS1 is a chaperone necessary for the incorporation of Rieske iron-sulfur protein UQCRFS1 into the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III. It plays an important role in the maintenance of mitochondrial tubular networks, respiratory chain assembly and formation of the LETM1 complex. This domain is normally found immediately C-terminal to Pfam:PF00004 and also associated with Pfam:PF08740. (from Pfam)

label: BSD2_CRD
comment: This domain is found in the chloroplastic Protein BUNDLE SHEATH DEFECTIVE 2 (BSD2) from Arabidopsis thaliana and related proteins. BSD2 is a chloroplast chaperone required for RuBisCo biogenesis and translational regulation of the RuBisCo large subunit (PMID: 29217567). It has a role in stabilizing an end-state assembly intermediate of eight RuBisCo large subunits until the small subunits become available. The structure of this domain has been determined and it has a hairpin architecture arranged around two Zn atoms, each coordinated by four cysteines (PMID: 29217567). Members with this domain contain a highly conserved CxxCxGxG sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_EMC1_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal beta-propeller domain of EMC1 (ER membrane protein complex subunit 1), a protein part of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane protein complex (EMC) that enables the energy-independent insertion into endoplasmic reticulum membranes of newly synthesized membrane proteins [1-3]. This complex preferentially accommodates proteins with transmembrane domains that are weakly hydrophobic or contain destabilising features such as charged and aromatic residues (PMID: 30415835). EMC1 contains two eight-bladed beta-propellers and stabilises the entire complex, contacting six of the remaining eight subunits (PMID: 32439656). The beta-propellers are in the lumen and may serve as a platform for recruitment of co-factors at the site of nascent protein insertion (PMID: 32439656). (from Pfam)

label: CGLA_M
comment: This entry represents a domain found in the middle of Lambda-carrageenase (CGLA), a protein that hydrolyses lambda-carrageenan with inversion of anomeric configuration (PMID: 16926183). (from Pfam)

label: CoiA_C
comment: This entry represents a domain found C-terminal in the Competence protein CoiA from Bacillus subtilis and related proteins. This domain is predicted to fold in a mainly alpha-helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7829
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha- helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7852
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich structure with long twisted strands. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7868
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It has similarity to the C-terminal domain of Haemocyanin and it is predicted to adopt similar beta-sandwich fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7884
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is usually found associated with methyltransferase domains such as Pfam:PF13489 and Pfam:PF13649 and is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta configuration. It has a conserved motif F/YWDG. (from Pfam)

label: GT_PLOD
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal GT domain found in the family of collagen lysyl hydroxylases (LH or PLOD). Enzymes belonging this family catalyse the lysine hydroxylation of collagens using Fe2+, 2-oxoglutarate, ascorbate and molecular oxygen [1,2]. In humans, PLOD genes encode for three LH enzyme isoforms sharing significant sequence similarity. Mutations in PLOD genes that reduce or abolish their activity are associated with severe connective tissue diseases including Ehlers-Danlos and Bruck syndromes [3,4]. PLOD3 is considered the evolutionary ancestor of the family as this isoform is the only one capable of further processing of hydroxylysines through glycosylation, whereas other isoforms might have lost such capability during evolution. These enzymes consist of three domains encompassing multiple active sites. The two N-terminal domains have a topology typical for glycosyltransferases whereas the C-terminal has a DSBH fold. The domain represented by this entry is the only catalytically active domain and is the solely responsible for the glycosyltransferase activity. (from Pfam)

label: Acb3
comment: This entry represents the Acb3 family of phage proteins that inhibit bacterial CBASS defense systems. Acb3 wraps around the CD-NTase enzyme and makes extensive contacts with both the nucleotidyltransferase active site and ligand binding domain. Despite low sequence similarity between different CD-NTases, Acb3 can inhibit diverse CBASS systems and even human cGAS. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-barrel_CAF17_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of the human putative transferase CAF17, mitochondrial and similar eukaryotic proteins. CAF17 is involved in the maturation of mitochondrial 4Fe-4S proteins functioning late in the iron-sulfur cluster assembly pathway [1,2]. CAF17 part of the COG0354 family which includes folate-dependent proteins such as YgfZ which shares structural similarity (PMID: 20489182). This entry also includes putative aminomethyltransferase folate-binding proteins in bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-prop_WDR36-Utp21_1st
comment: This entry includes WDR36 from human and its orthologue from yeasts, Utp21, which are part of the small subunit (SSU) processome, the first precursor of the small eukaryotic ribosomal subunit. They are involved in the nucleolar processing of SSU 18S rRNA [1,2]. This entry represents the first beta-propeller domain, found at the N-terminal of these proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7831
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins which form a compact domain. Structure prediction of Swiss:K2M825 suggests a highly confident homodimer (iPTM=0.93). This protein is found in a mixture of bacteria and phage. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7834
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised domain found at the C-terminus of proteins contains a Pfam:PF03235 domain at the N-terminus. This domain is composed of multiple alpha helices. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7841
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised bacteriophage family of proteins. Structure prediction with Swiss:G5H923 suggests that members of this family will form homodimeric complexes (iPTM=0.87 and pTM=0.89). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7843
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha-helical array. It is frequently found in combination with Pfam:PF13387 and Pfam:PF25222. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7844
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold onto a structure with significant similarity to Glucose-regulated metallo-peptidase M90. This domain is frequently found in combination with Pfam:PF13387. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7850
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Actinomycetes. It is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich structure with significant similarity to carbohydrate-binding modules in particular to CBM_4_9 (Pfam:PF02018). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7878
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to contain two structural beta(3)-alpha repeats that swap their alpha-helix in a similar way as observed in the known ssDNA-binding transcriptional regulator domains. It is likely that this domain is distantly related to them and probably represents the minimal two repeat containing fold. (from Pfam)

label: ETR1_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Ethylene receptor 1 from Arabidopsis thaliana (ETR1) and similar plant proteins. ETR1 acts as a redundant negative regulator of ethylene signalling. It is related to bacterial two-component regulators. This domain, which is predicted to adopt an all alpha structure, is often found associated to Pfam:PF01590. (from Pfam)

label: Ig_NUP210_16th
comment: This domain is found in human Nuclear pore membrane glycoprotein 210 (NUP210), which is essential for nuclear pore assembly and fusion, nuclear pore spacing, as well as structural integrity. NUP210 is composed of multiple immunoglobin-like (Ig-like) domains and forms a ring around the NPC within the NE lumen (PMID: 35679397). (from Pfam)

label: NonGDSL
comment: This entry represents a family of alpha/beta hydrolase enzymes. These presumed enzymes are most similar to the GDSL lipases. However the GDSL motif has been lost suggesting they may have lost their lipase activity. (from Pfam)

label: AIM3_BBC1_C
comment: This entry represents a C-terminal domain found in fungal proteins that contains a cysteine peptidase-like fold but appears to lack the conserved catalytic residues. The domain is found in proteins that also contain an N-terminal SH3 domain. BBC1 is involved in the regulation of actin patch assembly and AIM3 is involved in mitochondrial inheritance, though the specific role of this domain remains to be determined. (from Pfam)

label: Beta-barrel_SelB
comment: This domain is found in Selenocysteine-specific elongation factor from Escherichia coli (SelB) and similar bacterial proteins. SelB is a translation factor necessary for the incorporation of selenocysteine into proteins. It probably replaces EF-Tu for the insertion of selenocysteine directed by the UGA codon. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7873
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised actinobacterial proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7882
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins that are about 100 amino acids in length. These proteins are predicted to form homopentameric complexes. These proteins are found in actinomycete as well as a few phage genomes. (from Pfam)

label: ELLD
comment: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised phage and bacterial proteins. It is related to domains that are members of the NlpC/P60 and Bacteriophage peptidoglycan hydrolase families of Papain-like cysteine proteases, Pfam:PF00877 and Pfam:PF05382, respectively. This domain is probably catalytically active as it contains highly conserved cysteine and histidine residues. Some members of this entry are circularly permuted and their N-terminal two beta-strands occupy the position of the C-terminal strands in other members. (from Pfam)

label: OMP_b-brl_4
comment: This entry represents a large family of outer membrane beta barrel proteins. Many of these proteins contain an N-terminal Pfam:PF13620 domain. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_Bbp19
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised phage protein that is composed of three alpha helices. There is some evidence from structure predictions that this protein may homodimerise. These dimers are predicted to form a ring of eight dimers. The family includes Swiss:Q775C5 the Bbp19 protein from Bordetella BPP-1 phage. (from Pfam)

label: TPR_CHK1
comment: This region of tetratricopeptide (TPR)-like repeats is found in Histidine protein kinase 1 from Candida albicans (CHK1), which is involved in a two-component signaling pathway that regulates cell wall mannan and glucan biosynthesis. (from Pfam)

label: Tad5
comment: This entry represents the Tad5 family of phage proteins that inhibit the bacterial Type I Thoeris defense system. Tad5 binds to ThsB and interacts with its catalytic residue E85, though it does not completely block the active site pocket. (from Pfam)

label: TseH
product_name: Type VI secretion system effector TseH-like
name_orig: Type VI secretion system effector TseH-like
hmm_name: Type VI secretion system effector TseH-like
comment: This domain is found in the Type VI secretion system effector TseH and related bacterial proteins. V. cholerae T6SS effector TseH is a PAAR-dependent species-specific effector. It is highly toxic to Aeromonas and Edwardsiella species, bacteria that V. cholerae encounters in natural environments or common hosts. TseH structure has a significant similarity to papain-like proteases, including the conserved active site architecture. This domain is found standalone or in combination with Pfam:PF20405. (from Pfam)

label: VG15
comment: This entry represents the Gene 15 protein (VG15) from Mycobacterium phage D29 and L5 and related proteins from tailed bacteriophages. This family is probably distantly related to Pfam:PF06152 and likely represents phage capsid proteins. Members of this family contain two pairs of highly conserved cysteine residues that may constitute a metal binding site. (from Pfam)

label: YxzE
comment: This entry represents a putative bacteriocin family related to the YxzE protein found in B. subtilis. This entry contains both the leader peptide and the putative bacteriocin sequence. (from Pfam)

label: TM_PetC
comment: This transmembrane domain, consisting of a single transmembrane helix, is found in the Cytochrome b6-f complex iron-sulfur subunit PetC and related proteins. PetC, is a crucial component of the cytochrome b6f complex, which plays a central role in oxygenic photosynthesis [1,2]. PetC contains a [2Fe-2S] cluster, which is is essential for the electron transfer process within the complex. PetC interacts with other subunits to form the functional cytochrome b6f complex. The complex functions as a dimer, with each monomer composed of eight subunits in total [3-5]. (from Pfam)

label: bPH_11
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial PH domains found in actinomycete bacteria. These proteins contain a transmembrane helix which likely anchors these proteins in the bacterial membrane. According to STRING these proteins are functionally connected to large biosynthetic operon proteins. These proteins possibly act as structural components of large complexes of these proteins. (from Pfam)

label: WHD_RNase_II
comment: This entry represents a winged helix domain found in ribonuclease II (RNR1) from Arabidopsis thaliana and similar sequences from plants and cyanobacteria. RNR1 is a 3'-5' exoribonuclease that catalyses 3' maturation of chloroplast and mitochondrion ribosomal RNAs. It degrades short nucleotidic extensions to generate the mature 3'-ends [1,2]. It is involved in the maturation of 23S, 16S and 5S rRNAs. (from Pfam)

label: Spore_GerAC_N
hmm_name: Ger(x)C family spore germination protein N-terminal domain
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of spore germination proteins such as GerAC and GerBC. (from Pfam)

label: Tad8
comment: This entry represents the Tad8 family of phage proteins that inhibit the bacterial Type II Thoeris defense system. Tad8 forms a homodimer that binds to the Macro domain of the ThsA protein, inserting loops that occupy the His-ADPR binding pocket and prevent recognition of the immune signaling molecule. (from Pfam)

label: Kelch_FKB95
comment: This entry represents a domain consisting of Kelch repeats found in plant proteins that are also associated with a F-box domain, such as FKB95 from Arabidopsis, a protein that is a component of SCF(ASK-cullin-F-box) E3 ubiquitin ligase complexes, which mediate the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins. (from Pfam)

label: SCP2_Rv3818
comment: This domain is found in the putative Rieske 2Fe-2S iron-sulfur protein Rv3818 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis and similar bacterial proteins. Rv3818 was identified as a high-confidence drug target. This domain is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta configuration and is usually found associated with Pfam:PF13483 and Pfam:PF00355. (from Pfam)

label: Tad4
comment: This entry represents the Tad4 family of phage proteins that inhibit the bacterial Type I Thoeris defense system. Tad4 binds directly to ThsB and blocks its active site via a conserved loop region, preventing production of the immune signaling molecule gcADPR. Interestingly, Tad4 can also bind and inhibit plant and human TIR domain proteins including BdTIR and SARM1. These proteins form a small helical bundle domain structure. (from Pfam)

label: WD40_Gbeta
product_name: G protein beta WD-40 repeat protein
name_orig: G protein beta WD-40 repeat protein
hmm_name: G protein beta WD-40 repeat protein
comment: This entry represents the WD-40 repeat domain found in G protein beta subunits. G beta subunits are essential components of heterotrimeric G proteins, acting as molecular scaffolds that facilitate interactions between G alpha subunits and various downstream effector proteins. The structure consists of a beta-propeller formed by seven WD-40 repeats. (from Pfam)

label: transpos_IS110_2
comment: This HMM describes a variant form of IS110 family transposase, and overlaps some with model NF033542.

label: BT4005_BT4719
comment: Members of this lipoprotein family received the name NigD from a paper that has since been withdrawn, and that is not cited here. Subsequent work in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron by Pardue, et al., on paralogous proteins they designated NigD1 and NigD2 showed dramatic up-regulation by a regulatory circuit that governs the production of outer membrane vesicles. The specific function, however, remains unknown.

label: glycan_WsfD
comment: This family includes WsfD from Paenibacillus alvei, and full-length homologs from other species. WsfD belongs to a large locus involved in synthesizing a large glycan that becomes covalently attached to the S-layer glycoprotein SpaA. It is proposed to be a transferase of some hexose other than mannose, despite similarity to dolichyl-phosphate-mannose-protein mannosyltransferases (PMTs), because mannose is not found in the mature glycan.

label: PheS_related
comment: Members of this family resemble the phenylalanine--tRNA ligase alpha subunit. However, species with this protein always encode both PheS and PheT in addition. This family is broadly but sporadically distributed, although it is found mostly in the Actinomyctes. No other protein families are found regularly in its vicinity. Pending discovery of its function, this protein is named SrmL (pheS-Related Mystery Ligase).

label: DUF7919
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain likely contains a zinc binding site. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7931
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function mostly found in bacteria. According to structure predictions it might adopt a phospholipase D/nuclease fold. Whilst the typical phospholipase D motif HxK(x)4D(x)6GSxN is not strictly conserved the overall fold suggests a potential distant evolutionary relationship to the PLD superfamily. The PLD nucleases can have endonuclease or exonuclease activity. These enzymes use the imidazole group of histidine as a nucleophile in their catalytic mechanism [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7942
comment: This family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins is found mainly in Actinomycetes. Members of this family are predicted to contain three transmembrane helices. A member of this family, SCO4225, is a putative integral membrane protein found in Streptomyces coelicolor, Swiss:Q9FCE5. The gene encoding SCO4225 is part of a cluster of genes (phoU to sco4225) that are involved in phosphate regulation and metabolism. This gene cluster is regulated by the two-component system PhoR-PhoP, which responds to phosphate availability in the environment (PMID: 22466952). The expression of SCO4225 is directly regulated by MacR, a response regulator that binds to a specific sequence in the promoter region of SCO4225. This regulation links SCO4225 to other genes in the MacR regulon, many of which are also membrane proteins (PMID: 30530707). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7945
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins predominantly from Actinomycetes. It is predicted to fold into array of alpha-helices. (from Pfam)

label: FimV_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of the motility hub protein FimV that is located N-terminal to the LysM domain. This domain adopts an immunoglobulin (Ig)-fold structure. FimV is an inner membrane protein that plays a role in twitching motility, type IV pilus assembly, and type II secretion in bacteria like Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This domain is likely involved in interactions with other proteins and might contribute to the localization of components of the type IV pilus and type II secretion machinery to the bacterial cell poles. (from Pfam)

label: HP1_ORF34
name_orig: Bacteriophage HP1 ORF34 baseplate complex protein
hmm_name: baseplate complex protein, phage HP1 ORF34 family
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins predicted to be involved in the sheath-tube baseplate complex. Members of this family show structural similarity to the Pvc7 component of contractile injection systems Pfam:PF19266, suggesting a likely structural role in the phage tail assembly. The C-terminal region of the protein is predicted to be disordered. (from Pfam)

label: HTH_SB
comment: This entry represents the HTH domain, also known as PAI subdomain, found in Sleeping Beauty transposase and homologues. This domain improves the enzyme structural stability and transposon DNA-binding. (from Pfam)

label: PTS_EIIB_BC_N
product_name: PTS system fructose specific EIIB'BC N-terminal
name_orig: PTS system fructose specific EIIB'BC N-terminal
hmm_name: PTS system fructose specific EIIB'BC N-terminal
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of phosphotransferase system (PTS) permease fructose specific EII2 enzyme found predominantly found in bacteria. EII consists of at least three structurally distinct domains IIA, IIB and IIC. These can either be fused together in a single polypeptide chain or exist as two or three interactive chains. When IIB and IIC are fused together in the same polypeptide chain they are called IIBC. In Gram-negative bacteria, diverse IIB architectures have been observed. For example duplicated IIB N-terminal domains found in E.Coli. These proteins, then, have an N-terminal IIB and a central IIB. They are referred as IIB'B (PMID: 8626640). The fructose specific family are one of four structurally and functionally distinct group IIB PTS system cytoplasmic enzymes [1-4]. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_gp49
comment: This entry represents the gene 49 protein (gp49) found in Mycobacteriophage D29 and L5. The protein contains disordered regions at both the N-terminus (residues 1-49) and internally (residues 114-157). The C-terminal region contains several conserved cysteine residues that may be functionally important. The specific function of this protein within the phage life cycle has not yet been determined. (from Pfam)

label: BW3TFN
product_name: Baseplate wedge 3 tail fiber network component
name_orig: Baseplate wedge 3 tail fiber network component
hmm_name: Baseplate wedge 3 tail fiber network component
comment: This entry represents the Baseplate Wedge 3 Tail Fiber Network (BW3TFN) component found in bacteriophage A511 and related phages. The protein forms dimers that constitute an essential part of the bacteriophage tail fiber structure. The BW3TFN protein (gp105 in phage A511) is located in the proximal part of the tail fiber and interacts with the Baseplate Wedge 3 (BW3) protein, which crosses the surface of BW3TFN dimers. The protein retains the structure and functionality of T4 BW3TFN gp8 but has a more streamlined architecture, making it about half the size. BW3TFN proteins are found in many contractile tail bacteriophages and related injection systems. Multiple BW3TFN dimers arranged in series form a rigid scaffold that constitutes the proximal part of the phage tail fiber and is involved in the transmission of the conformational signal from the baseplate to the receptor binding proteins during host cell attachment. (from Pfam)

label: Bestrophin_2
comment: The Bestrophin family comprises voltage-dependent anion channel-forming proteins that are involved in the formation of ion channels across cellular membranes. These proteins are characterized by their ability to facilitate the transport of anions, such as chloride ions, across the membrane, which is crucial for maintaining cellular ion homeostasis and electrical stability. The family is associated with the bestrophin-like anion channel-forming proteins, which are known for their role in various physiological processes, including regulation of cell volume, signal transduction, and sensory perception. This entry includes bacterial, fungal and plant bestrophin homologues. (from Pfam)

label: Chimallin_Phikzvirus
comment: The Phikzvirus chimallin family consists of proteins that self-assemble to form a protective proteinaceous shell around viral DNA. This shell compartmentalizes proteins and DNA during viral infection, creating a micrometer-scale compartment with narrow pores. It serves as the site of viral replication, where proteins involved in DNA replication are localized. Additionally, the shell provides a docking surface for capsids during the packaging process. The structure likely plays a crucial role in protecting the viral genome against host defenses, ensuring successful viral replication and packaging. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7941
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of phage proteins from Uroviricota. These proteins are about 300 amino acids in length. They may represent phage structural proteins. (from Pfam)

label: MTRES1_C
product_name: Mitochondrial transcription rescue factor 1, C-terminal domain
name_orig: Mitochondrial transcription rescue factor 1, C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Mitochondrial transcription rescue factor 1, C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of human Mitochondrial transcription rescue factor 1 (MTRES1), which is involved in mitochondrial transcription regulation and functions as a protective factor to maintain proper mitochondrial RNA level during stress. This domain is predicted to fold as a beta-sheet with two alpha-helices on one side. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TTP_16
comment: This entry represents a family of bacteriophage tail tube proteins. The tail tube forms the inner channel of the contractile tail which is used for DNA transfer from the capsid to the host during infection. (from Pfam)

label: T4_Y03C
comment: This entry represents a family of small uncharacterized proteins found in bacteriophage T4. The prototype is the 10.3 kDa protein encoded in the Gp46-Gp47 intergenic region of T4 phage. The function of this protein family remains unknown. (from Pfam)

label: RelB_like_antitoxin
comment: This entry represents a putative family of antitoxin proteins that interact with ParE like toxin proteins. Structure prediction of Swiss:L8MAJ5 with an adjacent ParE-like protein Swiss:L8M3T8 shows confident interaction (iPTM=0.89). (from Pfam)

label: T4_Tape_measure
comment: This entry represents bacteriophage tape measure proteins (TMP) that serve as molecular rulers determining the length of phage tails. During tail assembly, the TMP acts as a template for tail tube polymerization, with the protein being incorporated in an initially unfolded form. As the tail tube forms, the TMP extends, determining the final length of the tail structure. The tape measure protein is also involved in DNA transfer, possibly forming a channel through which phage DNA passes into the host cell during infection. In phage T4, the tape measure protein (gp29) is located in the central hub of the baseplate and extends through the tail tube. (from Pfam)

label: TBCA_PH
comment: This entry represents the tubulin chaperone cofactor A (TBCA) domain in Pleckstrin homology (PH) domain-containing proteins, mostly found in eukaryotes. The TBCA fold displays three alfa-helices forming an antiparallel bundle. Human TBCA functions as a molecular chaperone for beta-tubulin (PMID: 12054808). PH domain-containing proteins, such as PKHA7, are crucial for the biogenesis and maintenance of zonula adherens, a type of cell-cell junction (PMID: 14594214). The specific function of the TBCA domain in PH domain-containing proteins has not been elucidated yet. (from Pfam)

label: Terminase_7
comment: This entry represents a putative phage small terminase subunit. Predicted structures show similarity albeit weak to the structure of the HK97 terminase (PDB:8pop). Furthermore structure prediction suggests members of this family can form homomeric rings with high confidence as expected for small subunit terminases. (from Pfam)

label: WXG100_2
comment: This entry represents a domain that is related to proteins in the WXG100 superfamily. Its function is unknown. This domain is found at the N-terminus of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis Outer membrane channel protein CpnT (Swiss:O05442). It has been suggested that this N-terminal domain acts as a membrane channel (PMID: 24753609). However, structure prediction does not show any regions of hydrophobic surface that would be expected in a channel protein. (from Pfam)

label: crAss_MUZ_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal beta sandwich domain found in the muzzle protein found at the distal end of the tail in bacteriophages of the Crassviridae family. This large protein forms a hexameric assembly at the tip of the tail barrel and exhibits a novel fold designated as the crass fold. The muzzle protein is composed of five domains: a ring-joining domain, a seven-bladed beta-propeller domain, two immunoglobulin-like domains (IG1 and IG2), and the crass domain. The muzzle protein forms a gate-like structure that likely serves as a gatekeeper controlling the ejection of cargo proteins and viral DNA during infection. The gate is formed by a loop within blade 4 of the propeller domain. The crass domain, with its exposed surface loops, likely plays a role in contacting the host cell surface, initiating conformational changes that open the gate. The muzzle protein is highly conserved among crassviruses, though with length variations resulting from insertions in the crass and IG2 domains that affect surface properties. This protein has been structurally characterized in Bacteroides phage crAss001 (PMID: 37138077). (from Pfam)

label: crAss_THB
comment: This entry represents the tail hub protein B (THB) found in bacteriophages. The protein forms a heterotrimer with tail hub protein A (THA), and these heterotrimers further assemble as 12 docking hubs that form a continuous collar around the tail barrel. The C-terminal segment of THB (residues 67-107) extends into the neighbouring hub, resulting in interlocking connections between adjacent hub assemblies. Each docking hub anchors the trimeric tail fibers. The tail hub proteins play an important structural role in phage assembly, serving as the attachment point for the tail fiber appendages. THB has been structurally characterized in the Bacteroides phage crAss001, revealing its role in the architecture of the phage tail (PMID: 37138077). (from Pfam)

label: AsqO_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Quinolone epoxide rearrangement protein asqO from Emericella nidulans and similar fungal proteins. AsqO is part of the gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of the aspoquinolone mycotoxins. Proteins in this family are predicted to consist of two similar beta-barrel domains: Pfam:PF24137 and this entry. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7927
comment: This domain of unknown function is found in multiple copies in a number of bacterial proteins. It is closely related to domains represented by DUF11 (Pfam:PF01345). Similarly to DUF11, this domain contains a conserved N-terminal lysine and a C-terminal asparagine with central aspartate/glutamate residues suggesting that it may contain an isopeptide bond. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7939
comment: This entry is a small alpha-helical domain found at the C-terminus of proteins a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins that have a set of beta sandwich domains towards the N-terminus including Pfam:PF13584. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7946
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found at the N-terminus of a set of bacterial and phage proteins. It is often associated with a C-terminal small beta barrel domain. (from Pfam)

label: GldD_lipo
comment: This entry represents the GldD lipoprotein family which is found in bacteria that exhibit gliding motility. GldD is a component of the gliding motility machinery. The protein is post-translationally modified as a lipoprotein. While GldD is essential for gliding motility, its precise molecular function remains to be determined. (from Pfam)

label: Ig_RIMBP2
comment: This immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domain is found in human RIMS -binding protein 2 (RIMBP2) and similar proteins mainly found in animals. RIMBP2 plays a role in the synaptic transmission as bifunctional linker. (from Pfam)

label: Inovirus_capsid
comment: The Inovirus capsid protein family is involved in the formation of helical capsids that encapsulate viral genomic DNA. These proteins self-assemble to create a filamentous structure with dimensions ranging from 760 to 1950 nm in length and 6 to 8 nm in width. The assembly and budding of the virion occur at the host's inner membrane, facilitating the viral life cycle. This structural role is crucial for the protection and delivery of viral genetic material during infection. (from Pfam)

label: Mycobacteriophage_Gene3
comment: This entry represents a family of small proteins found in mycobacteriophages. Members of this family include the Gene 3 protein (Gp3) from mycobacteriophages L5 and D29, which belong to the Fromanvirus genus. The function of these proteins remains unknown. The proteins are approximately 83 amino acids in length and show conservation in the central region, particularly around potential binding sites. (from Pfam)

label: Mycophage_Gp42
comment: This entry represents the Gene 42 protein (Gp42) found in mycobacteriophages such as D29 and L5. These are small proteins of approximately 70 amino acids in length. The specific function of this protein family is currently unknown. The predicted structure is composed of a three stranded beta sheet with an alpha helix between strands 1 and 2. Proteins in this family are often annotated as minor tail proteins. (from Pfam)

label: P2_C
product_name: Viral coat protein P2 C-terminal domain
name_orig: Viral coat protein P2 C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Viral coat protein P2 C-terminal domain
comment: P2 (30.2 kDa) is the major outer-coat protein of the marine lipid-containing bacteriophage PM2. Each sub-unit of P2 is composed of two beta barrel jelly rolls, disposed normal to the surface of the capsid, which lend pseudo-6-fold symmetry to the molecules, facilitating their close packing within the capsid. There is a Ca2+ ion located between the two beta barrels of P2 that helps PM2 molecular organisation stabilization. This entry represents the C-terminal jelly roll domain of P2 (PMID: 18775333). (from Pfam)

label: Phage_HCP1
comment: This entry represents a phage head completion protein 1 that forms part of the connector complex between the phage capsid and tail in lactococcal phages. The protein is primarily characterized in Lactococcus phage p2, a member of the Skunavirus genus (formerly 936 group of lactococcal phages) which infects Lactococcus lactis. The protein exhibits an open central channel for viral DNA ejection and plays a crucial role in the morphogenesis of the virion after genome packaging. In lactococcal phage p2, this protein (ORF-8) is located at a position normally occupied by the first head completion protein, binding to both the portal protein and the stopper (head completion protein 2). The connector complex is essential for packaging of phage DNA inside the capsid and subsequent DNA release during host infection. Similar head completion proteins are likely present in other members of the Skunavirus genus that infect dairy-relevant Lactococcus strains. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TTP_17
comment: This entry represents a family of phage tail tube proteins from a variety of phage including Bxb1. These proteins form homohexameric rings. The tail tube forms the inner channel of the contractile tail which is used for DNA transfer from the capsid to the host during infection. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_Y01A
comment: This entry represents a family of small proteins found in T4-like bacteriophages. The function of these proteins is currently unknown. The proteins are approximately 12 kDa in size and are highly conserved across a wide range of phages that infect different bacterial hosts, including Enterobacteria, Acinetobacter, Shewanella, Klebsiella, and other Gram-negative bacteria. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins are composed of a small beta sheet of three strands packed with two alpha helices with an additional beta hairpin between the two helices. Structure prediction also suggests these proteins are likely to form homodimers. (from Pfam)

label: RamC_N
product_name: class III lanthionine synthetase LanKC N-terminal domain-containing protein
hmm_name: class III lanthionine synthetase LanKC N-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Probable SapB synthase from Streptomyces coelicolor (RamC), which is required for aerial hyphae formation. It shows an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: SF0329
comment: This family is named for SF0329 (A0A384KI17) from Shigella flexneri. Full length homologs of SF0329 are found in hundreds of bacterial species. Note that the first 10 and last 17 amino acids of its 151 amino acid length perfectly match a 27 amino acid translation from Escherichia coli K-12 (Swiss:P0DPN2) that was mistaken for a small functional protein and named YkiD. We suggest that YkiD is nonfunctional remnant, and that the name YkiD should not be used. (from Pfam)

label: crAss_AuxCP
comment: This entry represents the auxiliary capsid protein found in Bacteroides phage crAss001. This protein forms an outer layer on the major capsid protein protrusions and is present in 535 copies in the virion. The central region (amino acids 75-237) is structurally similar to Helicobacter pylori flagellar cap protein FliD and is involved in interactions with the major capsid protein. (from Pfam)

label: crAss_CARG1
comment: This entry represents cargo protein 1 (C1) found in crassviruses. This protein is unique in that different portions of it are found in both the capsid and the tail of the virion. This entry represents residues 425-552 that fold into a compact domain that is bound to the portal protein wing domain inside the capsid, with 12 such segments interdigitating with wing loops (SH3-like domains) of the portal. Additionally, 12 copies of an alpha-helical segment of the same protein (residues 214-245) are located at the inner surface of the first and second rings of the tail barrel. A transmembrane helix is predicted in the N-terminal region (residues 136-158), which may insert into the host cell membrane. The presence of cargo protein 1 in both the capsid and tail suggests a mechanism for protein ejection prior to complete ejection of genomic DNA, likely involving partial unfolding of the protein as it is extruded through the tail. Cargo protein 1 is believed to be ejected in the N to C direction, with the N-terminal part located in the tail exiting first, followed by the C-terminal domain located in the capsid. This protein likely contributes to the formation of a transmembrane channel for DNA ejection. The protein is broadly conserved among crassviruses, although members of the epsilon group lack a detectable homologue (PMID: 37138077). (from Pfam)

label: T4_Spackle
comment: This entry represents the Spackle protein encoded by the early gene 61.3 of bacteriophage T4. Spackle is a periplasmic protein that plays a crucial role in superinfection exclusion by inhibiting the lysozyme activity of tail lysozyme (gp5) of superinfecting phages, thereby preventing their DNA from entering the host cell. The protein consists of five alpha-helices forming a disc-like shape with an average thickness of approximately 15 Angstroms. A notable structural feature is the intramolecular disulfide bond formed between Cys29 and Cys81, which provides additional stability and is consistent with Spackle's localization in the oxidising environment of the bacterial periplasm. The protein has a strikingly bipolar charge distribution on its surface, suggesting a potential mechanism for membrane association. Spackle inhibits gp5 lysozyme through a dual mechanism: by obstructing substrate entry and by preventing substrate binding site closure. (from Pfam)

label: T4_Y13H
comment: This entry represents the uncharacterized Y13H (cd.5) protein found in Enterobacteria phage T4. The protein is encoded in the cd-pseT intergenic region of the phage genome. The function of this small 8.7 kDa protein remains unknown. It may play a role in phage replication or host interaction. (from Pfam)

label: T5_p143
product_name: Bacteriophage T5 tail completion protein p143
name_orig: Bacteriophage T5 tail completion protein p143
hmm_name: Bacteriophage T5 tail completion protein p143
comment: This entry represents the tail completion protein p143 found in bacteriophage T5. Unlike typical tail completion proteins that are located at the head-tail joining region, p143 is found at the base of only one BHP pb3 monomer in the T5 tail tip. This protein appears to have a role in tail stability and may detach during the infection process. Cryo-EM structural studies have shown that this protein is absent from reconstructions of the tip after interaction with the bacterial receptor FhuA, suggesting a potential role in the infection mechanism. (from Pfam)

label: crAss_CARGO2
comment: This entry represents cargo protein 2, a protein stored in high quantity within bacteriophage capsids. This protein likely plays an important role during the phage infection process, particularly during genome ejection. Cargo proteins are packaged inside the viral capsid and are delivered to the host cell during infection, where they may assist in forming transmembrane channels for DNA ejection or perform other functions necessary for successful infection. Cargo protein 2 is present in 12 copies in the virion and has been detected in the capsid of Bacteroides phage crAss001, one of the most abundant bacteriophages in the human gut microbiome. The precise molecular function of this protein remains to be fully elucidated, but its conservation and abundance suggest it plays a critical role in the phage life cycle. (from Pfam)

label: crAss_THA
comment: This entry represents the tail hub protein A (THA) found in bacteriophages. The protein forms a heterotrimer with tail hub protein B (THB), with each assembly consisting of two copies of THA and one copy of THB (Pfam:PF25711). These heterotrimers further assemble as 12 docking hubs that form a continuous collar around the tail barrel. The docking hubs interact with the trimeric tail fiber protein, accommodating its N-terminal region. THA forms disulfide bonds with THB and with the ring proteins of the tail barrel, contributing to the stability of the tail assembly. The tail hub proteins play an important structural role in phage architecture, serving as the attachment point for the tail fiber appendages that are involved in host recognition. THA has been structurally characterized in the Bacteroides phage crAss001, revealing its role in the architecture of the phage tail (PMID: 37138077). (from Pfam)

label: AAA_lid_14
comment: This entry represents the alpha helical AAA+ lid domain that is found to the C-terminus of AAA domains. (from Pfam)

label: Arm_PDR
comment: This entry represents the Armadillo/beta-catenin-like (ARM) repeat, a specific subclass of alpha-helical solenoid domains. ARM repeats are composed of tandem three-helix bundles that form a superhelical structure, primarily facilitating protein-protein interactions (PMID: 9770300). ARM repeats are predominantly found in plastid division regulators (PDR), where they play a crucial role in the coordination and regulation of plastid division in plants (PMID: 28248291). Proteins containing this domain include ARC6 and CDP1, both of which contribute to the proper assembly and stabilization of the FtsZ ring, a key component of the plastid division machinery. ARC6 facilitates FtsZ ring assembly and promotes the recruitment of MCD1, which is essential for forming the chloroplast Z-ring. CDP1, on the other hand, is required for the localisation of PDV1 and the correct formation of the FtsZ ring in non green plastids (PMID: 23936263). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7925
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins predominantly from cyanobacteria. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich. Some members are likely to contain an isopeptide bond. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7934
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in Bacillota species. From genomic context it is likely to be a phage derived protein. It contains a helical domain composed of segments from the N-terminus and C-terminus connected by a coiled coil region. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7940
comment: This family contains a set of uncharacterised bacterial and phage proteins that are annotated as putative holins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7947
comment: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found at the C-terminus of a set of bacterial and phage proteins. It forms small five stranded beta barrel domain. (from Pfam)

label: Gad1
comment: This entry represents the Gabija anti-defense 1 (Gad1) protein family, which is encoded by bacteriophages to counteract the bacterial Gabija anti-phage defense system. Gad1 forms an octameric web that encases the Gabija GajAB complex, blocking its ability to bind and cleave phage DNA. The relatively large size of Gad1 (35 kDa) allows it to form multiple interaction interfaces with the host defense complex. Structural studies show that Gad1 contains distinctive fist, arm and shoulder domains that work together to inhibit GajA nuclease activity. The interaction between Gad1 and GajAB enables phages to overcome this widespread bacterial defense system. (from Pfam)

label: GldB_lipo
comment: This entry represents the GldB protein family, a component of the bacterial gliding motility machinery. GldB is required for gliding motility in Flavobacterium johnsoniae and related bacteria. The protein appears to be anchored to the cell membrane and is thought to be part of the gliding motility complex, though its precise molecular function remains to be determined. GldB works in concert with other Gld proteins to enable the unique form of bacterial surface movement known as gliding motility. This protein is distantly related to zincin type proteins although it lacks the characteristic zinc binding motif. (from Pfam)

label: LIP-1
comment: This entry describes the dimeric coiled coil (CC2) found in liprin-alpha proteins mainly from animals. Liprin-alpha family proteins are core synaptic scaffolds and important for the assembly and maturation of synapses (PMID: 33761347). The CC2 domain is located after the coiled coil domain 1 (CC1). The long CC2 coiled coils are toward the outside of this CC1 oligomer, making them accessible for recognition by presynaptic binding partners of liprin-alpha, such as ELKS and RIM (PMID: 33761347). This domain is usually found associated with Pfam:PF00536 and Pfam:PF07647. (from Pfam)

label: LRV_2
comment: This entry represents a likely small cytoplasmic domain found a a small set of bacterial integral membrane proteins. This domain is composed of a couple of leucine rich repeat variant repeats. The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Lysostaphin_N
comment: This entry represents a domain found toward the N-terminal end of Lysostaphin from Staphylococcus simulans, an extracellular glycylglycine endopeptidase that lyses staphylococcal cells by hydrolysing the polyglycine interpeptide bridges of the peptidoglycan [1,2]. This domain contains a repeated semi-conserved SHxxV[ED] sequence motif usually separated by 7-8 amino acid residues. (from Pfam)

label: N4_GP8
comment: This entry represents a phage-encoded inhibitor of bacterial DNA replication. The protein is encoded by coliphage N4 and targets the host DNA sliding clamp by interacting with the delta subunit of the E. coli DNA polymerase III clamp loader. The protein inhibits replication elongation and is bacteriostatic. N4 gp8 specifically interferes with DNAP III processivity by interacting with the E. coli DNAP III delta subunit and inhibiting clamp loading. This represents a novel target in the bacterial replisome for inhibition of bacterial growth. (from Pfam)

label: P22_gp7
product_name: Bacteriophage P22 DNA ejection protein gp7
name_orig: Bacteriophage P22 DNA ejection protein gp7
hmm_name: Bacteriophage P22 DNA ejection protein gp7
comment: This entry represents the bacteriophage P22 DNA ejection protein gp7. This protein is one of three ejection proteins (along with gp16 and gp20) that are required to facilitate transport of bacteriophage P22 double-stranded DNA safely through membranes of Salmonella (PMID: 29590587). These ejection proteins are lost from the virion and are presumed to be released with the DNA during ejection. Cryo-EM studies of empty P22 particles show a tube-like structure extending from the centre of the tail assembly that is likely composed of these ejection proteins. The specific functions of gp7 in this process are not fully understood, but they appear to be involved in forming a conduit for the transport of DNA into the host cytoplasm, possibly through the outer membrane, peptidoglycan layer, periplasmic space, and inner membrane. (from Pfam)

label: P3_C
comment: The P3 major capsid protein adopts a 'double-sandwich' structure comprising two eight-stranded viral beta-sandwich domains with jellyroll fold, each of which contains a 12-residue alpha-helix. This protein trimerises through a 'trimerisation loop' sequence, and is incorporated within the viral capsid (PMID: 11752778). This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the P3 protein. (from Pfam)

label: PTPase
comment: This entry represents the Phosphotyrosine Protein Phosphatase PTPase domain from plant proteins and related sequences. While it shares limited sequence similarity with known plant protein tyrosine phosphatase PTPs (such as AtPTP1 in Arabidopsis), its conserved structural features suggest a related Phosphotyrosine function (PMID: 26962298). Unlike classical PTPs, part of a well-defined family, PTPases may include enzymes that are not structurally related but still can dephosphorylate Phosphotyrosine. Given the crucial role of tyrosine phosphorylation in plant embryogenesis, seed germination, and plastid development, this domain may play a role in these processes [2-3]. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_T3_1_05
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in Enterobacteria phage T3. The function of this small phage protein is currently unknown. It is encoded by gene 1.05 of bacteriophage T3. Structure prediction suggests that this region forms a compact domain composed of 6 beta strands that form a small beta sandwich. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_T7_Gp5_9
comment: This entry represents a phage protein domain that acts as a DNA mimic to inhibit the bacterial RecBCD complex. The T7 gp5.9 protein adopts a parallel coiled-coil architecture with an N-terminal beta-sheet. The protein's highly acidic surface mimics DNA structure, allowing it to compete with DNA for the binding site on RecBCD. By binding predominantly to the RecB arm domain, gp5.9 prevents RecBCD from binding to DNA, thereby protecting the phage genome from degradation. This inhibitory mechanism is functionally similar to lambda phage Gam protein, though structurally distinct. Low nanomolar concentrations of gp5.9 are sufficient to inhibit RecBCD helicase activity in vitro. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_VG64
comment: This small phage protein is predicted to be a lipoprotein. Members of this family are found in a range of caudoviruses that infect mycobacteria and bacilli. Structure prediction shows that it forms small 6 stranded beta sandwich domain. Structure prediction suggests that this protein can form a homo-nonameric complex, which shows a flat disk like structure. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_depo_C
product_name: Phage depolymerase C-terminal beta sandwich domain
name_orig: Phage depolymerase C-terminal beta sandwich domain
hmm_name: Phage depolymerase C-terminal beta sandwich domain
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal beta sandwich domain found in bacteriophage-encoded depolymerases that target bacterial capsular polysaccharides. These enzymes are often components of phage tail spikes or tail fibers and enable phages to attach to and degrade bacterial capsules, particularly in Klebsiella species. The domain is found in phages with dual host specificity where each phage encodes two different capsule depolymerases with specificity for different capsular types. The domain is C-terminal to a pectin lyase-like fold with enzymatic activity that cleaves bacterial capsular polysaccharides into oligosaccharides. (from Pfam)

label: PhiKZ_VTX
comment: This entry represents the vertex-binding protein gp28 from jumbo bacteriophage PhiKZ that infects Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This alpha-helical protein functions as a component of the vertex-binding complex attached to the inner surface of the viral capsid. Gp28 forms a sandwich structure along with gp85 dimer and gp119 at the centre of the vertex-binding complex. Neighbouring vertex-binding complexes connect via interactions between gp28 from one complex and gp91/gp119 from an adjacent complex. This protein plays an important role in capsid assembly and stabilization by reinforcing the associations between the pentameric capsomer and the five hexameric capsomers encircling the vertex. Similar proteins are found in other jumbo phages, suggesting a conserved mechanism for capsid assembly and stabilization in large viruses. (from Pfam)

label: PhiKZ_gp91
comment: This entry represents the vertex-binding protein gp91 from jumbo bacteriophage PhiKZ that infects Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This alpha-helical protein is a component of the vertex-binding complex attached to the inner surface of the viral capsid. Gp91 extends towards the capsid vertex and, unlike other members of the vertex-binding complex that primarily interact with hexameric capsomer 1, gp91 mainly interacts with the pentameric capsomer via hydrophobic interactions and several salt bridges. It forms an important bridge between the vertex-binding complex and the pentameric capsomer. Gp91 also interacts with gp119, which in turn interacts with hexameric capsomer 1, thereby connecting the pentameric capsomer and hexameric capsomer 1. Neighbouring vertex-binding complexes are connected via interactions between gp28 from one complex and gp91 from an adjacent complex. This protein plays a critical role in stabilizing the capsid vertex by directly binding to the pentameric capsomer. Similar proteins are found in other jumbo phages, suggesting a conserved mechanism for capsid assembly and stabilization in large viruses. (from Pfam)

label: TPR
comment: This domain is found in Nuclear-pore anchor from Arabidopsis thaliana (NUA) and similar eukaryotic proteins. NUA, a component of the nuclear pore complex, acts as a docking site for activities required for desumoylation and mRNA export. It is required for the proper expression or localisation of a subset of miRNAs. This domain is often found associated with Pfam:PF07926 and is predicted to adopt an all-alpha structure. (from Pfam)

label: crAss_PVA
comment: This entry represents the portal vertex auxiliary protein found in bacteriophages. This protein forms a homodimer stabilized by disulfide bonds between residues 25-88 and 47-47 of the two subunits. It is localized at the portal vertex of the viral capsid, with two copies per virion. The protein interacts with the major capsid protein and substitutes for the capsid auxiliary protein at the portal vertex. The portal vertex auxiliary protein has been structurally characterized in the Bacteroides phage crAss001, where it plays an important role in the assembly and stability of the portal-containing vertex of the viral capsid. (from Pfam)

label: T9SS_PorZ
product_name: type IX secretion system anionic LPS delivery protein PorZ
hmm_name: type IX secretion system anionic LPS delivery protein PorZ
comment: PorZ participates in type IX secretion systems (T9SS) by furnishing anionic lipopolysaccharide to the transpeptidase PorU. At the C-terminus, PorZ itself has a type A domain for recognition and processing by T9SS.

label: Arg_dihydro
comment: In species (primarily Cyanobacteria) that produce the arginine-containing storage molecule cyanophycin, an ammonia-freeing catabolic pathway of arginine to proline is often found. This HMM describes sequence regions with arginine dihydrolase activity, typically seen as the N-terminal half of a bifunctional protein (called ArgZ or ArgE) that contains a C-terminal ornithine cyclodeaminase domain. Arginine dihydrolase uses two water molecules for hydrolysis and releases two ammonia molecules.

label: antitox_spr1629
comment: Members of this family of XRE-like transcriptional repressors, including spr1629 from Streptococcus pneumoniae, are encoded in a two-gene locus together with a homolog of spr1630, a protein revealed as a toxin lethal to the host bacterium in ClpX mutants. This conserved pairing suggests that members the spr1630 family, and of this family, act as a toxin-antitoxin system, and likely participate in some sort of regulatory network that provides some benefit to the cell.

label: transferase_LuxD
product_name: fatty acid reductase transferase subunit LuxD
hmm_name: fatty acid reductase transferase subunit LuxD

label: luciferase_Alph
comment: LuxA and LuxB, closely related paralogs, are the catalytic and helper subunits, respectively, of an FMN-dependent alkanal monooxygenase called luciferase because of its role in bacterial bioluminescence.

label: luciferase_Beta
comment: LuxA and LuxB, closely related paralogs, are the catalytic and helper subunits, respectively, of an FMN-dependent alkanal monooxygenase called luciferase because of its role in bacterial bioluminescence.

label: lmo0954_fam
comment: Members of this family are strongly hydrophobic through the length of the region covered by this HMM. Most but not all members have an additional C-terminal 20 amino acids with motifs containing both charged and aromatic amino acids.

label: PLP_TF_PdxR
product_name: MocR-like pyridoxine biosynthesis transcription factor PdxR
hmm_name: MocR-like pyridoxine biosynthesis transcription factor PdxR

label: ecto_TF_EhuR
product_name: MocR-like ectoine utilization transcription factor EhuR
hmm_name: MocR-like ectoine utilization transcription factor EhuR

label: T9SS_PorT_SprT
product_name: type IX secretion/gliding motility protein PorT/SprT
hmm_name: type IX secretion/gliding motility protein PorT/SprT

label: T9SS_PorW_SprE
product_name: type IX secretion system periplasmic lipoprotein PorW/SprE
hmm_name: type IX secretion system periplasmic lipoprotein PorW/SprE
comment: Proteins original identified as PorW in P. gingivalis and SprE in F. johnsoniae, homologous through much of their lengths, are the equivalent periplasmic lipoprotein of their shared type IX secretion system (T9SS). In species with gliding motility, such as F. johnsoniae, PorW/SprE is considered a gliding motililty, since that capability depends on a functional T9SS.

label: T9SS_plug
product_name: type IX secretion system plug protein
hmm_name: type IX secretion system plug protein

label: arylmal_decarb
comment: Arylmalonate decarboxylases are (EC 4.1.1.76) are a family of enzymes that perform decarboxylations on a number of related malonic acid derivatives. By homology, these enzymes belong to the larger aspartate/glutamate racemase superfamily. This HMM identifies members of one clade of arylmalonate decarboxylases.

label: ATPase_TcpF
comment: TcpF is one of two ATPases in the eleven-gene transfer clostridial plasmid (TCP) system for conjugal transfer of DNA in the Clostridium perfringens tetracycline resistance plasmid pCW3.

label: AggPromo_Cterm
comment: This HMM describes a region found at the C-terminal domain of aggregation-promoting factor (APF) as found in Lactobacillus. The region is called distantly related to recuscitation-promotiing factors.

label: ISCR_clade_Ia
product_name: ISCR element clade Ia family transposase
hmm_name: ISCR element clade Ia family transposase

label: YabN_Meth_PPase
comment: YabN, as found in Bacillus subtilis, is a fusion protein with an N-terminal tetrapyrrole methyltransferase-like domain and a C-terminal nucleoside triphosphate pyrophosphohydrolase-like domain. The function is not known.

label: PknI_Rv2253
comment: This domain occurs twice in protein of the model bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv, once in the minimally characterized secreted protein Rv2253, covering most of its length, and once as the C-terminal, extracellular sensor domain of serine/threonine protein kinase PknI (Rv2914c).

label: MBOE_33420_fam
comment: Members of this family are full-length homologs of the Sec-dependent membrane protein Rv2253 of Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv, and homologous to the the C-terminal, extracellular sensor domain of serine/threonine protein kinase PknI (Rv2914c).

label: TIGR_Tas_endo
comment: The RNA-guided endonuclease Tas, with distinctive but related forms designated TasA, TasH, and TasR, acts as an RNA-guided endonuclease. Tandem repeats may be found next to the tas gene, although the number of repeats may be small. Tas resembles the RNA-guided DNA transposase IS110.

label: BA5345_fam
comment: The founding member of this family, BA5345 from Bacillus anthracis, occurs in a prophage region, and is uncharacterized. Related proteins are broadly distributed in bacteria.

label: methyltran_MpqE
comment: MpqE, a methyltransferase, is responsible for methylation at the C2-position of the distinctive trimethyl-benzoquinone headgroup of methyl-plastoquinone, widespread in but restricted to the Nitrospirota.

label: NPN_LarAH10
comment: The nickel-pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor-dependent isomerases in this family, called LarAH10, have been shown to act on a varienty of hydrophobic 2-hydroxyacids such as 3-phenyllactate, and to perform the epimerization that interconverts D-gluconate and D-mannonate.

label: ODC_var
comment: Members of this family represent an out group to the nickel-pincer nucleotide cofactor (NPN)-dependent ornithine cyclodeaminase described in HMM TIGR00300. The NPN in several members of TIGR00300 was shown to contain adenine, rather than the cytosine of the NPN in lactate racemase and related isomerases. As several members of this family are located near arginase enzymes, which produce ornithine from arginine, it seems possible that this family likewise behaves as an ornithine cyclodeaminase. This family is unrelated to the ornithine cyclodeaminases of family NF005762.

label: LhaT_LP_ac_tran
comment: LhaT (Lipoprotein Heptaprenylglyceryl Acetyl Transferase), an integral membrane protein widespread at least in the genus Bacillus, is performs an extracellular N-acetyltransferase modification to the amino group of the Cys residue at the N-terminus of processed lipopropteins.

label: LarAH_14_15_16
comment: This HMM describes groups 14, 15, and 16 of a set of nickel pincer nucleotide cofactor-dependent enzymes related that are lactate racemase homologs (LarAH), as described in PMID:33093595. They are considered likely to act as racemases or epimerases of various 2-hydroxyacids, but specific substrates are unknown.

label: NPN_18_hexonate
hmm_name: nickel-dependent putative hexonate epimerase, LarAH18 family
comment: Members of this family, closely related to a proven gluconate epimerase clade, are nickel-pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor-dependent isomerases like to act as epimerases on a gluconate-related compound. The family was described as group 18 in PMID:33093595.

label: macro_16_ester
comment: Members of this family belong to the alpha/beta fold hydrolase superfamily, and act on 16-member ring macrolides such as tylosin. Members of this family include EstX, EstT, MleBCA, MleBCB, MleBRB, MlePBB, MleCBF, and MlePBA.

label: slr1658_cyano
comment: This family represents a clade within the broader superfamily described by model NF047703. Knockout of slr1658 multiple changes in gene expression, including of proteins required for proper recovery from iron starvation, but the mechanism of its action is not yet known.

label: Npun_F2552_fam
comment: This well-resolved clade of DUF362 domain-containing protein appears to be restricted to the Cyanobacteria and present in at least 85 percent of cyanobacterial species. While the function is not known, proximity to genes for a TLTLP motif-containing small probable membrane protein (NF052624) and for the structural RNA NsiR4 (nitrogen stress-induced RNA 4 - see Rfam entry RF02677) is observed in more than a quarter of species.

label: PQLLE_fam
comment: Members of this family are found sporadically in the Bacteroidota, often as small paralogous families, although with over 30 paralogs in Catalinimonas niigatensis. The family is named for the motif PQLLE found near the C-terminus in most but not all members of the family. The function is unknown.

label: CPF_0552_fam
comment: CPF_0552 from Clostridium perfringens ATCC 13124 and TM0179 from Thermotoga maritima MSB8 are members of this family of possible transcription factors. In contrast to members of the related family TIGR03959 ( iron-only hydrogenase system putative regulator"), members of the family have two nearly invariant Cys residues, suggesting the presence of a disulfide bond.

label: YPYG_dom
comment: This domain is found typically as the C-terminal domain of a longer protein that often is a lipoprotein and often contains a PASTA domain (PF03793).

label: nitric_RR_NosR
product_name: response regulator c-di-GMP phosphodiesterase, NosR family
hmm_name: response regulator c-di-GMP phosphodiesterase, NosR family
comment: The founding member of this family, NosR from Burkholderia pseudomallei, occurs in the context of nitric oxide-binding protein NosP and histidine kinase NosK, but most members do not. The effector (output) HD-GYP domain of this response regulator acts by cleaving a second messenger, probably c-di-GMP, rather than by binding specific target DNA in order to behave as a transcription factor. BlastRule NBR017547 describes actual NosR response regulator proteins, while this HMM describes a broader family of regulatory proteins with conserved architecture and high sequence similarity.

label: rpmI_bact
comment: This ribosomal protein is found in bacteria and organelles only. It is not closely related to any eukaryotic or archaeal ribosomal protein.

label: S16
comment: This model describes ribosomal S16 of bacteria and organelles. S16 binds to lower part of 30S body where it stabilizes two domains; required for efficient assembly of 30S. In Escherichia coli this protein has nuclease activity

label: infA
comment: This family consists of translation initiation factor IF-1 as found in bacteria and chloroplasts. This protein, about 70 residues in length, consists largely of an S1 RNA binding domain (PF00575).

label: L28
comment: This HMM describes bacterial and chloroplast forms of the 50S ribosomal protein L28, a polypeptide about 60 amino acids in length. Mitochondrial homologs differ substantially in architecture (e.g. SP|P36525 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which is 258 amino acids long) and are not included.

label: arsC
comment: This HMM describes a distinct clade, including ArsC itself, of the broader ArsC family described by Pfam PF03960. This clade is almost completely restricted to the Proteobacteria. An anion-translocating ATPase has been identified as the product of the arsenical resistance operon of resistance plasmid R773. When expressed in Escherichia coli this ATP-driven oxyanion pump catalyses extrusion of the oxyanions arsenite, antimonite and arsenate. The pump is composed of two polypeptides, the products of the arsA and arsB genes. The pump alone produces resistance to arsenite and antimonite. This protein, ArsC, catalyzes the reduction of arsenate to arsenite, and thus extends resistance to include arsenate. Some ArsC proteins are selenoproteins. This arsenate reductase requires both glutathione and glutaredoxin to convert arsenate to arsenite, after which the efflux transporter formed by ArsA and ArsB can extrude the arsenite from the cell, providing resistance.

label: cmk
comment: This family consists of cytidylate kinase, which catalyzes the phosphorylation of cytidine 5-monophosphate (dCMP) to cytidine 5 -diphosphate (dCDP) in the presence of ATP or GTP. UMP and dCMP can also act as acceptors.

label: panC
comment: This type of pantothenate synthetase, EC 6.3.2.1, is found in bacteria, and is unrelated to an archaeal form, EC 6.3.2.44 (see PRK13761).

label: prfA
comment: This HMM describes peptide chain release factor 1 (PrfA, RF-1), and excludes the related peptide chain release factor 2 (PrfB, RF-2). RF-1 helps recognize and terminate translation at UAA and UAG stop codons. The mitochondrial release factors are prfA-like, although not included above the trusted cutoff for this model. RF-1 does not have a translational frameshift.

label: prfB
comment: The bacterial peptide chain release factor 2 (RF-2), product of the prfB gene, recognizes the stop codons UGA and UAA during protein translation, and it is the only release factor to recognize UGA. In about 80 percent of known bacterial species, a +1 frameshift must occur at a UGA stop codon about 25 amino acids from the N-terminus, or translation is aborted by a premature termination. RF-2 can therefore regulate its own production by readthrough only when RF-2 is insufficient.

label: TIGR00022
comment: This family consists of conserved hypothetical proteins, about 150 amino acids in length. Members with limited information include YhcH, a possible sugar isomerase of sialic acid catabolism, and YjgK.

label: TIGR00023
comment: This HMM represents the full length of acylphosphate:glycerol 3-phosphate acyltransferase, and integral membrane protein about 200 amino acids in length, called PlsY in Streptococcus pneumoniae, YneS in Bacillus subtilis, and YgiH in E. coli. It is found in a single copy in a large number of bacteria, including the Mycoplasmas but not Mycobacteria or spirochetes, for example. Its partner is PlsX (see TIGR00182), and the pair can replace PlsB for synthesizing 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate.

label: hi_GC_TIGR00026
comment: This model represents a family of proteins found in paralogous families in the genera Mycobacterium and Streptomyces. Seven members are in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Member protein Rv3547 has been characterized as a deazaflavin-dependent nitroreductase.

label: Mtu_PIN_fam
product_name: TA system VapC family ribonuclease toxin
hmm_name: TA system VapC family ribonuclease toxin
comment: Members of this family are VapC proteins that consist almost entirely of a PIN (PilT N terminus) domain. This family was originally defined a set of twelve closely related paralogs found in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, but additional members are found now Synechococcus sp. WH8102, etc. This family includes ribonucleases VapC24 and Vap25 among others. They are the toxic component of a toxin-antitoxin (TA) module. They act as an RNase and all their toxic effects are neutralised by coexpression with cognate antitoxin

label: S20
comment: This family consists of bacterial (and chloroplast) examples of the bacteria ribosomal small subunit protein S20.

label: S21p
comment: This HMM describes bacterial ribosomal protein S21 and most mitochondrial and chloroplast equivalents.

label: aroFGH
comment: 3-deoxy-7-phosphoheptulonate synthase is involved in the biosynthesis of chorismate, the final common intermediate in the biosynthesis of phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan (the aromatic amino acids) as well as menaquinone, ubiquinone, and other products. Three isozymes in E. coli K-12 are designated AroF, AroG, and AroH.

label: efp
comment: Elongation factor P (EF-P) alleviates stalling of protein translation at polyproline sites. EF-P (and its archaeal and eukaryotic homologs) are post-translationally modified, on a critical lysine or arginine residue, in different ways in different lineages. Residues are modified with beta-lysine, rhamnose, 5-aminopentanol, or hypusine. The trusted cutoff of this model is set high enough to exclude members of TIGR02178, the EFP-like protein YeiP found in certain Gammaproteobacteria.

label: 6PTHBS
comment: Members of this family from animals are known to be 6-pyruvoyl tetrahydropterin synthase (EC 4.2.3.12). Bacterial members are 6-carboxytetrahydropterin synthase (EC4.1.2.50), QueD, an enzyme of queuosine biosynthesis. Queuosine is a hypermodified base in the wobble position of some tRNAs in most species. See TIGR03367 for a QueD equivalog model.

label: TIGR00043
comment: This metalloprotein family is represented by a single member sequence only in nearly every bacterium. Crystallography demonstrated metal-binding activity, possibly to nickel. It is a predicted to be a metallohydrolase, and more recently it was shown that mutants have a ribosomal RNA processing defect.

label: TIGR00045
comment: Members of this family include at least two different enzymes, the glycerate 3-kinase GlxK (EC 2.7.1.31) and the glycerate 2-kinase GarK (EC 2.7.1.165), both of which can be found in Escherichia coli K-12.

label: TIGR00046
comment: Members of this protein family, previously called conserved hypothetical protein TIGR00046, include the YggJ protein of E. coli, which has now been shown to methylate U1498 in 16S rRNA.

label: TIGR00052
comment: Members of this family include proteins of about 200 amino acids, including the recently characterized nudix hydrolase YffH, shows to be highly active as a GDP-mannose pyrophosphatase. It also includes the C-terminal half of a 361-amino acid protein, TrgB from Rhodobacter sphaeroides, shown experimentally to help confer tellurite resistance. This HMM also hits a region near the C-terminus of a 1092-amino acid protein of C. elegans.

label: TIGR00053
name_orig: addiction module toxin component, YafQ family
comment: This HMM represents a cluster of eubacterial proteins and a cluster of archaeal proteins, all of which are uncharacterized, from 85 to 102 residues in length, and similar in sequence. These include YafQ, a ribosome-associated endoribonuclease that serves as part of a toxin-antitoxin system, for which DinJ is the antidote component.

label: TIGR00054
comment: Members of this nearly universal bacterial protein family are regulated intramembrane proteolysis (RIP) proteases. Older and synonymous gene symbols include yaeL in E. coli, mmpA in Caulobacter crescentus, etc. This family includes a region that hits the PDZ domain, found in a number of proteins targeted to the membrane by binding to a peptide ligand. The N-terminal region of this family contains a perfectly conserved motif HEXGH as found in a number of metalloproteinases, where the Glu is the active site and the His residues coordinate the metal cation. Membership in this family is determined by an HMM built to force a match to the full length of the seed alignment. A model that detects fragments as well matches a number of members of the PEPTIDASE FAMILY S2C. The region of match appears not to overlap the active site domain.

label: TIGR00056
product_name: MlaE family lipid ABC transporter permease subunit
hmm_name: MlaE family lipid ABC transporter permease subunit
comment: This HMM describes a subfamily of ABC transporter permease subunits. One member of this family has been associated with the toluene tolerance phenotype of Pseudomonas putida, another with L-glutamate transport, another with maintenance of lipid asymmetry. Many bacterial species have one or two members. The Mycobacteria have large paralogous families included in the DUF140 family but excluded from this subfamily on based on extreme divergence at the amino end and on phylogenetic and UPGMA trees on the more conserved regions.

label: L17
comment: The bacterial 50S ribosomal protein L17 is a component of the macrolide binding site in the peptidyl transferase center.

label: L18_bact
comment: The archaeal and eukaryotic type rpL18 is not detectable under this model.

label: L21
comment: Eubacterial and chloroplast.

label: L27
comment: Involved in the peptidyltransferase reaction during translation.

label: glyox_I
comment: Lactoylglutathione lyase is also known as aldoketomutase and glyoxalase I. Glyoxylase I is a homodimer in many species. In some eukaryotes, including yeasts and plants, the orthologous protein carries a tandem duplication, is twice as long, and hits this HMM twice.

label: rbfA
comment: RbfA is a ribosome biogenesis protein involved in the processing of 16S rRNA.

label: smpB
comment: This model describes the SsrA-binding protein, also called tmRNA binding protein, small protein B, and SmpB. The small, stable RNA SsrA (also called tmRNA or 10Sa RNA) recognizes stalled ribosomes such as occur during translation from message that lacks a stop codon. It becomes charged with Ala like a tRNA, then acts as mRNA to resume translation started with the defective mRNA. The short C-terminal peptide tag added by the SsrA system marks the abortively translated protein for degradation.
