hmm_name: OXA-46 family oxacillin-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase
comment: Members of this family are narrow-spectrum class D beta-lactamases that have a tendency to be mobilized and occur in class I integron cassettes. OXA-46 decreases susceptibility to penicillins and narrow-spectrum cephalosporins, but not carbapenems, aztreonam, or extended spectrum cephalosporins.

label: cmlA_floR
product_name: CmlA/FloR family chloramphenicol efflux MFS transporter
name_orig: CmlA/FloR family chloramphenicol efflux MFS transporter
hmm_name: CmlA/FloR family chloramphenicol efflux MFS transporter
comment: This HMM identifies a number of distinctly named MFS transporters that perform efflux of chloramphenicol sufficient to confer resistance. Because members of the family include proteins designated CmlA, CmlB, and FloR, the generic term cml is now attached to this HMM. Note that this model does not include the rare, related protein originally found in plasmid R26 in 1986 and named Cml. Previously, this HMM carried the gene symbol "bcr/cflA", which we now judge to be misleading.

label: lipo_LIC11139
comment: Members of this family are restricted to the genus Leptospira. They are putative lipoproteins with only a single Cys residue, invariant at the proposed lipoprotein signal cleavage site. Residues in the -1 position are unusual for lipoproteins in general, but consistent with observations in Leptospira, as described in PMID:26890609.

label: c_type_nonphoto
comment: Members of this family are apparent c-type cytochromes that resemble the photosynthetic reaction center c-type cytochrome (PF02276) but are smaller and found in non-photosynthetic organisms.

label: MonaBetaBRL_TX
comment: Members of this family are secreted in a water-soluble pro-toxin form, but undergo cleavage and oligomerization to form beta-barrel pore. The founding member of the family is monalysin from Pseudomonas entomophila. This family is built narrowly, and therefore excludes a set of pore-forming proteins (not necessarily toxins) from a eukaryote, Dictyostelium. Analogous (but perhaps not homologous) beta-type pore-forming toxins include aerolysin and leukocidin.

label: T6SS_PAAR_dom
product_name: type VI secretion system PAAR protein
name_orig: type VI secretion system PAAR protein
hmm_name: type VI secretion system PAAR domain
comment: The PAAR domain is widespread, but this model represents a narrow clade that may occur in type VI secretion systems (T6SS), either free-standing or fused to a long extension. Effector domains of T6SS may be separate proteins, or may be fused to on of the tube or spike proteins: VgrG (spike), Hcp (tube), or this PAAR family (spike tip). Members of this family that have long extensions are likely to be T6SS effectors.

label: Lacal_2735_fam
comment: This small protein is widespread but uncharacterized. Most members are shorter than 60 amino acids in length.

label: Sul4
comment: Sul4 is a dihydropteroate synthase that is insensitive to, and provides resistance to, the antibiotic sulfonamide. It appears to be mobilized, but was discovered through functional metagenomics, and has not yet been seen in a cultured bacterial isolate.

label: floc_PepA
comment: PepA was described in Zoogloea resiniphila as a PEP-CTERM protein regulated by the PrsK/PrsR two-component system. Knocking out that system blocks flocculation, after which expression of recombinant PepA can restore flocculation.

label: MerTP_fusion
comment: MerTP is a transport protein for the mercuric ion, Hg(II). Once imported to the cytosol, the highly toxic ion can be converted by MerA, mercury(II) reductase, to the less toxic Hg atom.

label: acid_disulf_rpt
comment: The acidic double-disulfide repeat is an Asp-rich repeat with four nearly invariant Cys residues in a repeat length of about 35 amino acids.

label: stress_OB_fold
comment: Members of this family possess an N-terminal signal peptide, and are associated with tolerance to various toxic stresses. These include antimicrobial peptides (YdeI), hydrogen peroxide (YgiW and YdeI), and nickel (NcrY and NirD).

label: T9SS_sortase
product_name: type IX secretion system sortase PorU
name_orig: type IX secretion system sortase PorU
hmm_name: type IX secretion system sortase PorU
comment: PorU, part of type IX secretion systems (T9SS), is the protease responsible for both removing the C-terminal sorting signal found in substrates and for its replacement by anionic LPS, through which most T9SS substrates become attached to the cell surface after secretion.

label: T9SS_Cterm_ChiA
product_name: T9SS sorting signal type C domain-containing protein
name_orig: T9SS sorting signal type C domain-containing protein
comment: The sorting signals of type IX secretion systems (T9SS) in the CFB bacteria are long, compared to other prokaryotic C-terminal sorting motif-containing signals, including LPXTG, PEP-CTERM, and GlyGly-TERM, and they seem to contain multiple motifs. A few T9SS substrates, including ChiA, have a variant form of T9SS sorting signal that may score poorly to both TIGR04183 (type A) and TIGR04131 (type B), depend on T9SS for secretion, but are released from the cell rather than left anchored to the cell surface.

label: PorV_fam
comment: Proteins closely related to PorV, and its paralog PorQ, are found regularly in species with type IX secretion systems (T9SS), the system associated with a type of gliding motility in many of the Bacteroidetes.

label: T9SS_PorQ

label: gliding_CglC
comment: CglC (cell contact-dependent gliding (or conditional gliding) motility protein C, also called adventurous gliding motility protein AgmO, is found in delta-proteobacterial species that exhibit a taxonomically restricted form of gliding motility.

label: gliding_GltC
comment: GltC is a soluble periplasmic protein required for a type of gliding motility found in certain social delta-proteobacteria, including the model species Myxococcus xanthus.

label: gliding_CglB
comment: CglB is an outer membrane lipoprotein required for A-motility in Myxococcus xanthus and other delta-proteobacteria. It is transferable between cells that have a compatible TraAB system, and was therefore named conditional (or cell contact-dependent) gliding motility protein B, or CglB.

label: gliding_GltE
product_name: adventurous gliding motility TPR repeat lipoprotein GltE
name_orig: adventurous gliding motility TPR repeat lipoprotein GltE
hmm_name: adventurous gliding motility TPR repeat lipoprotein GltE
comment: GltE (also called AglT) is a tetratricopeptide repeat protein with a lipoprotein signal peptide and a role in A-motility (adventurous gliding motility) in Myxococcus xanthus and other delta-proteobacteria.

label: exchanger_TraA
comment: TraA, together with its partner TraB, mediates a large scale exchange of outer membrane lipoproteins, and lipids, between closely related strains or clonally identical cells, certain delta-proteobacterial species such as Myxococcus xanthus. The exchange mechanism is likely to involve fusion of outer membrane, probably done to coordinate the social behaviors these bacteria display.

label: gliding_GltG
comment: GltG proteins, including the founding member MXAN_4867 from Myxococcus xanthus, occur in certain delta-proteobacteria and are involved in adventurous gliding (A-)motility. GltG has an N-terminal forkhead-associated (FHA) domain domain, often associated with signal transduction.

label: gliding_GltJ
comment: Adventurous gliding motility protein GltJ, also known as AgmX, occurs in delta-proteobacteria such as Myxococcus xanthus.

label: social_mot_Tgl
product_name: social motility TPR repeat lipoprotein Tgl
name_orig: social motility TPR repeat lipoprotein Tgl
hmm_name: social motility TPR repeat lipoprotein Tgl
comment: Social motility in delta-proteobacterial species such as Myxococcus xanthus depends on a type VI pilus, which in turn depends on assembly of the PilQ secretin complex. Tgl, a tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) outer membrane lipoprotein, is required for PilQ assembly.

label: exchanger_TraB
comment: TraB, as described originally in the delta-proteobacterium, is a protein with a C-terminal OmpA-like domain, and is encoded in an operon with TraA. Together TraAB make it possible for bacterial cells with close enough kinship to exchange outer membrane lipoproteins, such that certain motility defects in mutant cells can be corrected through the exchange. This exchange most likely involves membrane fusion events, as large amounts of lipid are also exchanged, and it is restricted by a bi-directional kin recognition requirement. Among wild-type cells, these exchanges likely help coordinate various social behaviors.

label: gliding_CglF
comment: CglF, as originally described in Myxococcus xanthus, is a gliding motility protein. It has the property that motility in a cglF loss mutant can be restored by close contact with compatible kin strains where cglF is wild type. The restoration of motility depends on bidirectional kinship recognition, which is mediated by TraAB and leads to exchange of outer membrane proteins and lipids. This cell contact requirement leads to the gene symbol, cglF, meaning conditional (or, cell contact-dependent) gliding F. This protein has also been called GltF.

label: exosort_XrtU_C
comment: The XrtU family of exosortases is marked by a distinctive C-terminal region, modeled by the exosort_XrtU_C hidden Markov model. Because members of the archaeosortase and exosortase family perform cleavage of target proteins, in pathways thought to lead to new covalent attachment at the C-terminus and surface anchoring, the XrtU C-terminal domain may indicate the presence of a novel anchoring chemistry.

label: selen_YedE_FdhT
comment: Members of this family are predicted multiple membrane-spanning proteins, and therefore thought likely to be transporters. It appears that all species whose genomes encode a member of this family produce selenocysteine-containing enzymes, typically formate dehydrogenase. The family member from Campylobacter jejuni was show to be essential for formate dehydrogenase (a selenocysteine-containing enzyme) expression and activity, and so it was named a formate dehydrogenase accessory protein, FdhT. Note that this family is related to (but distinct from) that of TIGR04112, which is similarly restricted to species with pathways for selenium incorporation.

label: Myxo_non_zincin
comment: Members of this family resemble the archaemetzincins, a mostly archaeal family of Zn-dependent metalloproteases, but it lacks the critical catalytic glutamate (E) in the signature motif HEXXH, within the longer pattern HEXXHXXGX3CX4CXMX17CXXC that defines the archaemetzincins. Members of this family are found in Myxococcus xanthus and related members of the Delta-proteobacteria.

label: antiphage_ZorA_1
comment: Proteins of this subfamily are putative H+ channel proteins, but it has been reported that they are also involved in anti-phage defense.

label: antiphage_ZorA_3
comment: Proteins of this subfamily are putative H+ channel proteins, but it has been reported that they are also involved in anti-phage defense.

label: opr_porin_1
comment: Proteins hit by this HMM model are members of the Opr family porins, which are mainly found in Pseudomonas and other Gram-negative bacteria with different substrates.

label: opr_proin_2
comment: Proteins hit by this HMM model are members of the Opr family porins, which are mainly found in Pseudomonas and other Gram-negative bacteria with different substrates.

label: DUF5329
comment: This is a bacterial family of proteins with unknown function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5339
comment: This is a family of unknown function that can be found mostly in Proteobacteria. Some of the family members are predicted to contain a coiled coil region. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5334
comment: This is a family of unknown function which can is found mainly in Proteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: His_Me_b4a2
product_name: Hpy99I family type II restriction endonuclease
comment: This domain is found in Hpy991 present in Helicobacter pylori. Hpy991 is a beta-beta-alpha-Me restriction endonuclease that recognizes the CGWCG target sequence and cleaves both DNA strands with a stagger that leads to 5'-recessed ends in the cleavage products. This domain is the first of two beta4-alpha2 repeats found after the N-terminal domain. The two repeats have low overall sequence similarity but readily identified by a structural comparison. Both repeats contain contains two CXXC motifs that map to the first beta-hairpin and the first alpha-helix. The four cysteine residues coordinate a structurally bound Zn2+ ion tetrahedrally. The major groove is in contact with the first repeat, with the beta-hairpin 2 inserting deeply into the groove (PMID: 19380375). (from Pfam). The prototype restriction enzyme for this family is found in Helicobacter pylori and recognizes the site CGWCG.

label: SH3_18
comment: This is an SH3 domain found in antirepressor proteins such as CarS from Myxococcus xanthus. CarS antirepressor recognizes and neutralizes its cognate repressors to turn on a photo-inducible promoter. CarS physically interacts with the MerR-type winged-helix DNA-binding domain of these repressors leading to activation of carB operon. Structural studies of CarS from M. Xanthus reveals a beta-barrel fold akin to that in SH3 domains. However, it diverges from the typical SH3 domain fold in the lengths and conformations of the connecting loops. Functional analysis reveal that SH3 domain-like fold in the antirepressor CasS, mimics operator DNA in sequestering the repressor DNA recognition helix to activate transcription (PMID: 20410074). (from Pfam)

label: DUF5618
comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5623
comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in proteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5440
comment: This is a family of unknown function found in bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: HMUD2
comment: 5-hmdU DNA kinase 2 from phages which phosphorylates 5-hydroxymethyluracil (5hmdU) into 5-phosphomethyl-2'-deoxyuridine (5-PmdU) on DNA as a step in the pathway leading to thymidine hypermodifications in the viral genome [1-3], probably prevent degradation of viral by the host restriction-modification antiviral defense system [2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: HEPN-like_int
comment: This is a HEPN-like nuclease. Part of mobile integron element. The integron cassettes are known to be activated by stress conditions, thereby allowing swapping of genetic material that might be of adaptive value. Hence it is hypothesized that the HEPN domains present in some integron cassettes contribute to the stress response by functioning as RNases that induce dormancy by probably inhibiting translation and thus enabling survival of harsh conditions (PMID: 23768067). (from Pfam)

label: SipA_VBS
comment: This motif family includes the three vinculin binding sites found in the Shigella SipA/IpaA protein (PMID: 21525010). The family also includes some proteins from Chlamydia species. (from Pfam)

label: Tudor_RapA
comment: This is one of two Tudor-like domains found in the N-terminal region of RapA proteins. RapA is an abundant RNAP-associated protein of 110-kDa molecular weight with ATPase activity. It forms a stable complex with the RNAP core enzyme, but not with the holoenzyme. The ATPase activity of RapA increases upon its binding to RNAP (PMID: 25646438). The N-terminal region of RapA contains two copies of a Tudor-like domains, both folded as a highly bent antiparallel beta-sheet. This fold is also found in transcription factor NusG , ribosomal protein L24, human SMN (survival of motor neuron) protein, mammalian DNA repair factor 53BP1, putative fission yeast DNA repair factor Crb2 and bacterial transcription-repair coupling factor known as Mfd. The functional roles of the N-terminal region homologs in these proteins suggest that the Tudor-like domains of RapA may interact with both nucleic acids and RNAP (PMID: 18786404). (from Pfam)

label: SH3_17
comment: This is an N-terminal beta-barrel domain found in the Hpy99I protomer region. Hpy99I is a type II restriction endonuclease (REase) found in the gastric pathogen Helicobacter pylori. The beta-barrel domain has the SH3-domain fold. Deletion of the beta-barrel domain drastically reduced the activity of Hpy99I (PMID: 19380375). (from Pfam)

label: YcaO_C
comment: This is the proline-rich C-terminal domain found in ribosomal protein S12 methylthiotransferase accessory factor YcaO. It has been shown to be involved in both C protein recognition and cyclodehydration. The C-terminal domain resembles a tetratricopeptide repeat that mediates dimerization (PMID: 25129028). (from Pfam)

label: ORF_2_N
comment: This is the N-terminal domain found in ORF 2 (open reading frame 2), a protein encoded just downstream of asp (A. sobria serine protease). The ORF 2 N-terminal domain is essential for proper ASP folding. This domain is intrinsically disordered but forms some degree of secondary structure upon binding ASP [1, 2]. (from Pfam)

label: SGBP_B_XBD
name_orig: Surface glycan-binding protein B xyloglucan binding domain
comment: Members of this family are glycan-binding surface proteins, typically found in gut bacteria and involved in the utilization of plant polysaccharides such as xyloglucan.

label: Tsi6
comment: Tsi6 inhibits the NADase activity of Tse6, an integral membrane toxin from Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The Tsi6 immunity protein adopts an all-alpha-helical fold that binds to a surface of Tse6 (PMID: 29237732). (from Pfam)

label: Rap1a
comment: This domain occurs in immunity proteins from a number of type VI secretion system (T6SS) toxin-immunity pairs, and may occur twice in some immunity proteins.

label: LepB_N
comment: Rab GTPases constitute the largest family of small GTP-binding proteins that act as molecular switches in regulating vesicular transport in eukaryotic cells. LepB is a Rab GTPase-activating protein (GAP) effector found in Legionella pneumophila. This entry represents the N-terminal domain which is followed by a GAP domain (PMID: 23588383). (from Pfam)

label: Pallilysin
comment: The Treponema pallidum protein, Tp0751 (also known as pallilysin), possesses adhesive properties and has been previously reported to mediate attachment to the host extracellular matrix components laminin, fibronectin, and fibrinogen. Tp0751 adopts an eight-stranded beta-barrel with a profile of short conserved regions consistent with a non-canonical lipocalin fold. Lipocalins, along with fatty acid-binding proteins and avidins, are members of the calycin superfamily, which is defined by the distinct features of a central beta-barrel and a key structural signature consisting of three short conserved regions (SCR1, SCR2, and SCR3). However, Tp0751 does not contain all three conserved regions, hence it is considered an outlier to canonical lipocalins. In SCR1, there is a GxW motif (PMID: 27683203). (from Pfam)

label: bVLRF1
comment: Archaeo-eukaryotic release factor domain family belonging to the VLRF1 clade observed primarily in the bacteroidetes bacterial lineage. Contains a conserved glutamine residue in the release factor catalytic loop, suggesting it functions as an active peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase at the ribosome (PMID: 29632312). (from Pfam)

label: Suv3_C_1
comment: This domain is found in Suv3 present in Homo sapiens. Suv3 is an NTP-dependent RNA/DNA helicase that is necessary for the degradation of mature mtRNAs. Suv3 has been found to interact in vitro with polynucleotide phosphorylase. This domain makes up part of the C-terminal domain (PMID: 22101826). (from Pfam)

label: Tudor_1_RapA
comment: This is one of two Tudor-like domains found in the N-terminal region of RapA proteins. RapA is an abundant RNAP-associated protein of 110-kDa molecular weight with ATPase activity. It forms a stable complex with the RNAP core enzyme, but not with the holoenzyme. The ATPase activity of RapA increases upon its binding to RNAP (PMID: 25646438). The N-terminal region of RapA contains two copies of a Tudor-like domains, both folded as a highly bent antiparallel beta-sheet. This fold is also found in transcription factor NusG , ribosomal protein L24, human SMN (survival of motor neuron) protein, mammalian DNA repair factor 53BP1, putative fission yeast DNA repair factor Crb2 and bacterial transcription-repair coupling factor known as Mfd. The functional roles of the N-terminal region homologs in these proteins suggest that the Tudor-like domains of RapA may interact with both nucleic acids and RNAP (PMID: 18786404). (from Pfam)

label: GbpA_2
comment: This domain can be found in N-acetylglucosamine binding protein (GbpA) from Vibrio cholerae, a bacterial pathogen that colonizes the chitinous exoskeleton of zooplankton as well as the human gastrointestinal tract. GbpA binds to GlcNAc oligosaccharides. Structural comparison show that there are distant structural similarities between domain 2 of GbpA and the beta-domain of the flagellin protein p5. It is suggested that this domain interacts with the bacterial surface, and functions to project an alginate binding domain of the protein from the cell surface (PMID: 22253590). (from Pfam)

label: Tli4_C
product_name: T6SS immunity protein Tli4 family protein
name_orig: Tle cognate immunity protein 4 C-terminal domain
hmm_name: type 6 secretion system immunity protein Tli4 family C-terminal domain
comment: T6SS bacteria employ toxic effectors to inhibit rival cells and concurrently use effector cognate immunity proteins to protect their sibling cells. The effector and immunity pairs (E-I pairs) endow the bacteria with a great advantage in niche competition. This is the C-terminal domain of Tli4. The Tle cognate immunity proteins (Tlis) can directly disable the transported Tle protein and thereby mediate the self-protection process. The Tle-Tli effector-immunity (E-I) pairs confer substantial advantage to the donor cell during interbacterial competition. Tli4 displays a two-domain structure, in which a large lobe and a small lobe form a crab claw-like conformation. Tli4 uses this crab claw to grasp the cap domain of Tle4, especially the lid2 region, which prevents the interfacial activation of Tle4 and thus causes enzymatic dysfunction of Tle4. Structural comparison indicates similarity between this C-terminal domain of Tli4 and Tsi3, which is the cognate immunity protein of the effector protein Tse3 in P. aeruginosa PDB:4n7s (PMID: 25478841). (from Pfam)

comment: This is a domain of unknown function found in proteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5627

hmm_name: Nmad5 family putative nucleotide modification protein
comment: An alpha+beta fold domain associated with DNA base modifying genes in prokaryotes, and likely to be involved in modified DNA base biosynthesis (PMID: 23814188). (from Pfam)

label: signal_int_SinM
comment: SinM (signal integration modulator) is a regulatory partner of the hybrid histidine kinase/response regulator SinK (signal integrating kinase).

label: myxo_dep_M36
comment: Members of this bacterial protein family have an M36 family metallopeptidase domain, like fungalysin (see PF02128), and a C-terminal MYXO-CTERM domain (see TIGR03901), suggesting processing and surface-anchoring by a type II CAAX prenyl protease-related sorting enzyme, myxosortase. Members of this family include MXAN_3564 (mepA), part of the effector cargo of outer membrane vesicles that the species produces in large numbers during predation on other microbes.

label: Sden1266_dom
comment: The choice-of-anchor H domain is observed, in from one to four copies, in over 500 proteobacterial proteins with a C-terminal protein sorting signal, GlyGly-CTERM, that directs processing by rhombosortase, transport by a type II secretion system (T2SS), and (most likely) covalent attachment to the outer membrane. The domain is also observed occasionally, in up to 13 tandem copies, in proteins sorted and processed instead by a type IX secretion system (T9SS), which also implies transpeptidation and covalent attachment on the cell surface. One member of this family, Sden_1266, is toxic if expressed as a transgene in Escherichia coli, as might be expected given the lack of the required processing machinery in that species.

label: PEP_CTERM_QFxxD
comment: This family of PEP-CTERM proteins has a notable motif, QFxxD, near the PEP-CTERM region, for which it is named.

label: PEP_CTERM_TLD_A
comment: Members of this family represent one branch of the TLD domain family, predicted to be a family of enzymes (see PF07534). All members furthermore have a C-terminal region, PEP-CTERM (TIGR02595 or one of its variants) for recognition and processing by an exosortase, and presumably attachment on the cell surface.

label: exosort_XrtW
comment: Exosortase W is an EpsI domain-containing subtype of exosortase, a bacterial protein-sorting enzyme that is probably a transpeptidase rather than a simple hydrolase. It is most closely related to exosortase D, which is VPLPA-CTERM-specific. However, it is the sole exosortase in Candidatus Manganitrophus noduliformans, the nodule-forming Nitrospiraceae bacterium identified as the first manganese-oxidizing chemolithoautotroph. In that species, target proteins have the more classical PEP-CTERM sorting signal at the C-terminus.

label: maturase_GoxB
comment: GoxB, a flavoprotein, is responsible for the post-translational modification that forms the cysteine tryptophylquinone (CTQ) cofactor of the quinone glycine oxidase GoxA.

label: VI_Cas13b
product_name: type VI-B CRISPR-associated RNA-guided ribonuclease Cas13b
hmm_name: type VI-B CRISPR-associated RNA-guided ribonuclease Cas13b

product_name: Gar/GrdA family gentamicin resistance ATP-binding protein
hmm_name: Gar/GrdA family gentamicin resistance ATP-binding protein

This family is related to the tunicamycin resistance protein TmrB of Bacillus subtilis. provides resistance to garosamine-containing aminoglycosides such as gentamicin

label: exopoly_VpsF
comment: Vps genes contribute to biofilm formation by directing biosynthesis of the exopolysaccharide VPS (Vibrio polysaccharide), a major component of the biofilm matrix. Members of this family show some distant similarity to O-antigen ligases. VpsF, distantly related to oligosaccharide ligases, is encoded next to the probable flippase VpsE.

label: YjiT_fam
comment: Full length members of this family, about 1100 amino acids long, include STY4851 from Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhi str. Ty2 and ECs_5259. The family also includes the half-length pseudogene translation YjiT from Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655, for which the corresponding complete protein is WP_048814575. The function is unknown.

label: perm_prefix_2
comment: The permease prefix domain 2 is found as the N-terminal domain of putative permeases resembling ABC transporter permeases. In at least some permease families, this prefix domain is only variably present, and may be replaced by a different, seemingly unrelated prefix domain. This domain is considerably less common than permease prefix domain 1 (NF038404).

label: Por_Secre_tail
product_name: T9SS type A sorting domain-containing protein
hmm_name: T9SS secretion system C-terminal sorting domain
comment: Species that include Porphyromonas gingivalis, Fibrobacter succinogenes, Flavobacterium johnsoniae, Cytophaga hutchinsonii, Gramella forsetii, Prevotella intermedia, and Salinibacter ruber have on average twenty or more copies of this C-terminal domain, associated with sorting to the outer membrane and covalent modification. This domain targets proteins to type IX secretion systems and is secreted then cleaved off by a C-terminal signal peptidease (PMID: 22593568). Based on similarity to other families it is likely that this domain adopts an immunoglobulin like fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5924
comment: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found in bacteria. This entry represents a likely integral membrane region with six transmembrane helices. The family is found in association with Pfam:PF11141. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5929
comment: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in flavobacteria, and is approximately 220 amino acids in length. The family is found to the C-terminus of Pfam:PF04326. Proteins in this family vary in length from 377 to 380 amino acids. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6068
comment: This entry represents a member of a biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC). This BGC (BGC0001902) is described by MIBiG as an example of the following biosynthetic classes, NRP (non-ribosomal peptide) and polyketide. This family includes a protein from the bengamide biosynthetic gene cluster from Myxococcus virescens and appears to be predominantly found in cystobacterineae (PMID: 26514647). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6072
comment: This entry represents a member of a biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC). This BGC (BGC0000967) is described by MIBiG as an example of the following biosynthetic classes, NRP (non-ribosomal peptide) and polyketide. This family includes a protein from the calyculin A biosynthetic gene cluster from uncultured Candidatus Entotheonella sp. and appears to be predominantly found in bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6267
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is primarily found in myoviruses. Proteins in this family are typically between 298 and 400 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6341
comment: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 70 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs, WIF and YW. Probably, they are Uracil phosphoribosyltransferases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6370
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and it is functionally uncharacterised. Proteins in this family are approximately 110 amino acids in length. comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 210 amino acids in length and their N-terminal share a similar structure with the Crispr-associated endoribonuclease Cas2. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6768
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 130 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6787
comment: This family of proteins found in bacteria is functionally uncharacterised and is approximately 100 amino acids in length. Some members of this family are putative diacylglyceryl transferases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6797
comment: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain is found in bacteria, and is around 100 amino acids in length. This domain is found in association with Pfam:PF13442. There is a conserved sequence motif GPLP. (from Pfam)

label: PMT_C3
comment: Pasteurella multocida toxin (PMT) inhibits osteoblastic differentiation in mammals and birds. Its N-terminal region binds to target cells, while its C-terminal region, with a Trojan horse-like shape, carries the intracellularly active moiety. The latter consists of three distinct domains: C1 (Pfam:PF11647), C2 and C3. This entry represents the C-terminal catalytic domain C3, which has a Cys-His-Asp triad known to perform acyl-hydrolysis such as peptidase activity or an acyl-transfer reaction. This domain adopts a typical alpha-beta protein fold with seven beta-strands and eight helices. It is organised into two subdomains that form the the biologically active cleft space [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Gta3
comment: This family represents glutamyl-tRNA amidotransferase complex subunit Gta3 from S. pombe, an orthologue of yeast GTF1 and human Glutamyl-tRNA(Gln) amidotransferase subunit C (GATC). (from Pfam)

label: Dimerisation2-like_dom
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of bacterial methyltransferases, including SAM-dependent methyltransferase from Phocaeicola vulgatus (BVU_1015). It has a winged-helix structure and is usually found associated with Pfam:PF00891 and Pfam:PF13489. (from Pfam)

label: PRDM2_PR
product_name: PR domain zinc finger protein 2, PR domain
name_orig: PR domain zinc finger protein 2, PR domain
hmm_name: PR domain zinc finger protein 2, PR domain
comment: This domain is found in PR domain zinc protein 2 from humans (PRDM2) and similar proteins from animals. PRDM2 is a histone methyltransferase that functions as a DNA-binding transcription factor. It contains a PR (PRDI-BF1 and RIZ1 homology) domain, which is a distinct SET domain, that is responsible for its catalytic activity (this entry). This domain displays a typical SET fold consisting mainly of short beta-strands and intervening loops including a pseudo-knot at the C terminus (PMID: 18082620). (from Pfam)

label: Type_III_SycN
product_name: Type III secretory system chaperone SycN
name_orig: Type III secretory system chaperone SycN
hmm_name: Type III secretory system chaperone SycN
comment: Chaperone protein SycN is part of the type III secretion system and functions as a specific chaperone for YopN which may facilitate the secretion and the subsequent translocation of YopN (PMID: 15701523). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6878
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein that adopts a beta-grasp fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6819
comment: This domain of unknown function is found at the C-terminal of Pfam:PF16314 and it may have an alpha-helical fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6844
comment: This domain is found in proteins predominantly found in Gammaproteobacteria such as Hypothetical protein FTT_1539c from Francisella tularensis. It is located in the centre of the proteins included in this entry. (from Pfam)

label: HEAT_Maestro
comment: This entry represents HEAT repeats from maestro heat-like repeat-containing proteins. Maestro (Male-specific Transcription in the developing Reproductive Organs (MRO)) is expressed in human granulosa cumulus cells and in testicular germ cells (PMID: 28406912). SPIF (also known as MRO2B) may play a role in the process of sperm capacitation (PMID: 27105888). (from Pfam)

label: Thi_PPkinase_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of proteins predominantly found in Bacteroidetes, including Thiamin pyrophosphokinase from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron. This protein consists of a N-terminal catalytic domain (Pfam:PF04263) and a C- terminal domain (this entry), which shows an structure mainly composed of beta-strands. (from Pfam)

label: Mcp40H-20_sensor
product_name: Methyl-accepting chemotaxis sensory transducer, class 40H, sensor
name_orig: Methyl-accepting chemotaxis sensory transducer, class 40H, sensor
hmm_name: Methyl-accepting chemotaxis sensory transducer, class 40H, sensor
comment: This domain is found in Methyl-accepting chemotaxis sensory transducer, class 40H from Geobacter sulfurreducens (Mcp40H-20, Swiss:Q74EM7) and similar proteins predominantly from proteobacteria. This entry represents the periplasmic c-type heme-containing sensor domain, which is located between two transmembrane helices near the N terminus of the protein. This domain adopts a PAS-type domain fold with two helical segments followed by a four-stranded beta-sheet (PMID: 18329666). (from Pfam)

label: PMT_C2
comment: Pasteurella multocida toxin (PMT) inhibits osteoblastic differentiation in mammals and birds. Its N-terminal region binds to target cells, while its C-terminal region, with a Trojan horse-like shape, carries the intracellularly active moiety. The latter consists of three distinct domains: C1 (Pfam:PF11647), C2 and C3. This entry represents the larger of these domains, the central region C2, which has 18 helices and nine beta-strands and is organised into two subdomains with typical alpha-beta structures characteristic of nucleotide-binding proteins (PMID: 17360394). This domain is also found in the Ras/Rap1-specific endopeptidase (RRSP), an effector domain from the multifunctional-autoprocessing repeats-in- toxin (MARTX) toxin from Vibrio vulnificus responsible for the disruption of host innate immune defenses during infection [2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: TetR_C_42
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of prokaryotic transcriptional regulators, including AcrR1 from Aquifex aeolicus. It shows an all-alpha structure. (from Pfam)

label: GldM_2nd
comment: This immunoglobulin-like domain is found in bacteria in the GldM protein. GldM, is named for the member from Cytophaga johnsonae (Flavobacterium johnsoniae), which is required for a type of rapid gliding motility found in certain members of the Bacteriodetes (PMID: 16199564). (from Pfam)

label: DCTN5
comment: This entry includes dynactin 5 (DCTN5, also known as subunit p25). Dynactin is a major component of the activator complex that stimulates dynein-mediated vesicle transport. DCTN5 is part of the pointed-end subcomplex in dynactin that also includes p26, p27 (also known as dynactin 6), and Arp11 [1,2]. This subcomplex interacts with membranous cargoes. DCTN5 plays a dual role in cargo binding and dynactin regulation, being critical for this process. DCTN5 contains imperfect tandem repeats of a hexapeptide repeat motif (X-[STAV]-X-[LIV]-[GAED]-X) (PMID: 15043994). (from Pfam)

label: DACND
comment: This entry represents a potential sensor domain found at the N-terminal of bacterial diadenylate cyclases which are typically followed by the DAC (Pfam:PF02457). It may consist of four alpha-helices and three beta-strands according to structure predictions. This domain is mainly found in deltaproteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6850
product_name: DUF6850 family outer membrane beta-barrel protein
hmm_name: DUF6850 family outer membrane beta-barrel protein
comment: Several members of this family show induction in response to iron deficiency. Structural prediction shows an apparent outer membrane beta-barrel fold.

label: RMD1-3
comment: This is the C-terminal domain of Regulator of microtubule dynamics proteins 1-3 (RMD1-3) which consists of alpha-helical repeats. These are microtubule-binding proteins. RMD3 is involved in cellular calcium homeostasis regulation, and it may participate in differentiation and apoptosis of keratinocytes (PMID: 22131369). RMD1 from C. elegans functions in chromosome segregation (PMID: 18070910). (from Pfam)

label: IcmF_helical
product_name: Type VI secretion protein IcmF helical domain
name_orig: Type VI secretion protein IcmF helical domain
hmm_name: Type VI secretion protein IcmF helical domain
comment: This entry represents the alpha-helical domain from the Type VI secretion protein IcmF (PMID: 26200339). This domain is also found in the TssM protein where it forms part of the tip complex (PMID: 26200339). (from Pfam)

label: TPPII_Ig-like-1
comment: Tripeptidyl peptidase II (TPPII) is a crucial component of the proteolytic cascade acting downstream of the 26S proteasome in the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. It is an amino peptidase belonging to the subtilase family removing tripeptides from the free N terminus of oligopeptides. This protein adopts a dimeric assembly. Each monomer is organised into three main parts: the N-terminal subtilisine-like domain (Pfam:PF00082) a central domain and C-terminal domain (Pfam:PF12583). The central domain can be subdivided into two Ig-like domains and a GBD-like domain (Pfam:PF21316). This entry represents the first Ig-like domain, while Pfam:PF12580 represents the second one (PMID: 20676100). (from Pfam)

label: MXAN_5453_fam
comment: Members of this family contain a variable-length, low-complexity region rich in Gly, Pro, Asp, and Thr between the main globular domain and the MYXO-CTERM sorting signal that is recognized and cleaved by a myxosortase.

label: BT_3928_fam
comment: This family is named after the uncharacterized protein BT_3928 from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482, and the HMM covers the full length of the corrected (extended) length of that protein. The N-terminal region shows distant homology to the redox-associated membrane proteins DoxX and MauE. A number of the members of this family have a C-terminal extension with putative triose phosphate isomerase activity.

label: Mrt_dep_phytase
comment: Members of this family, including the putative phytase MXAN_5326 of Myxococcus xanthus, are restricted to species that encode the sorting enzyme myxosortase. All members of this family known so far have a version of the sorting signal with a doubled motif, GCGC, thought to be lipid-modified first, then cleaved by the myxosortase. MXAN_5326 was seen to be enriched in outer membrane vesicles (OMV).

label: blaMUN
product_name: MUN family extended-spectrum class A beta-lactamase
hmm_name: MUN family extended-spectrum class A beta-lactamase

label: seleno_TsoC
comment: TsoC (three selenoprotein operon C) is a novel selenoprotein family in a three (sometimes four) selenoprotein neighborhood. When structural annotation correctly shows a selenoprotein, the U typically occurs at position 14 or 15.

label: CxxCH_16_HmcA
product_name: sulfate respiration complex hexadecaheme cytochrome HmcA
hmm_name: sulfate respiration complex hexadecaheme cytochrome HmcA
comment: Members of this family are HmcA (high molecular weight cytochrome complex protein A), a periplasmic protein typically with 16 intact CxxCH motifs typical of c-type cytochromes. HmcA is encoded in a six-gene operon well-conserved in sulfur-reducing bacteria.

label: memb_anch_TmcC
product_name: TmcC family electron transfer complex membrane anchor subunit
hmm_name: TmcC family electron transfer complex membrane anchor subunit

label: PID_CTERM
comment: PID-CTERM is a C-terminal sorting signal in bacteria, processed by the exosortase XrtX.

label: CV_2116_dom
comment: The founding member of this family, CV_2116 from a prophage region in Chromobacterium violaceum, is an uncharacterized protein with a solved NMR structure. Although CV_2116 was suggested to be a phage tail assembly protein, this family appears to be a sister family to the HlyU family transcriptional regulators described by Pfam model PF10115.

label: DUF6911
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Proteobacteria. The structure of these proteins contains a six stranded beta sheet. (from Pfam)

label: OSBS_N
comment: This domain is found N-terminal in members of o-succinylbenzoate synthase (OSBS) family. It is also known as capping domain. In most members, this domain consists of a central three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet packed on one side with two helices. The second helix is truncated or missing in some members of the family (PMID: 24872444). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6934
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure consisting of a central mixed beta-sheet packed on both sides with alpha-helices that is reminiscent to the common structural core of N-acetyltransferases (NAT). (from Pfam)

label: OmcA-like_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of OmcA (Swiss:Q8EG33) from Shewanella oneidensis and similar proteins. OmcA is a decaheme c-type cytochrome homologue of MtrF and MtrC [1-5]. OmcA may be able to receive electrons from the MtrCAB or MtrFDE complexes through the interaction with MtrC or MtrF (PMID: 21606337). OmcA, MtrF and MtrC are involved in the use of manganese and iron as terminal electron acceptors. (from Pfam)

label: NMB1110-like_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Tail protein, 43 kDa Neisseria meningitidis (NMB1110) and similar sequences found in tailed bacteriophages and prophages from proteobacteria. This domain is usually found associated with Pfam:PF21683. (from Pfam)

label: MtxA_IG-like
comment: This immunoglobulin-like domain is found in the Magnetotaxis protein MtxA from Magnetospirillum gryphiswaldense (Swiss:A4TUL6) and similar sequences from magnetotactic aquatic proteobacteria. Magnetotaxis is believed to direct the swimming of cells toward growth-favoring microoxic zones in natural waters (PMID: 26052516). (from Pfam)

label: PqqF_C_3
product_name: PQQ synthase PqqF, C-terminal lobe domain 3
name_orig: PQQ synthase PqqF, C-terminal lobe domain 3
hmm_name: PQQ synthase PqqF, C-terminal lobe domain 3
comment: This entry represents domain 3 from the C-terminal lobe of PQQ synthase PqqF, a protein required for coenzyme pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) biosynthesis. It consists of four structurally similar domains organised in N-terminal (domain 1 represented in Pfam: PF00675 and domain 2 in Pfam:PF22454) and C-terminal (domain 3 and domain 4) lobes (PMID: 27231346). (from Pfam)

label: PqqF-like_C_4
product_name: PQQ synthase PqqF-like, C-terminal lobe domain 4
name_orig: PQQ synthase PqqF-like, C-terminal lobe domain 4
hmm_name: PQQ synthase PqqF-like, C-terminal lobe domain 4
comment: This entry represents domain 4 from the C-terminal lobe of PQQ synthase PqqF, a protein required for coenzyme pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) biosynthesis. It consists of four structurally similar domains organised in N-terminal (domain 1 represented in Pfam: PF00675 and domain 2 in Pfam:PF22454) and C-terminal (domain 3 and domain 4) lobes (PMID: 27231346). This domain is also found in other Peptidase M16 members, such as Nardilysin and insulin degrading enzymes from human. (from Pfam)

label: 2CompARG
comment: This entry represents the 2CompARG domain, which coupled with its partner 2CompART, forms a two-domain T-A-like association in the duplex-forming systems likely functioning as the principal effector of these systems. One is likely to function as the antitoxin, regulating the toxin activity of the other (PMID: 35609893). (from Pfam)

label: mSLOG
comment: This entry represents a domain predicted to be an active, minimal version of the SLOG domain. It is found N-terminally fused to the DUF4326 domain (Pfam:PF14216). It may play a role in base cleavage, potentially forming abasic sites acted on by DuOB domain (Pfam:PF22557) (PMID: 36968430). (from Pfam)

label: E217_gp29
comment: E217 is a Pseudomonas phage used in an experimental cocktail to eradicate cystic fibrosis-associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The gateway protein gp29 is a neck factor of the E217 virion that connects the neck to the sheath lattice (PMID: 37422479). (from Pfam)

label: ToxA_barrel
comment: Dermonecrotic toxin (ToxA), also known as Pasteurella multocida toxin (PMT), inhibits osteoblastic differentiation in mammals and birds. It consists of an N-terminal domain that binds to target cells, and a large C-terminal domain. This entry represents a presumed barrel-like domain found between the N- and C-terminal domains. (from Pfam)

label: GNAT_LYC1-like
comment: This domain is found C-terminal in Lysine acetyltransferase (LYC1) and other related fungal proteins. LYC1 catalyzes the first step the lysine degradation pathway. The domain represented by this entry is predicted to adopt GNAT-like fold. It is found usually upstream Acetyltransferase GNAT domain (Pfam:PF00583) suggesting a possible duplication event in these proteins. (from Pfam)

label: MtxA_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Magnetotaxis protein MtxA from Magnetospirillum gryphiswaldense (Swiss:A4TUL6) and similar sequences from magnetotactic aquatic proteobacteria. Magnetotaxis is believed to direct the swimming of cells toward growth-favoring microoxic zones in natural waters. This domain shows five anti-parallel alpha-helices-and-turn motifs folded as tetra-trico-peptide repeat (TPR) motifs (PMID: 26052516). (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_16
comment: This domain is about 60 amino acids in length and is found N-terminal to Pfam:PF19898 that resembles a DNA primase core domain. This domain has remote similarity to the zinc-ribbon domain of DNA primase and it is predicted to adopt the same structure. It has four nearly invariant Cys residues, two of which located in unusual conserved motif VGRCxxxxxCGYH. (from Pfam)

label: SelB_WH2
name_orig: Elongation factor SelB, second winged-helix domain
comment: This domain is found in Elongation factor SelB from Aquifex aeolicus and similar bacterial proteins. SelB is a selenocysteine(Sec)-specific elongation factor that brings the selenocysteinyl-tRNA(Sec) to the ribosome. It consists of three EF-Tu-like domains (D1-3, where Pfam:PF00009 is the first one), followed by four winged-helix domains (WHD1-4). This entry represents the second winged-helix domain (WHD2) (PMID: 26304550). (from Pfam)

label: PBP1_XylR
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of XylR, an atypical AraC protein. This D-xylose-binding domain contains a periplasmic-binding protein (PBP) fold, similar to LacI/GalR transcription regulators, and mediates dimerization (PMID: 23241389). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6952
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They contain highly conserved acidic residues and G[S/A]ID motif at the C terminus. (from Pfam)

label: Alg17C_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Exo-oligoalginate lyase from Saccharophagus degradans (Alg17C) and similar sequences from proteobacteria. Alg17C catalyses the depolymerisation of alginate through an exolytic mode of action, via a beta-elimination mechanism. This protein consists of two domains: an N-terminal imperfect alpha-barrel (Pfam:PF05426) and a C-terminal beta-sheet domain (Pfam:PF07940 and this entry) (PMID: 24478312). This domain adopts an all-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: SNaCT13
comment: The SNaCT domains are a rapidly evolving, monophyletic assemblage of domains found C-terminal to the NACHT module in several bacterial NACHT conflict systems. They contain a well-conserved aspartate near the N-terminus of the domain. SNaCT domains are thought to occlude the NTP-binding region, potentially until they interact with phage-encoded bNACHT inhibitors (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: GWD1_pHisD
comment: This domain is found in the homologues of Alpha-glucan water dikinase (GWD1). This enzyme is involved in the incorporation of phosphate into starch-like alpha-glucan, with preferred C-6 position of glucose units. It acts as an overall regulator of starch mobilization and it is required for starch degradation. The domain represented by this entry is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a beta-barrel decorated with alpha-helices. This domain has a significant sequence and structural similarity to phosphohistidine domain found in phosphate dikinases and PEP:sugar phosphotransferases. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6901
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins. The possess a beta sheet packed against an alpha helical subdomain. This alignment contains three fully conserved cysteines that look like they form an Fe-S cluster or zinc binding site in the predicted structures. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6931
comment: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share significant sequence similarity with immunity protein Imm5 and are predicted to adopt similar alpha-helical structure. (from Pfam)

label: MCP_V20_C
product_name: major capsid protein V20 domain-containing protein
name_orig: Major capsid protein V20 C-terminal domain
hmm_name: major capsid protein V20 domain-containing protein
comment: This is the C-terminal domain of major capsid protein V20. This domain folds into a beta-sandwich with a jelly-roll topology (PMID: 23091035). (from Pfam)

label: DUF6956
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either as standalone or in combination with other domains. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta structure with ferredoxin-like topology. (from Pfam)

label: IglE_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of the intracellular growth locus E (IglE) protein from Francisella tularensis subsp. novicida (PMID: 21139203). The lipoprotein IglE has been identified as a virulence factor that functions as a regulator of the Type IV system-mediated secretion (PMID: 27830989). (from Pfam)

label: NMB1110_3rd
comment: This domain is found in Tail protein, 43 kDa from Neisseria meningitidis (NMB1110) and similar sequences which are related to baseplate hub protein gp44 from Mu bacteriophage. This domain is located C-terminal to Pfam:PF22255 and N-terminal to Pfam:PF22174. (from Pfam)

label: Ape1_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of the peptidoglycan O-acetylesterase N875_00620 from Neisseria meningitidis (Ape1) and similar sequences mainly found in proteobacteria. Ape1, which occurs in bacteria that O-acetylate their peptidoglycan, has an SGNH catalytic domain (Pfam:PF13472) at the C-terminal end. This entry represents the N-terminal canonical beta-sandwich that consists of two antiparallel beta-sheets. It is likely to interact with a specific carbohydrate moiety (PMID: 25286847). (from Pfam)

label: PL28
comment: This entry represents the PL28 family of ulvan lyases. These enzymes degrade ulvan next to either epimer of uronic acid. They adopt a beta-sandwich structure with a jelly-roll topology containing a deep positively charged cleft that defines the substrate binding site (PMID: 29875159). (from Pfam)

label: Glu2-Pro
comment: This entry represents a novel glutamic protease unique to a few members of the family Secoviridae, such as Strawberry Mottle Virus (SMoV), which suggests it is a recent acquisition in the evolution of this family. This is a second protease required for processing of SMoV polyproteins (PMID: 30541838). It has two highly conserved glutamic acid residues spaced by 82 residues that are strictly required for protease activity (PMID: 30541838). This domain is predicted to share structural similarities fungal and bacterial glutamic proteases that adopt a lectin fold [1,https://doi.org/10.3390/f13111868]. (from Pfam)

label: BB0259_flg_lyt
comment: Members of this family, found exclusively in spirochetes, found exclusively in spirochetes, provide the peptidoglycan lysis necessary for proper assembly of periplasmic type (i.e. spirochete type) flagella. This is one of two functions performed in other species by a bifunctional FlgJ. In spirochetes with this family, FlgJ exists but is monofunctional.

label: post-PEP-CTERM_1
comment: The PEP-CTERM domain is a protein-sorting domain, about 25 amino acids in length, typically found as the most C-terminal domain feature in any bacterial protein. However, a subset of choice-of-anchor J family proteins with PEP-CTERM domains have an additional, extremely unusual novel domain located C-terminally to the PEP-CTERM domain. This domain is found also in proteins that have very little sequence N-terminal to this domain. This HMM represents the first observation of this that has resulting in the naming of a novel domain, and so the domain is named the post-PEP-CTERM-1 domain (PPC1 domain).

label: LA_2478_plus
comment: Members of the paralogous family of proteins from the genus Leptospira contain six invariant Cys residues in a stretch of about 140 amino acids, plus a nearly invariant seventh Cys at the end of the signal peptide region that suggests most family members are lipoproteins. The family is not characterized.

label: LIC_11975_fam
comment: LIC_11975 from Leptospira interrogans was designated Lsa36 (leptospiral surface adhesin 36).

label: CPBP_Sphingo
product_name: CPBP family intramembrane glutamic endopeptidase, BDIM_20840 family
hmm_name: CPBP family intramembrane glutamic endopeptidase, BDIM_20840 family

label: throspo3_MtsD
comment: MtsD belongs to the six gene mts (myxococcus thrombospondin D) operon, and is one of four with repeats described as thrombospondin type 3 (TSP3) repeats. Members of the locus participate in cell-cell cohesion that contributes to social motility and fruiting-body development, among other processes.

label: gliding_AgmC_N
hmm_name: adventurous gliding motility protein AgmC, N-terminal domain
comment: This family includes surface proteins with a wide variety of architectures, but a shared N-terminal region of just over 400 amino acids, from Myxococcus xanthus and related species. The founding member, AAO22852.1, was named AgmC after because loss of function affects adventurous gliding motility. It appears that essentially all members of the family have a MYXO-CTERM protein-sorting signal, for directing Cys side-chain lipid modification, cleavage distal to the Cys, transit of the outer membrane, and C-terminal lipid anchoring on the external face of the outer membrane. However, some longer members of the family such as WP_140865666.1 appear to be fusion proteins with an internal MYXO-CTERM domain and fused region C-terminal to it that likely is cleaved to function as a separate protein.

label: lipo_LBF_0142
comment: This subfamily of lipoproteins, named for LBF_0142 from the saprophytic species Leptospira biflexa, is found in a subset of Leptospira species, with additional members found outside the genus. Members belong to the broader DUF6503 family described by PF20113.2.

label: broad_LIC11966
comment: LIC11966 from Leptospira interrogans is a lipoprotein that was called "ErpY-like lipoprotein" based on reported sequence similarity (e.g. in PMID: 31548314) to outer membrane protein ErpY (Q9S0D9) from Borrelia. However, that sequence similarity may reflect a shared compositional bias toward charged amino acids rather than true homology by derivation from the same ancestral protein sequence. Model NF038294 describes the rather narrow family of full-length homologs of LIC11966, all lipoproteins from the genus Leptospira. This broader model hits a broader set of sequence, all with some type of signal peptide, although many are not lipoproteins. Some members of this family contain a DUF6620 domain C-terminal to the region described by this model.

label: RP439FamHumup
comment: Proteins in this family are upregulated in human cell lines

label: DUF7056
comment: This is a presumed domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. According to structure predictions, this domain is found towards the C-terminal, after a glycosyltransferase domain (Pfam:PF13231), and it may adopt an alpha/beta structure. In some instances, this domain is followed by and all-beta domain at the very C-terminal of the sequences (Pfam:PF23157). The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: YqgG
comment: This protein family includes Protein YqgG from Escherichia coli, a 47-residues micropeptide encoded by a small open reading frame (smORF) found antisense to yqgC. Proteins 50 or fewer residues -long have been shown to regulate the functions of larger proteins in a variety of organisms (PMID: 30837344). (from Pfam)

label: Phage_TTP_2
comment: This entry represents a family of phage proteins that by structural similarity are highly likely to be phage tail tube proteins that oligomerise to make the phage tail. These proteins are composed of a distinctive beta barrel structure. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_lipoprotein
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins that have an N-terminal lipoprotein attachment motif. This suggests that these proteins are expressed on the host bacterial cell membrane. (from Pfam)

label: HAB
comment: This entry represents a region found in proteins possibly related to plasmid partitioning. This domain is composed of two copies of this region each of which forms three strands of a 6-stranded beta barrel. This entry is named the HAB region for Half A Barrel. The beta barrel is capped at one end by two short beta strands, one from each region and at the other end of the barrel by a pair of longer alpha helices, again one contributed by each subunit. (from Pfam)

label: CdsD_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal of CdsD from Chlamydia trachomatis (Swiss:O84671) and similar sequences. CdsD is a structural contact-dependent secretion (Cds) protein that form part of the basal body of the type III secretion system (T3SS) injectisome of the bacteria. The periplasmic part of this protein contains at least 3 domains: PD1, PD2 (Pfam:PF22598) and PD3 (Pfam:PF04972), all of them sharing the same alpha-beta-beta-alpha-beta topology, known as the BON fold (PMID: 26914207). They are found in phages that infect Pseudomonas, Xanthomonas, Acinetobacter, Escherichia, Rhodobacter, Sphingomonas, Achromobacter, and Burkholderia bacteria. Bacterial proteins in the family are from Candidatus Macondimonas diazotrophica, Verrucomicrobium sp. GAS474 and Pelodictyon phaeoclathratiforme. The function of these proteins is currently unknown. label: DotM_C
comment: This entry represent the C-terminal cytoplasmic domain of DotM from Legionella pneumophila and related proteins found mainly in gammaproteobacteria. DotM is a component of Type 4B secretion (T4BS) system that translocates over 300 effectors into the host cell during infection. The DotM cytoplasmic domain adopts an alpha-helical structure consisting of 13 alpha-helices (PMID: 29410427). In the membrane-embedded T4 coupling complex (T4CC), DotM makes extensive contacts with DotL and also interacts with the DotN and DotZ proteins. The DotLMNYZ components form a hetero-pentameric core of the T4CC complex from which the flexible IcmSW module protrudes (PMID: 32513920). These hetero-pentameric complexes assemble and form an inner membrane channel for effectors to pass through. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7231
comment: This entry represents a family of unknown function found in phage proteins, typically 120-130 amino acids in length. Some members contain a C-terminal region enriched in basic residues that is predicted to be disordered. The N-terminus of the proteins contain a small globular domain. These proteins are found in the Ackermannviridae family of phages that infect Enterobacteria such as Salmonella, Escherichia, Shigella, and Dickeya. (from Pfam)

label: ARM_5
comment: This entry represents an array of alpha solenoid repeats found in a large family of fungal proteins. This domain is generally found at the N-terminus of the proteins followed by a NACHT domain Pfam:PF05729. (from Pfam)

label: IcmW
product_name: type IVB secretion system protein IcmW
hmm_name: type IVB secretion system protein IcmW
comment: This entry represent the type 4 adapter protein IcmW from Legionella pneumophila and related proteins found mainly in Gammaproteobacteria. IcmW is a component of Type 4B secretion (T4BS) system that translocates over 300 effectors into the host cell during infection. This protein is part of a subcomplex which recruits effector proteins and delivers them to the core transmembrane subcomplex (PMID: 32513920). In the membrane-embedded T4 coupling complex (T4CC), the DotLMNYZ components form a hetero-pentameric core of the T4CC complex from which the flexible IcmSW module protrudes (PMID: 32513920). These hetero-pentameric complexes assemble and form an inner membrane channel for effectors to pass through. The IcmS/IcmW complex plays an important role in protein translocation by interacting with multiple Dot/Icm effector proteins to facilitate their translocation into host cells (PMID: 15661013). The binding of the IcmSW complex to effectors enhances the effector protein delivery by mediating a conformational change that facilitates T4SS recognition of a translocation domain located in the carboxyl region of the effector protein (PMID: 18069892). (from Pfam)

comment: This family of uncharacterized proteins is found in viruses, primarily cyanophages that infect cyanobacteria such as Synechococcus and Prochlorococcus species. The family contains short sequences, generally between 45-50 amino acid residues in length. No functional information is available for members of this family. (from Pfam)

label: RoxB
comment: Proteins of this family are c-type cytochromes produced by Gram-negative rubber-degrading bacteria. RoxB shares a high sequence similarity with rubber dioxygenase RoxA. Both RoxA and B are c-type cytochromes. RoxA cleaves rubber (polyisoprene) into C15 oligo-isoprenoid, however, RoxB cleaves polyisoprene into a mixture of C20 and higher oligo-isoprenoids.

label: LIC10280_fam
comment: The lfb1 gene is widely used for Leptospira identification. A short signal peptide is found in the N-terminal of Lfb1 proteins. It has been reported that Lfb1 was associated with Leptospira interrogans virulence.

label: tryp_MXAN_2756
comment: Members of this family are restricted to species that encode the MYXO-CTERM-recognizing protein-sorting enzyme myxosortase MrtX, and regularly are encoded just upstream, with its stop codon overlapping the start of mrtX. The family is named for its founding member, MXAN_2756 from Myxococcus xanthus. By homology, members are trypsin-like serine proteases. Despite the conserved overlap 4 bp overlap with mrtX, the biological role is unknown, and may have little or nothing to do with MrtX-mediated protein-sorting to the cell surface, as other genes conserved nearby appear to have housekeeping functions unrelated to protein-sorting.

label: AGMP_C
comment: This entry includes Alkylglycerol monooxygenase (AGMO, also known as TMEM195) which is a glyceryl-ether monooxygenase that cleaves the O-alkyl bond of ether lipids (PMID: 20643956). These lipids are essential components of brain membranes (PMID: 31555905). This is the C-terminal domain which may adopt a four helical bundle fold. (from Pfam)

label: Allergen_Asp_f_4
comment: This entry represents a major allergen from Aspergillus fumigatus that is found in fungi and is strongly associated with allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) (PMID: 15013973). The protein contains four conserved cysteine residues at positions 81, 198, 236, and 243 that are important for IgE antibody binding and protein structure. The C-terminal cysteines appear particularly important for immunoreactivity. Based on ECOD classification, this protein belongs to the Osmotin-like superfamily, suggesting it likely adopts a beta-rich immunoglobulin-like fold similar to other antifungal proteins in this group. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7849

It is often found immediately N-terminal to Pfam:PF03171 and is predicted to show a predominantly alpha configuration. (from Pfam)

label: anti_phage_HalB
comment: The anti-phage Hailong system consists of HalA and HalB, which form a two-gene operon on the genome of many bacterial species. HalA is a membrane DNA-gated ion channel protein, and its activity is regulated by DNA signals produced by nucleotidyltransferase HalB.

label: KIF21A_4th
comment: This domain is found in human Kinesin-like protein KIF21A and similar eukaryotic sequences. KIF21A is a microtubule-binding motor protein probably involved in neuronal axonal transport. Mutations in this protein are associated with ocular abnormalities. This domain, which is found associated to Pfam:PF00225 and Pfam:PF16796 is predicted to adopt an alpha helical configuration. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7932
comment: This entry describes a domain of unknown function located at the N-terminal of proteins mostly found in fungi. According to structure predictions it might adopt an immunoglobulin, fibronectin type III fold. It is formed of two antiparallel beta-sheets stacked against each other, forming a beta-sandwich (PMID: 20176268). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7935
comment: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein family. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins form a membrane bound octameric complex. The N-terminus of the protein contains an transmembrane alpha helix and the rest of the protein adopts a four helical bundle domain. This family is often found associated with gliding motility proteins in STRING networks. (from Pfam)

(from Pfam)

label: Head_fiber_dimeric
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the head fiber dimeric protein (HFD) found in crassviruses from the order Crassvirales. The family also contains a small number of other non-phage proteins that share this domain. In the crAss001 virus, this protein (gp29) forms dimers that bind to winged hexon pockets at the capsid surface. The N-terminal domain (residues 1-58) interacts with the major capsid protein, while the C-terminal domain (residues 58-118) forms a beta-sandwich with structural similarity to the immunoglobulin-like fold. This protein is likely involved in host recognition and binding, with the two different fiber proteins (dimeric and trimeric) providing different binding specificities to external molecules. Homologues of this protein are present primarily in the Steigviridae (beta) and Crevaviridae (gamma) groups of crassviruses. (from Pfam)

While cyanophycin itself is a polyamide that has a backbone of aspartic acid residues whose side chains have attached arginine residues, it is unclear if the substance produced by the neighboring CphA-like proteins is a true cyanophycin or if it differs substantially substantially in makeup and properties.

LolA is involved in the delivery of lipoproteins generally, rather than just Lpp, and is an essential protein in E. coli, unlike Lpp itself.

It consists of the domain represented by this HMM and two tandem copies of mop-like domain, where Mop proteins are a family of 68-residue molybdenum-pterin binding proteins of Clostridium pasteurianum. This HMM also represents the full length of a pair of archaeal proteins that lack Mop-like domains. PSI-BLAST analysis shows similarity to helix-turn-helix regulatory proteins.

label: AAA
comment: These proteins are members of the ATP:ADP Antiporter (AAA) Family (TC 2.A.12), which consists of nucleotide transporters that have 12 GES predicted transmembrane regions. One protein from Rickettsia prowazekii functions to take up ATP from the eukaryotic cell cytoplasm into the bacterium in exchange for ADP. Five AAA family paralogues are encoded within the genome of R. prowazekii. This organism transports UMP and GMP but not CMP, and it seems likely that one or more of the AAA family paralogues are responsible. The genome of Chlamydia trachomatis encodes two AAA family members, Npt1 and Npt2, which catalyse ATP/ADP exchange and GTP, CTP, ATP and UTP uptake probably employing a proton symport mechanism. Two homologous adenylate translocators of Arabidopsis thaliana are postulated to be localized to the intracellular plastid membrane where they function as ATP importers.

label: NhaD
comment: These proteins are members of the NhaD Na+:H+ Antiporter (NhaD) Family (TC 2.A.62). A single member of the NhaD family has been characterized. This protein is the NhaD protein of Vibrio parahaemolyticus which has 12 GES predicted transmembrane regions. It has been shown to catalyze Na+/H+ antiport, but Li+ can also be a substrate.

This subfamily is specific for aromatic amino acid transporters and includes the tyrosine permease, TyrP, of E. coli, and the tryptophan transporters TnaB and Mtr of E. coli.

The homolog of SctR in flagellar systems is FliP (see TIGR01103). Lineage-specific names for SctR in various bacteria include YscR in Yersinia, BscR in Bordetella, EscR, SpaP, etc.

label: puhA
comment: This model describes the photosynthetic reaction center H subunit in non-oxygenic photosynthetic bacteria. The reaction center is an integral membrane pigment-protein that carries out light-driven electron transfer reactions. At the core of reaction center is a collection light-harvesting cofactors and closely associated polypeptides. The core protein complex is made of L, M and H subunits. The common cofactors include bacterichlorophyll, bacteriopheophytins, ubiquinone and no-heme ferrous iron. The net result of electron tranfer reactions is the establishment of proton electrochemical gradient and production of reducing equivalents in the form of NADH. Ultimately, the process results in the reduction of C02 to carbohydrates(C6H12O6) In non-oxygenic organisms, the electron donor is an organic acid rather than water. Much of our current functional understanding of photosynthesis comes from the structural determination and spectroscopic studies on the reaction center of Rhodobacter sphaeroides.

label: pufL
comment: This model describes the photosynthetic reaction center L subunit in non-oxygenic photosynthetic bacteria. Reaction center is an integral membrane pigment-protein that carries out light-driven electron transfer reactions. At the core of reaction center is a collection light-harvesting cofactors and closely associated polypeptides. The core protein complex is made of L, M and H subunits. The common cofactors include bacterichlorophyll, bacteriopheophytins, ubiquinone and no-heme ferrous iron. The net result of electron tranfer reactions is the establishment of proton electrochemical gradient and production of reducing equivalents in form of NADH. Ultimately the process results in the reduction of C02 to carbohydrates(C6H12O6) In non-oxygenic organisms, the electron donor is some organic acid and not water. Much of our current functional understanding of photosynthesis comes from the structural determination, spectroscopic studies and mutational analysis on the reaction center of Rhodobacter sphaeroides.

The cyclic beta-1,2-glucan in the bactrerial periplasmic space is suggested to confer the property of high osmolority. It has also been demonstrated that mutants in this loci have lost functions of virulence and motility. It is unclear as to how virulence and osmoadaptaion are related.

label: GMP_reduct_1
comment: A deep split separates two families of GMP reductase. This family includes both eukaryotic and some proteobacterial sequences, while the other family contains other bacterial sequences.

label: gltD_gamma_fam
comment: This HMM represents one of three built for the NADPH-dependent or NADH-dependent glutamate synthase (EC 1.4.1.13 and 1.4.1.14, respectively) small subunit and homologs. TIGR01317 describes the small subunit (or equivalent region from longer forms) in eukaryotes, Gram-positive bacteria, and some other lineages, both NADH and NADPH-dependent. TIGR01316 describes a protein of similar length, from Archaea and a number of bacterial lineages, that forms glutamate synthase homotetramers without a large subunit. This model describes both glutatate synthase small subunit and closely related paralogs of unknown function from a number of gamma and alpha subdivision Proteobacteria, including E. coli.
