label: SidC_C
comment: SidC is one of the effectors delivered by Legionella pneumophila into the host cell. Like its paralogue SdcA, SidC anchor on the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) to facilitate the recruitment of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) proteins. This protein is organised into four domains that are packed into an arch-like shape: the N- terminal SNL domain (Pfam:PF18219), the INS domain (which is inserted within the SNL domain), the P4C domain, and a C-terminal domain. This entry represents the latter, which shows an alpha-helical fold. Its function is unknown (PMID: 26067986). (from Pfam)

label: SidD_cat
comment: SidD from Legionella pneumophila is a virulence effector that plays a role in hijacking the host vesicular trafficking by recruiting the small guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) Rab1 to the cytosolic face of the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCVs). This entry represents the catalytic domain [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: SidC_lipid-bd
comment: SidC is one of the effectors delivered by Legionella pneumophila into the host cell. Like its paralogue SdcA, SidC anchor on the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) through binding to phosphatidylinositol-4-phosphate (PI(4)P) to facilitate the recruitment of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) proteins. SidC is organised into four domains that are packed into an arch-like shape: the N- terminal SNL domain (Pfam:PF18219), the INS domain (which is inserted within the SNL domain), the PI(4)P binding domain or P4C domain (this entry), and a C-terminal domain (Pfam:PF20875). The lipid binding domain shows a four alpha-helix bundle with one end sealed by a C-terminal short beta hairpin and a highly positively charged pocket at the other end formed by two loops connecting the alpha-helices. This pocket is thought to be the binding site, responsible for the stimulation of the E3 ligase activity of the SNL domain (PMID: 26067986). (from Pfam)

label: SidF
comment: Legionella pneumophila modulates the host metabolism of phosphoinositides (PIs) to impair membrane trafficking and establish the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCV) for its own replication. The virulence factor SidF is a unique PI phosphatase that specifically hydrolyses PI(3,4)P2 and PI(3,4,5)P3. This protein shows a large single domain that resembles a cowboy hat, which consists of 19 alpha-helices located around a 10-pleated beta-sheet core (PMID: 22872863). (from Pfam)

label: SidD_C
comment: SidD from Legionella pneumophila is a virulence effector that plays a role in hijacking the host vesicular trafficking by recruiting the small guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) Rab1 to the cytosolic face of the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCVs). This entry represents the C-terminal helical domain, which targets SidD to the Golgi and critical for membrane localization within host cells [1,2]. A two-helix bundle at the very C-terminal determines SidD specificity (PMID: 32853279). (from Pfam)

label: SdbC_C
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of the SdbC protein from Legionella pneumophila, which is thought to be a virulence factor or effector of the pathogen (PMID: 28212376). The structure of the domain is solved, showing a fold mostly consisting of beta-strands. (from Pfam)

label: lpg1496_N
comment: This domain is found at the N terminus of the uncharacterised Lpg1496 (also known as Lem10) protein from Legionella pneumophila [1,2]. It is also known as KLAMP domain. This domain adopts an alpha/beta structure with two alpha-helices flanked on one side by a five-stranded beta-sheet and a four-stranded on the other. Lpg1496 contains two copies of this domain, known as KLAMP1 and KLAMP2. (from Pfam)

label: adhesin_Lcl
comment: Lcl (Legionella collagen-like adhesin) is a virulence factor found in various species of Legionella, with a variable length central region of GPX tripeptide repeats and a conserved C-terminal DUF1566 (PF07603) domain. It binds sulfated glycosaminoglycans in host extracellular matrix.

label: HIT-like
comment: These are uncharacterised proteins that are related to proteins which are members of the HIT-like superfamily. (from Pfam)

label: Lgt1_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Glucosyltransferase Lgt1 from Legionella pneumophila, which has been suggested to be involved in pathogenesis. This domain adopts a completely alpha -helical configuration [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: VipD-like_C
comment: This domain is found in VipD from Legionella pneumophila (effector vacuolar protein sorting inhibitor protein D), which localises to early endosomal membranes and alters their lipid and protein composition. This process protects the pathogen from endosomal fusion. VipD adopts a two-domain fold, with a N-terminal domain homologous to patatin (Pfam:PF01734) and a C-terminal domain (this entry) that contains ten alpha-helices and two short beta-strands. VipD localises to early endosomes via this domain [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: AnkX_ins
comment: This entry represents the insertion domain of AnkX, a Legionella pneumophila PC transferase that mediates the recruitment of Rab1 to the cytosolic face of the Legionella-containing vacuole (LCVs). It is a virulence factor that modifies host RAB1 (RAB1A, RAB1B, or RAB1C) and RAB35 leading to the displacement of GDP dissociation inhibitors (GDI) and impairs accessibility to the GTPase effector LepB. It consists of two distinct structural units. The N-terminal contains a FIC domain, which encompasses the CDP-choline binding pocket and a C-terminal ankyrin repeats-containing domain [1,2]. Unlike other FIC enzymes, AnkX comprises an additional insert domain located in the conserved beta-hairpin which consists of alpha-helices and beta-sheets that protrudes from the enzyme and adapts a rigid, thorn-like structure (PMID: 32440549). (from Pfam)

label: RavJ_Peptidase
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal cysteine proteinase domain of RavJ from Legionella pneumophila (PMID: 27986836). (from Pfam)

label: PilZ-like
comment: This domain is found in Swiss:Q5ZYK8 from Legionella pneumophila and similar sequences mainly found in gammaproteobacteria. It shows a great structural similarity with Pfam:PF07238. (from Pfam)

label: MvcA_ins
comment: This entry represents the insertion domain of MvcA, the MavC paralogue A of bacterial effector MavC from Legionella pneumophila. MvcA catalyses the reverse reaction of MavC, removing Ub from Ube2N through hydrolysis which regulates MavC activity. MvcA is similar at sequence and structural levels to MavC, and it exhibits deamidase activity toward ubiquitin (PMID: 29642013). This domain is crucial for substrate recognition [1-5]. (from Pfam)

label: RavZ_cat
comment: The intracellular pathogen Legionella pneumophila interferes with autophagy by delivering an effector protein, cysteine protease RavZ, into the host cytosol. This effector protein cleaves membrane-conjugated Atg8/LC3 proteins from pre-autophagosomal structures [1-3]. RavZ is a two domain protein consisting of an N-terminal catalytic domain, which is represented in this entry, and a C-terminal phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P)-binding domain (Pfam:PF22225) (PMID: 26343456). (from Pfam)

label: blaSAM
comment: The founding (and so far only) member of this family, now called SAM-1 (Simiduia agarivorans metallo-beta-lactamase 1) was previously called MIM-2 (Maynooth IMipenemase-2), but is sufficiently distant from MIM-1 that it must be considered a separate family. SAM-1 is an unusual subclass B3 metallo-beta-lactamase with an ability to bind metal cofactors other than zinc, and to hydrolyze homoserine lactones for the modulation of quorum sensing networks. The dual role suggests an evolutionary origin for the development of beta-lactamase activity in subclass B3 enzymes.

label: blaDYB
comment: DYB (Dysgonomonas class B) is a family of subclass B1 metallo-beta-lactamases, found in the genus Dysgonomonas.

label: TerS_C
product_name: Phage G20C small terminase C-terminal domain
name_orig: Phage G20C small terminase C-terminal domain
hmm_name: Phage G20C small terminase C-terminal domain
comment: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of terminase small subunit (TerS) from Thermus phage G20c, which oligomerises into a nonamer that binds DNA, stimulates terminase large subunit ATPase activity, and inhibits TerL nuclease activity. TerS is organised into an N-terminal helix-turn-helix (HTH) motif (Pfam:PF21434) followed by an oligomerisation domain consisting of two antiparallel helices (this entry) that pack against the oligomerisation domain helices of the neighbouring subunit, forming a helical barrel (PMID: 32014998). (from Pfam)

label: vanZ-Pt
comment: Members of this family are the glycopeptide resistance protein VanZ of VanPt-type vancomycin resistance systems.

label: PRK13816.1
comment: Associates with free 30S ribosomal subunits; essential for efficient processing of 16S rRNA

label: ileS_w_GNAT
comment: This unusual form of isoleucine--tRNA ligase, found in at least six different species of Moraxella, has a GNAT-type N-acetyltransferase domain, about 170 amino acids long, inserted after position 270 of forms lacking the insert, such as that of Escherichia coli.

label: MCR_0457_fam
comment: Members of this family average about 125 amino acids in length. Two Cys, separated by about 65 amino acids, are the only two invariant residues in this family. Mutation of founding protein MCR_0457 in one strain of Moraxella catarrhalis resulted in a severe growth defect during iron starvation, but the mechanism for the defect was not described and the phenomenon was not well conserved among different isolates of the same species. Members of this family are found almost entirely in the genera Acinetobacter, Moraxella, and Psychrobacter.

label: DUF7944
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins mainly from Moraxellales. It is predicted to fold into an array of alpha-helices. It contains two invariant cysteine residues which are predicted to form a disulfide bond. (from Pfam)

hmm_name: OXA-213 family carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase

label: blaADC
product_name: ADC family extended-spectrum class C beta-lactamase
name_orig: ADC family cephalosporin-hydrolyzing class C beta-lactamase
hmm_name: ADC family extended-spectrum class C beta-lactamase
comment: Members of this family (Acinetobacter-Derived Cephalosporinase, or ADC) are chromosomal class C beta-lactamases (AmpC). Members in general show activity against cephalosporins (as expected for class C enzymes), including at 3rd generation cephalosporins ceftazidime and cefotaxime, making them extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBL). In general, expression levels are low and non-inducible, but insertion of mobile elements upstream, especially ISAba1, and create strong promoter activity for blaADC gene, making that strain clinically resistant. Note that ADC-68 has been shown to have carbapenem-hydrolyzing activity as well. ADC-33 and at least 8 related alleles, with a conserved pair of changes in the omega loop, are active against cefepime, a fourth generation cephalosporin.

label: AdeS_HK
comment: Mutations in this component of the two-component regulatory system for the AdeABC efflux pump can confer adaptive resistance to certain antibiotics, including tigecycline.

label: Ish1
comment: This entry represents a repeat found in the fungal protein Ish1, a protein which has a role in nuclear membrane organisation (PMID: 32848252). (from Pfam)

label: DUF4882
comment: This small family consists of several uncharacterized proteins around 325 residues in length and is mainly found in various Acinetobacter species. The function of this family is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4951
comment: This family consists of several uncharacterized proteins around 125 residues in length and is mainly found in various Acinetobacter baumannii species. The function of this family is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: B3_Acin_new2
comment: This is one of two families of putative metallo-beta-lactamases of subclass B3 that are restricted to the genus Acinetobacter, and undescribed as of January 2017.

label: ANT_3pp_II
comment: Members of this family occur the genus Acinetobacter, show evidence of lateral gene transfer despite the conserved chromosomal location, and confer resistance to streptomycin and spectinomycin.

label: OMP_33_36
comment: Members of this family are outer membrane beta-barrel proteins that facilitate passive transport from the extracellular milieu into the periplasm. Known members are limited to the genus Acinetobacter, and the name, Omp33-36, reflects variability of this protein across the lineage. Note that this HMM previously was named CarO in error. Both this protein and CarO affect carbapenem transport across the outer member and thus carbapenem susceptibility or resistance.

label: FosLL
comment: This putative fosfomycin resistance glutathione transferase (WP_000777201.1) was detected in mobile island RGP23 in Acinetobacter baumannii D1279779, and identical proteins or close homologs found in many other Acinetobacter isolates. It is referred to as FosLL by Kyriakidis, at al. (PMID:33808905, 2021), consistent with usage in this HMM.

label: blaMCA
comment: This family was named, during HMM construction, as blaMCA, since it appears to be a Mobile Cephalosporinase of Acinetobacter.

label: pilus_FilE
comment: FilE is found almost exclusively in the genus Acinetobacter, and is assigned as a putative pilus system protein from local genomic contexts that include several additional putative pilus system proteins. Note that some members of this protein family have proline-rich repeat regions for which spurious translation in another reading frame can give a false-positive match to Pfam's collagen repeat region HMM, PF01391.

label: blaOXA-274_like
product_name: OXA-274 family carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase
hmm_name: OXA-274 family carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase
comment: The OXA-274 family of class D beta-lactamase is carbapenem-hydrolyzing. It is intrinsic in Acinetobacter guillouiae and some other Acinetobacter spp. It has not been seen in A. baumannii (as of 2022).

label: AceI_fam_PACE
product_name: AceI family chlorhexidine efflux PACE transporter
name_orig: AceI family chlorhexidine efflux PACE transporter
hmm_name: AceI family chlorhexidine efflux PACE transporter
comment: The AceI family of proton-coupled multidrug/biocide efflux transporters includes several shown to respond to the presence of the biocide chlorhexidine and improve resistance to it, among other biocides and antibiotics. Members of the family seen so far, including founding member AceI, have been chromosomal and restricted to the genus Acinetobacter.

label: OMP_CarO
comment: The outer membrane porin CarO (carbapenem resistance-associated outer membrane protein), found in Acinetobacter, is of clinical interest because of its role in allowing entry of carbapenem antibiotics and its variability from strain to strain. CarO should not be confused with Omp33-36, an essentially unrelated outer membrane protein that is similar in size and that also affects carbapenem susceptibility.

label: acineto_lipo_PV
comment: This small lipoprotein, about 60 amino acids long on average in precursor form, is widespread in the genus Acinetobacter. The motif PVxxxDY is conserved in most members. The function is unknown.

label: Zn_piracy_ZnuD
comment: ZnuD, as described in Acinetobacter baumannii, works with the zinc uptake transporter ZnuABC to overcome sequestration of zinc by the host. ZnuD, TonB-dependent receptor, pirates zinc from the host protein calprotectin. A similar ZnuD family protein, outside the current scope of this model, has been characterized in Neisseria.

label: blaOXA-679_like
product_name: OXA-679 family carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase
hmm_name: OXA-679 family carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase
comment: The founding member of this family, found in Acinetobacter calcoaceticus and capable of reducing susceptibility to carbapenems, provides high level carbapenem resistance if transferred experimentally to A. baumannii.

label: blaOXA-294_like
comment: The OXA-294 subfamily of class D beta-lactamases is known so far only in the genus Acinetobacter.

label: Ig_like_BLP2
comment: Blp2 (BAP-like protein 2), found broadly in the genus Acinetobacter, resembles the much larger biofilm-associated proteins Bap and Blp1 in N-terminal sequence and the presence of tandem Ig-like repeats.

label: blaOXA-1036_like
product_name: OXA-1036 family carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase
hmm_name: OXA-1036 family carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamase
comment: Members of this family are carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamases. OXA-664, as originally discovered, is non-functional because of a Trp-to-Stop nonsense mutation, but mutation from Stop to Trp restores carbapenemase activity (PMID:30247543). The closely related protein OXA-1036, naturally occuring as a full-length enzyme, is chromosomal in Acinetobacter sp. ACNIH2, isolated from hospital waste water (PMID:29437920), but since that carbapenem-resistant strain carries a plasmid-borne carbanemase as well, KPC-2, the contribution of OXA-1036 to resistance has not yet been investigated directly.

label: benzoate_BenM
comment: The LysR family transcriptional regulator BenM is both a paralog and a neighbor of CatM. Both transcription factors sense the catabolite cis,cis-muconate in order to play a role in benzoate catabolism. This model describes BenM.

label: KGW_Acineto
comment: Members of this family of small proteins are found in the genus Acinetobacter. The family is named for KGW motif that is its best-conserved motif, at the midpoint of the 40 amino acid length sequence. C-terminal to that motif, the sequence is extremely hydrophobic. Members are found encoded next to a YqfO/Nif3 family protein. The function is unknown.

label: immunity_TaeI
product_name: type VI secretion system immunity protein, TaeI family
hmm_name: type VI secretion system immunity protein, TaeI family
comment: TaeI, as found in Acinetobacter baumannii, is an immunity protein for the anti-fungal type VI secretion system effector DNase TafE (see BlastRule NBR016091).

label: V4R_TF_MobR
comment: MobR, as described originally in Acinetobacter calcoaceticus NCIB8250, is an NtrC-related sigma-54-dependent transcriptional activator of phenol degradation. The sequence, over 500 amino acids in length, includes a hydrocarbon-binding V4R sensor domain (see PF02830).

label: lipo_J517_1871
comment: Members of this predicted lipoprotein family are most common in the genus Acinetobacter. AlphaFold database entry A0A009H4E4 shows a confidence structural prediction, past the lipoprotein cleavage site, with extensive beta sheet structure.

label: acin_4_helix
comment: AlphaFold structural prediction for this family includes four alpha-helices, the first of which is likely to be a signal peptide. Members of this family are found, so far, exclusively in the genus Acinetobacter.

label: lipo_PTPT
comment: Members of this family are uncharacterized proteins, all of which share an apparent N-terminal lipoprotein signal peptide, followed by a variable length stretch of Pro-Thr dipeptide repeats or a related Pro-rich region, followed by the non-repetitive domain modeled by this HMM. A short stretch in the C-terminal region is hit weakly by Pfam model PF13783 (DUF4177), sometimes above cutoff scores, sometimes not.

label: efflu_CzcI_Acin
comment: Members of this family are metal resistance efflux proteins, related to the cobalt-zinc-cadmium transporter protein CzcI.

label: Acin_mostly_LP
comment: Members of this family are found primarily in the genus Acinetobacter. Members have four widely spaced invariant Cys residues, suggesting an extracytoplasmic (surface or periplasmic) location. About half the members of this family have an apparent lipoprotein signal peptide.

label: efflux_ABUW_0982
comment: ABUW_0982, a homolog of export permeases for the quorum system autoinducer AI-2E, was identified in Acinetobacter baumannii as a determinant of chloramphenicol resistance. ABUW_0982-like transporters are found broadly in the genus Acinetobacter. Exported compounds include 5-bromo-4-chloro-3-indolylphosphate (XP), a test substrate that is chromogenic when acted on by phosphatases, as well as chloramphenicol. In consultation with the communicating author of PMID:29891596, this family is assigned the gene symbol cxpE (Chloramphenicol and XP Efflux).

label: ABUW_2363_fam_LP
comment: ABUW_2363 from Acinetobacter baumannii was identified in a proteomics study as a periplasmic lipoprotein that is up-regulated in the presence of the antibiotic imipenem. Knockout mutants are dramatically more sensitive to killing by complement in normal human serum.

label: FilE_C
comment: This entry represents a domain found C-terminal in FilE protein. FilE is found almost exclusively in Acinetobacter, and is assigned as a putative pilus system protein from local genomic contexts that include several additional putative pilus system proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure similar to galactose-binding domains. (from Pfam)

label: blaASDC
comment: ASDC (Acinetobacter soli-derived cephalosporinase) is a family of chromosomal class C beta-lactamases, expected to have cephalosporinase activity. The most similar characterized enzyme, with near 70% identity, is the enzyme from Acinetobacter baylyi currently called ADC-8 (until the name is improved). Members are less than 50% identical to true ADC (Acinetobacter-derived cephalosporinase) enzymes, which are found exclusively in Acinetobacter baumannii.

label: blaOXA-1258_like
comment: This family of class D beta-lactamases is known primarily from Acinetobacter faecalis.

label: CellDivBlhA

hmm_name: A1S_1983 family putative colistin resistance protein
comment: Members of this family average 215 amino acids in length, with six invariant Cys residues, suggesting disulfide bond formation. The family is broadly distributed in Acinetobacter, but appears limited to that genus. Mutational studies suggest that this protein contributes to resistance to the antibiotic colistin.

label: blaAVDC
comment: AVDC (Acinetobacter venetianus-derived cephalosporinase) is a chromosomal class C beta-lactamase (AmpC), related to ADC from Acinetobacter baumannii, ASDC (Acinetobacter soli-derived cephalosporinase), and the well-studied by currently misnamed ADC-8.

label: pilus_FilA
comment: FilA is found almost exclusively in the genus Acinetobacter and is assigned as a putative pilus assembly protein from local genomic contexts that include several additional putative pilus system proteins.

label: pilus_FilB

FilB belongs to the C39 family peptidases, but its function in pilus assembly has not been elucidated yet.

label: pilus_FilC
comment: FilC is found almost exclusively in the genus Acinetobacter and is assigned as a putative pilus assembly protein from local genomic contexts that include several additional putative pilus system proteins.

label: pilus_FilD

comment: FilD is found almost exclusively in the genus Acinetobacter and is assigned as a putative pilus assembly protein from local genomic contexts that include several additional putative pilus system proteins. FilD belongs to the OmpP1/FadL family transporters, but its role in pilus assembly in Acinetobacter genus has not been elucidated.

label: ABZJ_00068_fam
comment: Members of this Acinetobacter protein family were shown to be the second most differentially up-regulated protein during colistin challenge in one study, and in a colistin-dependent mutant strain in another study. Member proteins are small, about 58 amino acids long, with a hydrophobic N-terminal putative membrane insertion domain, a well-conserved motif SAW in the middle in most proteins, and a rather poorly conserved C-terminal region rich in Asp, Asn, Glu, and Gln.

label: efflux_CraA
comment: CraA (chloramphenicol resistance Acinetobacter) is a Major Facilitator Superfamily (MFS) multidrug efflux transporter that appears responsible for natural resistance to chloramphenicol. It is found broadly in the genus Acinetobacter, and appears to be in essentially every well sequenced and assembled genome of Acinetobacter baumannii. CraA is just over 40% identical in amino sequence to the multidrug efflux MFS transporter MdfA of Escherichia coli.

label: efflux_OMP_AbuO

hmm_name: multidrug efflux outer membrane protein AbuO
comment: Mutation of AbuO, a TolC-family outer membrane protein found in the genus Acinetobacter, leads to increased susceptibility in A. baumannii to amikacin, streptomycin, tigecycline, ceftriaxone, meropenem, and hospital disinfectants, suggesting a role in multidrug efflux.

label: GlyGly_RbtA
comment: Members of this protein family are found, so far, exclusively in the genus Acinetobacter. Members average just over 600 amino acids in length, including a 22-amino acid C-terminal putative protein sorting recognition sequence, GlyGly-CTERM (TIGR03501). The GlyGly-CTERM signal always co-occurs with a subfamily of the rhomboid family intramembrane serine proteases called rhombosortase (TIGR03902). Members occur paired with a second rhombosortase target, with which it also shares an N-terminal motif CSLREA. This protein is designated Acinetobacter rhombotarget A (rbtA).

comment: Proteins in this family include an accessory subunit of the higher eukaryotic NADH dehydrogenase complex. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the Isd11 protein (Swiss:Q6Q560) has been shown to play a role in Fe/S cluster biogenesis in mitochondria (PMID: 16341090)(PMID: 16341089). label: auto_Ata
comment: Ata (Acinetobacter trimeric autotransporter) has an architecture that consists of a long signal peptide, a repetitive passenger domain that varies in length from strain to strain, and a C-terminal domain of four transmembrane beta stands that forms one third of the pore for autotransporter activity and anchoring in the outer membrane.

label: DUF7454
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins from a set of mycobacterial phage including phage Bxb1 (gene 86). The members of the family range in length from 50 to 90 residues. Structurally, the domain shows some weak similarity to the N-terminal domain of IF5, which adopts an SH3 like barrel fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7456
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in Mycobacterial phage. The family includes gene 48 from phage Bxb1. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7190
comment: This entry represents a putative membrane protein found in several mycobacteriophages, especially those belonging to the genus Cheoctovirus. The function is unknown. Most members contain a predicted transmembrane helix near the N-terminus. The family shows some length variation, especially at the C-terminus. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7466

The C-terminal regulatory domain adopts two OB-folds per monomer. These are similar in topology to those seen in the NBD (nucleotide binding domain) from the maltose uptake ABC transporter, MalK. However, FbpC does not open as far as MalK when ATP is removed from their respective closed structures. This difference was suggested to be due to the substantial domain swap in the regulatory domain of FbpC (PMID: 19748342). (from Pfam)

label: BIg21
comment: This entry represents BIg21(Bacterial Immunoglobulin-like 21) found in InvasinE (InvE). Invasins are members of the inverse autotransporter (IAT) family also referred to as type Ve secretion system. In general, they consist of an N-terminal beta-barrel-like domain, which is responsible for attachment of invasin to the outer membrane region of bacteria, repetitive Immunoglobuli-like (Ig) domains, which vary significantly in number among all the invasins, and the C-terminal domain/adhesion domain (AD) Pfam:PF05689, which provides invasins with the specificity to bind to its host target molecules. The overall structure of InvE shows that it comprises of three domain architecture in which the domains BIg20 (Bacterial Immunoglobulin-like 20) and BIg21 adopt two layer beta-sandwich fold resembling eukaryotic members of Immunoglobulin-superfamily (IgSF), while the AD is a globular, alpha/beta-domain. The structure of BIg21 belongs to the I2 set of IgSF with a unique modification in the C-E interstrand loop, important for its interaction with AD. BIg21 and AD form a functional super-domain as well, necessary to target the host receptor (PMID: 28370712). (from Pfam)

label: InvE_AD
comment: This entry represents the Adhesion domain found in InvasinE (invE). Invasins are members of the inverse autotransporter (IAT) family also referred to as type Ve secretion system. In general, they consist of an N-terminal beta-barrel-like domain, which is responsible for attachment of invasin to the outer membrane region of bacteria, repetitive Immunoglobulin-like (Ig) domains, which vary significantly in number among all the invasins, and the C-terminal domain/adhesion domain (AD), which provides invasins with the specificity to bind to its host target molecules. InvE-AD adopts a C-type lectin-like domain (CTLD)fold with unique modifications. The core structure of the adhesion domain (AD) is made up of a globular alpha/beta fold and can be divided into three sub-sections. The first is a lasso-shaped loop structure termed the "adaptor ring" since it forms a ring-shaped platform that connects BIg21 Pfam:PF05688 with the two residual sub-sections in the AD. These two residual subsections are the "C-type lectin-like domain" and the "wedge module". InvE-CTLD lacks the ability to coordinate Ca2+, and motifs such as EPN, QPD, and WND that are responsible for the specificity of carbohydrate recognition are also absent, giving rise to the notion that the InvE-CTLD is not a carbohydrate binding domain (PMID: 28370712). (from Pfam)

The adhesive sheath is composed of two proteins, AfaD and AfaE, which are independently exposed at the bacterial cell surface. comment: This family consists of several enterobacterial haemolysin (HlyE) proteins.Hemolysin E (HlyE) is a novel pore-forming toxin of Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhi, and Shigella flexneri. HlyE is unrelated to the well characterised pore-forming E. coli hemolysins of the RTX family, haemolysin A (HlyA), and the enterohaemolysin encoded by the plasmid borne ehxA gene of E. coli 0157. However, it is evident that expression of HlyE in the absence of the RTX toxins is sufficient to give a hemolytic phenotype in E. coli. HlyE is a protein of 34 kDa that is expressed during anaerobic growth of E. coli. Anaerobic expression is controlled by the transcription factor, FNR, such that, upon ingestion and entry into the anaerobic mammalian intestine, HlyE is produced and may then contribute to the colonisation of the host (PMID: 10660049). These proteins participate in the synthesis of phospholipids, suggesting the functional relationship between SecG and membrane phospholipids. Over-expression of gnsA and gnsB causes a remarkable increase in the unsaturated fatty acid content. However, the gnsA-gnsB double null mutant exhibits no effect. Both proteins are predicted to possess a helix-turn-helix structure (PMID: 11544213). GnsAB is a family of putative bacterial toxins (both GnsA and GnsB) that, are neutralised by the antitoxin YmcE, Pfam:PF15939 (PMID: 21927020). (from Pfam)

label: phage_tail_N
product_name: prophage tail fiber N-terminal domain-containing protein
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminus of prophage tail fibre proteins. (from Pfam)

label: Flagellin_D3
comment: This domain is found in the central portion bacterial flagellin FliC. The domain contains a structural motif called a beta-folium fold (PMID: 11268201). Although no specific function is assigned to this domain its deletion leads to a reduction in filament stability (PMID: 7860589). (from Pfam)

label: Aca2_YdiL
comment: This domain is found in Aca2 repressor from Pectobacterium phage ZF40, the uncharacterised protein YdiL from Escherichia coli and related sequences. Aca2 regulates the transcription and translation of phage anti-CRISPR acrIF8 gene through DNA binding and translationally by binding conserved RNA stem-loops on mRNAs. This protein contains six alpha-helices and two parallel beta-strands [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF1889
comment: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins. They are probably cytoplasmic proteins. (from Pfam)

label: SipA
comment: Salmonella invasion protein A is an actin-binding protein that contributes to host cytoskeletal rearrangements by stimulating actin polymerisation and counteracting F-actin destabilising proteins. Members of this family possess an all-helical fold consisting of eight alpha-helices arranged so that six long, amphipathic helices form a compact fold that surrounds a final, predominantly hydrophobic helix in the middle of the molecule (PMID: 16507363). (from Pfam)

label: Tafi-CsgC
comment: Fimbriae are cell-surface protein polymers, of eg. E coli and Salmonella spp, that mediate interactions important for host and environmental persistence, development of biofilms, motility, colonisation and invasion of cells, and conjugation. Four general assembly pathways for different fimbriae have been proposed, one of which is extracellular nucleation-precipitation (ENP), that differs from the others in that fibre-growth occurs extracellularly. Thin aggregative fimbriae (Tafi) are the only fimbriae dependent on the ENP pathway. Tafi were first identified in Salmonella spp and the controlling operon termed agf; however subsequent isolation of the homologous operon in E coli led to its being called csg. Tafi are known as curli because, in the absence of extracellular polysaccharides, their morphology appears curled; however, when expressed with such polysaccharides their morphology appears as a tangled amorphous matrix. The gene agfC is found to be transcribed at low levels, localised to the periplasm in a mature form, and in combination with AgfE is important for AgfA extracellular assembly, which facilitates the synthesis of Tafi. The genes involved in Tafi production are organised into two adjacent divergently transcribed operons, agfBAC and agfDEFG, both of which are required for biosynthesis and assembly (PMID: 17379722). (from Pfam)

label: PilI
product_name: type IV pilus biogenesis protein PilI
hmm_name: type IV pilus biogenesis protein PilI
comment: The thin pilus of plasmid R64 belongs to the type IV family and is required for liquid matings. pilI is one of 14 genes that have been identified as being involved in biogenesis of the R64 thin pilus (PMID: 9171405). According to structure prediction proteins in this family adopt a compact domain composed of five beta strands and an alpha helix between strands two and three. (from Pfam)

label: CedA
comment: CedA is made up of four antiparallel beta-strands and an alpha-helix. It activates cell division by inhibiting chromosome over-replication. This is mediated by binding to dsDNA via the beta-sheet. [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2525
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. The family has a highly conserved sequence. (from Pfam)

label: YliH
comment: YliH is induced in biofilms and is involved in repression of motility in the biofilms (PMID: 16597943). YliH is also known as bssR (regulator of biofilm through signal secreton). (from Pfam)

label: DUF2542
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. The family has a highly conserved sequence. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2545
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function is restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. The sequence is highly conserved. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2554
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2574
comment: This family of proteins appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. Members of the family are annotated as yehE however currently no function is known. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2686
comment: Some members in this family of proteins are annotated as yjfZ however currently no function is known. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2689
comment: Members in this family of proteins are annotated as TrbD however currently no function is known. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2737
comment: This family of proteins has no known function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2754
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appear to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2755
comment: Some members in this family of proteins are annotated as YaiY however no function is known. The family appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: Anti-RecBCD_p2
comment: This phage protein modulates the activity of the host recBCD nuclease promoting phage growth and recombination, and protects the linear double stranded DNA from exonuclease degradation (PMID: 10669596). (from Pfam)

label: HycA_repressor
product_name: Transcriptional repressor of hyc and hyp operons
name_orig: Transcriptional repressor of hyc and hyp operons
hmm_name: Transcriptional repressor of hyc and hyp operons
comment: This family is conserved in Proteobacteria. It is likely to be the transcriptional repressor molecule for the hyc and hyp operons, which express, amongst others, the protein HycA. This protein may be harnessed for the reduction of technetium oxide, an unwelcome product of radio-nucleotide bioaccumulation. HycA produces formate hydrogenlyase, one of the key proteins necessary for metal compound reduction (PMID: 17521447). (from Pfam)

label: PmrD
comment: The IraM/RssC family consists of anti-adapter proteins that play a crucial role in regulating the stability of the sigma stress factor RpoS, particularly during magnesium starvation. These proteins inhibit the proteolysis of RpoS by modulating the activity of the RssB protein, thereby enhancing the stability of RpoS. This regulation is vital for bacterial stress response, allowing cells to adapt to challenging environmental conditions. Some members of the family may also be involved in the early steps of isoprenoid biosynthesis, potentially through their role as RssB regulators. PmrB forms a two-component system (TCS) with PmrA that allows Gram-negative bacteria to survive the cationic antimicrobial peptide polymyxin G (PMID: 17686460). The TCS is linked to another one via the polymyxin resistance protein PmrD. PmrD is the first protein identified to mediate the connectivity between the two TCSs. It binds to the N terminal domain of the PmrA response regulator which prevents its dephosphorylation, thereby promoting the the transcription of genes involved in polymyxin resistance (PMID: 15371344). (from Pfam)

label: DUF2544
comment: This is a bacterial family of proteins with unknown function. (from Pfam)

label: MxiM
product_name: MxiM family type III secretion system pilotin
hmm_name: MxiM family type III secretion system pilotin
comment: MxiM, a Shigella pilot protein, is essential for the assembly and membrane association of the Shigella secretin MxiD. MxiM contains an orthologous secretin component and has a specific binding domain for the acyl chains of bacterial lipids (PMID: 15775974). The C terminal domain of MxiD hinders lipid binding to MxiM (PMID: 15775974). (from Pfam)

label: Colicin_Ia
product_name: colicin Ia central receptor-binding domain-containing protein
comment: Colicins are toxic molecules secreted to kill other bacteria in times of stress. Colicin Ia kills susceptible E.coli cells by binding to the colicin I receptor leading to the formation of a voltage-dependent ion channel. The protein can be divided into three domains, a translocation domain, a receptor binding domain and a channel forming domain (PMID: 17464289). (from Pfam)

label: Ig_GpJ_C
name_orig: Tip attachment protein J, C-terminal receptor binding domain
hmm_name: phage lambda tail tip protein J-like host specificity factor
comment: The founding member of this protein is phage lambda tail tip protein J, which confers host specificity by binding to E. coli protein LamB (maltoporin), the lambda receptor.

label: DUF3927
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and viruses. Proteins in this family are approximately 50 amino acids in length. There is a conserved SVL sequence motif. There is a single completely conserved residue D that may be functionally important. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4014
comment: This is a bacterial and viral family of uncharacterised proteins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4049
comment: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in bacteria, and is typically between 310 and 324 amino acids in length. According to structure prediction and comparison (DALI server) it is suggested that it may adopt a metallo-dependent phosphatase fold. (from Pfam)

label: Peptidase_M85
comment: This family of bacterial metallo-peptidases is thought to compromise the inflammatory response by degrading p65 thereby down-regulating the NF-kappaB signalling pathway (PMID: 21187904). NF-kappa-B is a pleiotropic transcription factor which is present in almost all cell types and is involved in many biological processes such as inflammation, immunity, differentiation, cell growth, tumorigenesis and apoptosis. NF-kappa-B is a homo- or heterodimeric complex formed by the Rel-like domain-containing proteins RELA/p65, RELB, NFKB1/p105, NFKB1/p50, REL and NFKB2/p52; and the heterodimeric p65-p50 complex appears to be most abundant one. (from Pfam)

label: TisB_toxin
product_name: Toxin TisB, type I toxin-antitoxin system
name_orig: Toxin TisB, type I toxin-antitoxin system
hmm_name: Toxin TisB, type I toxin-antitoxin system
comment: TisB (toxicity-induced by SOS B) is an SOS-induced toxic peptide. It is a hydrophobic membrane-spanning protein which inhibits cell growth (PMID: 18761622). Its expression is inhibited by the antisense RNA IstR-1, which acts as an antitoxin (PMID: 15620655). (from Pfam)

label: Ibs_toxin
product_name: type I toxin-antitoxin system Ibs family toxin
name_orig: Toxin Ibs, type I toxin-antitoxin system
hmm_name: type I toxin-antitoxin system Ibs family toxin
comment: The Ibs (induction brings stasis) proteins are a family of toxic peptides. Their expression is inhibited by the Sib antisense RNAs, which act as antitoxins (PMID: 18710431). (from Pfam)

label: SopA
comment: This domain is found in the E. coli Type III secretion effector proteins SopA and NleL [1,2]. These proteins have been shown to act as E3 ubiquitin ligase enzymes. (from Pfam)

label: YsaB
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. These proteins are related to E.coli YsaB Swiss:Q0TBP2. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 100 amino acids in length. These proteins are lipoproteins. (from Pfam)

label: YjcZ
product_name: diguanylate cyclase regulator RdcB family protein
hmm_name: diguanylate cyclase regulator RdcB family protein
comment: RdcB of E. coli (previously YjcZ), together with the GTPase RdcA, acts in the regulation of diguanylate cyclase DgcE.

label: MarB
product_name: multiple antibiotic resistance regulatory protein MarB
hmm_name: multiple antibiotic resistance regulatory protein MarB
comment: The MarB protein is found in the multiple antibiotic resistance (mar) locus in Escherichia coli. The MarB protein is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 70 amino acids in length. There is a conserved GSDKSD sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: PAGK
comment: PAGK represents a new of virulence factors that is translocated into the host cytoplasm via bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMV). Members are small proteins composed of ~70 amino acids. In Salmonella they are secreted independently of the SPI-2 type-III secretion system, T3SS. The OMV functions as a vehicle for transferring virulence determinants to the cytoplasm of the infected host cell. OMVs are released from the cell envelopes of Gram-negative bacteria and comprise a variety of outer membrane and periplasmic constituents, including proteins, phospholipids, lipopolysaccharides, and DNA (PMID: 21464085). (from Pfam)

label: Imm-NTF2-2
comment: The NTF2 fold immunity proteins in this family include two from Escherichia coli K-12, YhhH and YbbC, for toxins RhsB and RhsD, respectively.

label: YjeJ
comment: YjeJ is a family of bacterial proteins. The domains and proteins in this family vary in length from 283 to 284 amino acids. The function is not yet known. All proteins are Gammaproteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: YmcE_antitoxin
product_name: Putative antitoxin of bacterial toxin-antitoxin system
name_orig: Putative antitoxin of bacterial toxin-antitoxin system
hmm_name: Putative antitoxin of bacterial toxin-antitoxin system
comment: YmcE_antitoxin is the putative antitoxin for the supposed bacterial toxin GnsA, UniProtKB:P0AC92, family Pfam:PF08178 (PMID: 21927020). (from Pfam)

label: DUF4751
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 140 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4754
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4765
comment: This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 90 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: AIDA
name_orig: Adhesin of bacterial autotransporter system, probable stalk
hmm_name: Adhesin of bacterial autotransporter system, probable stalk
comment: The AIDA repeat is found on bacterial autotransporter proteins. As the repeat is short and occurs multiple times, it is likely to be the region of the transporter that acts as the stalk between the beta-barrel inserted into the membrane and the N-terminal head domain. (from Pfam)

label: EutK_C
comment: This is the C-terminal domain of the ethanolamine utilization protein EutK. It is a helix-turn-helix domain and is predicted to bind to nucleic acids (PMID: 20044574). (from Pfam)

label: YmgD
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 110 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: MGTL
comment: MGTL is a bacterial protein that makes mgtA transcription sensitive to intracellular proline levels. When the levels of proline are low, this protein is not able to be translated and stem loop'C' forms in the mgt A 5'UTR which enables the transcription of the downstream mgtA gene (PMID: 20813261). (from Pfam)

label: SafA
comment: SafA is a bacterial transmembrane protein family that connects the signal transduction between the two component systems EvgS/EvgA and PhoQ/Phop. SafA interacts with PhoQ, leading to the PhoQ/PhoP system activation in response to acid stress conditions (PMID: 17998538). (from Pfam)

label: YjbT
comment: This is a family of bacterial proteins. The function is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: CHASE7
comment: CHASE7 is a conserved periplasmic sensor domain found in histidine kinases and diguanylate cyclases/phosphodiesterases, including the diguanylate cyclase DgcQ (YedQ) that regulates biofilm formation and motility in Escherichia coli [1, 2]. (from Pfam)

label: GAPES1
comment: GAPES1 (GAmmaproteobacterial PEriplasmic Sensor) domain is a periplasmic sensor domain found in diguanylate cyclases and methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins, including the diguanylate cyclase DgcJ (YeaJ) that regulates biofilm formation and motility in Escherichia coli [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: GAPES2
comment: GAPES2 (GAmmaproteobacterial PEriplasmic Sensor) domain is a periplasmic sensor domain found in diguanylate cyclases, including the diguanylate cyclase DgcI (YliF) of Escherichia coli (PMID: 26148715). It contains three conserved Cys residues that might participate in thiol-disulfide exchange. (from Pfam)

label: PAP2_near_MCR1
comment: Members of this family belong to the PAP2 superfamily (see PF01569). The founding members of this family are notable for being encoded next to mcr-1, a phosphoethanolamine--lipid A transferase that confers resistance to colistin.

label: fosA7
product_name: FosA7 family fosfomycin resistance glutathione transferase
name_orig: FosA family fosfomycin resistance glutathione transferase
hmm_name: FosA7 family fosfomycin resistance glutathione transferase
comment: Members of this family are putative fosfomycin resistance glutathione transferases. Members have been observed in genetic islands in isolates of Salmonella, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, and Citrobacter.

label: auto_AIDA-I
comment: AIDA-I (adhesin involved in diffuse adhesion) belongs to a large family of autotransporter adhesins.

label: auto_Ag43
comment: Members of this family, restricted to Escherichia coli (including E. coli K-12) are the autotransporter adhesin Ag43 (antigen 43), also known as flu, or its calcium-binding homolog Cah, differing mostly in the central region. The C-terminal region forms an outer membrane beta-barrel autotransporter domain, which enables type V secretion (autotransport).

label: PmrR
comment: Members of this family are PrmR, and extremely small protein at 29 amino acids in length.

label: lat_flg_LafA_1
comment: This HMM describes rare second type of flagellin from E. coli and some closely related species, called LafA, where the familiar and common flagellin, FliC, is nearly universal and carries the H-antigen used for serotyping strains. In contrast to FliC, whose center region is highly variable, LafA shows little variability in sequence. In many E. coli strains, the Flag-2 locus either is absent or is cryptic, appearing degraded and non-functional.

label: YneK
comment: Members of this family, YneK, are found so far only in Escherichia coli and Escherichia albertii, with 68% sequence identity but in identical gene neighborhoods. In E. coli O157:H7 strain Sakai, yneK has a nonsense mutation and is therefore truncated. The function is unknown.

label: T6SS_TagK
product_name: type VI secretion system-associated protein TagK
name_orig: type VI secretion system-associated protein TagK
hmm_name: type VI secretion system-associated protein TagK
comment: Members of this family have full-length homology to SciF, a type VI secretion system (T6SS) protein from Salmonella typhimurium island SPI-6. Homologs occur in some but not all T6SS loci, and the broader family is now called TagK.

label: inverse_SinH
comment: SinH, also called SivH (Salmonella invasin homologue), is an inverse autotransporter associated with virulence.

label: Xis_Gifsy_1
comment: Members of this family are excisionases such as Xis from the Gifsy-1 prophage of Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium str. LT2.

label: phi80_GamL
comment: Members of this family, including GamL from phage phi80, are phage inhibitors of host nucleases such as RecBCD and SbcCD. This family has a distant relationship to Gam (see PF06064), which inhibits RecBCD.

label: toxin_EAST1
comment: EAST1, the enteroaggregative E. coli heat-stable enterotoxin 1, is encoded within the reading frame of the putative transposase of insertion sequence IS1414.

label: trnsprt_adja_30
comment: Members of this family are very small, highly hydrophobic proteins regularly encoded adjacent to transporters and likely to be previously overlooked small subunits of transporters.

label: STM0539_fam
comment: STM0539, from Salmonella enterica strain LT2, is the founding member of family of proteins of unknown function, about 145 amino acids in length.

label: NleE_fam_methyl
product_name: NleE/OspZ family T3SS effector cysteine methyltransferase
name_orig: NleE/OspZ family T3SS effector cysteine methyltransferase
hmm_name: NleE/OspZ family T3SS effector cysteine methyltransferase
comment: NleE from Escherichia coli O157:H7 strain Sakai, and its homolog OspZ from Shigella, are the founding members of a family of SAM-dependent protein--cysteine methyltransferases. Both are type III secretion system (T3SS) effectors involved in virulence, and have the host protein NF-kappa-B as substrates.

label: KPN_two_small
comment: Members of this family, including paralogs KPN_01023 and KPN_01923 from Klebsiella pneumoniae subsp. pneumoniae MGH 78578, are small proteins, typically 40 amino acids in length. A highly hydrophobic region, about 25 amino acids in length with a composition typical of transmembrane segments, is followed by a highly basic region of about 15 amino acids. Analogous proteins of similar size, with apparently similar hydrophobic regions, have been described as membrane-associated proteins expressed in response to various types of cell envelope stress.

label: sm_mem_Ecr
product_name: Ecr family regulatory small membrane protein
name_orig: Ecr family regulatory small membrane protein
hmm_name: Ecr family regulatory small membrane protein
comment: Ecr, as described in the genus Enterobacter, is a small membrane protein predicted to span the inner membrane. It was found to modulate expression of PhoP, part of the PhoP-PhoQ two component system, which in turn induces the arnBCADTEF operon, leading to modification of LPS and conferring elevated resistance to colistin. The form described in PMID:31169899 (WP_048029797.1), at 72 amino acids in length, is aberrant compared with the typical length for the majority of family members, about 46 residues.

label: fosA8
product_name: FosA8 family fosfomycin resistance glutathione transferase
name_orig: FosA8 family fosfomycin resistance glutathione transferase
hmm_name: FosA8 family fosfomycin resistance glutathione transferase
comment: FosA8, founding allele of the FosA8 family, is a fosfomycin resistance-conferring glutathione transferase. While FosA8 was discovered as a plasmid-borne protein in Escherichia coli, it derives from a chromosomal enzyme in Leclercia adecarboxylata.

label: MccV
comment: Family members are bacterial microcin-V peptides MccV, also known as colicin V. MccV was the first antibiotic substance reported to be produced by E. coli. This antibacterial agent was initially named colicin V (ColV). However, on account of several characteristics (low molecular mass, non-inducible production, and dedicated export system), it became classified within the microcins. The structural gene cvaC, encodes the 103-aa MccV precursor. The dedicated export system of MccV has been well characterized and involves two genes that form the second operon. The MccV protein has an N-terminal double glycine motif which precedes the cleavage site for the precursor protein (PMID: 17653356). (from Pfam)

label: DUF5448
comment: This is a family of unknown function found in Gammaproteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5384
comment: This is a family of unknown function found in Proteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5445
comment: This is a family of unknown function found in Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_spike_2
comment: This Pfam entry includes some phage spike repeats that fail to be detected with the Pfam:PF18715 model. (from Pfam)

label: HEPN_STY4199
comment: STY4199-like HEPN nuclease domain (PMID: 23768067). (from Pfam)

label: YqgC
comment: This is a family of unknown function found in Enterobacteriaceae such as E.coli and Shigella. (from Pfam)

label: CKI
comment: Colicins are bacterial toxins produced by Escherichia coli strains and are active against E. coli or related strains. These bacterial antibiotic toxins play an important role in the E. coli colonization of environmental niches. Colicin K uses the Tsx nucleoside-specific receptor for binding at the cell surface, the OmpA protein for translocation through the outer membrane, and the TolABQR proteins for the transit through the periplasm. The N-terminal domain interacts with components of its import machinery, including the TolB and TolQ proteins (PMID: 20870776). Members of this family are colicin K immunity proteins. These proteins are able to protect a cell against colicin K (PMID: 7592493). (from Pfam). Members of this family include Cki (colicin K immunity protein) for the pore-forming toxin Cka (colicin K activity protein), as well as immunity proteins from other related colicin systems.

label: LaoB_over_CadC
comment: LaoB (L-arginine responsive overlapping gene) is a small, rare protein, encoded in an antisense frame to the gene for CadC in some strains of Escherichia coli. CadC, in response to acid stress and the presence of sufficient lysine, activates expression of a lysine decarboxlation and lysine/cadaverine antiport system, which provides resistance to the acidity. Note that the current version of NCBI's Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline may not predict this protein.

label: stress_YobI
comment: YobI, as found in strains of Escherichia coli and Shigella sonnei, is a hydrophobic protein of very small size, 21 amino acids, whose expression increases after heat shock.

label: peptide_16_IlvX
comment: The very short peptide IlvX, 16 amino acids long, is found in Escherchia coli and related species as the apparent first encoded peptide from the ilvXGEDA operon, for which ilvL, further upstream, is the classical attentuator system leader peptide controlling expression. IlvX is preceded by a ribosome binding site, terminates just two nucleotides from ilvG, and has evidence of increased protein expression during isoleucine expression. Its biological role is unknown, and skepticism that IlvX has any molecular function after its biosynthesis may be appropriate.

label: DNZ54_00345_fm
comment: Members of this uncharacterized protein family appear to be membrane proteins, and are found in bacteria encoded within prophage regions.

label: div_DrpB_YedR
comment: DrpB (division ring protein B) is a non-essential cell division protein with a limited taxonomic range, found in enteric bacteria such as Escherichia coli.

label: DUF5951
comment: This entry represents a member of a biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC). This BGC (BGC0001805) is described by MIBiG as an example of the following biosynthetic class, NRP (non-ribosomal peptide). (from Pfam)

label: ydjY_domain
comment: The founding member of this family is the poorly characterized protein YdjY, an apparent lipoprotein, of Escherichia coli K-12. Many members are lipoproteins. YdjY and other members of its branch of the broader family have an invariant GCxxCxxxC motif.

label: peri_YbiM_McbA
comment: McbA (YbiM) is a member of the DUF1471 family found in Escherichia coli K-12, where it is one of many paralogs, but not found in Salmonella enterica LT2. Many members of the DUF1471 family of small enterobacterial periplasmic proteins participate in response to various forms of stress, such as low pH.

label: peri_RclB
product_name: reactive chlorine resistance periplasmic protein RclB
hmm_name: reactive chlorine resistance periplasmic protein RclB

label: toxic_TimP
product_name: small toxic inner membrane protein TimP
hmm_name: small toxic inner membrane protein TimP
comment: The gene timP (toxic inner membrane protein) occurs within the small structural RNA ryfA. Proteins of the TimP family can be found encoded in Escherichia coli, Salmonella enterica, Citrobacter, and Klebsiella sp.

label: trans_reg_YciT
comment: Involved in osmolarity control regulation. All members of the seed alignment are encoded near a gene encoding the small protein YciZ (also called DeoL).

label: small_YadW
comment: Next to a transporter, as common for small proteins. Supported by cross species conservation, proteomics, and ribosome profiling. Has some overlap with next gene, but hydrophobic then amphipathic, next to a transporter, looks good.

label: microcin_B17
comment: Microcin B17 is a thiazole/oxazole modified microcin (TOMM), a type of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide natural product (RiPP). It is a toxin that corrupts gyrase activity and causes gyrase to to cleave chromosomal DNA, killing the cell.

label: TusA_like_YeeD
comment: YeeD (TsuB) is a TusA family putative sulfurtransferase associated with thiosulfate utilization.

label: thio_trans_TsuA
comment: TsuA (YeeE) is one of two paralogous transporters in Escherichia coli described by Pfam model PF04143. TsuA, and adjacent putative sulfurtransferase TsuB, are involved in thiosulfate utilization.

label: YdaE_coli
comment: Members of this family include YdaE from the Rac prophage region of Escherichia coli K-12, a homolog from the Gifsy-1 prophage region of Salmonella enterica LT2, and related proteins from other closely related species. The presence of four conserved Cys residues has led to annotations as a zinc-binding protein or metallothionein, but the actual function seems unclear.

label: DDRRRQL_YjdP
comment: Members of this family average 108 amino acids in length, with a signal peptide and with a highly charged C-terminal region of typically five tandem 7-mer repeats approximated by DDRRRQL. The family is named for founding member YjdP from Escherichia coli K-12.

label: membrane_YkgR
comment: This family of stress response membrane proteins is named for the founding protein YkgR from Escherichia coli K-12. YkgR expression is induced by the cyclic AMP response protein (CRP), and the expressed protein is inserted into the inner membrane.

label: membrane_YoaI
comment: YoaI, a small membrane protein found in Escherchia coli, Salmonella enterica, Citrobacter rodentium, and other members of the Enterobacterales, averages about 34 amino acids in length. The founding member of this family, from Escherichia coli K-12, was shown to be regulated as part of the phosphate regulon.

label: membrane_YldA
comment: This family of small membrane proteins, averaging about 29 amino acids in length, is named for YldA of Escherichia coli K-12 but is found in multiple members of the Enterobacterales. The family appears homologous to YoaI, also found in Escherichia coli K-12.

label: membrane_YmiC

label: MlrA_helical

MlrA it is also known as YehV, and has been shown to control cell-cell aggregation by co-regulating the expression of curli and extracellular matrix production in Escherichia coli and Salmonella yphimurium (PMID: 11489123). MlrA is part of a signaling cascade that regulates curli biosynthesis. These proteins have dissimilar C-terminal domains that may bind specific coactivator molecules. This entry represents an helical domain, similar to the B12-binding module cap domain (Pfam:PF02607). (from Pfam)

label: MrkH_YcgR_like
comment: This entry represents the YcgR-like domain found at the N-terminal of MrkH (Swiss:G3FT00) from Klebsiella pneumoniae and similar sequences (PMID: 27650952) which contain a PilZ domain at the C-terminal. MrkH is a c-di-GMP-related transcriptional regulator that affects type 3 fimbrial expression in response to cellular c-di-GMP level, playing and important role in biofilm formation. This protein binds to the promoter regulation fragments of mrkHI and mrkA mainly through its PilZ domain and this YcgR-like domain also participates in DNA-binding (PMID: 27650952). (from Pfam)

label: FliC-like_3rd
comment: This domain is found in Flagellin from Salmonella dublin (FliC) and similar sequences from proteobacteria. FliC is the subunit protein which polymerises to form the filaments of bacterial flagella. Binding of FliC to the Toll-like receptor 5 (TLR5) leads to activation of innate immune responses against flagellated bacteria. It consists of four domains. This entry represents its third domain (PMID: 22344444). (from Pfam)

label: Csa_translocation_dom
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal translocation domain of Colicin S4 from Escherichia coli (Csa), a polypeptide toxin produced and active against E.coli. This protein consists of four distinct domains, this domain, two receptor-binding domains (Pfam:PF20761) and the C-terminal pore-forming domain (Pfam:PF01024). This domain shows an antiparallel beta-sheet formed by three strands, an extended, glycine-rich loop structure and a short helix (PMID: 19056731). (from Pfam)

label: HK620_9_C

label: YoaL

label: ElaD_SseL-like_N
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal helical domain found in a group of CE proteases from human pathogens, including ElaD from E.coli, SseL from Salmonella typhimurium and ShiCE from Shigella [1,2], which are dedicated deubiquitinases (DUBs), proteases that reverse the addition of ubiquitin to substrates, and effectively hijacks the host's ubiquitination processes (PMID: 27425412). This domain is structurally similar to VHS domains and it serves to localise the catalytic domain (Pfam:PF22102) through an additional Ub binding site (PMID: 32109687). (from Pfam)

label: VID

VirG/IcsA consists of three major domains: an atypical signal peptide at the N-terminal, followed by the passenger domain (presented on the cell surface) and a beta-domain that anchors the protein to the bacterial outer membrane. This entry represents the insertion domain (VID) that appears to be inserted into a continuous sequence of beta-helical coils (PMID: 28268178). (from Pfam)

This domain is found adjacent to the C-terminal autotransporter domain (Pfam:PF03797) and is part of the passenger domain that is transported through the autotransporter barrel. The BigA protein is a surface-exposed virulence factor in pathogenic bacteria such as Salmonella. While the autotransporter domain forms a beta-barrel for translocation, the specific function of this beta sandwich domain remains to be determined. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7943
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha- helical bundle. This domain is found in the hypothetical protein ESA_00282 from Cronobacter sakazakii that plays a significant role in biofilm formation and bacterial adhesion. This protein contributes to the adhesion of C. sakazakii to biotic surfaces, such as intestinal epithelial cells and play a role in the pathogenesis (PMID: 20118366). (from Pfam)

This domain is located N-terminal to the repetitive region in BigA proteins and is part of the passenger domain that is transported through the C-terminal autotransporter barrel. While the BigA protein has been implicated in bacterial virulence, the specific function of this N-terminal domain remains to be determined. (from Pfam)

label: BPP1_LPA

It may function as the transcriptional activator of all late P1 functions. The protein has DNA-binding activity. (from Pfam)

No homology is detected to functionally similar mammalian enzymes. Alternate names for this enzyme include CDP-diglyceride hydrolase and CDP-diacylglycerol hydrolase.

This family consists only of sorbitol (also called glucitol)-specific transporters, and occur both in Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria.The system in E.Coli consists of a IIA protein, and a IIBC protein. This family is specific for the IIA component.

comment: This subfamily belongs to the major facilitator family. Members include the oxalate/formate antiporter of Oxalobacter formigenes, where one substrate is decarboxylated in the cytosol into the other to consume a proton and drive an ion gradient.

label: MPGP_rel
comment: This family consists of members of the HAD superfamily, subfamily IIB. All members are closely related to mannosyl-3-phosphoglycerate phosphatase, the second enzyme in a two-step pathway for biosynthesis of mannosylglycerate, a compatible solute present in some thermophiles and in Dehalococcoides ethenogenes. However, members of this family are separable in a neighbor-joining tree constructed from a multiple sequence alignment and are found only in mesophiles that lack the companion mannosyl-3-phosphoglycerate synthase (TIGR02460). Members of this family are like to act on a compound related to yet distinct from mannosyl-3-phosphoglycerate.

label: true_RNase_BN
comment: Members of this protein family are ribonuclease BN of Escherichia coli K-12 and closely related proteins believed to be equivalent in function. Note that E. coli appears to lack RNase Z per se, and this protein of E. coli appears orthologous to (but not functionally equivalent to) RNase Z of Bacillus subtilis and various other species. Meanwhile, the yihY gene product of E. coli previously was incorrectly identified as RNase BN.

label: phageshock_pspE
comment: Members of this very narrowly defined protein family are proteins active as rhodanese (EC 2.8.1.1) and found in the extended variants of the phage shock protein (psp operon) in Escherichia coli and a few closely related species. Note that the designation phage shock protein PspE has been applied, incorrectly, in many instances where the genome lacks the phage shock regulon entirely.

comment: Members of this family are the TisB toxin protein of a type I toxin-antitoxin system, meaning that the antitoxin is a non-coding RNA. TisB is induced by some types of stress (SOS, ciprofloxacin) and appears to induce a persister state by dissipating transmembrane potential, thus depleting ATP. Persister cells, unable to grow until the persister state changes, survive a number of challenges, including exposure to most antibiotics.

Its homologue from humans, together with the TTT complex and HSP90, may participate in the proper folding of newly synthesised phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-related protein kinase (PIKK) proteins [1-4]. label: Mycop_pep_DUF31

comment: This domain is found in various uncharacterised proteins and putative lipoproteins from mycoplasmas. Although its function is not clear, it has been suggested that this is a serine protease domain; sequence analysis revealed that the amino acid sequence is similar to that of serine proteases. It is related to pathogenicity as this domain is present in proteins encoded by animal and human pathogenic Mycoplasmas [1,2,3]. It has been proposed that the Ig binding protein M may function together with this domain playing a role in evading host Ig-mediated defense against the MIB-MIP (mycoplasma Ig binding protein (MIB) and mycoplasma Ig protease (MIP)) system, which is a novel mechanism that protects mycoplasma against host immune response (PMID: 31497004). The major plasma membrane proteins, pMGAs, of Mycoplasma gallisepticum are cell adhesin (hemagglutinin) molecules. It has been shown that the genetic determinants that code for the haemagglutinins are organised into a large family of genes and that only one of these genes is predominately expressed in any given strain [1,2,3]. (from Pfam)

It is thought that it is important in cytadherence and virulence (PMID: 9632619). The N-terminus contains two predicted transmembrane helices followed by a long region of a short 6 residue proline rich repeat. (from Pfam)

label: P1_N

P1 forms a transmembrane complex with P40/P90 called the 'Nap', which mediates motility and infectivity [1,2,3]. Structure of P1, revealed that it consists of a large N-terminal domain consisting of seven consecutive beta-sheets each with four antiparallel beta-strands, except for the seventh which has two strands, and adopts a beta-propeller topology [2,3]. Those two strands correspond to the cytoadherence epitope which has important immune properties (PMID: 33057023). The N-terminal domain is highly variable and described as a structured core surrounded by a fuzzy surface (PMID: 33057023). (from Pfam)
