name_orig: Enriched in aromatic and glycine Residues box
hmm_name: Enriched in aromatic and glycine Residues box
comment: The Enriched in Aromatic and Glycine Residues (EAGR) box is found in proteins from Mycoplasma, often tandemly repeated, and may have a role in cell motility (PMID: 22925012). (from Pfam)

label: glycerol3P_ox_II
comment: This FAD-dependent enzyme (EC 1.1.3.21), glycerol-3-phosphate oxidase, also called L-alpha-glycerophosphate oxidase, converts sn-glycerol 3-phosphate plus oxygen to glycerone phosphate plus hydrogen peroxide, which contributes to virulence. This form, called type 2, is shorter than type 1 and is found exclusively in Mycoplasmas and other members of the Mollicutes.

label: Mplas_variab_LP
comment: This HMM describes a homology domain of lipoprotein signal peptides restricted to the genus Mycoplasma, and found in paralogous families that typically are associated with antigenic phase variation, as expression of some members of the family is turned on, others turned off, by the means promoter region modifications by site-specific DNA invertases. The avg family of Mycoplasma agalactiae represents one such family of lipoproteins.

label: DUF5378
comment: This is a family of unknown function which is found in Mycoplasmataceae.Family members are predicted to contain 7 trans-membrane regions (from Pfam)

label: DUF5396
comment: Members of this paralogous family Mycoplasma and Malacoplasma include MG_321 from M. genitalium and MPN456 from M. pneumoniae. Truncated proteins called MPN459, MPN458, and MPN457, if strung together, become a full-length homolog of MPN456 and therefore are likely pseudogenes. MPN459, MPN458, and MPN457

label: DUF5443
comment: This is a family of unknown function found in Mycoplasma. (from Pfam)

label: c-di-AMP_CdaM
comment: CdaM is one of several classes of diadenylate cyclase (the cyclic di-AMP synthesizing enzyme), characterized originally in Mycoplasma pneumoniae.

label: MGP3_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain from the Mycoplasma genitalium p110 adhesin protein. This domain has an Ig fold (PMID: 30367053). It is adjacent to the membrane. This domain contains a bound potassium ion (PMID: 30367053). (from Pfam)

label: MG075_fam
product_name: P116 family lipid acquisition surface protein
hmm_name: P116 family lipid acquisition surface protein
comment: MPN_213 from Mycoplasma pneumoniae, named P116, is an essential surface protein, shown to form a homodimer with a large hydrophobic cavity, and to play a role in obtaining lipids such as phosphatidylcholine, sphingomyelin, and cholesterol.

label: lipo_P68
comment: Surface lipoproteins of this family that are discussed in the literature include Mhp390 and Mhp378 from Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae, MbovP579 from Mycoplasma bovis, and MPN284 from Mycoplasma pneumoniae. The latter appears to be contribute to glycerol transport, while Mhp390 is described as a contributor to adherence to host cells and to inflammation.

label: UU052_fam
comment: Members of this family are found broadly in Ureaplasma (e.g. UU052), Mycoplasma (e.g. MSC_0620), Mesomycoplasma, and related genera. Neighboring proteins include paralogs to the alpha, beta, gamma, and epsilon subunits of the F1 ATPase, and are subunits of a related complex found only in the Mycoplasmatota. This subunit includes transmembrane domains and is designated X0.

label: MYPU_1760_HExxH
comment: Members of this family average over 600 amino acids in length, and contain a region similar to a region of PF04228 family zinc metalloproteases, including the signature motif HEYxH. Members seem to be limited to the phylum Mycoplasmatota.

label: P60_lipo
comment: In Metamycoplasma hominis and other members of the phylum Mycoplasmatota, lipoprotein P60 and membrane protein P80 for a complex that interacts with HinT, a lineage-specific subgroup of the cytosolic histidine triad (HIT) family of proteins. A subset of the members of this family contain an additional central region of about 100 amino acids.

label: MMB_0454_fam
comment: This family, restricted to the phylum Mycoplasmatota, shows evidence of homology to some members of the Asp23 family (see PF03780), named for a Staphylococcus aureus stress protein called alkaline shock protein 23.

label: Mplas_Cys_pep
comment: This HMM describes a region about 240 amino acids long with local similarity to C39 and C10 family cysteine peptidases, including the region of the active site Cys. Most members of this family occur in the phylum Mycoplasmatota.

label: MG289_thiam_LP
product_name: ABC transporter thiamine pyrophosphate-binding lipoprotein p37/Cypl
hmm_name: ABC transporter thiamine pyrophosphate-binding lipoprotein p37/Cypl
comment: Members of this family, restricted to the phylum Mycoplasmatota, are surface lipoproteins encoded as part of an ABC transporter operon, and shown to bind thiamine pyrophosphate, although not directly demonstrate to act in ABC transport of that substrate. The protein has attracted attention for links to oncogenic transformation and host cell invasiveness. This model resembles Pfam model PF06646, but covers the length of member proteins PF06646 and is more narrowly defined.

label: SHxHSH_motif_LP
comment: Members of this family are lipoproteins from the Mycoplasmoidales. Members average about 330 amino acids in length, with average pairwise identity below 40 percent, but with strong conservation of the motif KNSHxHSHA, with three invariant His residues in a span of five residues. The function is unknown.

label: Ig_SerProt_MIP
hmm_name: MIP family Ig-specific serine endopeptidase, C-terminal region
comment: MIP (Mycoplasma immunoglobulin protease) is a serine protease that occurs on the surface of Mycoplasmas and related species. In the presence of MIB (Mycoplasma immunoglobulin binding protein), MIP is able to cleave IgG, IgA, and IgM heavy chains, contributing to evasion of immunity. This HMM identifies a subset of the much broader family of Mycoplasma serine protease family PF01732 (DUF31). Several paralogs of this family may be found in a single genome, usually including one encoded close to the gene for MIB, and therefore most likely to qualify as MIP itself (see the more specific model NF045842).

label: MIP_near_MIB
comment: MIP (Mycoplasma immunoglobulin protease) is a serine protease that occurs on the surface of Mycoplasmas and related species. In the presence of MIB (Mycoplasma immunoglobulin binding protein), the serine protease MIP, surface lipoprotein, is able to cleave IgG, IgA, and IgM heavy chains, contributing to evasion of immunity. This HMM identifies a narrow subset of the broader family NF045841 and of the much broader family of Mycoplasma serine proteases described by PF01732 (DUF31). Nearly all members of this family are encoded next to or within 10 kB the Mycoplasma immunoglobulin-binding protein MIB, which enables MIP to perform its cleavage.

label: MAG2960_Ser_prot
comment: Members of this family, including founder protein MAG2960 from Mycoplasma agalactiae, are serine endopeptidase surface lipoproteins in the DUF31 (PF01732) family, but are quite different in sequence from the Ig-specific serine endopeptidase MIP (see NF045842).

label: MGA1079_SerProt
hmm_name: MGA_1079 family surface serine endopeptidase, C-terminal domain
comment: MGA_1079 from Mycoplasma gallisepticum str. R, the founding member of this family, was identified as one of two putative peptidases in the strain, with a trypsin-like peptidase motif in the 900 amino acid C-terminal homology domain it shares exclusively with other members of the Mycoplasmoidales. Full-length members of the proteins average about 2000 amino acids in length, with lipoprotein-type signal peptides indicating a cell surface location, followed by a region highly variable in length, averaging about 1000 amino acids, with little conservation between species. In species such as Mycoplasmopsis canis or Mycoplasmopsis meleagridis, three or more paralogs may be found. MGA_1079 mutants showed greatly reduced ability to maintain infection in chicken respiratory tract, suggesting that members of this family are virulence factors.

label: ABC_Mplas_LP
product_name: OppA family ABC transporter substrate-binding lipoprotein
hmm_name: OppA family ABC transporter substrate-binding lipoprotein
comment: Members of this family are surface lipoproteins of the Mycoplasmoidales, bacteria that a plasma membrane but no outer membrane and no cell well. Members are associated with ABC transporter permease and ATPase subunit, and assigned a role in oligopeptide import, but have additional functions such as cytoadhesion.

label: mem_nucl_MnuA
comment: Members of this family are nucleases expressed on the cell surface of bacteria belonging to the Mycoplasmoidales. This HMM describes the well-conserved C-terminal domain. The N-terminal regions of member proteins have either a lipoprotein signal peptide or an uncleaved signal-anchor sequence, followed by a poorly conserved region highly variable in length. A number of related proteins, excluded by this model, have a circularly permuted form of the nuclease domain. The ability of membrane nuclease to degrade neutrophil extracellular traps likely contributes to virulence.

However, it has an N-terminal extension signature region that those other proteins lack.

label: GGPL_Ptran_Mf1
comment: Mf1 in Mycoplasma fermentans produces GGPL-I from alpha-glucopyranosyl-1,2-dipalmitoilglycerol and CDP-choline. GGPL-I is 6'-O-phosphocholine-alpha-glucopyranosyl-(1'-3)-1,2-diacylglycerol.

label: PheT_Nterm_rel
product_name: TyrS-associated PheT N-terminal domain-related protein TapR
hmm_name: TyrS-associated PheT N-terminal domain-related protein TapR
comment: This family of proteins, found exclusively in the Mycoplasmoidales, is related to PheT (phenylalanine--tRNA ligase subunit beta), found in the same species, but always encoded next to the tyrosine--tRNA ligase TyrS, and perhaps involved in tyrosine--tRNA ligase function. We name this probable tRNA-binding protein TapR (TyrS-Associated PheT-Related).

label: MPN551_DNA_bnd
comment: Members of this family include the DNA-binding protein MPN551 of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and are more distantly related to nucleases such as phage lambda exonuclease.

label: UU173_fam
comment: The founding member of this family, UU173 of Ureaplasma parvum, is mentioned briefly as a protein encoded next to an element that encodes UU172, a phase-variable surface membrane protein paralogous to multiple-banded antigen (MBA). A small region with this family is called DUF2779 by Pfam model PF11074.

label: MAGa7180_fam_nucl
comment: Members of this family are restricted to the Mycoplasmoidales order of bacteria. The family belongs to the YqaJ-like viral recombinase, which includes YqaJ, encoded in a prophage region of Bacillus subtilis 168, as well as the exonuclease of phage lambda. Despite that relationship, members appear in genomic contexts that suggest a bacterial rather than viral function.

label: ICE_Mbov_0400
comment: Members of this family that have been identified as belonging to Integrating Conjugative Elements (ICE) include Mbov_0400 from Mycoplasmopsis bovis, MLC_3590 and MLC_3600 from Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri, and MAGa3690 from Mycoplasma agalactiae.

label: ICE_Mbov_0399
comment: Members of this family, such as Mbov_0399 from Mycoplasmopsis bovis, MAG3890 from Mycoplasma agalactiae, and SFLOR_RS04885 from Spiroplasma floricola, are large proteins from Integrating Conjugative Elements (ICE) of a type related to VirB-like type IV secretion systems and prevalent in the Mycoplasmatota.

label: ICE_LP_CDS14
comment: Integrative conjugative elements (ICE) in Mycoplasma-related wall-less bacteria undergo lateral gene transfer by mechanisms that require living donor and recipient cells. Members of this highly diverse family are large lipoproteins encoded in ICE loci. A founding member of the family, CDS14, was shown to be required to enable DNA transfer. Note that as with most or all protein families active in the spread of selfish genetic elements, truncated forms are common and in most cases should represent pseudogenized remnants.

label: MAG6090_repeat
comment: This short domain, often tandemly repeated, is observed only in surface lipoproteins of wall-less Mycoplasma-like bacteria.

label: MAG0110_fam
comment: MAG0110, a strongly hydrophobic integral membrane protein, is a homolog of the eukaryotic protein BAX inhibitor-1 (BI-1) and of the uncharacterized seven transmembrane helix protein YbhL of Escherichia coli. This HMM describes a family of MAG0110 and its homologs that is restricted to Mycoplasma and related bacteria that similarly lack a cell wall.

label: DCM_methyl_Nterm
comment: This HMM describes a protein region of a restriction system that occurs only in the Mycoplasmatota, as either the N-terminal region of a DNA (cytosine-5-)-methyltransferase or as a small protein, probably a small subunit, encoded next to a larger DNA (cytosine-5-)-methyltransferase subunit. Members of this family are found encoded near MAG4270 family putative restriction endonucleases (see NF045952). Member protein MAG4250 (CAL59123.1) is suggested to be a pseudogene, but the wide distribution of split forms of the DNA (cytosine-5-)-methyltransferase, in over twenty species, suggests the protein is functional. Because a region of GA dinucleotide repeats occurs near the end of the coding region for this domain (translating to Arg-Glu dipeptide repeats) in multiple short versions of this protein, we suggest that this N-terminal domain/subunit is always made, but that production of a full-length methyltransferase may be phase-variable in some species.

label: MAG1430_dom
hmm_name: MAG1430 family putative surface protein central domain
comment: This HMM describes a well-conserved central region of putative proteins from the Mycoplasmatota. Member proteins have apparent N-terminal signal-anchor sequences but are not lipoproteins. The family is highly divergent, but the motif S[FY]ANDxxGxL[FY]L is extremely well conserved. The function is unknown.

label: MHO_1590_dom
comment: Members of this family average about 145 amino acids in length, with a signal peptide, a variable length low-complexity region rich in N, D, Q, E, K, and R, and the roughly 80 amino acid C-terminal region described by this HMM. A few members of the family have candidate lipoprotein signal peptides. The family is named for member protein MHO_1590 from Mycoplasma hominis.

label: LppA_rel_LP
comment: This HMM describes a core region shared by members of TIGR03490 and an additional, broader set of surface lipoproteins of the Mycoplasmatota. Although this model is largely redundant with TIGR03490, the high variability of surface lipoproteins in the lineage makes this HMM helpful in their classification.

label: MAG5150_fam_LP
comment: Members of this family, including founding member MAG5150 from Mycoplasma agalactiae, are lipoproteins from the Mycoplasmatota. The most conspicuous feature after the lipoprotein signal peptide is an invariant HxHSH motif.

label: RibF_rel
comment: Members of this family appear to be variant forms of FAD synthase.

label: YcsE_rel_Pase
comment: Members of this family, restricted to the Mycoplasmatota, resemble 5-amino-6-(5-phospho-D-ribitylamino)uracil phosphatase YcsE from Bacillus subtilis, a HAD family phosphatase that can perform a dephosphorylation step to complete the bioysnthesis of riboflavin. Members are nearly always encoded next to an Mycoplasmatota-only enzyme involved in the biosynthesis of FAD from riboflavin and related to other FAD synthetases.

label: mutase_MAG5620
comment: Members of this family, restricted to the Mycoplasmatota, are uncharacterized, but show distant homology to phosphomannomutases and phosphoglucomutases.

label: trig_like_plasma
comment: Members of this family, restricted to the Mycoplasmatota, resemble trigger factor (see TIGR00115) more than it resembles other chaperones such as SurA, and appears along with trigger factor, as a paralog, in Mycoplasmopsis species such as M. iners, M. columbina, M. phocirhinis, M. alligatoris, etc.

label: VirB4_plasma
product_name: Mbov_0397 family ICE element conjugal transfer ATPase
hmm_name: Mbov_0397 family ICE element conjugal transfer ATPase

label: MAG1360_fam
comment: Members of this family, found in the Mycoplasmatota, resemble the ATP-binding protein OppF of oligopeptide transporters, but lack the P-loop motif (GxxGxGKT) that signifies ATP-binding.

label: MAG6410_fam_LP
comment: This HMM describes the C-terminal 625 amino acid transglutaminase-related domain of the MAG6410 family of lipoproteins. The additional N-terminal region of family members, averaging about 145 residues in length, begins with a lipoprotein signal peptide, but then is highly variable in both length and sequence.

label: MAG0865_DivIVA
comment: Members of this family average about 80 amino acids in length, and appear to be a variant short form of DivIVA-related protein in a subset of Mycoplasma-like species. The function of these proteins is uncertain, as authentic DivIVA appears to play a role in cell wall morphogenesis, while species containing this protein instead lack a peptidoglycan-containing cell wall. Note that Pfam model PF05103 describes a region of about 130 amino acids that is well conserved in authentic DivIVA proteins.

label: MAG0920_fam
comment: Members of this family include Mbov_0101 and Mbov_0775 from Mycoplasmopsis bovis, and two paralogs also from Mycoplasmopsis agalactiae. The family is named after MAG0920 from M. agalactiae.

label: cleave_ABC_plasm
product_name: Mbov_0121 family peptidase domain-containing ABC transporter
hmm_name: Mbov_0121 family peptidase domain-containing ABC transporter
comment: Members of this family, found in Mycoplasmopsis bovis and related species, contain an N-terminal C39-family cysteine peptidase domain, followed by an ABC transporter permease domain and an ABC transporter ATP-binding cassette domain. This architecture is typical of transporters that combine cleavage of a bacteriocin or peptide pheromone precursor at a Gly-Gly dipeptide site with export from the cell. However, so far no peptide precursor has been detected near members of this family.

label: SecDF_plasm

label: ICE_Mbov_0401
product_name: Mbov_0401 family ICE element transposase-like protein

comment: Members of this family, including founding protein Mbov_0401 from Mycoplasmopsis bovis, resemble transposases of the ISLre2 family of insertion sequences (IS elements), but instead are restricted to the Mycoplasmatota and occur in integrating conjugative elements (ICE) there.

label: MAGa3780_fam
comment: Members of this family, such as MAGa3780 from Mycoplasmopsis agalactiae, are membrane proteins. This family appears to be a sister family to the Pr6Pr family membrane proteins described by model NF038065, based on work by TCDB.

label: memb_MPN527
product_name: MPN527 family putative ECF transporter permease subunit
hmm_name: MPN527 family putative ECF transporter permease subunit
comment: Members of this family are membrane proteins, restricted to the Mycoplasma, Ureaplasma, and similar genera. Similarity to proteins in the family of PF12822 (ECF transporter, substrate-specific component) suggests a transport function, although no substrate is known.

label: P116
comment: The P116 protein (MPN213) from Mycoplasma pneumoniae is an essential cell surface protein that extracts lipids, including cholesterol, phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin, from the host environment for incorporation into the bacterial membrane. The structure of P116, solved by cryo-electron microscopy, reveals a novel protein fold consisting of a homodimeric core domain with a large hydrophobic cavity that binds and extracts lipids. Each monomer also contains an N-terminal domain. Conformational changes between the lipid-bound and lipid-free states suggest a mechanism for lipid uptake and delivery into the mycoplasma membrane. P116 orthologs are found in several other Mycoplasma species (PMID: 36782049). (from Pfam)

label: Mycoplas_LppA
comment: Members of this family the lipoprotein LppA, or its paralogs, as the name is used in Mycoplasma mycoides, Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae, and closely related Mycoplasma species. Note that the designation LppA, derived from the name "lipoprotein A", has been used also for unrelated lipoproteins from other lineages. Note that the name for certain characterized members, p72, reflects an anomalous apparent molecular weight, given a theoretical MW of about 61 kDa.

label: EAGR_box
comment: The EAGR box (Enriched in Aromatic and Glycine Residues) is found in three different proteins of the Mycoplasma genitalium terminal organelle, which acts in both cytadherence and gliding motility. The presence of this domain in a genome predicts the Mycoplasma-type terminal organelle structure, gliding motility, and cytadherence. The EAGR box may occur from one to nine times in a protein.

label: aro_clust_Mycop
comment: Members of this family are absolutely restricted to the Mollicutes (Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma). All have a signal peptide, usually of the lipoprotein type, suggesting surface expression. Most members have lengths of about 280 residues but some members have a nearly full-length duplication. The mostly nearly invariant residue, a Trp,is part of a strongly conserved 9-residue motif, [ND]-W-[LY]-[WF]-X-[LF]-X-N-[LI], where X usually is hydrophobic. Because the hydrophobic six-residue core of this motif almost always contains three to four aromatic residues, we name this family aromatic cluster surface protein. Multiple paralogs may occur in a given Mycoplasma, usually clustered on the genome.

label: mycoplas_M_dom
comment: This model defines a domain restricted to Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma proteins. Members include protein M of Mycoplasma genitalium, MG_281, a virulence protein that binds the IgG light chain to block the binding of antibody to antigen. The crystal structure of the protein M antibody-binding region is solved (PDB|4NZR), and includes this homology domain. Full-length homologs to MG_281 are known in a few other Mycoplasma species, but this model's seed alignment demonstrates distant homology to many additional proteins with a much wider distribution across the Mollicutes. Member proteins include paralogous families in some species, such as MCAP_0345, MCAP_0347, MCAP_0349, and MCAP_0351 in Mycoplasma capricolum.

label: predic_Ig_block
comment: Members of this family are putative virulence proteins of Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma species. Members share a region of sequence similarity (see TIGR04524) with protein M, a Mycoplasma genitalium protein that binds a conserved light chain region of IgG and blocks its protective function of antigen-specific binding. The seed alignment for this model includes an N-terminal signal-anchor domain and a proline-rich linker domain, and a C-terminal extension, in addition to the protein M-like domain recognized by TIGR04524.

label: 3TM_mycoplas
comment: Members of this rare family are small, highly hydrophobic, and restricted so far to the genus Mycoplasma, where it appears not be be essential. All members have three hydrophobic transmembrane helical segments.

label: blaACT
product_name: ACT family cephalosporin-hydrolyzing class C beta-lactamase

hmm_name: ACT family cephalosporin-hydrolyzing class C beta-lactamase

label: blaCMH
comment: CMH is a class C beta-lactamase regularly found in the chromosome of Enterobacter cloacae in a seemingly non-mobile context. Early examples of members from the family, CMH-1 (AFI56422.1) and CMH-2 (AKC92684.1) were inferred to be plasmid-borne based demonstrations of transfer, but the sequences provided do not provide flanking sequence and therefore do not provide evidence from genomic context.

hmm_name: CMY2-MIR-ACT-EC family cephalosporin-hydrolyzing class C beta-lactamase
comment: This HMM identifies a small subset of chromosomal class C beta-lactamases (AmpC) typical of Enterobacter cancerogenus.

label: LsoB_effector
comment: Proteins of this family are short effectors of Candidatus Liberibacter solanacearum (Lso). They play important roles in plant iImmune responses.

label: PRK15386.1-5
product_name: EspK/GogB family type III secretion system effector
hmm_name: EspK/GogB family type III secretion system effector
comment: Members of this family, typically found in some strains of Escherichia coli, are a type III secretion system (T3SS) effector homologous at about 70% identity to EspK from enterohaemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC), and at about 32% identity to the anti-inflammatory effector GogB from Salmonella enterica.

label: Tir_receptor_M
comment: Intimin and its translocated intimin receptor (Tir) are bacterial proteins that mediate adhesion between mammalian cells and attaching and effacing (A/E) pathogens. A unique and essential feature of A/E bacterial pathogens is the formation of actin-rich pedestals beneath the intimately adherent bacteria and localised destruction of the intestinal brush border. The bacterial outer membrane adhesin, intimin, is necessary for the production of the A/E lesion and diarrhoea. The A/E bacteria translocate their own receptor for intimin, Tir, into the membrane of mammalian cells using the type III secretion system. The translocated Tir triggers additional host signalling events and actin nucleation, which are essential for lesion formation (PMID: 10890451). This family represents the Tir intimin-binding domain (Tir IBD) which is needed to bind intimin and support the predicted topology for Tir, with both N- and C-terminal regions in the mammalian cell cytosol (PMID: 11207537). (from Pfam)

label: SepZ
comment: SepZ is a component of the type III secretion system use in bacteria. SepZ is a gene within the enterocyte effacement locus. SepZ mutants exhibit reduced invasion efficiency and lack of tyrosine phosphorylation of Hp90 (PMID: 8878013). (from Pfam)

label: DUF1106
comment: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins found in Escherichia coli and Citrobacter rodentium. The function of this family is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Tir_receptor_C
comment: Intimin and its translocated intimin receptor (Tir) are bacterial proteins that mediate adhesion between mammalian cells and attaching and effacing (A/E) pathogens. A unique and essential feature of A/E bacterial pathogens is the formation of actin-rich pedestals beneath the intimately adherent bacteria and localised destruction of the intestinal brush border. The bacterial outer membrane adhesin, intimin, is necessary for the production of the A/E lesion and diarrhoea. The A/E bacteria translocate their own receptor for intimin, Tir, into the membrane of mammalian cells using the type III secretion system. The translocated Tir triggers additional host signalling events and actin nucleation, which are essential for lesion formation (PMID: 10890451). This family represents the Tir C-terminal domain which has been reported to bind uninfected host cells and beta-1 integrins although the role of intimin binding to integrins is unclear. This intimin C-terminal domain has also been shown to be sufficient for Tir recognition (PMID: 11207537). (from Pfam)

label: Tir_receptor_N
comment: Intimin and its translocated intimin receptor (Tir) are bacterial proteins that mediate adhesion between mammalian cells and attaching and effacing (A/E) pathogens. A unique and essential feature of A/E bacterial pathogens is the formation of actin-rich pedestals beneath the intimately adherent bacteria and localised destruction of the intestinal brush border. The bacterial outer membrane adhesin, intimin, is necessary for the production of the A/E lesion and diarrhoea. The A/E bacteria translocate their own receptor for intimin, Tir, into the membrane of mammalian cells using the type III secretion system. The translocated Tir triggers additional host signalling events and actin nucleation, which are essential for lesion formation (PMID: 10890451). This family represents the Tir N-terminal domain which is involved in Tir stability and Tir secretion (PMID: 11207537). (from Pfam)

label: T3SchapCesA
product_name: type III secretion system filament chaperone
name_orig: Type III secretion system filament chaperone CesA
hmm_name: type III secretion system filament chaperone
comment: This family represents a chaperone protein for the type III secretion system - TTSS - translocon protein EspA, to prevent the latter's self-polymerisation. The TTSS is a highly specialised bacterial protein secretory pathway, similar in many ways to the flagellar system, that is essential for the pathogenesis of many Gram-negative bacteria. The twenty or so proteins making up the TTSS apparatus, referred to as the needle complex, allow the injection of virulence proteins (known as effectors) directly into the cytoplasm of the eukaryotic host cells they infect; however, the injection process itself is mediated by a subset of extracellular proteins that are secreted by the needle complex to the bacterial surface and assembled into the type III translocon - EspA. EspB and EspD. EspA polymerises into an extracellular filament, and, as with other fibrous proteins, is apt to undergo massive polymerisation when overexpressed. CesA is the secretion chaperone protein that binds to EspA. CesA is dimeric and helical, and it traps EspA in a monomeric state and inhibits its polymerisation. (from Pfam)

The protein has a cluster of exposed hydrophobic side-chains at one end and structural homology to the pore-forming proteins perfringolysin O and alpha-haemolysin. label: Mpv17_PMP22
comment: The 22-kDa peroxisomal membrane protein (PMP22) is a major component of peroxisomal membranes. PMP22 seems to be involved in pore forming activity and may contribute to the unspecific permeability of the organelle membrane. PMP22 is synthesised on free cytosolic ribosomes and then directed to the peroxisome membrane by specific targeting information (PMID: 11590176). Mpv17 is a closely related peroxisomal protein. In mouse, the Mpv17 protein is involved in the development of early-onset glomerulosclerosis (PMID: 11327696). More recently a homolog of Mpv17 in S. cerevisiae has been been found to be an integral membrane protein of the inner mitochondrial membrane where it has been proposed to have a role in ethanol metabolism and tolerance during heat-shock (PMID: 15189984). Defects in MPV17 is associated with mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome (MDDS) and Navajo neurohepatopathy (NNH) (PMID: 16582910)(PMID: 16909392). MDDS is a clinically heterogeneous group of disorders characterised by a reduction in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copy number. Primary mtDNA depletion is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait and may affect single organs, typically muscle or liver, or multiple tissues. Individuals with the hepatocerebral form of mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome have early progressive liver failure and neurologic abnormalities, hypoglycemia, and increased lactate in body fluids. NNH is an autosomal recessive disease that is prevalent among Navajo children in the South Western states of America. ToxS serves as a mediator of ToxR function, perhaps by influencing its stability and/or capacity to dimerize, hence ToxS plays an important function in transcriptional activation of Vibrio cholerae virulence genes (PMID: 20053280). Some AHLs are synthesized by LuxM (AHL synthase) and homologs (VanM and opaM)(PMID: 26655754). LuxM enzymes use S-adenosyl-methionine (SAM) as one of its two substrates and are capable of using either acyl-acyl-carrier-protein (acyl-ACP) or acyl-coenzyme A (acyl-CoA) as the other substrate (PMID: 22825856). VanM, the LuxM homolog, produces two auto-inducers C6HSL and 3OC6HSL. Both autoinducers are detected by the VanN receptor. The autoinducers HAI-1, is synthesized by the cytoplasmic enzymes LuxM (PMID: 19686078). (from Pfam)

This entry describes domain 1 located at the N-terminal region of RctB proteins. Mutational analysis show that it binds oriCII DNA, and that this function is critical for the capacity of RctB to mediate oriCII-based replication (PMID: 28031373). (from Pfam)

label: bCoV_NSP3_N
comment: This domain family corresponds to the N-terminal domain of NSP3 (non-structural protein 3, also known as nsp3) found in Betacoronavirus, which is encoded on the replicase polyprotein. This family includes the NSP3a domain which has the ubiquitin-like 1 (UB1) and glutamic acid-rich acidic (AC) hypervariable domains (PMID: 18367524). NSP3a interacts with numerous other proteins involved in replication and transcription and may serve as a scaffolding protein for these processes. The N-terminal NSP3a domain interacts with N (nucleocapsid) protein to colocalise genomic RNA with the nascent replicase-transcriptase complex at the earliest stages of infection, essential for the virus (PMID: 23943763). The C-terminal Glu-rich subdomain is best described as a flexible tail attached to the globular UB1 subdomain (PMID: 17728234). The family is found in association with Pfam:PF08716, Pfam:PF01661, Pfam:PF05409, Pfam:PF06471, Pfam:PF08717, Pfam:PF06478, Pfam:PF09401, Pfam:PF06460, Pfam:PF08715, Pfam:PF08710. (from Pfam)

From a larger set of proteins assigned as 1.5.1.20 and 1.7.99.5, this model describes the subset of proteins found in eukaryotes and designated 1.5.1.20. label: PEFG-CTERM
comment: This putative protein sorting/processing domain occurs about ten times per genome in members of the Thaumarchaeota. Its putative handling protein, a member of the archaeosortase/exosortase protein family, is exceptional in having a Ser rather than Cys at the putative active site. The highly conserved motif resembles the PEF-CTERM protein sorting domain of family TIGR03024, but membership does not overlap.

This family is unusual in that the suspected active site residue, Cys in every other defined subfamily of archaeosortases and exosortases is replaced by Ser.

label: UDG-inhib_P56
comment: Protein p56 from Bacillus subtilis phage phi29 inhibits the host uracil-DNA glycosylase (UDG) activity, preventing its binding to DNA and therefore viral replication from being compromised. p56 adopts a dimeric fold, with three anti-parallel beta sheets and a helical region linked by three short loops in each polypeptide chain. The highly anionic region of the protein plays a key role in the inhibition, which occurs by mimicking the DNA substrate [1-5]. This domain family is mainly found in tailed bacteriophages. (from Pfam)

label: Myrrcad
comment: This domain appears at or near the C-terminus in expanded paralogous families of proteins in Mycoplasma and Candidatus Mycoplasma genomes. Proteins with this domain typically show an N-terminal sequence regions followed by a repeat region, highly variable in length and similar to the leucine-rich repeat. The center region of this domain resembles alpha-helical hydrophobic transmembrane segments. The domain ends with a cluster of basic residues, suggesting an orientation in which the C-terminal residues of the domain face the cytosol. The coinage "MyrrCad", rendered without full capitalization because it is an acronym rather than an amino acid sequence motif, signifies "MYcoplasma Repeat-Rich protein C-terminal Anchor Domain"

label: Mycopla_NOT_gsn
comment: Members of this family occur strictly in the genus Mycoplasma, average 1050 in length with little length variability, have an N-terminal signal sequence, and exhibit no detectable sequence similarity to any characterized protein. Up to four tandem copies occur in some Mycoplasma (e.g. M. putrefaciens KS1). Incorrect inclusion of a 57-amino acid stretch of one family member in Pfam model PF08178, for a helix-turn-helix transcriptional regulator in several E. coli phage, has caused many members of this family to be annotated, in error, as GnsA/GnsB family proteins. We suggest the name STREFT (Secreted Thousand Residue Frequently Tandem) protein as a distinctive name to spread and replace the incorrect GnsA/GnsB designation.

label: Mplasa_alph_rch

Sequences are predicted (Jpred 3) to be almost entirely alpha-helical. These sequences show strong periodicity (consistent with long alpha helical structures) and low complexity rich in D,E,N,Q, and K. Genes encoding these proteins are often found in tandem. The function is unknown.

comment: Members of this narrowly defined family, closely related to known xanthine phosphoribosyltransferases (EC 2.4.2.22), were previously, and apparently incorrectly, named Tet(34) and ascribed a role in resistance to oxytetracycline. Subsequent work has shown no correlation between the presence of Tet(34) tetracycline resistance. Inspection of Vibrio genomes shows members of this family are generally chromosomally incorporated, and are the only candidate xanthine phosphoribosyltransferase encoded in the genome. Annotation has been revised to show member proteins are xanthine phosphoribosyltransferase, but "Tet(34)" was preserved in the same to make this annotation history more easily discoverable.

label: VarG_fam_MBL
comment: VarG was characterized in 2017 as a novel subclass B1-like metallo-beta-lactamase that is most active on meropenem, with about 10% of the activity of NDM-1. VarG is widespread in Vibrio cholerae and Vibrio vulnificus, and occurs also in some related species.

label: ExsE2_fam
comment: ExsE2, as described in two Vibrio species, is called functionally equivalent to ExsE from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, but appears to lack detectable sequence homology. In each model organism, a type III secretion system (T3SS) contains a DNA-binding transcriptional activator ExsA, an anti-activator ExsD that binds ExsA and inhibits its activity, and a secretion chaperone ExsC that can bind to and counteract ExsD. ExsE2 (in V. alginolyticus) or ExsE (in P. aeruginosa) can bind its chaperone ExsC until it exits the cell by successful T3SS translocation, providing fine tuning of T3SS gene expression through these interactions. We renamed the Vibrio family from ExsE to ExsE2 to help minimize confusion between these two very dissimilar families.

label: HAM1_N
comment: This entry represents a domain found at the N-terminal end of the putative cell signalling protein HAM1 from Cryptococcus neoformans and similar fungal sequences. HAM1 may act as a negative regulator of mating during vegetative growth (PMID: 38842336). Proteins with this domain often also contain a C-terminal domain Pfam:PF14613. (from Pfam)

label: quorum_TF_HapR
comment: Members of this family are closely related quorum-sensing master transcriptional regulators in the genus Vibrio, and belong to the broader TetR family, in the genus Vibrio. Members include the virulence gene master regulator HapR in V. cholerae, LuxR in Vibrio harveyi, OpaR in Vibrio parahaemolyticus, and SmcR in Vibrio vulnificus.

label: VtrA_C
comment: VtrA forms a complex with VtrC on the surface of the membrane that surrounds the bacterial cell. These two proteins create a platform that can bind to bile salts and trigger the release of bacterial toxins. This entry represents the C-terminal periplasmic domain of VtrA that interacts with the VtrC periplasmic domain. The VtrA periplasmic domain adopts an alpha/beta structure consisting of a five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and two helices packed on one side of it (PMID: 27377244). (from Pfam)

label: RbmA-like_FnIII
comment: This entry represents both fibronectin type III (FnIII) domains found in RbmA protein from Vibrio cholerae (Swiss:Q9KTH4), a biofilm matrix protein essential for both maintenance of rugose colony morphology and development of wild-type biofilm architecture. RbmA contains two FnIII domains connected by a linker segment. The two folds run antiparallel to each other but do not form extensive interactions. Each FnIII domain shows a beta-sandwich comprised of three beta-sheets plus four beta-sheets (PMID: 24340031). (from Pfam)

label: VtrC
comment: This entry represents a lipocalin-like beta barrel domain found in the Vibrio parahaemolyticus VtrC protein (PMID: 27377244). VtrC, along with VtrA and VtrB, are required for activating the virulence type III secretion system 2 in response to bile salts. The VtrA/VtrC complex activates VtrB in the presence of bile salts. The crystal structure of the periplasmic domains of the VtrA/VtrC heterodimer reveals a beta-barrel with a hydrophobic inner chamber (PMID: 27377244). (from Pfam)

label: TcpS
comment: The toxin-coregulated pilus (TCP) and cholera toxin (CT) are two main virulence factors produced by V. cholerae, which allows the bacterium to colonize and establish an infection in a host and to cause the physical symptoms of the disease, respectively. Increased expression of the TCP, a type IV pilus expressed by the tcp operon (tcpABQCRDSTEF) located on the Vibrio pathogenicity island (VPI), has been associated with enhanced attachment and is essential for colonization of the intestinal epithelium (PMID: 27668288). This domain of unknown function is found in TcpS proteins in Vibrionaceae such as Vibrio choleae. (from Pfam)

label: ToxT_N

ToxT serves as the culminating factor in the regulatory pathway, ensuring the coordinated production of two virulence factors: the toxin-coregulated pilus (TCP) and cholera toxin (CT), which are crucial for the pathogenicity of V. cholerae in causing cholera. ToxT possesses dimerization and regulatory elements in its cupin-like N-terminal domain, while its C-terminus harbors two HTH AraC-like DNA binding domains [3,4]. (from Pfam)

label: GldE
comment: Members of this protein family are exclusive to the Bacteroidetes phylum (previously Cytophaga-Flavobacteria-Bacteroides). GldC is a protein linked to a type of rapid surface gliding motility found in certain Bacteroidetes, such as Flavobacterium johnsoniae and Cytophaga hutchinsonii. GldE was discovered because of its adjacency to GldD in F. johnsonii. Overexpression of GldE partially supresses the effects of a GldB point mutant suggesting that GldB and GldE interact [1]. Gliding motility appears closely linked to chitin utilization in the model species Flavobacterium johnsoniae. Not all Bacteroidetes with members of this protein family appear to have all of the genes associated with gliding motility and in fact some do not appear to express the gliding phenotype.

label: IncD
comment: The chlamydial inclusion membrane is extensively modified by the insertion of type III secreted effector proteins (PMID: 23696825). These inclusion membrane proteins (Incs) have two major characteristics: an N-terminal type III secretion signal that is necessary for their secretion out of the bacterium and a hydrophobic region consisting of at least two trans-membrane helices that allows insertion into the inclusion membrane. Generally, both the N- and C-terminal regions of the Inc are exposed to the host cell cytosol (PMID: 25717440). This family has members such as the IncD proteins found in Chlamydia trachomatis. This C. trachomatis effector protein IncD has been shown to recruit the lipid transfer protein CERT to the inclusion membrane by directly interacting with CERT PH domain, which mediates the FFAT motif-dependent recruitment of the ER-resident protein VAPB (vesicle-associated membrane protein-associated protein) to the inclusion (PMID: 25930206). label: IncE
comment: The chlamydial inclusion membrane is extensively modified by the insertion of type III secreted effector proteins (PMID: 23696825). These inclusion membrane proteins (Incs) have two major characteristics: an N-terminal type III secretion signal that is necessary for their secretion out of the bacterium and a hydrophobic region consisting of at least two trans-membrane helices that allows insertion into the inclusion membrane. Generally, both the N- and C-terminal regions of the Inc are exposed to the host cell cytosol (PMID: 25717440). This family has members such as the IncE (also known as CT116) proteins found in Chlamydia trachomatis. IncE Interacts with Retromer-Associated Sorting Nexins (SNXs) directly binding the PX-domains of SNX5/6. It is expressed within the first 2 hours of C. trachomatis infection. IncE region 101-132 is the binding site for SNX5/6 causing re-localization of SNX5/6 from endosomes to the inclusion membrane. IncE101-132 expression was shown to be sufficient to maintain CI-MPR (Cation-Independent Mannose-6-Phosphate Receptor) in retromer-containing compartments, thereby disrupting efficient CI-MPR trafficking to the trans-Golgi. It has been suggested that SNX5/6 bind directly to IncE independently of phosphoinositides and that the predicted IncE C-terminal beta-hairpin is required. IncE-mediated sequestration of retromer SNX-BAR proteins may promote Golgi fragmentation, a process that facilitates lipid acquisition by C. trachomatis and enhances progeny production (PMID: 26118995). (from Pfam)

label: IncF
comment: The chlamydial inclusion membrane is extensively modified by the insertion of type III secreted effector proteins. These inclusion membrane proteins (Incs) are exposed to the cytosol and share a common structural feature of a long, bi-lobed hydrophobic domain but little or no primary amino acid sequence similarity (PMID: 23696825). This family has members such as the IncF proteins found in Chlamydia trachomatis. IncF, is enriched at the point of contact of RBs (reticulate bodies) with the inclusion membrane (PMID: 23696825). It is expressed early in the developmental cycle and interacts with many other Inc proteins, like Ct058 or Ct850, which are expressed later during the cycle. Thus, IncF could act as an interaction node for Inc proteins. IncF consists of 104 amino acids of which 38 N-terminal amino acids encoding the signal sequence for the type III system and 12 C-terminal amino acids may be localized in the host cell cytoplasm. Suggesting that IncF or other small Incs interact with other Inc proteins by their trans-membrane domain. It has been identified to be capable of homo-oligomerization and also displayed self-interacting properties (PMID: 25717440). (from Pfam)

A related family (NF047744, CG0192_rel) describes another, well-separated set of homologs also about 200 amino acids in length.

label: lipo_LppU
comment: Members of this family have eight invariant Cys residues, plus a ninth in most members in a putative lipoprotein signal peptide. Members that lack the lipoprotein signal peptide-like N-terminal region instead have a long, poorly conserved N-terminal region, of unknown function, rich in both Gly and Pro residues. Members include Rv2784c from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, called LppU. The region with eight Cys residues appears to result from an ancient duplication, with each copy of the duplicated domain resembling the C-terminal region of SCO3897 (see NF049863) from Streptomyces coelicolor, a protein called involved in differentiation in that species.

label: LpqS_Mycobact
comment: LpqS, a putative lipoprotein from Mycobacterium, was shown to be important for survival inside host macrophages. LpqS belongs to the copper-responsive RicR regulon. The specific molecular function is not yet known. The putative lipoprotein signal motif is somewhat atypical in M. tuberculosis, and critical Cys is absent in many other members of the family.

label: drrC
comment: The model describes daunorubicin resistance protein C in bacteria. This protein confers the function of daunorubicin resistance. The protein seems to share strong sequence similarity to UvrA proteins, which are involved in excision repair of DNA. Disruption of drrC gene showed increased sensitivity upon exposure to duanorubicin. However it failed to complement uvrA mutants to exposure to UV irradiation. The mechanism on how it confers duanomycin resistance is unclear, but has been suggested to be different from DrrA and DrrB which are antiporters.

label: PA_Ig-like
comment: Anthrax protective antigen (PA) is one of the three proteins forming the anthrax toxin. It is involved in the first step of toxin entry into host cells, enabling lethal factor (LF) and oedema factor (EF) to cross to the cytosol. PA undergoes cleavage by Furin to generate PA20 and PA63. The latter, which adopts a ring-shaped heptameric assembly, shows four distinct domains. The fourth domain, a carboxy- terminal receptor-binding domain, shows an initial hairpin and helix, followed by a beta-sandwich with an immunoglobulin-like fold (this entry) [1-5]. (from Pfam)

It is required for timely anaphase onset during mitosis, when chromosomes undergo bipolar attachment on spindle microtubules leading to silencing of the spindle checkpoint (PMID: 22483620). (from Pfam)

label: AgrD
comment: This family consists of several AgrD proteins from many Staphylococcus species. The agr locus was initially described in Staphylococcus aureus as an element controlling the production of exoproteins implicated in virulence. Its pattern of action has been shown to be complex, upregulating certain extracellular toxins and enzymes expressed post-exponentially and repressing some exponential-phase surface components. AgrD encodes the precursor of the autoinducing peptide (AIP).The AIP derived from AgrD by the action of AgrB interacts with AgrC in the membrane to activate AgrA, which upregulates transcription both from promoter P2, amplifying the response, and from P3, initiating the production of a novel effector: RNAIII. In S. aureus, delta-hemolysin is the only translation product of RNA III and is not involved in the regulatory functions of the transcript, which is therefore the primary agent for modulating the expression of other operons controlled by agr (PMID: 11807079). (from Pfam)

MecR1 and BlaR1 are full-length homologs of each other and of additional proteins that tend be found in the context of a BlaI-like penicillinase repressor and a beta-lactamase. This model hits only MecR1 itself.

It has transpeptidase activity, provides low level beta-lactam resistance, and in mutant strains can contribute to high level beta-lactam resistance.

label: TF_SarA
comment: SarA (staphylococcal accessory regulator) is a transcription factor affecting multiple virulence-associated processes, such as biofilm formation and protease secretion.

label: SdrH_fam_CTERM
comment: The founding member of this family of staphylococcal proteins, SdrH from Staphylococcus epidermidis, is one of three MSCRAMM family proteins, but is atypical in lacking a recognizable LPXTG-like C-terminal recognition sequence for cell wall anchoring. This HMM represents the entire region C-terminal to the repetitive, low-complexity region that is a feature of all members of this family. That repetitive region consists mostly of Ser-Asp dipeptides in S. epidermidis but has radically different compositions in other species.

label: DUF6007

This family includes a protein from the capsular polysaccharide biosynthetic gene cluster from Staphylococcus aureus (PMID: 7961465) (from Pfam)

label: S1_dom_Ygs
comment: Ygs, as first described in Staphylococcus epidermidis, is a full-length homolog of GSP13 (YugI) from Bacillus subtilis. Each has a single copy of the S1 domain, an RNA-binding domain repeated several times in ribosomal small subunit protein S1, and each has been shown to be induced by stress and improve survival. Ygs was shown in Staphylococcus epidermidis to affect polysaccharide intercellular adhesin biosynthesis, and through it, biofilm formation. More recently, the full-length homolog CvfD was shown to be a post-transcriptional regulator, suggesting all members of this family are.

label: SE2200_fam
comment: Members of this staphylococcal protein family are small, typically 33 amino acids long, with the first 18 amino acids resembling a signal-anchor domain for membrane insertion. A proteomics study demonstrates significant protein expression in Staphylococcus aureus, and conservation in the genus suggests purifying selection as would be expected for a real protein. This family, broadly distributed in the genus Staphylococcus, was once described as DUF2648 by Pfam model PF10855, but at the time this model was built (April 2022), that Pfam model had been retired under suspicion of not identifying real proteins.

It has been reported that this small protein is a type II toxin-antitoxin system toxin with the activity of DNA gyrase inhibitor ( PMIDs: 31375497 and 36148483).

This system responds to a quorum-signaling autoinducing peptide (AIP) that is ribosomally translated from agrD, but post-translationally modified by cleavage and cyclization to form a peptide thiolactone.

MroQ often is encoded within 6 kilobases of the agr (accessory gene regulator) quorum-sensing system, and it is involved in leader peptide removal from the autoinducer peptide (AIP) after it is cleaved and cyclized at a Cys side chain the cysteine peptidase AgrB.

The particulars of its function in response to glucose and glutamate availability have not be described, although a transcriptional activator role in the presence of glucose and relative lack of glutamate is expected.

label: GGDEF_GdpS

The GGDEF domain, located toward the C-terminus, has diguanylate cyclase activity, creating a regulatory molecule with complex regulatory effects. However, the first half of the gdpS mRNA appears itself to be functional, through the process of binding the upstream region of sarS mRNA, thereby influencing expression of the SarS regulon.

The family does not carry the YGNGVXC motif characteristic of pediocin-like Bacteriocins, Bacteriocin_II Pfam:PF01721. The producer bacteria are protected from the effects of their own bacteriocins by production of a specific immunity protein which is co-transcribed with the genes encoding the bacteriocins, eg family EntA_Immun Pfam:PF08951. The bacteriocins are structurally more specific than their immunity-protein counterparts. Typically, production of the bacteriocin gene is from within an operon carrying up to 6 genes including a typical two-component regulatory system (R and H), a small peptide pheromone (C), and a dedicated ABC transporter (A and -B) as well as an immunity protein (PMID: 17074857). The ABC transporter is thought to recognise the N termini of both the pheromone and the bacteriocins and to transport these peptides across the cytoplasmic membrane, concurrent with cleavage at the conserved double-glycine motif. Cleaved extracellular C can then bind to the sensor kinase, H, resulting in activation of R and up-regulation of the entire gene cluster via binding to consensus sequences within each promoter (PMID: 17298586).
