label: DUF6509
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 100 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: DPTGI and ILA. (from Pfam)

label: adhesin_AbpA
comment: AbpA, an adhesin of oral streptococci, binds the host salivary protein alpha-amylase, contributing to colonization. Its C-terminal motif for cell wall attachment, LPKTxAVK-COOH, is recognized and processed by a dedicated B-type sortase.

label: SrtB_LPKTxSAVK
comment: This branch of the class B sortase family is found in multiple species of Streptococcus and Gemella. It processes target proteins that end with the motif LPKTxAVK-COOH, which differ from most sortase recognition sites in lacking an additional C-terminal transmembrane helix. Substrates of this sortase include the amylase-binding adhesin AbpA, as well of other proteins with similar N-terminal and C-terminal domains but unrelated central regions.

label: LiaF_C_term
product_name: cell wall-active antibiotics response protein LiaF
hmm_name: cell wall-active antibiotics response protein LiaF, C-terminal domain
comment: This HMM represents the conserved C-terminal domain of LiaF (called VraT in Staphylococcus), an additional key component of the histidine kinase LiaS and response regulator LiaR system. The system responds to cell envelop stress in the Firmicutes, and plays a role in resistance to cell wall-targeting antibiotics.

label: Nt5e_LPXTG
comment: Members of this family, found in Streptococcus sanguinis and related species, are LPXTG-anchored cell surface proteins. By hydrolyzing pro-inflammatory extracellular ATP in the host, it may blunt immune responses and contribute to virulence. Nt5e has also been called adenosine synthase AdsA.

label: SGO_0316_fam
comment: Members of this family are cell wall-anchored streptococcal serine peptidases from MEROPS family S8, which contains subtilisin and its homologs. In several species, such as Streptococcus gordonii, two members of this family are encoded by a tandem gene pair.

label: Tn5252_Orf10
product_name: SAG1252 family conjugative relaxosome accessory protein
hmm_name: SAG1252 family conjugative relaxosome accessory protein
comment: SAG1252, a member of the Tn5252 ORF10 family, occurs in mobile elements from a class associated with the movement of bacteriocins and antibiotic resistance proteins in Streptococcus. This HMM excludes related MobC proteins, such as the adjacent SAG1251, a homolog over the short length of these small proteins except for a small central region recognized by Pfam model PF05713 (MobC).

label: ryptide_rSAM
product_name: radical SAM/SPASM ryptide class RiPP maturase
hmm_name: radical SAM/SPASM ryptide class RiPP maturase

label: ABC_lipo_SloC
comment: Members of this family, such as SloC from Streptococcus mutans, are lipoproteins found in metal ABC transporter cassettes. The panel of metals bound and transported can vary from member to member but typically includes manganese, and names provided in publications differ as well. It appears that some members of this so-called LraI family of lipoproteins moonlight as adhesins.

label: pilin_ComGF
product_name: competence type IV pilus minor pilin ComGF
hmm_name: competence type IV pilus minor pilin ComGF
comment: ComGF is one of several minor pilins in the type IV pilus involved in the competence system of natural transformation by various Gram-positive bacteria. Oddly, while nearly all members have an N-terminal region with a consensus site for cleavage and methylation, ComGF from Bacillus subtilis appears N-terminally truncated, and may be functional despite the truncation.

label: T4P_ComGB
product_name: competence type IV pilus assembly protein ComGB
hmm_name: competence type IV pilus assembly protein ComGB
comment: Members of this family occur in Gram-positive bacteria as part of a type IV pilus system used for DNA binding and uptake when species such as Streptococcus pneumoniae or Bacilus subtilis are in a competent state for natural transformation. Members of this family, typically called ComGB (second protein of the ComG operon), belong more broadly to the family of GspF, part of type 2 secretion systems (T2SS) in Gram-negative bacteria.

label: T4P_ComGE
product_name: competence type IV pilus minor pilin ComGE
hmm_name: competence type IV pilus minor pilin ComGE

label: ryptide_ex_MFS
comment: Members of this family are MFS transporters that belong to a system in which ryptide precursor RiPP peptides are produced, modified by a radical SAM/SPASM enzyme that introduces an arginine-tryptophan crosslink, and exported.

label: PrgP
product_name: ParA superfamily DNA segregation protein PrgP
hmm_name: ParA superfamily DNA segregation protein PrgP

label: SepM_fam_S16
comment: This HMM describes a peptide pheromone-processing S16-type serine protease found broadly in Gram-positive bacteria, and named for the founding member from Streptococcus mutans (see BlastRule NBR014542). The Lon-like catalytic domain is located toward the C-terminus, and has a Ser-Lys active site dyad rather than the more common Ser-His-Asp triad found in large numbers of serine proteases. Members of this family also have a PDZ domain.

label: PepG1
product_name: type I toxin-antitoxin system toxin PepG1
hmm_name: type I toxin-antitoxin system toxin PepG1

label: lipo_FMN_PplA
hmm_name: extracellular electron transfer flavoprotein PplA, long form
comment: PplA, as found in extracellular electron transfer (EET) locus of Listeria monocytogenes, is a cell surface flavoprotein with covalently attached FMN. Flavinylation is performed by FmnB, a family ApbE surface lipoprotein, using FAD as the source molecule. This HMM describes a long form of PplA, with a duplication of the flavinylated domain and with two bound FMN molecules.

label: Big_15
comment: This bacterial Ig-like domain is found in the stalk regions of bacterial cell surface adhesins. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6681
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 258 and 288 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: pAdhesive_17
comment: The structure model of this domain folds into 10 beta strands arranged in two beta sheets as well as 4-5 elongated alpha helices. The beta sheets distantly resemble the Collagen_bind (Pfam:PF05737) domain. It is annotated N-terminal to repeating stalk domains in bacterial surface proteins. This domain can be found on a E. faecalis protein encoded by the EF3314 gene, which was proposed to contribute to the interaction of E. faecalis with the host and to the bacterial virulence (PMID: 19856273). (from Pfam)

label: SIALI-17
comment: This HMM represents two tandem copies of a typically 17-amino acid repeat with a characteristic EXPEF or EXPEY motif, found mostly in Streptococcus surface-bound glycoside or peptide hydrolases with LPXTG motifs for covalent anchoring on the cell well. Member proteins are also found in Gemella and Granulicatella. It occurs in the C-terminal region of the sialidase NanA (CAA51473.1) of Streptococcus pneumoniae, a region not described as either catalytic or carbohydrate-binding, but instead as P/G/S/T-rich and repeat-containing. Multiple copies of the repeat occur also in the IgA1 protease ZmpD, another Streptococcus pneumoniae virulence factor.

label: PrkC-like_PASTA-like
product_name: Serine/threonine protein kinase-like, C-terminal PASTA-like domain
name_orig: Serine/threonine protein kinase-like, C-terminal PASTA-like domain
hmm_name: Serine/threonine protein kinase-like, C-terminal PASTA-like domain
comment: This domain is found in Non-specific serine/threonine protein kinase from Staphylococcus aureus (PrkC) and similar bacterial proteins. PrkC is responsible for triggering spore germination in response to muropeptides, signaling bacteria to exit dormancy. The extracellular region of PrkC is a linear modular structure composed of three PASTA (penicillin binding-associated and serine/threonine kinase- associated, Pfam:PF03793) domains and a PASTA-like C-terminal domain, which presents an immunoglobulin-like fold and the typical features of adhesive proteins [1-3]. (from Pfam)

label: TraK_2
comment: This entry represents the TraK protein found in the pIP501 Type IV Secretion System operon. The protein localised to the cell envelope, facing towards the cell exterior, and behaves as a monomer under the tested conditions (PMID: 24699656). It adopts a mixed alpha-beta fold with seven alpha helices and nine beta strands. (from Pfam)

label: Ybfg_C
comment: This is the presumed C-terminal domain found the uncharacterized protein YbfG from Bacillus subtilis. This domain may adopt an alpha/beta structure. YbfG has a peptidoglycan-binding domain at the N-terminal (Pfam:PF01471) and a central catalytic glycosyl hydrolase family 25 (GH25) domain (Pfam:PF08924). YbfG has a significant degree of homology to BacA (PMID: 24235140) from E. faecalis, which together with BacL1, show cell wall lytic activity (PMID: 24235140). (from Pfam)

label: YqgU
comment: This entry represents a beta propeller domain found in the B. subtilis YqgU protein. The proteins in this family contain an N-terminal lipid attachment motif suggesting they are lipoproteins. (from Pfam)

label: TraH_VirB8-like
comment: This entry represents the VirB8-like domain present in TraH protein. TraH is part of the type IV secretion system (T4SS) (PMID: 27103580). This domain shows structural similarity to the VirB8 domain (Pfam:PF04335). (from Pfam)

label: InlK_D2
comment: This domain is found at the elbow of internalin surface proteins InlK-like, used by the bacteria to invade mammalian cells. This domain has a beta-sandwich-like fold (PMID: 23958637). (from Pfam)

label: Lreu_0056_like
comment: This entry represents a domain found in a family of Lactobacillus proteins whose structure has been characterised (PDB:2mqd). (from Pfam)

label: AbpA-like
comment: Amylase binding streptococci only colonize hosts that produce amylase in their saliva. In Streptococcus gordonii, amylase binding is mediated by amylase-binding protein A (AbpA). This protein folds into an elongated structure that consists of two domains: an N-terminal helical domain and a small C-terminal alpha/beta domain consisting of a three-stranded beta-sheet packed with helix (PMID: 25739638). The helical domain has shown to be responsible for the amylase binding while the C-terminal domain interacts with SrtB. (from Pfam)

label: choline_R_CudC
comment: Members of this family are MarR family transcriptional regulators involved in the processes such as choline uptake and conversion of choline to the compatible solute glycine-betaine (often called simply betaine), which helps prevent damage from desiccation. All members of the seed alignment were chosen for being encoded in close proximity to betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase, suggesting a role regulating the processes of choline uptake and conversion to betaine.

label: FNG
comment: This entry shows a beta sandwich structure that shows similarity to known carbohydrate binding domain families CBM61 and CBM70. This domain is found at the N-terminus of proteins that contain repeated domains, suggesting these proteins may act as carbohydrate binding adhesins. This domain contains a conserved FNG sequence after which the domain is named. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7679
comment: This entry represents a small family of Lactobacillus proteins of unknown function. The predicted structure suggests these proteins contain two subdomains, with an N-terminal partly open beta barrel and C-terminal alpha/beta subdomain. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7649
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a non-compact structure consisting of four highly hydrophobic alpha-helices that could potentially dimerise. (from Pfam)

label: rSAM_WgK_link
comment: Member of this family, named WgkB, are radical SAM/SPASM domain peptide maturases for tryglysin family RiPP peptides, which have a Trp-Gly-Lys (WGK) tripeptide motif that becomes cyclized. The peptide natural products made from the precursors include tryglysins A and B from Streptococcus mutans and S. ferus, which have antimicrobial activity.

label: tryglysin_RiPP
comment: Tryglysin family RiPP (ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide) precursors have a conserved Tryptophan-Glycine-Lysine motif near the C-terminus that becomes the site for cyclization by a radical SAM/SPASM maturation protein. In Streptococcus mutans and S. ferus, production of this antibacterial RiPP natural product is governed by an equally small signalling peptide names SHP (Small Hydrophobic Peptide).

label: PqqD_rel_WgkC
product_name: PqqD family peptide maturation chaperone WgkC
hmm_name: PqqD family peptide maturation chaperone WgkC
comment: WgkC is a PqqD-like peptide chaperone involved in cyclization of the WGK motif in tryglysin (TRYptophan-GLysine-LYSine) family peptides. The radical SAM/SPASM enzyme that performs the cyclization is wgkB.

label: TransRegFabT
product_name: fatty acid biosynthesis transcriptional regulator FabT
hmm_name: fatty acid biosynthesis transcriptional regulator FabT

label: Nucleoprot-TPR
comment: This domain is found in human Nucleoprotein TPR, a component of the nuclear pore complex, which is required for the trafficking across the nuclear envelope. This domain is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical configuration. (from Pfam)

label: PBP4_5_Efaec
comment: Members of this family have been called penicillin-binding protein 4 (PBP4) in Enterococcus faecalis , and related Gram-positive bacteria.

label: HU_inhibitor
product_name: Bacteriophage inhibitor of histone-like protein HU
name_orig: Bacteriophage inhibitor of histone-like protein HU
hmm_name: Bacteriophage inhibitor of histone-like protein HU
comment: This entry represents a bacteriophage protein that acts as an inhibitor of bacterial histone-like protein HU. The protein binds to HU, occupying its DNA binding motif and preventing HU-DNA complex formation. This inhibition leads to defects in chromosome segregation and causes filamentous cell morphology in bacteria. The protein forms a 1:2 complex with HU dimers, utilising both electrostatic interactions and key hydrophobic contacts. Key residues F22 and D63 are important for the interaction with HU. The protein is capable of binding HU proteins from a wide range of bacteria and Apicomplexan parasites due to the conservation of key interaction residues. (from Pfam)

label: spr1630_fam
comment: Members of this family include SA0141 from Staphylococcus aureus and spr1630 from Streptococcus pneumoniae. The latter is notable because its accumulation in mutants lacking the protease ClpXP is toxic, making clpX mutations lethal.

label: lmo1851_S41
comment: Loss of this protein, an S41 family serine protease, was observed to improve tolerance to palmitoleic acid, a free fatty acid with antimicrobial effects.

label: adhes_AsaA_N
hmm_name: sialic acid-binding adhesin AsaA N-terminal domain
comment: Members of this family of streptococcal adhesins contain an N-terminal YSIRK-type signal peptide, then a non-repetitive sialic acid-binding domain (described by this HMM), then a large and variable number of tandem DUF1542 domains forming a stalk, and lastly, an LPXTG motif-containing C-terminal sorting signal that mediates sortase-dependent anchoring to the cell wall. Lengths over 3000 amino acids are typical.

label: polys_exp_MPA1
product_name: CspC family polysaccharide chain length determinant protein
hmm_name: CspC family polysaccharide chain length determinant protein
comment: This family contains members from Low GC Gram-positive bacteria. Many members have been named as CspC (capsular polysaccharide biosynthesis protein C), part of a trio of proteins that includes tyrosine kinase activity and that governs polymer length.

label: lacB
comment: This family contains four members from low GC gram-positive bacteria. Galactose-6-phosphate isomerase is involved in lactose catabolism by the tagatose-6-phosphate pathway.

label: YSIRK_signal
comment: The [YF]SIRKxxxGxxS type of signal peptide appears at the start of many proteins of Streptococcus, Staphylococcus, and Enterococcus, but not in other lineages such as Bacillus. Recent work in Staphylococcus aureus has shown that septal secretion (targeting to the crosswall in dividing cells) of the YSIRK-containing staphylococcal protein A depends on SecA, SecDF, and the lipoteichoic acid synthase LtaS, all of which co-purify when the motif is modified to YSIRKxxxGxxL to block processing. The YSIRK form of extended signal peptide directs nascent proteins to the cross-wall site, while signal peptides lacking YSIRK direct proteins instead to the cell pole. A large fraction of YSIRK proteins are surface proteins anchored by sortase-mediated processing of a C-terminal LPXTG motif.

label: Gpos_tandem_5TM
comment: Members of this family of proteins, with average length of 210, have no invariant residues but five predicted transmembrane segments. Strangely, most members occur in groups of consecutive paralogous genes. A striking example is a set of eleven encoded consecutively, head-to-tail, in Staphylococcus aureus strain COL.

label: ccpA
comment: Catabolite control protein A is a LacI family global transcriptional regulator found in Gram-positive bacteria. CcpA is involved in repressing carbohydrate utilization genes [ex: alpha-amylase (amyE), acetyl-coenzyme A synthase (acsA)] and in activating genes involved in transporting excess carbon from the cell [ex: acetate kinase (ackA), alpha-acetolactate synthase (alsS)]. Additionally, disruption of CcpA in Bacillus megaterium, Staphylococcus xylosus, Lactobacillus casei and Lactocacillus pentosus also decreases growth rate, which suggests CcpA is involved in the regulation of other metabolic pathways.

label: bact_immun_7tm
comment: This HMM represents a family of integral membrane proteins, most of which are about 650 residues in size and predicted to span the membrane seven times. Nearly half of the members of this family are found in association with a member of the lactococcin 972 family of bacteriocins (TIGR01653). Others may be associated with uncharacterized proteins that may also act as bacteriocins. Although this protein is suggested to be an immunity protein, and the bacteriocin is suggested to be exported by a Sec-dependent process, the role of this protein is unclear.

label: ComEB
comment: This protein is found in the ComE operon for "late competence" as characterized in B. subtilis [1]. Proteins in this family contain homology to a cytidine/deoxycytidine deaminase domain family (PF00383), and may carry out this activity.

label: acc_sec_Y2
product_name: accessory Sec system protein translocase subunit SecY2
hmm_name: accessory Sec system protein translocase subunit SecY2
comment: Members of this family are restricted to the Firmicutes lineage (low-GC Gram-positive bacteria) and appear to be paralogous to, and much more divergent than, the preprotein translocase SecY. Members include the SecY2 protein of the accessory Sec system in Streptococcus gordonii, involved in export of the highly glycosylated platelet-binding protein GspB.

label: perox_SACOL1771
comment: This protein family belongs to the OsmC/Ohr family (PF02566, OsmC-like protein) of peroxiredoxins.

label: IsdC
comment: Isd proteins are iron-regulated surface proteins found in Bacillus, Staphylococcus and Listeria species and are responsible for heme scavenging from hemoproteins [1]. The IsdC protein consists of an N-terminal hydrophobic signal sequence, a central NEAT (NEAr Transporter, PF05031) domain which confers the ability to bind heme [2] and a C-terminal SrtB processing signal which targets the protein to the cell wall [3]. IsdC is believed to make a direct contact with, and transfer heme to, the heme-binding component (IsdE) of an ABC transporter in the cytoplasmic membrane, and to receive heme from other NEAT-containing heme-binding proteins also localized in the cell wall.

label: KxYKxGKxW
comment: This model describes a novel form of signal peptide that occurs as an N-terminal domain with a recognizable motif, reminiscent of the YSIRK and PEP-CTERM forms of signal peptide. This domain tends to occur on long, low-complexity (usually Serine-rich and heavily glycosylated) proteins of the Firmicutes, and (as with YSIRK) the majority of these proteins have the LPXTG cell wall-anchoring motif at the C-terminus.

label: exospor_lead
hmm_name: exosporium leader peptide, Bacillus cereus type
comment: This domain is found as a leader peptide in at least a subset of proteins targeted to the type of exosporium that occurs as the outermost layer of Bacillus anthracis, B. cereus, and B. thuringiensis spores. The exosporium consists of a basal layer and a nap of hair-like filaments. BclA, the major protein of the nap filaments, is targeted there by this leader peptide. In known examples of proteins in this family, the exosporium leader peptide is followed immediately by collagen-like Pro-rich tripeptide repeats. The last six residues of the seed alignment represent the first two PXG repeats.

label: T7SS_EssA_Firm
comment: Members of this family are associated with type VII secretion of WXG100 family targets in the Firmicutes, but not in the Actinobacteria. This highly divergent protein family consists largely of a central region of highly polar low-complexity sequence containing occasional LF motifs in weak repeats about 17 residues in length, flanked by hydrophobic N- and C-terminal regions.

label: expor_sig_YdyF
comment: This family describes a rare family of small proteins, about 50 residues in length, that includes YydF from Bacillus subtilis and SAG_2028 from Streptococcus agalactiae 2603V/R. The founding member of this family, YydF, is epimerized twice (hence "epipeptide") by the radical SAM enzyme YydG (see TIGR04078), which is peptide-modifying but lacks any SPASM domain. The genome context regularly found with members of this family includes an ABC transporter for export. YydF, a membrane perturbing antimicrobial peptide, triggers a cell envelope stress response involving LiaRS two-component system, even in producer strains.

label: rSAM_yydG
product_name: YydG family radical SAM peptide epimerase
name_orig: peptide modification radical SAM enzyme, YydG family
hmm_name: YydG family radical SAM peptide epimerase
comment: Members of this radical SAM protein modify YydF family peptides (see TIGR04077 ) by epimerization, and in contrast to many other peptide maturases, lack any SPASM domain. In Bacillus subtilis, this protein (YydG) acts on its cognate target peptide (YydF) prior to its export, helping to generate a membrane-permeabilizing antimicrobial peptide, one of whose effects is to induce the LiaRS envelope stress response two-component system.

label: T7SS_SACOL2603
product_name: TIGR04197 family type VII secretion effector
name_orig: type VII secretion effector, TIGR04197 family
hmm_name: TIGR04197 family type VII secretion effector
comment: Members of this protein family are similar in length and sequence (although remotely) to the WXG100 family of type VII secretion system (T7SS) targets, described by family TIGR03930. Phylogenetic profiling shows that members of this family are similarly restricted to species with T7SS, marking this family as a related set of T7SS effectors. Members include SACOL2603 from Staphylococcus aureus subsp. aureus COL. Oddly, members of family PF10824 (DUF2580), which appears also to be related, seem not to be tied to T7SS.

label: Surf_Exclu_PgrA
comment: This model describes a conserved domain found in surface proteins of a number of Firmutes. Many members have LPXTG C-terminal anchoring motifs and a substantial number have the KxYKxGKxW putative sorting signal at the N-terminus. The tetracycline resistance plasmid pCF10 in Enterococcus faecalis promotes conjugal plasmid transfer in response to sex pheromones, but PgrA/Sec10 encoded by that plasmid, a member of this family, specifically inhibits the ability of cells to receive homologous plasmids. The phenomenon is called surface exclusion.

label: SecA2_Bac_anthr
comment: Members of this family always occur in genomes with the preprotein translocase SecA (TIGR00963) and closely resemble it, hence the designation SecA2. However, this appears to mark a different type of accessory Sec system SecA2 (TIGR03714) from the serine-rich glycoprotein type found in Staphylococcus and Streptococcus, and the actinobacterial SecA2 (TIGR04221). This type occurs in species including Bacillus anthracis, Geobacillus thermoglucosidasius, Solibacillus silvestris, etc.

label: acc_Sec_SLAP
product_name: accessory Sec system S-layer assembly protein
name_orig: accessory Sec system S-layer assembly protein
hmm_name: accessory Sec system S-layer assembly protein
comment: Members of this family, designated S-layer assembly protein (SlaP), occur next to a Bacillus anthracis-type accessory Sec system SecA2. . Members have two tandem copies of a duplicated domain (TIGR04398) that may also occur in other contexts. SlaP is found both free in the cytoplasm and membrane-associated. SecA2 and SlaP appear to work together to modify Sec for efficient S-layer secretion.

label: RiPP_SkfA
comment: Members of this family are ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide natural products, modified by sulfur-to-alpha-carbon cross-link introduced by a radical SAM enzyme, SkfB (TIGR04403).

label: Gpos_C8_like
comment: This model describes full-length proteins of Gram-positive bacteria that consist of an N-terminal signal peptide, a central region of unknown function, and a Cys-rich C-terminal region. In both the overall architecture and the apparent weak homology of the C-terminal region itself, these proteins resemble archaeal proteins such as the halocin C8 precursor. In that precursor, the C-terminal region is a bacteriocin but the N-terminal region functions as the immunity protein. The related family of halocin C8-like bacteriocins and their bacterial homologs are recognized by model TIGR04449.

label: Cullin
comment: This entry represents the N-terminal alpha solenoid domain of the Cullin family. The Cullin family proteins are core components of various cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes. These complexes mediate the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins, playing crucial roles in cell cycle regulation, signal transduction, and transcription. Cullins act as scaffold proteins, contributing to catalysis by positioning substrates and ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes. The functional specificity of these complexes is determined by variable substrate recognition components, such as F-box proteins in SCF complexes or SOCS box-containing proteins in ECS complexes. Cullins are involved in diverse biological processes, including cell cycle transitions, DNA repair, circadian clock regulation, and stress responses. They also participate in pathways like Wnt signaling, auxin signaling in plants, and hypoxia response through the ubiquitination of hypoxia-inducible factors. (from Pfam)

The chaperone-binding domain is highly conserved, and is essential for the correct assembly of the pili structure when aided by the chaperone molecule PapD [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: Tra_M
comment: The TraM protein is an essential part of the DNA transfer machinery of the conjugative resistance plasmid R1 (IncFII). On the basis of mutational analyses, it was shown that the essential transfer protein TraM has at least two functions. First, a functional TraM protein was found to be required for normal levels of transfer gene expression. Second, experimental evidence was obtained that TraM stimulates efficient site-specific single-stranded DNA cleavage at the oriT, in vivo. Furthermore, a specific interaction of the cytoplasmic TraM protein with the membrane protein TraD was demonstrated, suggesting that the TraM protein creates a physical link between the relaxosomal nucleoprotein complex and the membrane-bound DNA transfer apparatus (PMID: 11258958). (from Pfam)

Once a recipient cell acquires pPD1, it starts to produce an inhibitor of cPD1, termed iPD1, which functions as a TraA antagonist and blocks self-induction in donor cells. TraA transduces the signal of cPD1 to the mating response (PMID: 12399504). (from Pfam)

For FtsZ it inhibits its GTPase activity and GTP-dependent polymerisation, and for MreB it inhibits its ATP-dependent polymerisation. It is thought to be a hydrophobic protein that forms inclusion bodies within the bacterial cell, and may be secreted by the Mxi system (PMID: 7591128). Most members of this family are annotated as putative enterotoxins, but one member (Swiss:Q8X606) is a regulator of acetyl CoA synthetase, and another two members (Swiss:P76205 and Swiss:P23325) are annotated as ankyrin-like regulatory proteins and contain Ank repeats (Pfam:PF00023). The leader RNA contains translational start and stop signals, a cluster of four leucine codons and overlapping regions of dyad symmetry that are capable of forming stem-and-loop structures (PMID: 3922957). comment: The head binding domain found in the Phage P22 tailspike protein contains two regular beta-sheets, A and B, oriented nearly perpendicular to each other and composed of five and three strands respectively. The topology of the strands is exclusively antiparallel. The tailspike protein trimerises through this domain, and the direction of the strands with respect to the molecular triad is almost parallel for beta-sheet A, whereas beta-sheet B is perpendicular to the triad, forming a dome-like structure. This domain is dispensable for thermostability and SDS resistance of the intact protein, and its deletion has only minor effects on tailspike folding kinetics (PMID: 9135118). (from Pfam)

label: FimH_man-bind
comment: Members of this family adopt a secondary structure consisting of a beta sandwich, with nine strands arranged in two sheets in a Greek key topology. They are predominantly found in bacterial mannose-specific adhesins, since they are capable of binding to D-mannose (PMID: 12010488). (from Pfam)

label: Antig_Caf1
comment: Members of this family are predominantly found in the F1 capsule antigen Caf1 synthesised by Yersinia bacteria. They adopt a structure consisting of a seven strands arranged in two beta-sheets, in a Greek-key topology, and mediate targeting of the bacterium to sites of infection (PMID: 12787500). (from Pfam)

label: Phage-scaffold
comment: Members of this family of scaffolding proteins are produced by various bacteriophages (PMID: 10764583). (from Pfam)

label: Porin_OmpG
comment: Porins are channel proteins in the outer membrane of gram negative bacteria which mediate the uptake of molecules required for growth and survival. Escherichia coli OmpG forms a 14 stranded beta-barrel and in contrast to most porins, appears to function as a monomer (PMID: 16797588). The central pore of OmpG is wider than other E. coli porins and it is speculated that it may form a non-specific channel for the transport of larger oligosaccharides (PMID: 16797588). (from Pfam)

label: RcsC
comment: This domain is found in the C-terminus of the phospho-relay kinase RcsC between Pfam:PF00512 and Pfam:PF00072, and forms a discrete alpha/beta/loop structure (PMID: 17005198). (from Pfam)

label: TraQ
product_name: Type-F conjugative transfer system pilin chaperone (TraQ)
name_orig: Type-F conjugative transfer system pilin chaperone (TraQ)
hmm_name: Type-F conjugative transfer system pilin chaperone (TraQ)
comment: This entry represents TraQ, a protein that makes a specific interaction with pilin (TraA) to aid its transfer through the inner membrane during the process of F-type conjugative pilus assembly. (from Pfam)

label: TraS
product_name: Plasmid conjugative transfer entry exclusion protein TraS
name_orig: Plasmid conjugative transfer entry exclusion protein TraS
hmm_name: Plasmid conjugative transfer entry exclusion protein TraS
comment: Entry exclusion (Eex) is a process which prevents redundant transfer of DNA between donor cells. TraS is a protein involved in Eex. It blocks redundant conjugative DNA synthesis and transport between donor cells, and it is suggested that TraS interferes with a signalling pathway that is required to trigger DNA transfer (PMID: 17259615). TraS on the recipient cell is known to form an interaction with TraG on the donor cell (PMID: 17259615). (from Pfam)

label: DUF2509
comment: This family is conserved in Proteobacteria. The function is not known but many of the members are annotated as protein YgdB. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2526
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function is restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. The family has a highly conserved sequence. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2527
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to a family of Enterobacterial proteins. It has a highly conserved sequence. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_Cox
comment: This family of phage Cox proteins is expressed by Enterobacteria phages. The Cox protein is a 79-residue basic protein with a predicted strong helix-turn-helix DNA-binding motif. It inhibits integrative recombination and it activates site-specific excision of the HP1 genome from the Haemophilus influenzae chromosome, Hp1. Cox appears to function as a tetramer. Cox binding sites consist of two direct repeats of the consensus motif 5'-GGTMAWWWWA, one Cox tetramer binding to each motif. Cox binding interferes with the interaction of HP1 integrase with one of its binding sites, IBS5. This competition is central to directional control. Both Cox binding sites are needed for full inhibition of integration and for activating excision, because it plays a positive role in assembling the nucleoprotein complexes that produce excisive recombination, by inducing the formation of a critical conformation in those complexes (PMID: 9079698). (from Pfam)

label: HofP
comment: This family includes the Escherischia coli protein HofP, one of eight genes shown to be required for the utilization of extracellular DNA as a nutrient source in starving conditions, allowing DNA to be the sole source for carbon and energy (PMID: 16707682). Proteins in this entry appear are found only in Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2534
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: Toxin_GhoT_OrtT
comment: GhoT is part of the GhoT-GhoS type V toxin-antitoxin (TA) system [1, 2]. OrtT is homologous to GhoT, but it is not part of a TA pair. In this case, it acts as an independent toxin to reduce growth during stress related to amino acid and DNA synthesis (PMID: 25643179). (from Pfam)

label: YbaJ
comment: YbaJ regulates biofilm formation. It also has an important role in the regulation of motility in the biofilm. YbaJ functions in increasing conjugation, aggregation and decreasing the motility, resulting in an increase of biofilm (PMID: 16317765) (from Pfam)

label: DUF2583
comment: Some members in this family of proteins are annotated as YchH however currently no function is known. (from Pfam)

label: AcrZ
product_name: AcrZ family multidrug efflux pump-associated protein
hmm_name: AcrZ family multidrug efflux pump-associated protein
comment: AcrZ is associated with the AcrA-TolC multidrug efflux pump, it may enhance the ability of the pump to recognise and export certain substrates (PMID: 23010927). (from Pfam)

label: YbjO_DH-like
comment: This family of proteins includes the Inner membrane protein YbjO which appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. From AlphaFold structure predictions, it has been suggested that these proteins may function as dehydrogenases. (from Pfam)

label: YlaC
comment: Members of this family include proteins annotated as inner membrane protein YlaC in E. coli and Salmonella. The function of this family is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: DSRB
comment: DSRB is a novel dextransucrase which produces a dextran different from the typical dextran, as it contains (1-6) and (1-2) linkages, when this strain is grown in the presence of sucrose (PMID: 9503626). (from Pfam)

label: Plasmid_stab_B
comment: This family is conserved in the Enterobacteriales. It is a putative plasmid stability protein in that it is expressed from the operon involved in stability, but its actual function has not yet been characterised. (from Pfam)

label: Anti-adapt_IraP
comment: This family is conserved in Enterobacteriaceae. It is one of a series of proteins, expressed by these bacteria in response to stress, that help to regulate Sigma-S, the stationary phase sigma factor of Escherichia coli and Salmonella. IraP is essential for Sigma-S stabilisation in some but not all starvation conditions (PMID: 18383615). (from Pfam)

label: DUF2543
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appear to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. The family has a highly conserved sequence. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2556
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2560
comment: This family of proteins has no known function. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2645
comment: This family of proteins appear to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. Some members in the family are annotated as YjeO however no function for this protein is currently known. (from Pfam)

label: Phage_186_Fil
product_name: phage filamentation protein Fil family protein
hmm_name: phage filamentation protein Fil family protein
comment: This family is represented by Bacteriophage 186, Fil, a protein that causes filamentation. The characteristics of the protein distribution suggest prophage matches in addition to the phage matches. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2756
comment: Some members in this family of proteins are annotated yhhA however currently no function is known. The family appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2767
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2770
comment: Members in this family of proteins are annotated as yceO however currently no function is known. (from Pfam)

label: YbjM
name_orig: Putative inner membrane protein of Enterobacteriaceae
comment: This family is conserved in the Enterobacteriaceae. It is a putative inner membrane protein, named YbjM, but the function is not known. (from Pfam)

label: YbhQ
comment: This family is conserved in Proteobacteria. The function is not known but most members are annotated as being inner membrane protein YbhQ. (from Pfam)

label: GhoS

hmm_name: type V toxin-antitoxin system endoribonuclease antitoxin GhoS
comment: GhoS is part of the GhoT-GhoS type V toxin-antitoxin (TA) system. GhoT is inhibited by antitoxin GhoS, which specifically cleaves its mRNA [1, 2]. (from Pfam)

label: TrbE
comment: TrbE is essential for conjugation and phage adsorption. It contains four common motifs and one conserved domain (PMID: 12533481). (from Pfam)

label: DUF2623
comment: This family is conserved in the Enterobacteriaceae family. Several members are named as YghW. The function is not known. (from Pfam)

label: DUF2633
comment: This family is conserved largely in Gammaproteobacteria. Several members are named as YfgG. The function is not known. (from Pfam)

label: Repressor_Mnt
comment: Mnt is a repressor which is involved in the genetic switch between lysogenic and lytic growth in bacteriophage P22. The C-terminal domain of the protein consists of a dimer of two antiparallel coiled coils with a right handed twist, which is both stronger and has closer inter-helical separation compared with those found in left-handed coiled coils (PMID: 10426954). (from Pfam)

label: DUF3251
comment: This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. This domain is found in a group of bacterial lipoproteins such as YajI from E.coli and SadB from Salmonella typhimurium. SadB is required for proper surface expression of the autotransporter adhesin SadA (PMID: 24369174). (from Pfam)

label: Zn_ribbon_11
comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins with unknown function and appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae. It is predicted to adopt a structure typical for zinc-ribbon domains. (from Pfam)

label: DUF3561
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This protein is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are about 110 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DeaD_C
comment: This region family is found at the C-terminus of the DeaD helicase, which are involved in various cellular processes such as transcription, translation and DNA recombination (PMID: 8552679). This region contains several repeats which contain an ERRE sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: LRR_TTSS
name_orig: Type III secretion system leucine rich repeat protein
hmm_name: Type III secretion system leucine rich repeat protein
comment: This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 50 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved residues (Y and W) that may be functionally important. This family consists of leucine-rich repeat proteins involved in type III secretion. (from Pfam)

label: T2SSppdC

hmm_name: Type II secretion prepilin peptidase dependent protein C

label: DUF3748
comment: This domain family is found in bacteria and eukaryotes, and is approximately 120 amino acids in length. It is likely to contain 2 to 3 copies of a PD40-like repeat. (from Pfam)

label: FinO_N
comment: This domain family is found in bacteria, and is typically between 62 and 102 amino acids in length. The family is found in association with Pfam:PF04352. The FinOP (fertility inhibition) system of F-like plasmids consists of an antisense RNA (FinP) and a 22 kDa protein (FinO) which act in concert to prevent the translation of TraJ, the positive regulator of the transfer operon. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4060
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: VEVV and SYVAT. (from Pfam)

label: T3SS_LEE_assoc
product_name: type III secretion system domain-containing protein
comment: This is a family of bacterial putative type III secretion apparatus proteins associated with the locus of enterocyte effacement (LEE). (from Pfam)

label: Lipoprotein_20
comment: This family includes the YfhG protein from E. coli Swiss:P0AD44. Members of this family have an N-terminal lipoprotein attachment site. The members of this family are functionally uncharacterized. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4222
comment: This short protein is likely to be of phage origin. For example it is found in the Swiss:B6DZ51 Enterobacteria phage YYZ-2008. It is largely found in enteric bacteria. The molecular function of this protein is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: SopA_C
comment: This domain is found in the E. coli Type III secretion effector proteins SopA and NleL [1,2]. These proteins have been shown to act as E3 ubiquitin ligase enzymes. This domain contains the active site cysteine residue. (from Pfam)

label: UPF0370
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 70 amino acids in length. There is a conserved DWP sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: YbfN
comment: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 110 amino acids in length. Members of this family are lipoproteins. (from Pfam)

label: MsyB
comment: The MsyB protein has been found to be able to restore protein export defects caused by a temperature-sensitive secY or secA mutation (PMID: 1537791). However, its exact molecular function is still unknown, but it may play a role in protein export. Proteins in this family are approximately 120 amino acids in length. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: YbgS
comment: Members of this family, a putative secreted protein, are named for YbgS of Escherichia coli.

label: YedD
comment: This family of proteins related to the YedD protein is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 140 amino acids in length. These proteins are lipoproteins. (from Pfam)

label: YejG
comment: The YejG protein family is a group of functionally uncharacterised proteins related to Swiss:P0AD21. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 110 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: BssS
comment: The BssS protein family is a group of proteins that are involved in regulation of biofilm formation (PMID: 16597943). Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: YccJ
comment: The YccJ-like family of proteins includes the E. coli YccJ protein (PMID: 9868784) Swiss:P0AB14 which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: YebF
comment: Members of this family include both YebF as found in Escherichia coli str. K-12 and Salmonella enterica str. LT2, and the distantly related colicin M immunity protein Cmi (see NBR005890).

label: YobH
comment: The YobH-like protein family includes the YobH protein from E. coli Swiss:Q2MB16 which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: GYG and GLGL. (from Pfam)

label: PBP1_TM
product_name: Transmembrane domain of transglycosylase PBP1 at N-terminal
name_orig: Transmembrane domain of transglycosylase PBP1 at N-terminal
hmm_name: Transmembrane domain of transglycosylase PBP1 at N-terminal
comment: This is the N-terminal, transmembrane, domain of the transglycosylases ()penicillin-binding proteins), the multi-domain membrane proteins essential for cell wall synthesis that are targeted by penicillin antibiotics. The TM domain is a single helix, several of whose residues lie in close proximity to hydrophobic residues in the TGT domain. The TM helix seems to be necessary for stabilizing the protein-membrane interaction, and the resulting orientation limits the interaction between PBPb1 and lipid II in the membrane in a 2D lateral diffusion fashion (PMID: 19458048). (from Pfam)

label: YjcB
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 90 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4752
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and viruses. Proteins in this family are typically between 90 and 105 amino acids in length. There is a conserved GLA sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4761
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 110 amino acids in length. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4762
comment: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 70 amino acids in length. There is a conserved TTC sequence motif. (from Pfam)

label: TonB_N
comment: TonB from Escherichia coli and its homologues are critical for the uptake of siderophores through the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria using chemiosmotic energy. The proline-rich segment of TonB exists in a PPII-like conformation (PMID: 20095050). The result implies that the proline-rich segment of TonB possesses a length of more than 15 nm, sufficient to span the periplasm of Gram-negative bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: RcsD_ABL
comment: This domain is part of the RcsD histidine kinase. It recognises the effector domain of RcsB (PMID: 21481780). (from Pfam)

label: MatB
product_name: common pilus major fimbrillin subunit EcpA
hmm_name: common pilus major fimbrillin subunit EcpA
comment: This is a family of fimbrial proteins (PMID: 11466275). (from Pfam)

label: NleF_casp_inhib
comment: Binds to and inhibits caspase-9, caspase-8 and caspase-4. therefore preventing caspase-induced apoptosis in the host cell (PMID: 23516580). (from Pfam)

label: Inj_translocase
name_orig: DNA/protein translocase of phage P22 injectosome
comment: Inj_translocase is a family of putative phage translocases that are involved in the injectosome mechanism. Phage P22 of Salmonella typhimurium ejects four proteins, gp7, gp16, gp20 and gp26, which are ejected from the phage virion into the bacterial cell after absorption. These four proteins may play a role in DNA ejection [1,2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: GAPES3
comment: GAPES3 (GAmmaproteobacterial PEriplasmic Sensor) domain is a periplasmic sensor domain found in diguanylate cyclases/phosphodiesterases, including the c-di-GMP phosphodiesterases PdeK (YhjK) of Escherichia coli and HmsP of Yersinia pestis [1,2,3]. (from Pfam)

label: phage_ECs1072
comment: Members of this family are found broadly in the prophage regions in Gammaproteobacteriam and may be a marker of temperate phage or prophage. Members cited in publications and discoverable via PaperBLAST include STMMW_20121 from Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium str. D23580, with proof of transcription, and ECs1072 from Escherichia coli O157:H7 str. Sakai.

label: small_Blr
comment: Members of this family are Blr, named beta-lactam resistance protein because mutants have heightened sensitivity to beta-lactam antibiotics, but actually involved in cell division. The protein is very small.

label: penta_rpt_QnrE
product_name: QnrE family quinolone resistance pentapeptide repeat protein
name_orig: QnrE family quinolone resistance pentapeptide repeat protein
hmm_name: QnrE family quinolone resistance pentapeptide repeat protein
comment: Members of this family are QnrE, a pentapeptide repeat protein that confers a reduced sensitivity to quinolone family antibiotics. The QnrE family is most closely related to QnrB.

label: mlaB_1
comment: MlaB belongs to a system that maintains asymmetry in the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, with LPS in the outer leaflet and phospholipids in the inner leaflet. Several components of the system share homology with typical ABC transporters.

label: pqiC
comment: PqiC (YmbA), a lipoprotein, has been identified as part of the PqiABC system, a transporter that bridges the inner and outer membranes in species such as Escherichia coli and is important to membrane integrity.

label: HpxX
comment: HpxX is a small protein of unknown function, about 60 residues in length, encoded in the set of four genes, hpxWXYZ, that belong to the oxalurate metabolism portion of a complete pathway for hypoxanthine (hpx) utilization, as in Klebsiella pneumoniae.

label: acid_shock_Asr
product_name: acid resistance repetitive basic protein Asr
name_orig: acid resistance repetitive basic protein Asr
hmm_name: acid resistance repetitive basic protein Asr
comment: Asr (acid shock RNA) is an acid shock-inducible periplasmic protein that provides tolerance to low pH conditions. Beyond its signal peptide, most of its length consists of repeats rich in Lys, His, Ala, and Gln, such as APAAQKAQAAKKHKKVAKK.

label: stress_AzuC
comment: AzuC is a basic, extremely small protein (28 amino acids in Escherichia coli K-12) whose expression is repressed by cyclic AMP response protein (CRP) and stimulated by acidic pH.

label: polymyxin_MCR8
comment: MCR-8 was first described on a transferrable IncFII-type plasmid found in Klebsiella pneumoniae.

label: leader_RseD
comment: RseD, as described originally in Escherichia coli, is a leader peptide translationally coupled to the extracytoplasmic stress response sigma factor RpoE. It participates in the CrsA-mediated fine-tuning of the stress response. It is found also in Salmonella enterica, Cedecea neteri, etc. The corresponding locus in Klebsiella pneumoniae appears to be split into an upstream and a downstream peptide.

label: yciY_fam
comment: Members of the YciY family are named after the gene symbol given in E. coli K-12, but members of the family are found also in Salmonella, Klebsiella, Yersinia, Erwinia, etc.

label: phos_trans_PitA
comment: PitA is a low-affinity transporter for inorganic phosphate. It imports phosphate complexed to divalent cations such as Mg(2+) or Ca(2+). Loss of PitA function can confer reduced sensitivity to high levels of Zn(2+). The PitA of Escherichia coli has a closely related paralog, PitB, that is functional but only minimally expressed. Note that the term PitA is used broadly. This exception-level HMM identifies a rather narrow clade of PitA transporters which, however, includes both PitA and PitB of E. coli K-12.

label: entry_exc2_fam
comment: Exc2, a plasmid-encoded predicted lipoprotein of small size, was once described as a plasmid entry exclusion protein (1985). However, a more recent article (1995), says entry exclusion activity should instead be ascribed to MbeD.

label: small_MgtS
comment: MgtS, previously called YneM, is a small inner membrane protein that modulates Mg(2+) concentrations through its effects on the P-type transporter MgtA.

label: PsaF
product_name: PsaF/MyfF family fimbrial adhesin regulatory protein
hmm_name: PsaF/MyfF family fimbrial adhesin regulatory protein
comment: Members of this family regulate expression of fimbrial adhesins PsaA (pH 6 antigen) in Yersinia pestis and MyfA (mucoid Yersina factor A) in Yersinia enterocolitica.

label: DUF5375
comment: This is a family of unknown function found in Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: DUF5431
comment: This is a family of unknown function found in Enterobacteriaceae. (from Pfam)

label: CadC_C1
comment: CadC is an integral membrane protein of 512 amino acids comprising an N-terminal cytoplasmic DNA-binding domain, a transmembrane helix, and a C-terminal periplasmic domain. CadC belongs to the ToxR-like regulators that encompass biochemically non-modified one-component systems with similar gross topology, including several low pH-induced transcription regulators. Structural analysis of the C-terminal periplasmic domain indicates that it resembles the sensory domain of a (pH-activated) ToxR-like regulator. Furthermore, it is composed of two subdomains with a cavity at their interface that is suited to accommodate cadaverine, the feedback inhibitor of the Cad system. This is the N-terminal subdomain of the C-terminal periplasmic domain. It is composed of five-stranded beta-sheets (PMID: 21308846). (from Pfam)

label: pilot_rel_YacC
comment: Members of this, including YacC from Escherichia coli K-12, resemble the lipoprotein GspS of type II secretion systems (T2SS), but in general are not lipoproteins. In E. coli K-12, where the T2SS is cryptic (not expressed, but able to function after manipulation to force its express), YacC is encoded far from the locus where the main set of T2SS genes are found, and it is not clear that YacC is a true GspS.

comment: This narrowly built model for CueP includes periplasmic proteins from Salmonella enterica, in which it contributes to an increased tolerance to copper, and from various other Gram-negative bacteria. It does not include CueP lipoproteins from species such as Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

label: RipC_Ccl
comment: Third step in itaconate degradation.

label: LapC_YejM_PbgA
comment: YejM (LapC, PbgA) belongs to a regulatory system that controls the activity of LpxC, the enzyme that catalyzes the first committed step in the LPS synthesis. The earlier report (2015) by Dalebroux, et al (PMID: 25856753), which assigned a role in cardiolipin transport and introduced the name PbgA (phoPQ-barrier gene A), is no longer considered accurate.

label: AB5_pltB_like
product_name: subtilase family AB5 toxin binding subunit
hmm_name: subtilase family AB5 toxin binding subunit
comment: Members of this family are the B subunit of AB5 toxins such as the ADP-ribosylating cytotoxin subtilase, which is related to pertussis toxin. These B subunits, in general, form homopentamers. This family does not include any related pertussis toxin subunits (such as PtxB, PtxC, or PtxE), although some members of this family may have carried legacy annotations saying they are pertussis toxin proteins.

label: DUF6347
comment: This entry represents a member of a biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC). This BGC (BGC0001130) is described by MIBiG as an example of the following biosynthetic classes, NRP (non-ribosomal peptide) and polyketide, in particular the fabclavine Ia biosynthetic gene cluster from Xenorhabdus budapestensis (PMID: 24532262). (from Pfam)

label: ydgH_STM1478
comment: YdgH is the rare paralog in the DUF1471 family (PF07338) with three tandem copies of the DUF1471 domain instead of just one. Note that STM1478 from the Salmonella enterica model strain LT2 is also called SssB.

label: ZirU_fam
comment: ZirU, as found in Salmonella, shares with ZirS the property of requiring ZirT for its type Vb-like secretion. This HMM describes a broader family of ZirU homologs. The N-terminal half of this HMM shows detectable homology (although scoring below the cutoffs set for the model) to ZirT (zinc regulated transporter), but no similarity to ZirS (zinc regulated secreted protein)

label: dnaB_SPI-7_type
comment: Members of this family are DnaB-PI, a pathogenicity island (PI) variant of the replicative DNA helicase DnaB. Members are found with other conjugative element replication proteins such as ParA, ParB in genetic islands whose core proteins (but not cargo proteins) are shared with the Salmonella typhi SPI-7 island.

label: LdtF_DpaA_YafK
comment: DpaA (previously YafK and LdtF) murein L,D-transpeptidases, but actually functions as an amidase. In E. coli, the most abundant protein is the lipoprotein Lpp, anchored to the inner face of the outer membrane, but cross-linked to the peptidoglycan cell wall by the transpeptidases LdtA, LdtB, and LdtC. DpaA (peptidoglycan meso-diaminopimelic acid protein amidase A) is an amidase that hydrolyzes those linkages.

label: partner_SinI

label: Pesticin_RB
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Pesticin from Yersinia pestis (Pst). Pst is a toxin that kills related bacteria of the same niche as Y.pestis. It is organised into three domains: an N-terminal translocation domain, the intermediate receptor binding domain (RB, this entry), and a C-terminal activity domain (Pfam:PF16754). This domain shows a beta-sheet of seven anti-parallel beta-strands together with three helices. It is essential for the intimate contact with the outer membrane protein receptor [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: WHD_1st_3rd_SelB
comment: This domain is found twice in Selenocysteine-specific elongation factor from Escherichia coli (SelB) and in similar proteins mainly found in proteobacteria. SelB is a translation factor necessary for the incorporation of selenocysteine into proteins. SelB is composed of a N-terminal region, which contains Pfam:PF00009 and Pfam:PF03144, and a C-terminal extension that consists of four winged-helix (WH) domains arranged in tandem. This entry represents the first and third of these motifs, each containing three helices flanked by a three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet (PMID: 17537456). (from Pfam)

label: MgtS-like
comment: This family includes Small protein MgtS from Escherichia coli and similar sequences mainly found in gammaproteobacteria. MgtS, also known as YneM, is the product of a small open reading frame (smORF). This 31-amino-acid protein modulates intracellular magnesium levels to maintain cellular integrity [1,2]. It forms a single transmembrane helix (PMID: 29416041). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7024
comment: This domain has a structure that resembles the galactose-binding domain. This domain is often associated with a Pfam:PF00884 sulfatase like domain. Suggesting that this domain may be part of an enzyme that modifies some kind of carbohydrate. (from Pfam)

label: TcdA1_RBD_3
comment: This domain is found in TcdA1 from Photorhabdus luminescens and similar sequences from proteobacteria. TcdA1 is one of the three subunits of the Tc toxins. TcdA1 acts as an injecting device responsible for translocating the actual toxic component into host cells. TcA has four receptor-binding domains. This domain is one of 4 receptor binding domains found in TcA. All four domains have an immunoglobulin (Ig)-like beta-sandwich fold of two sheets with antiparallel beta-strands [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: ElaD-SseL-like_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal catalytic domain from a group of CE proteases from human pathogens including ElaD from E.coli, SseL from Salmonella typhimurium and ShiCE from Shigella [1,2], which are dedicated deubiquitinases (DUBs), proteases that reverse the addition of ubiquitin to substrates, and effectively hijacks the host's ubiquitination processes (PMID: 32109687). (from Pfam)

label: CofB_beta-rpt
comment: CofB is a minor pilin involved in type IV pili assembly. It consists of a pilin domain at the N-terminal, followed by a beta-repeat hinge-like domain and a C-terminal beta-sheet-rich lectin domain [1,2]. This entry represents the central beta-repeat domain which has two three-stranded anti-parallel beta-sheets [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: G7C_C
comment: This entry represents the Tailspike Concanavalin-like C-terminal domain, also known as domain 6 (d6) of the tailspike receptor-binding protein (RBP) gp63.1 of bacteriophage G7C. This domain is structurally similar to carbohydrate-binding domains and is putatively involved in substrate binding (PMID: 28513100). This beta-sandwich fold consists of two anti-parallel beta-sheets, each containing six strands. (from Pfam)

label: PssL
comment: This family includes Protein PssL from Escherichia coli, the product of a small open reading frame (smORF), which may serve a regulatory role in expression of downstream gene (PMID: 30837344). (from Pfam)

label: CofB_C
comment: CofB is a minor pilin involved in type IV pili assembly. It consists of a pilin domain at the N-terminal, followed by a beta-repeat hinge-like domain and a C-terminal beta-sheet-rich domain, similar to H-type lectins [1,2]. This entry represents the C-terminal domain which is required for CofB to initiate pilus assembly [1,2]. (from Pfam)

label: MlrA_C
comment: The HTH transcription regulator MlrA belongs to the MerR superfamily of transcription regulators that promote expression of several stress regulon genes by re configuring the spacer between the -35 and -10 promoter elements. MlrA it is also known as YehV, and has been shown to control cell-cell aggregation by co-regulating the expression of curli and extracellular matrix production in Escherichia coli and Salmonella yphimurium (PMID: 11489123). MlrA is part of a signaling cascade that regulates curli biosynthesis. These proteins have dissimilar C-terminal domains bind specific coactivator molecules. This entry represents the C-terminal domain, which is structurally similar to a B12 binding domain (Pfam:PF02310). (from Pfam)

label: ArgL-like

This protein is associated to strain virulence and is involved in surface adherence, biofilm formation and autoaggregation, essential for bladder and kidney colonization (PMID: 28017513). The family typically contains proteins between 80-120 amino acids in length. The function of this protein family is currently unknown. (from Pfam)

label: Blr_divisome
comment: This entry represents the Blr family, which consists of proteins that are components of the cell division machinery. These proteins are likely involved in the stabilization of the divisome, particularly under certain stress conditions. Blr is a short membrane protein that interacts with the essential cell division protein FtsL. Mutations in Blr have been shown to increase the sensitivity of bacteria to beta-lactam antibiotics or their resistance to cell envelope stress (PMID: 10931331). (from Pfam)

label: Msl2-3_C
comment: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of Mechanosensitive ion channel proteins 2 and 3 from Arabidopsis and related plant sequences. These channels open in response to stretch forces in the membrane lipid bilayer and control plastid size, shape, and perhaps division during normal plant development by altering ion flux in response to changes in membrane tension (PMID: 16401419). They act as a component of the chloroplast division machinery (PMID: 21810996). These channels are closely related to MscS from bacteria. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7823

label: DUF7828

Note that the correct length for STM2230 appears to be 129 amino acids, not 156. Homologs that are bacterial chromosomal proteins, such as UmuD, may be longer and remain inactive until the SOS response cleaves and removes an N-terminal propeptide, leaving an active protein about the length of HumD.

label: sbcc
comment: All proteins in this family for which functions are known are part of an exonuclease complex with sbcD homologs. This complex is involved in the initiation of recombination to regulate the levels of palindromic sequences in DNA. SulA proteins, like FtsZ, differ greatly by lineage; SulA of Pseudomonas is architecturally somewhat different and is described by a different model, NF041583.

label: 2A0120
comment: This family of proteins is an efflux system for lactose, glucose, aromatic glucosides and galactosides, cellobiose, maltose, a-methyl glucoside and other sugar compounds. They are found in both gram-negative and gram-postitive bacteria.

label: YfhB_g-proteo
comment: PgpC (previously YfhB), as found in Escherichia coli, is a member of the haloacid dehalogenase (HAD) superfamily of aspartate-dependent hydrolases.

label: HpaX
comment: This protein is a part of the Major Facilitator Superfamily (Pfam family PF07690). Member of this family are found in a number of proteobacterial genomes, but only in the context of having genes for 4-hydroxyphenylacetate (4-HPA) degradation. The protein is characterized by Prieto, et al. (PMID:9315705) as 4-hydroxyphenylacetate permease in E. coli, where 3-HPA and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetate are shown to competitively inhibit 4-HPA transport and therefore also interact specificially.

label: dak_ATP
comment: This family consists of examples of the form of dihydroxyacetone kinase (also called glycerone kinase) that uses ATP (2.7.1.29) as the phosphate donor, rather than a phosphoprotein as in E. coli. This form is composed of a single chain with separable domains homologous to the K and L subunits of the E. coli enzyme, and is found in yeasts and other eukaryotes and in some bacteria, including Citrobacter freundii. The member from tomato has been shown to phosphorylate dihydroxyacetone, 3,4-dihydroxy-2-butanone, and some other aldoses and ketoses (PMID:11985845).

label: wecD_rffC
comment: This model represents the WecD protein (Formerly RffC) for the biosynthesis of enterobacterial common antigen (ECA), an outer leaflet, outer membrane glycolipid with a trisaccharide repeat unit. WecD is a member of the GNAT family of acetytransferases (PF00583).

Although strictly associated with type III secretion systems, this protein seems not yet to have been characterized as part of the apparatus or as an effector protein.

label: rep_term_tus

This protein, DNA replication terminus site-binding protein, binds specific DNA sites near the replication terminus to arrest the DNA replication fork.

label: symport_actP
comment: Members of this family belong to the Sodium:solute symporter family. Both members of this family and other close homologs tend to be encoded next to a member of Pfam family PF04341, a set of uncharacterized membrane proteins. The characterized member from E. coli is encoded near and cotranscribed with the acetyl coenzyme A synthetase (acs) gene. Proximity to an acs gene was used as one criterion for determining the trusted cutoff for this model. Closely related proteins may differ in function and are excluded by the high cutoffs of this model; members of the family of phenylacetic acid transporter PhaJ can score as high as 1011 bits.

label: TraA_TIGR

hmm_name: type IV conjugative transfer system pilin TraA
comment: TraA is the single structural subunit of the pilus found in type IV conjugative transfer systems. This family is generally found in gammaproteobacteria. The pilins show considerable heterogeneity among the different conjugative plasmit types. All of them however contain an N-terminal part which is cleaved off by a leader peptidase (LepB, or similar) to result in a 68-78 amino acid product. Pilins may be further processed by acetylation (in F-like systems by the TraX protein) or by cyclization (in P-like systems by the TraF protein) [1].

label: ABALDH
comment: Members of this protein family are Aminobutyraldehyde dehydrogenase (EC 1.2.1.19), also called 1-pyrroline dehydrogenase and gamma-aminobutyraldehyde dehydrogenase. This enzyme can follow putrescine aminotransferase (EC 2.6.1.82) for a two-step conversion of putrescine to gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA). The member from Escherichia coli is characterized as a homotetramer that binds one NADH per momomer. This enzyme belongs to the medium-chain aldehyde dehydrogenases, and is quite similar in sequence to the betaine aldehyde dehydrogenase (EC 1.2.1.8) family.

label: cellullose_BcsF
comment: Members of this protein family are found invariably together with genes of bacterial cellulose biosynthesis, and are presumed to be involved in the process. Members average about 63 amino acids in length and are not uncharacterized. The gene has been designated both YhjT and BcsF (bacterial cellulose synthesis F).

label: FliZ
comment: FliZ is involved in the regulation of flagellar assembly [1] and possibly also the down-regulation of the motile phenotype [2]. FliZ interacts with the flagellar translational activator FlhCD complex.

label: FnlA
comment: The FnlA enzyme is the first step in the biosynthesis of UDP-FucNAc from UDP-GlcNAc in E. coli (along with FnlB and FnlC). The proteins identified by this model include FnlA homologs in the O-antigen clusters of O4, O25, O26, O29 (Shigella D11), O118, O145 and O172 serotype strains, all of which produce O-antigens containing FucNAc (or the further modified FucNAm). A homolog from Pseudomonas aerugiosa serotype O11, WbjB, also involved in the biosynthesis of UDP-FucNAc has been characterized and is now believed to carry out both the initial 4,6-dehydratase reaction and the subsequent epimerization of the resulting methyl group at C-5 [1]. A phylogenetic tree of related sequences shows a distinct clade of enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of UDP-QuiNAc (Qui=qinovosamine). This clade appears to be descendant from the common ancestor of the Pseudomonas and E. coli fucose-biosynthesis enzymes. It has been hypothesized [2] that the first step in the biosynthesis of these two compounds may be the same, and thus that these enzymes all have the same function. At present, lacking sufficient confirmation of this, the current model trusted cutoff only covers the tree segment surrounding the E. coli genes. The clades containing the Pseudomonas and QuiNAc biosynthesis enzymes score above the noise cutoff. Immediately below the noise cutoff are enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of UDP-RhaNAc (Rha=rhamnose), which again may or may not produce the same product.

label: RiPP_XyeA
comment: Members of this family are short polypeptides with a conserved GG motif as found in bacteriocins that are cleaved upon export. Each gene occurs immediately upstream of a gene for a peptide-modifying radical SAM/SPASM domain protein. The system was originally designated XYE by TIGRFAMs for genera Xenorhabdus, Yersinia, and Erwinia, hence XyeA for the precursor peptide. Subsequent work established that the modifications made are the introduction of strained aromatic rings, called cyclophanes, by cross-linking the side chains of the first and third residues of tripeptides such as WXN, WXR, FXN, etc. The biosynthnthetic gene cluster (BGC) context as a rule contains also a transport protein with a C39 family peptidase domain (see PF03412), characteristic of GG motif cleave-on-export systems, and may contain additional tailoring enzymes. Individual members of this family may assigned more specific names, applicable in one species or isolate only, such as XncA from Xenorhabdus nematophila DSM 3370, or YkcA from Yersinia kristensenii.

hmm_name: Sec-independent protein translocase subunit TatB, alphaprotobacterial type
comment: Members of this family, found widely in members of the Rickettsiales, shares N-terminal homology with the TatB protein of twin arginine translocation.

label: C_WD1278_WD0630
comment: This domain is restricted to Wolbachia-like bacteria, where it occurs near the C-terminus of distantly related paralogs WD_1278 and WD_0630. WD_1278 has been named TomO (toxic manipulator of oogenesis) for its effects on cultured Drosophila cells.

label: cpg1_fam
comment: Cpg1 (Cowdria polymorphic gene 1) is named for a locus described in Ehrlichia (previously Cowdria) ruminantium and investigated as a possible vaccine antigen. E. ruminantium, an obligately intracellular pathogen, causes the disease heartwater. Members of this family are found in additional species of Ehrlichia, as well as in Anaplasma and Neoehrlichia species.

label: Erum7620_fam
comment: Erum7620 was identified as an immunogenic protein of the alphaproteobacterial bacterium Ehrlichia ruminantium, an obligate intracellular animal pathogen that causes the disease heartwater. ECH_0207 is a similar immunogenetic protein from Ehrlichia chaffeensis and has been called a putative type I secretion system (T1SS) effector. Members of the Erum7620/ECH_0207 family are DUF2628 domain-containing proteins (see PF10947). Close homologs of Erum7620 are found also multiple species of Ehrlichia and Anaplasma.

label: ECH1013_TF_S24
comment: Members of this putative transcription factor family of unknown role include ECH_1013 from Ehrlichia chaffeensis and APH_1100 (equivalent to HGE1_04712) from Anaplasma phagocytophilum. The N-terminal region contains an XRE-like helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain, while the C-terminal region contains a LexA-like S24 family serine protease domain. The expression of ECH_1013 was predicted to depend on a sigma-32 family sigma factor.

label: ECH_0659_fam
comment: Proteins of this family are conserved across some Ehrlichia and Wolbachia species. The gene encodes ECH_0659 family protein is tightly linked to several genes encoding phage proteins.

label: DUF3023
comment: This bacterial family of proteins with unknown function appear to be restricted to Alphaproteobacteria. (from Pfam)

label: EtpE
comment: It has been reported that the surface protein EtpE of Ehrlichia chaffeensis binds to GPI-Anchored protein DNase X and triggers entry into mammalian cells.

label: VLPT
comment: This family consists of a number of 29 residue repeats which seem to be specific to the Ehrlichia chaffeensis variable length PCR target (VLPT) protein. Ehrlichia chaffeensis is a tick-transmitted rickettsial agent and is responsible for human monocytic ehrlichiosis (HME). The function of this family is unknown (PMID: 12496165). (from Pfam)

label: Ehrlichia_rpt
name_orig: Ehrlichia chaffeensis immunodominant surface protein repeat
comment: This HMM represents 77 residues of an 80 amino acid (240 nucleotide) tandem repeat, found in a variable number of copies in TRP120, an immunodominant 120 kD outer membrane protein of Ehrlichia chaffeensis, a tick-borne obligate intracellular pathogen.

label: HGE-14_Nterm

comment: Anaplasma phagocytophilum (Ehrlichia phagocytophila) is a tick-borne intracellular pathogen that causes disease called anaplasmosis, human granulocytic anaplasmosis (HGA), or human granulocytic ehrlichiosis (HGE). A type IV secretion system (T4SS) secretes HGE-14 and paralogs that share this N-terminal domain of about 400 amino acids. HGE-14 itself (AAK69700.1) has a C-terminal region with a repeat region highly similar to that of a human host protein, mediator of DNA damage checkpoint protein 1 (NFBD1/MDC1), which is involved in responses to DNA damage and can help prevent apoptosis.

label: CcmD_like_Wolb
