comment: Members of this family are small proteins, about 45 amino acids in length, with a strongly hydrophobic N-terminal half, and with considerable sequence similarity to the longer protein CcmD described by Pfam model PF04995. This family occurs strictly in the genus Wolbachia, encoded next to an apparent CcmE protein.

label: T4SS_WalE1_fam
product_name: actin-bundling T4SS effector WalE1 family protein
hmm_name: actin-bundling T4SS effector WalE1 family protein
comment: WD_0830 from the Wolbachia endosymbiont of Drosophila melanogaster was characterized as an actin-bundling type IV secretion system effector, and designated WalE1 (Wolbachia actin-localizing effector 1). WalE1 alters Drosophila endocytosis, and acts as an embryonic defect-causing protein factor. WalE1 was described as related to eukaryotic alpha-synuclein, but it scores below cutoffs to the Pfam model PF01387. Homologs of WalE1 are widespread in the genus Wolbachia. This HMM covers most of the lengths of WalE1 and its homologs from other related endosymbionts.

label: porin_WD0745
comment: This family, including members WD0745 and Wbm0010, is widespread in Wolbachia endosymbionts. Members are predicted to be porins, based on sequence similarity to Asp55 from Anaplasma phagocytophilum and on HMM hits to family members by the shorter but more broadly defined Pfam HMM PF13609.

label: TomO_WD1278
comment: This HMM represents the conserved core region of surface-exposed or secreted protein TomO (WD_1278) from the Wolbachia endosymbiont of Drosophila melanogaster and its homologs from other species of Wolbachia. TomO contains also a separately described hydrophobic tail region that it shares with WD_0630 and its orthologs. In additition, some TomO proteins contain an ankyrin repeat domain or a lipase domain. TomO (Toxic Manipulator of Oogenesis) was found to colocalize with host (Drosophila) RNA-binding proteins and to reverse the sterility of female fruit flies carrying the sex-lethal (sxl) mutation.

label: WBM0748_T4SS
comment: The founding member of this family, WBM0748 from the Wolbachia endosymbiont of Brugia malayi, was observed to be coexpressed with type IV secretion system (T4SS) apparatus proteins, as were several neighboring proteins. It was therefore suggested to be a T4SS effector, although coexpression without evidence of secretion or of homology to previously described effector proteins makes the hypothesis of effector activity somewhat weak. Homologs are found broadly in Wolbachia endosymbionts.

label: WD_0736_fam
comment: This family, restricted to the Wolbachia-like alphaproteobacterial endosymbionts, appears distantly related to the DUF4293 (PF14126) family of putative membrane proteins.

label: tandem_WD_0033
comment: This HMM describes a tandem repeat region of about 48 amino acids that occurs widely in Wolbachia, including three proteins from the Wolbachia endosymbiont of Drosophila melanogaster, namely WD_0033, WD_0034, and WD_0290. Proteins with this repeat are variable in length, with variable numbers of the repeat.

label: WPE_wolbac
hmm_name: Wolbachia palindromic element WPE insertion domain
comment: This domain conceptually resembles TIGR01045, the Rickettsial palindromic element (RPE) domain. In both cases, a protein-coding palindromic element spreads through a genome, inserting usually in protein-coding regions. The additional protein coding sequence is thought to allow function of the host protein because of location in surface-exposed regions of the protein structure.

label: BD_b_sandwich
comment: A beta-sandwich domain exclusively found at the N-terminal of CHROMO domains in many Bdellovibrio proteins (PMID: 29670199). (from Pfam)

label: Bd2520-like_N
comment: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Putative lactoylglutathione lyase from Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus (Bd2520) and similar sequences predominantly found in prokaryotes. It shows a three-stranded beta-sheet and one alpha-helix. (from Pfam)

label: DUF4776

label: ALOG_dom
comment: The 125-residue ALOG (Arabidopsis LSH1 and oryza G1) domain is rich in basic amino acids, especially arginine, and is highly conserved among land plants. Members of the ALOG family of proteins function as key developmental regulators. It has been proposed that the ALOG domain originated from the N-terminal DNA-binding domains of integrases belonging to the tyrosine recombinase superfamily encoded by a distinct type of DIRS1-like LTR retrotransposon found in several eukaryotes. Secondary structure predictions revealed an all-alpha helical domain with four conserved helices [1,2]. Some proteins known to contain an ALOG domain are Arabidopsis thaliana LIGHT_DEPENDENT SHORT HYPOCOTYLS1 (LSH1),involved in phytochrome- dependent light signalling; Oryza G1, involved in the specification of sterile lemma identity and Plant defence proteins. (from Pfam)

label: P_gingi_FimA
hmm_name: Porphyromonas gingivalis FimA family fimbrial protein N-terminal domain
comment: This HMM describes a domain shared by various fimbrial major and minor subunit proteins, including FimA, FimC, Mfa3, and MfA4 in Porphyromonas gingivalis, typically found about 40 amino acids from the N-terminus and representing about a quarter of the total length of the protein.

label: BT_3987-like_N
comment: This domain, previously known as DUF1735, is found in a number of proteins mainly found in firmicutes, including BT_3987 from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, which displays hydrolytic activity against Hy-type N-glycans, probably initiating the degradation of this type of glycan in the human gut (PMID: 34324829). This domain adopts a beta-sandwich fold. (from Pfam)

label: Mfa2
name_orig: Fimbrillin-A associated anchor proteins Mfa1 and Mfa2
comment: This family of proteins may be lipoproteins principally from bacilli. They are between 300 and 400 residues. Many Bacteroides-like bacterial species, including Porphyromonas gingivalis, the causal agent of periodontal infection, carry at least two types of fimbriae, namely FimA and Mfa1 fimbriae, following the names of their major subunit proteins (PMID: 15972485). Normally, FimA fimbriae are long filaments that are easily detached from cells, whereas Mfa1 fimbriae are short filaments that are tightly bound to cells; however, in the absence of Mfa2 protein, the Mfa1 fimbriae are also very long and are not attached. Mfa2 and Mfa1 are associated with each other in whole P. gingivalis cells to the extent that Mfa2 is located on the cell surface and probably associated with Mfa1 fimbriae in such a way that it anchors the Mfa1 fimbriae to the cell surface and regulates Mfa1 filament length (PMID: 19589838). (from Pfam)

label: SPIN90_LRD
comment: This is the conserved leucine-rich domain (LRD) within the C-terminal domain of SPIN90 (also known as NCK interacting protein with SH3 domain (NCKIPSD)) from animals, Ldb17 from budding yeasts and Dip1 from fission yeasts (PMID: 30322896). Ldb17 is involved in the regulation of endocytosis in yeast (PMID: 19506040). SPIN90 is an F-actin binding protein that regulates actin polymerization and endocytosis (PMID: 17453829). It associates with and activates the Arp2/3 complex, without requiring a preformed actin filament [2,4,5]. This LRD, within the C-terminal armadillo repeat (ARM) domain of SPIN90, is important for activation of Arp2/3 complex (PMID: 30322896). (from Pfam)

label: DUF2027
comment: This protein domain is of unknown function. though putatively involved in DNA mismatch repair. It is associated with Pfam:PF01713. (from Pfam)

comment: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins from Bacteroidetes. This domain has a beta-sandwich prealbumin-like fold. (from Pfam)

label: DUF3843
comment: A family of uncharacterized proteins found by clustering human gut metagenomic sequences (PMID: 20532204). (from Pfam)

label: Mfa_like_1
comment: A family of putative fimbrillin proteins found by clustering human gut metagenomic sequences (PMID: 20532204). Analysis of structural comparisons shows this family to be part of the FimbA (CL0450) superfamily of adhesin components or fimbrillins. (from Pfam)

label: BT_3044-like_C
comment: This entry represents a domain found at the C-terminal end of a group of proteins from bacteroidetes, including BT_3044 from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, a glycan binding enzyme that could degrade oligosaccharides or even large molecular size glycans (PMID: 34420703). (from Pfam)

label: Bacteroid_pep
comment: Ribosomally synthesized peptide that is usually in the gene neighborhood of a RimK-like ATP-grasp, and an ABC ATPase fused to a papain-like domain. It is often present in multiple tandem gene copies. The gene contexts suggest that it is modified by the ATP-grasp as in the biosynthesis of microviridin and marinostatin. They might function in defense or development or as peptide antibiotics (PMID: 20023723). (from Pfam)

label: PLCC
comment: A small family of bacterial proteins, found in several Bacteroides species. Structure determination (NMR and Xray) shows an immunoglobulin beta-barrel fold. Multiple homologues have been found in human gut metagenomics data sets. Structural experimentation shows it to share features with two well-established protein architectures in the SCOP database, ie, C2 (calcium/lipid-binding domain) of [pfam:PF00168] and PLAT/LH2 (lipase/lipooxigenase domain) of [pfam:PF01477]. The C2 and PLAT/LH2 domains bind Ca2+ in their functions of targeting proteins to cell-membranes; this domain is also shown to bind Ca2+ as well as to be a novel fold (PMID: 23681886). (from Pfam)

label: DUF4488
comment: In most members this domain covers almost the whole sequence, but a few member-sequences also carry a TonB_C domain, PF03544. This domain has a lipocalin fold. (from Pfam)

hmm_name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4595) with porin-like fold
comment: Large family of predicted secreted proteins mostly from CFG group, but also from Burkholderia, Pseudomonas and Streptomyces. Function of these proteins is not known. A 3D structure of a representative of this family from Bacteroides uniformis was solved by JCSG and deposited to PDB as 4ghb. There is some overlap with RHS-repeat (PF05593) family despite lack of obvious repeats in the structure. (from Pfam)

comment: Fimbrillin_C is a C-terminal family of major fimbrial subunit protein type IV proteins largely from Bacillus species. The family is associated with family P_gingi_FimA, Pfam:PF06321. (from Pfam)

label: lant_leader_L1b
comment: This HMM describes a homology domain found regularly as a leader peptide, ending with a GlyGly dipeptide (a leader peptide cleavage site), of putative lanthipeptides (probably lantibiotics in most cases) encoded in the vicinity of a class I lanthionine synthase, or LanC. The designation L1b reflects model construction for class I lantibiotics (L1), second in a possible series (L1b), from the lanthipeptide RiPP collection found in PMID:32493223. Because the leader peptide may reflect constraints on cleavage and export, it may be expected that some members of the family undergo modifications other than lanthionine bridge formation, or no special modifications at all, but amino acid composition of member proteins C-terminal to the leader domain suggests that all are lanthipeptides, and probably act as lantibiotics.

comment: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Bacteroidetes and its function is unknown. It is approximately 60 amino acids in length. It contains a conserved motif DxxxW and a highly conserved tyrosine residue. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6633

label: DUF6808
comment: This is a domain of unknown function that is found in archaea and bacteria. This domain is typically around 110 amino acids in length. There are two conserved motifs, RW and VSG. (from Pfam)

label: HAD_phos_BT0820
comment: This family of hydrolases is named for BT0820 from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, which belongs to the HAD superfamily and was shown to hydrolyze phosphotyrosine. Members of this well-conserved protein family are found in multiple species of Bacteroides, Prevotella, Phocaeicola, etc. The physiologically relevant substrate of this enzyme is not yet known.

label: XrtY_assoc_Gly1
comment: XrtY is an exosortase family cysteine protease, and probable protein-sorting enzyme, although its substrates are unknown. Like many exosortases, it is associated with a large polysaccharide biosynthesis locus. This protein, here named XYAG1, appears to be one of the signature enzymes of the type of locus in which XrtY itself is found.

label: DUF6926
comment: This domain of unknown function is found in bacterial proteins. It is probably distantly related to dodecin. It is predicted to adopt a simple fold consisting of a core of 3 strands, forming a curved sheet, and two short helices. (from Pfam)

label: SNaCT9
comment: The SNaCT domains are a rapidly evolving, monophyletic assemblage of domains found C-terminal to the NACHT module in several bacterial NACHT conflict systems. They contain a well-conserved aspartate near the N-terminus of the domain. SNaCT domains are thought to occlude the NTP-binding region, potentially until they interact with phage-encoded bNACHT inhibitors (PMID: 37160116). (from Pfam)

label: PDXDC1-like_cen2
comment: This entry represents a domain found in Pyridoxal-dependent decarboxylase domain-containing protein 1 (PDXDC1) and related proteins. PDXDC1 has been associated with the modulation of prepulse inhibition of acoustic startle, perhaps through the metabolism of catecholamine neurotransmitters (PMID: 28485732). The function of this domain is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: BACOVA_00961-like
comment: This family represents BACOVA_00961 from Bacteroides ovatus (Swiss:A7LT22) and similar sequences mainly found in bacteroidetes. This protein shows an alpha-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: DUF6965
comment: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins which are predicted to form a small three helical bundle containing a beta hairpin between helices 1 and 2. (from Pfam)

label: DUF7015
comment: This domain of unknown function is found at the C-terminal of a group of bacterial proteins and, according to structure predictions, it may adopt a beta-barrel structure. It is often associated with an Ig-like domain (Pfam:PF08522). (from Pfam)

label: DUF7688
comment: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised protein found in bacteria. They are predicted to adopt alpha+beta structure defined as beta(2)alpha(2)beta(2) structural elements in which the beta-strands form an antiparallel beta-sheet.The function of these proteins is unknown. (from Pfam)

label: ChrA_rel_RiPP
comment: Members of this family closely resemble the chryseobasin RiPP precursor ChrA (see NF050124), especially in having the seven C-terminal residues as CP[GA]CG[LM]G. However, the central region differs greatly, is substantially shorter, and contains an invariant Cys residue whose significance is not yet clear. Members are found in multiple species of Chitinophaga, Hymenobacter, Dyadobacter, are various other genera. Like chryseobasins, members of this family are encoded next to a multinuclear non-heme iron dependent oxidative (MNIO) peptide maturase.

label: At5g54830
comment: This domain is found in Cytochrome b561, DM13 and DOMON domain -containing protein At5g54830 from Arabidopsis thaliana, which may act as a catecholamine-responsive trans-membrane electron transporter. This domain is predicted to adopt an all-beta configuration. (from Pfam)

label: PorU_rel_Nterm
product_name: putative type IX secretion system sortase PorU2
hmm_name: putative type IX secretion system sortase PorU2, N-terminal domain
comment: Members of this family are membrane-embedded cysteine proteinases that differ from the sortase PorU of characterized type IX secretion systems (T9SS) that is described in NF033707, and are only about 30 percent as abundant. Species with this family invariably have other proteins of the T9SS apparatus, often including PorU itself, but sometimes found where PorU is not found. Because members of this family often are encoded next to the homolog of T9SS proteins PorV and PorQ that we designate PorV2 (see NF052325), we suggest that this protein acts in a variant form of T9SS.

label: FlmA_fam_RIPP
comment: Members of this family are RiPP precursor peptides. Some, but not all, are found in the context of FlmR family peptide arginases such as WP_106143370.1, which convert arginine residues in peptides to ornithine post-translationally. All known members of this family have a C-terminal motif of [IL][LI]F.

label: rSAM_FlmE_OhkG
product_name: FlmE/OhkG family radical SAM/SPASM peptide maturase
hmm_name: FlmE/OhkG family radical SAM/SPASM peptide maturase

label: Riean_0653_fam
comment: The founding member of this family, Riean_0653 from poultry pathogen Riemerella anatipestifer, was found to be a requirement for competence to lyse duck erthyrocytes. However, recombinant protein does not have hemolytic activity, and the function is unknown. The family is widespread in the Flavobacteriales. Pfam model PF19765.5 (DUF6252) describes a domain with regions of homology to this family, and hits about half the members of this family with scores above its gathering thresholds.

label: CPBP_M949_0222
comment: Members of this family, named for WP_014938859.1 (M949_0223) from the duck pathogen Riemerella anatipestifer (a member of the Flavobacteriales), are CPBP family glutamic-type intramembrane endopeptidases. Disruption of the gene for this protein causes a defect in lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis. Although the mechanism for this effect is unknown, enzymes if this family often play a role in protein trafficking to the outer leaflet of the outer membrane.

label: adm_rel
comment: Members of this family have been described as secreted proteins with growth factor activity and regions of adenosine deaminase homology in insects, mollusks, and vertebrates.

label: squal_synth
comment: This HMM describes farnesyl-diphosphate farnesyltransferase, also known as squalene synthase, as found in eukaryotes. This family is related to phytoene synthases. Tentatively identified archaeal homologs (excluded from this model) lack the C-terminal predicted transmembrane region universally conserved among members of this family.

label: cas_csp2
comment: Members of this protein family are cas, or CRISPR-associated, proteins. The two sequences in the alignment seed are found within cas gene clusters that are adjacent to CRISPR DNA repeats in two members of the order Bacteroidales, Porphyromonas gingivalis W83 and Bacteroides forsythus ATCC 43037. This cas protein family is unique to the Pging (Porphyromonas gingivalis) subtype.

label: GldJ_short
comment: Members of this protein family are exclusive to the Bacteroidetes phylum (previously Cytophaga-Flavobacteria-Bacteroides). GldJ is a lipoprotein linked to a type of rapid surface gliding motility found in certain Bacteroidetes, such as Flavobacterium johnsoniae [1]. Knockouts of GldJ abolish the gliding phenotype. GldJ is homologous to GldK. This model represents the GldJ homolog in Cytophaga hutchinsonii and several other species which is of shorter architecture than that found in Flavobacterium johnsoniae and is represented by a separate model (TIGR03524). Gliding motility appears closely linked to chitin utilization in the model species Flavobacterium johnsoniae. Bacteroidetes with members of this protein family appear to have all of the genes associated with gliding motility.

label: metzin_BF0631
comment: Members of this protein family are zinc-dependent metalloproteinases, related to ulilysin and other members of the pappalysin family. Members occur as predicted lipoproteins and occur mostly in the genera Bacteriodes and Prevotella.

label: Bac_Flav_CTERM
product_name: T9SS type B sorting domain-containing protein
comment: Type IX secretions systems (T9SS) occur in the Bacteroidetes, such as Cytophaga hutchinsonii and Flavobacterium johnsoniae, and are required for the type of gliding motility seen in that lineage, although they are not limited processing target proteins from that system. The C-terminal domain described by TIGR04131, recognized as sorting signal by T9SS, is now known as type B, and is quite distinct from type A (see TIGR04183). Most targets of T9SS are cleaved by a transpeptidase and then attached to a component of the outer membrane, but a few are released in soluble form.

label: grasp_w_spasm_A
comment: This HMM describes the leader peptide domain, ending in a Gly-Gly cleavage motif, for a post-ribosomal natural product (PRNP) precursor. The corresponding modification enzymes include an ATP-GRASP enzyme and a SPASM-domain protein, related to the C-terminal region of numerous peptide-modification radical SAM enzymes.

label: LP_HExxH_w_tonB
comment: Members of this family are lipoproteins with the typical zinc metallohydrolase HExxH motif and additional similarities to a better-documented zinc peptidase family, PF06167. The seed alignment begins immediately after the lipoprotein motif Cys residue. Up to five members of this protein family occur per genome, in the context of certain gene pairs related to RagA and RagB, or to SusC and SusD. Those gene pairs, like the present family, are restricted to the Bacteriodetes, may number up to 100 pairs per genome, and are linked to TonB-dependent uptake of biopolymer-derived nutrients such as glycans. A possible function for this lipoprotein is to hydrolyse larger molecules to prepare substrates for import and utilization.

label: DUF3273
comment: Some members in this family of proteins are annotated as multi-transmembrane proteins however this cannot be confirmed. Currently this family has no known function. (from Pfam)
